english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a tiny fungus that loves high humidity and shade. Pruning overhead tree branches to let sunlight and air into your farm helps keep the pods dry and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungi bibii kɛ black pod hela baa. No sumɔɔ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni nɔ kwɔ. Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni oookpa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves soil soaked in water for days, air is forced out, causing fungal organisms to multiply and rot the underground tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo. Abaashwie kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas in my field help the soil grow better maize next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Cowpeas and beans have natural helpers on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the dirt. When the cowpea plants die, that trapped nitrogen acts as free fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji cowpea tso lɛ gbo Nitrogen ni amɔ lɛ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they suffer from stress like severe midday heat, lack of water, or dry soil. Watering regularly at the roots and putting mulch around the stem keeps the soil cool so the plant holds its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli. Nu fɔmɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa ni okɛ sũ awo amɛhe. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam plants make energy for growing big underground tubers through their leaves catching sunlight. Lifting the vines up on stakes helps leaves get maximum sun and prevents diseases that breed on damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei haa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji kɛtsɔ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ awó wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni ehaaa helai aba hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my tomato stems with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Tomato tsei ni jwɛi ni egbi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) shades the soil from the hot sun, stopping water from evaporating quickly so your tomatoes stay hydrated longer between waterings.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni nu lɛ akatsɔ la oya. Enɛ baaha o-tomatoi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ teŋ.

english: Why do my okra leaves get a white dusty powder on top of them during humid weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra baai lɛ hiɛ sũ yɛŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: That white dust is a fungal infection called powdery mildew, which thrives in warm, crowded spaces. Planting your okra further apart gives air room to flow between plants, keeping the leaves dry and clear.
ga: Nakai sũ yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Eshwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni gbɔmɛi eyi obɔ lɛ. Okra ni aduɔ srɔtoi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe tseɔ.

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster than my cultivated crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted for centuries to sprout immediately with tiny amounts of water. Cultivated crop seeds take longer to wake up, so clearing weeds early gives your seeds room to catch up.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ nu fioo ko pɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛteɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛshɛ he.

english: Why does lowland swamp rice need to stay flooded with water while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni nu awo ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni baa shi lɛ mli beni edaa lɛ?

english: Swamp rice thrives in submerged soil, but most wild weeds cannot survive underwater. Flooding the field keeps competing weeds away while allowing the rice roots to soak up all available soil nutrients.
ga: Swamp rice lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ nɔ. Shi koo mli jwɛi babaoo nyɛɛɛ ahi shi yɛ nu shishi. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid putting too much chemical fertilizer on food crops I want to feed my family?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ niyenii mli ni he hiaa mi koni mikɛha miweku lɛ niyenii babaoo he lɛ?

english: Using excess chemical fertilizer can make your crops soft and prone to quick spoilage, alter the natural taste of your harvest, and pollute nearby ground water, reducing the natural wholesomeness of the food.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee blɛoo ni efite oya. Tsakemɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ ni oha shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ afee muji Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii lɛ mli adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow if I do not apply fertilizer to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ?

english: Maize is a heavy-feeding crop that requires large amounts of nitrogen to stay green and build grain. When the soil lacks nutrients, the leaves turn yellow because the plant cannot feed itself properly.
ga: Abɛi ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ nitrogen babaoo koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmaa. Kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ eye niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Are there good food crops I can plant in Ghana that do not need expensive fertilizer to yield well?
ga: Niyenii tsei kpakpai yɛ. Nɛgbɛ manyɛ madu tsei ni he ehiaaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, crops like cassava, sweet potatoes, cowpeas, and groundnuts grow very well in low-nutrient soil. Legumes like cowpeas even pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, feeding themselves naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas hu gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛyeɔ nii.

english: Which crops should I plant if I have a very low budget for farm inputs this season?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ madu kɛji akɛ miyɛ shika fioo kwraa kɛha nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hardy tubers like cassava and leguminous crops like cowpea or Bambara groundnut are best for low budgets because they thrive in marginal soils without requiring heavy chemical fertilizers.
ga: Tubers ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei tamɔ cowpea loo Bambara ŋmei. Ehi kɛha shweremɔ yɛ jara ni waaa nɔ. Ejaakɛ edaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo awo mli.

english: How can I grow healthy, wholesome food without buying commercial fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni miheee jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can feed your soil naturally by adding decomposed animal manure, farm compost, or by practicing crop rotation with beans and groundnuts, which naturally restore nutrients into the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Kompost ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can planting beans alongside my main crop reduce my need for fertilizer?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ni he hiaa lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, leguminous plants like beans have nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, providing free nutrients to surrounding crops like maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa niyenii kpakpai ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: How do I know if my soil already has enough natural nutrients to grow food without fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha makwɛ niyenii ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii?

english: Soil that is rich usually looks dark, feels crumbly, retains moisture easily, and shows abundant wild plant growth and earthworm activity before you clear it for planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, enuɔ he akɛ ekpɔtɔ, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli oya. ni otsɔɔ koo mli tsei ni edaa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii babaoo dani ojie mli kɛha dumɔ.

english: I see random food crops scattered and growing by themselves in my farm; should I spend time fertilizing them?
ga: Mina niyenii tsei ni baa trukaa ni egbɛ eshwã ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmiida yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ani esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛwo amɛmli?

english: It is usually better not to spend your money or effort on scattered volunteer crops, as they are not properly spaced and will yield poorly compared to your main organized field crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofite shika loo mɔdɛŋbɔɔ yɛ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe eha ni egbɛ eshwã lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛbaawo yibii kpakpai kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni oto he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do wild plants in the bush stay green without anyone giving them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo amɛmli lɛ?

english: Wild plants have deep root systems that reach hidden water and nutrients deep underground, and they benefit from constant natural compost made by decaying fallen leaves.
ga: Koo mli tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛnáa nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Ni amɛnáa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbee shi lɛ amli lɛ he sɛɛ.

english: Does using heavy fertilizer affect how long my harvested crops will stay fresh in storage?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaná be abɔ ni mikpamɔ lɛ baahi shi ehee yɛ nitoohe lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, over-fertilizing causes crops like yams and vegetables to absorb excess water, making their tissues soft and causing them to rot much faster after harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ aduawai lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa fãji lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya kwraa yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Sir, is it safe for me to cut off some leaves from my plantain trees to feed my farm animals?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafo plantain baai koni mikɛha kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii?

english: Yes, plantain leaves are safe and rich in nutrients for livestock, but you must be careful not to remove too many green leaves. Leaves act as the plant's food factory, so leaving at least six to eight healthy green leaves ensures the plantain tree continues to grow strong and produce big fruit bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantain baai lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni niyenii babaoo yɛ mli kɛha kooloi. Shi esa akɛ okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ koni okajie baai eŋɔli lɛ babaoo. Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ niyenii feemɔ nitsumɔhe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ ashi baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 6-8 lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: What health benefits do green plantain leaves give to goats and sheep when they eat them?
ga: Mɛɛ hewalɛnamɔ he sɛɛ plantain baai eŋɔli lɛ kɛhaa tooi kɛ tooi kɛji aye amɛ?

english: Green plantain leaves are rich in vitamins, water, and key minerals that keep livestock hydrated, improve digestion, and boost their immunity, especially during the dry season when fresh pasture grass is hard to find.
ga: Vitamins, nu kɛ minerals ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi lɛ náa nu babaoo yɛ plantain baa ni ji green lɛ mli. ehaa niyenii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ helai anaa lɛ yaa hiɛ Titri lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni jwɛi heei ni anaa lɛ wa lɛ.

english: If I prune healthy green leaves off my crops, will it affect how much food the plant produces?
ga: Kɛji mifo baai eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ Ani ebaana niyenii ni tsei lɛ woɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, cutting away too many healthy green leaves reduces the crop's ability to make food from sunlight, which can shrink your harvest. You should mainly cut off dry, yellowed, or diseased leaves to keep the plant healthy without lowering your crop yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni aaafo lɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaafee niyenii kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha nibii ni ofeɔ lɛ aba shi. Esa akɛ ofolɔ baai ni egbi, ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ titri koni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ akafee nɔ ni baa shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my plantain plants turning yellow and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Bottom leaves on plantain trees turn yellow naturally as they age, but it can also mean the crop lacks water or key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Removing old, yellow leaves helps the plant focus its energy on fresh, healthy growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ashishi baai lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Shi ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Baai momo ni miifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl up in the hot afternoon heat to trap moisture and protect themselves from drying out. If the leaves bounce back and stand tall by evening, the plant is healthy, but if they stay limp, your crop needs water urgently.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ gbɛkɛ lɛ Tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔlɔ nyiɛ lolo lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia nu oya.

english: Sir, what causes dark brown or black spots on my plantain leaves, and does it hurt the plant?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ ni yɔɔ mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa? Ni ani efiteɔ tso lɛ?

english: Dark spots on plantain leaves are usually caused by fungal leaf diseases like Black Sigatoka. This disease damages the leaves so they cannot feed the plant properly, leading to small plantain fruits that ripen prematurely before they fully grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Hela nɛɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ aahu akɛ enyɛɛɛ eha tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ oya dani amɛshɛɔ shweremɔ he.

english: Why do small shoots keep growing out from the root of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛjɛ mi plantain tso titri lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers, and they are the natural way a plantain crop multiplies. If you let too many grow at once, they will fight the main plant for water and nutrients, so it is best to leave only one or two strong suckers per stand.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. ni eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ plantains lɛ eshwaa Kɛji oha ekwɛ̃ babaoo shikome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni damɔ shi.

english: How can I protect my young crops from free-roaming livestock that come to eat the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni baa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ahe?

english: Roaming animals like goats and sheep are attracted to tender leaves. You can protect your field by building simple wooden fences, planting living barriers like spiky hedges around your farm border, or placing wire mesh guards around young crop stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni nyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ tooi kɛ tooi lɛ sumɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔji lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ tso gbogbo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni oootswa lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ wala gbɛtsii nii ko, tamɔ dade ni akɛ ŋmeii ebɔle he. oŋmɔ lɛ naa Aloo okɛ waya tsɔne abɔle tsei bibii ahe.

english: Sir, what should I do with all the plantain leaves that fall or get trimmed off the trees?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni ofeɔ kɛ plantain baai ni shwieɔ shi loo afoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can lay trimmed plantain leaves on the ground around the base of your crops as mulch. The leaves act as a cover that keeps the soil moist, prevents weed growth, and gradually decays into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ plantain baai ni afolɔ mli lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii.

english: Can I grow other crops like cocoyam or vegetables directly under my plantain trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ kookoo loo aduawai yɛ mi plantain lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, young plantain trees offer good light shade that helps crops like cocoyam, leafy vegetables, or cocoa seedlings thrive. Just make sure the companion plants are spaced properly so their roots do not choke each other.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui bibii haa hulutsoo kpakpa ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo, aduawai ni yɔɔ baai loo kookoo dumɔwui ni amɛdaraa. Kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ akɛ tsei ni fata he lɛ kɛ amɛhe ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ akatsi amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land when I am establishing a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ́ ama kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Why should I leave measured space between my crops instead of planting them close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he ko? Mohu ɔ, i du mɛ ngɛ he ko nɛ a kɛ ye zugba ɔ nɛ sa saminya.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak plants and small yields. Proper spacing gives roots room to spread and allows air to flow, which keeps plants healthy.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhe wa

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea can restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha shishijee su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge bushy leaves above the ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen or if the cassava is planted in deep shade, the plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu ŋmei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai wuji moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ starch baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my land yield less food every year if I plant maize on the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over. Rotating your crops or planting beans and peanuts helps put natural nutrients back into the dirt.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if it is safe to start planting my seeds after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best not to plant right after the very first rain because the soil underneath may still be dry. Wait until you get two or three steady rains so the ground holds enough deep moisture to keep seeds alive.
ga: Kaadu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without forming any fruit when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants get stressed and pollen dries up, preventing the flowers from forming fruit. Keeping the soil mulched with dry grass helps keep the roots cool.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii Mulching kɛ jwɛi ni egbi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the young leaves inside the center funnel of my maize plants, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. They hide inside the central leaves to stay safe from the sun, so you need to spray safe bio-pesticides or neem water directly into the center of the plant early in the morning or late evening.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la he. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem nu afɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off extra branches and chupons from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛ supong kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Removing extra unwanted branches (pruning) allows sunlight and fresh air to pass through the tree. This dries out wet leaves, preventing fungal diseases like Black Pod, and forces the tree to put energy into growing pods instead of leaves.
ga: Niji ni ataooo lɛ ni ajieɔ (Pruning) lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji anaa ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni miida lɛ amli yɛ baai najiaŋ.

english: Why is it better for me to buy certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je ní kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to konɛ o du ngɛ be nɛ maa ba ɔ mi.

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over time and often carry diseases from the old farm. Certified seeds are specially produced to resist local pests, survive tough weather, and yield far more food.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he waaa yɛ be ni sa mli ni bei pii lɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ baa. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Ohi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli ni owo niyenii babaoo.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong, or when waterlogged soil prevents the roots from breathing.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava cuttings too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in tall thin stems with very small tubers instead of big, heavy roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shishifãi wuji ni tsii yɔɔ mli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ baa.

english: What is causing tiny ragged holes in my corn leaves with small worms hiding inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ baai lɛ amli ni ŋmei bibioo ko ni akɛtee teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that eats young corn leaves and hides inside the leaf funnel, damaging the plant before it can produce ears.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillar, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni ekɛ ehe woɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Kpatamɔ tso lɛ hiɛ dani enyɛ ewo toi.

english: Why should I clear old crop leaves back into the soil instead of burning them before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tso baai momoi lɛ kɛku sɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ dani madu?

english: Burning destroys soil food and kills good insects, whereas letting old leaves rot into the soil adds natural manure, helps ground stay moist, and improves soil structure for your next crop.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ kooloi kpakpai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni baai momoi lɛ fite kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii afata he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii aya hiɛ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay near the top of the soil, making the plant top-heavy and easily uprooted by wind unless supported by wooden props or planted deep enough.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tsiimɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ oya. Ja tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ loo adu amɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to yield heavily only in their first planting; saving seeds from that harvest will produce weak plants with small and unequal yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abaajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛwo yibii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into tomatoes when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee tomato kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and damages the pollen inside the blossoms, causing the flower to drop off so the plant can save energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite.

english: Why is it necessary to cut away extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning allows sunlight and air to move freely through the cocoa farm, which reduces wetness that causes black pod disease and helps the tree put energy into developing large pods.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even after I have added fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida fiofio eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that drink up the applied fertilizer and water before your crops get a chance to use them, starving your plants of nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni baanu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛ nu dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii. ni haa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and trap it inside the soil through their roots, acting as natural fertilizer for crops planted in that field afterward.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as essential food for the crop, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and strength.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does covering the ground around my crop roots with dry grass help them survive hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛhaa mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, giving your crops water for a longer time.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ha onibii amli nu ahi ohe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land with my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily scorch under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and provide wide leaves that shade the young cocoa plants until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tso bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat the center leaves of my maize, and why is the crop stopping its growth?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ tsei kpaa kwɛ̃mɔ?

english: These pests are likely fall armyworms, which hide inside the growing center of the plant and destroy new leaves before they open, leaving the plant unable to process sunlight and grow cobs properly.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji cutworms. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ baai heei dani amɛgbeleɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put four or five maize seeds into one single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ ŋmãa bu kome pɛ mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in the same hole, the plants fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, tall stalks with very small or empty cobs instead of healthy, productive plants.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Tsei wuɔ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ ngɛ he wami nɛ e woɔ yiblii.

english: Yam plants are vines that need sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tubers underground. Lifting the leaves off the hot ground with sticks prevents disease and helps the roots grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni he hiaa hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ owó baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa kɛ niji lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akamɔ amɛ, ni ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara babaoo.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or receives irregular water. The plant gets stressed and sheds its flowers to save energy to survive rather than producing fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo enine shɛ nu ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee nɔ. Tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my garden eggs die when heavy rains leave stagnant water on my farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ gboiɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like people do. Standing water drowns the roots by blocking oxygen, which causes the root system to rot and the whole plant to die.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gboɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crop plants grow weak and small even when I plant on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mitso titri lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni efee bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be naa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal the fertilizer, soil water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds early allows your main crop to get all the resources it needs.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ye obua onibii titri lɛ ni ená nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully grown underground and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the base of the plant begins to crack open from the expanding tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ eshwɛ ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni eyitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain seedlings next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantain dumɔwui yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily by strong direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and holding moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: What will happen to my crop if I plant my maize seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the stalks to grow tall and thin, resulting in small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni egbɔjɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ feɔ bibioo loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall leaves on top instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji yɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up quickly even after a small rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ fioo po lɛ?

english: Yam roots need soft, deep soil to capture and keep water. If the soil is too hard or compact, the rain washes off the surface instead of reaching the roots, causing the vine to dry under the afternoon sun.
ga: Sweet potato shishifãi hia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛhiɛ nu mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ, Nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ha wain tsei lɛ agbi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ shishi.

english: How does planting groundnut on my farm help prepare the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, they leave enriched soil that helps heavy-feeding crops like maize grow better.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa Eshiɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni yeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni tsii ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow and curling up early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow and curling leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or the plant is being attacked by pests like armyworms at the roots. Adding fertilizer or checking under the leaves for small caterpillars can help identify the fix.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ etutua tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo nibii bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ana tsabaa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of regular water, or strong winds stress the tomato plant. When stressed, the plant drops its blossoms to save energy rather than using resources to form fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa shii abɔ Loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper fruits develop dark, rotten spots at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni amɛgboɔ yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering or dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ daa loo hɔmɔ be ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds on my farm grow much faster than my main crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with aggressive root systems that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than domestic crops, allowing them to shoot up quickly if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo mli ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya kɛji ajieee amɛ oya.

english: Why do small insects destroy my harvested maize when I keep it in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpa lɛ beni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils thrive when maize is stored before it is completely dry. Any remaining moisture inside the grain attracts pests and allows mold to multiply rapidly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa to dani egbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i fɛɛ ni eshwɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ baagbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: How far apart should I space my maize seeds when planting my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛ́ mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ miidu?

english: Spacing maize about 75 centimeters between rows and 25 to 30 centimeters between plants ensures each stalk gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji aaafee sɛntimitai 75 kɛ sɛntimitai 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ tsei ateŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that your soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient crops need to grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ niyenii titri ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: What causes my tomato plant flowers to drop off before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ tomato?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off because of high heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What are these small caterpillars eating ragged holes through the leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ yeɔ kɛtsɔɔ bu mli? Kɛtsɔ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common crop pest in Ghana. They hide in the center leaves of the plant and can be managed using approved spray treatments early in the morning or late evening.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ, ni abaanyɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu he nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Curling leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to keep your farm healthy.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know it is the right time to start planting after the dry season ends?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ odu nii yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the major rains become consistent—usually after two or three heavy rainfalls that thoroughly soak the soil—so your seeds do not dry up and die after sprouting.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi wuji ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baa—bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni odumɔwui lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Can I still grow vegetables like pepper during the dry season without expensive machinery?
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ani wɔbaanyɛ wɔdu aduawai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lolo ni wɔkɛ tsɔnei ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, you can grow peppers during the dry season near a water source by using manual watering and placing dried grass mulch around the plants to prevent soil moisture from drying out.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli yɛ nu jɛɛhe ko he kɛtsɔ nu ni okɛwoɔ ohe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. tsei koni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akagbi

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are ready to be dug up and harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ atsa ni akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves begin turning yellow and falling off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why should I cut down the plantain stem after I cut off the mature fruit bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo plantain tsei lɛ ahe beni mifo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A plantain stem produces fruit only once in its lifetime. Cutting it down allows the underground root system to send all its food and energy to the young sucker shoots growing next to it for the next harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui woɔ yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kudɔɔ eniyenii kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ anɔ. kɛha nikpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to grow leaves and stay green. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer feeds the plant so it can produce healthy green leaves again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ awo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and its roots rot in the ground, that nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow lots of leaves but very little fruit after I put plenty of fresh chicken manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baa babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo beni mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee babaoo efata he lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fresh animal manure contains very high nitrogen, which encourages the plant to build big stems and leafy foliage. To get plenty of peppers, the plant also needs phosphorus and potassium, which trigger flowering and fruit growth.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei amli waa. Enɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ baai. Bɔni afee ni oná chili babaoo lɛ, Tsei hu he miihia fɔsfɔs kɛ potasiɔm. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them under full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and fragile root systems that dry out fast in intense heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains beside them shields the cocoa from direct sun and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my yam plants produce bigger tubers when I stake the vines with tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji kɛji mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko wo wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to make food that gets stored in the tuber under the ground. Staking lifts the vine off the muddy ground and spreads out leaves so they can catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ ni egbɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ eshwaa koni enyɛ ená hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants yield very thin tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ naa ŋmeii ni mli tse waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava stakes are planted too close, the underground roots fight for limited space, water, and soil nutrients, causing the tubers to remain small and thin.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná he ko ni faaa, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ bibioo ni eyɛ mlɛo.

english: Why does cutting off the top tips of my pepper plant make it yield more fruit later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ afo pepper tso lɛ naa lɛ, ehaa ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pinching the top growing tip stops the plant from growing straight up and forces it to branch out sideways. More side branches mean more flower spots, which leads to a bigger harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ atsi tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ naa lɛ, ehaaa eda tɛ̃ɛ, ni enyɛɔ niji anɔ koni amɛje kpo kɛya sɛɛgbɛ. Niji babaoo tsɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Enɛ kɛ kpamɔ babaoo baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures stress the tomato plant and cause pollen to dry out. When pollination fails, the plant naturally drops its flowers to save energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: How do weeds reduce my crop yields even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal essential plant nutrients, light, and root space from the soil, depriving your crops of what they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni he hia, la kɛ shishifãi gbɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ejieɔ nɔ ni he hiaa otso lɛ koni enyɛ eda waa lɛ kɛjɛɔ odɛŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the middle of the afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, water evaporates from leaf pores faster than the roots can drink it up. Wilting is the plant's natural defense to curl up and lose less water until the day cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Wilting ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni ekɛbaabɔle ehe ni nu fioo pɛ efo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ.

english: Officer, how many acres make up one hectare when I am measuring my farmland?
ga: Officer Acres enyiɛ kɛ hectare kome yeɔ egbɔ kɛji misusu miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: One hectare is equal to about 2.5 acres. If you have a plot of land that is two and a half acres, that is roughly one hectare.
ga: Hectare kome kɛ aaafee acre 2.5 yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛji oyɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre enyɔ kɛ fã lɛ, no lɛ aaafee hectare kome.

english: How far apart should I plant coconut seedlings on my land so they do not crowd each other when they grow big?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Coconut trees need broad spacing—usually about 7.5 to 9 meters (25 to 30 feet) apart. This ensures their root systems and large fronds have enough space to get sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing.
ga: Esa akɛ atse ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 7.5 kɛyashi 9 (naji 25 kɛyashi 30) koni shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai wuji lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Why are my young coconut trees taking so many years before they start producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Traditional tall coconut varieties take about 5 to 7 years to start fruiting, whereas dwarf or hybrid varieties can yield in 3 to 4 years. Coconuts also need full sunlight, regular water, and good nutrients like potassium to flower and bear fruit.
ga: Kusum mli ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Yɛ be mli ni dwarf coconut henɔi loo hybrids baanyɛ awo yibii yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli lɛ, coconut hu he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa, nu ni anáa daa kɛ niyenii kpakpai tamɔ potassium koni enyɛ ewo yibii.

english: Why are the lower branches of my coconut trees turning yellow and dropping early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves can be a sign of drought stress, lack of nutrients like nitrogen or potassium in the soil, or damage from pests. Ensuring proper soil fertility and moisture helps keep the foliage green and productive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee hɔmɔ he haomɔ he okadi. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo nɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ ni edɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is vital for foliage growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore green leaves and improves grain size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen ni fa babaoo loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ ni eha dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legume crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear all the big trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or large forest trees to shelter them and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei wuji koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed by severe heat, erratic watering, or pest damage. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulched helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Should I keep watering my watermelon crop heavily when the fruits are already large and almost ready to harvest?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maya nɔ mawo mi-watermelon tsei lɛ anɔ nu babaoo kɛji watermelon lɛ dara ni kpamɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ?

english: No, you should reduce watering as watermelons reach maturity. Excess water near harvest time lowers the sugar content, making the melons less sweet, and can cause the fruits to split open.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ otsi nu ni okɛhaa lɛ nɔ be mli ni watermelon lɛ daa lɛ. Nu babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni bɛŋkɛɔ kpamɔ be lɛ baaha sugar ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aba shi. Ha melon lɛ afee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ fioo ni ebaanyɛ eha aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What causes the leaves of my tomato plants to curl up and stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is often caused by viruses spread by insects like whiteflies, or by environmental stress such as hot, dry weather. Managing whiteflies early and keeping the soil damp helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa loo shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Whitefly nɔkwɛmɔ mra Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enaa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also prevents diseases and allows the plant to direct more energy into growing large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai anaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds your maize, keeping the soil rich and healthy for future seasons.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa o-corn lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting up with yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This yellowing and leaf curling is caused by a plant disease spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. It prevents the cassava roots from growing big, so using disease-resistant planting stems is the best defense.
ga: Tse helai ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ cassava shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving small brown droppings in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii feɔ ŋmeii ahe baai ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmeii? yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by a pest called the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Catching them early and applying recommended natural sprays like neem extract into the center funnel of the maize helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmei. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite nii waa. Ni kɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ, tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ tsu nii yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my pepper fruits turning black and rotten before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium and irregular water supply in the soil while the fruit is growing. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the roots absorb calcium and stops the rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa kɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium ni amɛkpaa fitemɔ.

english: Why are my young maize plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green. Applying fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure gives them the food they need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before any fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet. Keeping the soil covered with dried leaves or straw helps stabilize the temperature and moisture.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ahi shi daa.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over during rainstorms before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep in the ground, making the heavy bunch of fruit top-heavy. Supporting the stem with a strong bamboo fork prop before the fruit grows heavy keeps the tree standing.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai ni tsii yɛ kui amli lɛ feɔ shwiili babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei fɔk tsu nii ni akɛfi tso lɛ shishi dani aduawai lɛ afee nɔ ni tsii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi gbee.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to grow green leaves. This often happens after heavy rain washes nutrients away or when the soil has been used for many seasons without adding manure or fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ loo beni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsu nii bei babaoo ni ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my land yield fewer crops every year even when I plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ nii yɛ be kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Soil gets exhausted when the same crop is planted year after year because it continuously removes the same nutrients. Rotating crops or leaving the land to rest helps the soil recover its natural fertility.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛjieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahaa ejɔɔ ehe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni enáa bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The Harmattan brings dry winds and intense sun that pull moisture out of leaves faster than small, shallow roots can soak up water from dry ground. Planting shade crops like plantains near young cocoa helps protect them from this dry wind and heat.
ga: Harmattan kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ kɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain floods the ground for long periods, water blocks air from reaching the roots, causing rot-causing microbes to grow and ruin the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa nibii bibii ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather gets too hot, when plants don't get enough water, or if insects damage the blossoms before they can naturally form into tomato fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛbatsɔ adebɔɔ mli tomatoi.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller on the older trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ tsei ni edara lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: A plantain tree shares its food and water with all the young shoots growing around its base. If you do not remove extra suckers, they steal nutrients from the main stem, resulting in smaller bunches.
ga: Plantains kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jaa niyenii kɛ nu kɛji ojieee ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ. Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Efeɔ ŋmeii bibii

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy, which then goes down into the ground to build large tubers. Staking lifts leaves off the shady ground so they can catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, egbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni efeɔ yitso agbo. Stake elevator lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ he babaoo.

english: How do weeds harm my crops when they are growing in the same soil?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. They grow faster than crops and steal the essential resources your crops need to stay strong and give a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why are there small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and brown dust inside the leaf whorls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ani sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of young maize plants during the day, eating fresh leaves and leaving behind powdery droppings.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Ye baai heei lɛ ni oshi jwɛi lɛ yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable garden early in the morning or during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so roots can soak up water before heat sets in. Watering during the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate into the air before roots can drink it.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ dani latsaa lɛ aba.Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane mli ni edɔ waa lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu lɛ etswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight when they are small. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh heat, the sun burns their delicate leaves and makes the plant struggle to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ kɛ́ amɛji bibii. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ Bɔni afee ni akatsi dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa lɛ Hulu la shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni ehi shi.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and take over my field when my crop plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya ni amɛmiihe mihegbɛ lɛ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Small crops have few leaves, leaving bare soil completely exposed to direct sunlight. Weeds thrive on this exposed light and will quickly outgrow and choke your young crops if the soil is left uncovered.
ga: Nibii bibii ni aduɔ lɛ bɛ baai fioo pɛ. Okɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ awo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ la ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛbaakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaafite oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli.

english: Why does the soil on my farm get so hard and cracked when I clear all the vegetation before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa ni egbɛ eshwa beni mijieɔ tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ dani miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Bare soil has no cover to shield it from the intense midday sun. Without living plants or leafy cover, the heat bakes the ground, evaporates all moisture, and makes it difficult for crop roots to grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ, he ko ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane teŋ lɛ bɛ. Kɛji tso ni hiɛ ka loo baa ni haa nɔ ko bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ baashã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Fɛ̃i lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃

english: Why is it important for me to leave space between my maize plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough light and food so it does not struggle to produce big, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ana toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Can I plant pepper plants directly under tall crops like maize, or will they suffer?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu pepper tsei yɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo a maa na nɔ́?

english: Tall crops like maize create heavy shade that prevents smaller pepper plants from receiving enough sunlight to flower and fruit. Pepper plants need plenty of light, so planting them right beneath tall stalks will cause them to struggle.
ga: Tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ hulutsoo be ni tsii koni ekɛtsi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii. La babaoo he miihia pepper tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high in the air to catch maximum sunlight for tuber growth. If left on the ground, the leaves get shaded, wet, and exposed to soil diseases, which reduces your total harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ni fa babaoo aba kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Kɛji ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ. Enɛ baaha nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crop plants help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass, or mulching, acts like a protective blanket over the soil. It keeps the ground cool and moist, prevents the hot sun from scorching the roots, and stops weed seeds from getting sunlight to grow.
ga: Hay loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Etsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashã shishifãi lɛ. ni etsĩ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la koni amɛkwɛ̃

english: Why do my plantain trees fall down when they start carrying heavy bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ ebɔi aduawai babaoo womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are soft and hold a lot of water, so a heavy fruit bunch shifts the plant's weight and pulls it down. Using wooden props or bamboo stakes to support the main stem prevents the tree from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ahe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhiɛ nu babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai akuu ko ni tsii baajie tso lɛ muji lɛ ni egbala lɛ kɛba shi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ he loo ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii kɛfi tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Why do my cassava plants fall over whenever there is heavy rain or strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too shallowly or without proper soil mounds, its root structure cannot hold the heavy top part upright against strong wind and wet soil, causing the plant to lodge or break.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni sa bɛ nɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ eyiteŋ ni tsii lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ he. Ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ akumɔ loo ekumɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my tomato plants rotting after rain splashes dirt onto them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil contains natural fungi and bacteria that cause plant diseases. When rain bounces off bare ground onto low leaves, it exposes the plant to these germs, so covering the soil with mulch keeps the crop safe.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni kɛ tsei ahelai baa lɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ naa nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to harsh sunlight and heat. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa seedlings from drying out while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the central part of the stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii lɛ? Minɔ lɛ yɛ bu ni akɛtee tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm. The young worms crawl into the central leaves (the whorl) where it is dark and moist to eat the growing tips of the plant, which can stunt or ruin the crop if not managed quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai bibii shwieɔ baai lɛ ateŋ (ring) ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli koni amɛye tso lɛ naagbeehei lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee mlɛo loo efite kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii oya.

english: Why does my cassava produce very tall stems with bushy leaves but only thin, weak roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ waa kɛ baai akutsei lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, or when plants are crowded, the cassava plant sends most of its food and energy upward to grow leaves instead of storing energy downward in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. aloo kɛ́ tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ yɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ eniyenii kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekwɛ baai.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant sacrifices its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli baa lɛ he. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei kɛ fɔfɔi shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.
