english: Why should I cover fertilizer with soil after placing it near my crops instead of leaving it open on top of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ sũ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe beni mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi lɛ ni egbele yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Leaving fertilizer exposed on top of the soil allows heat and sunlight to evaporate key nutrients into the air, or heavy rains to wash them away before the roots can absorb them.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii titrii lɛ amli kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ ahe dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunches get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni eyɛ aduawai akui wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems near the surface rather than deep taproots. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the high center of gravity pulls the plant down, so propping the trunk with bamboo or wooden poles supports the heavy yield.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsiimɔ Hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbalaa tso lɛ kɛyaa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni anáa yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus disrupts the plant's ability to transport food, causing leaves to curl, yellow, and produce small or poor-quality fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Virus tsiɔ tso nyɛmɔ ni ekɛ niyenii yaa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii loo nɔ ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often a false start to the rainy season and can be followed by a week or two of dry weather. If you plant too early, seeds will germinate and then scorch and die in the dry soil before the main rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji amale shishijee kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ. ni ekolɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ baanyiɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛshãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow so slow and look weak when weeds are growing close to their stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ beni jwɛi lɛ miida ni bɛŋkɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Because weeds are aggressive growers, they steal the plant food before your crop roots can reach it.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ ji jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ waa. Amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb up tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse sweet potato wain tso ko koni enyɛ ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need plenty of direct sunlight on their leaves to make the energy required to grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the shady, damp ground where they might rot or suffer from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela aba.

english: Which direction should I align my crop rows to stop strong winds from blowing down my plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ mato miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akatswa tsei lɛ shi?

english: Planting crop rows across (perpendicular to) the main wind direction breaks the force of the wind as it moves through the field. This prevents tall crops like maize and cassava from bending or snapping during heavy rainstorms.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ (ni damɔ) kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbɛ titri lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hewalɛ aba shi beni etsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ anaa. Bent loo efo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli.

english: Can I plant permanent economic trees along my farm boundary to mark my land ownership?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu shika helɛtemɔ tsei ni baahi shi daa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he koni mikɛkadi shikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting long-lasting crops or boundary trees like cashew, oil palm, or teak along borders clearly marks your land boundaries. However, keep them slightly inside your line and trim them so their shade does not prevent your neighbor's crops from growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo loo husu tsei, tamɔ cashew ŋmeii, mu tsei loo teak tsei ni ooodu yɛ ohusu lɛ he lɛ tsɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ husui lɛ faŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, okɛ amɛ awo ogbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli fioo ni ofo mli koni hulutsoo akatsi okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn easily and lose water too quickly. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains or Gliricidia trees to protect them while their roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni nu lɛ hu sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ. Amɛbiɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo glicidia tsei amli. koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ maa lɛ

english: Why are my cassava plants producing thick green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing heavy leaves and stems above ground instead of sending food down to expand the tubers below ground. Balanced nutrients with adequate potassium are needed for big tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Niyenii ni ja kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia kɛha bulbs wuji.

english: Why do I need to use wooden stakes to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso atsu nii koni mikɛwo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight for food production while keeping the leaves off damp soil, which prevents fungal diseases from spreading and rotting the plant.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akafee nɔ ni sũ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akagbɛ eshwa ni ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I harvest more corn from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too close causes crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks with tiny cobs or no corn at all. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ejieɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. loo ŋmãa ko kwraa He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmãa wuji ni mli wa baa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry leaves instead of burning them away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Nibii ni aduɔ ni baai egbi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ashãa amɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material (mulching) acts as a blanket that traps moisture in the dirt, cools root temperatures during hot dry spells, and slowly breaks down into free fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Nibii ni akɛ tsei ni egbi woɔ mli (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli latsaa lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be baa lɛ, ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ onibii amli ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or poor pollination. Consistent watering and preserving beneficial insects that pollinate flowers help the blossoms turn into healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo pollination ni ehiii. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahiɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know it is safe to sow my maize seeds at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait until the soil is thoroughly wet to a depth of about 15 centimeters (hand length) after a major rain. Planting after just one light drizzle often causes seeds to germinate and then dry up when the heat returns.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ aaafee sɛntimitai 15 (nine sɛɛ) yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ sɛɛ Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ la ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I mound soil around the base of my growing maize and cassava stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabua sũ naa yɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ shishi lɛ he?

english: Mounding soil around the base (earthing up) covers support roots, giving plants a firm anchor against strong winds and providing soft, extra soil for tubers or root systems to spread easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he (shikpɔŋ ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ) baaha shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ebaaha tsei lɛ anyɛ agbala amɛhe jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo kroko aha bɔni afee ni bulb loo shishifã lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: What is the main difference between traditional cocoa and the Agric Amazonia variety?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ blema kookoo kɛ Agric Amazonia henɔi lɛ ateŋ?

english: Traditional cocoa trees take longer to mature and bear fruit, but they can live for many decades. Agric Amazonia is an improved hybrid variety that grows much faster, bears pods earlier, and yields larger harvests under good farm care.
ga: Kusum tsei ni ji cacao lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii. Agric Amazonia ji tso ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni daa oya kwraa. Pods lɛ jeɔ kpo oya. ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi

english: Why do older cocoa farmers refer to some trees as 'Dark Agric' or traditional cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi ni edara lɛ tsɛɔ tsei komɛi akɛ ‘Dark Agric’ loo kusum kookoo lɛ?

english: Dark Agric' refers to the older, traditional Amelonado cocoa strains distributed by agricultural officers in past decades. They are known for their dark green pods before ripening and their classic, rich chocolate flavor.
ga: Dark Agric’ tsɔɔ Amelonado kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ ja yɛ afii nyɔŋma ni eho lɛ mli lɛ. Ale lɛ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ, e-pods ni eshɛko momo kɛ klassik, tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I visually tell if a tree on my farm is Agric Amazonia or a traditional cocoa tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji Agric Amazonia loo blema cacao?

english: Agric Amazonia trees generally have broader leaves, a bushiest canopy, and start producing pods lower on the main stem, whereas traditional cocoa trees grow taller, slimmer, and branch out higher before fruiting.
ga: Agric Amazonia tsei lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Canopy ni bɛ deka fe fɛɛ lɛ ni ebɔi shishigbɛ pods lɛ feemɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, blema cacao tsei lɛ daraa, amɛfeɔ mlɛo, ni amɛniji shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the pods on my traditional cocoa trees smaller than the pods on Amazonia trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi kusum cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji bibii fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties naturally produce smaller, smooth-skinned pods with smaller seeds. Amazonia varieties were bred specifically to develop larger, ridged pods with bigger cocoa beans.
ga: Kusum kooloi henɔi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii, ni hiɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni dumɔwui bibii yɔɔ mli. Akwɛ Amazon henɔi lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛná ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii kɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How many years will it take for my new Agric Amazonia cocoa trees to start bearing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani mi Agric Amazonia cacao tso hee lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi?

english: Agric Amazonia cocoa trees typically start flowering and producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, compared to traditional varieties which usually take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Agric Amazonia cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu amɛ lɛ, kɛ akɛto blema tsei srɔtoi ni bei pii lɛ amɛheɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ ahe.

english: Can I plant Agric Amazonia cocoa seedlings in the same farm area as my old traditional cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu Agric Amazonia kookoo dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mi shishijee kookoo tsei lɛ wo mli lɛ?

english: It is better to keep them in separate plots. Agric Amazonia grows faster and creates a denser canopy, which can overcrowd and block light from older or slower-growing traditional trees.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha amɛhi shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ. Agric Amazonia lɛ daa oya ni efeɔ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ni egbɔ loo ni daraa blɛoo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Does the Agric Amazonia cocoa variety need more shade or more sunlight to grow well?
ga: Ani Agric Amazonia kookoo lɛ he miihia hulutsoo babaoo loo hulu la babaoo koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: While young Amazonia trees need shade just like traditional cocoa, mature Agric Amazonia trees can tolerate more open sunlight and convert that light into higher pod yields if the soil is properly fertilized.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ Amazonia tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa hulutsoo tamɔ daa kookoo moŋ, shi Amazonia tsei ni eda lɛ baanyɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni mli tse babaoo nɔ. ni etsake nakai la lɛ ewo pod yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ mli kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ewo mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do I need to prune my Agric Amazonia cocoa trees differently than traditional cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafo Agric Amazonia cacao tsei lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe blema cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, because Agric Amazonia grows rapidly and branches heavily, it requires more regular pruning of side branches (chupons) to keep the center open for air and sunshine to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ Agric Amazonia lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ niji babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni afolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ (chupons) lɛ daa koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Is the Agric Amazonia cocoa variety better at resisting common cocoa diseases than traditional cocoa?
ga: Ani Agric Amazonia kookoo lɛ nyɛɔ eshiɔ kookoo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ fe blema kookoo lɛ?

english: Yes, Agric Amazonia was bred to be more vigorous and resistant to common field issues such as swollen shoot virus and black pod disease compared to older traditional varieties.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔse Agric Amazonia koni ehiɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛ naagbai ni afɔɔ namɔ tamɔ bud swollen virus kɛ black pod hela lɛ akpee naa. Kɛ akɛto kusum mli henɔi ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ahe

english: Will traditional cocoa trees remain productive for longer than Agric Amazonia trees?
ga: Ani blema cacao tsei lɛ baaya nɔ awo yibii be kakadaŋŋ fe Agric Amazonia tsei lɛ?

english: Traditional cocoa trees have a longer natural lifespan and can produce pods reliably for 30 to 40 years or more, whereas high-yielding varieties like Amazonia may exhaust themselves earlier and need replacing after 20 to 25 years.
ga: Kusum mli cacao tsei lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmeii afii 30 kɛyashi 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo tamɔ Amazonia lɛ baanyɛ afite oya, ni ehe baahia ni atsake amɛ yɛ afii 20 kɛyashi 25 sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle intense sunlight and dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts as a shield, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt and drop their flowers when the afternoon heat becomes too strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely hot, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Dropping flowers is a crop's natural survival mechanism to save moisture and energy during extreme heat stress.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ kɛha aduawai tsei. Koni eye ebua ni akwɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hewalɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be ni naa wa waa baa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce tiny cobs when I put four seeds in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ wo bu kome mli lɛ

english: Planted too closely together, crop roots compete aggressively for the same nutrients, water, and sunlight. Planting only one or two seeds per hole gives each maize stalk enough feeding space to grow thick and yield large cobs.
ga: ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kome lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni mli tse ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and skinny even though the leaves above ground look very green and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni eyɛ ŋmɔji waa moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing top leaves instead of food roots. Root crops need balanced nutrients and loose, uncompacted soil to swell into large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ niyenii lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ. Niyenii ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni ehiɛɛɛ shi lɛ he miihia tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the earth and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to settle in the soil. Alternating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the land naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my chemical fertilizer on the farm right before a big rain starts falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ anɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash away loose fertilizer from topsoil into gutters before plant roots have time to take it in. Applying fertilizer when the soil is already damp after moderate rain ensures the nutrients soak down to the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli kɛyaa nubui lɛ amli dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛwoɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ebote shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do people spread dry leaves and palm leaves over the soil after planting groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmei tsei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdu ŋmeii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. Covering the dirt keeps the hot sun from evaporating soil water, stops weed seeds from sprouting quickly, and decomposes into rich natural compost over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Muji ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots sprouting around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Extra side shoots, called suckers, steal water and food meant for the main mother plant. Cutting away surplus suckers allows the main plantain tree to direct all its energy into growing a bigger, heavier bunch.
ga: Side shoots ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa plantain wulu lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛwo tso ni da ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ mli.

english: Why do seeds I buy in sealed packets give me better crops than seeds I collect from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ paketii ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Packaged seeds are specially bred hybrid varieties selected for disease resistance and high yield, whereas saved seeds often lose their strength and carry hidden diseases from the previous season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awoɔ kotoku mli lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afɔ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni ahala koni helai akamɔ amɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛhiɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that plant roots are sitting in excess water. Improving drainage and adding well-rotted manure fixes this nutritional imbalance.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo nu babaoo yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni abaafee lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni asaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ejaaa nɛɛ.

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means the crop is lacking nitrogen food in the soil. Adding proper fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps the plant green up and grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa tamɔ urea loo NPK wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why is my maize producing a flower at the top before I see any cobs forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ ŋwɛi dani anaa ŋmei lɛ?

english: The flower at the top is called a tassel, and its job is to release pollen. The cobs grow lower down the stalk shortly after and catch this pollen to form grains.
ga: Atsɛɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ akɛ tassel. ni eyɛ nitsumɔ ni ji fɔfɔi amli muji ni ajieɔ lɛ Cob lɛ daa kɛyaa shishigbɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ no sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ ni eŋɔɔ muji nɛɛ, ni etsɔɔ lɛ dumɔwu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are easily scorched by direct, harsh sunshine. They need shade from larger trees or temporary shade crops like plantains to keep them cool while their roots grow deep.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the field without draining away, the roots drown and decay under the wet soil.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbee ŋmɔji amli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing big fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii wuji kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the seedlings fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. They spend all their energy growing tall to reach light instead of producing big fruits or cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baawuu kɛha hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛdara ni amɛshɛ la he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo aduawai loo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Will applying fertilizer to my crop during a heavy downpour help it work faster?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsu nii oya?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away into gutters before the plant's roots can soak it up. Fertilizer works best when applied in moist soil on a calm day without torrential rain.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ nubui lɛ amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ gbi ni nɔ efee kpoo ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without making any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or the soil gets too dry. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and water helps the plant hold its flowers to turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding in the funnel leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ a-cone baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are pests like Fall Armyworm that target the tender, sweet growth in the center of young maize. Checking your field early and spraying with recommended remedies prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my plants staying small even though the soil in my field is soft and rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni ewoɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds growing around your plants act like thieves, stealing water, sunlight, and food from the soil before your crop can reach it. Clearing weeds early gives your crop full access to food.
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Otsei lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii kwraa.

english: Why do my seed yams start sprouting green shoots inside the barn before I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ bɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shweremɔ dani midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up after resting for a few months. The warmth and air inside the barn signal to the yam that it is time to start growing a new plant.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ teɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛjɔɔ amɛhe nyɔji fioo komɛi. Dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛje tsei heei ashishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate roots that cannot withstand intense sun and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to cocoa trees creates a canopy that shields the young plants and keeps the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tso ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa, tamɔ plantain, yɛ kookoo tso ko masɛi lɛ, ehaa tso bibioo lɛ he feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong rains and winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy tops, especially when carrying large bunches of fruit. Without proper windbreaks, deep planting, or propping the stems with wooden poles, heavy rains soften the soil and strong winds can push them over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ aduawai lɛ ebɔi ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ hebuu ni sa bɛ lɛ, dumɔ ni mli kwɔ loo tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curling and yellow leaves on cassava are usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. The virus weakens the plant, preventing its leaves from making food efficiently and leading to a low yield of tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Virus haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ ebaai lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ koni ekahoo. ni ehaa tuber ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo

english: Why are my maize leaves turning light green and yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miitsɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the primary food plants need to grow green and leafy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores the plant's health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungal disease that spreads quickly in damp, shady, and cool conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let in sunlight and air helps prevent moisture buildup that allows the fungus to grow.
ga: Black pod rot ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji krokomɛi amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ daa lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn lɛ mli baai lɛ?

english: These pests are Fall Armyworms, which target the soft, growing centers of young maize plants. Farmers inspect their fields early in the morning or evening to catch the infestation early before the worms damage the growing point of the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ hei ni ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Okwaafoi kwɛɔ amɛŋmɔji amli leebi loo gbɛkɛ koni amɛna helai ni baa mra. Dani ŋmeii lɛ baafite hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants fall off without forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho ni amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper blossoms drop off when the crop experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Consistent watering and protecting the soil with mulch around the base of the plant help reduce leaf and flower loss.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ haa baa kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my harvested yam tubers growing out bent and twisted instead of straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ daa ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yams grow crooked when the soil is hard, rocky, or poorly cleared, making it difficult for the tuber to expand smoothly underground. Making tall, soft, and clear mounds or ridges allows the roots to grow straight and large.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo ajieee nɔ ko jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ, ni yɔɔ blɛoo, ni atsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛdaraa.

english: How do I know if my soil is moist enough to start planting maize after the first rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Soil is ready for planting when you can scoop up a handful, squeeze it into a ball, and it holds together without water dripping out or crumbling into dry dust. This ensures the seed gets enough moisture to sprout without rotting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ beni obaanyɛ okɛ nine awo mli lɛ. ŋmɔ mli ni efee bɔɔlu Ni ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ he ni nu shwieee shi loo egbɛɛɛ etsɔɔɔ sũ ni egbi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbooo.

english: Why does covering the ground with dry grass around my tomatoes help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-tomato lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly in the heat. It also prevents weeds from growing and taking nutrients away from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaatsi nu lɛ naa oya yɛ latsaa be mli. Ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ hu shwieɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant is missing nitrogen, which is the key nutrient needed to keep leaves green. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even though the leafy tops are huge and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Mɛɛ baa ŋmɔji dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from overly rich soil or fertilizer, it spends all its energy growing tall leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa tsɔ mli lɛ mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ato tuber lɛ mli yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: If I plant beans together with my maize in the same field, will it harm my maize?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmei fata ŋmei he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ani ebaaye ŋmei lɛ awui?

english: No, planting beans with maize actually helps. Beans gather nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps feed the maize naturally without taking away its food.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ. Beans buaa nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ nyɛɔ eyeɔ kooloi lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni eshi niyenii lɛ.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up tightly into rolls?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites, thrips, or aphids sucking sap from the young leaves, or by viral diseases carried into the field by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites, thrips, loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli kɛbaa lɛ amli

english: Why are my vegetable seedlings falling over and dying right after they sprout from the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This happens due to a fungal disease called damping-off, which attacks tender young stems at soil level when the soil stays too wet, shaded, or crowded.
ga: Enɛ baa mli yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening off, ni tutuaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ, eyɛ hulutsoo, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is my plantain crop falling over during minor winds even when the leaves look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli po

english: Plantain stems fall easily when tiny soil pests like nematodes or banana weevils eat away the roots underground, leaving the heavy plant without a firm grip in the soil.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii ye shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off before any tomatoes form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when dry weather causes water stress, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer in the soil.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ ekɛ nu he haomɔ baa. aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fa tsɔ

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting under the soil before it is time to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam rot underground happens when water stays trapped around the tuber due to poor soil drainage, allowing harmful soil fungi or worms called nematodes to enter and spoil the root.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato rot lɛ baa kɛji nu tsɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa sũ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ boteɔ mli ni amɛfiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why is my mango tree dropping most of its tiny young fruits right after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ shwieɔ eyibii bibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo kɛji ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Trees drop young fruit when they do not have enough water or nutrients to feed all of them, causing the tree to shed excess fruits to save the remaining ones.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ fɛɛ lɛ bɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ yibii ni fa fe nine koni eha yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ akafite.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees around my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ he lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and burn under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide big leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas to keep the young cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛshãa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why should I try new cocoa farming methods instead of continuing with the traditional ways my family used?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka gbɛ hee ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ kookoo lɛ makwɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaya nɔ amɛfee nɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni weku lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: New farming methods are developed to help cocoa trees grow stronger, resist new pests and changing weather, and produce far more beans on the same size of land than older methods allowed.
ga: Afee okwaayeli gbɛi heei ni baaye abua cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛdara waa. Eteɔ shi ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai heei kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ he ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni blema gbɛi lɛ ŋmɛɔ gbɛ.

english: How does cutting off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa tree help it produce more pods?
ga: Te niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mifolɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo baa lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree. This reduces fungal diseases and forces the tree to direct its energy into growing big pods rather than excess leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ aya ŋmɔji wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeehiɛ baai babaoo.

english: Cocoa flowers often fall off because of insect pests sucking their juices, lack of moisture in the soil, or inadequate nutrients. Properly feeding and protecting the trees helps flowers develop into healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ. aloo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ Niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa tso lɛ ni abuɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni he wa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers directly on the thick trunk instead of the small branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ni mli tse nɔ moŋ fe tsei niji bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow flowers on their thick trunks and main branches because cocoa pods are heavy. The strong trunk provides the solid support needed to hold heavy pods until they ripen.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ tsei niji wuji anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ cocoa tsei lɛ amli tsii. Tso lɛ tsei ni wa lɛ haa yelikɛbuamɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni he hiaa koni akɛmɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily burn under strong sun. They need temporary shade trees, like plantain or shade trees, to protect them and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Will I harvest more cocoa beans if I plant my trees very close together?
ga: Ani makpa kookoo yibii babaoo kɛji midu tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Planting trees too closely makes them fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to small yields. Proper spacing gives each tree enough room and nourishment to produce maximum pods.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa tree leaves very green, but the tree is producing almost no pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi eshwɛ fioo ni tso lɛ bɛ ŋmeii?

english: Very green leaves mean the tree has plenty of nitrogen for growth, but forming pods requires other nutrients like phosphorus and potassium. Without a balanced soil feed, the tree will grow leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Shi bɔni afee ni akumɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni aná niyenii krokomɛi, tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium. Kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cocoa trees drop during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry periods as a self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss. Covering the soil around the tree base with dry leaves or husks helps keep moisture in the ground longer.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmãa ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do cocoa pods on my farm turn black and rot before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, overly shaded, and wet farms. Keeping weeds short and pruning excess branches lets air flow through to dry the pods and stop the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fɔ̃ɔ ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Shade babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ha jwɛi lɛ afee kuku ni ofolɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ekpa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to leave fully ripe cocoa pods hanging on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaashi kookoo ŋmeii ni egbɔ kwraa lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree invites pests and diseases, and causes the seeds inside to start sprouting, which ruins the quality and value of the harvested cocoa beans.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ekɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai baa. ni eha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ baafite kookoo yibii ni akpa lɛ kpakpa kɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees produce many flowers but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny midges or hand pollination to transfer pollen from flower to flower. If pollination does not happen, the flowers simply dry up and drop off without developing into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia bibii. loo nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli koni akɛjie fɔfɔi lɛ kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ No lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛyaaa hiɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: How does hand pollination help me harvest more bags of cocoa from my farm?
ga: Te nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni mikɛkpaa kookoo kotokui babaoo kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Hand pollination ensures that a high percentage of healthy flowers receive enough pollen to form pods, whereas relying only on natural insects leaves many flowers unpollinated, which limits your harvest.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ateŋ oha mlijaa 100 lɛ naa fɔfɔi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee ŋmeii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ akɛ he fɔ̃ adebɔɔ mli kooloi anɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ fɔfɔi babaoo baafee nɔ ni shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa okpamɔ lɛ feɔ husu.

english: Why do cocoa flowers dry up and fall off the tree before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when they are not pollinated, or when the tree experiences stress from poor soil nutrients, pest attacks, or lack of water.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ. aloo kɛ́ tsei kɛ haomɔ kpeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii, kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ mli.

english: What triggers my cocoa trees to start producing flowers during the year?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi yɛ afi lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa trees usually flower heavily after the first rain following a dry spell, as the combination of warm weather and fresh moisture signals the tree to begin its flowering cycle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Enɛ jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni akɛfee ekome lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ leɔ akɛ eje efɔfɔi fɔmɔ shishi.

english: What happens to my cocoa pods when the dry season lasts longer than normal?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Extended dry weather causes cocoa trees to drop their leaves and smaller premature pods to conserve water, resulting in smaller harvests unless shade trees or mulching are used to retain soil moisture.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ amɛmli oya koni amɛbu nu he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fioo. Ja akɛ tsei tsu nii koni akɛha hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra branches from my growing cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches so sunlight and air can reach the trunk where pods grow, while directing the tree's energy into producing bigger pods instead of excess leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tsei ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How does shade management affect how many pods my cocoa trees produce?
ga: Te shade nɔkwɛmɔ saa pods enyiɛ ni mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Too much shade prevents trees from getting enough light to produce food and flowers, while too little shade burns young trees. Balanced shade protects the cocoa while encouraging maximum pod growth.
ga: Shade babaoo baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkaná la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo niyenii kɛ fɔfɔi. yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be fioo pɛ baaha tsei bibii ashã. Shade ni ja lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa pod lɛ daa babaoo.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal infection that spreads fast in humid, wet conditions, especially when trees are planted too close together or have too much shade.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛ hulutsoo tsɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm needs fertilizer to increase its yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: If your cocoa trees have yellowish leaves, grow slowly, or produce very few pods despite having flowers, your soil is likely lacking key nutrients and requires cocoa fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ, edaa blɛoo, loo ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ni eyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: What key things should I consider before expanding my cocoa farm to a larger scale?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa esa akɛ masusu he dani magbɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mashwa kɛyashɛ he ko ni da?

english: Before expanding, ensure you have enough labor for labor-intensive tasks like pruning and pollination, secure quality planting materials, and have enough money saved to maintain the farm until the new trees yield fruit.
ga: dani obaagbɛ oshwã Kwɛmɔ ni oná nitsulɔi ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nitsumɔi ni heɔ nitsumɔ babaoo tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ anɔ ni oná shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛkwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi tsei heei lɛ baawo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off in the dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛyashɛ la ni mli egbi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under full sun. Without shade trees or plantains to shield them and trap soil moisture, the harsh sun causes the leaves to dry up, turn yellow, and drop off.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbee shi

english: Why are small holes appearing in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar hides deep inside the growing funnel of the maize plant and eats the tender leaves before they unfold, leaving visible holes as the plant grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baa, ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpoɔ Buji ni anaa beni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: What is making the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies, thrips, or mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaves, or by a viral disease transmitted by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce plenty of flowers but very few actual bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi pea pods diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ?

english: Tiny insects called flower thrips feed on cowpea blossoms, causing the flowers to damage, wither, and drop off before they can develop into healthy bean pods.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ flower thrips lɛ yeɔ tsina fɔfɔii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow very tall with plenty of leaves, but the tubers underground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or the field gets too much shade, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo he ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli ewo hulutsoo tsɔ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my seed yams rot in the soil before they can sprout new shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmeii heei jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Seed yams rot underground when planted in soil that stays waterlogged, or when planted directly in hot, dry soil without straw mulch to shield them from high soil heat and soil fungi.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛ nɔ ko wooo mli koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the plant without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or heavy rains during flowering. When conditions get too harsh, the plant discards its flowers to preserve energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Beni shihilɛi lɛ ehiii tsɔ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when the fruit bunches start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that cannot easily support heavy tops. As the fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy and can easily snap or tip over during strong winds unless supported with bamboo or wooden stakes.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ aye abua ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ mlɛo. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ daraa Tsei lɛ tsii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkumɔ loo amɛku amɛsɛɛ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. ja ŋmei loo tsei ahe tsei fiɔ sɛɛ

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is exhausted and needs a break or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni asaa nɔ loo awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Exhausted soil shows signs like slow crop growth, pale green leaves instead of deep green, low yield during harvest, and the sudden spread of stubborn weeds like spear grass that thrive in nutrient-poor soils.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baatsɔɔ okadii tamɔ tsei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo. Baai lɛ ji eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli kɛ jwɛi ni wa ni gbɛɔ eshwaa trukaa, tamɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii bɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Does letting weeds grow close to my crops really lower my harvest, or can I wait to clear them later?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mahã akwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha mikpamɔ lɛ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ? Aloo manyɛ mamɛ ni mikɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii sɛɛ mli?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. If left unchecked during the early weeks of planting, they starve your crops, leading to weak plants and much lower yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsi ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ Amɛbaahã hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my corn when the rainy season keeps shifting?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje ŋmãa dumɔ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ be lɛ tsake?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because it might be a false start. Wait until you get two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the soil within a single week before putting your seeds in the ground.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ enɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Mɛɛ ni oná nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ otsi kome mli dani okɛ dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weather announcements say we will get plenty of rain, but my farm still ends up drying out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he adafitswaa lɛ kɛɛ nugbɔ baanɛ waa lɛ? Shi miŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi?

english: General weather reports cover large regions, but rainfall in tropical areas can be very local—it can pour on a neighboring farm and completely miss yours. It is always safest to check the actual soil moisture on your own land before planting.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he amaniɛbɔi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ kɔɔ he ko ni da he. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hei ni latsaa yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Nugbɔ baanyɛ anɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli ni efo bo nɔ lɛ mli kwraa. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ be fɛɛ be akɛ oookwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni yɔɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani okɛdu.

english: Why did my corn grow nicely up to my knees and then suddenly stop growing and wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni eshwɛ fioo ni ebaashɛ enaji ahe ni trukaa lɛ ekpaa dalɛ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: As corn grows taller, its leaves widen and it needs much more water to build strong stalks. If the rains stop when the corn is knee-high, the soil runs out of water quickly, causing the plants to stress, stop growing, and dry up.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ da Ebaai lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni ebiɔ nu babaoo koni ekɛfee ŋmãa ni wa. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe lɛ Nu baatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ lɛ kpaɔ amɛdalɛ ni amɛgboɔ

english: What simple step can I take on my field to protect my young crops when the rain suddenly stops?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii bibii manyɛ mafee yɛ ŋmɔ mli koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ trukaa?

english: Covering the bare ground around your crops with dry leaves, straw, or grass—a practice called mulching—acts like a blanket that keeps the sun from drying out the soil water too quickly.
ga: Ha he ni agbele ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Okɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya tsɔ.

english: Is it wise for me to spend money renting a tractor to clear all my land before the rain fully sets in?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mafite shika yɛ trakta ni mikɛhaa koni mikɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa dani nugbɔ lɛ aba?

english: Plowing all your land early exposes bare soil to the hot sun, making it dry out faster if the rains delay. It is safer to prepare land in stages or ensure steady rains have begun so you do not waste money on inputs if dry weather continues.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ nitsumɔ mra Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ aná hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha egbi oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaasa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Aloo kwɛmɔ ni nugbɔ aje shishi nɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ ji koni ehe akahia ni ofite shika yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ tee nɔ.

english: Why does removing all the bushes and trees from my farm make the ground feel hotter and drier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mijie jwɛi kɛ tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Trees and bushes provide shade and block hot winds. When you clear all vegetation from a farm, direct sunlight bakes the topsoil and evaporates ground moisture much faster than on shaded land.
ga: Tsei kɛ tsei bibii haa hɔɔŋ kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Beni ojieɔ tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I easily test if my soil has enough moisture before I plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa dani madu dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ?

english: Dig a small hole hand-deep into the soil, grab a handful of dirt, and squeeze it tightly. If it forms a ball that holds its shape without crumbling or dripping water, the soil has good moisture for planting.
ga: Okɛ onine atsa bu bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni okɛ onine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni okɛmimɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ etamɔ bɔɔlu lɛ, ehiɔ shi yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli, ni efoŋ loo efoŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui.

english: What can I mix into my soil to help it hold onto rainwater for a longer time?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua lɛ ni ehiɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Adding well-rotted animal manure or decomposed compost into your soil acts like a sponge, holding onto rainwater deeper down so crop roots can keep drinking during dry days.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni egbo ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu ni emɔɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu nu yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Are there special corn seeds I can buy that will survive if the rain stops unexpectedly?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ ni manyɛ mahe ni baahi shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa?

english: Yes, agriculture offices sell early-maturing and drought-tolerant seed varieties that grow faster and require less total water to produce grain compared to traditional seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ hɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛbiɔ nu babaoo fioo koni amɛwo dumɔwui kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ahe.

english: What other food crops can I plant instead of corn if I am worried the rains will be poor this year?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii manyɛ madu yɛ ŋmãa najiaŋ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛŋ afi nɛɛ he miihao?

english: Crops like cassava, cowpeas (beans), sorghum, and millet have deep roots and tough leaves that allow them to survive with far less water than corn during dry seasons.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ cassava, cowpea (pea), sorghum, kɛ millet yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛtsɔ nu fioo ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii fe ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Do yam plants have male and female types, and how do they work together?
ga: Ayɛ sweet potato tsei ni ji hii kɛ yei. Ni te amɛfeɔ tɛŋŋ amɛfeɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii?

english: Yes, yams have separate male and female plants. When pollen from a male plant fertilizes a female plant, it produces seeds that can grow into entirely new yam varieties.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potato yɛ tsei ni ji hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Beni pollen ni jɛ tso nuu mli lɛ kɛ tso yoo ko feɔ ekome. Ebaawo dumɔwui ni baanyɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ sweet potato henɔi heei.

english: How can I tell if my yam plant is a male or a female plant in the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi sweet potato tsei lɛ ji hii loo yei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can tell during the flowering season by looking at the flowers. Male plants produce small, clustered flower spikes, while female plants produce flowers that eventually form seed pods.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole fɔfɔi be mli kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ. Tso ni ji nuu lɛ baawo fɔfɔi bibii. jeɔ kpo yɛ kui amli yɛ be mli ni tso yoo lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛyashi naagbee lɛ ebaatsɔ dumɔwui akui.

english: Can I produce a new type of yam by combining two different yam varieties?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ŋmɔtɔ henɔ hee kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ henɔi srɔtoi enyɔ ni mikɛfutuɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, by taking the male flower of one variety and crossing it with the female flower of another variety, you get seeds that combine traits from both parents to form a new variety.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi hii ni yɔɔ tso kome mli lɛ ni akɛfutuɔ fɔfɔi yei ni yɔɔ tso kroko mli lɛ nɔ. Onaa dumɔwui ni kɛ sui feɔ ekome kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ adɛŋ koni ekɛfee srɔtoi hee.

english: How do crop scientists create new yam seeds that give better yields?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nilelɔi afee sweet potato dumɔwui hee ko ni woɔ yibii kpakpai?

english: Scientists select a pure male plant and a strong female plant with desirable traits, carefully pollinate them, and collect the resulting seeds to grow improved yam varieties.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi halaa tsei hii ni he tse kɛ tsei yei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sui ni ataoɔ lɛ. Okɛ pollin awo mli jogbaŋŋ. ni abua dumɔwui ni ana lɛ anaa koni akɛfee sweet potato henɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes a yam variety have a good eating quality or good meal when cooked?
ga: Mɛni haa sweet potato henɔ lɛ feɔ niyenii kpakpa loo niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ahoo lɛ?

english: Good meal quality comes from high dry matter and starch content inherited from parent plants, giving the cooked yam a firm, non-watery texture that tastes good.
ga: Niyenii lɛ kpakpa lɛ jɛɔ nibii ni egbi ni fa babaoo kɛ starch ni yɔɔ mli ni anáa kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa sweet potato ni ahoo lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa, ni jeee nɔ ni hoɔ, ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the difference between a pure traditional yam and a new crossed variety?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ blema ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hee ni akɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: A pure traditional variety has stable, fixed characteristics passed down over time, while a new crossed variety combines the strong qualities of two different parents into one plant.
ga: Hetsemɔ, shishijee henɔi lɛ yɛ sui ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni akɛhaa yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai heei ni akɛfee tsofai sɔrɔtoi lɛ kɛ fɔlɔi sɔrɔtoi enyɔ asui ni mli wa lɛ feɔ tso kome.

english: If I plant a seed from a crossed yam, will the tuber taste like both parent plants?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui kɛjɛ sweet potatoes mli Ani bulbs lɛ baafee nɔ ni tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It will inherit qualities from both parents, often blending the best taste and texture traits of the male and female parent plants.
ga: Ebaaŋɔ nibii kɛjɛ fɔlɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ adɛŋ akɛ gboshinii. Bei pii lɛ, amɛkɛ tsei ni ji hii kɛ yei lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔi kɛ ŋmɔlɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: Why do some yam varieties stay firm after boiling while others become watery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi hiɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ ahoo amɛ sɛɛ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ nu?

english: This behavior depends on the genetic traits of the variety; certain varieties naturally hold less water and more starch, giving them that preferred firm, dry texture.
ga: Nɛkɛ subaŋ nɛɛ damɔ fɔmɔ nii ni yɔɔ tsina lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Henɔi komɛi hiɛɔ nu fioo yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ŋmeii babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi nɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why is the Pona yam variety so popular in the Ghanaian market compared to other yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Pona yam henɔ lɛ ehe gbɛi waa yɛ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ kɛ akɛto yam henɔi krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Pona is highly popular because it combines excellent meal quality, superior taste, and the ideal texture that consumers across the country prefer.
ga: Pona ji nɔ ko ni mɛi sumɔɔ waa ejaakɛ ekɛ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ feɔ ekome. ŋmɔlɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ sumɔɔ

english: Why should I consider market demand before choosing which yam variety to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu nibii ni jarayelihe lɛ taoɔ lɛ ahe dani mahala sweet potato henɔ ni esa akɛ makwɛ lɛ?

english: Planting a high-demand variety like Pona guarantees that buyers and consumers will want your harvest, allowing you to sell faster and at better prices.
ga: Nibii ni ataoɔ waa tamɔ Pona lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baasumɔ nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ oya ni okɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ hu hɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because harsh, direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil. Leaving some tall trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides living shade that keeps the plants cool and moist during their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛná hɔnɔ fioo koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaa bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. ni ejieɔ tsei kakadaji loo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ emasɛi lɛ Cocoa haa hulutsoo ni haa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the soil is short on nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build healthy green leaves. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish new foliage, signaling that you need to add compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ afata he.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same piece of land three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks the life cycle of pests.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil if the heavy rains stay for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with excess water, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing the tubers to suffocate and decay. Cassava grows best in well-drained or sloped soil so that water flows away easily rather than pooling around the roots.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ. Yucca kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni ŋshɔ yɔɔ nɔ ni haa nu hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabua amɛhe naa amɛbɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme afternoon heat or irregular watering. Maintaining consistent moisture in the soil and mulching around the plant base helps keep root temperatures steady so the flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ mli fɛ̃i yaa nɔ daa bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the mother stem, they all compete for the same food and water in the soil, resulting in small bunches. Removing extra suckers and keeping only two or three ensures the main plant gets enough nourishment to produce large plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmei) kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe tsɔ nyɛ tso lɛ Nakai ŋmeii lɛ baatswa akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii bibii ni jeɔ kpo. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ toɔ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the new leaves on my pepper bushes curling up and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the sap of tender leaves, damaging them and sometimes passing on viruses. Checking under leaves and controlling these pests early prevents leaf damage and stops disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Amɛfiteɔ nii ni bei komɛi lɛ amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwãa. Baai lɛ ashishi kwɛmɔ kɛ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ akafite ni ekpaa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do I need to put tall wood stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight so their leaves can trap solar energy to feed the underground tuber. Keeping the leaves lifted off the damp ground also prevents foliage rot and leads to bigger, healthier yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni ebaa lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu hewalɛ ni ekɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛkafiteɔ, ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I plant them immediately after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by several hot, dry days that scorch sprouted seeds beneath the soil surface. Waiting until the rains become frequent ensures the soil stays consistently wet enough for young roots to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ ni edɔɔ ni shãa dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛmɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When these plants die, the trapped nitrogen stays in the earth, acting as natural food for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ gboi Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up and turn yellow during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize leaves roll up, the plant is trying to save water by reducing evaporation from its leaf surface. Yellowing leaves mean the plant is stressed and lacks moisture to carry nutrients, showing that it urgently needs water.
