ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he kɛtsɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛbaa shi lɛ nɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao ni ebɛ nu ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ baaya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia tso lɛ oya.

english: How do I know if my vegetables are getting too much water from the irrigation canal?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ aduawai miihe nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli?

english: If vegetables receive too much water, their leaves turn pale yellow, drop off, and their roots start to rot because wet soil blocks air. Good soil should be damp like a squeezed cloth, not muddy or soaked.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aduawai ná nu babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa. Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa afee nɔ ni mli edɔ tamɔ mama ni mli efɔ. Jeee muji loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ

english: Why is it better to water my crop early in the morning instead of in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows crop roots to drink before the sun gets hot. If you water during the intense afternoon heat, hot sun causes most water to evaporate into the air before roots can absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu leebi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Kɛji okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Can I use water from the community dam directly on my farm during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ akutso lɛ mli nu ŋshɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, dam water is ideal for dry season farming, but it should be directed gently to the crop roots using buckets or channels. Pouring high volumes of water directly onto crops can wash away topsoil and damage delicate stems.
ga: Hɛɛ, dam nu lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha okwaayeli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Shi esa akɛ akɛ baagi loo tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ aya tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli blɛoo. Nu babaoo ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni efite tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow well in the first year but give smaller yields every year after on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo daa afi yɛ no sɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the soil to grow. If you keep planting the same crop without adding manure, compost, or resting the land, the soil becomes empty of food and yields will drop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo hejɔɔmɔ fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops dry up faster when rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Weeds have tough, fast-growing roots that steal soil moisture and nutrients away from your crops. When rain stops, weeds drink up the remaining soil water first, leaving your crops thirsty.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa, ni daa oya ni juɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, jwɛi lɛ nuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ha kumai aye oŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do my crops produce smaller fruits when I plant many of them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii beni midu tsei babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots fight underground for water and soil nutrients while leaves block each other from sunlight. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to grow large fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii wuji.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there are no bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily in direct sunlight. Shading trees act like umbrellas, shielding them from strong heat and keeping the soil moist until roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Buu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or lack of water. Dropping flowers helps the plant preserve its energy and water just to stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu toɔ koni ehi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: Why does cassava survive long dry seasons much better than maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cassava has thick underground roots that store food and water, allowing it to rest during dry periods. Maize has shallow roots that dry out quickly if rain fails.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni kɛ niyenii kɛ nu toɔ. Ha ejɔɔ ehe yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, egbiɔ oya.

english: Why do my crops look sickly even after I apply expensive fertilizer to the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Crops struggle in soil that is too 'sour' or acidic. Most crops perform best when the soil balance (pH) is neutral to slightly acidic, around six. If the soil acidity is wrong, the plant roots get locked out and cannot absorb the fertilizer you apply until you fix the soil balance.
ga: Tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ‘edɔ’ loo edɔ tsɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei babaoo tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi ŋta (pH) lɛ ji nɔ ni bɛ ŋtayaa kɛyashi ŋtayaa fioo, ni miihe ashɛ digrii 6. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ acidity lɛ ejaaa lɛ, Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ baatsi amɛhe ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛyashi obaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekome.

english: How do I know if my farm soil balance is right for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔ?

english: When soil is too acidic, plants show stress through yellowing leaves, stunted stems, and poor root growth. Extension officers can test your soil to check if it reaches the target balance level of six, which is ideal for maize absorption of soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tsei jieɔ haomɔ kpo kɛtsɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ. shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ kɛ shishifãi ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ Extension nitsulɔi baanyɛ aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ amɛkwɛ kɛji eshɛ Target Balance Level 6, ni ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the afternoon sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses crops, making them react by shedding flowers to conserve water and survive. Providing partial shade or mulching the roots reduces heat stress and allows the plant to hold onto its flowers and produce peppers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei feɔ amɛnii kɛtsɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo fã ko ha loo akɛha shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ chili ŋmɔtɔ

english: Does pruning my crop branches really help them produce bigger yields?
ga: Ani mitsei lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Applying mild pressure through pruning removes excess leaves that consume food. This forces the plant to direct its energy into developing bigger fruits and grains instead of useless bushy growth.
ga: Kɛtsɔ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ajieɔ baai ni fa fe nine ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii koni amɛwo aduawai kɛ ŋmaa wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ ni sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he yɛ kui amli lɛ

english: Why do my crops wilt so fast during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind draws water out of plant leaves faster than roots can drink. Mulching around the base of the crop retains moisture in the soil, helping plants withstand harsh weather stress.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa mli baa lɛ.

english: What is the difference between foundation seeds from officers and seeds saved from my old harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni jɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni ahere amɛ kɛjɛ mikpamɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Foundation seeds are pure, high-quality seeds carefully multiplied under strict research conditions. Unlike seeds saved from old harvests, foundation seeds guarantee uniform growth, strong disease resistance, and higher yield potential.
ga: Dumɔwui shishijee ji dumɔwui ni he tse, ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Fɔmɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ niiamlitaomɔ shihilɛi ni mli wa shishi. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nikpamɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ he. Primer dumɔwui haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ amɛdaraa po. Helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo baa

english: Why should I avoid buying seed grain from the local food market for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahemɔ he yɛ maŋ lɛ mli niyenii ajarayelihe lɛ koni mikɛdu lɛ?

english: Grains sold in food markets are meant for consumption and may carry hidden seed-borne diseases or have low germination rates. Certified seed supplies undergo laboratory testing to ensure high sprouting power.
ga: Akɛ ŋmaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ niyenii ajarayelihei lɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛye ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ dumɔwui helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo ehiɛ shweremɔ ni baa shi. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli mli lɛ akwɛɔ yɛ laboratori mli koni ana akɛ eyɛ hewalɛ waa.

english: How much seed do I need to prepare if I want to expand to large commercial farming?
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni ogbɛ oshwa kɛya jarayeli okwaayeli wulu mli Dumɔwui enyiɛ ehe miihia ni masaa?

english: Large commercial farming requires buying seed in bulk tons calculated per acre. Using certified high-volume seed guarantees that every field sprouts evenly without leaving blank spaces.
ga: Jarayeli okwaayeli ni da lɛ biɔ ni ahe dumɔwui yɛ tɔn kome mli yɛ acre kome mli. Dumɔwui ni fa babaoo ni awo he odaseyeli akɛtsu nii lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ baakwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni eshiŋ gbɛ ko kwraa.

english: Why do my maize cobs come out small and thin when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ bibii ni eyɛ mlɛo waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting too close creates intense pressure and competition among crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Correct row spacing gives each crop room to feed and grow full-sized cobs.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa tsei ateŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Gbɛjegbɛ ni ja ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa tsu fɛɛ tsu ni edaa lɛ naa he ko ni edaa cob ni dalɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings need temporary shade when I first put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ he hiaa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo be mli ni mikɛ amɛ duɔ shikpɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young plant seedlings have shallow roots and cannot handle full tropical sunlight right away. Temporary shade shields them from heat stress until their roots grow deep enough to suck up groundwater.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen runs out, the plant moves what little food it has from older lower leaves to keep the top new leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen lɛ ba naagbee Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni eha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How do groundnut plants help make my soil better for other crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tso aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Groundnut plants have special roots that work with tiny beneficial soil organisms to capture nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the earth, leaving natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ aaamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: If maize seeds are planted too deep, they exhaust all their stored food energy trying to push through the heavy soil, leading to weak sprouts or seeds dying before reaching sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ Niyenii ni ato lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii loo dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ dani hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water covers the soil for too long without draining, air cannot enter, causing the underground roots to suffocate and decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abote mli, enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither when planted in open sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that lose moisture quickly under strong heat. Plantain or shade trees act like living umbrellas, providing the cooler, moist air young cocoa needs to grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi. Plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Koni eye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves off the damp ground to capture as much sunlight as possible, which helps the plant manufacture food to produce bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their small flowers before pods form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani pods lɛ baakwɛ̃?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if tiny beneficial insects do not pollinate them, or if the tree experiences heat stress and sheds flowers to save water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛji kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ efɔɔɔ amɛ, loo kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni ehi shi.

english: Why do my crops grow so poorly when weeds spread around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ be mli ni jwɛi egbɛ eshwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for space, soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, stealing essential resources away from your main plants.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná he ko. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli, ni ejuɔ nibii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies are sucking sap from the leaves, or transmitting viruses that distort leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies, miinu nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ. loo egbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ eshwaa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom end rot, caused when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, usually due to irregular or uneven watering during fruit growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa loo ni ejaaa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen fertilizer or the soil is too waterlogged. Nitrogen moves to the new upper leaves first, leaving the old lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Nitrogen lɛ baafã kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ha shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry up so quickly in sandy soil near the coastal areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔnaa hei lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large particles that cannot hold water or nutrients for long. Water drains through it quickly, and high salt levels near the coast can draw moisture away from crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ nibii bibii wuji ni nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Nu lɛ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli oya. Ni ŋmei ni fa babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ baanyɛ agbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tsei shishifãi amli.

english: Why does applying too much chemical fertilizer burn my plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is high in salts. When you apply too much, it pulls water out of the plant roots instead of feeding them, causing the plant to dehydrate and the leaf tips to turn brown or burn.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmei fa babaoo. Kɛ okɛwo mli babaoo Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli ni baa lɛ naa tsɔɔ asarasu loo shãa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground before I am ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for long periods due to poor drainage. Fungi in the wet soil attack the root tubers, causing them to spoil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Fungus ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ, ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, or viruses spread by them. They suck the sap from tender leaves, causing them to wrinkle and distort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi baa

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu bɛ tsei amli loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that hold heavy fruit stems. Tiny worms called nematodes or root fungi often weaken these roots underground, making the tree easy for wind to knock down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni haa aduawai lɛ ashishifãi ni tsii lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo root fungi lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ehaa tsei shwieɔ shi oya

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big shade trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh, direct sunlight and dry winds. Big trees provide shade and keep the air and soil cool until the cocoa stems grow mature enough to tolerate full sun.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do I get smaller crops when I plant my seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ yɛ be mli ni adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other underground for food and water, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another, leading to weak plants and lower yield.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my yam vines grow huge leaves but produce very small yam tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes yams to spend all their energy producing green leaves and stems above ground instead of sending nutrients down to build a large tuber.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi

english: I want to grow pawpaw, but someone told me some trees are male and won't give fruit. How many male trees do I need to keep in my farm for the female trees to produce well?
ga: Miisumɔ ni makwɛ papaya shi akɛɛ mi akɛ tsei komɛi ji hii ni amɛwooo yibii. Tsei hii enyiɛ ehe miihia ni mahi miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mawo tsei yei kpakpai?

english: Pawpaw plants have different sexes: male trees produce pollen but no fruit, while female trees produce fruit when pollinated. You do not need many male trees—having just one male tree for every eight to ten female trees is enough for insects and wind to pollinate the farm effectively.
ga: Pawpaw tsei lɛ yɛ bɔlɛnamɔi srɔtoi. Tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ pollen shi amɛwooo yibii. yɛ be mli ni tsei yei woɔ yibii kɛji akɛ amɛwo amɛhe ŋmɔtɔ. Ohe ehiaaa tsei hii babaoo. Tso kome pɛ ni ji nuu kɛyashi tsei yei 8-10 ni yɔɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha kooloi bibii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ aba ŋmɔ ko mli.

english: If I harvest good hybrid maize this season, can I save some of the seeds to plant again next year?
ga: Kɛji mikpa hybrid ŋmãa kpakpa yɛ be nɛɛ mli Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui komɛi ato koni madu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: It is not advisable to replant seeds harvested from hybrid maize. Hybrid seeds are specially cross-bred in laboratories for high yield; if you plant their saved seeds, the crop offspring will lose those special qualities, resulting in weak plants and a poor harvest.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ ekoŋŋ. Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ yɛ laboratori ko mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ato lɛ Nibii ni adu lɛ seshibii lɛ baafite nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How many years does it usually take for a newly planted cocoa tree to start bearing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties take about 3 to 5 years to produce their first pods. However, improved hybrid cocoa varieties developed for Ghanaian farmers can start bearing fruit in about 2 to 3 years if given proper water, fertilizer, and care.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi amli kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛfeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni afee aha Ghana okwaafoi lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, kɛji akɛ aha amɛ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ tomato?

english: Tomato flowers usually drop without forming fruits when temperatures are too high, when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing leaf growth instead of fruiting, or when there are no bees and wind to help pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ lɛ, baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni baaye abua ni ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo mli.

english: Why is it bad to allow many young shoots to grow around the base of one main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwu titri kome shishitoo ji nɔ fɔŋ.

english: Allowing too many shoots (suckers) to grow around one plantain stem creates competition for nutrients, soil moisture, and sunlight. Pruning extra shoots and leaving only two or three healthy suckers ensures the main tree grows a large, heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Plantain tso kome he lɛ fa tsɔ. Enɛ baaha akaŋshii aba kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: What happens if I plant three or four maize seeds in one small hole instead of spacing them out?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ wo bu bibioo ko mli? Bu kome moŋ fe ni aaaje kpo

english: Planting too many seeds together causes overcrowding. The growing maize plants will fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, tall stalks that yield small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa mɛi ayiɔ obɔ fe nine. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe tseee, ni no haa dumɔwui bibii loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Can I grow cassava using stem cuttings, or do I have to collect seeds from cassava flowers?
ga: Ani obaanyɛ odu ŋmei? Aloo esa akɛ obua dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmei fɔfɔi amli?

english: Cassava is grown using stem cuttings taken from healthy, mature plants. Planting 20 to 25 cm long stem cuttings directly into raised soil beds allows the crop to grow faster and produce reliable roots compared to growing from tiny seeds.
ga: Akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eda lɛ amli tsei ni afolɔ mli lɛ duɔ cassava. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kɛlɛ ji 20 kɛyashi 25 cm tɛ̃ɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edaa oya ni ehaa shishifãi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui bibii amli shweremɔ he

english: Why should I buy grafted mango seedlings instead of planting seeds directly from a sweet mango I ate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ mango ni ŋɔɔ ni miyeɔ lɛ mli?

english: Mango trees grown directly from seed take 7 to 10 years to bear fruit and may not taste as sweet as the parent mango. Grafted seedlings join a sweet branch to a strong root base, producing fruits in just 2 to 3 years while guaranteeing the same high quality.
ga: Mango tsei ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ afii 7 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Ni ekolɛ eŋɔɔɔɔ tamɔ shishijee mango lɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni ŋɔɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shishitoo ni wa nɔ. Ehaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni ehaa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ maa nɔ mi.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall and thin under big shade trees, but fail to produce peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miida ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo yɛ ŋwɛitsu agbo ko shishi lɛ? shi enyɛŋ ekɛ chili ŋmɔtɔ aba

english: Pepper plants need direct sunlight to produce energy for flowering and fruiting. When grown in heavy shade, the plant stretches upward searching for light, spending all its energy on stem growth instead of making peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tso lɛ baakpã kɛya ŋwɛi koni eyatao la. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ ŋmeii lɛ moŋ fe ni eeefee chili.

english: If I plant sweet corn next to yellow field corn, will it change the taste of my sweet corn?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni ji yellow lɛ masɛi Ani ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ŋɔɔmɔ baatsake?

english: Yes, corn is pollinated by wind, so pollen from yellow field corn will easily drift to the sweet corn flowers. This cross-pollination causes the sweet corn to grow tough, starchy yellow kernels instead of remaining tender and sweet.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmãa. No hewɔ lɛ, pollen ni jɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa fɔfɔi ni ŋɔɔ lɛ anɔ oya. Nɛkɛ cross-pollination nɛɛ haa ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ ni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wa ni eyɛ ŋmãa lɛ baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeehi shi blɛoo ni ŋɔɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when the sunshine becomes too harsh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like small children—their leaves are tender and easily burn under direct hot sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and traps moisture in the soil to help the cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii tamɔ gbekɛbii bibii. Baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛ shɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha ená hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi koni eye ebua kookoo lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the cobs are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for healthy green growth. Applying manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base of the plant helps feed it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni eyeɔ niyenii.

english: How should I stick my cassava stems into the ground so that they grow properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be planted with the small buds pointing upward toward the sky. Slanting the stick at an angle and burying about two-thirds of it in the soil gives it strong roots and plenty of space underground to form tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ shwie shi yɛ koŋ nɔ ni ofu gbɛ lɛ mli aaafee mlijaa enyɔ mli ekome kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni wa kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he babaoo aba koni ekɛfee bulbs.

english: Why do I need to clear tall trees and raise stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei kakadaji kɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato wain tsei amli koni manyɛ makwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to produce the food that swells the tuber underground. Climbing up wooden stakes lifts the foliage into the sunshine and keeps the leaves from rotting on the wet soil.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni fũuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Tso lɛ nɔ ni akwɔɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ. ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Why does my field soil dry out so quickly after the rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛ lɛ, sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Soil loses moisture fast when it lacks organic matter and is left exposed to the direct sun. Leaving dry grass, cut weeds, or crop leftovers on top of the soil as mulch acts like a cover, trapping water in the dirt for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli, ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. jwɛi ni afolɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Enɛ ji akɛ, jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni haa nɔ. Ha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When is the right time during the day or season for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo be mli ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning when the soil is already moist from rain or dew. Never apply fertilizer onto bone-dry soil or right before a heavy downpour, as dry soil can burn roots and heavy rain will wash the nutrient away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi be mli ni nugbɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ eba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ momo. Kaawo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ loo dani nugbɔ nɛ waa. Ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛyaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from very hot temperatures, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently damp and planting flowers nearby to attract bees helps flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning wrinkly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny, invisible insects hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices. Spraying the leaves with a simple mixture of soapy water or neem seed oil helps clear the insects so new green leaves can grow straight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ chili baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Akɛni anaaa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni ekɛ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo neem dumɔwui amli fɔ efutu mli lɛ baashwie baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie kooloi bibii kɛjɛ jɛmɛ koni baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Will planting groundnuts together in the same field as my maize harm my crop yield?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baaná mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: No, interplanting groundnuts with maize actually helps both crops. Groundnuts pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to survive hard weather and poor soil, so they sprout quickly to drink all available water and soil nutrients. Clearing them while they are small keeps them from stealing food from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdaraa oya koni amɛnu nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ, ebaaha amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do cocoa trees need bigger shade trees planted around them on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei he hiaa ni adu tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct hot sunlight and strong winds. Planting shade trees around them protects the young cocoa from heat stress, keeps the soil moist, and creates a cooler climate that cocoa trees need to thrive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni aduɔ koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha yɛ Cacao he lɛ buɔ cacao tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛshwere lɛ baa.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves turning brown and drying up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow root systems that cannot reach deep underground water. During the dry season, intense heat and lack of moisture cause the leaves to dry out and fall off unless they have enough shade and watering.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Ja hulutsoo kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and soft while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during damp, rainy weather. Removing the infected pods immediately prevents the fungal spores from spreading to your healthy cocoa pods.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã o-cocoa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: How long does a cashew tree usually take after planting before it starts bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ cashew tso heɔ kɛji adu lɛ dani ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Cashew trees typically start producing a few fruits in their second or third year, but they reach full, commercial production around their fourth or fifth year as the tree canopy grows larger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei jeɔ yibii fioo komɛi shishi yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ loo etɛ lɛ mli. Shi ashɛɔ jarayeli nitsumɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ he yɛ afi ni ji ejwɛ loo enumɔ lɛ mli beni tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ feɔ agbo lɛ.

english: Can I plant crops like cassava or maize between my cashew trees while they are still small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping works very well during the first two to three years. Because young cashew trees are small and spaced far apart, planting food crops in between helps you make good use of the land and soil nutrients before the trees grow wide.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, cashew tsei lɛ daraaa ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛ. Niyenii ni ooodu yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ dani tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How do I know when my cashew nuts are completely ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ cashew ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cashew nuts are fully ripe when the cashew apple turns bright red or yellow and drops naturally from the tree to the ground. You should collect them from the ground rather than picking green ones off the branches.
ga: Cashew ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ aduawai lɛ batsɔ tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ egbeeɔ shikpɔŋ Esa akɛ otsi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni oootsi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli.

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my mango tree before they can turn into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mango tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Mango flower drop happens due to sudden water stress, insect pests like thrips, or bad weather. Ensuring the tree gets adequate water during flowering and managing pests helps more flowers turn into actual fruit.
ga: Mango fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa yɛ nu mli haomɔ ni baa trukaa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ thrips, loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Ni aaakwɛ koni aha tsei lɛ nu bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni anáa fɔfɔi babaoo ni tsɔɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why does my mango tree produce a heavy crop one year, but gives almost no fruit the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli shi afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ewooo yibii kwraa lɛ?

english: This is known as alternate bearing. A heavy harvest drains the mango tree of its nutrient reserves, so it spends the following year recovering its energy and leaves before it can produce a large harvest again.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ bearing ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ. Nikpamɔ ni tsii haa mango tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fiteɔ. No hewɔ lɛ eheɔ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ dani enáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni eshiɔ dani enyɛɔ ewoɔ yibii babaoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are black spots appearing on my mangoes and causing them to rot on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mangoi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni egbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots are commonly caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose or by fruit fly attacks. Rainy weather encourages the fungus to spread, so keeping the tree pruned for good air movement helps reduce rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose loo aduawai amli ŋmeii ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji baa. Nugbɔshiimɔ haa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ aba shi.

english: How does adding animal manure to my farm soil help my tree crops grow better harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Animal manure enriches the soil with essential nutrients, improves the soil's ability to hold moisture during dry spells, and feeds helpful soil organisms, leading to stronger root growth and healthier crop yields.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni ekɛ niyenii haa nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa waa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hu baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. The plant moves the little nitrogen it has to the newer top leaves, leaving the older bottom leaves to starve unless fertilizer or compost is added.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen fioo ko kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ja awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo afee amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers drop off without growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the weather gets too hot, when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Gently shaking the plants in the morning can help pollination and encourage fruit to set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni kooloi nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Tso lɛ ni oookpokpo blɛoo Leebi lɛ ebaanyɛ eye ebua yɛ pollination mli ni ewo yibii lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves dry up and drop off during the dry season, and does it mean the plant is dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to protect itself and save water in its roots. The plant is not dead; as soon as the rainy season starts, it will grow fresh green leaves and continue growing underground tubers.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ebu ehe ni ekɛ nu ahi eshishifãi lɛ amli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ kɛkɛ ni baai lɛ baafee eŋɔli ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baaya nɔ adara.

english: How do I know when my underground yam tubers are mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yams tell you they are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry completely. This signals that the plant has stopped growing and has stored all its energy into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes kɛɔ bo akɛ amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I harvest more food from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ makpa niyenii kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Ani manyɛ maná mi nɔ babaoo?

english: Planting too close together causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tiny cobs or thin stems. Giving each seed proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough energy to produce big, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmei bibioo loo ŋmei bibii. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why are my pepper seedlings growing tall, thin, and weak instead of short and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ miidara, amɛmiifee mlɛo ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ kukuji kɛ ŋmɔji najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch out and become thin when they are not receiving enough direct sunlight, often because they are planted under heavy shade or too close together. Giving them full sunshine makes their stems grow thick and strong.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe ni amɛbaafee bibioo kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ waa loo amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: What causes black spots to spread across my cocoa pods during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are caused by a fungal disease called black pod, which spreads rapidly in cool, humid conditions with dense shade. Pruning overgrown trees to let sunlight in and removing infected pods helps keep the disease from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni edara fe nine lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves of my papaya trees curling inward and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya baai lɛ miihoso kɛmiiya mli ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in papaya is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses. Keeping weeds down and spraying insecticidal soap can protect the leaves from vector insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni kɛ hela lɛ baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my watermelon leaves wilt in the middle of the hot afternoon even when the soil was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ watermelon baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi?

english: Watermelon leaves wilt in the midday sun because the plant loses water through its leaves faster than its roots can drink it from the soil. As long as the soil stays moist, the leaves will bounce back and stand up once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Watermelon baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ tso lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi ni amɛteɔ shi beni hulu lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my okro crop take so long to produce pods when my neighbor's okro grows so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-okra lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekɛ pods baa be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ okra lɛ daa oya lɛ?

english: Okro grows slowly when planted in poor, hard soil or in shady areas. Adding organic compost to enrich the soil and ensuring the farm receives full, direct sunlight speeds up growth and encourages early flowering.
ga: Okra daa blɛoo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni wa nɔ loo he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo, ni akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ awo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ewo fɔfɔii ni baa mra lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up when the sun is bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their young leaves dry out quickly. They need temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava planted around them to act as natural sunshades while they establish deep roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaa bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava, ni adu yɛ amɛhe. koni amɛtsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why is my maize crop growing weak and yellowish instead of deep green and tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ miida ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ekwɛɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize plants turn pale yellow when the soil lacks essential nutrients, especially nitrogen. Adding organic manure or recommended fertilizers like NPK early in the plant's growth provides the food needed for dark green leaves and thick stalks.
ga: Abɛi tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa tamɔ NPK fataa he yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ shishijee bei amli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ ana niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛha ebaai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa kɛ eshishifãi ni mli tse lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava stems curling up and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings prevents this virus from spreading.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji cassava mosaic hela ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ Cassava ni afolɔ ni hela nyɛɔ eyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ dumɔ baaye abua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: You should wait until the rainy season settles and the soil remains wet deep down for several days, rather than planting after the very first rain shower. Planting too early in dry, hot soil will scorch the seeds before they can sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lolo. gbii babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaashã dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crops to produce very small yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital food, water, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds grow close to your crops, your crops starve and cannot develop healthy fruits or tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: If too many young shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain tree, they all compete for the same soil water and nutrients. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmei) babaoo yɛ ni miida yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he. Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot and dry or when the soil lacks steady moisture. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the base of the plant helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my pepper plant leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome

english: Tiny holes on leaves are usually caused by insects like beetles or caterpillars that feed on crop foliage at night. Catching them early or using safe insect treatments protects the leaves so the plant can continue growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ladybugs loo caterpillars ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ baa. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Aloo okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni baabu baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ aya nɔ eda lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines to climb up wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makudɔ sweet potato wain tso ko koni ekwɔ tso tso ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to create energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sunlight, which increases tuber size and prevents leaf rot diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tuber lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around crop roots with dry grass during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves (mulching) acts like a blanket. It shades the soil from hot sun, stops soil water from evaporating quickly, and keeps the roots cool so the crop survives hot spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii anyɛ ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli.

english: Young cocoa plants suffer from excessive sunlight and heat, which causes water loss faster than the roots can pull from the soil. Providing shade crops like plantains or shade trees helps reduce heat stress and keeps moisture around the leaves so they don't burn.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine kɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ha lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔle baai lɛ ahe lɛ akashã.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow starting from the middle while the outer edges stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ be mli ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the central leaf vein is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in maize. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed compost early in the growth cycle helps restore dark green leaves and supports healthy stalk growth.
ga: Yellowing ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ fãji lɛ ahe lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ ŋmãa mli. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ shishijee mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba, ni eye ebua ni ewaje tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: How do I know if my cassava plants are putting energy into growing big tubers under the ground instead of just growing tall leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu baai kakadaji kɛkɛ?

english: When cassava plants receive balanced nutrients and adequate sunlight without excessive nitrogen, they shift energy to root growth. Thickening stem bases and steady growth without overgrown top leaves indicate that the plant is successfully storing food in its underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ná niyenii ni sa kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni nitrogen babaoo bɛ mli lɛ, Etsakeɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Tso shishi ni mli wa kɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni ŋwɛi baai ni edaaa fe nine bɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ nyɛ ekɛ niyenii to eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Why do caterpillars attack the hidden inner leaves inside the central funnel of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mligbɛ baai ni akɛtee mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworm prefer the tender inner leaves inside the plant funnel because they are moist, soft to eat, and protected from direct sunlight and predators. Treatments must be directed directly into the center funnel of the plant to effectively reach them.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ sumɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Yɛ hulutsoo be hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ blɛoo ni ayeɔ ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe. Esa akɛ atsɔɔ tsofa lɛ gbɛ kɛya tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli koni anyɛ ashɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when plants experience extreme dry spells followed by heavy watering. Extreme heat damages the pollen, preventing fertilization, so maintaining steady soil moisture and light shade during heatwaves helps fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa kpeɔ ni nu ni mli wa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I remove extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Extra shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain mother plant for water, light, and soil nutrients, which reduces the size of the ultimate fruit bunch. Keeping only one or two strong suckers allows the mother plant to focus its energy on producing a large harvest.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine (tsoji) kɛ tso nyɛ titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha naagbee kuu lɛ dalɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hi shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early stops the leaves from crumpling and allows normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to guide and stake my yam vines on tall poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔɔ gbɛ ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei ama tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight without being shaded by weeds or rotting from wet ground contact. Staking keeps leaves healthy and photosynthesizing, which directly boosts the size of the yam tuber underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni jwɛi akafee amɛ shade loo amɛkafite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ fotosintɛtik. ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea and groundnut roots have small round bumps on them when I pull them out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea kɛ mi-peanut shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Beni mijieɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Those tiny bumps are root nodules containing beneficial bacteria that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food. This natural process feeds the crop and leaves extra nitrogen behind to enrich the soil for future crops.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji shishifãi ni mli ewo muji ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii ni eshiɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop down during the hot afternoon sun but stand up straight again by the next morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ enɔ jetsɛremɔ.

english: Drooping in afternoon heat is a temporary defense mechanism where the plant closes leaf pores to prevent losing water too fast. Once the sun sets and temperatures cool down, the roots absorb enough water overnight to restore leaf strength by morning.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ ji be kukuoo mli hebuu gbɛ. He ni tsei tsiɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni nu akafite oya tsɔ. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nyɔɔŋ kome koni eha baai ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ leebi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without any bigger shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides living umbrellas that keep the soil moist and protect the cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaabu kookoo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaakwɛ̃.

english: Which part of the cassava stem should I cut to plant if I want to get a good yield of tubers?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ mafo ni madu kɛji miisumɔ ni maná ŋmeii kpakpai?

english: You should use the hard, mature middle section of a healthy cassava stem, cut into pieces about 20 to 30 centimeters long. Avoid the soft green tips at the top and the very base of the stem.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɛ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii. Kpɔ̃ɔ mli bibii ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain can be misleading, and the soil might dry out quickly if a dry spell follows. Waiting for two or three steady rains ensures there is enough moisture deep in the soil so your seeds don't germinate and then dry up.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi oya kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Koni dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they could rot and exposes them to full sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ ni ebaaha hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: Can I pick any small shoot growing around my plantain tree to plant elsewhere, or are some shoots better than others?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii. growing around Ani abaanyɛ adu mi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he kroko? Aloo ani ŋmeii komɛi hi fe ekrokomɛi?

english: You should choose 'sword suckers', which have narrow leaves and a strong, wide base. Avoid 'water suckers' with broad leaves early on, as they grow into weak plants that yield small bunches.
ga: Halamɔ ‘sword shoot’ ni yɔɔ baai bibii kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ‘sucker shoot’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ he mra. Ejaakɛ edaa ni etsɔɔ tso ni he waaa ni woɔ yibii kui bibii.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before turning into actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛbatsɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme dry soil. Giving the plants consistent water and mulching the base helps keep the root zone cool so the flowers stay on.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in an inverted 'V' shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the tip down the middle of lower maize leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or decomposed poultry manure will help the plant regain its green color.
ga: Yellow ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi kɛyaa shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmɔŋ ni egbo fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year without changing crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi ni mitsakeee ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot rapidly drains the soil of specific nutrients like nitrogen and lets pests multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnut helps restore nitrogen naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ

english: Why should I dry and store fresh chicken manure before putting it on my crop beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi ni mabua tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee naa dani mikɛwo midumɔ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is 'hot' and high in ammonia, which can burn plant roots and carry harmful germs. Allowing it to dry and decompose breaks down the strong chemicals so crops can safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ ‘dɔ’ ni ammonia fa yɛ mli. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ oshara aba Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbi ni efite lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akumɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ bu ni ekpɔtɔ ni akɛtee ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the growing tip of maize. Checking plants early and applying targeted neem extracts or recommended insecticides into the shoot center helps stop them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni akwɛɔ yɛ tsei amli mra Ni akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ bud centers lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni akpa amɛ.

english: Why do I need to mix water into sandy soil when preparing a seedbed for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ nu afutu shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ mli beni miisaa dumɔwui ashishi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Sandy soil loses moisture very quickly. Adding water while preparing the bed helps bind the loose sand grains together so tender roots can anchor securely and easily absorb nutrients without drying out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa. Nu ni akɛbaafata he beni asaa saatso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋã ni egbɔjɔ lɛ akpɛtɛ he. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: What makes light, sandy soil hold onto water better so my seedlings do not dry up?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ ni tsiimɔ waaa ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ? Bɔni afee ni midumɔwui lɛ akagbi

english: Sand grains are large and let water drain fast. Adding organic compost along with water creates a spongy mix that traps moisture around plant roots, keeping them hydrated throughout the day.
ga: Ŋshɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ dara ni ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he kɛfata nu he lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ewo muji ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ baa, ni ehaa tsei lɛ náa nu yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Can using water contaminated with farm chemicals harm my crop roots?
ga: Ani nu ni tsofai yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ awui?

english: Yes, water containing harsh agrochemicals can burn soft feeder roots, stunt growth, and prevent the crop from drinking up clean moisture, causing the plant to wilt even if the soil is wet.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni okwaayeli mli tsofai ni mli wa yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã niyenii ni mli jɔ lɛ ashishifãi. eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni eha tsei lɛ akaŋɔ nu ni mli tse. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: How do I know if the river or well water I use for my farm is damaging my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji faa loo nu bu mli nu ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: If crop leaves suddenly turn yellow, scorch at the tips, or curl up shortly after watering, your water source may contain harmful chemical runoff, excess salts, or pollutants.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa lɛ Shãa loo efoɔ enaagbee lɛ beni awo lɛ nu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Ekolɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni hoɔ yɛ nu ni okɛhaa lɛ mli. Nu loo mujiwoo ni fa fe nine

english: Why do my young seedlings rot and collapse at the stem level when the ground stays wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛkuɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ tso lɛ shishi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Excess water in warm soil creates an environment where harmful fungi thrive, causing 'damping-off' disease that rots the tender stems of young seedlings before they grow strong.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ko ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa yɛ mli lɛ baa, ni ekɛ hela ni ji ‘fɔmɔ’ ni haa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa waa lɛ baa.

english: How can I keep small soil pests and organisms from destroying my seedling nursery?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite mi ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Maintaining proper soil drainage, avoiding over-watering, and using recommended organic or chemical soil treatments kills harmful pests while protecting tender root growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ he. kɛ sũ ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he ŋaawoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ adalɛ he.

english: Why do crop leaves look scorched if I spray liquid fertilizer on them on a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã kɛji mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Droplets of chemical liquid on leaves act like tiny magnifying glasses under strong sunlight, causing intense heat that burns and damages the delicate surface of the plant.
ga: Tsofa mli nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Enɛ haa dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni shãa ni efiteɔ tsei lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baa.

english: What should I do if I accidentally apply too much chemical liquid to my young crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni ji nu babaoo tsu nii yɛ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ oshara mli?

english: Immediately flush the plants and surrounding soil with plenty of clean, fresh water to dilute the chemical concentration before it causes severe root burn or kills the crop.
ga: Oya nɔŋŋ ni okɛ nu ni mli tse babaoo afɔ tso lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ koni tsofa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee mlɛo dani eshã shishifãi lɛ waa loo egbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I protect my crop field if chemical runoff from a nearby farm washes in after rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he? Kɛji tsofai ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ hoɔ kɛbaa yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ

english: Dig shallow drainage ditches around your field boundary to divert dirty runoff water away, and flush affected beds with clean water to rinse chemical residues out of the root zone.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he koni okɛ nu ni hoɔ ni he tseee lɛ akudɔ. Ni okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ saatso ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ nɔ koni tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ ajie.

english: How do I help my crops recover after they suffer severe shock from bad water or chemical burns?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ waa yɛ be mli ni amɛna shoofeemɔ ni naa wa kɛjɛ nu ni mli ewo muji loo tsofai ni akɛshãa lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Shade the damaged plants from harsh direct sunlight, flush the soil with clean water, and hold off on applying any strong fertilizers until the plants sprout fresh, healthy green leaves.
ga: Shade tsei ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ baai ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: I want to start planting cocoa on my land this year, but how long will I have to wait before the trees start giving me pods?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi kookoo dumɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi nɛɛ. Shi be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani tso lɛ aje shishi ewo ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa trees usually take 3 to 5 years to start bearing fruit, but improved hybrid varieties can begin producing pods in about 2 to 3 years if they receive proper shade, water, and care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema cacao tsei lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi hybrid henɔi ni atsake amɛ lɛ baanyɛ aje pods feemɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji amɛná hulutsoo, nu kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside young cocoa keeps the soil cool and moist, protecting the young plants from drying out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Buu tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: My neighbor gets many more bags of cocoa than me even though our farms are side by side; what could cause this difference?
ga: Mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa kookoo kotokui babaoo fe mi eyɛ mli akɛ wɔŋmɔji lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe moŋ. Mɛni kɛ srɔtofeemɔ nɛɛ baa?

english: Higher cocoa yields depend on consistent maintenance practices, such as regular pruning, timely weeding, applying the right fertilizer to feed the soil, and spraying approved chemicals to control pests and diseases.
ga: Kookoo yibii babaoo damɔ saamɔ nifeemɔi ni yaa nɔ daa, tamɔ tsei ni afoɔ daa lɛ nɔ. jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa mli Nibii ni sa ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ koni akɛkudɔ jwɛi kɛ helai.

english: Can I just buy any chemical sold at the local store to spray on my cocoa trees when they look sick?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahe tsofai ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ shwapoi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ koni mikɛshwie mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛtamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ?
