english: No, you should only use government-approved agrochemicals specifically made for cocoa. Using unapproved or fake chemicals can damage your trees, destroy friendly insects, or leave harmful chemical residues in your cocoa beans.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okɛ agrochemicals ni nɔyeli lɛ kpɛlɛ nɔ ni afee aha kookoo pɛ atsu nii. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ loo amalei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite tsei. Kpatamɔ kooloi ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo lɛ ahiɛ. Aloo amɛbaanyɛ amɛshi tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ kookoo yibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off the tree before turning into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛtsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔji diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree is attacked by sap-sucking insects like mirids, affected by fungal diseases, or lacks necessary soil nutrients and water. Proper pest control and soil feeding help flowers stay on the tree and develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ ji kooloi ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ mirids, ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ yeɔ enɔ. loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do people advise me to cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa tree if I want to get more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mifolɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni maná ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary or overcrowding branches so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree. This reduces fungal diseases and allows the tree to direct its energy into growing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni eha kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs fertilizer or if my cocoa trees are just naturally weak?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli?

english: If your mature cocoa trees have pale yellow leaves, grow slowly, or produce very few small pods despite getting enough rain, the soil is likely exhausted of nutrients and needs cocoa-specific fertilizer to replenish it.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cacao tso ko ni eda lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, edaa blɛoo, loo ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ, Etamɔ nɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hu faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe baahia ni akɛ cacao ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning excess branches to let air flow, and spraying approved fungicides before the heavy rains start will protect your pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aje shishi lɛ baaye abua ni ebu o-pods lɛ ahe.

english: There are agricultural input companies offering products in our village; how can working with them benefit my farm?
ga: Nitsumɔhe ko ni feɔ okwaayeli nibii ni akɛ nibii haa lɛ yɛ wɔ akrowa lɛ mli. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Reputable agricultural companies provide genuine, high-quality fertilizers and crop protection products, along with training on correct application methods so you get maximum crop yield for the money you invest.
ga: Okwaayeli nitsumɔhei ni ehe gbɛi lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji anɔkwale ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ haa. kɛfata tsɔsemɔ ni kɔɔ bɔ ni akɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ he Bɔni afee ni onine ashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe fɛɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ mli.

english: Why is it harmful to let tall weeds grow around the stems of my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle he? No hewɔ lɛ mi-kookoo tso ni eda lɛ shishifã lɛ yɛ oshara.

english: Tall weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients away from your cocoa trees. They also trap humidity around the trunk and harbor insect pests and fungal diseases that can damage your crop.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ hu. Shishifãi lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ afite onibii lɛ yɔɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my yellow maize turning yellow and drying up before the crop is even ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani tso lɛ po feɔ klalo akɛ ebaakpa lɛ?

english: This yellowing usually means your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. When nitrogen is short in the soil, the plant steals it from older lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my hot pepper plants drop all their flowers instead of turning them into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from high heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Ensuring regular watering during dry spells and applying compost or balanced fertilizer before flowering helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa atsu nii dani fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ koni eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What causes the leaves on my tomato plants to curl up tightly and turn pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by the Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early and removing heavily infected plants stops the disease from spreading through your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, ni ji ŋmeii yɛŋ bibioo ko lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli. Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Mra Ni tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily during small rains even when the stem is not broken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo po mli lɛ? Ni tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ efoko?

english: When plantain trees easily fall over, tiny worms called nematodes or plantain root borers have destroyed the underground root system. Without strong roots anchored in the ground, the heavy plantain tree cannot support its own weight during light wind or rain.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ gbee shi oya lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ Dumɔwui ni tsii nyɛŋ akwɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ muji lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli.

english: Why are tiny insects chewing holes in my cowpea leaves and flowers before the pods even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-cowpea baai kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli dani ŋmeii lɛ po feɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea crops are very attractive to pests like aphids and pod borers at the flowering stage. These pests feed on fresh leaves and blossoms, so applying organic or approved insect control right before and during flowering protects the crop so pods can grow.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ aphids kɛ pod borers waa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baai kɛ fɔfɔi heei. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛyeɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ tsu nii dani fɔfɔii lɛ baa kɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt and die during the hot afternoon sun even though I watered the farm in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni amɛgbooo lɛ? Namɔ shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi?

english: This sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by bacterial wilt or root-knot nematodes attacking the roots. Damaged roots lose the ability to pump water up to the leaves when the sun is hot, causing the plant to dry up despite moist soil.
ga: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilting or nematodes attacking the roots. Damaged roots lose their ability to pump water up the leaves when exposed to hot sunlight. Ha tsei lɛ agbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ po.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the ground before I dig them up for market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani atsaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when the soil stays too wet for too long or when rot-causing fungi attack the roots in poorly drained land. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava root rot occurs when the soil is too wet for too long. aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ tutua shishifãi yɛ hei ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my harvested seed yams start shooting sprouts too early while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shweremɔ oya tsɔ beni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Seed yams break dormancy and sprout early when the storage barn gets too warm or humid. Keeping the barn well-ventilated, shady, and cool delays sprouting so the seed yams remain fresh until the next planting season.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baawɔ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ oya kɛ́ shĩa lɛ mli edɔ loo edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ bɔni afee ni sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi ehee kɛyashi be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers but fail to grow into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ miiwo fɔfɔii babaoo shi edaaa kwraa ni etsɔɔɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need tiny beneficial insects called midges to carry pollen from flower to flower so pods can form. Excessive farm spraying with non-targeted chemicals or heavy shade removal kills these insects, leading to poor pod formation.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge koni ekɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ koni pods afee. Tsofai ni akɛtsuuu nii loo hulutsoo ni tsii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔji amli fe nine lɛ baagbe nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. Enɛ haaa pod lɛ afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize farm after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛwo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ sɛɛ?

english: The best approach is split application: apply the first round of fertilizer about 10 to 14 days after seedlings emerge to build roots, and apply the second round when the maize reaches knee-high to boost stalk strength and cob formation.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojara mli: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ koni amɛfee shishifãi lɛ. Ni okɛ kpokpaa ni ji enyɔ lɛ atsu nii beni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe lɛ koni eha ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa lɛ feemɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the large trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains, as well as permanent canopy trees, to shield their tender leaves and maintain soil moisture while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛbiɔ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛ agbɛnɛ hu tsei ni kwɛɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɔ shi daa lɛ adɛŋ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my land is suitable for planting cocoa before I spend money on seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ dani mafite shika yɛ dumɔwui ahe?

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, dark, and rich in organic matter, holding moisture well without becoming waterlogged. You can test your land by checking for good drainage and consulting a local extension officer to inspect soil depth and quality.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ nu shwieee shi. Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ maŋ lɛ mli nitsulɔ ko ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it safe to plant food crops like cassava and plantain on the same field with my new cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ niyenii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-cacao tsei heei lɛ?

english: Yes, planting plantains and fast-growing food crops alongside young cocoa provides vital shade and weed control. It also gives you food and income while you wait for the cocoa trees to mature, as long as crops aren't planted too close to crowd the cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains kɛ niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ jwɛi ni akudɔ. Ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika hu yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ. Shii abɔ ni aduuu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo lɛ tsɔ lɛ,.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before turning into young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔii dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Flower dropping usually happens when the tree experiences stress from drought, poor soil nutrients, or pest attacks. Ensuring adequate shade, moist soil, and proper soil nutrients helps the tree retain its flowers so they can develop into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ kpe. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akwɛ koni aná hulutsoo ni sa, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and growing slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida blɛoo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves typically indicate that the plant is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen or is sitting in waterlogged soil. Applying balanced fertilizer and improving field drainage will restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii ni aha nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How many times in a year should I expect my cocoa trees to produce pods in Ghana?
ga: Pods enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ cacao tso ko baawo yɛ afi mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Cocoa trees in Ghana generally have two main harvest periods each year: the main crop season, which runs from September to March with high yields, and the minor crop season, which runs from May to August.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be titrii enyɔ daa afi: be titri ni akɛkpaa lɛ, ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ September kɛyashiɔ March, be mli ni anáa nii babaoo lɛ; kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ ni ji enyɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ May kɛyashiɔ August lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while still attached to the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads during cool, wet weather. Pruning extra canopy branches to allow sunlight and airflow, harvesting ripe pods promptly, and removing infected pods helps prevent its spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ mli. Afolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ ahe koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Nibii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ Ni ajieɔ nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ naa.

english: How much distance should I leave between my cocoa plants when putting them in the ground?
ga: He enyiɛ esa akɛ makɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: The standard recommended spacing for cocoa is 3 meters by 3 meters (10 feet by 10 feet). This gives each tree enough room to spread its branches and root system without competing with neighboring trees for light and nutrients.
ga: Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akɛto kookoo he lɛ ji mitai 3 x mitai 3 (naji 10 x naji 10), ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ eniji kɛ eshishifãi lɛ agbɛɔ eshwaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ kɛha la kɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it bad for my cocoa farm if rainwater collects and sits on the land for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ ehiii kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cocoa roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits on the land for long periods, it drowns the roots, leading to root rot, falling leaves, and eventual tree death.
ga: Cocoa shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting before my new cocoa farm starts yielding pods?
ga: Kɛ́ adu agbe naa lɛ, be enyiɛ ehe baahia ni emɛ dani kookoo ŋmɔ hee ko aje ŋmɔshi nibii afeemɔ shishi?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually begin producing flowers and pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years to yield their first crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ahe shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛfeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves start curling up and turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by heat stress, lack of consistent soil moisture, or tiny insects like whiteflies that spread viruses. Keeping the soil covered with mulch and providing water at the root level helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ he haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa yɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my young crop shoots grow tall and thin instead of thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ miidara ni amɛmiifee mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Plants grow tall and skinny when they are competing for sunlight because they are planted too close together or shaded by larger trees. Giving each plant proper spacing allows enough light to reach them so they grow sturdy stems.
ga: Tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ́ amɛmiitswa hulu la he akaŋ ejaakɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo tsei wuji tsiɔ amɛnaa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaha la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ he koni eshishifã lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds blow through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not anchor deeply in the soil. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the plant becomes top-heavy, so supporting the stem with a bamboo or wooden prop keeps it from falling over before harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni eshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ da Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei loo tsei fĩ tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbee shi dani akpa.

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking so long to produce fruit after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains need rich soil high in organic matter and regular moisture to fruit quickly. If you leave too many suckers attached to one parent plant, they steal nutrients from each other, which delays fruit development.
ga: Plantains he miihia shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa koni ewo yibii oya. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ fɔlɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ, Ebaaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei krokomɛi amli. Enɛ baaha nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining steady water supply and mulching the root area helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Nu jɛɛhe ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ shishifãi lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my ripe tomatoes rotting from the bottom before I can even pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miifite kɛmiijɛ tsɛnsi lɛ shishi dani manyɛ maŋɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: This is usually blossom-end rot, caused by a calcium shortage in the plant due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady so the roots can continuously draw up nutrients stops the fruit bottoms from turning black.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ baatsi aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same plot of land without harming my yield?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni enaaa miŋmɔmɔ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works very well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, leaving space and light for the slower-growing cassava to expand afterwards.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Kɛtsɔ he ko ni ashiɔ kɛ la ni haa ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo ni sɛɛ mli lɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I tell if my crops are suffering from lack of water or lack of fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu efo miŋmɔshi nibii amli loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves wilt and droop during the afternoon heat but bounce back in the evening. When crops lack nutrients, the leaves permanently change color—turning yellow or pale—even when the soil is moist.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ bɛ nu lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa gbɛkɛ mli. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ Baai lɛ baatsake su kɛya naanɔ—ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ—kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do small worms eat holes in my young maize leaves right after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli beni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which attack young, tender maize leaves early in the season. Checking the center funnel of young plants regularly and applying recommended controls early protects the crop from severe damage.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii, bibii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Nibii ni yɔɔ tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ daa kɛ nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Ebaabu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite waa.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly while I am taking them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛtee jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes spoil rapidly if harvested fully ripe under hot midday sun or stacked in deep, heavy containers that crush the bottom fruit. Harvesting slightly firm tomatoes early in the morning and using well-ventilated baskets prevents bruising and rot.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi. Aloo okɛto tsɛnsii ni mli kwɔ ni tsii amli koni okɛkumɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tomato ni mli wa fioo lɛ shwie shi leebi ni okɛ tsɛnsi ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why should I talk to an agricultural officer before buying chemical medicine for my sick crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko agba sane dani mahe tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Using the wrong chemical medicine or incorrect dosage can ruin your soil, burn your plants, or make the food unsafe to eat. An extension officer helps identify the exact problem so you use the right medicine safely.
ga: Tsofa ni ejaaa loo falɛ ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ, ashã tsei, loo eha niyenii afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ helatsamɔhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛyɔseɔ naagba lɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni onyɛ okɛ tsofa ni sa lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe.

english: Why shouldn't I mix two different crop medicines together in the same sprayer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ futuɔ tsɔne kome mli lɛ?

english: Mixing chemicals without expert guidance can cause a reaction that cancels out their strength, destroys your crop leaves, or creates toxic fumes that harm your health.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ŋaawolɔi komɛi bɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai lɛ amli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aba shi. Kpata oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ ahiɛ loo feemɔ lasu ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yeɔ ohewalɛ nɔ awui

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni awo mli ŋmãa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves can turn yellow if the soil has too much water, which prevents roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients, or if the fertilizer was applied when the soil was too dry.
ga: Abɛi baai baanyɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning pale during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl to conserve water during dry heat, but if severe, it can be a sign of mosaic disease spread by small insects like whiteflies.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ nu mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Shi kɛji akɛ edɔ waa lɛ Ebaanyɛ efee mosaic hela ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi.

english: Why do my bean plants drop their flowers without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Bean plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or lack water, shedding flowers to save energy when conditions are tough.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ lɛ kpe. Fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ koni akɛto hewalɛ he yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and die even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil often means root rot caused by a waterborne fungus or bacteria, which prevents roots from bringing water up to the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu kɛyashɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and twisted instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become misshapen when planted in hard, rocky soil because the roots cannot easily push outward and expand deep into the ground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ kponɔgbɛ oya ni amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year if I do not let it rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi kɛji mihaaa ejɔɔ ehe lɛ?

english: Planting continuously without resting the soil drains its natural food reserves, leaving future crops weak and undernourished unless nutrients are replaced.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii ni aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni eyɔɔ lɛ ajɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnáaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ja akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ tsake.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves have fresh holes in them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ náa bulɛi heei daa leebi lɛ?

english: Night-feeding insects like armyworms, beetles, and snails hide from the hot sun during the day and feed on leaves when it cools down at night.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kooloi tamɔ armyworms, ladybugs kɛ snails teɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ baai lɛ kɛ́ edɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts between their rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting like natural fertilizer that helps the neighboring maize grow strong.
ga: Peanut tsei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my piece of land is better suited for planting maize or cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Different crops prefer different types of ground. Maize needs deep, rich soil that holds moisture and nutrients well, while cassava is very hardy and can yield well even in dry, sandy, or less fertile soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmãa. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmei wa waa, ni ebaanyɛ ewo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni baaa yibii babaoo lɛ po nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to support a good harvest before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua nikpamɔ kpakpa dani madu nii?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, feels crumbly when squeezed, stays moist without turning into swampy mud, and has earthworms or small bugs living inside it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Enuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ kɛ́ amɔ lɛ Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii hiɔ mli

english: Why do my crops grow well on one side of my farm but struggle on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fa kome shi amɛmiibɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ fa kroko lɛ?

english: Soil depth, water drainage, and nutrient levels can change across the same plot of land. One area might hold too much water or have rocky underground layers that stop roots from spreading.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ he kome lɛ fɛɛ. Ekolɛ nu babaoo yɛ he ko loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and snap off during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry, dusty harmattan winds pull moisture out of plantain leaves much faster than the roots can drink water from dry soil, causing the leaves to dry out and collapse.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ plantain baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before turning into pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛtsɔ pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot weather, inconsistent water supply, or a lack of key nutrients in the soil needed to build fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai afeemɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stop growing after heavy rain sits on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpa kwɛ̃mɔ beni nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When rain waterlogged the soil and cannot drain away, crop roots get choked because they cannot breathe oxygen or absorb nutrients, causing leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, sũ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he ni enyɛɛɛ eho kɛje kpo. Tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa loo amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why does planting the exact same crop on my farm every year make my yields smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same soil nutrients every season and gives plant pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply in the land.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai náa shia ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli daa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farmland better for my next crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural, free fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ehe kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot underground before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa amɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when planted in low land where water settles and stays wet, allowing fungal diseases to attack the tubers in the damp soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu eyi mli obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and rot during the wet months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that thrives in cold, wet, and shady conditions where air cannot flow freely around the cocoa trees to dry off the moisture.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle amɛhe lɛ. Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ heyeli koni amɛgbi ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build healthy leaves. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the new growth at the top to stay alive, showing you that the soil needs fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni wa Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Etsɔɔ bo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight cups and stopping green growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛmiikpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out plant sap, or by viruses spread by these insects. Spraying neem oil solution or insecticidal soap helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily burn or dry out. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa plants while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la he waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã loo amɛgbi oya. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin with small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops must compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The stalks stretch tall to reach sunlight instead of spending energy to build strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei ni wa kɛ tsei wuji lɛ, tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to conserve water. By losing leaves, the plant stops losing moisture through evaporation, keeping its roots alive under the ground until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛbu nu he. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ haaa tso lɛ mli nu lɛ afite kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni eha eshishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when day or night temperatures get too high because extreme heat prevents successful pollination inside the flower. Keeping the soil cool with mulch and watering regularly helps lower heat stress.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ejaakɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ baatsi pollination ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa koni ekaye omanye. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo he haomɔ aba shi.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning dark brown or black and rotting during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning dense branches to let in air and sunlight and harvesting ripe pods quickly prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ mli babaoo koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Ni kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ oya lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are there holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ yɛ bu ko ni akɛtee teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that burrows into the growing center (the 'whorl') of maize plants to feed. Applying targeted biopesticides or ash into the whorl early in the morning can help destroy the caterpillars.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei ("rings") lɛ amli koni eye niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo sũ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ wo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni efite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread flat on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb poles so their leaves can get maximum sunlight to create food for the roots. Staking prevents leaves from rotting on wet soil and ensures all energy goes into growing large tubers below ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛbaa lɛ aná hulu la babaoo koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shishifãi lɛ. Staking tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. ni ekwɛɔ koni hewalɛ fɛɛ aya ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over right when the fruit bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi trukaa beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems. When a bunch grows large, the top heavy weight, combined with strong winds or microscopic root parasites (nematodes), easily pulls the plant out of the ground unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa. Kɛji akɛ kuu lɛ da Top heavy weight ni akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shishifãi bibii ni kwɛɔ nii amli lɛ fataa he. (Nematodes) lɛ gbalaa tsei kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. ja tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ

english: How do I know if a new seed variety will actually grow well on my farm before I buy it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui heei baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mahe?

english: Before recommended seed varieties are sold in shops, agricultural researchers test them across different soil types and rainfall zones in Ghana. When you buy certified seed varieties meant for your district, you are using seeds that have already been proven to thrive in your area.
ga: Dani abaahɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni ajie yi lɛ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ, okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi lɛ baaka dumɔwui nɛɛ amɛkwɛ yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ. kɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ yɛ Ghana Kɛji ohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛha okpokpaa lɛ Okɛ dumɔwui ni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsu nii.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from an agro-input shop instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe shwapo mli moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Seeds saved from past harvests gradually lose their vigor, attract pests, and produce smaller yields every season. Certified seeds bought from authorized shops are specifically tested and treated to give high germination rates, resist diseases, and produce much larger harvests.
ga: Seeds collected from past harvests will gradually grow. hewalɛ ni elaaje Gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ehaaa yibii babaoo aba daa be mli Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ shwapoi ni aŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ amli lɛ akwɛɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni eha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ babaoo, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some of my crop seeds fail to sprout even after I water the land properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ nu ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds can fail to sprout if they are damaged by pests, stored in hot places, or too old. Using tested and certified seeds ensures high germination because only good quality, healthy seeds are packed for farmers.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai efite amɛ. Okɛto he ko ni mli edɔ. or too old Using tested and certified seeds ensures high germination. This is because farmers package only good and healthy seeds.

english: How can I tell which crop variety is best suited for the rain patterns in my region?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei srɔtoi ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops are bred for different growing periods. If your district gets short rains, early-maturing varieties finish growing quickly before the dry season hits, while long-duration varieties require areas with extended rainy seasons to yield fully.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei yɛ bei srɔtoi ni amɛdaraa lɛ anaa. Kɛji akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ daa oya dani hulutsoo be lɛ baashɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ biɔ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: What does it mean when a seed variety is called 'drought-tolerant', and how will it help me?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni atsɛɔ dumɔwu ko akɛ ‘enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa’ lɛ shishi? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua bo?

english: Drought-tolerant crop varieties are developed to survive dry spells by growing deeper roots or using less water. They protect your investment by still producing a decent harvest even if the rain stops unexpectedly during the season.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo nu fioo ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Amɛbuɔ oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ he kɛtsɔ yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛhaa lolo lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ be lɛ mli po.

english: Why do crops of the same type perform differently when planted in different fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komekomei lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ lɛ?

english: Crops respond to local soil nutrients, water drainage, and sunlight. A crop variety tested for sandy or loamy soils will perform better in those specific conditions than in heavy clay soil that holds too much water.
ga: Tsei hereɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nu ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la nɔ. Tsei srɔtoi ni aka amɛ akwɛ yɛ ŋã loo sũ mli sũi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli fe shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni tsii ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my neighbor get a higher yield than me even though we planted our crops on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa yibii babaoo fe mi eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Higher yields depend on using high-yielding certified seed varieties, correct plant spacing, and proper soil management. Improved seeds are specifically bred to convert soil nutrients into heavier grain or fruit far better than uncertified seeds.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ damɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ odaseyeli he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni ja kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ekɛtsake niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ewo dumɔwui loo aduawai ni tsii fe dumɔwui ni atsuuu he nii.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants start turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen or that heavy rains have waterlogged the soil, preventing roots from breathing. Using balanced fertilizers and ensuring field drainage helps keep plants green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otsei lɛ amli, loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Nibii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How does chemical seed coating help my crops grow better after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seed coatings contain protective treatments that act like a shield against soil insects, birds, and fungal diseases during the critical early days in the ground, allowing seedling roots to establish safely.
ga: Nɔ ni fata dumɔwui ahe nibii ahe ji tsofa ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi, okpoi kɛ mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛma shi shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I prevent diseases from ruining my farm yield before harvest time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi hela naa koni ekafite miŋmɔ mli nibii lɛ dani kpamɔ be ashɛ?

english: The best defense is planting disease-resistant crop varieties that have been tested to fight off local plant viruses and fungi. Inspecting your farm regularly also lets you catch and treat early signs of pest attack before damage spreads.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa ji ni adu tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni amɛkɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii awuu yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ daa lɛ hu yeɔ ebua bo ni omɔɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutua bo lɛ mra dani nɔ ni efite lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What is pollination, and why is it important for my cocoa trees to make pods?
ga: Mɛni ji pollination? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ afee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Pollination is how plants reproduce. For cocoa, tiny insects transfer pollen from one flower to another so the tree can fertilize them and turn those small flowers into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Pollination ji bɔ ni tsei fɔɔ amɛbii. Kɛha kookoo lɛ, kooloi bibii jieɔ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ afɔ ni amɛfee fɔfɔi bibii. Mɛi ni yɔɔ kookoo pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ.

english: I hear other farmers talk about hand pollination for cocoa; how does doing it by hand actually help my farm?
ga: Minu okwaafoi krokomɛi Awieɔ nine ni akɛwoɔ kookoo mli lɛ he. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nitsumɔi ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Hand pollination means manually moving pollen to cocoa flowers using tiny brushes or tweezers. This ensures that almost every targeted flower becomes a pod, which can significantly increase your harvest compared to relying only on natural insects.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, akɛ brɔsh bibioo loo tweezers baatsɔ nine nɔ ajie pollen lɛ kɛya kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi ni akɛma hiɛ lɛ baatsɔ pod. Enɛ baanyɛ aha nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ aya hiɛ waa. Kɛ akɛto adebɔɔ mli kooloi pɛ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ he

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage get pollinated or receive enough water and food. Unpollinated or weak flowers dry up and fall off so the tree can save its energy.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ ji mɛi ni shwieɔ amɛhe loo amɛnáa nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Fɔfɔi ni bɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Once a cocoa flower is successfully pollinated, how long does it take to grow into a pod ready for harvesting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ye omanye yɛ pollination mli lɛ Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani edara ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni asaa he kɛha kpamɔ?

english: It usually takes about 5 to 6 months from the time a cocoa flower is pollinated for it to develop and mature into a full, ripe cocoa pod ready for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ baa. No sɛɛ lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daa ni amɛshwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni asaa he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How old does my young cocoa tree need to be before it starts producing its first flowers and pods?
ga: Esa akɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ aye afii enyiɛ dani amɛje amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔii kɛ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ afeemɔ shishi?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana usually start flowering and producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties can take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: How does heavy rain during the flowering season affect the flowers on my cocoa trees?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ saa mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rainfall can knock delicate flowers off the branches or make it difficult for tiny pollinating midges to fly, which can reduce the number of pods that form during wet periods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbo kɛjɛ tsei aniji anɔ loo eha ewa aha kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ akɛ amɛaafã, ni baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni feɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my small growing cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So mine lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Small pods often turn black and shrivel due to fungal infections like Black Pod disease, or because the tree lacks sufficient water and nutrients to feed all the pods at the same time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe hela ko, tamɔ ŋmeii diji hela hewɔ, loo akɛni tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ aye abua yɛ be kome mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: How does cutting off excess branches help my cocoa tree produce more healthy pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ni cacao tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Pruning lets more sunlight and air flow through the branches, which reduces high humidity that causes disease. It also helps the tree direct more nutrients directly into flower and pod growth.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo tsɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo ni baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ hu ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Do cocoa trees need full sunlight or shade to produce the best flowers and pods?
ga: Ani hulu loo hulutsoo be babaoo he miihia kookoo tsei kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Cocoa trees prefer moderate shade, receiving around 30 to 50 percent sunlight. Too much shade limits flower production, while too much direct sun can stress the tree and cause flowers to drop.
ga: Cocoa tsei sumɔɔ hulutsoo be ni sa. Amɛnáa hulu aaafee oha mlijaa 30 kɛyashi 50. Shade babaoo haaa fɔfɔii afeemɔ aya hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ ni eha efɔfɔi lɛ agbo.

english: What kind of nourishment or fertilizer should I give my cocoa trees so they hold onto their flowers?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo niyenii esa akɛ aha kookoo tso lɛ koni ewo fɔfɔi?

english: Cocoa trees need rich nutrients, especially phosphorus and potassium, during the flowering stage. Applying recommended cocoa fertilizers before the main flowering season helps trees hold flowers and grow healthy pods.
ga: Niyenii babaoo he miihia cacao tsei. Titri lɛ, fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ wo tso lɛ mli dani fɔfɔii afeemɔ be titri lɛ aba lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ fɔfɔi ni mli wa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food they need to grow strong. It can also happen if the soil is too waterlogged, which suffocates the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or dry, or if the plant lacks water during flowering. When heat stress occurs, the plant cannot properly fertilize the flowers to form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Be mli ni dɔlɛ he haomɔ ba lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do young cocoa trees grow better under shade trees instead of direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ fe hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense heat. Shade trees protect them from harsh sunlight and help keep the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge leafy tops but yield very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa yitsei wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: If cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted in soil extremely rich in organic waste, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of storing food in its roots.
ga: If cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or is grown in soil with a lot of organic waste. Plants use up all the energy they use to grow leaves and stems. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding under the leaves and sucking out plant sap, or by viruses spread by those same pests.
ga: Leaf curling in peppers is often caused by tiny insects such as thrips or whiteflies hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's sap. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ nɔŋŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my plantain suckers too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting plantains too close together forces them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stems that easily blow down in storms and produce very small bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ahum tswaa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why do my vegetable crops look droopy in the afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. They temporarily wilt to save water and usually recover by evening when temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛsumɔɔɔ ni amɛtoɔ nu he be kukuoo ko ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops when they are growing in the same farm?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for the fertilizer, water, and sunlight available in the field. When weeds take over, your crops stay weak and stunted because they are starved of nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ ye nɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food that builds big tubers. Raising the vines on stakes helps all the leaves catch sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji. Wein tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la, ni ehaaa helai aba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer in the same hole as my seeds on the day I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ bu kome mli kɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ gbi ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds do not have roots yet to feed on fertilizer. Placing strong fertilizer directly against fresh seeds can burn and destroy the tender seeds before they get the chance to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni baawo ŋmɔshi nibii lolo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo dumɔwui heei amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã ni egbe dumɔwui bibii lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small ears when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛtoi bibii yɔɔ mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants waste their energy stretching upwards to reach the sun instead of using that energy to grow big, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛshɛɔ hulu lɛ he lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu ŋmãa wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my cassava so much when the cassava plants are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-cassava lɛ dalɛ baa shi waa eyɛ mli akɛ Cassava tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Young cassava plants have small roots and very few leaves, making them weak competitors. Weeds grow much faster and drink up the water and soil nutrients before the young cassava roots can reach them.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai fioo ko pɛ. ni haa efeɔ akaŋshilɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Without shade plants like plantains or shade trees to shelter them, the hot sun dries out the soil and scorches the young plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni eshãa tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce much bigger tubers when I give them wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs ni dara kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ beni mihaa amɛ tsei ni akɛkwɔɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves high off the ground where they can catch plenty of sunlight. Leaves use sunlight to make food, and when they make extra food, they store it underground to build large yam tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii. Ni kɛ́ amɛfee niyenii babaoo lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without forming any fruit when the weather gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Very high temperatures damage the pollen inside tomato flowers so they cannot form seeds. To protect itself from heat stress, the plant drops its unpollinated flowers to conserve energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛŋ ebɔ dumɔwui. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he Bɔni afee ni okɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily after heavy rain and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots; they only have shallow roots near the top of the soil. When heavy rain softens the ground, these shallow roots cannot support the heavy weight of the tree and fruit bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ pɛ yɔɔ. Yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ pɛ Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ, nɛkɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɛɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ tsei kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize help the maize produce a better yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ du tsina ŋmã lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmã lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that can take nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into food in the soil through their roots. Maize feeds on this trapped nitrogen, which helps it grow stronger green leaves and better grain.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmei tso ko ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔ eshishifãi anɔ etsɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Abɛi yeɔ nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ. Enɛ haa baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow thick green leaves on top but produce tiny cassava roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ ŋwɛi shi cassava shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium. Nitrogen makes the plant put all its food into growing leaves and stems, leaving very little energy to grow starchy roots below.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ shi potassium bɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei kɛ amɛ niyenii fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ahi shi koni akɛkwɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots from my plantain stump instead of letting all of them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ plantain shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: All shoots attached to one plantain stump share the same root system. If you leave too many shoots, they split the food and water among themselves, resulting in weak stems and very small fruit bunches.
ga: Tsobii fɛɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ dumɔwu shishifã kome he lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo kome. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Ebaagbala niyenii kɛ nu mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and turning light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually a sign that tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies are sucking the sap out of the leaves, or that a virus has entered the plant, stopping the leaf from expanding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies miimu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. loo hela ko ebote tso lɛ mli Enɛ haa baai lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted coconut tree to start producing fruits in Ghana?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii yɛ Ghana?

english: Dwarf coconut varieties usually start bearing fruit within 3 to 4 years, whereas traditional tall varieties take about 6 to 10 years to produce their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ji dwarf lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young coconut trees turning yellow and dropping off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young coconut palms are typically a sign of nitrogen or potassium deficiency in the soil, poor water drainage, or prolonged dry spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ

english: Is it good to plant coconut trees very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni aná he ko babaoo?

english: No, planting coconuts too close forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, weak trunks and significantly fewer coconuts.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni ŋmeii lɛ hu faaa kwraa.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as temporary natural umbrellas to protect the young cocoa until it establishes strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni efeɔ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the trunk before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during heavy rains and high humidity when there is poor airflow through the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why is my maize crop producing flowers when the stalks are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ lɛ? Ani tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ kuku waa lolo?

english: Maize plants flower prematurely when they experience severe water stress or poor soil fertility early in their growth cycle, forcing the plant to produce seeds quickly to survive.
ga: Abɛi baawo fɔfɔi oya kɛji akɛ nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ kpe yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ tsei awo dumɔwui oya dani amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Which way should I point my cassava stem cuttings when planting them in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ atsɔ nɔ atsɔɔ ŋmei niji lɛ?

english: Cassava stems should be planted with the raised buds pointing upward toward the sky so the roots can develop downward and the stems can shoot straight up into the light.
ga: Esa akɛ adu Yucca tsei lɛ ni amɛshishifãi ni awó nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya shishi ni amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ atswa tɛ̃ɛ kɛya la lɛ mli.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow steals water and nutrients from the main plantain stem, which results in smaller bunches and slower harvest times.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ plantain tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii, ni kpamɔ be lɛ hu yaa hiɛ blɛoo.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but no fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers without forming fruit if the weather gets too hot or if there is excessive nitrogen in the soil, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato baafɔ̃ ni ewooo yibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and stop expanding during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɛɛɛ eshwaaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing water during extreme heat, or as a reaction to sap-sucking pests like aphids and thrips that attack the underside of young leaves.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ hulutsoo be mli. aloo akɛ nɔ ni afeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids kɛ thrips ni tutuaa baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea will help the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same plot of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land depletes specific soil nutrients and allows pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural nitrogen into the earth.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot underground before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa?

english: Cassava root rot typically happens when water settles around the roots due to poorly drained soil or flooding. Planting your cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nu afua hewɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering in the early morning allows plant roots to soak up water before the sun heat rises. In the hot afternoon, much of the water evaporates into the air before the roots can absorb it.
ga: Nu ni afɔseɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu lɛ dɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu babaoo shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the leaves of my cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Moths lay eggs on cabbage leaves which hatch into hungry caterpillars. You can control them by checking under leaves to pick them off manually or spraying a mixture of soapy water and natural neem oil extract.
ga: Kplukai woɔ wɔji yɛ kaabe baai anɔ, ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni oookwɛ koni okɛ onine ajie amɛ lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ nu ni akɛ samla kɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ afutu nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly between dry and wet. Mulching around the roots keeps the ground cool and moist, helping the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Mulching around Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves around the bases of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ashwã he lɛ? miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishitoo

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the soil quickly, keeps weeds from sprouting, and breaks down into fertile compost over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to come up out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep, if the soil is packed too hard, or if there isn't enough moisture. Plant seeds at a depth equal to two or three times their size in soft, damp soil.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ. aloo hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa Dumɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ amɛdalɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: How can I tell when my yams are fully mature and ready to dig out?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines above ground turn yellow and dry up completely. This shows the plant has stopped growing leaves and has stored all its energy inside the underground tuber.
