ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha nikpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: How does the chemical powder I sprinkle on my crops actually kill the tiny insects?
ga: Tsofa powda ni mikɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii. Te ooofee tɛŋŋ onine ashɛ nɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: The chemical powder works either when insects eat the treated leaves or when the dust sticks to their bodies, poisoning their nervous system or drying them out until they die.
ga: Tsofa powda lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ́ kooloi ye baai ni atsa amɛ lɛ. aloo kɛ́ sũ kpɛtɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ he Eji tsofa fɔŋ kɛha tsitsii lɛ. loo egbi kɛyashi egbo

english: If I fumigate my crop store to kill pests, will it affect the maize or beans I want to sell later?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ la wo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni mikɛjie tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ, Ani enɛ baaná ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni misumɔɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Fumigation kills hidden insects in stored crops, but you must strictly follow the required waiting period before selling or eating the grain so the chemical gas can clear out safely.
ga: Fumigation gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ amli. Shi esa akɛ onyiɛ be ni ataoɔ ni akɛmɛ lɛ sɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani ohɔ̃ɔ loo oye dumɔwui lɛ koni tsofa mli kɔɔyɔɔi lɛ anyɛ ajo foi shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I tell if the pest powder I applied on my farm is working properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: You will see dead insects dropping onto the soil around your plants, fresh leaf damage will stop, and new shoots will grow without new pest attacks.
ga: Obaana kooloi bibii ni egboi lɛ ni baagbee shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ, ni baai heei ni afiteɔ lɛ baakpa. Ni ŋmeii heei baakwɛ̃ ni ŋmeii heei etutuuu amɛ.

english: Why do I see dead insects lying on the ground shortly after spraying my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi ni egboi ni ekã shikpɔŋ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pests drop to the ground because crop chemicals act quickly on their nervous systems, causing immediate paralysis and forcing them off the leaves as they die.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ejaakɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya yɛ tsitsii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛhe feɔ shoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ, ni enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛshwie amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji amɛgboi pɛ.

english: Why do some insects still survive on my farm even after I have dusted the crops with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii komɛi hiɔ shi lolo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Insects can survive if rain washes the powder away, if the dose applied was too weak, or if the pests have built up resistance to that particular chemical over time.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji nugbɔ shwie powda lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ faaa tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ tswa nakai tsofa lɛ he hewalɛ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli.

english: What brings so many pests to my farm right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo boteɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ?

english: Rainfall encourages crops to sprout tender leaves and fresh shoots, which attract insects looking for easy food and moist places to lay their eggs.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hewalɛ koni amɛwo baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii heei. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii ni miitao niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛwuji lɛ baawo lɛ.

english: If I use chemical powders to kill crop pests, will it also kill lizards and mice on my farm?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa powda gbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Ani ebaagbe ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hu?

english: Strong chemicals can harm non-target animals like lizards and mice if they eat the poisoned insects or get direct contact with heavy amounts of the chemical powder.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa baanyɛ aye koolooi ni asusuuu amɛhe, tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ahe awui. Kɛji amɛye kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei loo amɛkɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma powda babaoo kpe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ,.

english: Is it safe to plant new seeds in soil where strong pest chemicals were recently sprayed?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli wa eshwie nɔ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ nɔ?

english: You should wait for the recommended period before planting, because strong chemical residues in the soil can burn young roots and stop new seeds from germinating properly.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ be ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ dani okɛdu. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai ni mli wa ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha dumɔwui heei akakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will using chemical powders on my farm continuously damage my soil over time?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaya nɔ afite mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Overusing strong chemicals can kill beneficial soil organisms like earthworms and good microbes, which reduces the soil's natural fertility over time if organic matter is not added.
ga: Tsofai ni mli edɔ babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ agbe shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni hi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli kɛji akɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he.

english: Why should I cover my nose and mouth when applying pest dust on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha migugɔ kɛ mi daaŋ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sũ miiwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Fine chemical dust floats easily in the air and can enter your lungs, causing coughing, dizziness, or long-term health problems if inhaled.
ga: Tsofa mli sũ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya, ni ebaanyɛ ebote fɛ̃i lɛ mli. Ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ, tsitsi ni tsɔɔ mɔ he, loo helatsamɔ mli naagbai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa kɛji akɛ amu.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings dying even though I planted them carefully?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo yɛ bɔ ni mikwɛ nɔ miha lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees require specific soil conditions to survive. If land is physically unsuitable—such as having soil that is too rocky, shallow, or poorly drained—the roots cannot grow properly or absorb water, causing the young trees to fail regardless of how well you plant them.
ga: Cacao tsei biɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ tsɔ, ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ ehiii lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ adara jogbaŋŋ loo amɛŋɔ nu. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni obaadu amɛ jogbaŋŋ oha.

english: How can I know if a piece of land is suitable for planting cocoa before spending money on seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ko hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ dani mafite shika kɛdu dumɔwui?

english: Good cocoa land has deep, dark, rich soil that lets rainwater drain away while keeping enough moisture for roots. You can test the land by digging down to check for deep soil without hard rocks or water pooling at the surface.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli edɔ, ni baa nii ni haa nugbɔ nu hoɔ kɛyaa, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ hiɔ shi. Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oootsi koni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tɛi ni wa loo nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant cocoa in swampy areas where water stays on top of the ground?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nu yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, swampy land is physically unsuitable for cocoa because cocoa roots need air in the soil to breathe. Standing water suffocates the roots and causes them to rot, leading to crop failure.
ga: Dabi, hei ni ŋmɔji yɔɔ lɛ esaaa kɛha kookoo yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ ejaakɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii.

english: Why does cocoa refuse to grow well on steep or rocky hills?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo tɛsaai anɔ lɛ?

english: Rocky or steep land often has very shallow soil that dries out quickly in the sun. Cocoa trees need deep soil so their taproots can go far underground to find water during dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔji ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ loo shikpɔji ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa ni hulu la kpɛɔ oya. Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao nu yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why is farmland that produced good cocoa years ago no longer suitable for cocoa today?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji ni wo kookoo kpakpa afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ esaaa dɔŋŋ kɛha kookoo dumɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ?

english: Land changes over time due to weather shifts, soil erosion, and loss of nutrients from continuous farming. Land that was once moist and shaded can become dry and degraded, making it physically unsuitable for cocoa now.
ga: Shikpɔŋ tsakemɔi yɛ be kɛ bei amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu ko lɛ edɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni efite. ni no haa esaaa akɛ aduɔ kookoo amrɔ nɛɛ

english: Why does cutting down all the big shade trees make my land bad for cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Big shade trees protect the soil from intense sun heat and keep moisture in the ground. When you clear all trees, the soil dries out and hardens, turning suitable land into an environment where cocoa seedlings cannot survive.
ga: Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo, amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie tsei lɛ fɛɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi ni ebaawa. Enɛ haa he ni sa lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ko ni kookoo dumɔwui nyɛŋ ahi mli.

english: What are the warning signs that my land is turning bad for growing cocoa?
ga: Mɛni ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miiba shi yɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Signs include soil that bakes hard like brick during dry weather, water that stays trapped in puddles for days after rain, or cocoa leaves turning yellow and falling off even when there are no pests.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii lɛ ahe ji shikpɔŋ ni wa tamɔ brikii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Nu ni hiɔ nubu mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Aloo kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli moŋ.

english: If a part of my land is bad for cocoa, can I do something to force cocoa to grow there?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko ehiii kɛha kookoo Ani manyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni mikɛnyɛ kookoo nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: If the physical condition of the land is fundamentally unsuitable—like heavy rock formations or constant waterlogging—you cannot easily force cocoa to succeed. It is usually better to choose crops that fit that specific soil type.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ lɛ ejaaa kwraa, tamɔ tɛi ni mli tse loo nu ni hiɛɔ be fɛɛ be. Onyɛŋ onyɛ Cocoa nɔ mlɛo koni eye omanye. Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohala tsei ni sa nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What should I plant on parts of my farm where cocoa has failed to grow?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi ni kookoo kwɛɛɛ yɛ lɛ amli?

english: Land that is unsuitable for cocoa can often support other useful crops. For example, wet areas can be good for oil palm or sugar cane, while drier, sandy soils might suit cassava or cashew trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni esaaa akɛ aduɔ kookoo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ efɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mu loo ŋmei. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sa kɛha ŋã loo ŋã tsei.

english: What happens if I plant cocoa on bad land and just add more chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ewo muji nɔ ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fata he kɛkɛ?

english: Fertilizer adds plant food, but it cannot fix basic physical land problems like poor water drainage or hard rocks. If the site itself is unsuitable, fertilizer will be wasted because the trees still cannot build strong roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsei aniyenii yaa hiɛ. Shi etsuuu shikpɔŋ nɔ naagbai ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo tɛi ni wa lɛ ahe nii. Kɛji he ni eyɔɔ lɛ esaaa lɛ Afiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK early in the season helps restore green growth and increase yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛwo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and stem-like even though the foliage above ground grew very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛtamɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛlɛ waa moŋ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted in overly wet soil, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and branches instead of expanding its underground roots. Balancing soil nutrients encourages root development.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ nɔ. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei aniji lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding on leaf juices, or by viruses spread by whiteflies. Spraying with neem oil solution or appropriate insect control protects the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: What is causing large holes in my maize leaves and ragged damage inside the leaf whorls?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli kɛ fitemɔ ni yɔɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the growing center of young maize plants. Catching the caterpillars early and applying recommended pest treatments into the leaf whorl prevents severe crop destruction.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni aaamɔ ŋmeii mra Ni akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii waa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings rapidly between dry and very wet. Watering your crop regularly at ground level and maintaining light shade during extreme heat helps flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya yɛ nɔ ni egbi kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ waa teŋ. Nu ni oooha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out crooked, short, and small instead of straight and large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe, amɛfeɔ kukuji, ni amɛfeɔ bibii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep, soft soil to extend downward easily. If your mounds or ridges contain hard soil clumps or rocks, or are not built high enough, the growing tuber gets restricted and develops into an irregular shape.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa oya. Kɛji ogɔŋ loo ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ muji loo tɛi ni wa loo amako nɔ ni nɔ kwɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ Atsiɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anaa ni amɛfeɔ su ni ejaaa.

english: Why should I cut away excess shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from the main mother stem. Removing all but one or two healthy replacement suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ pɛ shi ekome loo enyɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantains wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees shed their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry spells as a natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss. Plantain shade trees planted alongside cocoa trees help block dry Harmattan winds and keep soil moist, keeping young cocoa trees green year-round.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ eŋɔli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my cabbage garden early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo kaabii abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is better because the sun quickly dries off wet leaves during the daytime. Evening watering leaves foliage damp overnight, which creates ideal conditions for fungal leaf diseases to spread.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ hulu la lɛ haa baai ni efɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Nu ni oooha amɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha fungal leaf helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts before planting maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii dani midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and fix it directly into the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on that natural nitrogen left behind, growing better with less reliance on chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ. Ehaa edaa jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔ nɔ fioo lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the proper way to open cocoa pods so I do not spoil the beans inside?
ga: Te aaafee agbele kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ jogbaŋŋ Kaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ miigbo?

english: Cocoa pods should be broken open carefully using a blunt wooden mallet or wooden stick rather than a sharp cutlass to avoid slicing into and damaging the seeds inside.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ mallet loo tso ni mli edɔ afo kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ tsɔne ni mli wa baatsu nii Enɛ ji koni akafite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to spread out and dry my cocoa beans bit by bit in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ ashwã fiofio kɛtsɔ hulutsoo be mli ni mikɛgbiɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spreading cocoa beans in thin layers and turning them regularly allows moisture to evaporate slowly and evenly, which prevents mold growth and preserves quality.
ga: Okɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii bibii amli. Ni kɛ́ otsake lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ atsɔ mli fiofio ni efee ekome, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ aya hiɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long can I leave harvested cocoa pods on the ground before breaking them open?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ mashi mi-kookoo ni mikpa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ dani magbele?

english: It is best to break open harvested cocoa pods within five to six days after picking so the beans do not start germinating inside or rot before drying.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookumɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ mli yɛ gbii enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni akpa lɛ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akaje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ mli loo amɛkafite dani amɛgbi.

english: Why do I need to sort out damaged cocoa beans from good ones before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie kookoo ŋmeii ni efite lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni hi lɛ amli dani amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Sorting out flat, diseased, or insect-damaged beans prevents bad flavors and mold from spreading to healthy beans during drying, ensuring a higher market price.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni kooloi efite lɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni ehiii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ jarayeli jara lɛ baafee nɔ ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why must cocoa beans undergo fermentation before being sun-dried?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afee kookoo yibii lɛ ŋmɔtɔ dani agbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the beans to break down the sweet mucilage pulp, kill the seed germ, and unlock the brown color and rich flavor required for cocoa export.
ga: Fermentation haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ amli. Gbemɔ helai ni yɔɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ ni ogbele su ni tsuɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ.

english: How should I care for my young cocoa seedlings right after planting them in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ makwɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ aha tɛŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli sɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are like nursing babies; they need shade from harsh sun, light moisture, and gentle care until their roots are strong enough to handle full weather.
ga: Kookoo tso bibioo tamɔ abifao ni miiye fufɔ. Amɛmiitao hɔnɔ kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. hulutsoo fioo kɛ kwɛmɔ blɛoo kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkpee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ anaa kwraa.

english: When is the right time to start giving strong fertilizer to my young crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi mitsei bibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ?

english: Just like weaning a child, crops should only receive full-strength fertilizer once they have passed the delicate seedling stage and developed mature roots that can absorb nutrients.
ga: Nakai eji yɛ gbekɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli lɛ he. Esa akɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ mli kɛji amɛho dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli ni amɛná shishifãi ni eda ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa plants need different types of care as they grow older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Crops go through distinct growth stages, moving from delicate young plants that require heavy shade and light water to mature trees that need open sun, pruning, and heavy feeding.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ dalɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi amli. Amɛyeɔ tsei bibii ni waaa ni he hiaa hulutsoo kɛ nu ni mli jɔ lɛ anajiaŋ. Eji tso ni eda ni hulu la he miihia lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ. ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni tsii

english: When should I start removing the shade plants growing around my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mabɔi shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ajiemɔ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Shade trees should be thinned out gradually as the cocoa trees mature, because adult cocoa trees require more direct sunlight to produce plenty of pods.
ga: Esa akɛ Afolɔ kookoo tso lɛ fiofio koni ená hulutsoo be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, cacao tsei ni eda lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo koni amɛná ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why can mature cocoa trees take full fertilizer while young seedlings get damaged by it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kwraa yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui bibii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Mature plants have deep, tough root systems capable of processing rich soil nutrients, whereas tender seedling roots get scorched by concentrated chemical fertilizers.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni baanyɛ atsu niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe nii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ shãa dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need for healthy green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant make strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans in the same field with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmeii?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull natural food (nitrogen) out of the air and put it into the soil. This feeds the soil and helps your corn grow bigger without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmã lɛ ni edara ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why are many of the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop extra flowers naturally, but losing too many flowers is usually caused by lack of shade, dry soil, or tiny insects like mirids damaging the flowers before pods can form.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔii krɛdɛɛi kɛjɛɔ ehe yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ baa ji hulutsoo ni bɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and making the plant look stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny invisible pests like thrips or mites sucking the juice from the leaves. Spraying early with neem water or insect spray stops them from damaging young shoots.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper mli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli Neem nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and sunken before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efoɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant does not get enough regular water to carry calcium from the soil into the developing fruit during hot weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa ni baaha amɛná calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds early when my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil food. Cleaning them early gives your crops full room to build strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Hetsemɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do farmers spread dry grass on the soil around young crops during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ ni amɛduɔ nii bibii lɛ ahe yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the hot sun from drying out the dirt, keeping water in the soil longer for your crop's roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi kɛhaa onibii shishifãi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to make big earth mounds to plant my yams instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama sũ agbo ko ni akɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow long and thick underground. Soft earth mounds give the roots loose soil to expand easily without hitting hard ground, while keeping excess rainwater from rotting the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni abua naa lɛ haa shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekaha ŋmeii lɛ egbo.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots (suckers) act like children competing for the mother tree's food and water. Leaving only 2 or 3 strong shoots allows the main plantain tree to grow large, heavy bunches.
ga: Nibii ni fata he lɛ (tsoji) lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbekɛbii. Okɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛ nyɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ aka akaŋ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwu titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ tsei agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning soft and brown inside if I harvest them late in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji mikpa amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: When the soil gets very dry, cassava plants draw water and stored starch back out of their roots to survive, which makes the tubers woody, fibrous, or prone to rot.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa lɛ, Cassava tsei lɛ jieɔ nu ni amɛkɛ starch toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ tsei, ŋmeii, loo amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi oya.

english: Why is it better to start my crop seeds in a nursery before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mabɔi mitsei lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Nursing seeds allows you to protect tender young plants from harsh sun, heavy rain, and pests while they are weak, ensuring that only the healthiest plants are planted out in your main farm.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: If it has already rained today, do I still need to water my seedlings in the nursery?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ŋmɛnɛ Ani ehe miihia ni mawo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nu lolo?

english: Not always. You should check the soil with your finger first; if the top soil is wet, you do not need to water, but if the rain did not reach under your nursery shade structure, the seedlings may still need water.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Esa akɛ okɛ onine akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ nɔ edɔ Ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu awo nɔ. Shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ shɛɛɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Ekolɛ nu he baahia dumɔwui lɛ lolo.

english: How does heavy sunlight affect young crop seedlings while they are growing in the nursery?
ga: Te hulu la ni naa wa lɛ saa dumɔwui bibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ beni akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: Direct harsh sunlight can burn delicate leaves and heat up the root zone quickly, drying out young plants before their roots are strong enough to draw deep soil moisture.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni eha shishifã lɛ mli adɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my nursery seedlings look tall and thin instead of strong and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-nursery dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings grow thin and tall when they are searching for sunlight, which usually happens if they are kept under too much shade or planted too close together.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baafee mlɛo ni amɛkwɔ be mli ni amɛtaoɔ hulu la lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo shishi tsɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting too much or too little water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni miduɔ lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ?

english: If crops get too little water, their leaves wilt and dry up. If they get too much water, their roots cannot breathe, causing the leaves to turn yellow and the plant to rot.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ nu fioo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbi. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Is natural rainwater better for my young crops than water from a well or tap?
ga: Ani nugbɔshiimɔ nu ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ fe nu ni jɛɔ nu bu loo pɔmpi mli?

english: Yes, rainwater is soft and naturally contains small amounts of nitrogen from the air, which helps crops grow faster and greener compared to well or tap water.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, nitrogen fioo ko ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya, ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãaa gbee kɛ akɛto nubu mli nu loo pɔmpi mli nu he.

english: Why do some seeds fail to sprout even after I plant them and give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni midu ni mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if they are planted too deep in the soil, if the soil is pressed down too hard, or if the seed itself is old and damaged.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. aloo atswa shikpɔŋ lɛ waa tsɔ loo kɛji dumɔwu lɛ egbɔ ni efite

english: Why is it better to sell or supply my crop seedlings to farmers who are close by?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ loo mikɛ mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ aha okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Selling to nearby farmers reduces travel time, which prevents the seedlings from drying out, getting crushed, or suffering root stress during long journeys.
ga: Ni ahɔ̃ɔ ahaa okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ haa gbɛfaa be baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi, amɛkakumɔ, loo amɛkaná shishifãi ahe haomɔ yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How can I tell when a seedling is strong enough to be moved to the main farm field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are usually ready when they have developed several dark green leaves, a thick stem that does not easily bend, and a well-formed root ball.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛji amɛyɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo. Tsoi ni mli tse ni shwieee shi mlɛo ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shihilɛ kpakpa mli

english: What is the best way to move seedlings to the field so they do not die after planting?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ dumɔwui awoɔ ŋmɔ mli koni amɛkagboi beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Water the seedlings well before moving them, handle them gently by the root ball rather than the stem, and plant them early in the morning or late in the evening when the weather is cool.
ga: Okɛ nu awo dumɔwui lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ dani okɛ amɛ aya he kroko, ni okɛ shishifã bɔɔlu lɛ atsu nii blɛoo yɛ shishifã lɛ najiaŋ. Ni odu leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Which crops can I plant in Ghana that will mature very fast so I can harvest and sell within two to three months?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana ni baakwɛ̃ oya ni abaanyɛ akpa ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli?

english: Short-duration crops like cucumber, watermelon, and leafy vegetables (such as gboma or aleefu) mature within 8 to 10 weeks, allowing you to harvest quickly and generate fast income.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ kukumba, watermelon, kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai (tamɔ koboma loo alifu) lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ otsii 8 kɛyashi 10 mli, ni ebaaha okpa nii oya ni oná shika oya.

english: How can I make sure I am harvesting crops continuously throughout the year instead of everything maturing at once?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ maná ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ.

english: You can use staggered planting, which means planting small batches of seeds every two to three weeks so that different sections of your farm mature at different times for a non-stop harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ adu dumɔwui bibii daa otsii enyɔ loo etɛ. koni fãi srɔtoi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ada yɛ bei srɔtoi amli kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni akpaaa.

english: How can I help my cassava and yam tubers grow very big and heavy before harvest time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-cassava kɛ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsii dani akpa?

english: Root crops like cassava and yam need loose, well-drained soil so the tubers can expand easily, along with fertilizers rich in potassium which direct energy into growing large tubers.
ga: Shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. koni yitso lɛ anyɛ alɛɛ mli oya Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ ni haa hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛhaa ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ fataa he.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant them too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which results in thin, weak plants with small and light harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, ni no haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo faaa ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from high temperatures, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai anɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain trees curl up and droop during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up during intense heat to reduce water evaporation from their broad surface, acting as a natural survival mechanism when the soil is dry.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔji wuji anɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and grow thin when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Maize requires full sunlight to create food through its leaves, so growing it under shade deprives it of light, making the plant weak, yellow, and unable to produce full cobs.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ etsɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ efee niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko da yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaa la bɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants get diseased and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ yeɔ helai ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause high humidity and waterlogging, creating perfect conditions for fungal diseases and root rot to attack sensitive crops like tomatoes.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛ nu ni hoɔ baa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ koni amɛtutua tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ tomato.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings look weak and wilted right after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings go through 'transplant shock' when their roots are disturbed; moving them late in the afternoon and watering them immediately helps them recover quickly.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ atsɔ ‘Graft shock’ mli kɛji shishifãi lɛ gbala amɛ Kɛ́ ajie amɛ shwane mli ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ oya.

english: How do crops use chemical fertilizer, and why does my farm soil need it?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ? Ni mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts as food for crops, replacing lost soil nutrients like Nitrogen for green leaves, Phosphorus for strong roots, and Potassium for heavy, healthy yields.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii. Ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ yeɔ najiaŋ. Fosfɔs kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ potassium kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why am I only getting three bags of cocoa from my farm while my neighbor gets so much more?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛ kookoo kotokui etɛ pɛ nɔ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ná kookoo babaoo lɛ?

english: Low yield often happens because cocoa trees aren't getting proper pruning, shade control, or soil nutrients. Following correct agronomic practices like clearing parasitic mistletoe, weeding regularly, and feeding the soil at the right time can dramatically increase your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa ejaakɛ afolɔɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ, ahaaa amɛ hulutsoo loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni ja lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni ji mistletoe ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ ajiemɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: How does sunlight affect how my cocoa trees produce pods?
ga: Te hulu la lɛ saa kookoo ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees need a careful balance of light and shade. Too much shade encourages fungal diseases like black pod, while too much direct sunlight scorches leaves and stresses the tree, causing it to drop its flowers and produce fewer pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei biɔ ni akwɛ la kɛ hulutsoo nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shade babaoo kɛ fungal helai tamɔ black pods baa, yɛ be mli ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ fe nine lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree if I want it to grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni eda waa?

english: Pruning removes unproductive, dead, or diseased branches so the tree does not waste energy maintaining them. Opening up the canopy allows sunlight and air to reach the main trunk, directing all the tree's energy into growing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii, ni egboi, loo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ amɛkwɛmɔ mli. Kɛ́ agbele ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa lɛ, hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ daa ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my crops need fertilizer or if the soil is already good?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ momo?

english: When soil runs out of nutrients, crops show clear signs like yellowing leaves, slow growth, or poor flowering. Applying the right crop-specific fertilizer replenishes essential minerals like nitrogen and potassium that crops take out of the ground as they grow.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ baajie okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛdalɛ blɛoo loo fɔfɔi ni ehiii. Kɛ́ akɛ tso pɔtɛɛ ko he ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium aba ekoŋŋ. ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni edaa lɛ

english: Cocoa flowers drop when they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or when the tree is stressed by drought or poor nutrition. Protecting beneficial insects and keeping the ground moist helps flowers stay on the tree to become full pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo be mli ni hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni esaaa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ abuɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe, ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ eyiɔ obɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa trees too close together?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting trees too closely makes them fight each other for water, soil food, and sunlight. It also creates a dark, damp environment where pests and fungal diseases spread easily from tree to tree.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la he. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli edɔ hu baa, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ oya.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slower and produce less food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiiwo niyenii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act as thieves on your farm by competing directly with your crops for soil nutrients, rain, and sunlight. Keeping your field clean ensures all the food in the soil goes straight into feeding your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ akaŋshii ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nugbɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔji lɛ amli tse lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa tree turn black and rot before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease caused by excess moisture and humidity around the tree. Removing infected pods immediately, clearing weeds, and trimming high branches to let wind blow through helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ mli baa. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya, ajieɔ jwɛi, ni afoɔ tsei niji ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahe koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my trees look weak during the dry season even though they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli eyɛ mli akɛ edara kwraa moŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees have roots close to the soil surface that dry out quickly without rain. Leaving cut weed mulch around the root zone acts like a blanket, holding moisture in the soil and keeping root temperature cool during dry spells.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ ashishifãi bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ. Ashiɔ jwɛi ni afolɔ abɔleɔ Shishifã lɛ he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli dɔlɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli

english: Is it possible for an old cocoa farm that produces very little to start giving high yields again?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ kookoo ŋmɔji momo ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔji ni woɔ yibii babaoo ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, an old farm can be brought back to life without cutting everything down. Practices like grafting improved varieties onto old stems, replacing dead trees, and feeding the soil can step-by-step turn an unproductive farm into a high-yielding one.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, abaanyɛ atsake ŋmɔji momoi ni afooo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ mli. Nifeemɔi tamɔ tsei srɔtoi ni asaa amɛhe lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tsei momo amli lɛ. Tsei ni egboi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii najiaŋdamɔlɔi Abaanyɛ atsake ŋmɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ afee ŋmɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ.

english: Who do I need to register with if I want to produce and sell crop seeds in Ghana?
ga: Namɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mihe awo mli kɛji miisumɔ ni mafee dumɔwui ni mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: You must register with the Plant Protection and Regulatory Services Directorate (PPRS). They are the government body in Ghana responsible for monitoring and certifying anyone who wants to produce seeds for sale.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ohe awo Tsei Ahe Bulɛ kɛ Nitsumɔi Ahe Nitsumɔhe (PPRS) lɛ mli. Amɛji nɔyeli nitsumɔhe ko ni yɔɔ Ghana ni amɛkwɛɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni miisumɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui abaahɔɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛha lɛ odaseyeli.

english: Why is it illegal for me to sell commercial seeds without registering my farm first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji mlakwamɔ akɛ abaahɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui kɛha jarayeli ni aŋmalaaa ŋmɔ lɛ he wolo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Seed registration laws protect farmers from buying low-quality or diseased seeds. Registering ensures that officers can monitor your production process so that only healthy, high-yielding seeds enter the market.
ga: Dumɔwui ahe woloŋmaa he mlai buɔ okwaafoi ahe kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni ehiii loo helai ahemɔ he. Woloŋmaa haa onukpai lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ bɔ ni ofeɔ onii ohaa lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii babaoo pɛ aba jara nɔ.

english: What is PPRS, and how do they affect my work if I want to become a seed producer?
ga: Mɛni ji PPRS ni te ebaaná minitsumɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miisumɔ ni matsɔ dumɔwui akwɛlɔ?

english: PPRS stands for the Plant Protection and Regulatory Services Directorate. They regulate seed quality in Ghana by checking your land, monitoring crop growth, and making sure the seeds you produce meet official standards before you sell them.
ga: PPRS damɔ shi kɛha Tsei Ahe Bulɛ kɛ Nitsumɔi Ahe Nitsumɔhe lɛ. Amɛkwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ. Nyiɛmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ Ni okwɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni owoɔ lɛ kɛ maŋ mlai lɛ kpãa gbee dani okɛhɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why must an officer come to inspect my land before I start growing crops for seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni onukpai lɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛdu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: An officer inspects your land to make sure the soil is healthy, free from dangerous pests or diseases, and located far enough from other crops to prevent unwanted cross-pollination.
ga: Mɔ ko ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kwɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ena nɔmimaa akɛ eyɛ hewalɛ lo. Ebɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui. ni ekɛ ehe akabɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe Enɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baatsi cross-pollination ni ataooo lɛ naa.

english: What do agricultural officers look for when they come to inspect my farmland for seed production?
ga: Mɛni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi taoɔ beni amɛkwɛɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ dumɔwui?

english: They check the history of your land, soil health, water drainage, and the distance between your field and neighboring farms to ensure your seed crop will grow pure and disease-free.
ga: Amɛkwɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yinɔsane, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ ha lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni helai bɛ amɛhe.

english: Can I produce certified seeds on any piece of land I own, or are there special land requirements?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mawo dumɔwui ni awo he odase yɛ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Te nɔ ni manyɛ maná? Aloo ani shikpɔŋ he taomɔ nii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ?

english: You cannot use just any land. Your land must pass an official inspection to ensure it is isolated from other fields of the same crop and is free of soil-borne diseases that could ruin seed quality.
ga: Onyɛŋ okɛ shikpɔŋ ko kwraa atsu nii. Esa akɛ amralo lɛ akwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ena akɛ egbala kɛjɛ hei krokomɛi ahe. ni ji tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni baanyɛ afite dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ bɛ mli

english: Why shouldn't I just save seeds from my best harvest and sell them to my neighbors as certified seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaa ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ mikutsoŋbii lɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Grain saved from a regular harvest can carry hidden diseases or produce weaker plants in the next generation. Certified seeds must be grown under strict supervision and inspected by PPRS to guarantee high yield and purity.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaa ni akpaa daa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo amɛwo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa shishi ni PPRS akwɛ mli koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ amɛbaawo yibii babaoo ni amɛhe tse.

english: Why do my seed crops need to be planted far away from my regular food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ mi daa niyenii tsei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Planting them far away prevents pollen from regular crops from mixing with your seed crops. This isolation keeps the crop's variety pure so the resulting seeds grow into strong, reliable plants.
ga: Kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi pollen ni jɛ tsei ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ amli lɛ naa koni ekɛ odumɔwui tsei lɛ akafutu. Nɛkɛ mligbalamɔ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ he tseɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ.

english: How does government inspection of my seed field protect other farmers in my community?
ga: Te nɔyeli lɛ baakwɛ mi dumɔwui ashikpɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ baabu okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Inspections catch diseases and poor crop traits early before seeds are harvested. This prevents bad seeds from spreading crop diseases and low yields across neighboring farms in your district.
ga: Kwɛmɔi naa helai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii mra. dani okpa dumɔwui Enɛ baatsi dumɔwui gbohii anaa koni amɛkagbɛ tsei ahe hela kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ amli.

english: How can I get my farm included in government pilot projects for testing new crop varieties?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔ lɛ afata nɔyeli lɛ kaa nitsumɔ ko ni akɛkaa tsei srɔtoi heei lɛ akwɛ lɛ he?

english: You can express interest through your local extension officer, but your farm will first need to be inspected by regulatory officers to confirm that your land meets the conditions required for trial farming.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie miishɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ kpo kɛtsɔ Extension Officer ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi esa akɛ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ akwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Koni ama nɔ mi akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ shihilɛi ni he hiaa kɛha okwaayeli kaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and scorching during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight and extreme heat when they are small. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them shields the young cocoa from harsh sun rays and retains moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa

english: What is eating the center of my young maize plants and leaving holes and small dark droppings on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni miiye mi ŋmã tso bibioo lɛ tsui lɛ? Ni eshiɔ bu bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that burrows into the growing center (whorl) of maize plants. Applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem oil mixtures early in the morning or late evening directly into the leaf whorls controls them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ awo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ lɛ dani ekpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites, which feed on leaf sap and can transfer plant viruses. Spraying neem extract or appropriate insecticides early helps keep these insects off the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, ni yeɔ baa nu ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tso lɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. Neem mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akajɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with lots of green leaves, but the tubers underground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When farm soil has too much nitrogen and lacks potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of expanding its underground roots. Using balanced fertilizers rich in potassium encourages strong tuber development.
ga: Beni ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my land help my maize grow better in the next farming season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ okwaayeli be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and convert it into natural plant food in the soil. When you plant maize after harvesting legumes, the maize feeds on this leftover nitrogen and grows stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔ lɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa beni okpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ ŋmãa lɛ baaye nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ebaada waa.

english: How can I tell if my soil has become weak and needs nourishment before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni aha lɛ niyenii dani madu nii?

english: Signs of tired soil include crops growing very slowly, leaves turning pale yellow early in the season, low harvest yields despite good rain, and the sudden appearance of parasitic weeds that only grow in poor soils.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite lɛ he ji: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa blɛoo waa. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Nibii ni akpaa lɛ faaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. kɛ jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii pɛ nɔ lɛ ni baa trukaa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off the plant instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of essential nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and ensuring balanced plant feeding helps flowers convert into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ amɛmli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni ja ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my plantain farm producing smaller and lighter bunches than when I first started?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛhe waaa fe beni mibɔi amɛdumɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Over time, plantain plants produce many extra shoots called suckers. These extra suckers compete with the main tree for food and water. Pruning the extra suckers so that only two or three strong ones remain per mat allows the plant to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Beni be hoɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi babaoo ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii. Nɛkɛ suckers pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ amli babaoo bɔni afee ni tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi yɛ mat kome mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my yams starting to rot from the inside even though the outside skin looks smooth and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛjɛɔ mli eyɛ mli akɛ kponɔgbɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Internal yam rot is often caused by microscopic worms (nematodes) or fungal infections that enter the yam through small scratches during harvest or from infected seed yams. Handling yams gently during harvest and storing them in well-ventilated, dry storage areas prevents internal decay.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii waa ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato mli fitemɔ baa. (nematodes) loo fungal helai ni boteɔ sweet potatoes mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli loo kɛjɛ seed yams ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes tsu nii blɛoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli ni okɛto he ko ni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite emli.

english: What is this weed with pink-purple flowers that sticks to my maize roots and stops the corn from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni ji jwɛi nɛɛ ni fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekpɛtɛɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi ahe ni ehaaa eda lɛ?

english: This weed is called Striga (or witchweed), a parasitic weed that attaches itself to maize roots and steals nutrients directly from the plant. Rotating your maize field with non-cereal crops like soybean helps starve and clear Striga seeds from the soil.
ga: Nɛkɛ jwɛi nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Striga (loo Witchweed) lɛ ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe ni ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔji ni jeee ŋmaa, tamɔ soybeans tsake oŋmɔji lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hɔmɔ yeɔ Striga dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. The maize plant moves the limited nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed the new growing leaves at the top, which causes the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei jieɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer to my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can safely absorb it. When applied to dry soil, concentrated fertilizer salts draw water out of the roots instead, causing the plant roots to burn and dry out.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and becoming small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiitsake lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies, thrips, or mites. As these pests feed on the leaves, they often spread plant viruses that cause the leaves to curl and stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies, thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa, ejaakɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baai lɛ. Bei pii lɛ amɛ gbɛɔ tsei amli helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛ tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to hide inside the leaves of my young maize and eat holes through them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai amli ni amɛyeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. The adult moth lays eggs on maize leaves, and once the caterpillars hatch, they crawl into the central funnel of the plant to feed on the soft, young leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni eda ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmei baa nɔ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce large leaves that provide essential shade and retain soil moisture, helping young cocoa plants survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers but drop most of them before growing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop flowers if they lack sufficient soil nutrients, water, or shade to support pod development. It can also happen if there are not enough tiny insects, like midges, in the farm to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, loo hulutsoo be mli ni baaye abua pod lɛ shweremɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: Why do I need to erect tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight so their leaves can manufacture enough food. Staking spreads the leaves out to catch solar energy, which fuels the growth of big tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Staking gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa koni emɔ hulu hewalɛ. ni ji tsofa ni haa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when the soil remains too wet due to poor drainage or heavy rain. Waterlogged soil prevents roots from breathing and creates ideal conditions for soil fungi to infect and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fitemɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ aná hela ni amɛgboi.

english: Why does my cassava start changing color and going bad just two days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ bɔi su tsakemɔ ni efite yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Once cassava tubers are cut from the plant stem, a natural chemical reaction called post-harvest oxidation starts immediately. Because cassava roots lack a thick protective skin, exposure to air causes rapid internal spoilage within 48 to 72 hours.
ga: Beni afoɔ ŋmei shishifã lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ oxidation lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi bɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni mli wa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa emli fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without forming tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing proper fertilization. When fertilization fails due to heat stress, the plant sheds the useless blossoms to conserve its water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa aná fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ fɔmɔ nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and wilting during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or gliricidia provides shade, cools the soil, and helps young cocoa seedlings survive until their own canopy develops.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo glicidia ni aduɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ baa.

english: Why do extension officers advise against cutting down large forest trees when establishing a new farm area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ efooo koo mli tsei wuji beni amɛtoɔ ŋmɔji heei ahe gbɛjianɔ lɛ?

english: Large forest trees act as windbreaks and preserve soil moisture. Keeping some mature trees creates a mild microclimate that protects cash crops from strong winds and intense heat waves.
ga: Koo mli tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsiimɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Tsei ni eda lɛ akwɛmɔ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni buɔ shika ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ latsaa he lɛ baa.

english: What is causing small green worms to eat the leaves and centers of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛteŋgbɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They lay eggs on young leaves, and the caterpillars feed on the growing point of the plant. Applying early treatments like neem oil extracts or recommended pesticides can control them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai bibii anɔ. Ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Abaanyɛ akudɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra tamɔ neem fɔ mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni ekpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit a virus to the plant. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf twisting and keeps the plant producing fruit.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ amɛhe ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but have small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni eeekɛ ŋmei ato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for the next crop without relying entirely on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ he afɔ̃ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anɔ kwraa.

english: Why should I avoid growing maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ he?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot depletes specific soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and fungal diseases to build up in the soil, reducing yields over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmãa he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How deep should I plant my maize seeds when the early rains begin?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmã dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi mra lɛ?

english: Maize seeds should be buried about two to three centimeters deep. Planting too shallow leaves seeds vulnerable to birds and heat, while planting too deep prevents the sprout from reaching sunlight.
ga: Esa akɛ afu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ aaafee sɛntimitai enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha okpoi kɛ dɔlɛ afee amɛ mlɛo. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ baatsi tso bibioo lɛ naa koni hulu la akashɛ enɔ.

english: Why should I avoid applying NPK fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes granular fertilizer off the soil surface or deep underground into the water table before crop roots have a chance to absorb it, wasting your investment.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyaa nu mli. dani tso shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ nu ni haa ofiteɔ onibii ni okɛwo mli lɛ

english: Why does leaving cut grass and dead leaves on top of the soil help my crop field during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni afolɔ kɛ baai ni egboi ni mishiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa nibii ni miduɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dried plant matter acts as mulch, which keeps soil temperatures cool, prevents moisture from evaporating too fast, and slows down weed growth.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to grow strong and healthy. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure helps restore nitrogen to the soil and turns the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ená hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow alongside or before maize, they naturally fertilize the soil, making it richer for the maize without requiring as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ adu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo dani adu lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha ŋmãa afee ŋmãa babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmãa babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree before they are ready for harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads easily in dark, overly wet, and humid conditions. Clearing overgrown weeds, pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and air, and removing infected pods helps keep the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ. Efɔ ni edɔ tsɔ. Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine. Tso niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves that make them look like they were chewed by insects?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii eye.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing center of the plant and eats the tender leaves. Checking your crops early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract when caterpillars are small helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ dalɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Okwɛ onibii amli mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii beni ŋmeii lɛ darako lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants get dark spots and wither during heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains splash soil onto plant leaves, spreading fungal spores that cause leaf blight. Staking tomato plants to keep them off the ground and removing the lowest leaves stops muddy water from touching the foliage and reduces fungal disease.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa sũ shwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ. Egbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɛ baai shwieɔ shi lɛ eshwaa. Tomato tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋtayaai amli koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ akataa baai lɛ ahe, ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct, hot sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa trees need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi lolo.
