english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my pepper plants help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops water in the soil from drying out quickly in the sun. It also keeps the soil cool and prevents weeds from growing and competing with your crops for food.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akagbi oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akaŋ koni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny cobs when I plant the seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and resources to grow strong stalks and large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with lots of green leaves, but the roots underground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen or if plants receive too much leafy fertilizer, the cassava puts all its energy into growing stem and leaves above ground. To get big roots, cassava needs soil rich in potassium and loose soil that allows tubers to expand.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛji tso lɛ ená baai amli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ahe kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni Cassava aná shishifãi wuji lɛ, ehe miihia ni ená shikpɔŋ ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before producing any actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or too much fertilizer. Keeping the soil regularly watered and providing light shade during very hot weather helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa ni aha hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my mature cocoa trees dying one after another across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei ni eda lɛ miigboi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This often happens due to contagious diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus or root rot. Once an infected tree's roots touch neighboring roots or insects like mealybugs spread the virus, the sickness moves from tree to tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ahewɔ enɛ baa, kɛ́ tso ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ loo kooloi bibii, tamɔ mealybugs lɛ kpe, ni amɛgbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã. Helai jɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and curl up even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually point to Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by whiteflies. The virus prevents the plant from using nutrients properly, causing leaves to discolor despite rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ yucca mosaic hela. ni ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ whiteflies lɛ Virus tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su.

english: Why are some of my yam tubers rotting underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Underground tuber rot is usually caused by waterlogged soil with poor drainage, which allows soil fungi and nematodes to penetrate the skin of the yam.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tuber fitemɔ baa. Enɛ haa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ nematodes boteɔ sweet potato lɛ hewolo mli.

english: Why are my maize stalks falling over long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks collapse when pests like stem borers eat through the inside of the stem, weakening the plant's structural strength so light winds knock it over.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛji kooloi tamɔ stem borers ye amɛ gbɛ kɛtsɔ tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shishitoo hewalɛ lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo miitswa ni ebagbee nɔ.

english: Why are my plantain trees snapping at the trunk during light rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ fãa yɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees snap when microscopic soil worms called nematodes attack their roots or stem borers hollow out the base, destroying the tree's anchor.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ fãa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutua shishifãi loo ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. gbee tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli

english: Why do crop leaves curl into tight rolls during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up naturally to reduce water loss under bright sun, but if they stay curled, it means sap-sucking insects like aphids are hiding underneath and feeding on the plant.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni nu ni laajeɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ aba shi. Shi kɛji amɛkoto Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ shishi ni amɛyeɔ nii.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers instead of growing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi moŋ ni eeekwɛ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stress occurs—usually from sudden heat, irregular watering, or tiny insects called thrips damaging the blossom buds.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi bibii Atsɛɔ amɛ thrips ni fiteɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi.

english: Why are my tomatoes developing dark, sunken patches on the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom end rot. It happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, which is often caused by inconsistent soil moisture.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are my older cocoa trees producing much less fruit than they used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni edara lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop in productivity after 25 to 30 years as their vascular systems age, requiring pruning, soil enrichment, or gradual replacement with new seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ ayibii baa shi yɛ afii 25 kɛyashi 30 sɛɛ beni lá fãji lɛ daraa lɛ. Enɛ biɔ ni afolɔ tsei lɛ amli, aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ, loo akɛ dumɔwui heei awo najiaŋ fiofio.

english: Why does my farmland soil dry out much faster now than it did in previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho oya fe bɔ ni eji yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Soil loses its moisture-holding ability when organic matter like dry leaves and mulch are cleared or burned away, leaving bare soil exposed to direct sun and erosion.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛji ajie nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ashã. Ha shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ awo hulu la kɛ ŋshɔkei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct, hot sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil before their roots can grow deep enough to reach groundwater.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he.

english: Yam leaves need maximum exposure to sunlight to create food for the growing tuber underground. Lifting the vines up on stakes allows the leaves to catch more light, resulting in bigger, healthier yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa la babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potatoes ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stem cuttings when I stick them in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ matsɔɔ ŋmei niji lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must always be planted with the small buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots will struggle to grow upward, leading to weak plants or dead crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi bibii. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ohiɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaafee nɔ ni wa akɛ ookwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo tsei ni egboi baa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for limited water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to absorb what it needs to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛŋɔ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo tso agbo ni mli wa.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that your crop lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help your plants regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi fee ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legume crops that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, restoring soil richness naturally for the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants roll up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves inward during hot periods as a natural defense mechanism to reduce moisture loss and protect themselves from burning in the heat.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds reduce my crop harvest more when the crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi babaoo be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and small leaves, making them too weak to compete with fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Once crops grow tall, they shade out weeds naturally.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai bibii. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii beni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ. Amɛbaafee jwɛi lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rot before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, are caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually triggered by irregular or uneven watering while the plant is flowering and fruiting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do insects get inside my bags of dried maize even when the bags are tied shut?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi boteɔ mi-ŋmã kotoku ni egbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ akpɛtɛ kotoku lɛ he moŋ?

english: Insects often lay tiny, invisible eggs inside the maize kernels while the ears are still standing in the field. After harvest, these eggs hatch inside warm storage bags into visible grain pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi fɔɔ wuji bibii. Anaaa ŋmãa lɛ mli be mli ni toi lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. beni akpa kpamɔ sɛɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotokui ni mli edɔ lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni anaa.

english: Why do my maize plants look healthy on the outside, but when I break open the stem, the inside is hollow and damaged?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ? Shi kɛ́ atse tso lɛ shishi lɛ, Ani Mli lɛ mli ewo muji ni efite?

english: This internal damage is usually caused by stem borer caterpillars. The insect lays eggs on the leaves, and once they hatch, the young caterpillars tunnel into the centre of the stem to feed, eating the plant from the inside out without showing immediate damage on the exterior.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, stem borers ji nɔ ni kɛ mligbɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni kɛ́ amɛfɔ Caterpillars tunnel kɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛyatao niyenii. Amɛyeɔ tsei kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ ni amɛjieee kponɔgbɛ nɔ ko ni efite lɛ kpo amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark and rotting from the inside before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ duŋ ni amɛmiifite kɛmiijɛ mli dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, shaded conditions. The fungus penetrates the pod skin and rots the beans inside, causing internal damage before the pod completely turns black on the outside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Fuŋ lɛ boteɔ pod lɛ hewolo mli ni ehaa kɔfe yibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ mli. Enɛ haa mligbɛ fitemɔ baa dani kponɔgbɛ tsɔne lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa.

english: Why do my harvested beans look whole in storage, but when I press them, they crumble into empty dust?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kɔfi yibii ni mikpa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ? Shi kɛ́ minyɛ nɔ Moŋ lɛ, efoɔ sũ?

english: This happens when bean weevils lay microscopic eggs on the pods or stored seeds. The larvae burrow inside the seed, eat the inner flesh while growing, and leave behind only an empty outer shell.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmei ŋmei lɛ woɔ ŋmei bibioo ko yɛ ŋmei loo dumɔwui ni ato lɛ anɔ. Lala lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli. Ye mligbɛ loo lɛ be mli ni odara lɛ. Ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ pɛ eshwɛ.

english: I planted hundreds of cassava stem cuttings in my field, so why have many of them failed to sprout and died off?
ga: Midu ŋmei tsei ohai abɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ tsei babaoo kwɛɛɛ ni amɛgboiii lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings often fail to survive if the stem wood was too old or dry when cut, planted upside down, or planted in soil that lacks enough moisture for the first roots to emerge.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca tsei ni afo lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi kɛji tsei lɛ egbɔ tsɔ loo amɛgbi beni afo amɛ, adu amɛ ŋwɛi, loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu bɛ nɔ bɔ ni sa ni klɛŋklɛŋ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why did a large number of my young tomato seedlings wilt and die right after I transplanted them into the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This loss usually happens because of transplant shock or soil fungi causing 'damping-off.' If the young roots are damaged during moving or placed in dry, hot soil, the seedling collapses near the ground line and dies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ laajemɔ nɛɛ baa yɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ loo ŋmei ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni kɛ ebaa lɛ hewɔ. ‘Damping’ kɛji shishifãi bibii lɛ efite yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ amɛ loo akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience severe stress, such as extreme hot weather, prolonged dry spells, or receiving too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant drops flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ haomɔ ni naa wa, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale yellow when my field stays flooded with water after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe. When water covers the soil for days, air is trapped out, suffocating the roots so they can no longer take up essential nutrients like nitrogen, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatsi. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen dɔŋŋ. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why are my plantain bunches ripening early while the fruits are still very small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ daraaa kwraa ni eyɛ mlɛo lolo lɛ?

english: Early ripening and stunted fruit occur when the plantain tree suffers from severe water stress or root damage caused by microscopic soil worms called nematodes. The plant senses danger and rushes to ripen its seeds early to survive.
ga: Yibii ni shwereɔ mra ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa kɛji dumɔwui lɛ na piŋmɔ waa yɛ nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa loo shishifãi ni sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Tsei nuɔ oshara he ni amɛfeɔ oya koni amɛdumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya koni amɛhi shi.

english: What happens to my crops if I mix and apply too much fertilizer at one time?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo futu mli ni mikɛwo mli shikome?

english: Applying too much chemical fertilizer causes 'fertilizer burn.' High concentration of mineral salts draws moisture out of the roots instead of letting them drink, causing the leaf edges to scorch, turn brown, and die.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ kɛ 'ŋmei shãa' baa. Mineral salts ni fa babaoo lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha efee nɔ ni anyɛɔ anuɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ shãa. Tsɔmɔmɔ brown ni ogbo

english: Why is it important for me to categorize and sort my harvested yams into different groups before storing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majara mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ mli ni majara mli awo kui srɔtoi amli dani mikɛto?

english: Sorting allows you to separate bruised or infected yams from healthy ones. Damaged yams release rot-causing fungi and moisture in storage, which quickly spreads and spoils the healthy yams next to them.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni otseɔ sweet potatoes ni egbɔjɔ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ateŋ. Atomɔ ni efite lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Enɛ baagbɛ eshwa oya ni efite ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ emasɛi lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees looking weak and no longer producing good pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwooo ŋmeii kpakpai dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age or lose soil nutrients, their yield drops and they become weak. Over time, exhausted soil, hidden diseases like Black Pod or Swollen Shoot, and lack of shade can cause trees to stop producing fruit.
ga: Beni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ, Nibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baa shi ni amɛbaafee gbɔjɔmɔ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite Helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ ŋmeii diji loo ŋmeii ni efuu Kɛ hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ akpa yibiiwoo.

english: How many years can a cocoa tree produce pods before it becomes too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ cacao tso baanyɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ dani eda tsɔ?

english: Cocoa trees produce their best yields between 10 and 20 years of age. By around 23 to 25 years, trees often get too old, yields drop significantly, and the farm may need to be rehabilitated or replanted.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ́ amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 20. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ eye aaafee afii 23 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, bei pii lɛ amɛdara tsɔ. Nibii ni anáa lɛ nɔ baa shi waa. Ni ekolɛ ehe baahia ni asaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo adu ekoŋŋ.

english: How long do I have to wait after planting cocoa seedlings before I can harvest my first pods?
ga: Kɛ́ odu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani onyɛ okpa oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take 4 to 5 years to bear fruit, but modern hybrid varieties can start producing pods in just 2 to 3 years if well cared for.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrid henɔi lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What are the main types of cocoa varieties I can choose to plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji kookoo henɔi titri ni manyɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: In Ghana, cocoa generally falls into three main types: Amelonado (traditional), Upper Amazon, and Hybrid cocoa. Hybrid varieties are popular because they grow faster, bear fruit earlier, and yield more.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, ajaa kookoo mli awo henɔi titrii etɛ mli: Amelonado (kusum nifeemɔ), Amazon ŋwɛigbɛ, kɛ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii. Hybrid henɔi lɛ ahe gbɛi waa ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya, amɛwoɔ yibii oya, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I start over or rehabilitate an old cocoa farm that isn't yielding anymore?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maje kookoo ŋmɔ momo ko ni wooo yibii dɔŋŋ lɛ shishi ekoŋŋ loo matswa lɛ shi ekoŋŋ?

english: To restart an old farm, clear out dead or diseased trees, cut back overgrown shade trees, improve soil fertility with recommended fertilizers, and replant with fresh hybrid seedlings alongside shade crops like plantains.
ga: Ani oosumɔ ni obɔi ŋmɔ momo hee? Jiemɔ tsei ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Fɔlɔmɔ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ aya hiɛ. ni okɛ dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains lɛ ahe.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings in the exact same spot where old cocoa trees just died?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he ni kookoo tso momo ko gbo yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is best to treat the soil and clear old root debris first. Old tree spots can harbor soil-borne diseases and pests, so conditioning the soil with organic matter or shifting the planting spot slightly gives new seedlings a healthier start.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ojie shishifãi momo ni efite lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsake shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo otsake he ni aduɔ lɛ fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui heei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Will spraying pest medicine or chemicals harm my cocoa trees or reduce my yield?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye mi-cacao tsei lɛ awui loo ebaaha mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: When applied correctly according to instructions, approved farm medicines protect your trees from pests and diseases. However, using the wrong chemical or over-spraying can burn young leaves, damage flowers, and lower your yield.
ga: Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ taakɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baabu otsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe. Shi kɛlɛ, tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha baai bibii lɛ ashã. fɔfɔi ni efite ni ebaanyɛ eha nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi

english: Can driving heavy farm machinery through my cocoa farm damage the crop?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli tsɔnei ni tsii ni mikɛbaatsɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, heavy machinery compresses the topsoil, making it hard for roots to breathe and absorb water. It can also physically damage shallow cocoa roots and break lower branches, causing the tree to weaken.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsɔnei ni tsii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛmɔmɔ nu. Ebaanyɛ efite kookoo shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ hu. ni shishigbɛ nine lɛ fã Ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crop failure is caused by poor soil strength?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: Signs of poor soil strength include yellowing leaves, slow growth, small cocoa pods, and trees that look tired even when there is enough rainfall. Applying compost or recommended cocoa fertilizers helps restore soil strength.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe ji baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo. kookoo ŋmɔji bibii kɛ tsei ni tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ. Kompost loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Black pods are usually caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in cool, very wet, or overly shaded conditions. Regular weeding, proper tree pruning, and approved fungicide spraying prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ waa, loo hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine. Tso lɛ mli jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa Tso lɛ mli nibii ni sa Kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, a major food component they need to stay healthy. The plant pulls nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed the new top growth, showing that your soil needs manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa. Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans on my field help improve the land for my next main crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha he ni miyɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have tiny natural nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the plants die and decompose, they leave this natural nitrogen in the ground for your next crop to feed on.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ Emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsei gboi ni amɛfite lɛ Amɛshiɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye.

english: Why is my cassava producing very tall stems with lots of leaves but only small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishitso lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava puts too much energy into leaves and stems if the soil has too much nitrogen or if plants are shaded. When the plant focuses all its energy above ground, it leaves very little food energy to swell the tubers below.
ga: Yucca kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ ebaai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo. Kɛ tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ to shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Eshiɔ niyenii hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ehaa yitso lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to space out my maize seeds during planting instead of dropping many into one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijaraa ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui babaoo awo bu kome mli lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil food. Spacing them out allows each plant to build a thick stalk and grow full, heavy cobs instead of thin, weak plants with small cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni kã tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ ni tsii. Mohu ɔ, du tsohi nɛ a he wa we, nɛ a ngɛ tsɔwi nyafii.

english: Why is it important for me to stake my yam vines high up on wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ ama tso ko nɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch direct sunlight, which the plant uses to manufacture its food. The more sunlight the leaves receive, the more food flows down to build a large, heavy yam tuber.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ, ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, babaoo ni niyenii baaho kɛba shi, ni ebaaha yam ŋmeii wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ aba.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by extreme hot weather, dry soil, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil damp and encouraging beneficial insects can help the flowers stay on and turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni oha kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many tiny flowers but very few actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo shi cocoa ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen from flower to flower. If your farm lacks shade or leaf litter where midges live, or if the trees lack water, most flowers will wither and fall without forming pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen ajɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ bɛ hulutsoo loo baai amli jwɛi yɛ hei ni ŋmeii hiɔ lɛ. Aloo kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi babaoo baagbo ni amɛbaagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning black and rotting before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani etsɔɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant transport calcium to the fruit tip to keep it healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa aduawai lɛ ashishi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and brown around the edges even when it is raining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ?

english: Yellow and brown edges on plantain leaves are often caused by leaf spot diseases like Sigatoka, which spread quickly in warm, wet weather. Removing infected lower leaves helps stop the disease from spreading to healthy new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa, tamɔ Sigatoka, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ shishigbɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, hela lɛ haaa egbɛ eshwa baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my young crops with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks the sun from drying out the earth. It traps moisture in the soil, keeps root temperatures cool, and stops weeds from taking over your crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu lɛ naa ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha shishifã lɛ mli latsaa lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye onibii anɔ.

english: Why are my newly planted cocoa seedlings turning brown and dying in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves and shallow roots. Direct, intense sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the plants before their root system is strong enough to survive on its own.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha tso lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa plants are getting too much sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tsɔ?

english: When cocoa plants get too much direct sun, the leaves develop dry, yellowish-brown burnt edges, droop heavily during the afternoon heat, and eventually drop off the stem.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei lɛ ná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ, amɛbaai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, ni amɛshishigbɛ lɛ shãa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gbɛjegbɛ ni mli wa waa yɛ shwane mli latsaa be lɛ mli. Ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa saplings get dry spots during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ anɔ hei ni egbi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry spots on young cocoa leaves are usually caused by sun scorching. Hot sunlight heats up the leaf surface faster than the young roots can draw water from the soil, causing the leaf tissue to burn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ hei ni egbi yɛ kookoo baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha baa lɛ nɔ adɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ehaa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ shãa

english: Can I plant my cocoa seedlings on fresh land at the same time as my shade trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ sũ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛfata tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ahe?

english: It is better to plant shade trees first and let them grow for some time. If you plant them together, the shade trees will be too small to cover the cocoa, and the bright sun will burn your young seedlings.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni oha amɛkwɛ̃ be fioo. Kɛji okɛ amɛ wo he kome lɛ Shade tsei lɛ baafee bibii tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha kookoo nɔ. Ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã odumɔwui bibii lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa plants if I clear away all the forest trees before planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mijie tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ dani midu?

english: Clearing all trees completely exposes your land to strong sunlight and hot winds, which quickly dries out soil moisture and scorches young cocoa plants, leading to high seedling loss.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso ni ooojie lɛ baaha hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ aba he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui babaoo ni laajeɔ.

english: How far in advance should I start growing shade on my farm before putting in cocoa?
ga: Te esa akɛ mabɔi shade dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ kookoo afata he kɛtsɔ hiɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: It is best to start planting your shade crops or economic trees about a year or one rainy season before putting cocoa seedlings in the ground so the trees can form a protective canopy.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooje hulutsoo tsei loo shika helɛtemɔ tsei adumɔ shishi aaafee afi loo nugbɔshiimɔ be kome dani okɛ kookoo dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tsei lɛ anyɛ afee hulutsoo.

english: Which types of trees should I plant on my farm to protect my cocoa from heat?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛbu mikoo lɛ he kɛjɛ latsaa he?

english: You can plant temporary shade crops like plantains alongside long-term economic trees like timber or fruit trees. They block harsh sunlight while keeping the farm cool.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ tsei bibii, kɛ shika helɛtemɔ tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ, tamɔ tsei loo aduawai tsei. Amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting food crops like plantain before cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu niyenii nibii tamɔ plantains dani adu kookoo lɛ?

english: Fast-growing food crops like plantains provide broad-leaf canopy shade quickly to shield fragile young cocoa plants from the sun, while giving you food and early income.
ga: Niyenii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ haa baai ni mli kwɔ oya koni ekɛbu kookoo tsei ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika oya.

english: Will planting economic trees on my farm steal water and food from my cocoa plants?
ga: Ani shika helɛtemɔ tsei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ mikokoo tsei lɛ amli?

english: When spaced correctly, shade trees help cocoa plants more than they hurt them by keeping the soil cool and moist, while also providing you with secondary crops or valuable timber to sell.
ga: Kɛji akɛ he ni jɛkɛmɔ lɛ sa lɛ Shade tsei lɛ baaye abua kookoo tsei lɛ fe ni amɛaaye amɛ awui kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni amɛaaha efee fɛ̃i ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa bo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ loo tsei ni jara wa hu ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa plants need so much extra care and shade during their first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulutsoo yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In their first year on the field, cocoa seedlings are establishing their primary roots and are extremely sensitive to drought and severe heat. Proper shade during this year ensures they survive into healthy, high-yielding trees.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni aduɔ lɛ mli lɛ, kookoo dumɔwui ji shishitoo titri. ni enuɔ hɔmɔ kɛ latsaa ni naa wa he waa. Shade ni sa yɛ afi lɛ mli be nɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds too close to each other in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Spacing them properly ensures each stalk grows strong and produces full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko daa waa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during long dry spells to save water and protect itself from drying out completely. Once the rains start again, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing tubers.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi ehe koni ekagbi kwraa. Kɛ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei ni bulb lɛ baaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: During intense midday heat, pepper leaves lose water faster than their roots can absorb it from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to reduce water loss, but it usually bounces back by evening as temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi efɔɔ sɛɛkuu gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants roll up and get tiny green worms on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling can be a reaction to stress or pests like caterpillars feeding on the leaves. Removing weeds around the plants and using recommended bio-pesticides early will stop the worms from damaging your tomato fruits.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli loo kooloi ni yeɔ baa, tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa lɛ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ajiemɔ Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii Enɛ baaye abua ni kooloi akafite o-tomato yibii lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my orange trees turn yellow with dark green veins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni fãji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves with green veins usually mean the soil lacks essential micro-nutrients like zinc or magnesium, or the roots are struggling to feed. Applying the right crop nutrients or organic compost helps restore normal leaf color and fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni fãji eŋɔli yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii bibii ni he hiaa tamɔ zinc loo magnesium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo shishifãi lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛna niyenii. Kɛ akɛ tso mli niyenii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahe su kɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Groundnut plants pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth through their roots, naturally fertilizing the field for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanut tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my farm while my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your crops need. Clearing weeds early gives your young plants the best chance to grow strong and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seed maize instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests, tolerate drought, and produce higher yields. Seeds saved from past harvests lose their strength over time, resulting in smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni ekɛ yibii babaoo baa Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up completely. This shows that the plant has stopped growing above ground and all its energy is stored safely inside the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ ni akɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ ŋmei lɛ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: What is causing all these small holes in my young maize leaves, and why are the center leaves looking chewed up?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Enɛɛmɛi yɛ mi-baby corn leaves lɛ amli Ni mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the central stem (funnel) of young maize plants. It eats the tender leaves before they unfold, which weakens the plant if not treated early with appropriate pesticides or neem oil extracts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ (cone) lɛ mli. Eyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra. kɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ mli nu

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking into small, hard bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii ni wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking the juices out of the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from twisting and preserves your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ni ebaaha onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he kome.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them properly allows each plant to get enough food and light to develop strong stems and large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the vines up off the wet ground, exposing more leaves to sunlight and protecting them from rot and ground pests.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni wain tso lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe.

english: Why should I remove some of the small shoot suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: If too many suckers grow around the main plantain stem, they steal food and water from the mother plant. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem yields a large, heavy cluster of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii wuji ni tsii aba.

english: How can I tell if my soil is exhausted and needs manure or fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ, ni kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia mi dani madu nii?

english: Signs of tired soil include crops growing very slowly, leaves turning light green or yellow early in the season, and lower yields year after year even when there is enough rain.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite lɛ he ji: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa blɛoo waa. Baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves turn yellow and drop off when there is heavy, continuous rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa yaa nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much standing water in the soil drowns plant roots, preventing them from breathing and absorbing nutrients. Good drainage channels around your farm help excess rainwater flow away so roots remain healthy.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo lɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu. Enɛ haaa anyɛ amu ni aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii. Nu homɔ gbɛi kpakpai ni ebɔle he fɛɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akashɛ he. Shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and sunken before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efo dani ebatsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering during fruit growth, causing the tissue at the bottom of the tomato to collapse and rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Enɛ haa fãji ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ gbálaa ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and turn brown when there are no big trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Planting nurse crops like plantains around young cocoa provides temporary shade and keeps the air moist, helping the young cocoa trees survive.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: How do I know underground cassava roots are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ ni mifooo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the plant reaches 9 to 12 months, the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo beni tso lɛ eye nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for planting mango trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha mango ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Mango trees need deep, well-draining soil where rain water does not stand in pools for days. They also require plenty of direct sunlight throughout the day to grow strong and produce sweet fruits.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. he ni nugbɔ nu lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ hu he miihia amɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Why must I leave plenty of space between each mango tree when planting them on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ mango tso fɛɛ tso teŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mango trees eventually grow into large, wide canopy trees. Giving them adequate space prevents their branches from shading each other out and stops their roots from competing for water and nutrients in the soil.
ga: Yɛ naagbee lɛ, mango tso lɛ da ni etsɔ ŋmei agbo. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni aaaha lɛ baatsi niji anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe naa. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do grafted mango trees produce fruit much faster than the ones I plant directly from seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni akɛwo mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe mango ni miduɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Grafted seedlings are made by joining a branch from a mature tree that is already producing fruit onto a young root stock. Because the branch comes from an adult tree, it skips the long juvenile growth phase that a seed must go through.
ga: Akɛ tso ni eda ni ewo yibii momo lɛ nine ni akɛwoɔ shishifã bibioo ko nɔ lɛ feɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niji lɛ jɛɔ tso ni eda mli. No hewɔ lɛ, efoɔ tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ be ni esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ atsɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant food crops like maize or cassava between my young mango trees while they are still small?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ani ebaanyɛ ehi mango tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, you can plant short crops like maize or legumes between young mango trees during their first two to three years. This provides food and income while the trees grow, as long as you keep a clear circle around each mango stem so the crops do not choke them.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kukuji tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. mango tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli Enɛ baaha niyenii kɛ shika aba be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ. Shii abɔ ni obaahiɛ kooyigbɛ ni mli ka shi faŋŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli. Mango tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko Koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akatsi amɛhe

english: Do my young mango trees need watering during the dry season, or can they survive on rain alone?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni awo mi mango tso lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo nugbɔ pɛ ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ etsui shi?

english: Young trees have shallow roots that cannot reach deep underground water yet. Watering them regularly during their first two dry seasons keeps them alive and helps them develop deep root systems that will survive future droughts on their own.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he lolo. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ hɔmɔ bei enyɔ lɛ amli lɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds and place dry grass around the base of my young trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo jwɛi ni mikɛ jwɛi awo mitsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds prevents them from stealing nutrients and water from your tree stem. Putting dry grass around the base acts as mulch, which traps moisture in the soil, keeps the roots cool, and slows down new weed growth.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛbaabɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni baaha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi heei daalɛ baa shi

english: Why is it important to cut off some of the inner or dry branches of my mango tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ mango tso niji ni yɔɔ mli loo niji ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree. This reduces humidity that causes diseases and directs the tree's energy into growing bigger, healthier fruits on the strong branches.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ helai baa lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ niji ni he wa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are all the flowers falling off my mango tree before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ mango tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Mango flowers drop easily due to dry weather stress, strong winds, or damage from tiny pests like thrips. Ensuring the soil has adequate moisture during flowering and protecting trees from pests helps the flowers successfully turn into small fruits.
ga: Mango fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips fiteɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ni abuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai bibii yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: What causes black spots on my mangoes that make them rot before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ mango nɔ lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Black spots are usually caused by a fungal infection called anthracnose, which thrives in wet and humid weather. Trimming branches to allow air flow and harvesting fruits early before heavy rains can help protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsuɔ diŋ baa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Nibii ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli kɛ aduawai ni akpaa dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why does my mango tree yield a huge harvest one year and then produce almost no fruit the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli, ni afi kroko lɛ ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: This pattern is called alternate bearing. Producing a massive harvest exhausts the tree's stored food reserves, so it takes a full year off to rest, build up new leafy branches, and store energy for the next big harvest season.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ style nɛɛ akɛ bearing ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ. Nikpamɔ babaoo baaha tso lɛ niyenii ni eto lɛ afite. No hewɔ lɛ, eheɔ afi muu fɛɛ dani ejɔɔ ehe. bɔɔ niji heei ni okɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha kpamɔɔ be wulu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Can my cocoa trees be sick even if I do not see any signs of disease on them?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei lɛ baanyɛ aná hela eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa hela lɛ he okadi ko kwraa moŋ?

english: Yes, some diseases like the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus can live and grow inside a tree for up to a year before visible symptoms show on the leaves or stems.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai komɛi, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛdara yɛ tso lɛ mli kɛyashi afi. dani hela lɛ he okadii lɛ baaje kpo yɛ baai loo tsei lɛ anɔ

english: How can an agricultural extension officer spot a disease on my farm that I cannot see myself?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ ana helai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛna lɛ?

english: Extension officers are trained to recognize tiny, early warning signs—such as subtle leaf pattern changes or slight branch swellings—long before full symptoms appear.
ga: Atsɔɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ koni amɛyoo kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii bibii kɛtsɔ hiɛ, tamɔ tsakemɔi fioo yɛ baa lɛ mli. loo niji lɛ ni efuu fioo dani hela lɛ he okadii lɛ jieɔ amɛhe kpo kwraa

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet weather and heavy shade. Clearing excess shade and removing infected pods helps stop it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ojie hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa.

english: Can dirty tools like cutlasses spread diseases from sick trees to my healthy ones?
ga: Ani nibii ni he tseee tamɔ dadei baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã kɛjɛ mitso ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ kɛya mitso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, sap from a diseased plant sticks to your cutlass or pruning shears. If you cut a healthy tree with the same tool, you can transfer the infection directly into it.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni jɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ baakpɛtɛ otsɔnei loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Kɛji okɛ dɛŋdade kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ fo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ hela lɛ awo tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: If my neighbor's farm has a crop disease, how do I know if my farm is in danger?
ga: Kɛji mikutsoŋnyo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tso hela yɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ oshara mli?

english: Diseases often travel to nearby farms through insects, wind, or shared tools. Inspecting the trees closest to your boundary line weekly helps catch early infections.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela yaa ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii, kɔɔyɔɔ loo nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛjaraa nɔ. Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ohusu lɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ daa otsi lɛ baaye abua ni ana hela yɛ eshishijee mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are suffocating from too much standing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu efo shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo hewɔ.

english: Crops drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack of soil nutrients, insect pests, or when there are not enough insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the afternoon heat even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Leaves droop in peak afternoon heat to slow down water loss. If the leaves stand back up in the cooler evening, the plant is behaving normally to protect itself.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli dɔlɛ be mli koni nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ te shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ subaŋ ni sa ni ekɛbuɔ ehe he.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with thick leaves but give me very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much shade or heavy nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing tall leaves instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ náa hulutsoo be babaoo loo akɛ nitrogen babaoo woɔ amɛmli lɛ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kakadaji ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why do my older cocoa trees produce fewer pods now than they did five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni edara lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo fe afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As trees age past 25 to 30 years, their roots absorb nutrients less effectively and they become weaker, making them yield less and catch diseases more easily.
ga: Kɛ́ tso ko ye fe afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haaa ewo yibii babaoo, ni helai hu yeɔ lɛ oya.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key food plant needs to stay green and grow strong cobs. Rain can wash nitrogen away, so applying fertilizer like urea or compost at the right time fixes this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa. Nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen lɛ kɛya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves, but the tubers underground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too little potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build thick tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo potassium fioo tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛya shi koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my maize harvest getting smaller every single year when I plant on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the specific nutrients maize needs and lets maize-specific pests multiply in the soil. Rotating your plot with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɛi lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, damp conditions. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight in and removing rotten pods quickly stops it from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ. Ekpaa gbɛfaŋnɔ oya kɛyaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking leaf juices and spreading viruses. Neem oil spray or planting insect-trapping flowers around your farm helps protect the peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Okɛ neem fɔ afɔ nɔ loo okɛ fɔfɔi ni mɔ̃ɔ kooloi lɛ abɔle he. Okwaafoi lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do small worms bore holes into my cowpea pods before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ mi-cowpea ŋmeii lɛ amli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: These are pod borer caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid on cowpea flowers. Spraying safe organic treatments or planting early in the season helps crop pods mature before the pests multiply.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji pod borers ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tsina fɔfɔi anɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ loo adu yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too high, water supply is uneven, or bees are not available to move pollen inside the flower. Mulching the root area keeps soil moist and reduces heat stress.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. Aloo ŋmeii nyɛŋ ajie pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo he haomɔ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to keep the soil soft around my groundnut plants after they flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi-peanut tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ.

english: Groundnuts flower above ground, but after pollination, growing stems called 'pegs' must push down into the dirt to grow nuts. Hard, dry soil blocks these pegs from entering the ground.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ esa akɛ ashɛ Stems ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘pegs’ lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shi.

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and tiny soil worms (nematodes) or stem borers can weaken them further. Supporting heavy fruiting trees with wooden props and planting in healthy soil keeps them standing.
ga: Plantain shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ sũ mli ŋmeii bibii (Nematodes) loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ yibii babaoo fiɔ tsei ni akɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ, ni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi.

english: How can I stop my harvested yams from rotting or sprouting too quickly in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite loo ekwɛ̃ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Yams rot when exposed to heat, moisture, or damage. Storing undamaged yams in a cool, raised, and well-ventilated traditional yam barn away from direct floor contact stops rot and delays sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes baa fite kɛji akɛ amɛ wo dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i, loo nɔ ko ni efite mli. Kɛ atomɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ ato blema atomɔ shĩa ni mli ejɔ, ni awo nɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akabɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa fitemɔ kpaa ni ehaa shweremɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Is it good for me to tie my freshly harvested crops in plastic bags until I take them to the market?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa ehee lɛ awo plastic kotokui amli kɛyashi mikɛbaaya jara nɔ koni miyahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Tying fresh crops inside plastic bags traps heat and moisture, which causes the crops to sweat, build up heat, and rot rapidly before you can sell them.
ga: Nibii heei ni akɛwoɔ plastic kotokui amli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ latsaa, amɛbuaa dɔlɛ naa, ni amɛgboiɔ oya dani obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ.

english: What kind of containers should I use to collect my produce when harvesting on the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ tsɛnsi esa akɛ mikɛto nibii ni mikɛwo mli lɛ ahe kɛji mikpa nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should use clean, well-ventilated baskets or plastic crates that allow air to circulate around the produce and protect them from getting crushed.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ plastic tsɛnsi loo adeka ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii koni kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle he. shweremɔ ni ebu amɛhe koni akakumɔ amɛ.

english: Can I leave my harvested crops in piles on the farm ground for a few days before carrying them home?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi mikpamɔ lɛ yɛ ŋtayaa mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani mikɛya shia?

english: Leaving harvested crops exposed on the open ground subjects them to hot sunlight, soil pests, and moisture loss, which quickly degrades their quality and causes decay.
ga: Nibii ni akpa lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ. Kplukai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi Enɛ baafite oya yɛ ekpakpafeemɔ mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Why does my extension officer tell me to burn diseased plant parts that I cut off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mashã tso lɛ fãi ni hela emɔ amɛ ni mifo lɛ?

english: Burning infected plant parts completely destroys the fungi and pests inside them so the disease cannot spread to your healthy crops or live in the soil.
ga: Tso lɛ fãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ashãa lɛ baafite ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, hela lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli loo ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What should I do with rotting fruits that have fallen onto the farm floor?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ aduawai ni egboi ni gbeeɔ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he?

english: You must collect all fallen, rotting fruits and remove or burn them properly away from the field so they do not breed pests and spread rot to the rest of your trees.
ga: Esa akɛ obua aduawai ni egbee shi ni egboi lɛ fɛɛ anaa. ni ojie loo oshã amɛ bɔ ni sa yɛ he ko ni kɛ ŋmɔji teŋ jɛkɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛkafɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ amɛshwã tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it dangerous to leave crop residues sitting in the field for months after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli nyɔji babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Old crop residues left sitting in the field act as breeding grounds and shelters for insect pests and plant diseases during the off-season.
ga: Nibii ni egbɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai fɔɔ yɛ kɛ he ni amɛhiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I cover my harvested maize heaps with plastic sheets while trying to dry them outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ plastic tsɔne haa mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ he be mli ni mibɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni egbi yɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering wet grains tightly with plastic traps water vapor inside, creating a warm, damp environment that quickly causes mold and poisonous toxins like aflatoxin to grow.
ga: Okɛ plastic aha dumɔwui ni efɔ lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ, ni okɛ hulutsoo lɛ awo mli. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ tsofai fɔji tamɔ aflatoxin lɛ daa oya.

english: Why do my cocoa beans turn bad if I cover them too tightly right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji miŋa amɛ tsɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fresh cocoa beans need proper airflow during their initial fermentation and drying; tight covers lock in excessive heat and water, spoiling the quality of the beans.
ga: Cocoa yibii heei biɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa yɛ shishijee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ egbimɔ be mli. Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsiɔ la naa ni nu babaoo fiteɔ kɔfi yibii lɛ ahe.

english: How can I pack my harvested tomatoes so they do not get squashed when transporting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ mli koni akagu amɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ gbɛfaa mli lɛ?

english: Pack your tomatoes gently into shallow wooden or plastic crates with ventilation holes rather than heavy, overcrowded sacks that crush the lower layer of fruit.
ga: Okɛ tomatoi lɛ awo tso loo plastic adekai ni mli ekwɔɔɔ mli blɛoo. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bu yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛwo kotoku ni tsii mli ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to gather all my harvested crops immediately instead of leaving them scattered around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabua minibii ni mikpa lɛ anaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni mahã agbɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Gathering your crops immediately protects them from direct sun damage, unexpected rain showers, and damage by wild animals or farm pests.
ga: Kɛ́ obua oŋmɔshi nibii anaa oya lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ nɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baafite amɛ lɛ he. Nugbɔ ni nɛ trukaa kɛ nibii ni koolooi loo kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: What does 'value addition' mean for a farmer, and how does it help me get higher prices for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ‘sɛɛnamɔ ni akɛfataa he’ tsɔɔ kɛha okwaafoi? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ enɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi koni maná miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe jara ni nɔ kwɔ?

english: Value addition means transforming a raw crop into a processed product—such as turning fresh coconuts into oil or cassava into gari. This increases the shelf life of your harvest and allows you to sell to bigger markets at a significantly higher price.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ aaatsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɛɛ lɛ afee nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii, tamɔ ŋmei heei ni atsakeɔ awoɔ fɔ mli. loo cassava gari Enɛ haa onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ kɛyaa jara wulu ko nɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa nɔ.

english: How can I make more money from my coconut farm when selling fresh coconuts is no longer profitable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika babaoo kɛjɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Beni ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii heei lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he dɔŋŋ.

english: Instead of selling only fresh nuts to roadside vendors, you can add value by processing coconuts into coconut oil, dried coconut chips, or using the husk fiber for nursery mulch, which targets higher-paying industrial and grocery markets.
ga: Mohu ɔ, ngma ehe pɛ nɛ a jua kɛ ha gbɛjegbɛ nɔ jua yeli. Obaanyɛ okɛ sɛɛnamɔ afata he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ooofee ŋmeii fɔ lɛ nɔ. Coconut ni Egbi Aloo okɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ fibers atsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Ekɛ ehiɛ fɔɔ nitsumɔhei kɛ jarayeli hei ni shika babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do coconut prices drop when everyone in my district harvests at the same time, and how can I avoid losing money?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jara baa shi yɛ be mli ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ kpaɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mihe kɛjɛ shika ni mifiteɔ lɛ he?

english: When supply is high during peak harvest season, buyers pay less. You can avoid low prices by processing your harvest into non-perishable goods like oil or copra, which can be stored safely and sold when market supply goes down and prices rise.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ fa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baawo nyɔmɔ fioo. Obaanyɛ okpa jara ni baa shi kɛtsɔ onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni ooofee nibii ni fiteee tamɔ fɔ loo kopra lɛ nɔ. Abaanyɛ akɛ enɛ ato shweshweeshwe ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ́ jarayeli nibii lɛ ba shi ni amɛjara hu tee ŋwɛi.

english: My coconut tree flowers heavily, but most of the tiny young nuts fall off before growing big. Why is this happening?
ga: Mi ŋmei tso lɛ ewo fɔfɔi waa. Shi ŋmeii bibii Mɛi babaoo shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: Premature nut drop usually happens due to severe dry spells without enough water, nutrient deficiencies in the soil (especially potassium), or insect pests damaging the flower stalks. Adding compost and watering during dry months helps trees retain fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ baa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli (Titri lɛ potassium) loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni akɛ nu wo mli yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my coconut palms turning yellow and brown, and how will it affect my fruit production?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni te ebaaná minitsumɔ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often indicate a lack of nitrogen or potassium in the soil. When leaves lose their green color, the tree produces less food through photosynthesis, leading to fewer and smaller coconuts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo potassium bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ ehiɛ su eŋɔli lɛ Tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii fioo kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, akoko lɛ bafeɔ bibioo.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is lacking nutrients without sending it to a distant laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa ni mikɛyaaa laboratori ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ?

english: You can look at crop leaf signals: yellowish leaves mean low nitrogen, stunted roots or purplish leaves suggest low phosphorus, and burnt or brown leaf tips usually point to a shortage of potassium.
