ga: Obaanyɛ ona tso baai ahe okadii. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ loo baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Ni bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishifãi ni eshã loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa.

english: What is the difference between dwarf coconut trees and tall coconut trees, and which one should I plant?
ga: Kokoo tso bibioo kɛ kooko tso kakadaŋŋ Te amɛsoro amɛhe amɛha tɛŋŋ? Ni te nɔ ni esa akɛ adu?

english: Dwarf coconut trees grow shorter, start producing fruit much earlier (around 3 years), and are easier to harvest. Tall coconut trees take longer to fruit (6–8 years) but live much longer and yield nuts with higher oil content. Hybrids combine the fast fruiting of dwarfs with the strong yield of talls.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ daa kuku. Ejeɔ yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa (aaafee afii 3) ni ekpamɔ waaa. Kokoo tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii (afii 6-8) shi amɛhiɔ shi be babaoo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni fɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Hybrids kɛ dwarf yibii ni woɔ oya kɛ yibii babaoo feɔ ekome.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize between my young coconut trees without harming their growth?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ ni mifiteee ŋmei lɛ dalɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping works very well during the first few years while coconut trees are still young and small. Planting food crops or legumes between rows gives you continuous income while providing ground cover that reduces weeds around the trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni eyɛ bibioo Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa shika ni yaa nɔ kɛfataa ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ he koni eye ebua ni jwɛi ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ aba shi.

english: Why does my harvested cassava start spoiling within two days, and how can I stop this loss?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa nɛkɛ laajemɔ nɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots naturally rot fast after harvesting because oxygen causes rapid chemical breakdown. Processing the tubers into gari or flour immediately after harvest stops spoilage and secures the crop's financial value.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akpa amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ haa tsofai lɛ fiteɔ oya. Ni akɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii ni afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Ehaa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ kpaa, ni ehaa shika helɛtemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: How does proper drying of harvested coconut flesh affect the final quality and market price?
ga: Te ŋmei loo ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ saa bɔ ni ehi ha kɛ naagbee jara ni eyɔɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Drying coconut flesh into copra removes excess moisture, preventing mold growth and pest infestations. Buyers and oil processors pay higher prices for clean, well-dried copra because it yields higher-quality oil with longer shelf life.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi ŋmei loo lɛ awo ŋmei mli ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi mli lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa. Mɛi ni heɔ mu kɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ he nii lɛ woɔ kopra ni he tse ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ jara babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa mu ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa, ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What key things do extension officers look out for when inspecting a farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa ni mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baasusu he kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Officers examine leaf color, plant spacing, weed levels, and shade cover to spot problems like crop crowding, nutrient shortages, or over-shading before they harm production.
ga: Ofisa ni kwɛɔ baa lɛ su Abaanyɛ akɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ, jwɛi lɛ ayibɔ kɛ hulutsoo lɛ atsu nii ni akɛyoo naagbai tamɔ tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔ. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa loo shading ni fe nine dani enaa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do farmers plant plantain or banana trees in the same field as young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantain loo banana tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛduɔ kookoo bibii lɛ?

english: Plantain and banana trees grow rapidly with broad leaves that provide temporary shade, protecting delicate young cocoa plants from harsh sunlight while they establish roots.
ga: Banana dumɔwui kɛ tsei daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Buu cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Can growing plantains or bananas together with cocoa cause harm to the cocoa trees?
ga: Ani plantains loo banana ni akɛ kookoo duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye kookoo tso lɛ awui?

english: Yes, if left unmanaged or unharvested, fast-growing banana and plantain plants block too much light and compete aggressively for water and soil nutrients, suppressing cocoa growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ashi ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ loo akpaaa. Banana kɛ plantain tsei ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo tsɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ he. ni tsiɔ kookoo lɛ dalɛ naa lɛ

english: Why do banana plants seem to spread and grow so much faster than cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni banana tsei gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛdaraa oya fe cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Banana plants naturally possess high growth vigor and expansive root systems, allowing them to absorb nutrients and produce heavy foliage much faster than tree crops like cocoa.
ga: Banana tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ ni kɛlɛ kɛ shishifãi babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ baai ni tsii oya fe tsei tamɔ kookoo.

english: Why do my cocoa plants look thin and stunted when growing close to banana plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛhe efee shoo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ banana tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Heavy banana foliage casts deep shade that deprives cocoa of necessary sunlight, while their vigorous roots steal soil moisture, effectively suppressing the cocoa's growth.
ga: Banana baai ni tsii lɛ haa hulutsoo ni mli kwɔ ni haaa kookoo lɛ aná hulu la ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi ni wa lɛ juɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni etsĩɔ kookoo lɛ dalɛ naa jogbaŋŋ

english: What happens if I delay harvesting mature plantains and bananas in my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ plantains kɛ banana ni eda yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ tsɛ?

english: Delaying harvest allows companion crops to become overgrown and wild, which blocks air circulation and light, ultimately ruining the main cocoa crop beneath them.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa tsei ni fata he lɛ daa fe nine ni amɛfeɔ koo mli. Enɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la naa. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efite kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why is timely harvesting of temporary shade crops important for main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ ni akpaa yɛ be naa lɛ he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ?

english: Harvesting on time controls the canopy size, allowing enough sunlight to reach the underlying main crop so it can mature and yield well.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ be naa lɛ kudɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ dalɛ. Kɛtsɔ hulu la ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni eshɛɔ tsei titrii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛɔ edaa ni ekɛ yibii kpakpai baa.

english: Should I prune or remove old banana and plantain foliage after harvesting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo loo majie banana kɛ plantain baai momoi lɛ beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, clearing out old leaves and extra stems reduces excessive shade and prevents plant competition, ensuring your main crops get sunlight and space to thrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai momo kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni fa fe nine aba shi ni ebaatsi tsei akaŋshii naa. Enɛ baaha onibii titrii lɛ aná hulu la kɛ he ko ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting too much shade from companion crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cocoa tso lɛ miiná hulutsoo babaoo kɛmiijɛ tsei ni fata ehe lɛ amli?

english: If cocoa plants look tall, slender, weak, or produce pale, sparse leaves, they are likely struggling under too much shade and need more sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cacao tso ko tamɔ nɔ ni kɛlɛ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɛ hewalɛ, loo eyɛ baai ni etsake, ni ebɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, no lɛ ekolɛ eebɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ hulutsoo be babaoo mli, ni ehe miihia ni hulu la babaoo aná lɛ.

english: How do I balance getting extra food crops like plantain without ruining my primary cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee niyenii krokomɛi ni aduɔ tamɔ plantain lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni mifiteee mi-kookoo ŋmɔ titri lɛ?

english: Keep proper spacing between crops and regularly thin or harvest plantains so they provide gentle shade without overcrowding or suppressing the cocoa trees.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ahi ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ plantains ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo ni akpaa lɛ ateŋ daa. Koni ekɛ hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ blɛoo aha ni ekɛ cacao tsei lɛ eyimɔ obɔbɔ loo etsĩii amɛnaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow and rolling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellowing and rolling leaves usually mean your maize is suffering from nitrogen deficiency in the soil or lack of sufficient rain. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea when the soil is moist will help the plants regain their deep green color and grow strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ enɛko bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ eshishifãi ni wa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I stop small green worms from eating holes inside my corn leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ?

english: Those worms are Fall Armyworms, a pest that attacks maize across Ghana. You can protect your crop by checking the centers of the leaves early in the season and applying approved treatments or neem oil solutions directly into the leaf whorls before the pests destroy the growing tip.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa ŋmãa yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ni oookwɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ awo baa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ afite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpea in the same farm where I planted my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil naturally for your cassava plants. Planting them together also covers the ground quickly, preventing weed growth and keeping the soil moist during hot weather.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ kɛhaa o-cassava tsei lɛ. Hefatalɔi ni aduɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have wild, deep root systems that quickly absorb water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops can. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting gives your crops a fair chance to feed and grow tall without being choked.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛyeɔ nii ni amɛdaraa ni amɛtsiii amɛhe.

english: What causes my pepper plant leaves to curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the plant sap and spreading viruses. Controlling these small pests using neem extracts or soap sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem mli nu loo samla ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ahe nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the heat becomes too intense, when watering is uneven, or when there is too little phosphorus in the soil. Giving your plants consistent moisture and well-balanced compost helps the flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni fɔsfɔs fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ ooha tso lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is suitable for growing big yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii agboi akwɛmɔ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep, and well-drained soil so they can expand downward without bending or rotting. If your soil is hard clay or rocky, creating high mounds mixed with decomposed manure will help the yams grow big and straight.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa kɛya shi ni efoŋ loo egbooo. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛsaa Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ efutu mli lɛ ni ooofee lɛ baaye abua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my saved groundnut seeds fail to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut seeds fail to sprout if they were stored in damp conditions, damaged by beetles, or harvested before they fully matured. Storing thoroughly dried seeds in airtight containers mixed with clean wood ash keeps them healthy for the next planting season.
ga: Peanut dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nibii ni ŋmeii efite loo akpaa amɛ dani amɛdaraa kwraa Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ to tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni akɛ tso sũ ni he tse efutu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly humid conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let light and air into the farm and removing infected pods early stops the disease from destroying your yield.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni edɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni helai akafite onibii.

english: How can I tell that my plantain bunch is fully ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa?

english: Plantains are mature when the individual fingers look plump and round, losing their sharp side edges. You should cut the bunch while it is still firm and green so it can travel to the market without ripening prematurely.
ga: Plantains lɛ eda kwraa kɛ́ nine fɛɛ nine fee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe. Elaajeɔ esɛɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ ŋmeii amli be mli ni amɛyɛ shiŋŋ ni amɛji ŋmɔji lolo koni amɛya jara nɔ ni amɛkakwɛ̃ mra.

english: Do I need to plant both male and female palm trees on my farm for them to bear fruit?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni madu ŋmei tsei hii kɛ yei fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛwo yibii?

english: No, you do not need separate male and female trees. Palm trees carry both male and female flower parts on the same plant, so a single tree is capable of producing fruit on its own.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni ogbala tsei hii kɛ yei ateŋ. Palm tsei yɛ fɔfɔii hii kɛ yei ahe fãi yɛ tso kome nɔ. Enɛ ɔ he ɔ, tso kake pɛ ma nyɛ maa wo yiblii ngɛ lɛ nitsɛ e he.

english: How do crop flowers make seeds or fruits on their own?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe fɔfɔii woɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛdumɔwui loo amɛyibii?

english: Many crop flowers contain both male parts (which produce pollen) and female parts (which receive pollen) inside the same blossom. This allows the flower to self-pollinate and form fruit without needing another plant.
ga: Tso fɔfɔi henɔi babaoo yɛ nuu kɛ yoo fãi fɛɛ. (ni feɔ pollen) kɛ yei ahe nibii (ni nine shɛɔ pollen nɔ) yɛ fɔfɔi kome mli Ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ pollen ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛdu tsei krokomɛi.

english: Why do some of the flowers on my coconut tree fall off without turning into coconuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ akokoso tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛtsɔko akokoso lɛ?

english: For fruit to form, pollen from the male flower parts must successfully reach the female parts. If rain, heat, or a lack of insects prevents this transfer, the unfertilized flowers will simply fall off.
ga: koni nɔ ni jɛ mli ba lɛ aba lɛ, esa akɛ Pollen ni jɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fã ni ji nuu lɛ mli lɛ aye omanye ni eshɛ yoo lɛ fã lɛ he kɛji nugbɔ, latsaa, loo kooloi tsii gbɛ ni ekɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ fɔ lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Do I need bees and insects on my farm for my palm trees to produce fruit?
ga: Ani ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii he miihia mi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mi-palm tsei lɛ awo yibii?

english: While wind can move pollen, insects like bees speed up the process by carrying pollen directly from the male parts of the flower to the female parts, leading to better fruit production.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ajie pollen moŋ, shi kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii haa nifeemɔ lɛ yaa oya kɛtsɔ pollen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fã ni ji nuu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa yoo lɛ fã lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do flowers on the same palm tree look different from each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso kome nɔ lɛ yɛ srɔto lɛ?

english: Palm trees produce distinct male and female flowers in separate clusters on the same tree. The male flowers produce light pollen, while the larger female flowers grow into the actual fruit once fertilized.
ga: Palm tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei ni yɔɔ srɔtoi yɛ kui amli yɛ tso kome nɔ. Fɔfɔi hii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tseee, yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi yei wuji lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ anɔkwa yibii kɛji akɛ amɛwo fɔmɔ mli pɛ.

english: Why do some coconut trees on neighboring farms stay short while others grow very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ yɛ kuku ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɔ waa lɛ?

english: This difference comes down to the variety. Dwarf coconut varieties stay short and bear fruit quickly, while Tall varieties take longer to grow but produce larger fruits and live much longer.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔ nɛɛ damɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ. Kokooi bibii lɛ hiɔ shi be kukuoo, ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya. Kokooi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ shi ewoɔ yibii ni dara ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I choose which coconut variety is best to plant for my farm in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei srɔtoi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaakwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Your choice depends on your market. If you want quick yields for fresh drinking coconut water, dwarf varieties are best. If you want to produce copra or coconut oil, tall or hybrid varieties are preferred for their high oil content.
ga: Nɔ ni obaahala lɛ damɔ jara ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ oyaiyeli he miihia bo kɛha ŋmei nu ni anuɔ ehee. Dwarf henɔi lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Kɛji oosumɔ ni ofee ŋmei loo fɔ loo ŋmei fɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ loo ŋmeii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ atsu nii yɛ fɔ ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: If I plant a seed from a sweet coconut I bought at the market, will the new tree produce the exact same sweet coconut?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ ni mihe yɛ jara nɔ lɛ mli Ani tso hee lɛ baawo ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Not always. Coconut trees often mix pollen from neighboring trees, which means the seedling might inherit traits from different parent trees rather than being an exact copy of the fruit you bought.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui baanyɛ aná sui kɛjɛ fɔlɔi tsei srɔtoi amli. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso yiblii nɛ o he ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why are agricultural officers bringing foreign coconut varieties into Ghana instead of only using local ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛ maŋsɛɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi baa Ghana moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi pɛ baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Foreign varieties are often introduced to breed stronger crops that resist local diseases, produce higher yields, or adapt better to changing weather conditions on local farms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ maŋsɛɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛfɔ tsei ni wa ni helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛye amɛnɔ lɛ. Yibiiwoo ni fa loo ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant crop seeds brought in from another country directly on my land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui ni akɛjɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ aba lɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: It is best to source seeds through agricultural extension services. Foreign seeds must be checked and tested first to ensure they do not introduce foreign plant diseases or pests to Ghanaian soil.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni ana dumɔwui kɛtsɔ okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ nitsumɔi anɔ. Esa akɛ akwɛ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli klɛŋklɛŋ ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni ana akɛ amɛkɛ maŋsɛɛ tsei ahe helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai baaa Ghana shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong, so when the soil runs out of it, the maize plant pulls nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed the new growth on top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ etee lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmãa hee ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off before growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or too much water. When stressed, the plant tries to save energy and water by getting rid of its blossoms instead of producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. be kakadaŋŋ ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ mli loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli Kɛji haomɔ ba Tso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ato kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even when the green leaves look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or grows in hard, unworked soil, the plant spends all its energy making leafy stems above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akɛtsuuu nii nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ baato amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: How come my yam tubers are growing into twisted, branched shapes instead of straight smooth tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ daa ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ niji moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist and split when they hit hard rocks, compacted soil, or insect pests inside the mound as they expand downwards. Loosening the soil deeply before planting lets the tuber push down smoothly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbalaa kɛji tɛi ni wa, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, loo kooloi ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tswa amɛ be mli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and crack during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbalaɔ yɛ harmatta be ni nu egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds pull moisture out of broad plantain leaves faster than roots can drink from the dry soil. The plant cracks its leaves to reduce surface area and slow down water loss so it can survive the drought.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ plantain baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fiofio bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Black Pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly in cold, wet weather. Excessive shade and heavy moisture trap water on the cocoa pods, creating perfect conditions for the fungus to grow and destroy the pod.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shade babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa baaha nu amɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmei lɛ adara ni efite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my tomato plants to curl up and become sticky to touch?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji mɔ ko ta he?

english: Sticky, curled leaves are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies. As they feed on leaf juice, they secrete a sugary liquid called honeydew, which makes the plant sticky and leaves it vulnerable to black mold.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni ebɔle ehe ni wa lɛ baa, be mli ni amɛyeɔ baa nu lɛ. Amɛjieɔ nu ko ni mli edɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ honeydew lɛ kpo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ diŋ oya.

english: Why do my stored maize kernels turn into fine dust with tiny holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ sũ bibii kɛ buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Tiny insects called grain weevils bore into dry maize kernels to lay eggs. As the young insects hatch and eat their way out, they hollow out the grains, leaving holes and powdery dust behind.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ boteɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli koni amɛwo amɛwui. Kɛji kooloi bibii fɔ ni amɛye kpojee lɛ Amɛbaatsɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Eshiɔ bu kɛ sũ yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why does my pumpkin vine produce so many yellow flowers but no actual pumpkins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pumpkin wain tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi pɔmpii diɛŋtsɛ komɛi bɛ.

english: Pumpkins have separate male and female flowers on the same vine. Only female flowers grow into fruits, and they need bees or other insects to carry pollen from the male flowers to fertilize them.
ga: Pumpkins yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ wain tso kome nɔ. Fɔfɔi yei lɛ pɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ aduawai. Ni ehe miihia ni amɛwo ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii krokomɛi koni amɛkɛ pollen ni jɛ fɔfɔi hii amli lɛ aya koni amɛkɛbote gbalashihilɛ mli.

english: How do I know underground groundnuts are mature and ready for harvest without digging everything up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ efoŋ?

english: You can test maturity by digging up just one or two plants: if the inner shell of the pod has turned dark brown or black instead of white, and the plant leaves start yellowing, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka hewalɛnamɔ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome loo enyɔ ni oootsi lɛ nɔ: kɛji akɛ tso lɛ mli fã lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ. ni tso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ eshɛ nikpamɔ.

english: Can rice really grow well in places like Agogo, or does it only grow in traditional swampy areas?
ga: Ani ŋmãa baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei tamɔ Agogo, aloo ebaakwɛ̃ yɛ kusum naa hei ni ŋmeii yɔɔ lɛ pɛ?

english: Rice can grow exceptionally well in towns like Agogo and similar inland areas in Ghana because certain improved rice varieties thrive in moist valley soils and rain-fed plains, not just permanent swamps.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ titri lɛ yɛ maji tamɔ Agogo kɛ hei ni tamɔ nakai ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa henɔi komɛi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli shikpɔji ni mli efɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Jeee ŋshɔ ni hiɔ shi daa kɛkɛ

english: Is the Ashanti Region suitable for commercial rice farming?
ga: Ani Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛheɔ jarayeli?

english: Yes, parts of the Ashanti Region have abundant fertile land and favorable weather conditions that make rice cultivation highly successful and profitable.
ga: Hɛɛ, Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ fãi komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni hi ni haa ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ omanye waa ni sɛɛnamɔ hu baa.

english: How do I know if the land I have is suitable for planting rice?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Good rice land usually has soil that retains moisture well, such as clay or heavy loam soils, and is often located in flat areas or gentle lowlands where water collects naturally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa shikpɔji ni hi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ loo sũ ni tsii. Ni bei pii lɛ, amɛyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: Does rice always require a river next to the farm to grow properly?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ŋmãa adamɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, rice does not strictly need a river. Many high-yielding rice varieties grown in Ghana are rain-fed, meaning natural seasonal rainfall is sufficient if the soil holds water well.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni ŋmãa aná faa kwraa. Omɔ henɔi babaoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli lɛ fa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: How much land do I need to start growing rice successfully?
ga: Shikpɔŋ enyiɛ he hiaa koni anyɛ aje ŋmãa dumɔ shishi yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: You can start growing rice on as little as one acre, but having access to larger plots of land allows you to scale up production and make better use of farm tools and harvesting equipment.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa acre 1 pɛ aje shishi, shi shikpɔŋ ni da nɔ lɛ baaha onyɛ okɛ ŋmãa aya hiɛ ni okɛ okwaayeli nibii kɛ ŋmãa nibii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does rice need full sunlight all day to give a good yield?
ga: Ani hulu ni tsoɔ waa he miihia ŋmãa gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Yes, rice needs open fields with plenty of direct sunlight so the plants can photosynthesize, grow strong stems, and produce full, heavy grain heads.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa he miihia ŋmɔji ni hulu la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei nyɛɔ amɛfeɔ fotosintɛsis. kwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni wa ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni tsii ni eyi obɔ

english: Why is proper spacing important when I am planting my rice seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ he ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ he hiaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Giving rice plants enough space ensures they do not fight each other for soil nutrients, water, and sun, which allows each plant to tiller well and yield more grains.
ga: Kɛ́ aha ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha amɛkawuu amɛhe kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la, ni no baaye abua ŋmãa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Why do some farmers get very high rice yields while others on nearby land get very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi naa ŋmãa babaoo waa lɛ? yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ?

english: High yields come from using certified high-quality seed varieties suited to the area, managing weeds early, and planting on land with good water retention.
ga: Nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli babaoo lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ odaseyeli, ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni sa kɛha jɛmɛ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. Jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ mra kɛ dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hiɔ mli jogbaŋŋ nɔ

english: How many months does it take from the day I plant rice until it is ready to harvest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ ŋmãa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Most modern rice varieties cultivated in Ghana mature between 90 and 120 days, which is roughly three to four months after planting.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa henɔi ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwereɔ yɛ gbii 90 kɛyashi 120 mli, ni ji aaafee nyɔji 3-4 yɛ ŋmãa ni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm young rice plants more than other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii awui fe tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Young rice sprouts grow slowly in their early weeks and have shallow roots, making it easy for fast-growing weeds to choke them out and steal their water and nutrients.
ga: Omɔ tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo. yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli ni eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni no haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baamɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do farmers plant plantains together with young cocoa trees on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ plantains kɛ cocoa tsei bibii feɔ ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides essential shade to protect young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight, keeps the soil moist, and gives you plantains to harvest and eat or sell while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ni oyeɔ loo ohɔ̃ɔ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings wilting and dying when the sun gets very strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulu lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. Without shade from fast-growing plants like plantains, the intense sun dries out the soil and burns the cocoa leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni eshã kookoo baai lɛ.

english: What happens to the plantain trees when my cocoa trees grow tall and strong?
ga: Mɛni baaba dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa?

english: As cocoa trees grow and form a full leaf canopy, they need less shade. Once mature, you can gradually cut back the plantains so the cocoa trees receive enough sunlight to produce heavy pods.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ eda ni ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ baai. Amɛbiɔ hulutsoo be babaoo. Kɛji eda kwraa Obaanyɛ Ofo plantains lɛ fiofio koni cacao tso lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsii aba.

english: Will planting plantains next to my cocoa steal all the nutrients from the soil?
ga: plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ani mi-kookoo lɛ baaju niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If you leave enough space between them, plantains and cocoa can share the land well. Plantain roots feeder at different soil depths, and when plantain leaves drop and rot, they turn into rich organic matter that feeds the soil.
ga: Kɛji oshi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ Plantains kɛ cocoa baanyɛ aja gbɛ jogbaŋŋ. Plantain shishifã niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔi srɔtoi amli kɛ be mli ni plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ Amɛbafeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Can plantains pass plant diseases or bad insects to my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani plantains baanyɛ agbɛ tsei ahe helai gbohii loo kooloi bibii ashwã mi kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: No, cocoa and plantains are affected by different types of pests and diseases, so growing them together is generally safe as long as you clear weeds and care for the farm properly.
ga: Dabi, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi yeɔ cocoa kɛ plantain nɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, cocoa kɛ plantain ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe, kɛji akɛ obaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does growing plantains near my crops help keep moisture in the ground during dry weather?
ga: Ani plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, plantain stems hold a lot of water and their large, broad leaves block direct sunlight from heating up the earth, helping the soil retain moisture much longer.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantain tsei lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo. Ni amɛbaai wuji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni no haaa shibɔlemɔ ŋulami lɛ mli adɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be babaoo.

english: How long will I have to wait to harvest plantains compared to waiting for cocoa?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa plantains? Kɛ akɛto kookoo mɛmɔ he?

english: Plantains grow quickly and usually yield food within 10 to 12 months, whereas cocoa trees take about 3 to 5 years before they start bearing full crops of cocoa pods.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni bei pii lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nyɔji 10 kɛyashi 12 mli, yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ cocoa ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ shishi.

english: How do I know the correct spacing to leave between my plantains and cocoa plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni sa ni ka dumɔwui lɛ kɛ cacao tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa is typically planted about 3 meters apart in a grid pattern, with plantain suckers placed directly between them so both plants have sufficient room for roots and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduɔ kookoo yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai etɛ yɛ grid gbɛ nɔ. Akɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ji koni eha tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha shishifãi kɛ baai.

english: How can an agricultural extension instructor help me plan my crop field?
ga: Te okwaayeli he shweremɔ he tsɔɔlɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mato he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Extension instructors visit your farm to guide you on proper row spacing, soil preparation, pest control, and proper planting techniques tailored to your specific land.
ga: Tsɔɔlɔ ko baasara oŋmɔ lɛ koni ewo bo ŋaa yɛ gbɛ ni kã ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ, shikpɔŋ saamɔ, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ. kɛ dumɔwui ahe ŋaai ni sa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What kind of assistance can I get from the Ministry of Agriculture for starting a new crop farm?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ manyɛ maná kɛjɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ dɛŋ koni maje tsei ahe ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: The Ministry of Agriculture provides trained field agents, technical farming advice, educational workshops, and sometimes access to subsidized inputs or improved seedlings.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ kɛ ŋmɔ mli najiaŋdamɔlɔi ni atsɔse amɛ haa. Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he ŋaawoo tsɔsemɔ nitsumɔhe ni bei komɛi lɛ amɛnáa nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akɛyeɔ abuaa amɛ loo dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ.

english: Why are ants attacking my young cocoa plants so much during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shii abɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, natural food and water sources in the bush dry up. Ants migrate to young cocoa and tender crops because the new stems and leaves contain fresh moisture and sap that the ants need to survive.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ nu jɛɛhei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ baagbi. Akpɔlɔi fãa kɛyaa kookoo tsei bibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nu hee ni he hiaa ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ yɛ tsei kɛ baai heei amli.

english: Is there a safe chemical I can use to stop ants from destroying my newly planted crops?
ga: Ani tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ ni manyɛ mikɛtsu nii koni ŋmeii akafite miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu ehee lɛ?

english: Yes, there are approved insecticides and soil treatments specifically formulated to repel or control ants without harming young seedlings when applied in the correct dosages.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii kɛ tsofai ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ yɛ ni afee krɛdɛɛ koni akɛshwie ŋmeii loo akudɔ amɛ ni eyeee tsei bibii awui kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ bɔ ni sa mli.

english: How do I know if ants are the main reason my young shoots are drooping and dying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii ji nɔ titri ni haa mibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Ants often strip delicate leaves, build dirt nests around the base of young stems, or cultivate sap-sucking insects like mealybugs on soft branches, causing the plant to wilt and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋtayaai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei bibii lɛ ashishi loo okɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs awo tsei lɛ aniji bibii anɔ, ni eha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to spray chemical treatments against pests on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ ashwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to apply protective treatments early in the morning or late in the afternoon at the onset of the dry season, before pest populations build up and damage new growth.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ gbɛi ni akɛbuɔ he lɛ baatsu nii leebi loo shwane yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Dani tsɛŋemɔ helai baabɔ ni amɛfiteɔ dalɛ hee

english: Why do my newly planted crops seem to suffer more damage than my mature trees when the hot weather starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu ehee lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efite fe tsei ni eda lɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Young plants have tender stems, shallow root systems, and soft leaves, making them easier targets for hungry pests and more vulnerable to drying out compared to mature trees with deep roots and tough bark.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo, shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, kɛ baai bibii, ni no haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ akɛto tsei ni eda ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ amɛhewolo ni wa lɛ ahe.

english: What simple steps can I take to protect my young cocoa seedlings during the long dry season?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛɛ gbɛjianɔtoi ato koni akɛbu kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli?

english: Providing shade trees, spreading organic mulch around the base of plants to hold soil moisture, and checking regularly for early signs of insect attacks will help young seedlings survive severe dry spells.
ga: Too tsei ahe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo. Okɛ jwɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ abɔle he. Tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi. Ni kɛji akɛ akwɛ mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ebatutua amɛ lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei bibii ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni mli wa amli.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more intensely when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: When rain stops, wild plants dry up and lose their nutrients. Insects are forced to move onto cultivated farm crops to find water, sap, and food.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, koo mli tsei lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpai. Anyɛɔ kooloi anɔ koni amɛfã kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ amli koni amɛyatao nu, nu, kɛ niyenii.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me when pests attack my crops?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Extension officers visit farms to identify specific pests or crop diseases, recommend safe and effective chemical treatments, and teach best management practices tailored to your local area.
ga: Mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yaa ŋmɔji amli koni amɛyoo tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi loo tsei ahe helai. Tsɔɔmɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. ni otsɔɔ nitsumɔ nɔkwɛmɔ nifeemɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni kɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Who should I contact in my district when I face a severe pest outbreak on my farm?
ga: Namɔ esa akɛ mikɛ lɛ abɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ kɛ́ mikɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni naa wa kpe yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should reach out to your local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) district office or your assigned community agricultural extension officer for guidance and emergency advice.
ga: Esa akɛ oya kpokpaa nɔ nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) loo akutsoŋ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni ahala lɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ koni ona oyaiyeli ŋaawoo kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ.

english: Where can I find the official extension officer assigned to look after farmers in my community?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana extension officer ko ni akɛwo okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ adɛŋ?

english: Extension officers are typically stationed at the local District Department of Agriculture office, and they also make scheduled visits to local farmer groups, chief palaces, and community centers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ kpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe lɛ. Ayasara maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi akuu ko hu. maŋtsɛwe wulu lɛ kɛ akutso lɛ mli hei yɛ bei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ amli hu.

english: Can I use black mud or sediment from water bodies like lagoons to fertilize my farmland?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ sũ diŋ loo sũ ni jɛ nu ko mli, tamɔ ŋshɔ mli lɛ atsu nii ni mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Sediment from water bodies is often rich in decayed plant matter and nutrients washed down from surrounding land. However, you should let it dry out first and test a small area, as some lagoon silt can contain salt or chemicals that might hurt young plant roots if applied directly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni jɛɔ nu jɛɛhei amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsei ni egboi kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni nu lɛ efo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ oha egbi klɛŋklɛŋ ni oka he bibioo ko okwɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii loo tsofai ni baanyɛ aye tsei bibii ashishifãi awui yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii komɛi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How does spreading decomposed plant material and waste onto my soil help my crops grow better food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ahe nibii ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ni mikɛshwãa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Adding decomposed organic material acts like a sponge in the soil. It holds rainwater much longer during dry spells, improves soil texture, and slowly releases essential nutrients that crops need to produce heavy yields.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbo ni akɛfataa he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ kpo fiofio.

english: What type of cassava stem should I look for if I want to sell tubers to starch and gari processors?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso esa akɛ matao kɛji miisumɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ maha mɛi ni feɔ ashikiŋsha kɛ kari lɛ?

english: You should ask extension officers for high-starch improved varieties like 'Bankye HEMAA' or 'Sefa'. These varieties yield a higher percentage of dry starch and flour per tuber compared to traditional sweet varieties meant only for boiling.
ga: Esa akɛ obi osɛɛgbɛ nitsulɔ lɛ nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli tamɔ 'Bankye HEMAA' loo 'Sefa'. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni egbi babaoo baa mɔ kome nɔ. Kɛ akɛto blema sweet srɔtoi ni afee kɛha dãafeemɔ pɛ lɛ he.

english: Why does my harvested cassava start rotting and turning dark blue just a couple of days after I dig it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ ni etsɔ bluu ni mli edɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ ni mikɛfo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a natural outer bark to protect them once dug up, so high water content causes quick rot and oxidation. To stop this loss, you must process the roots into products like gari or starch within 48 hours of harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ amɛhe kɛji atsa amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni fa babaoo lɛ baaha egbo oya ni ekɛ okside aba. Bɔni afee ni okpa nɛkɛ laajemɔ nɛɛ Esa akɛ Otsu shishifãi lɛ ahe nii ni ofee nɔ ko, tamɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ, yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni akpa.

english: Why is it better to pile soil into mounds or ridges before I plant my cassava cuttings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ato shikpɔŋ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ ni efee gɔŋji loo ŋmeii dani adu ŋmei?

english: Loose, heaped soil makes it much easier for cassava roots to swell into large, smooth tubers under the ground. Mounds also drain excess water away during heavy rains so the cassava roots do not sit in water and rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Gɔŋ lɛ hu hoɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ akabote nu mli ni amɛkafite.

english: Is it better to plant my cassava stem cuttings flat in the ground or slanting upright?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ja nɔ?

english: Planting stem cuttings at a slanting angle (about 45 degrees) with the eye buds pointing upward gives best results. It ensures roots grow deep into moist soil while shoots easily grow into the sunlight.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ koŋ nɔ (aaafee digrii 45) ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, no haa nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ

english: How far apart should I space my cassava plants so they don't crowd each other out?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-cassava tsei lɛ amli bɔni afee ni amɛkabɔle amɛhe?

english: A recommended standard distance is 1 meter by 1 meter between plants. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, soil moisture, and nutrients to produce big roots.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ esa akɛ afee lɛ ji mita 1 x mita 1 yɛ tsei ateŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi wuji afee

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with plenty of leaves, but the roots under the ground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: This usually happens when soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. Nitrogen builds tall stems and leafy foliage, but plants need potassium to transfer energy down into swelling their tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen feɔ tsei ashishifãi kakadaji kɛ tsei ahe tsei ahe tsei. Shi tsei he miihia potassium koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba shi koni eha amɛ bulbs lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time that my planted cassava is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni mi-cassava ni midu lɛ baafee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Most improved cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can test maturity by carefully harvesting one or two roots from a sample plant to see if they are firm and filled with starchy flesh.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ oka tso lɛ shishifãi kome loo enyɔ ni ooojie jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ tso ko ni akɛfee nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ mli lɛ okwɛ kɛji eshishifãi lɛ mli wa ni eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Will planting cassava continuously on the same land exhaust my soil for future crops?
ga: Ani kɛ́ maya nɔ madu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afite kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, cassava feeds heavily on soil nutrients, especially potassium, over time. To keep your farm productive, rotate your cassava with leguminous crops like cowpeas or peanuts, which put nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Titri lɛ, potassium yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔ lɛ awo yibii Rotate cassava kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpeas loo ŋmeii. Enɛ haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. This often happens when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when we get too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits in the soil without draining, it suffocates the roots and encourages rot-causing fungi to attack the plant under the ground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before they turn into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they are stressed by dry weather, lack of shade, or when tiny pests like mirids attack them. It is also the tree's natural way of reducing extra flowers it cannot afford to feed.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen lɛ tutua cacao tsei lɛ. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ efoɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ eye lɛ hu.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a plant virus carried by tiny whiteflies. It can also happen when the plant experiences extreme heat and dry soil, causing it to curl its leaves to save water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ hiɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji tsei na dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each crop gets enough light and nutrients to grow strong and yields better harvests.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily once the bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that stay near the surface of the soil. As the heavy bunch grows at the top, the tree becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind to uproot it unless you support it with a strong wooden pole.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji kuu lɛ da yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa ni efo shishifãi lɛ. Ja okɛ tso ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants lose their flowers without producing fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants and destroys the pollen inside the flowers. When the flowers fail to get pollinated properly, the plant drops them to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ haoɔ ni egbeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen jogbaŋŋ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso he hiaa mi koni makwɔ ŋmei tso ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch sunlight, which the plant uses to feed and grow the underground tuber. Keeping vines off the wet ground also protects leaves from fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. ni tsei ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛkwɛɔ wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ahe helai ahe.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool and moist by slowing down water evaporation. It also stops weeds from taking over and turns into rich natural fertilizer as it rots.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛtsɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni amɛkaye nɔ ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it dangerous to plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a heatwave or dry spell before the main rains begin. If seeds sprout during this short wet window, the young seedlings will quickly dry out and die when the sun returns.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ dɔlɛ be loo nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nɛkɛ samflɛ kuku ni mli efɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baagbi oya ni amɛbaagboi kɛ́ hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: How many times in a single year can I grow and harvest rice on my land in Ghana?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ madu ni makpa ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nɔ yɛ afi mli?

english: Depending on your access to water and irrigation, you can harvest rice up to two times a year—once during the main rainy season and a second time during the minor season if you have a reliable irrigation system.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa ŋmãa shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli. Shikome yɛ nugbɔ be titri lɛ mli, ni shii enyɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji oyɛ nu shwiemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ Enɛ damɔ nu kɛ nu shwiemɔ ni onáa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does rice require so much more standing water to grow than maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ fe ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice roots are naturally adapted to grow in submerged soils, which helps suppress weed growth and ensures the plant receives continuous moisture needed to fill the grain heads properly.
ga: Omɔ shishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ sũ ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa tsei lɛ naa nu ni he hiaa be fɛɛ be koni amɛkɛwo ŋmaa yitsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice crop turning yellow instead of remaining bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your rice plants lack essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil drainage is poor, causing root damage that prevents nutrient uptake.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ o-rice tsei lɛ amli. Efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and overcrowd my rice field compared to my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni eyiɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli kɛ akɛto mi ŋmãa krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Young rice seedlings grow slowly during their first few weeks, allowing fast-growing weeds to capture available sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before the rice canopy can close.
ga: Omɔ tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli Enɛ haa jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ ŋmɛɔ.

english: Is it better for my yield if I sow rice seeds directly onto the field or raise them in a nursery first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo aaadu yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Transplanting seedlings from a nursery takes more labor, but it gives your plants a head start against weeds, resulting in stronger growth and higher yields than direct seed sowing.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ heɔ nitsumɔ babaoo. Shi ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ejie jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni mli wa kɛ yibii babaoo baa fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my rice crop is fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Your rice is ready for harvest when about 80% to 85% of the grain heads turn a clear golden-yellow color and the lower stems begin to turn brown.
ga: O-rice lɛ efee klalo akɛ obaakpa be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei aaafee 80% kɛyashi 85% etsɔ shika tsuru ni mli tse. ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ jeɔ shishi etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my harvested rice grains break into tiny pieces when I take them to be milled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ fãa bibii bibii kɛ́ atsɔ mli lɛ?

english: Rice grains crack internally and break during milling if the harvested crop was dried too quickly under harsh, direct sunlight or left in the field too long past maturity.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa mli fãa yɛ mli ni efoɔ beni ashɛreɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni akpa lɛ egbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi, loo ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ kɛyashi ebaakwɛ̃.

english: Why are my bagged rice grains developing mold and rotting after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ mli woɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rice mold occurs when grains are put into storage bags while still holding too much moisture; grains must be sun-dried thoroughly until crisp before bagging.
ga: Omɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmaa wo nitoo kotoku mli ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo eshwɛ. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani akɛwo kotokui amli.

english: How can I prevent pest birds from destroying my rice grains when the heads begin to fill up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi okpoi ni haoɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmãa lɛ beni ŋmãa yitsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛyiɔ lɛ?

english: Birds target rice during the softer 'milky' stage of grain development, so installing reflective ribbons, scarecrows, or clearing nearby brush early helps deter them.
ga: Okpoi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa nɔ kɛji ebɔi ‘mliki’ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ feemɔ, no hewɔ lɛ, okɛ tsɔnei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ, gbeyeishemɔi loo jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ awo mli mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi amɛnaa.

english: What can I do during harvest to ensure my rice grains are clean enough for local market buyers?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli koni mana akɛ miŋmaa lɛ he tse bɔ ni sa kɛha mɛi ni baahe nii yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Threshing your harvested rice onto clean tarpaulins rather than bare ground prevents mud, stones, and debris from mixing with the grains, making it attractive to buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ ashɛre ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ awo tarp ni he tse nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ, tɛi, kɛ sũ ni etse ehe lɛ kɛ ŋmãa lɛ futuuu. Ha efee nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ yɔɔ miishɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn very dark green after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ waa beni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Dark green leaves mean your cocoa trees are absorbing nutrients like nitrogen properly, which helps the plant manufacture food efficiently and build strength for pod production.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-cacao tso lɛ miihe niyenii tamɔ nitrogen jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa hewalɛ kɛha pod feemɔ.

english: Can local manure or compost work as effectively as imported chemical fertilizers for my crops?
ga: Ani maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ tamɔ tsofai ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, local organic compost enriches the soil structure and releases nutrients steadily over time, often keeping the soil healthier in the long run than imported chemical fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ kpo be fɛɛ be yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli fe tsofai ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ.

english: Does dark-colored soil mean my land is rich enough for growing cocoa?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ ediŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kookoo?

english: Dark soil usually indicates high organic matter content, which retains moisture and essential nutrients well, making it very suitable for cocoa cultivation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli. ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect the fertilizer I put around my cocoa trees?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Moderate rain helps dissolve fertilizer so roots can absorb it, but heavy downpours can wash the nutrients away before the plant gets a chance to use them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani tsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: How can I tell if the fertilizer I used is actually working on my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ kɛhaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: You will notice new dark green leaves sprouting, faster tree growth, increased flowering, and healthier pod formation within a few weeks to months.
ga: Obaana baai heei ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni miikwɛ̃. Tsei lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛhewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ otsii loo nyɔji fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why are some cocoa trees on my farm loaded with many pods while others right next to them have very few?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi eyi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ? yɛ be mli ni cacao tso ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Differences in soil nutrients, sunlight exposure, pest damage, or shade levels can cause neighboring trees to produce vastly different numbers of pods.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ sũ mli niyenii, hulu la, kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ amli. Aloo, bɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ afee ŋmeii ayibɔ ni yɔɔ srɔtoi kwraa.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I never apply any fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ko fataaa ŋmɔ lɛ he kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: Without added nutrients, the soil slowly loses its food supply, causing cocoa trees to produce fewer pods, show pale leaves, and become weak against diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he lɛ, fiofio lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite niyenii ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa helai yeɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why do young cocoa pods change color as they mature on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su beni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods start green or deep red to protect themselves while growing, and shift to bright yellow or orange when the seeds inside are fully ripe and ready for harvest.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ.

english: What causes young cocoa pods to turn black and dry up before they get big?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is commonly caused by fungal infections like Black Pod disease or pest attacks, which spread easily during wet weather if trees are not well pruned.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko tamɔ black pod hela loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ afooo tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How often should I feed my cocoa trees with fertilizer to get a high yield?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha mi cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛná yibii babaoo?

english: Cocoa trees usually benefit from fertilizer twice a year—once at the start of the major rainy season and once during the minor rainy season to support pod growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei náa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe sɛɛ shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni eye ebua ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why is proper watering so important for making my farm healthy and productive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni sa ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa koni miŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Water carries vital nutrients from the soil up into the crop. Proper and regular watering keeps leaves green, prevents stress during hot days, and ensures crops produce full, healthy yields.
ga: Nu hiɛɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni afeɔ daa lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli. Tsi haomɔ naa yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli ni oye obua ni ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii.

english: Should I rely only on rainfall for my crops, or should I actively water my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ pɛ nɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii? Aloo esa akɛ mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu?

english: Relying only on rain leaves your crops vulnerable to unexpected dry spells. Adding manual watering or simple irrigation keeps your farm green and thriving even when rainfall is unreliable.
ga: Nugbɔ pɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ oshara yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ amli. Ohe nu loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛbaafata he Ye obua oŋmɔ lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eshwere kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nɔ po.

english: How can I tell if my crops are actually growing well before it is time to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ?

english: A healthy crop shows deep green leaves, sturdy stems, and steady growth. If your field looks lush and colorful without yellowing leaves, it means your care and watering routines are working well.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa. tso ni mli wa kɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ Kɛji oŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe tseee ni baai lɛ efeee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ No tsɔɔ akɛ okwɛmɔ kɛ nu ni okɛhaa lɛ miiya nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up and turn yellow during hot, bright weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Yellow and dry leaves are usually a sign of moisture stress. When the sun is strong and soil is dry, plants drop leaves to save water, which stops them from growing proper fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ miihao. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli wa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ Tsei baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Enɛ haaa amɛwo yibii ni sa.

english: Why do some nearby farms look so beautiful and lush while mine struggles in the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji komɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ feɔ fɛo ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni minɔ lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ miiwuu lɛ?

english: Farms that stay green in hot weather usually benefit from consistent soil moisture, well-spaced planting, and good crop management, which protect plants from heat stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni feɔ ŋmɔji yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ náa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa lɛ he sɛɛ. Tsei ni aduɔ kɛ gbɛ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kpakpa Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Is it worth changing my traditional ways to try new farming techniques on my land?
ga: Ani ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ matsake mi blema gbɛi lɛ koni maka okwaayeli gbɛ̀i heei aka yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, adopting improved methods like consistent watering and modern field management yields bigger, healthier crops, turning your extra effort into much higher profits.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni atsake nɔ tamɔ nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba. Tsɔmɔmɔ mɔdɛŋ ni obɔɔ babaoo lɛ mli owo sɛɛnamɔi ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa.

english: How can a small farmer like me begin improving crop growth without spending too much?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi lɛ aje ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ shishi ni amɛfiteee shika babaoo?

english: You can start small by establishing reliable watering routines, using compost or fertilizer properly, and learning successful practices from experienced farmers in your district.
ga: Obaanyɛ oje shishi bibioo kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. Kompost loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni okase nifeemɔi ni yeɔ omanye kɛjɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Why is hard labor and daily care on the farm worth the trouble in the long run?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsumɔ ni wa kɛ daa gbi kwɛmɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sa haomɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Daily effort on soil care and watering prevents crop loss. The time spent pays off at harvest when you get high yields that secure your food and income.
ga: Mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ daa gbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite. Be ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ baafee nɔ ni sa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli beni onine shɛɔ yibii babaoo ni haa oniyenii kɛ shika ni onáa lɛ hiɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: How do I grow produce that is attractive enough to get top prices from buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu nibii ni ŋɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni maná jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ adɛŋ?

english: Giving crops enough water and nutrients yields larger, unblemished, and vibrant crops that market buyers prefer over smaller, water-stressed produce.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha amɛdara, nɔ ko nɔ ko akafee amɛ, ni amɛbaaná hewalɛ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayelihe lɛ miitao nɔ ni fe nibii bibii ni nu babaoo heɔ.

english: Can farmers in Ghana grow crops good enough to sell across borders to neighboring countries like Burkina Faso?
ga: Ani okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ husu lɛ naa kɛya maji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tamɔ Burkina Faso lɛ amli?

english: Yes, when crops are grown with reliable water and proper care, their quality meets export standards, allowing farmers to sell surplus harvest across borders for foreign earnings.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa miidu tsei. Nɔ ni hi lɛ baashɛ maŋsɛɛ nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ ahe mlai lɛ ahe. Ehaa okwaafoi hɔ̃ɔ nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛtsɔɔ husui anɔ koni amɛná shika yɛ maŋsɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and curling up tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually caused by small insects like whiteflies transmitting Cassava Mosaic Disease, which stops the plant from making food and growing healthy roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ whiteflies, ni ji ŋmeii mosaic hela lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afee niyenii ni ekwɛɛɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like pencils during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ pensil yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward during hot afternoons to reduce leaf surface area, which helps them save water and prevent drying out in excessive heat.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni baa lɛ hiɛ he lɛ aba shi Enɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ ni ehaaa baa lɛ agbi yɛ la ni mli edɔ fe nine mli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without setting fruit when daytime temperatures get too high or when moisture is irregular, which prevents successful pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa. ni tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa.

english: Why are my plantain bunches taking so much longer to grow and fill out during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa ni amɛdaraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains require large amounts of water to carry soil nutrients up into the fruit; when moisture drops during dry spells, fruit development slows down significantly.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba aduawai amli. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, tso yibii lɛ adalɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I cut down all the shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaf skins that burn under full sun; big trees act as protective umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo, ni amɛhaa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I put many seeds into a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds together forces the crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and small harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa, ni akpaa nii fioo.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce shells with no nuts inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts produce empty shells (called pops) when the soil lacks enough calcium, a vital nutrient the plant absorbs through its underground pegs to form seeds inside the pods.
ga: Peanuts baajie ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. (ni atsɛɔ lɛ pop) beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli koni amɛfee dumɔwui yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when heavy rain falls just before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa dani kpamɔ baa lɛ?
