english: Heavy rains soak the ground and cut off oxygen to the soil, creating wet conditions where fungi easily attack and rot the waterlogged cassava roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ baa ni ŋmeii tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do I find holes eaten into my pepper leaves in the morning, but I never see insects during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni yeɔ pepper baai leebi shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ minaaa kooloi komɛi?

english: Many leaf-eating pests, such as caterpillars and beetles, hide under leaves or in the soil during the hot afternoon sun and only come out to feed at night or early in the morning.
ga: Nɔ ni fata kooloi ni yeɔ baai babaoo ahe ji ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai ashishi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ni ebaaje kpo pɛ koni eyatao niyenii gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa.

english: Why does my harvested yam start growing long green sprouts even when stored in a cool barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii kakadaji akwɛ̃mɔ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally enter a dormant period after harvest, but after a few months, internal plant signals automatically wake up the tuber to sprout so it can grow a new plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes boteɔ wɔɔhe be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ Tsei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ bulb lɛ okadi akɛ amɛkwɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei heei.

english: Why is my maize turning yellow instead of dark green even when it gets enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for healthy green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help your crop regain its dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This leaves natural fertilizer in the soil for the next crop, such as maize, to grow bigger and stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, koni eda ni ewa.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or mites feeding on the plant's juices. Spraying the leaves with a mixture of neem leaf extract and water can help control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛ nu ni akɛfutu mli lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why are there small ragged holes in my corn leaves and dark waste in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Mɔ ni etse ni eyɛ fãi ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar hiding inside the growing point of the corn. Applying neem extract or recommended pest treatments directly into the center of the plant early in the morning kills the worms.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa lɛ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ko ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open clear field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn under direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain next to them provides temporary leaf cover and protects them until they are old enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Tso lɛ haa tso lɛ baa nɔ be kukuoo mli kɛ hebuu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yam vines produce tubers by converting sunlight into energy through their leaves. Staking lifts the vines off the wet ground so the leaves get full sunlight and remain free from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulutsoo be fɛɛ ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays around them in heavy soil without draining. Planting cassava on raised earthen mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from sudden water stress or extreme heat. Watering your plants consistently and placing dried grass mulch around the base keeps the soil moist and prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nu he haomɔ loo latsaa ni naa wa kpe amɛ. Ha tso lɛ nu daa ni okɛ sũ awo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he. shishi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni fɔfɔi akagbee shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to support the heavy weight of a maturing bunch during strong winds. Propping up the stem with a strong, bamboo or wooden fork stick supports the weight until harvest.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni ekɛfi ŋmeii ni eda lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni wa fĩ tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye ebua amɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce small fruits even if I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa moŋ.

english: Weeds act as thieves in your farm by stealing nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures all the food in the soil goes directly to growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo koni akɛtsu nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is pollination, and how does it actually help my crops produce more fruit?
ga: Mɛni ji pollination? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Pollination is when pollen is moved from the male part of a flower to the female part. Without this movement, flowers dry up and fall off without producing any pods or fruits. Proper pollination ensures that a higher percentage of your farm's flowers turn into harvested produce.
ga: Pollination ji be mli ni ajieɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ nuu fã lɛ mli kɛyaa yoo fã lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ko bɛ ni tsiɔ ehe lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo ŋmɔtɔ loo aduawai ko. Pollination ni sa haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa 100 lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmaa.

english: Can human beings manually pollinate crop flowers, or must we wait for insects and wind to do it?
ga: Ani adesai baanyɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwo tsei amli ŋmɔtɔ? Aloo esa akɛ omɛ ni kooloi bibii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Farmers can manually pollinate flowers by hand using small brushes or direct contact. While natural insects do this work, hand pollination guarantees that almost every flower receives pollen, leading to much higher crop yields.
ga: Okwaafoi baanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛdɛŋ atsu nii ni amɛkɛ brɔshi bibioo ko atsu nii loo kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛaashɛ he tɛ̃ɛ nɔ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ be mli ni adebɔɔ mli kooloi tsuɔ nɛkɛ nitsumɔ nɛɛ, Nine nɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi baaná fɔfɔi fɔfɔi. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baafee babaoo kwraa.

english: How can I measure my harvest to know if a new farming method is actually giving me more profit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu mikpamɔ lɛ he koni male kɛji gbɛi heei ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can track your gains by counting the number of healthy pods or bags harvested from a specific section of your farm before and after using a new technique. Comparing these counts shows you the exact increase in crop yield.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni oná lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii loo kotokui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akpa kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli lɛ ayibɔ ni oookane dani okɛ ŋaa hee lɛ atsu nii kɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ yibɔi nɛɛ to he lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ bo bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ etee hiɛ eha pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but very few turn into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ fɔɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ mli?

english: Many flowers drop off because natural pollinators like tiny midges might be missing, or the tree lacks enough nutrients to support every flower. Without proper pollination and care, the tree naturally sheds excess flowers.
ga: Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ afite, loo tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ aye abua. Kɛji akɛ pollination kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I spend time doing hand pollination instead of relying on traditional natural methods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛ miniji afee mifɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ mihe baafɔ blema, adebɔɔ mli gbɛi anɔ?

english: Relying purely on nature leaves your crop yields to chance. Hand pollination is a proven management practice that boosts crop production significantly beyond what natural insect pollination achieves on its own.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ adebɔɔ nɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ. Nine nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji nɔkwɛmɔ nifeemɔ ko ni ana akɛ ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ fe bɔ ni adebɔɔ mli kooloi ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ afee yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe.

english: Are all the small insects flying around my crop flowers harmful pests that I need to spray?
ga: Kplukai bibii fɛɛ ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Ani mifɔfɔi lɛ ji kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara ni ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsofa ashwie nɔ?

english: No, many small insects are beneficial pollinators that carry pollen between flowers so your crops can produce fruit. Spraying harsh chemicals without care can kill these helpful insects and lower your harvest.
ga: Dabi, kooloi bibii babaoo ji ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni kɛ pollen baa koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii. Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe nɛkɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ ni eha onibii ni onáa lɛ aba shi.

english: How quickly can I expect to see physical results on my plants after trying a new farm practice?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa gbɛ akɛ mana nɔ ni jɛɔ mitsei lɛ amli baa yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ beni mika okwaayeli gbɛ hee ko mikwɛ sɛɛ?

english: Some results, like improved flower retention or visible pod setting, can be seen within days or weeks, but total yield gains are fully measured at the end of the harvesting season.
ga: Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba lɛ ekomɛi ji hiɛyaa yɛ fɔfɔi ni ahiɔ mli loo pod ni anaa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo mli. Abaanyɛ ana enɛ yɛ gbii loo otsii komɛi amli. Shi asusuɔ nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ mliyaa lɛ he kwraa yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ naagbee.

english: Why does my neighbor's farm yield more cocoa than mine even though our land is right next to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ kokoo babaoo fe minɔ lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛŋkɛ wɔhe moŋ?

english: Differences in yields often come down to farm practices such as regular pruning, active pollination, soil fertility management, and controlling pests, rather than just location or soil type.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ daa, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ nɔ. kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ Jeee he ni eyɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ henɔ pɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to keep records and count my pods during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ saji awo wolo nɔ ni makane pods yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Counting your developing pods allows you to estimate your future income, plan for labor and storage needs, and identify which areas of your farm need extra attention before harvest time.
ga: Pods ni yaa hiɛ lɛ akanemɔ haa onyɛɔ osusuɔ shika ni obaaná wɔsɛɛ lɛ he. Too nitsumɔ kɛ nitoo he hiamɔ nii ahe gbɛjianɔ. ni oyɔse hei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why do some of my small cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ gboɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This is often due to poor pollination, nutrient stress, or fungal disease. When flowers are not well pollinated or the tree cannot feed all the young pods, it naturally aborts them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji pollination ni ehiii. niyenii he haomɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela Beni fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ loo tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ efɔfɔi bibii lɛ fɛɛ. Ebaaŋmɛ gbɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up into tight rolls during the afternoon heat in January?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmãa ni mli wa yɛ January shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense to protect themselves from losing water. During hot, dry weather like the Harmattan period in January, leaf rolling reduces the area exposed to sun and wind, helping the plant conserve its moisture.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi, tamɔ yɛ Harmattan beaŋ yɛ January mli lɛ, baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry out during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight and dry winds. Without shade plants like shade trees or plantains to protect them, they lose water faster than their roots can absorb it, causing the leaves to scorch.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ hulutsoo tsei loo plantains ni buɔ he lɛ bɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very thin instead of growing big and fat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ waa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee fɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to swell if the soil is too hard and compacted or lacks essential nutrients like potassium. The roots need loose, rich soil so they can easily expand and store starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe. loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baa nii lɛ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmli amɛshwã ni amɛkɛ ŋmeii ato mlɛo.

english: Why does my land grow better maize after I have harvested cowpeas or groundnuts from it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa kpakpa baa beni mikpa tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa kɛjɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their root nodules. This leaves behind natural fertilizer that nourishes the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ shĩɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves start turning yellow from the bottom of the plant going up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant is low on nitrogen or that the roots are getting too much water. The plant moves its remaining nutrients to the new leaves at the top, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce empty pods with no nuts inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called 'pops', occur when there is a lack of calcium in the soil while the pods are developing underground. Calcium is required for the seed inside the shell to form properly.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ 'pops' lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Calcium he miihia koni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ anyɛ afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers often drop when the temperature gets too high or when the plant experiences water stress. High heat causes stress, leading the plant to drop its flowers to save energy and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ haomɔ baa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why are my crops growing thick, dark green leaves very fast but taking a long time to produce fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi eheɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: This happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Excess nitrogen encourages rapid leaf and stem growth, but it delays flowering and fruiting because the plant focuses all its energy on vegetative growth.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ woɔ baa kɛ shishifã lɛ dalɛ oya he hewalɛ. Shi ebaaha fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo asɛɛ afo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ he nii.

english: Why does my mature plantain tree fall over easily when it produces a large bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya nɛkɛ? Ni ekɛ tso agbo ko ba?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the top of the soil. When a heavy bunch forms, the weight shifts the plant's balance, causing it to uproot easily unless supported with wooden props or planted in deep, well-anchored soil.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ yɛ lɛ Muji lɛ baatsake tso lɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa. Ehaa shishifãi ni aaawo lɛ feɔ mlɛo ja akɛtsu nii akɛ yelikɛbuamɔ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni ŋmɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers splitting open or growing out of shape under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli gbalaa loo amɛmiida ni amɛfite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers split or grow deformed when they hit hard, rocky soil or when soil moisture suddenly changes from very dry to very wet while the tuber is expanding rapidly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baagbala loo amɛbaafite kɛji shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tswa amɛ. Aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛyaa nɔ ni edɔ waa nɔ yɛ be mli ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya lɛ.

english: Why should I clear and plow my land with a tractor before planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ trakta ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni matsu nii dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Plowing breaks up hard soil, allows rainwater to sink in deeper, and buries weeds so your young maize roots can easily spread and absorb nutrients without competing with grass.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baagbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ni fuu jwɛi lɛ koni obi lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Why are my crops growing so poorly even when I apply fertilizer on land near muddy river streams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faa ni mli ewo muji lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: When nearby soil or water is polluted with heavy mud or chemicals from bad environmental practices, plant roots become choked or damaged, preventing them from taking up nutrients even if fertilizer is added.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ loo nu ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli eyi kɛ muji ni tsii loo tsofai ni jɛ shihilɛ mli nifeemɔi ni ehiii amli lɛ. Abaatsi tso shishifãi lɛ anaa loo amɛbaafite. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he po.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally refreshing the land so your next crop of maize grows strong without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa No hewɔ lɛ o-maise ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa waa ni tsofa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field with no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sun. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains to act as living umbrellas, keeping them cool and conserving moisture until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo tsei ni hiɛ ka. Ha tso lɛ mli ajɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak stalks and very small corn cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa baa.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem burns the plant's delicate skin and surface roots; it is best placed in a small ring a few inches away so the roots can safely reach out to absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ akɛwo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko mli. No ji inchi fioo komɛi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ajie amɛhe kpo koni amɛŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to conserve water. It goes into a resting state to survive the drought, and fresh green leaves will sprout once the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni akɛbu nu he. Ebabote hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Ni baai eŋɔli heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do caterpillars and worms attack my crop leaves right after the first rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: The combination of warmth and fresh rain causes insect eggs in the soil to hatch, and the young, tender leaves that sprout after rain are the primary food source these pests seek.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni feɔ ekome lɛ haa kooloi wuji ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ ji niyenii titri ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ taoɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my yam plants when the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are hardy wild plants that respond instantly to water, growing rapidly to steal food and light before your planted crops have time to establish their root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni kɛ nu shwie amɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Edaa oya koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ la atswa akaŋ dani otso lɛ aná be ni ekɛto eshishifãi lɛ ama shi.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are ready to harvest under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanuts lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the leaves of the groundnut plant begin to turn yellow and dry up, test harvest one plant; if the inner shells have dark markings and the seeds are firm, the whole farm is ready to be pulled up.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi lɛ Ha wɔka wɔkwɛ ni wɔkpa tso kome. Kɛji akɛ mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ ofee klalo akɛ obaajie ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them directly under the bright afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight dries out their tender leaves and soil too fast. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside them protects the young cocoa until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ gĩɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava lɛ kɛfata amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi cacao lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes when the hot sun comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi kɛ́ hulu lɛ je kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without forming fruit when the afternoon temperatures get too high or the plant lacks moisture. Providing light shade and keeping the soil evenly watered helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ shwane mli loo tsei lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ni mli tse ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni afɔ lɛ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer or water my crops in the middle of the afternoon when the sun is hottest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu woɔ otsei lɛ amli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Applying water or fertilizer during the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate quickly and can cause fertilizer to burn the leaves. Doing this early in the morning or late in the evening allows the soil to absorb nutrients and moisture safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashã baai lɛ. Enɛ ni afeɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a major food for plants. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves back their dark green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ ni ebaaha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen gas from the air and traps it in the soil through their root nodules. When these plants decay, they naturally feed the soil with nitrogen for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji legume weku lɛ mli bii, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ fite lɛ Amɛkɛ nitrogen haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ tsei.

english: Why do some farmers push cassava sticks straight into the soil, while others plant them slanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi tsiɔ ŋmei kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mɛi komɛi duɔ nii yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava sticks at a slant produces tubers near the soil surface, making them easier to dig up during harvest. Planting them straight down pushes tubers deeper into the ground, which helps the plant survive long dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ abɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaatsa yɛ nikpamɔ be mli. tsei ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to tie my yam vines to tall wooden stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akpɛtɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he beni edaa lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sunlight so they can catch more light to build big underground tubers. It also prevents soil-borne diseases from touching and damaging the leaves.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa hulu lɛ mli koni amɛná la babaoo ni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji. Ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ ata baai lɛ ahe ni amɛfite.

english: Extra small shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water in the soil. Pruning away all but one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree gets enough food to grow a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso bibii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ fɛɛ amli, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and becoming hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices out of the leaves. Controlling these insects using approved spray methods helps new leaves grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni baai heei lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why is it risky for me to clear my field and plant seed right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ mafo ŋmɔji amli ni madu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain after a long dry season is often followed by a short dry spell that can scorch newly germinated seeds. Waiting for the rains to become regular ensures there is enough lasting soil moisture for the crops to survive.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. No baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashã. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get stressed easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary canopy protection, keeping the soil moist and shielding the young plants until they are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ haoɔ oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋwɛitsu lɛ he yɛ be kukuoo mli. Enɛ haa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow starting from the tips down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green and build leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-based fertilizer gives the plants the food they need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛ eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛfee baai. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the soil lacks proper drainage. Planting cassava on raised soil ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots oxygenated and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put wooden stakes next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? ni ekɛ tso ko ma sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need tall sticks to lift their leaves high up into the sunlight. When yam leaves get plenty of direct light without weeds blocking them, the plant makes more food to grow large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ niji ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ shɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni jwɛi tsiii amɛnaa lɛ, Tsei lɛ baafee niyenii babaoo ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants and saw-dust like material inside the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ nibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that burrows into the growing center of the maize plant. Catching them early allows you to apply safe biological treatments like neem extracts or approved sprays to save your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni shwieɔ ŋmei tso ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ehaa okɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Koni okɛhere okpamɔ lɛ yiwala

english: Why do my tomato plants produce lots of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without growing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni aduuu tomato?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the soil suddenly shifts from very dry to very wet, or when temperatures get too high. Covering the soil with grass mulch keeps the moisture steady so the flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. aloo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi daa bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my plot after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, refreshing the land for future crops.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa he lɛ he jɔɔ koni adu nii wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny ears when I plant many seeds close together in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ toi bibii beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots compete heavily for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every single plant enough room and food to produce full, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛtoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight cups and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛmiikpa tso lɛ dalɛ naa lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is caused by tiny insects like whiteflies feeding on the sap and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these sucking insects early keeps the plant healthy so it can keep growing new leaves and peppers.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa curl baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhe wa No hewɔ lɛ abaanyɛ adu baai kɛ ŋmeii heei.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my crops right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive in tough conditions, so their roots quickly soak up water and food faster than crop seeds can. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your crops the advantage they need to grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii oya fe bɔ ni dumɔwui baanyɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why should I leave big trees on my farm instead of cutting them all down to make space for crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo amɛ fɛɛ koni maná gbɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Trees provide shade that protects crops from extreme sun, block harsh winds that break crop stems, and drop leaves that decompose into natural organic fertilizer for your soil.
ga: Tsei haa hɔɔŋ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni fiteɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ ahe. ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Will planting trees on my farm steal water and nutrients away from my food crops?
ga: Ani tsei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ mi niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ mli?

english: Deep-rooted trees pull nutrients and water from deep underground that crops cannot reach, bringing those nutrients up to the surface leaves which eventually fall and feed your crops.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Ekɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ baa baai lɛ anɔ he ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: What kind of trees can I plant alongside my crops to improve my land while earning extra money?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni mikɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ni maná shika babaoo?

english: You can plant fruit trees like citrus or economic trees like cashew and leguminous shade trees; they restore soil fertility by trapping nitrogen while giving you extra produce to sell.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei ni woɔ yibii tamɔ citrus loo shika helɛtemɔ tsei tamɔ cashew tsei kɛ nut tsei ni haa hulutsoo. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛmɔɔ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni amɛhaa bo nibii krokomɛi ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: My farmlands have become dry, hard, and poor since all the natural trees were cut down; how can I fix the ground?
ga: Miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehiii kwraa ejaakɛ afolɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei lɛ fɛɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: You can revive degraded land by planting fast-growing leguminous cover crops and shade trees, which loosen hard soil with their roots and trap moisture in the earth.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ kɛ hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do plants put nutrient goodness back into old farmlands that no longer grow healthy crops?
ga: Te tsei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa ŋmɔshi shikpɔji momo ni nyɛŋ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: Certain plants and trees take nitrogen from the air and fix it directly into the soil through their roots, acting as free natural fertilizer for worn-out ground.
ga: Tsei kɛ tsei komɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ.

english: Is it harmful to burn dry leaves and trees on my farm to clear the land before planting?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ mashã baai kɛ tsei ni egbi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛjie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ dani adu?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and good soil microbes that hold moisture; letting dead plant matter rot naturally builds healthy topsoil instead.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii kpakpai ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba moŋ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away all my good topsoil now that there are no trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ? Amrɔ nɛɛ ni tsei bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tree roots act like nets that hold the soil together during storms, while leaves break the fall of heavy raindrops so water can gently sink into the ground instead of washing soil away.
ga: Tso shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋshɔŋloo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ ahum be mli. yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ. koni nu lɛ Atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fiofio yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning brown and drying up during the hot season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ moŋ?

english: Without shade trees to cool down the field, extreme heat causes crops to lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up from the hot ground.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni haa ŋmɔji lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tall crops like maize keep falling over during strong rainstorms, and how do trees help?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ ahum ni naa wa waa mli lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei baanyɛ aye abua?

english: Trees act as living windbreaks that slow down heavy storm gusts before they hit your open field, protecting tall crops from being blown down.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hiɛ ka ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ahum ni naa wa lɛ baa shi dani etswaa oŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ahe koni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa amɛ.

english: Why is it important to protect natural forests near our farming communities?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni abu adebɔɔ mli kooi ni bɛŋkɛ wɔ okwaayeli akutsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Forests regulate local rainfall patterns and cool down the air across the whole region, keeping local weather stable enough for your farm crops to grow properly.
ga: Kooi kudɔɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Ha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni oŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the nutrient that gives plants their green color and growth energy. It can also happen when the soil stays too wet for long periods, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni haa tsei feɔ ŋmɔji ni ehaa hewalɛ koni amɛdara Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye nii.

english: Why do some of my corn cobs have missing grains or empty spaces along the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when high heat or drought strikes right when the corn is flowering. If the silks dry up before pollen lands on them, those kernel spots will not fertilize or form seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ba beni ŋmãa lɛ ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ siliki tsɔji lɛ gĩ dani pollen lɛ kpɛtɛ siliki tsɔji lɛ ahe lɛ, Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ewooo fɔ loo ebaafee dumɔwui.

english: Why do my cassava leaves drop off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants intentionally drop their leaves during dry conditions to conserve water. By shedding leaves, the plant stops water from evaporating into the air, allowing the roots to survive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Tsei tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside leaf funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the soft, tender inner leaves of young corn. They hide deep inside the funnel of the plant where it is dark and moist, eating the new growth before the crop can mature.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa mli baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why does my harvested corn develop black mold when I store it in a room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ kɛ́ mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn ears still contain high moisture when newly harvested. Storing damp corn inside a closed room without proper airflow traps the moisture, creating a wet environment where destructive molds thrive.
ga: Abɛi toi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo lolo kɛ́ akpa amɛ ehee. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni mli efɔ to tsu ko ni aŋã mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmãa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How can I check if my harvested corn is dry enough to safely put into storage bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo baagi mli shweshweeshwe?

english: Press your thumbnail hard into a grain. If it leaves a soft dent, the corn is still too wet. Properly dry corn feels rock hard, and dropping a handful of grains onto a hard surface should create a sharp, metallic ringing sound.
ga: Nyɛɛ omfoniri bibioo lɛ nɔ waa. Ha lɛ tso ŋmãa he mfoniri. Kɛji ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ba Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lolo. Abɛi ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ewa tamɔ tɛ. Ni kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui fioo ko shwie nɔ ko ni wa nɔ lɛ, ehaa gbee ni naa wa ni tamɔ dade ni tswaa lɛ baa.

english: Why do tiny holes and white powdery dust appear on my stored dried corn after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni sũ yɛŋ je kpo yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ nɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: The small holes and white dust are caused by grain weevils. These tiny insects burrow inside the dry corn kernels to feed on the inner starch and lay their eggs, turning the insides of the grains into fine powder.
ga: Buji bibii kɛ sũ yɛŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmãa ŋmeii kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii. Ha ŋmãa lɛ mli atsɔ ŋmãa kpakpa.

english: Why does grass growing close to my corn plants make the corn stalks weak and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds and grass compete directly with your crop for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When weeds crowd young corn, the corn stalks stretch upward to reach sunlight, making them tall, thin, and prone to falling over.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ eyi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbee shi.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting cowpeas alongside maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cowpea kɛfata ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This enriches the soil, sharing nutrients that help neighboring maize grow stronger without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo. ni amɛja niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni edara waa ni jarayeli ŋmãa babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly in areas where water stays standing after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When water sits on top of the soil for days, it fills up all the air spaces around the plant roots. Without air, root tissues suffocate, turn black, and can no longer absorb nutrients to feed the growing plant.
ga: Kɛ nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Shishifã lɛ mli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi. etsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ niyenii ni haa tso ni miida lɛ niyenii dɔŋŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi koko tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Taller trees or plantain crops shield young cocoa from harsh sun and strong winds, keeping the soil cool and moist so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei kakadaji loo dumɔwui buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tuber through their leaves using sunlight. Guiding the vines up tall sticks spreads the leaves out to catch sunlight and airflow, preventing leaf diseases and helping the tuber grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ wain tso lɛ ba tso nine ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaagbɛ ebaa lɛ eshwa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the ground that stops the sun from evaporating water from the soil too fast. It keeps the roots cool, conserves moisture, and eventually decomposes into nutrient-rich organic manure.
ga: Hay tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la akajie nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the stalk usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Applying proper fertilizer like NPK or compost gives the soil the nutrients the plant needs to turn green and form healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa, tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curling leaves in pepper plants are often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids feeding on the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Protecting the crop early with neem oil spray helps keep new leaves growing flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ baa. Nibii ni abuɔ he mra Kɛtsɔ neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai heei daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, damp, and shady conditions. Pruning excess cocoa branches and clearing weeds allows sunlight and fresh air to dry the pods faster, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fuŋ ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Kookoo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ oya. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Why are flowers falling off my tomato plants without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress or drought. When the plant does not get enough water during high temperatures, it drops its blossoms to conserve energy rather than trying to nourish fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ mli baa lɛ. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ Ebaafɔlɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato moŋ fe ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha aduawai lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside when heavy rains flood the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rains waterlog the farm for days, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing the tubers to drown and allowing rot-causing soil fungi to infect them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ha nu yi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni miifite lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunch grows large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni aduawai akuu lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and spread sideways near the soil surface rather than going deep. As the fruit bunch gets heavier, the heavy top pulls the shallow roots right out of soft, wet soil, which is why tall sticks are needed to prop up the stem.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa yɛ afãgbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shɔŋŋ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ bafee nɔ ni tsii lɛ Yiteŋ fã ni tsii lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni akɛ tso lɛ atsu nii koni akɛfi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to grow properly if I plant right after the very first small rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first light rain only moistens the top inch of soil, while the ground deeper down remains bone dry. If rain stops for a few days after, the scorching sun quickly dries out the surface and burns the tender emerging seed sprouts.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ pɛ mli fũu. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli egbi lolo lɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ oya ni eshãa dumɔwui ni egbɔjɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and provide wide leaves that act as natural shade, protecting the cocoa saplings and keeping the soil moist during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main tree. Removing most of them and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main plant grows strong enough to yield a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo kɛjɛ mli ni ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni ená hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant regain its color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni tso lɛ aya hiɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená ehiɛ su kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my maize if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil food. This results in thin, weak stalks with small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli loo ŋmeii bɛ mli kwraa.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my maize leaves with small caterpillars inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii Yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the soft leaves. Catching them early and applying bio-pesticides or recommended spray protects the crop from being destroyed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ. Mɔ amɛ mra. Ni tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil cuts off air supply, allowing fungi to attack and cause the underground tubers to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves toward sunlight to produce energy for growing big underground tubers. Staking holds leaves off wet ground, capturing sunlight and preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni baa lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ shi kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ. Emɔɔ hulu la ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Tomato plants drop flowers due to extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping soil evenly moist and well-nourished helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ laajeɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni ehi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and growing very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking plant sap and spreading viruses. Controlling these pests early stops the curling and restores normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shweremɔ ni sa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if they are just growing in the same farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. By clearing weeds early, you ensure your crops receive all the food they need to give a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Obaanyɛ oná nɔmimaa akɛ onibii lɛ baaná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it best for me to spray my crops very early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ tsofa lɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ?

english: Early morning has cooler temperatures and calm air. This allows crop leaves to properly absorb liquid treatments before the intense heat of the sun causes the liquid to evaporate.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni yɔɔ dioo baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ nuɔ nu ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani hulu ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: What will happen to my crops if I spray them while the hot sun is high in the sky?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ be mli ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋwɛi?

english: Spraying during hot weather can burn or scorch your crop leaves because liquid droplets act like magnifying glasses under heat, and the spray dries up before the plant can absorb it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo eshã tso lɛ baai. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu mli nu ni hoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo yɛ la ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Ni tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: How does strong afternoon heat affect how my crops take in water and nutrients?
ga: Te shwane mli latsaa lɛ saa bɔ ni mitsei lɛ heɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ amɛhaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When heat is intense, plants experience stress and lose moisture quickly. During this time, their pores close up to save water, making it harder for them to take in sprayed nutrients.
ga: Kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa lɛ Tso lɛ naa haomɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ oya. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Amɛ ŋmeii lɛ efo kwraa koni amɛbu nu he. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa amɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Does strong sunlight weaken the power of the chemical spray I put on my farm?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi?

english: Yes, intense sunlight and high heat break down the active ingredients in many agricultural sprays very quickly, making them much less effective against pests and diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni yɔɔ okwaayeli mli tsofai babaoo amli lɛ oya. Enɛ haaa etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Is it dangerous if water mixed with fertilizer or spray gets into my mouth?
ga: Ani oshara yɛ he kɛji nu ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi efutu mli lɛ bote odaaŋ?

english: Yes, water mixed with farm chemicals contains harmful substances that are toxic to human health. You should never ingest farm chemical water or let farm animals drink it.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ efutu mli lɛ yɛ nibii ni yɔɔ oshara ni yeɔ adesai ahewalɛ nɔ. Esaaa akɛ onuɔ tsofa nu yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɔkɔɔkɔ loo oŋmɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi gbɛ ni amɛnuɔ.

english: What safety precautions should I take so chemical spray doesn't enter my body while working?
ga: Mɛɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he gbɛjianɔtoi esa akɛ mafee? Koni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ akabote gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli beni etsuɔ ​​nii lɛ

english: Always wear protective gear like long sleeves, face masks, and goggles. Stand upwind while spraying so the vapor blows away from you, and wash your hands thoroughly with soap before eating or drinking.
ga: Wo hebuu nibii tamɔ shɛɛtii ni hiɛ nine kakadaji kɛ masks. kɛ glase be fɛɛ be Damɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli beni okɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ koni lasu lɛ ajie kɛjɛ ohe. Ni okɛ samla afɔ oniji ahe jogbaŋŋ dani oye nii loo onu nii.

english: Can applying liquid fertilizer too many times harm my crops?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli shii abɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, over-applying chemical mixtures can overload the plant, causing root burn, leaf yellowing, or even killing the crop completely. Always follow recommended application schedules.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei atsu nii fe nine. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi ni shãa, baai ni tsuɔ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpãtãa kwraa. Nyiɛmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbiɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops look burnt after I apply liquid spray?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mikɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf burn happens when chemical mixtures are too strong, applied too frequently, or sprayed during the hottest part of the day when the sun amplifies the liquid's effect on the leaves.
ga: Baai shãa baa kɛji tsofa ni akɛfutu lɛ mli wa tsɔ, akɛwo mli shii abɔ tsɔ, loo akɛshwie nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni hulu la lɛ haa hewalɛ ni nu lɛ yɔɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Should I spray my crops multiple times in a single day to get faster results?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ shii abɔ yɛ gbi kome mli koni maná nɔ ko oya?

english: No, crops only need one proper application according to the recommended schedule. Spraying multiple times a day damages the plant and wastes expensive input materials.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ ni akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ shikome pɛ yɛ be ni ato he ŋaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie tso lɛ nɔ shii abɔ yɛ gbi kome mli lɛ, efiteɔ tso lɛ ni efiteɔ nibii ni jara wa.

english: Why does liquid spray stay on my crop leaves longer when the air is cool?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ hiɔ mitsei lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ?

english: Cool air holds humidity and prevents fast evaporation. This allows the liquid to stay on the leaf surface long enough for the crop to fully soak up the nutrients or medicine.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa efo oya. Enɛ haa nu lɛ hiɔ baa lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni tso lɛ aŋɔ niyenii loo tsofa lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or shade trees to protect them from heat and keep the soil moist until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ baabu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baa mli.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees if I want them to produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ cacao tso ni eda lɛ nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni mawo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning extra or overlapping branches allows sunlight and airflow to reach all parts of the tree, which prevents damp diseases and directs the tree's energy into growing big, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ hela ni mli edɔ naa. ni okɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why are the green pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Removing infected pods regularly and opening up the canopy to let in air helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa ni agbeleɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What causes the young shoots on my cocoa trees to get brown spots and die back during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by small insects called capsids (or mirids) that suck sap from young stems and pods, causing leaves and shoots to dry up and die back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Atsɛɔ amɛ capsids (loo mirids), ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Ehaa baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers before forming any fruits during periods of high heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water during hot periods, they drop their flowers as a survival mechanism to conserve water and protect the main plant from dying.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nu nɔ ni abuɔ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ gbele he.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to produce green leaves and make energy for growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛfee hewalɛ kɛha dalɛ.

english: How do weeds actually reduce my harvest if there is enough soil for all the plants in the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha mikpamɔ lɛ aba shi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your main crops, leaving your plants weak and unable to yield well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs extra fertilizer or manure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi awo mli?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have pale leaves, or yield smaller fruits than usual despite getting enough water, the soil is likely low on nutrients and needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ miida blɛoo, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewoɔ yibii bibii fe bɔ ni ewoɔ daa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ enine shɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ moŋ. Etamɔ nɔ ni niyenii hu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Is it safe to plant cassava right next to my young cocoa trees, or will it hurt the cocoa?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ masɛi? Aloo ebaafite kookoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots grow very large and aggressively absorb water and nutrients from the soil, which can choke and stunt nearby young cocoa seedlings if planted too close.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ dara waa ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods so the beans inside don't spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ? Enɛ ji koni kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akafite.

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when their skin changes completely from green or dark red to a bright yellow or orange color; picking them too early or late reduces bean quality.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji amɛhiɛ tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse waa. Kɛ́ ajie mra loo sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ahe afee fɛo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green leaves so the maize can grow strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with many leaves, but the roots under the ground are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy foliage instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and tender roots that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains beside them creates natural shade and traps soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Nurse tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ Ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Staking spreads out the yam leaves so they can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which is then sent down into the ground to swell the yam tubers.
ga: Gbalamɔ o-sweet potato baai lɛ amli koni onine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, akɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets extremely hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɛ

english: Why does my mango tree drop most of its small young fruits before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ shwieɔ eyibii bibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young mango fruits drop early mainly due to sudden dry spells, lack of nutrients, or attacks from fruit flies. Ensuring light watering during dry periods and keeping fruit flies away helps the fruits stay attached until harvest.
ga: Mango aduawai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya, bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbiɔ trukaa, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, loo aduawai amli ŋmeii tutuaa amɛ. Nu fioo ni akɛhaa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli, ni ajieɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoot suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many suckers allows them to steal water and food from the mother plantain tree. Removing extra shoots leaves only the strongest stem to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ feɔ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: What happens to my maize if I plant too many seeds in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are crowded together, the seedlings compete fiercely for soil food, water, and light, resulting in thin, weak stems and tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua dumɔwui lɛ anaa lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ la mli lɛ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?
