english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids hiding on the underside of the leaves, which can also spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ashwã tsei amli hu

english: Why are there ragged holes appearing in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yaafo nu ko jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes inside the central funnel of young maize plants are typically caused by hungry caterpillars like fall armyworms feeding on the tender new leaves at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ fall armyworms, ni yeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive rain washes away vital nutrients like nitrogen from the topsoil and fills soil air pockets with water, suffocating the roots so the crop cannot feed properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ. ni okɛ nu afata kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my seeds after I plant them on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ midumɔwui lɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too shallowly on loose, bare soil leaves them vulnerable to water runoff. Covering the soil with organic matter like dry grass and planting at the correct depth holds the seeds firmly in place.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ dumɔwui lɛ oya. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ dumɔ yɛ he ni sa lɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ ahi amɛhe.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees on the same plot as my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ mikoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, keeping the cocoa shaded and cool during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa edɔɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant cassava together with my maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving space and light for the slower-growing cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi he ko kɛ la koni ŋmei ni miida blɛoo lɛ atsɔ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why are ants building mounds around the base of my cassava stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii feɔ gɔji kɛbɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ? Mi ŋmei ŋmei?

english: Ants are usually attracted to tiny sap-sucking insects like mealybugs living on your crops. The ants feed on the sweet liquid those pests produce, which signals that your plants may have an insect attack underlying the soil surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs ni hiɔ onibii amli lɛ gbalaa amɛ. Ants yeɔ nu ni ŋɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai feɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ebatutua otso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why are my pepper plants drooping during the day even though the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ? He ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ lɛ?

english: Daytime wilting in wet soil usually means root rot or a soil disease has damaged the root system, preventing the plant from absorbing water fast enough to keep up with the sun's heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ egbo loo hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛye hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How deep should I place my maize seeds in the soil during planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ yɛ dumɔ be mli?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep. Planting too shallow leaves seeds weak and exposed, while planting too deep wastes the seed's energy before it can sprout above ground.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimita 3 kɛyashi 5. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛje kpo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hewalɛ afite dani amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it good for my crop field if I burn all the dried bushes before planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mishã tsei bibii ni egbi lɛ fɛɛ dani midu?

english: While burning clears the land quickly, it kills beneficial soil organisms and destroys organic matter that keeps the soil fertile and moist for your crops.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ oya. Shi ekpãtãa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛha onibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plants experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of balanced nutrients, which prevents the flowers from successfully pollinating.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa bɛ mli. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni yeɔ omanye.

english: Why does my harvested maize get eaten by insects inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ miiye mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Storing maize before it is completely dry leaves hidden moisture inside the grains, creating an warm, damp atmosphere that attracts storage beetles and encourages mold growth.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa to dani egbi kwraa lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa ŋmãa lɛ mli. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ gbalaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize turn yellow when there is too much standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water sits on your farm for too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil. Crop roots need air to breathe and collect nutrients; without it, the roots choke, and the leaves turn yellow from lack of food.
ga: Kɛ nu hi oŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu ni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ato. Kɛ́ ebɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni bɛ hewɔ.

english: What simple step can I take on my land to stop heavy rains from flooding my field?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akaho miŋmɔji lɛ amli?

english: You can dig narrow drainage channels or ditches around and between your farm rows. These channels give excess rainwater a path to flow away into streams or low areas before it stays and rots your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu homɔ gbɛi bibii loo nubui yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋtayaai lɛ ahe kɛ amɛteŋ. Nɛkɛ gbɛi nɛɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa faai loo hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli. Dani ebaatsɔ ais ni efite onibii

english: How does planting my crops on raised soil mounds or ridges help them survive heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mitsei lɛ ni mikɛduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Raised mounds elevate the main roots above the water level. Excess rain collects in the valleys between ridges, keeping the main root system from drowning while still providing moisture.
ga: Awoɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni akɛwo shishifãi titrii lɛ anɔ kɛho nu lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ gɔji lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa shishifã titri lɛ shwieee nu mli yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lolo.

english: If the heavy rains do not start in June like they usually do, how do I decide when to plant my seeds?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ejeee shishi yɛ June mli tamɔ bɔ ni eji daa lɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ be ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ he?

english: Instead of relying on specific months on the calendar, wait for the first two or three steady, deep rains that thoroughly soak the soil before planting, ensuring the seeds have enough moisture to germinate safely.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ nyɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ yɛ kalanda lɛ nɔ lɛ, mɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ dani odu. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: What happens to my mature crops if heavy rains continue late into November when it should be dry?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa lɛ tee nɔ nɛ kɛyashi November mli? ni esa akɛ egbi

english: Late rains prevent mature crops like maize, legumes, and cocoa from drying properly on the field, leading to mold and rotting. In such cases, harvest mature crops early and dry them under shelter or raised drying racks.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ naagbee be lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ kookoo naa koni amɛkagbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Yɛ shihilɛ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ mli lɛ, Kpamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ mra. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛfɔ̃ shi koni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo okɛwo tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: If my field gets completely flooded, can I dig up my growing crops and replant them on dry ground?
ga: Kɛji nu eyi miŋmɔji amli lɛ Ani manyɛ mafo ŋmɔshi nibii ni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ?

english: Once crops are established, digging them up destroys their delicate feeder roots and usually causes the plant to die. It is better to drain the water from the current field rather than attempting to relocate grown crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Amɛfomɔ fiteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ni bei pii lɛ egbeɔ tso lɛ. Ehi akɛ abaajie nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ mli moŋ fe ni abaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ.

english: Which crops are better at surviving in areas of my farm that always collect water after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni bei pii lɛ amɛhiɛɔ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops like rice, sugar cane, and taro (cocoyam) can tolerate wet or flooded soil, whereas crops like cassava, groundnuts, and beans rot quickly if left in standing water.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ taro (kookoo) baanyɛ akpɛlɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ loo nu afua nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei baafite oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: How do I know if my crops are dying from too much soil water or from an insect attack?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi yɛ nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ loo yɛ kooloi bibii ni tutuaa mi lɛ ahewɔ?

english: Waterlogged plants will have soft, smelly, or rotted stems near the soil surface and soft roots. Insect damage usually leaves visible holes in leaves, chewed stems, or pests directly on the plant.
ga: Tsei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaná shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni shãa loo ni fiteɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa bu yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. tso lɛ shishi loo ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ ana yɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does heavy rainfall wash away the good topsoil on my farm, and how can I keep it in place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain drops hit bare soil directly and wash away the fertile top layer. Planting cover crops like cowpeas or leaving dry leaves as mulch cushions the soil against rain impact and holds the dirt together.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni efoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni baa nii lɛ. Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ loo baai ni egboi ni ashiɔ akɛ mulch lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee mlɛo kɛjɛ nugbɔ nɔ ni ebaaha muji lɛ ahi shi.

english: If water is released from a nearby dam or reservoir, can I use it directly on my farm during dry spells?
ga: Kɛji nu je kpo kɛjɛ faa loo nutoohe ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, dam water is good for crops during dry periods, but you should channel it gently into furrows rather than flooding the field all at once, which can wash away soil nutrients and weaken plant stems.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni yɔɔ faai amli lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Shi esa akɛ okɛtsu nii blɛoo. Gbalamɔ nu kɛya nubu lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ fɛɛ aba shikome. ni baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dropping off when the sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain plants or shade trees are grown beside them to act like umbrellas, shielding the young cocoa from direct sun and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa is mature enough to withstand heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Aduɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa amɛmasɛi koni amɛtsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ latsaa lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow big. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer to the soil helps the plant regain its bright green color and produce good ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmei toi kpakpai.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge bushy green leaves above ground but only small, thin tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much water or excess nitrogen from rich soil, it puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy foliage. To get thick cassava roots, the plant needs a balanced soil where it can focus on storing food underground rather than growing branches.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nu babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ baai. Bɔni afee ni aná cassava shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ Tsei he miihia shikpɔŋ ni ja ni baanyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama niyenii ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ moŋ fe tsei niji ni miida.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. If the ground dries out completely and then gets flooded with water, or if the afternoon temperatures get too high, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa ni no sɛɛ lɛ nu shwie nɔ loo kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ shwane mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in the same field as my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the dirt. As the cowpea roots decay, they feed natural nitrogen into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the nearby maize.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji cowpea shishifãi lɛ fite Ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves high up into the sun to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread easily and allows maximum sunlight to reach the leaves so the underground yam tuber can grow large.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la lɛ mli bɔni afee ni efee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni ehaa hulu la babaoo shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually a sign of tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf damage that stops pepper fruits from developing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites miinu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli. loo virus ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite baai ni haaa pepper aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: The extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, food, and sunlight from the main plantain trunk. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant gets full nourishment to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ plantain tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my crop seeds rot in the soil if I plant them immediately after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛ fioo lɛ? Klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: The very first light rain heats up the dry soil without soaking it deeply. Seeds planted too early sit in hot, slightly damp dirt that encourages soil fungi to attack and rot the seeds before steady rainy-season rains arrive to help them sprout.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛwooo mli tsɔ. Esa akɛ dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ fioo nɔ, ni woɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛtutua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛfite, dani nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be koni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn into powder and get full of small holes after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Eyi obɔ beni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ?

english: Small beetles called grain weevils burrow inside dry maize kernels to lay eggs, and the hatching insects eat the inside of the grain. Properly drying maize to very low moisture levels and storing it in sealed, airtight bags prevents weevils from surviving and eating the harvest.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli koni amɛwo amɛwui. Ni kooloi bibii ni baa lɛ baaye ŋmãa wui lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi waa tsu nii ni akɛgbi ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa lɛ naa koni amɛkajo foi ni amɛye ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize get small holes in it and turn into powder after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ powda beni akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Weevils and other storage insects attack maize grains when they carry moisture or are left unprotected. Drying your maize thoroughly in the sun until the kernels are hard, and using airtight hermetic bags or approved storage dust, protects your harvest from insect damage.
ga: Moths kɛ kooloi krokomɛi buaa Attacks corn kernels lɛ anaa kɛji amɛhe edɔ loo ashi amɛ ni abuuu amɛhe. Akɛ ŋmãa ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee shiŋŋ ni akɛ vacuum loo sũ kotoku ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛto. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growth period helps the crop regain its rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ adara lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei lɛ amli mra yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gĩ ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under strong direct sunlight. Planting quick-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade that keeps the plants cool and moist until they mature.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and fold up during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants close up and droop their leaves during hot afternoon hours to save water and reduce moisture loss. This is a natural defense behavior, and the leaves usually bounce back once the evening air cools down.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ ŋmɛɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Koni akɛ nu akafite ni ajie ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu su. Ni bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off the stems before any pepper pods form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as dry soil, extreme heat, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots during flowering prevents the plant from dropping its blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafo baai.

english: Why do my yam tubers start rotting underground when heavy rains make water stand on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the land for long periods, it starves the roots of air, causing them to drown and allowing rot-causing fungi to destroy the tubers.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha ŋwɛi shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nu mli gbee ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to come up out of the soil when I bury them deep in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry only a small amount of stored energy to send their first shoot up into the air. If planted too deep, the shoot exhausts its food reserves before reaching the surface sunlight and dies underground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato ni amɛkɛbaatsu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛji adu mli tsɔ lɛ, niyenii ni ato lɛ baaho dani eshɛ hulu la he ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What happens to my maize crop if rain stops falling right when the plants start showing tassels and silk?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be mli ni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛ siliki lɛ?

english: Flowering is the most water-sensitive stage of a crop's life. Lack of rain during tassel and silk formation prevents proper pollination, resulting in missing grains or completely empty cobs.
ga: Fɔfɔii ji be ni nu he hiaa fe fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashihilɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ yɛ tassel kɛ silk feemɔ be mli lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ loo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ efolo kwraa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and choke my crops even though I cleared the land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya waa ni amɛmiigba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu nii moŋ.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, and their seeds wake up quickly when rain hits cleared soil. Clearing weeds early in the first four weeks ensures your crops do not lose water, light, and fertilizer to weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Ni amɛdumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ kwɛmɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite nu, la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha jwɛi lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my maize in the field is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is fully mature when the outer leaves turn straw-brown, the cob hangs downward, and a tiny black spot forms at the base of each grain where it meets the cob, showing that the plant has stopped feeding the kernel.
ga: Abɛi eda kɛji akɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ jwɛi ŋmɔtɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ shwie shi, ni ŋmɔtɔi bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Efeɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi yɛ he ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa edumɔwui lɛ niyenii hamɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because full sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil moisture rapidly before their roots are strong enough to drink enough water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni baaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya dani amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛnuɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose almost all their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to save water. This natural behavior stops the plant from losing moisture through leaves while keeping the underground roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni akɛbu nu he. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli subaŋ nɛɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ baai lɛ anɔ efo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden stakes to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground helps the plant generate more energy to produce larger tubers underneath the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo baa koni ekɛwo bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize crop turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or the ground is too waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and wrinkle, making the plants look stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe, ni no haa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the leaves, or a virus they spread that stops healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni tsiɔ hewalɛnamɔ nɔ dalɛ naa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when weather temperatures become too high or when watering is irregular, causing stress that makes the plant reject the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa tsei kpooɔ fɔfɔi baa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, causing all of them to grow tall and weak instead of strong.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my farm than the maize I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmãa ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive hard conditions, so they quickly drink water and steal nutrients from the soil before your crop gets a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛnuɔ nu oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same spot on my land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does heavy rain during flowering cut down the amount of grain I harvest from my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Heavy rain during the flowering stage washes away pollen from the silk and flowers, which stops the corn ears from getting fully pollinated and forming complete kernels.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ tsuɔ pollen ni yɔɔ siliki kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ he. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa toi lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ebatsɔ dumɔwui ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do my cassava roots spoil quickly in the ground if I do not harvest them before the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji mikpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers absorb excess water during heavy rains, which causes them to rot rapidly in waterlogged soil if they are left unharvested past their maturity period.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha egbo oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ kɛho be ni ekɛdaraa waa lɛ he.

english: If I use a tractor or machine to clear my land, will it ruin the soil for my crops?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ trakta loo tsɔne tsu nii kɛfo shikpɔŋ lɛ Ani ebaafite shikpɔŋ ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy machinery can compact the topsoil and stop rain from sinking in, but using light equipment or tilling at the correct depth keeps the soil loose and healthy for root growth.
ga: Nibii ni tsii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha nugbɔ akabote mli Shi kɛ akɛ nibii ni tsiimɔ waaa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ he ni sa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and short roots that burn easily in direct sunlight, which is why planting shade trees or plantains around them keeps the soil moist and cools the plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Cocoa nut lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong leaves and green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli.

english: How do fall armyworms manage to destroy my maize farm overnight without me seeing them during the day?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni cutworms afite mi-corn ŋmɔ lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome mli ni minaaa amɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the central leaves of the maize stem during the hot daytime and feed at night when it is cool, multiplying rapidly.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni ayeɔ nii gbɛkɛ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ

english: How do I know the right time to put my cassava cuttings in the soil when the rain is unpredictable?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli? Be ni nugbɔ baanɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba?

english: Plant your cuttings right after two or three steady rains when the soil is wet deep down, giving the stem cuttings enough moisture to establish roots before any dry spell.
ga: Dumɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee shishifãi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my pepper plants after I clear the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-pepper tsei lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds stay asleep under the dirt for years; clearing the farm exposes them to sunlight and rain, causing them to sprout much faster than planted seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kã shikpɔŋ shishi afii babaoo. Kɛ́ amɛjie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, hulu kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kwraa fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need stakes to lift their leaves up to reach sunlight, allowing the plant to generate energy to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hulu la mli. Ehaa tsei feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of small holes and powder after a few months in the storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni okɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ehi nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Grain weevils lay tiny eggs inside maize kernels, and if the grain is not dried completely before storage, those eggs hatch into insects that eat the maize from the inside.
ga: Dumɔwui ŋmei lɛ woɔ wɔji bibii. mli ŋmãa dumɔwui Ni kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto Nakai ŋmãa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: Why should I plant cowpea or groundnuts on the same land after I finish harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legume plants like cowpea trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for the next crop without needing chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen nutrients or when roots are waterlogged from heavy rains. Adding nitrogen fertilizer such as NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shishifãi lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ nu. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba emuuyeli mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before setting any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience water stress during dry spells or when tiny sap-sucking insects attack the blossoms. Maintaining proper shade trees and keeping soil moist helps the flowers stay attached and form pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, hulutsoo ni sa ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist while the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers produce small bunches when planted very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa?

english: When plantains are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to absorb nutrients and produce large bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni efeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava leaves dry up and fall off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of conserving water during drought. The plant enters a survival mode to protect its roots and will quickly sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ lɛ ji ŋmei adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli koni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe. ni ebaakwɛ baai heei oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without making fruits during heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains knock off delicate tomato blossoms and cause high humidity that leads to fungal diseases on the flowers. Growing tomatoes on raised beds or using rain protection helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa hulutsoo be babaoo baa, ni no haa tsɛŋemɔ hela baa fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu tomato yɛ saatsoi ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ loo akɛtsu nii koni akɛha nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking leaf sap, or by a plant virus they spread. Controlling these pests early with neem oil or appropriate sprays prevents leaf curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baa mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo spray ni sa nɔ lɛ obaanyɛ otsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is a white powdery substance appearing on the leaves of my garden egg plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔ ko ni tamɔ powda yɛŋ miije kpo yɛ eggplant lɛ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: The white powder is a fungal disease called powdery mildew that spreads in warm, humid weather. Pruning crowded branches to improve airflow and removing infected leaves stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my cassava roots staying thin even though the top leaves look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin if the soil is too hard for tubers to expand or if the soil lacks potassium nutrients. Loosening the soil into soft mounds before planting allows the roots to swell into large tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ji potassium Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ni efeɔ gɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo dani aduɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my young yam vines wilt when the soil around the mound gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi beni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle gɔŋ lɛ he lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Hot soil bakes the delicate young roots near the surface and causes moisture to evaporate rapidly. Mulching around the base of the yam mound with dry grass keeps the soil cool and retains moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shãa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle o-sweet potato pile lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my young corn leaves turn yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young corn usually mean the plants are starving for nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding a balanced fertilizer like NPK early in the plant's life helps it turn green and grow strong.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa tamɔ NPK fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni eda waa.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up tight like straws during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a crop's natural defense to protect itself from losing water in extreme heat. The plant reduces its surface area exposed to the sun to hold onto moisture until the day cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni elaajeɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Tsei baa amɛhiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ.

english: What causes my corn plants to produce tall tassels at the top but end up with empty cobs without grains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele tsei lɛ náa ŋmeii kakadaji yɛ amɛyiteŋ shi amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko ni dumɔwui bɛ mli?

english: If corn experiences severe dry weather or lack of water when the silks and tassels form, the pollen dies before it can fertilize the cob, leading to missing or empty kernels.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ na kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa loo nu ni bɛ beni siliki kɛ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ lɛ, Pollen lɛ gboɔ dani ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni elaaje loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my corn seeds very close together on my land?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin stems and tiny cobs. Giving plants proper space allows each crop to grow to its full potential.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. He ni sa ni tso yɔɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa kɛyashɛɔ he ni ebaanyɛ eshɛ.

english: Why should I buy packaged corn seeds from the market instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni awo kotoku mli kɛjɛ jara nɔ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Certified market seeds are specially bred to resist common local diseases, handle short dry spells, and produce high yields. Seeds saved from previous harvests lose these protective traits over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ jara nɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛte shi ewo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kpeemɔ be kukuoo ni mli egbi lɛ naa ni owo yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baafite nɛkɛ hebuu sui nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do weeds actually prevent my crops from growing well?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farmland. They aggressively suck up the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your crops need, leaving your main plants weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa onibii waa lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, otso titri lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaagbɔjɔ.

english: How can I know if a spray or pesticide is safe to use on my food crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi niyenii tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Always look for approved regulatory labels from agencies like the FDA or EPA Ghana on the bottle, and consult an extension officer. Unapproved or fake chemicals can destroy your crop and leave harmful poisons in the harvested food.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, taomɔ mla he wolo ni nitsumɔhe ko tamɔ FDA loo EPA Ghana kpɛlɛ nɔ yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ o-extension officer lɛ agba sane. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ loo amalei baanyɛ afite oŋmɔshi nibii ni ashi tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ niyenii ni akpa lɛ mli.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my corn so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mawo ŋmãa koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy rainfall. Burying the fertilizer slightly into the soil a few centimeters away from the plant stem keeps the rain from washing it away before roots can drink it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Ni aaafu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fioo awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, sɛntimitai fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he. Enɛ baaha nugbɔ lɛ akaho dani shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why does my soil produce lower crop yields if I plant corn on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating corn with beans or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the earth and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa efeɔ fɛo.

english: Why does my stored corn turn into powder and get tiny holes after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ

english: Grain insects called weevils burrow inside dried corn to feed and lay eggs. Properly drying your corn to a hard crunch and using safe, approved grain-storage powders keeps the insects from destroying your harvest.
ga: Kplukai ni yɔɔ ŋmaa mli, ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ, shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli koni amɛtao niyenii ni amɛwo wɔji. Kɛ́ ogbala o-corn lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ powda ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui ahe lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under strong sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a living canopy that protects the cocoa from heat and keeps the soil moist while they grow.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ latsaa he lɛ baa. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni oduɔ nii lɛ

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which gives leaves their green color. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the soil's nutrients and allows maize pests to multiply in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass acts as a mulch that traps soil moisture during dry weather, prevents weeds from taking over, and protects the soil from burning under direct sunlight.
ga: Mulch ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch ni mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi.

english: What is eating holes in the center leaf funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar hiding inside the young whorl of the leaf. Applying neem tree extract or clean wood ash directly into the plant's center funnel early in the morning can stop them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem tso mli nu loo tso mli sũ ni he tse wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves. Spraying plants with a mild soapy water solution or neem oil helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ Loo neem fɔ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped in flooded, poorly drained soil because root systems need air to stay healthy. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu babaoo atsɔ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over before the bunches are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support the heavy weight of a mature bunch during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy wooden fork or bamboo prop prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ni tsii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekagbee shi.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they experience stress from hot weather, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen feeding. Giving plants steady moisture and shade during peak midday heat keeps flowers intact.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo nitrogen ni akɛhaa lɛ babaoo Ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to water my garden crops in the early morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha abɔɔ mli tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi maŋkpa loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows plant roots to drink fully before the afternoon heat causes water to evaporate, keeping plants hydrated throughout the hottest part of the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu dani shwane mli latsaa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ha tsei lɛ aná nu yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to leave specific spaces between my crops instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ gbɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin and weak plants. Proper spacing lets each plant get enough air and food to yield bigger harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni ekɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I plant my pepper seeds in a nursery box first before moving them to my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ dumɔwui adekai amli dani mikɛya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are very tiny and delicate. Starting them in a sheltered nursery allows you to protect the young seedlings from harsh heat, heavy rain, and insects until they are strong enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ ji bibii waa ni amɛhe yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Kɛ́ obɔi tsei yɛ he ko ni akwɛɔ tsei yɛ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an important food they need to grow. It can also happen when the soil is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdu. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why do my crops give me poor yields when I plant maize on the exact same land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts puts natural nutrients back into the soil and starves the pests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how can it help my vegetables grow better than in the open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: A greenhouse is a structure covered with clear plastic or mesh netting that protects crops from scorching heat, heavy downpours, and destructive insects. It creates a safe environment so you can grow high-quality vegetables like tomatoes all year round.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsu ko ni akɛ plastic loo ŋshɔŋlooi ni mli tse ehà nɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ koolooi ni fiteɔ nii ahe. It creates a safe environment. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ odu aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ tomato afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot mainly when rain water sits on the soil for too long without draining, causing soil fungi to attack the tubers. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps surplus water drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or whiteflies sucking the juice from the leaves, or by a sickness spread by these insects. Keeping your farm free of weeds helps reduce where these pests hide.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi akafee nɔ ko lɛ, ebaaha hei ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ lɛ aba shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil which causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of setting fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why is it recommended to leave some big trees standing on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ ashi tsei wuji yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Big trees provide shade that protects young cocoa trees from intense sunlight, keeps the soil cool during dry seasons, and drops leaves that decay into rich natural fertilizer for your cocoa.
ga: Tsei wuji lɛ haa hɔɔŋ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni etsɔɔ baai ni miifite lɛ mli efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛha o-cocoa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain suckers turning brown and drying up from the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Drying leaves are often caused by a lack of water during dry periods or by fungal diseases in the soil. Clearing weeds around the stem and covering the ground around the base with dried leaves helps keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbi lɛ baa. Jwɛi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ kɛ baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade plants like plantain or cassava grown around them to block harsh sun rays and keep the soil moist until the trees grow strong enough to withstand full heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛhe. Bɔni afee ni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside leaves of my young maize plants during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide in the deep center whorl of young maize leaves where it is moist and tender. Catching them early with neem oil or recommended sprays prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant before cobs can form.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii ni mli kwɔ, ni mli edɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ mɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ yitsei lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ afee.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and curl up tightly during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpɛɔ amɛhe waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried and spread by tiny whiteflies. The insect population grows in warm weather, so planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. ni whiteflies woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kplukai ayibɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil lacks food for my crops before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa miduɔ nii dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: If your previous crop leaves turned pale yellow from the bottom up or produced weak harvests, the soil is low in nutrients like nitrogen. Checking leaf color in early growth or looking for thin crop stems tells you that compost or fertilizer needs to be added.
ga: Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛtee ŋwɛi loo amɛwooo yibii kpakpai. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ahe su yɛ be mli ni edara mra loo otao tsei bibii lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ bo kɛji ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots, and when too many small shoot suckers grow around the base of one main stem, they fight for root space and weaken the main tree. Removing extra suckers and keeping only two or three strong stems per mat allows deeper root anchorage.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ Too babaoo ni miida yɛ tso wulu kome shishi lɛ he. Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ shishifãi ahe ni amɛhaa tso titri lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akpɛtɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akpɛtɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Blossom drop happens when temperatures get too high, when watering is uneven, or when plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and reducing heavy nitrogen during flowering helps the blossoms set into healthy fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo kɛji tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ mulch woɔ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nitrogen ni tsii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔii amli lɛ haa aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise planting groundnuts or cowpeas on the farm before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔji amli dani adu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that pull natural nitrogen food from the air into the dirt. When you harvest them, the plant roots rot in the ground and leave behind free soil food that helps the next maize crop grow larger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛshiɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni edara.

english: Why are my green pepper fruits getting dark rotten patches at the bottom end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili aduawai eŋɔli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the developing fruit, which often happens when watering is irregular. Watering your pepper plants regularly keeps nutrients moving smoothly from the soil into the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Calcium ni faaa yɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ afɔ pepper tsei anɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does clearing weeds early in the first few weeks make such a big difference to my final harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa minaagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ feɔ srɔto kwraa nɛkɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients during the critical early stages of crop development. Removing weeds within the first 3 to 4 weeks allows your young crops to build strong stems and deep roots without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shishijee bei ni he hiaa waa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha odumɔwui lɛ afee tsei ni wa ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear land and put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mawo tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight for tuber growth. Staking also keeps the leaves dry and off the wet soil, which prevents leaf spot fungal diseases from spreading and destroying the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni egbiɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela ni ji leaf spot lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ni efite tsei.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the large trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because intense, direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them acts as a protective shield until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baatsu nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tsei koni makwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efo kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves on stakes helps them catch maximum sunlight to make food for big tuber growth. It also keeps the leaves off the hot, wet ground, which prevents fungal rot and diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai ni awóɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji lɛ adalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ hei ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key plant nutrient. When soil nitrogen is low, the plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the young growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha gbekɛbii ni daraa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my field yield less maize every season even though I plant at the same time every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli daa afi moŋ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas helps put valuable nitrogen back into the earth naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake o-corn lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen ni jara wa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow very tall with bushy leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much leaf-building nutrients (like nitrogen) or too much water, the cassava plant spends all its energy developing leaves and branches above ground instead of storing food in its root tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ mlɛo (tamɔ nitrogen) loo nu babaoo lɛ, Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ niji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small fruits when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves compete heavily with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough food to produce big fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Akɛ jwɛi loo baai ŋmɔɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out soil moisture, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from getting sunlight to grow.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ebaatsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashã ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaha jwɛi lɛ akaná hulu la koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or lack of water. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of saving energy to keep itself alive during stressful weather.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ he. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni haoɔ mɔ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain plants curl downwards during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl during intense heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the strong sun. This protects the plant from losing water faster than its roots can drink it up.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ buɔ tso lɛ he koni nu lɛ akafite oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stay greener on my farm than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep root systems naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions, whereas cultivated crops are bred for yield and need extra care, water, and weed control to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ tsei ni aduɔ lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, ni ehe miihia ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, nu, kɛ jwɛi ni akudɔ koni amɛshwere.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa leaves are changing color because of chemical spray or because of a new disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo baai anɔ loo hela hee ko hewɔ etsake amɛhe su?

english: Chemical damage usually appears quickly and evenly across all sprayed trees shortly after application, whereas disease symptoms spread gradually from tree to tree over time and often show distinct spots, rotting, or unusual growths.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa oya ni efeɔ ekome yɛ tso ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni hela lɛ he okadii lɛ baagbɛ eshwa fiofio kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa anaa otii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ fitemɔ loo dalɛ ni ejaaa

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees sometimes change or look damaged after I spray them with farm chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ tsakeɔ loo amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfite beni mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai eshwie amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves can change color or show stress after spraying if the chemical mixture is too strong, applied during hot sunshine, or if the tree is experiencing a temporary reaction as it absorbs the treatment.
ga: Baai lɛ baanyɛ atsake amɛhe loo amɛjie haomɔ kpo yɛ be mli ni afɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛji tsofa ni akɛfutu lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛtsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli. aloo kɛji tso lɛ na nɔ ko ni baaha efee nɔ ko yɛ be kukuoo mli beni ekɛ tsofa lɛ miitsu nii lɛ.

english: Can spraying too much chemical medicine burn or damage my cocoa leaves?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo baai lɛ ashã loo efite?

english: Yes, using more than the recommended dosage or spraying too frequently can scorch leaves, cause them to fall off early, and weaken the tree instead of helping it.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ni fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii loo akɛshwie nɔ shii abɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã, amɛgbee shi oya, ni eha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua lɛ.

english: How do chemical medicines actually work inside my cocoa tree to fight off sickness?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni tsofa ni akɛfee tsofa lɛ tsu nii diɛŋtsɛ yɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ mli koni ekɛwu eshi hela lɛ?

english: Some chemicals stay on the surface of the leaves to block pests and fungi from entering, while systemic chemicals are absorbed into the plant's sap to kill diseases living inside the leaves and stem.
ga: Tsofai komɛi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii akabote mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli koni egbe helai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Should I still go to check on my cocoa farm regularly after I have already sprayed it with medicine?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa lɛ wo mihe lɛ, ani esa akɛ makwɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lolo?

english: Yes, you must continue visiting your farm regularly after spraying to confirm that the medicine is working, check for any unintended leaf damage, and catch any new pest or disease outbreaks early.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ oya nɔ oyasara oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa yɛ tsofa ni okɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ tsofa lɛ miitsu nii. Kwɛmɔ kɛji baa lɛ efite yɛ oshara mli. ni ana tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai heei Eba mli mra.

english: How often am I supposed to walk through my farm to inspect my cocoa trees for diseases?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ kɛji kookoo hela yɛ?

english: It is best to inspect your cocoa farm at least once a week so you can spot early signs of disease, such as changing leaf colors or pod spots, before the infection spreads to the whole farm.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ ona hela he okadii mra, tamɔ baai lɛ ahe su ni tsakeɔ loo pod spots. dani hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: What basic steps should I take if I spot a strange new disease on my cocoa trees for the first time?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ kpe mi? Yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa?

english: Mark the affected trees, avoid transferring tools from sick trees to healthy ones, take photos or samples if possible, and contact an extension officer to confirm the disease before buying any spray.
ga: Mark ná tsei anɔ hewalɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dɛŋdadei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ ahe. Tsɔ mfoniri loo okɛ nɔkwɛmɔnii aba kɛji ebaahi. Ni okɛ extension officer lɛ abɔ ni ema hela lɛ nɔ mi dani ohe tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ.

english: Why is it risky for me to spend a lot of money buying farm chemicals without showing my crops to an officer first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ mafite shika babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ahe ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etsɔɔɔ onukpai lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: If you misidentify the problem, you might spend hard-earned money on the wrong spray, which will fail to cure the disease and could potentially harm your cocoa trees.
ga: Kɛji otsɔɔ naagba ni ejaaa lɛ Ekolɛ Okɛ oshika ni okɛtsu nii waa lɛ miifite yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ejaaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsaŋ hela lɛ, ni ebaanyɛ eye o-cacao tsei lɛ awui.

english: Why are my cocoa trees still getting sick even after I bought expensive treatments for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mihe tsofai ni jara wa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ moŋ?
