english: Trees can stay sick if the chemical bought was for a different disease, if it was applied at the wrong time of day, or if the disease has already spread deep into the tree's roots and stem.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ aná hela kɛji tsofai ni amɛheɔ lɛ ji helai krokomɛi ahe tsofai. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa mli loo kɛji akɛ hela lɛ egbɛ eshwa tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishigbɛ shɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off during the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf yellowing and drop can be caused by several factors, including attack from mirid bugs, fungal infections, poor soil nutrition, severe drought, or chemical stress.
ga: Nibii babaoo baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Nɔ ni fata he ji mirid kooloi tutuamɔi, fungal helai. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo tsofafeemɔ he haomɔ

english: Why is it harder for me to tell when my crops are sick compared to my goats or chickens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa mi akɛ male be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ lɛ kɛ akɛto tooi loo tsinabii ahe lɛ?

english: Unlike animals that cry out, stop moving, or show immediate distress when sick, plants do not have nerves or voice. A crop can carry a disease silently inside its tissues for a long time before yellowing or wilting appears on the outside.
ga: esoro lɛ kwraa yɛ koolooi ni foɔ ni amɛkpaa nyiɛmɔ loo amɛjieɔ haomɔ kpo amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ hela mɔ amɛ Tsei lɛ bɛ tsitsii loo gbeei. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ atere helai ni gbeɔ mɔ dioo. Eboteɔ fãji lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo egbo yɛ kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do my crops sometimes look healthy today and then suddenly collapse and die a few days later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ŋmɛnɛ, shi trukaa lɛ amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Many plant diseases attack the internal water pipes or roots of the crop first. The plant looks fine on the outside while fighting the disease, but once the internal damage becomes total, the crop collapses very quickly.
ga: Tsei amli helai babaoo tutuaa nu paipii loo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ akwɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ, tso lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekɛ helai miiwu lɛ. Shi kɛ́ mligbɛ nibii ni efite lɛ tee lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baafite oya.

english: Why don't plants show early warning signs of disease the way sick livestock do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ejieee hela he kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii kpo mra tamɔ bɔ ni kooloi ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Animals have blood circulation that spreads illness rapidly, causing fast symptoms like fever. Plants transport water and food much slower, so a plant disease builds up quietly inside over time before any outward signs show.
ga: Koolooi yɛ lá ni hoɔ ni haa hela gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Ekɛ okadii ni baa oya tamɔ atridii baa Tsei kɛ nu kɛ niyenii yaa blɛoo kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei ahe helai buaa amɛhe naa dioo yɛ mli. Beni be hoɔ dani kponɔgbɛ okadii jeɔ kpo lɛ

english: If a crop sickness destroys my farm this season, can that same sickness stay hidden in my soil for many years?
ga: Kɛji tsei ahe hela kpata miŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Ani hela lɛ baanyɛ ahi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo?

english: Yes, many crop diseases caused by fungi or bacteria form tough spores that can sleep in the soil for up to ten years, waiting until you plant a fresh crop before waking up to attack again.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo ni ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛbaa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni wa ni baanyɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli kɛyashi afii nyɔŋma. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaadu ŋmɔshi nibii heei dani ote shi ni otutua bo ekoŋŋ.

english: If I pull up and burn a diseased plant from my field, does the sickness leave the land immediately?
ga: Kɛ́ mijie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni mishã amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Ani hela lɛ baaho kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Removing the sick plant removes the main source of spread, but microscopic disease germs often remain in the surrounding soil and tiny root fragments left underground.
ga: Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ nɔ titri ni kɛ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛyaa. Shi bei pii lɛ, helai bibii ni anaaa lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ amli. ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Will leaving my field fallow for just one season clear out all the plant sickness in the soil?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mishi miŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kome pɛ lɛ, ebaajie tsei ahe helai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛya?

english: Not always. Some crop diseases are very stubborn and can survive in the bare soil for several years without needing a living plant to feed on.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Tsei ahelai komɛi ahe wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ tsei ni hiɛ ka nɔ kɛha niyenii.

english: How can I tell if my crop is wilting because of a disease in the soil or just because there is no rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛkɛ hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: If a crop is wilting purely from dry weather, it will bounce back after you water it or when rain falls. If it is suffering from a soil disease, watering it will not reverse the wilting and the stem near the ground may look discolored or rotten.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi pɛ hewɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji okɛ nu ha amɛ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ hela ji lɛ Nu ni awoɔ lɛ haŋ ŋmɔtɔ aku sɛɛ aba. Ni tsei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛsu etsake loo amɛgboi.

english: Can putting the wrong chemical or fertilizer on my crops actually cause them to get sick?
ga: Ani tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha hela mɔ amɛ?

english: Yes, using improper chemicals or wrong fertilizer amounts can damage a plant's roots and weak leaves. This weakens the crop's natural defenses, allowing diseases sitting in the soil or air to easily infect it.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni ejaaa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite tso shishifãi kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baa shi. Helai ni bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ loo kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni aaagbɛ ashwã mlɛo

english: Is it possible for my crops to carry a disease inside them without looking sick at all?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná hela yɛ mli ni efeee tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ mi kwraa?

english: Yes, plants can harbor latent infections. The disease lives quietly inside the crop without harming it until a trigger—like extreme heat, bad weather, or poor soil—weakens the plant and lets the sickness take over.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei baanyɛ afee helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ jɛɛhe. Hela nɛɛ hiɔ shi yɛ dioofeemɔ mli. yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni eyeee amɛ awui kɛyashi nɔ ko ni kanyaa amɛ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa helai yeɔ nɔ.

english: Why does a plant disease suddenly break out in my field right after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai baa miŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Many plant disease germs are already present in the soil or air in a sleeping state. Heavy moisture and warm conditions act as a trigger that activates these germs and helps them spread fast across your field.
ga: Tsei amli helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ loo kɔɔyɔɔ mli momo yɛ shihilɛ ni mli wa mli. Fɛ̃i babaoo kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni tsiɔ helai nɛɛ anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya yɛ oyale mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants are a common sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is an essential food for crops to stay green and grow strong; when the soil lacks enough nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has to the top leaves, causing the lower ones to turn yellow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa koni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does growing cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the leaves and roots decay, that natural food stays in the soil, feeding whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Adebɔɔ mli niyenii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do experienced cocoa farmers plant shade trees like plantains alongside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that shield young cocoa from harsh sun, retain soil moisture, and help the young trees survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oye obua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhi shi

english: Why do I need to cut off extra side shoots and old leaves from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ cacao tso ko he ŋmeii kɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or unnecessary branches so the tree does not waste water and food on useless growth. It also opens up the tree canopy to let in sunlight and fresh air, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod from spreading.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akafite nu kɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ dalɛ ni he ehiaaa nɔ. Egbeleɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ hu koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are fall armyworms attacking my maize leaves so fast right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ tutuaa mi-corn baa lɛ oya beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms thrive in warm, humid weather after rains begin, and tender young maize leaves give them plenty of fresh food. They multiply rapidly under these conditions, eating through the soft leaves inside the plant's funnel.
ga: Autumn cutworms yeɔ omanye yɛ dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Ni ŋmãa bibii lɛ hu haa amɛ niyenii hee babaoo. Amɛfɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi nɛɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl inward during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants during strong heat is a natural survival trick to conserve water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and dry air, stopping water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni akɛshwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ baa shi lɛ baa shi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots fight underground for space, water, and nutrients. Instead of growing large, fat tubers, the plant produces many thin, woody roots that yield very little harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii, moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ ŋmei wuji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔ. Mohu ɔ, tso ɔ sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ nyafii ɔ daa. Ehe babaoo woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do my yam mounds need to be built high with soft, loose soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama yam ŋtayaa lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ni akɛ sũ ni mli tse ni egbɔjɔ awo mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downwards straight into the earth. Loose, tall soil mounds remove obstacles so the underground yam tuber can expand freely into a long, thick root without struggling against packed, hard ground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ gbɛtsii nii. No hewɔ lɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛfee shishifãi kakadaji ni mli tse ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ ebɔko.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off mainly due to extreme heat or irregular watering. Very high temperatures damage the flower's pollen, making it unable to form fruits, so the plant drops the dead flower.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni fe nine loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ. ni ehaa enyɛŋ afee nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni egboi lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crop is ready to be dug up from the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaaku?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower stem becomes thick and woody, the leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack from expanding roots underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shɛɔ dalɛ he beni shishigbɛ tso lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tsei. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or getting too much water. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving drainage in wet spots helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo amɛmiiná nu babaoo. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ urea ni akɛbaafata he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants curl and droop their leaves during peak afternoon heat to protect themselves from losing water. It is a natural defense mechanism to survive hot hours, and they usually stand back up by evening.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ayeɔ wala yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Ni bei pii lɛ, amɛteɔ shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when the weather is too hot, when they do not get enough water, or if tiny insects are damaging the blooms. Keeping the soil moist and protecting the plants from pests helps the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii miifite fɔfɔi Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tso lɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and small roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains beside young cocoa provides shelter from the hot sun so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds when the rainy season keeps changing?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tsakeɔ lɛ?

english: Wait to plant until the soil receives a deep, soaking rain for two or three days in a row so the ground stays moist. Planting right after a single light rainfall can cause seeds to sprout and quickly wither if the rain stops.
ga: Mɛɛ ni odu kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Will my plantain plants yield bigger fruit bunches if I plant them close together?
ga: Ani mi plantains lɛ baawo aduawai akui wuji kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Planting plantains too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to smaller bunches. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the roots to spread and produce larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ baaha plantain lɛ afee bibioo. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does cassava manage to grow well in poor sandy soil where my maize fails?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni mi ŋmãa lɛ bɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep, hardy roots that can dig far underground to find food and water in poor soils. Maize has shallow roots and needs richer soil with high nutrients to produce big cobs.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni baanyɛ atsa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni ena niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Abɛi shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni ehe miihia shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the ground, leaving the soil weak. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap natural nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. gbɔjɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei lɛ ŋmɛɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni okɛ babaoo aku sɛɛ aba oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are fall armyworms attacking my green maize shoots so early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ tutuaa mi-green corn shoots lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Armyworms prefer soft, young maize shoots because tender leaves are easy for them to eat and hide inside. Checking your field early and treating the central leaves when the plants are small prevents them from ruining the harvest.
ga: Cutworms sumɔɔ ŋmãa bibii ejaakɛ baai bibii lɛ yeli waaa ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mli. Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ beni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting or rotting quickly inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ loo amɛmiifite oya yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers start sprouting when they feel warmth and air moisture, and rot when piled up without fresh air. Storing yams on open wooden racks in a cool, well-ventilated, and shaded barn keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji amɛnu kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i he. ni egbo kɛji akɛ ato he kome ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Kɛ atomo ni ŋɔɔ ato tso adekai ni agbele nɔ yɛ hulutsoo shĩa ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to start clearing and preparing our land in December or January before the main rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ aje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ kɛ he saamɔ shishi yɛ December loo January mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Preparing land during the dry months of December and January gives you enough time to clear brush, turn the soil, and gather planting materials so your field is ready for immediate sowing as soon as the first major rains arrive in March or April.
ga: Kɛ́ osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ December kɛ January nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha oná be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛjie tsei bibii, otsake shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni obua nibii ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ anaa. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ wulu lɛ ba yɛ March loo April mli pɛ.

english: What happens to my maize seeds if I plant them in dry ground before the rain starts falling?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Seeds planted in dry ground will remain dormant waiting for moisture. However, if the dry spell lasts too long, high soil heat, ants, and mice can destroy or eat the seeds before they get the chance to germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baakã he ahi shi. koni amɛmɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Shi, kɛji hɔmɔ lɛ hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ afite loo amɛye dumɔwui dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants drop off during the dry Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods like the Harmattan to reduce water loss. The plant goes into a resting state to preserve moisture while keeping the tubers underground safe until the rains return.
ga: Taakɛ Harmattan ji lɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tsei lɛ baabote hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ hu hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl inward during intense heat to reduce the leaf surface exposed to sunlight, which helps the plant save water. If curling persists in the morning, it could be a sign of pests or a virus.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni hulu la ni shɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛji akɛ tsitsi lɛ tee nɔ ehi shi leebi lɛ Ebaanyɛ efee tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ he okadi.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I harvest more food from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani minyɛŋ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leads to weak stems and smaller fruits, resulting in a lower total harvest than properly spaced plants.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ abɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ baa shi fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains specific nutrients like nitrogen and lets maize-specific pests build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, ni ehaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when plants don't get consistent moisture. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to drop its flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he.

english: If I put chemical fertilizer right touching the stem of my young crop, will it grow faster?
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso bibioo lɛ shishi lɛ, ani ebaada oya?

english: No, placing concentrated chemical fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's roots and stem base. Fertilizer should always be applied a few inches away from the stem in a ring or line.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishi. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli 2-3 inch kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ ŋwɛi loo line mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to harsh local conditions. They take up soil nutrients, water, and sunlight much faster than farm crops, which is why clearing them early is essential for crop growth.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ebɔ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe. Amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie amɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia kɛha tsei adalɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plant turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often mean the plant lacks nitrogen or is losing older leaves to feed new growth at the top. It can also happen when the plant is overwatered or root growth is restricted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo baai momoi lɛ elaaje koni ekɛye ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ niyenii. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji tsei lɛ yɛ nu babaoo loo etsĩ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why should I clear farmland and plant seed crops instead of just gathering them from the forest bush where they already grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni madu dumɔwui? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobua amɛnaa kɛjɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli he ni amɛkwɛ̃ momo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting crops on your farm allows you to control their growth, protect them from pests, and harvest larger, predictable yields easily instead of spending hours searching for wild plants in the bush.
ga: Nibii ni oduɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ amɛdalɛ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. ni akpa yibiiwoo ni da, ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooye ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo ni otao koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Does growing crops on a farm produce more yield than just leaving them to grow naturally in the bush?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe ni aaaha amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ jwɛi amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe?

english: Yes, crops on a farm receive targeted care, sunlight, and soil nutrients without fighting forest weeds for survival, which leads to healthier plants and much bigger harvests.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ naa kwɛmɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ koo mli jwɛi awuu koni ehi shi. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa babaoo baa.

english: What basic maintenance do crops need after I plant them on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee saamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Every crop requires a few basic steps to thrive: regular weeding so plants do not fight for nutrients, adequate water, gentle clearing around the base, and protection from animals and pests.
ga: Nibii fioo komɛi he miihia nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛshwere: Okɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii daa koni tsei lɛ akabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛná niyenii kpakpai, amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa, ni amɛjie shishifãi lɛ ahe blɛoo. ni ebu he kɛjɛ kooloi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe.

english: Do all crops require the same kind of care, or does each crop have different requirements?
ga: Ani tsei fɛɛ he miihia ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ? Aloo ani tsei srɔtoi yɛ taomɔ nii srɔtoi?

english: Each crop has its own specific needs—some crops need full sunlight and well-drained soil, while others prefer shade, heavy watering, or rich composted soil to grow properly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehiamɔ nii pɔtɛɛ. Tsei komɛi biɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi biɔ hulutsoo Nu babaoo loo shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni eha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my crops are healthy and getting what they need from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛmiiná nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy crops usually have vibrant green leaves, strong stems, and steady growth. If leaves turn yellow, wilt, or stop growing, the plant is telling you it lacks nutrients, water, or protection from pests.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ naa baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ, tsei ni wa, kɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ Gbimɔ loo ekpa dalɛ Tso lɛ miikɛɛ bo akɛ ebɛ niyenii, nu, loo hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: How do I protect my newly planted crops from being destroyed on the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu ehee lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can protect young crops by clearing nearby weeds, building simple boundary fencing against livestock, applying safe pest treatments, and providing temporary shade if the direct sun is too harsh.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni ooojie kɛjɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ gbogbo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kooloi akabote mli. Kɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe atsu nii ni okɛjie tsɛŋemɔ helai. ni eha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko aba kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli wa tsɔ.

english: Why do plants in the forest survive without weeding, but my farm crops suffer if I leave weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi kɛji jwɛi bɛ amɛhe lɛ? Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa amanehulu kɛji mishi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he.

english: Forest plants are wild and aggressive, but cultivated food crops are bred to produce high yields and need your help to stop weeds from stealing their soil food, light, and water.
ga: Koo mli tsei ji koo mli tsei ni feɔ basabasa. Shi akwɛɔ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ koni ewo yibii babaoo. Ni ehe miihia ni oye obua lɛ koni jwɛi akaju shikpɔŋ niyenii, kane, kɛ nu.

english: Will a wild plant taken from the bush grow well if I move it straight onto my open farmland?
ga: Ani koo mli tso ni ajie kɛjɛ jwɛi mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛtee he ni miduɔ nii yɛ ni agbele naa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: It will grow, but it needs time to adapt. Wild forest plants often prefer partial shade and rich organic mulch, so you must recreate some of those natural forest conditions on your farm.
ga: Ebaada, shi ebaahe be dani enyɛ etsake ehe. Bei pii lɛ, koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ sumɔɔ hulutsoo be fioo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ okɛ adebɔɔ mli koo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to give my crops proper spacing on the farm instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each crop gets enough root space, soil nutrients, air, and sunlight to produce big, healthy fruits or tubers without crowding out neighboring plants.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa shishifãi ahe gbɛ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai loo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba. ni ekɛ ehe wooo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli

english: What special care do young seedlings need during their first few weeks on the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ he hiaa dumɔwui bibii yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Young seedlings are delicate like babies; they need moist soil, protection from intense direct sunlight, careful weeding around their roots, and shielding from insects that like to eat tender leaves.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ waaa tamɔ abifao. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ he miihia amɛ. Buu ohe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Okɛ shishifãi atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni ebu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ahe

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that provide vital shade and protect moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hebuu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la lɛ baashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes where leaves used to grow on the stem; those buds must point upwards toward the sky so the new stems can grow correctly out of the ground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii lɛ. Ebɛŋkɛ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Ehe miihia ni nakai ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii heei anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How deep should I bury my seeds when planting maize or beans?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu midumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: A good guide is to bury seeds about two to three centimeters deep—roughly the depth of your thumb tip—so they get enough moisture to sprout without being buried too deep to reach the surface.
ga: Nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ji ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ afu aaafee sɛntimitai 2-3 (aaafee otsitsi bibioo lɛ naa) koni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni okɛfuuu amɛ tsɔ ni amɛshɛɛɛ ŋwɛi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow. Applying animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will help them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to put sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ niji awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they get maximum sun and stay safe from soil rots.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ená hulu la babaoo ni eha amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from your soil every season and lets specific pests build up; swapping with groundnuts or cowpeas puts nutrients back into your soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsake lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to apply fertilizer to my crops during a heavy rainstorm or after the rain stops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo midumɔ nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer right after the rain stops when the soil is moist. Heavy rainfall during a storm will wash your expensive fertilizer away before the plant roots can drink it in.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ ahum be mli lɛ baajie o-fertilizer ni jara wa lɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any tomatoes grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures become too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or when there are no insects around to shake and pollinate the blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ he ni baakpokpo ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What is making the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant juices. Spraying neem leaf water or mild soapy water helps remove these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa curl baa. Neem baa nu loo samla ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Black pod is caused by a water mold that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches lets air and sunlight in to keep your pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nu mli tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ hulutsoo be kroko mli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ mli koni eha o-pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my young cocoa trees when starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei ahe kɛ́ mije ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive and easily burn under intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight so their leaves can produce food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground also protects the leaves from soil-borne diseases and encourages larger tubers to grow under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii aha tso lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe, ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the rest of the plant is green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base of the plant will help restore healthy leaf color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baa lɛ dalɛ Kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛbaabɔle he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans on my land help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and traps it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize on that same plot afterward, the maize uses that leftover nitrogen to grow faster and produce larger yields.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. Ejɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ ŋmãa kɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ baatsu nii ni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ekɛ yibii babaoo aba.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to be harvested from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower stem leaves start turning yellow and dropping off. You can carefully scrape away soil around one plant to check if the roots are thick and swollen before harvesting the rest of the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso kome he lɛ nɔ okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni efuu dani okpa ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist by watering regularly and placing dry grass around the plant base keeps the root zone cool and helps flowers set into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni okɛwo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahe feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my pepper plants with dried leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with organic material, known as mulching, prevents hot sun from drying out the ground quickly. It retains soil moisture, keeps the roots cool during dry spells, and stops weeds from growing and taking nutrients away from your peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ

english: How does planting my maize at the very start of the major rainy season help my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi yɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting right as the major rainy season begins ensures the seeds receive reliable moisture when sprouting and developing deep roots, allowing the crop to complete its critical growing period before drier weather sets in.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ dani kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat the inner leaves of my young maize plants, and how do I catch them early?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mamɔ mli mra?

english: These caterpillars are typically fall armyworms, which target the fresh, unrolling leaves inside the central whorl of the maize plant. Inspecting the center of young plants weekly allows you to spot small holes early and apply safe control treatments directly into the whorl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni afolɔ, ni amɛkwɛɔ baai ni ajie ehee ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ dumɔwu lɛ teŋgbɛ daa otsi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona buji bibii. Na kɛjɛ shishijee ni okɛ safe control atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ band lɛ nɔ.

english: Which young sucker shoot should I cut from an old plantain tree to plant a new healthy stand?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei bibii esa akɛ mafolɔ kɛjɛ dumɔwu momo ko mli koni ekwɛ̃ tso hee ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Choose 'sword suckers' that have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a thick base rather than suckers with broad leaves. Sword suckers grow into stronger plantain trees with deeper root systems and produce heavier fruit bunches.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud’ ni baai lɛ mli tse, ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse. Mohu ɔ, hla tso ɔmɛ nɛ a bami ɔmɛ a mi tsɔ. Sword suckers lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ plantains ni he wa ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii.

english: I want to start growing plantains on my land, but how do I know if my soil is good enough for them?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi plantains dumɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha amɛ?

english: Plantains grow best in deep, rich soil that holds moisture well but drains excess water quickly. If your soil stays soggy like a swamp, the roots will rot, but if it is full of organic compost or decayed leaves, plantains will thrive.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Kɛ́ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagboi. Shi kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egboi lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to plant plantains in Ghana so they don't dry up?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ Ghana? Koni ekagbo?

english: The best time to plant is at the onset of the main rainy season, usually around March or April. Planting early in the rains gives the young plant enough time to build strong roots before the dry season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee March loo April. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: How far apart should I space my plantain plants when I am planting them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-plantains lɛ abɔ he beni miduɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains should be planted about 3 meters (around 10 feet) apart in every direction. This gives each plant enough space to spread its large leaves, catch sunlight, and feed from the soil without competing with its neighbors.
ga: Esa akɛ adu plantains aaafee mitai 3 (aaafee ninetalɔi 10) kɛjɛ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa agboi lɛ eshwaa, ni enáa hulu la, ni enaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: How do I choose a healthy sucker from an old plantain plant to start a new one?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ plantain tso momo ko mli koni maje ehe shishi?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—these are small shoots with spear-shaped, narrow leaves and a heavy base. Avoid shoots with broad, flat leaves ('water suckers') as they grow weak and produce smaller bunches.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishitoo ni tsii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe. (‘ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu’) ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii bibii.

english: My plantain plant is growing many small shoots around the bottom; should I leave all of them?
ga: Mi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Mɛi babaoo yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ shishi. Ani esa akɛ mashɛ amɛ fɛɛ mashwie?

english: No, you should cut away most of the extra shoots and keep only one or two strong ones. If you leave too many shoots, they will steal food and water from the main mother plant, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni okɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my plantain plant turning yellow and hanging down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifo shi lɛ?

english: It is natural for older bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up as the plant grows new ones. However, if many leaves turn yellow quickly, it could mean the plant needs nitrogen fertilizer, more water, or is affected by a soil disease.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi be mli ni tso lɛ daa ekoŋŋ lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai babaoo batsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ, Ekolɛ etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. nu babaoo he miihia loo helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ egba enaa

english: How many months will I wait from the day I plant a plantain until I can harvest the fruit?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ kɛjɛ gbi ni odu plantain lɛ nɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa aduawai lɛ?

english: Most plantain varieties take between 11 and 15 months from the day you plant them until the fruit is mature and ready to harvest, depending on rainfall and soil fertility.
ga: Plantain henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 kɛjɛɔ be mli ni oduɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa. Edamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: How do successful farmers protect their tall plantain trees from falling over during heavy winds?
ga: Te okwaafoi ni yeɔ omanye lɛ baanyɛ abu plantains kakadaji ahe koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: When the plantain bunch grows heavy, experienced farmers use strong wooden poles or bamboo forks to support the stem (a practice called 'propping') so heavy winds do not snap the tree before harvest.
ga: Beni plantains akuu lɛ daraa lɛ Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ kɛ tsei ni wa loo ŋmeii ni akɛfee ŋmeii tsuɔ nii kɛfiɔ ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛ. (nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ ‘ŋmɔshi nibii’) koni akɛtsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekakumɔ tsei lɛ dani akpa ŋmaa.

english: Can I plant other crops like maize or cassava on the same plot where I planted plantains?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ani ebaanyɛ ehi he ni aduɔ plantains yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop plantains with fast-growing crops like maize, beans, or cassava during the first few months. This makes good use of the open space until the plantain leaves grow big enough to shade the ground completely.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa awo mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli. Gbɛ nɛɛ haa akɛ he ni agbele lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni plantain baai lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: What key steps do I need to follow if I want to become a successful 'Best Farmer' in my district?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa esa akɛ mafee kɛji miisumɔ ni matsɔ eko? ‘Okwaafoi ni hi fe fɛɛ’ ni yeɔ omanye yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Becoming a top farmer requires using good planting materials, following proper crop spacing, weeding regularly, applying recommended fertilizers at the right time, and constantly learning improved techniques from extension officers and successful peers.
ga: Okwaafonyo ni nɔ kwɔ ni aaafee lɛ biɔ ni akɛ nibii kpakpai ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ atsu nii. Nyiɛmɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa sɛɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ ohe daa. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo mli yɛ be ni sa mli. ni amɛkase ŋaai ni aya hiɛ be fɛɛ be kɛjɛ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ nitsulɔi kɛ nanemɛi nitsulɔi ni yeɔ omanye lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to full sunlight and strong winds. They need shade from fast-growing nurse crops like plantains to protect their soft leaves and keep the soil moist until their root system is strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ amli baawa.

english: Why do I need to lift and tie my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ ni mikɛfiɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need plenty of direct sunlight to manufacture food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the ground prevents diseases from the soil and allows maximum sunlight to reach the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ anaa, ni ehaa hulu la ni fa babaoo shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the tips of lower leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient maize needs to build green stems and leafy growth. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer usually solves this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ŋmãa lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but give me small underground tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akpa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots underground. Loose, well-drained soil helps tuber development.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ wa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɛha tuber lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Why does my soil dry out and crack open so quickly a few days after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture fast because direct heat from the sun bakes it. Covering the soil with dried leaves or straw (mulching) blocks direct heat and traps water in the soil longer for your roots to absorb.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ejaakɛ la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ebaaha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛre.

english: Why should I remove small shoot suckers growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ Ajieɔ.

english: When too many shoots grow from the same plantain stool, they all fight for the same food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only the main stem to produce a much bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantain tsei babaoo ni jɛ tso kome mli lɛ miida lɛ, Nakai tsei lɛ hu baatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ pɛ ni ehaa plantains ni dara ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Why do my maize crops grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they shade each other out and compete for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows it to grow a thick stem and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Consistent watering and shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do the fresh center leaves of my young maize plants look shredded with small green droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai heei lɛ tamɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the central shoot of maize plants and chews the tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei ashishifãi lɛ ateŋ ni ekɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or viruses they carry. These insects suck juices from young leaves, causing them to twist and stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe ni amɛhaa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and have broad leaves that provide temporary shade and moisture, protecting the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli kɛ fɛ̃i. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more plants in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni tsei babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to grow big ears of maize rather than many weak plants with small ears.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa toi wuji. Mohu ɔ, mo du tsohi nɛ a he wa we nɛ tue nyafii ngɛ a mi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha tsei lɛ aná su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil each season and allows specific soil pests to multiply. Rotating your crop with beans or groundnuts adds fresh nutrients back into the soil and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa sũ mli kooloi komɛi feɔ babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii heei baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to be tied to tall wooden sticks to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ sweet potato wain tsei akpɛtɛ tsei kakadaji ahe koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to get access to sunlight. Supporting them with sticks raises their leaves high into the light, allowing the plant to generate more energy and grow much larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei fi amɛsɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛbaai lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya la lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ babaoo. ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara kwraa

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. When water is scarce or temperatures are too high, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ nu faaa loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do weeds in my field make my main crops grow so thin and short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ miifee bibioo ni efee kuku nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than regular crops and steal essential water, fertilizer nutrients, and sunlight away from your crops, leaving your plants starved.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu ni he hiaa, niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that feeds on the central growing tip of maize plants. Controlling them early prevents them from destroying the plant's main growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni miida yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ najiaŋ. Amɛ nɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei titri ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies, or by viruses they carry. Managing these small insects early prevents leaf damage and stops growth stunting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ mli kooloi bibii akwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Etsiɔ baa lɛ fitemɔ naa ni ekpaa dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. Signs of maturity include the bottom leaves turning yellow and falling off, alongside cracks appearing in the soil at the base of the plant where tubers have expanded.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ edara lɛ ahe ji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Kɛfata he lɛ, ŋmeii ni jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi he ni ŋmeii lɛ egbɛ eshwã lɛ.

english: Why are some of the crops on my farm growing strong while the ones right next to them are struggling and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa waa yɛ be mli ni mɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ daraa waa lɛ? Ani oobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oyɛ bibioo lolo?

english: Plants compete for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight just like children sharing a small bowl of food. If seeds are planted too close together or if the soil fertility is uneven, the stronger plant will absorb most of the food, leaving the nearby plant weak and stunted.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ tamɔ gbekɛbii. Jaa niyenii yɛ tsɛnsii bibii amli. Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ejaaa Tsei ni tsii fe fɛɛ lɛ shwieɔ niyenii lɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow well when they are small and then suddenly stop growing and turn weak as they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ beni amɛji bibii ni trukaa lɛ amɛkpaa dalɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: As a plant grows bigger, it needs much more food and space for its roots. If the soil nutrients run out or if tiny pests like nematodes attack the expanding roots underground, the plant will stall and weaken even if it looked healthy at first.
ga: Be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ, niyenii kɛ gbɛ babaoo he miihia lɛ kɛha eshishifãi lɛ. Kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes tutua shishifãi ni miigbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ shishijee lɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ po.

english: Why do my crops sometimes look healthy on the outside, but then suddenly dry up and die out of nowhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ, shi trukaa lɛ, amɛgboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Many crop diseases attack from inside the stem or down in the roots where you cannot see. By the time you notice yellow leaves or wilting above the ground, the sickness has already damaged the inside of the plant beyond recovery.
ga: Tsei ahe helai babaoo tutuaa kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi loo kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli he ni onyɛɛɛ ona amɛ. Kɛji ona baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Hela lɛ efite tso lɛ mligbɛ ni enyɛŋ etsa.

english: What early signs should I look out for to know if my young plants are getting sick before it is too late?
ga: Mɛɛ mra be mli okadii esa akɛ makwɛ jogbaŋŋ koni mana kɛji hela mɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ dani eshɛ sɛɛ tsɔ?

english: Look closely for faint yellow spots under leaves, slow growth compared to surrounding plants, curling leaf edges, or mild wilting during cool mornings. These subtle signs appear long before the entire plant dries up and dies.
ga: Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛdaraa blɛoo kɛ akɛto tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe, baai lɛ ashishigbɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe, loo amɛshwieɔ fioo yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli. Nɛkɛ okadii ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɛɛ jeɔ kpo dani tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbiɔ ni egboɔ.

english: If I notice one plant in my farm dying from a sickness, can it spread and kill the healthy crops around it?
ga: Kɛji miyɔse tso ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni hela miigbo lɛ Ebaagbɛ eshwa ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Ani manyɛ maná nakai tso lɛ?

english: Yes, plant sicknesses caused by fungi, bacteria, or viruses spread easily through rain splash, wind, insects, or even your farm tools. Uprooting and destroying a sick plant early stops the disease from jumping to neighboring healthy crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai ni ŋmeii, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛbaa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ oŋmɔ mli nibii po anɔ. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ashishijee mra kɛ amɛhiɛkpatamɔ Ehaa helai shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How often do I need to walk through my farm to inspect my crops for hidden sickness?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ mli?

english: Walking through your field at least two to three times a week allows you to keep a close eye on your plants. Regular checks help you spot pests or diseases at the very beginning when they are still easy to treat.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ otsɔ ŋmɔji amli shii fioo komɛi yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okwɛ amɛhe daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai mra, be mli ni amɛtsamɔ waaa lolo lɛ.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout and die underground before they even come out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ ni amɛgbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds are extremely delicate while developing underground. If the soil is too wet, infected with fungi, or infested with soil insects, the seed will rot or get eaten before its shoot can reach the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa beni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ, ŋmeii emɔ mli, loo ŋmeii emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi loo abaaye amɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some seedlings in my nursery die off while others in the same bed stay completely healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ saatso kome nɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ?

english: Nursery beds can hold pocket areas of excess water or soil fungi that cause 'damping off' disease. Because young seedlings have tender stems, a localized infection in the soil can quickly kill a few seedlings while others nearby remain untouched.
ga: Nursery beds baanyɛ ahiɛ nu loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni kɛ ‘damp’ hela baa ejaakɛ tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe tsei bibii komɛi oya. yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ kã he amɛtako he.

english: What simple things can I do to protect my crop seeds so they do not rot in the soil after planting?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Treating your seeds with approved protective seed coatings before planting and ensuring your soil is well-drained prevents harmful soil fungi and insects from destroying the seed before it can germinate.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ahe tsɔne ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu dumɔwui ahe nii dani odu ni okwɛ koni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if a young shoot coming out of the soil is healthy or if it is already infected with disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso bibioo ko ni miijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ loo eyɛ hela momo?

english: A healthy shoot emerges firm, upright, and with a bright green color. If the young stem looks brown, soft, pinched at the soil level, or pale, it has likely picked up a soil disease during germination.
ga: Tsoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ wa, amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛyɛ eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ, bɔdɔɔ, ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ekolɛ shikpɔŋ hela emɔ amɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land where I am putting my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ he ni mikɛ mi-kokoo dumɔwui heei lɛ wo lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the soil cool while your young cocoa trees establish their roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni o-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava together with my young cocoa trees on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ cocoa tsei afee ekome kɛdu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: It is best to avoid planting cassava close to young cocoa trees. Cassava roots feed heavily on soil nutrients and water, competing directly with cocoa, and its bushy growth can choke out light from your young trees.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ. Cassava shishifãi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Ekɛ kookoo yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Ni bɔ ni edaa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie la kɛjɛ odumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that your plants are under stress. This is often caused by a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, insufficient shade protecting them from harsh sunlight, or prolonged dry spells without enough moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ enɛ jɛɔ niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. aloo hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal infection known as Black Pod disease. It thrives in wet, cool, and humid conditions. Keeping the farm clear of weeds, pruning heavy branches to let in air, and removing affected pods quickly helps control it.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ehe miihia waa ni jwɛi akafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni ena naagbai lɛ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to cut off branches from my cocoa tree, or will it stop the tree from fruiting?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ? Aloo ebaatsi tso lɛ yibiiwoo naa?

english: Pruning actually encourages more fruit growth. Cutting off weak, diseased, or overcrowded branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the main trunk where cocoa pods form, while also preventing pests from hiding.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa aduawai lɛ daa babaoo. Niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he, he ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is at the start of the rainy season when the soil is moist. The moisture helps the roots absorb the nutrients quickly right as the tree enters its main growing and flowering period.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya beni tso lɛ boteɔ edalɛ kɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to weed around my crops regularly instead of letting the grass grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ daa Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha jwɛi lɛ akwɛ̃

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and nutrients away from your crops. They also act as hiding places for harmful insects and fungal diseases that can easily spread to your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ he ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ amli oya lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ.

english: What should I do about the green bush plants growing directly on the main branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nine titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Those are parasitic plants called mistletoe. They sink roots into your cocoa tree's branches to steal food and water, which eventually kills the branch. You must physically cut them off below where they attach to the tree.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ mistletoe. Amɛwoɔ o-cocoa tsei lɛ aniji amli koni amɛju niyenii kɛ nu. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbe nine lɛ. Esa akɛ ofo amɛ yɛ shishigbɛ he ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ.

english: My cocoa trees produce so many flowers, so why do most of them fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mi koko tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii babaoo. Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: It is natural for cocoa trees to shed many of their flowers. However, heavy shedding happens if there are not enough tiny insects (midges) to pollinate them, or if the tree is stressed by dry weather and low soil nutrients.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi babaoo, shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔi ni tsii baaba kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii (ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ) ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni faaa lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: How many years after planting can I expect my new cocoa trees to start bearing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu nii? Ani manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ cacao tsei heei baaje shishi amɛwo ŋmeii?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties typically start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting if properly cared for, whereas older traditional varieties may take 4 to 5 years to begin producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛje yibiiwoo shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is stressed due to a lack of key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or from receiving too much or too little water. When nutrients are missing, the plant cannot produce chlorophyll, which gives leaves their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu ni fa babaoo loo fioo ni enine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii laaje lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee klorofil. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a survival behavior. During intense heat, plantain plants curl their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing water from evaporating too quickly from inside the plant.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ subaŋ. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baafo amɛbaai lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji koni nu akajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small ragged holes in them like someone sprayed them with tiny bullets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Etamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko ŋɔ tu bibioo ko ni ekɛshwie nɔ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are a classic sign of Fall Armyworm feeding. The caterpillars hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day and eat the tender growing leaves.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm yeɔ nii. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and shady conditions. The fungus attacks the husk of the pod, causing it to turn dark brown or black and spread quickly if infected pods aren't removed.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Fungi lɛ tutuaa pod lɛ mli fã lɛ. Enɛ haa etsɔɔ blɔfo loo ediŋŋ. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji ajieee ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ.
