english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava tubers now compared to three years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa fe afii etɛ ni eho lɛ?

english: Soil loses its fertility when crops are grown continuously without replacing lost nutrients. Cassava draws heavy nutrients from the earth, and over time, depleted soil results in smaller, thinner tubers unless manure or fertilizer is added.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be ni akɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ etsakeee. Cassava jieɔ niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni beni be hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa bulbs bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa. Ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: How do I tell if my crops need fertilizer or if they are just suffering from heavy rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia amɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miipiŋ amɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Heavy rain causes temporary wilting or yellowing due to flooded roots, but plants recover once the soil dries. If leaves stay pale yellow, stems grow thin, and overall growth stops even in good weather, the soil is lacking nutrients and needs fertilizer.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ. Shi tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo lɛ, tso lɛ shishi lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni dalɛ fɛɛ kpaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpakpai amli po. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant three or four maize seeds together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting multiple seeds too close together forces the young plants to compete against each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with weak, thin stems and tiny corn ears instead of one strong plant with a large cob.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso kake nɛ he wa nɛ e ngɛ tso agbo.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any fruit actually grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience environmental shock, such as sudden hot spells, prolonged dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, causing the plant to protect itself by shedding flowers instead of making fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛyashɛ shihilɛi ni ehiii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa trukaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo nitrogen fertilizer babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ buɔ ehe he kɛtsɔ efɔfɔi ni ekɛshwieɔ shi yɛ yibii ni ewoɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the tall trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight and extreme soil heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a cooler microclimate and protects young cocoa leaves from scorching.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ naa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi. Ebaaha nu lɛ daaŋ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe koni amɛkashã.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my farm than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over centuries to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than domesticated crops. Because they grow so aggressively, clearing them early stops them from starving your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and provide broad leafy shade that protects young cocoa trees from intense heat during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ehaa hulutsoo baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy leaf growth. Rain can wash this nutrient away, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni mli wa lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ baanyɛ atsumɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during prolonged drought as a survival mechanism to conserve water. Once the rains return, the plant quickly sprouts fresh leaves and continues growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛto nu he. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the central leaves inside my young maize stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mibii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the soft growth center of maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended treatments into the center tube protects the crop from severe damage.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei bibii ni daraa lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii yɛ paipii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ baabu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ fitemɔ ni mli wa he.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer that helps neighboring maize plants grow bigger and stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: What causes the flowers on my tomato plants to drop off before setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely high or when plants experience inconsistent watering. Extreme heat stresses the plant, making it drop flowers to preserve its survival energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Ha fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi koni akɛto hewalɛ ni akɛhi shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut off mistletoe plants growing on my cocoa branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo mistletoe ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Mistletoe is a parasite that taps into cocoa branches to steal water and food. Leaving mistletoe on your tree weakens the branches, lowers pod yield, and can eventually kill parts of the cocoa tree.
ga: Mistletoe ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ kookoo niji anɔ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ashi mistletoe yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aniji lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni ebaaha pod lɛ yibiiwoo aba shi, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ekolɛ ebaaha cacao tso lɛ fãi komɛi agboi.

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium. Nitrogen promotes big leafy growth above ground, while potassium is the key food required to swell the roots into large tubers.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛto potassium he. Nitrogen haa baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa. Yɛ be mli ni potassium ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants crinkling up and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Crinkled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by viral infections spread by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies. Controlling these sap-sucking insects helps prevent the virus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does the surface of my farm soil turn hard like stone after a heavy rain followed by hot sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soils low in organic matter tend to compact tightly when wet and bake hard under direct sun. Adding compost, manure, or dry leaves breaks up the hard crust so plant roots can breathe and suck up water easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji edɔ ni etswaa waa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo baai ni egbi fata he lɛ, ebaagbala tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa lɛ amli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ nu oya.

english: How do I know if the land I want to farm on is rich enough to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni misumɔɔ ni matsu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ baa nii jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu nii kpakpai?

english: Rich land is usually dark, feels soft, and holds moisture well. If the soil is very light in color, hard, or crops turn yellow quickly without growing tall, it means the soil lacks essential nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ woɔ duŋ. Ehaa mɔ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ mli tse waa, ewa, loo tso lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ oya ni ekwɛɛɛ shɔŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What can I do to make my poor land rich again without buying expensive commercial fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mishikpɔŋ ni yeɔ ohia lɛ afee niiatsɛmɛi ekoŋŋ ni miheee jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa?

english: You can improve poor soil by adding animal manure, rotted plant compost, or planting leguminous cover crops like cowpeas, which pull nitrogen from the air and naturally feed the ground.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ kooloi aŋmei ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. compost rotting plants Aloo dumɔ ŋmãa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa, tamɔ tsina ŋmãa, ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: Does leaving my farm uncultivated for a few years really make the soil stronger?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mishi miŋmɔ lɛ mli afii fioo komɛi ni mitsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, leaving land to rest allows native wild plants to grow, deep roots to bring up buried nutrients, and falling leaves to rot, which naturally restores nutrients back into the topsoil.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ashiɔ koni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ baaha koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ aya hiɛ. Eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni afu lɛ. kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ koni amɛgboi Enɛ baaye abua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does a newly planted mango tree take so many years before it starts giving fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani mango tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Fruit trees like mangoes need three to five years to develop a deep root system and strong stem to gather enough water and support the weight of heavy fruits before producing.
ga: Yibii tsei tamɔ mango he miihia afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa koni amɛbua nu ni fa bɔ ni sa naa ni amɛye amɛbua yibii ni tsii lɛ amli tsiimɔ dani amɛwo.

english: Why are my crops growing poorly when I plant them close to old tree stumps?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tso momo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Old tree roots stay in the ground for a long time, stealing water and nutrients from the soil while physically blocking young crop roots from spreading.
ga: Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ ashishifãi hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow and fall off even when it is not the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi eyɛ mli akɛ jeee hulutsoo be ji lɛ?

english: When crops face stress—such as poor soil nutrients, water shortage, or root damage—they drop their leaves to conserve water and protect themselves from dying.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ haomɔi kpe, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii, nu ni faaa loo shishifãi ni efite lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Does stress on my plants affect the size and quality of my harvest?
ga: Ani nɔnyɛɛ ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛ bɔ ni ehi ha lɛ he?

english: Yes, when plants are stressed by hot weather or bad soil, they focus their energy on survival rather than flowering or making large, healthy fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii miigba tsei anaa. Tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa wala mlihilɛ nɔ fe fɔfɔi loo aduawai wuji ni mli wa ni amɛwoɔ lɛ.

english: Is burning old plants and trees on my farm a good way to clear land for planting?
ga: Ani tsei kɛ tsei momo ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ shikpɔŋ kɛha dumɔwui?

english: Burning quick-clears the land and provides ash that temporarily feeds the soil, but doing it repeatedly destroys beneficial soil organisms and burns away organic matter over time.
ga: Shãa haa he lɛ mli tseɔ oya ni ehaa sũ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ baa. Shi nakai ni afeɔ shii abɔ lɛ Ekpãtãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ ni eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Does the ash left behind after burning tree branches actually help my crops grow?
ga: Ani sũ ni eshwɛɔ yɛ tsei niji ni ashã lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Ash contains potassium and lime which briefly fertilize the soil and reduce acidity, giving your new seeds a fast startup boost for the first season.
ga: Potassium kɛ lime yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo be kukuoo ko. ni okɛ acidity aba shi Ha odumɔwui heei lɛ aje shishi oya yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my elders recommend uprooting old, tired crops before putting new ones in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi onukpai lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ dani adu eheei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Uprooting old crops clears out hidden pests and diseases living in their old roots, giving your fresh seeds clean soil and a healthy start.
ga: Nibii ni egbɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shishifãi momo lɛ amli lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. Odumɔwui heei ni oooha amɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ ji he ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni obaanyɛ oje shishi yɛ.

english: Sir, why do my maize plants start turning yellow and wilting as soon as the rains stop for a few weeks?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi pɛ?

english: Crops need water to carry nutrients from the soil up into their leaves. When the rain stops, the plant loses water through its leaves faster than its roots can drink from the dry ground, causing the leaves to wilt and turn yellow to save energy.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn roll up tight into tubes during the hottest part of the day when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from heat. By rolling up, the leaf exposes less surface to the sun and wind, which slows down water loss while the plant waits for cooler weather.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. kɛji akɛ abɔle ehe lɛ Baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he tsɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ mɛɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ lɛ.

english: Sir, why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into fruits during this dry period?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ nɛkɛ hɔmɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water during hot weather, they drop their flowers to save water and stay alive, because producing fruit requires a lot of moisture and energy that the plant currently lacks.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere nu ni ehi wala mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai afeemɔ biɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ babaoo, ni ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ tsei lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants stay short and stop growing leaves when the dry spell lasts long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ feɔ kuku ni ekpaa baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, plants go into a survival mode. Instead of using energy to grow taller or make new leaves, they pause their growth to keep their underground roots alive until water returns.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Tso lɛ baaya wala shihilɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ daa aloo a peeɔ ba ehehi. Amɛkpaa dalɛ be kukuoo ko koni amɛkwɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ kɛyashi nu lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I keep growing food on my farm if the rains stop falling completely this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maya nɔ madu niyenii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: When rains fail, farmers can adapt by collecting water for simple drip irrigation, covering the soil with leaves to keep it cool, and planting dry-season crops that require very little water to survive.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, okwaafoi baanyɛ atsake amɛhe kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛbua naa kɛha nu ni shwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nɔ. Okɛ baai aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni edɔ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ni kɛ nu fioo ko pɛ tsuɔ nii koni wala ahi shi lɛ

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my crops with dry grass and leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Nibii ni jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with leaves or grass, known as mulching, shades the soil from the hot sun. This stops water from evaporating quickly and keeps the soil moist for your crops for a much longer time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Sir, what will happen to my crop seeds if I plant them before the rain fully establishes?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛ kwraa?

english: If seeds get just enough rain to sprout but the rain stops right after, the fragile young roots will dry out in the hot soil and the crop will die before it can grow deep into the ground.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwu ko ná nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkwɛ̃ shi nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ, shishifãi bibii ni waaa lɛ baagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagboi dani eda kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out and form hard cracks so quickly after the rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Soil cracks when it lacks organic matter like compost or animal manure to hold moisture. Hot sunlight bakes the bare soil, causing the clay inside it to shrink and split open.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fãa kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ. Enɛ haa sũ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Which crops can survive and give me a harvest if the weather stays very dry in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii aha mi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ mli edɔ waa yɛ Ghana?

english: Crops like cassava, cowpeas, millet, and sorghum have deep roots or tough leaves that allow them to endure heat and produce food with much less rain than crops like maize or vegetables.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ dɔlɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo fe ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Sir, why do big mango trees stay green in the dry season while my vegetables dry up completely?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mango tso agbo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo yɛ fɛ̃i be mli shi mi-aduawai lɛ fɛɛ gboɔ lɛ?

english: Large fruit trees have long taproots that grow deep underground to drink hidden water, while vegetable crops have short roots that can only reach the top layer of soil, which dries out quickly without rain.
ga: Tsei wuji ni woɔ yibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kakadaji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛnu nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, aduawai tsei yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni baanyɛ ashɛ sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ pɛ. ni baagbi oya ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there is too much sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects the young trees and keeps the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tso bibioo lɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers during the hottest part of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and the air is dry, pepper plants drop their blossoms to save energy and water. Providing partial shade or watering early in the morning helps the plants retain their flowers so they can produce fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛre loo nu shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize draws the same nutrients out of the ground every season, leaving the soil weak and tired over time. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts goodness back into the soil and breaks crop disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ. Ye obua ni okɛ ekpakpafeemɔ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. ni efo tso helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to support good crop growth without chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua tsei ni dara jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Healthy soil is dark, soft, crumbles easily in your hands, and holds water well after rain. If natural weeds grow thick and dark green on the plot before clearing, it shows the soil has good natural plant food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ yɛ ediŋŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli. ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ Kɛji adebɔɔ mli jwɛi kwɛ̃ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ajie lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why do my garden eggs wilt in the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the ground. Covering the bare soil around the plants with dried grass or leaves helps trap moisture and keep root temperatures cool.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: How do I know the right time to put seeds in the ground after the dry season ends?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until after two or three strong, steady rains have thoroughly soaked the soil deep down. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if dry weather returns immediately.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba trukaa.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide inside the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli?

english: These caterpillars, known as fall armyworms, hatch from tiny eggs laid by moths on the corn leaves. Inspecting plants early and applying neem leaf juice or recommended treatments into the leaf funnel stops them from destroying the plant center.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi. Efɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔŋloo bibioo ko mli. he ni ŋmeii jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa baai anɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra kɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ ni akɛwoɔ baa lɛ mli gbɛi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akafite tso lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellowish-white?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ-yɛŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is often caused by a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Using clean, disease-free cassava stem cuttings for planting prevents this sickness from taking over your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei niji ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii kɛ́ oodu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela nɛɛ akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rot before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom end rot, happen when plants cannot get enough calcium due to irregular soil moisture. Keeping the soil consistently damp by watering regularly prevents the fruit from rotting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooshwie nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to produce large, healthy cobs instead of many weak ones.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa. Yɛ cob ni bɛ hewalɛ kuu ko najiaŋ

english: Root rot usually happens when water gets trapped around the roots in heavy soil, allowing fungus to grow. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ta shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ, ni no haa ŋmeii daa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋma lɛ mli?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer twice: first about two weeks after sprouting when the young plants start growing leaves, and again when the maize is knee-high. Applying it when the soil is moist helps the roots absorb the nutrients quickly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shii enyɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni tsei bibii lɛ ekwɛ̃, beni tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ baai shishi lɛ. Ni agbɛnɛ hu, kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ shɛ tsitsi nɔ Kɛ́ akɛwo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, preventing fungal diseases and helping the tubers grow much larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by severe heat, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients. Mulching the soil around the plants keeps the roots cool and moist, helping the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Mulching around Tso lɛ haa eshishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I buy certified hybrid seeds instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and easily succumb to local pests and dry spells. Certified seeds are bred to resist common diseases and yield significantly more grain under local conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛhe oya yɛ jɛmɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni amɛwo dumɔwui babaoo yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry winds and heat, cocoa trees lose water quickly. Dropping some of their leaves is a natural survival trick to conserve water until the rainy season returns.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ latsaa be mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ nu fiteɔ oya. Baai lɛ ekomɛi ni ashiɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo he ŋaa ni akɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and yellow even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal nitrogen and fertilizer from the soil before your crops can reach them. Without these nutrients, your crops look hungry and weak even with plenty of rain.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nitrogen kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Kɛji niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ bɛ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni hɔmɔ miiye amɛ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up in the afternoon heat even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛfeee nakai moŋ lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In hot sun, tomato leaves curl up to reduce the leaf surface exposed to heat, stopping moisture from evaporating too quickly. As long as the soil remains moist, the leaves usually open back up when the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ baabɔle amɛhe koni eha baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulutsoo baa lɛ aba shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Baai lɛ hu sumɔɔ ni amɛgbele be mli ni gbɛkɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right crop to farm if I want to get good income for all my effort and money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ? Kɛji miisumɔ ni maná shika kpakpa kɛjɛ mimɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ shika fɛɛ mli?

english: Choosing the right crop depends on your local soil, rainfall pattern, and market demand in your local market. Vegetables like tomatoes and pepper grow fast for quick cash, while tree crops like cocoa or oil palm require patience but offer long-term income.
ga: Nibii ni sa ni abaahala lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ yɛ omaŋ jarayelihe lɛ. Aduawai tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛná shika oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo mu tso biɔ tsuishitoo shi ehaa shika ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why should I clear my land without burning the bush before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shãaa jwɛi lɛ dani madu nii?

english: Burning destroys the good organic matter and beneficial insects in the topsoil, leaving the ground dry and weak. Clearing without burning leaves organic mulch that decomposes into free natural food for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baafite akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko, ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What do agricultural officers mean when they say crops need the 'big three' nutrients to grow well?
ga: Mɛni okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ tsɔɔ beni amɛkɛɛ tsei he miihia niyenii mli hewalɛ? ‘Nibii etɛ ni he hiaa’ kɛha dalɛ kpakpa

english: Crops main survival needs come from three major nutrients: Nitrogen for leaf greenness, Phosphorus for strong root growth, and Potassium for flower and fruit development. These are commonly supplied together in NPK fertilizers.
ga: Hiamɔ nii titri ni tsei yɔɔ koni amɛhi shi lɛ jɛɔ niyenii titrii etɛ mli: Nitrogen kɛha baai lɛ aŋɔli. Fosfɔs kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ potassium kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai adalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ ekome yɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the plant is starving for nitrogen or suffering from too much water in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure brings back the green leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miipiŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, be mli ni mi hu shwieee lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink from the soil. Placing dry grass or leaves around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and slows down water loss.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ pepper aduawai?

english: Flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when watering is uneven, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ni haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant my cassava cuttings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yucca tsei niji ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over soil food, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives each plant room to spread its roots and produce larger tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni efeɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by small pests like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of young leaves. Spraying early with neem oil or recommended organic treatments protects the leaves so they can expand normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem fɔ ni ashwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than the crops I spent money to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni mifite shika kɛdu lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that adapt very easily to local soil and weather conditions. They steal water and fertilizer meant for your crop, which is why clearing them early gives your crop the advantage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni tsakeɔ ehe ehaa shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mlɛo waa. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie nibii amli mra lɛ. Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why do seeds bought from the agro-chemical store perform better than seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ agrochemical shwapoi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought certified seeds are selected and tested to resist local diseases, tolerate drought, and give high yields, whereas seeds saved year after year lose their strength and yield over time.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye maŋ lɛ mli helai anɔ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do farmers make large soil mounds or ridges before planting yams instead of planting directly in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi maa gɔji wuji dani amɛduɔ ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Making high soil mounds creates loose, deep soil that allows yam tubers to expand easily underground while also improving water drainage so the seed pieces do not rot during heavy rains.
ga: Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, afeɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni dumɔwui amli fãi lɛ akafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Can I cut a whole yam into pieces to plant my farm, and how do I prevent the cut pieces from rotting in the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafolɔ sweet potato muu koni makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ enaa koni ekafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can cut clean, healthy yams into smaller seed pieces, but you should coat the cut surfaces with wood ash or fungicide and let them dry briefly to protect them from soil pests and rot before planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni okɛfee dumɔwui bibii, shi esa akɛ okɛ tso sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii awo he ni ofolɔ lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ha egbi be kukuoo ko koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akafite dani adu.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden stakes to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji ni amɛkwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb tall stakes so their leaves can trap sunlight efficiently to make food for growing large tubers, while also keeping the leaves off the damp soil to prevent disease.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛkwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛha niyenii aha ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni helai akamɔ bo.

english: How do I know if my yam crop is focusing on growing leaves above ground or actually developing tubers under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ema baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: During the first few months, the yam plant spends its energy building a dense vine and leaf canopy above ground; once the leaves are fully established, the plant shifts its energy downward to form and swell the tuber.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ, Sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ wain tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ egbe naa lɛ Tsei lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ shi koni amɛfee bulbs ni amɛfuu.

english: What kind of soil is best for starting a successful yam farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha sweet potato ŋmɔ ni yeɔ omanye shishijee yɛ Ghana?

english: Yams grow best in deep, well-drained fertile soils like sandy loams that stay moist without trapping excess standing water, as heavy clay soils restrict tuber growth and cause rotting.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ ŋã ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni nu ni damɔ shi babaoo ehiɛɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni tsii lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my yam farm so the crop benefits the most?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná tsei lɛ ahe sɛɛ babaoo?

english: Fertilizer is best applied around 8 to 12 weeks after planting, once the yam vine has sprouted strong leaves and healthy roots that can actively absorb the nutrients to feed the developing tuber.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ otsii 8 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni sweet potato wain tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ, eshishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa. ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ekɛha bulb ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Is it good for me to plant crops like groundnuts or beans in the spaces between my yam mounds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu tsei tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ he ni yɔɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting low-growing legumes like groundnuts between yam mounds covers the bare soil to reduce weeds, protects the ground from drying out, and naturally adds nitrogen to enrich the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni shwereɔ fioo tamɔ ŋmeii ni ato yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi lɛ aba shi. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi ni okɛ nitrogen afata he yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines turning yellow and showing dark spots during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ diji yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves with dark spots in wet weather are usually caused by a fungal leaf disease like anthracnose, which spreads in high moisture and can be controlled using crop rotation and recommended fungicides.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ahelai tamɔ anthracnose, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ, ni abaanyɛ akudɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ akudɔ baai lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my yams are fully mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole mound?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ni okɛ sũ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Yams are mature when the leaves and vines begin to naturally turn yellow and dry up at the end of the rainy season, showing that the plant has finished transferring nutrients into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my harvested yams sprout or soft-rot quickly when I store them at home, and how can I keep them fresh longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ loo egboɔ oya kɛ mikɛto shia lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yams rot or sprout prematurely when kept in hot, dark, or poorly ventilated places; storing them raised off the ground in a shade-covered, well-ventilated yam barn keeps them cool and fresh for months.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni edɔɔ, duŋ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ. Ha sweet potatoi aka shikpɔŋ yɛ sweet potatoi ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Ehaa amɛhe jɔɔ ni amɛhe jɔɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: How can I grow crops on grassland (sare) when I don't have any river or irrigation system nearby?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔji amli (saris) be mli ni mibɛ faa loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Grassland soils dry out quickly without nearby water sources. You can conserve rainwater in the soil by mulching (covering the soil with dry grass or leaves) or by choosing drought-tolerant crops like cassava, sorghum, or cowpeas that grow well on rain alone.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jwɛi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni nu jɛɛhe ko bɛ ni bɛŋkɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ nugbɔ nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oookɛwo mli lɛ nɔ. (Ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ) loo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, loo tsina ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ pɛ nɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and turn yellow during the dry season when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need water to pull nutrients from the soil up into their leaves. During dry periods without irrigation, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from dry earth, causing them to wilt and stop growing to save energy.
ga: Nu he miihia tsei koni amɛgbala niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, nu shwieee nɔ. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei gboɔ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Can I still plant vegetable crops like tomatoes if my farm is in a dry area with no stream?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai tamɔ tomato lolo kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni nu bɛ ni faai bɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Vegetables need steady moisture to produce good fruit. In dry areas without streams, you can build rainwater collection pits or switch to hardier crops like okra and peppers that survive better in hot, dry conditions.
ga: Ehe miihia ni aduawai lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai. Yɛ hei ni egbi ni faai bɛ lɛ Obaanyɛ oma nugbɔ nu ni akɛkpaa ŋshɔ loo otsake kɛya tsei ni wa ni kwɛ̃ɔ tamɔ okra kɛ pepper nɔ. koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ

english: If I spray weedkiller all over my farm, will it harm the crops I planted alongside the weeds?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Ani ebaaye ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ jwɛi lɛ ahe lɛ awui?

english: General weedkillers (non-selective herbicides) kill any green plant they touch, including your crops. You must protect your crops with a spray shield or use crop-specific herbicides that only target broadleaf weeds or grasses.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi (tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa) gbeɔ tsei eŋɔli ni amɛkɛkpeɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii fata he. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ abu onibii ahe. Aloo okɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli ni gbeɔ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ pɛ atsu nii.

english: How do I know the correct amount of chemical to mix so I don't destroy my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛfutu lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, efiteee midumɔ nii lɛ.

english: Using too much chemical can burn crop leaves and ruin the soil, while using too little will not control pests. Always use the recommended measuring cup on the bottle label or ask an agricultural extension officer to help calculate the correct dose for your sprayer.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni akɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, enyɛŋ eye tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ nɔ. Kɛ susumɔ kɔɔpoo ni atsɔɔ yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be. Aloo bi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni eye ebua bo ni obu shika ni sa kɛha o-sprayer lɛ he akɔntaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize curling up after my neighbor sprayed chemicals on his farm nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni akutsoŋnyo ko kɛ tsofai eshwie ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wind can carry chemical spray from a neighbor's field onto your crops, a problem known as chemical drift. When unintended herbicides land on your maize, they disrupt the plant's normal growth and burn or curl the leaves.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛjɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛba onibii anɔ. Enɛ ji naagba ko ni ale lɛ akɛ tsofa ni shwieɔ shi. Kɛji tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ bagbee ŋmãa nɔ yɛ oshara mli Ebaatsi tso lɛ dalɛ ni sa lɛ naa. ni baai lɛ baashã loo amɛbaakpãtã.

english: How long do I need to wait after spraying chemicals on my farm before it is safe to harvest the crops?
ga: Beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani efee shweshweeshwe akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Every farm chemical has a safe waiting period called a pre-harvest interval (PHI). Harvesting too soon leaves dangerous chemical residues on the crop that can make consumers sick.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛmɛɔ ni ale lɛ akɛ be ni akɛkpaa nii dani akpaa nii (PHI). Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ lɛ haa tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni baanyɛ aha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ hela mɔ amɛ.

english: Is it good to burn dry grass on my farmland before planting, or does it hurt the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu? Aloo ebaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Burning grass clears land quickly, but the intense heat destroys essential soil nutrients and friendly earthworms while drying out the land. Clearing manually and letting dry grass rot into the soil creates natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo lɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ. Nine ni okɛjieɔ jwɛi lɛ ni ohaa efiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do crops grow well in dark forest soil but struggle to produce yields in open grassland soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ koo mli shikpɔji ni mli ewo duŋ nɔ shi amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛwo yibii yɛ jwɛi shikpɔji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Grassland soil often lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen and holds less organic matter compared to shaded forest soil. Adding animal manure or compost helps grassland soil hold moisture and feed crop roots properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔji ni yɔɔ jwɛi shikpɔji anɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni amɛbɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo kɛ akɛto shikpɔji ni yɔɔ kooi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ mli lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kooloi alɛɛhei lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaa niyenii ni sa kɛha tsei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster after I clear open land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni adu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing land exposes weed seeds buried in the soil to direct sunlight and rain, which triggers them to sprout fast. Planting cover crops like mucuna right after clearing helps shade out weed seeds before they take over.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ mucilage amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani akɛwo mli.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning dark and rotting just two days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ bɔi duŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni mikɛfo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain active, living tissues after harvest. Once exposed to air, chemical reactions inside the root cause rapid oxidation and internal rotting within 48 to 72 hours unless processed or stored properly.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ miitsu nii lolo. Eji fãji ni hiɛ ka yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo kɔɔyɔɔ mli Tsofai ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ kɛ oksideshin baa oya kɛ mligbɛ fitemɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli ja atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ loo akɛto.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot much faster when I leave them under direct sunlight before taking them home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya waa kɛ́ mishi amɛ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ dani mikɛba shia lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight bakes the outer skin of harvested yams, weakening their natural natural protective coat and creating heat damage that allows decay bacteria and fungi to quickly break down the tuber inside.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ŋmɔtɔ ni akpa lɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ. Enɛ haa ebɔɔ su ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ baa shi. Ni ekɛ dɔlɛ fiteɔ nii ni haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɔnei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ oya.

english: Why does my stored maize get hot and moldy even when kept inside a covered room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli edɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto tsu ko ni aha nɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Grains trap moisture inside if they are not completely dried before storage. Fungi and insects feed on this trapped moisture, generating heat and condensation that cause the surrounding grain to spoil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baahi mli kɛji amɛgbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Fungi kɛ kooloi bibii yeɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli nɛɛ. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni hoɔ ni fiteɔ dumɔwui ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ baa.

english: Why do my fresh tomatoes turn soft and spoil quickly when kept in tied plastic bags during transport?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato hee lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya kɛ́ akɛwo plastic kotoku mli beni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continuously release heat and a natural gas called ethylene as they mature. Sealed plastic traps this heat and moisture, creating a warm environment that drastically speeds up ripening and rot.
ga: Tomatoi jieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ be fɛɛ be beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Plastic ni atsĩ naa lɛ mɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni shwereɔ ni egboɔ oya kwraa lɛ baa.

english: Why do the bottom leaves on my maize plants turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, it pulls this essential food from its older bottom leaves and sends it up to feed the new growth, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and die off first.
ga: Beni nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eyaha ŋmãa heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants abort their flowers when stressed by intense heat, drought, or nutrient shortages. The plant drops flowers to save its limited water and energy just to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baaŋmɛɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ fioo ko he koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pod is a disease caused by mold that thrives in damp, dark environments. Excess shade and rain splash carry spores onto the pods, causing them to rot rapidly right on the tree.
ga: Black pod ji hela ko ni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ duŋ kɛbaa. Shade babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie spores kɛya pods lɛ amli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛgboɔ oya yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow thin and weak if I let many of them grow around one mother plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe waaa kɛji miha babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe lɛ? nyɛ kome tso

english: Multiple suckers connected to the same base compete against each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Removing extra suckers leaves more nutrients for the main plant to yield larger bunches.
ga: Suckers babaoo ni kɛ amɛhe ebɔ shishitoo kome he lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Suckers ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ naa niyenii babaoo koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my young mango trees drop most of their small fruit long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii lɛ? Bei pii lɛ dani kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Trees drop excess immature fruit when they realize they do not have enough water or nutrients to support all of them to maturity, protecting the tree from exhausting itself.
ga: Tso lɛ baashwie aduawai ni eshɛko babaoo tsɔ beni eyɔse akɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛdara lɛ bɛ lɛ. Buu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ tɔlɛ he

english: Why do my sweet potatoes become watery and lose their sweetness if left in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ nu ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once sweet potato leaves dry and yellow, the tubers stop making sugar. Left too long in wet soil, the roots absorb excessive water and start breaking down, reducing sweetness and starch quality.
ga: Beni sweet potato baai lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Tubers lɛ baakpa sugar feemɔ. Ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ashikishaŋ lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ ekpakpafeemɔ baa shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the top young leaves to keep growing, leaving the older bottom leaves hungry and yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni baai lɛ aya nɔ ada. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee momo, hɔmɔ kɛ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas in my field improve the growth of my maize crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea roots decay, they release this nitrogen, feeding the maize crop naturally.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji cowpea shishifãi lɛ fite Ebaajie nitrogen ni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly wet, and humid conditions. Pruning heavy branches lets sunshine and airflow into the farm to stop the fungi from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ duŋ mli Fɛ̃i tsɔ ni edɔ waa, ŋmei ni afolɔ waa lɛ baatsi hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ŋmei lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and stop growing healthy fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, or viruses spread by these insects. Sprinkling clean water under leaves or using soap-water sprays can deter these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tso mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nu ni mli tse ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ kooloi nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete intensely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They spend all their energy stretching upward for light instead of making thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Akɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala kane lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi, moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings when starting a new farm in Techiman?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe beni mijeɔ ŋmɔ hee shishi yɛ Techiman lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct overhead sunlight. Fast-growing plantain leaves act as natural broad umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and cooler soil during its first few years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui shãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain baai ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli kwɔ. Ha coco shade ni mli tse kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot, when the soil dries out suddenly, or when pollinators like bees are absent to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ trukaa Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi, tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ koni amɛha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell if cassava tubers under the soil are mature enough to harvest without digging up the whole crop?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa ni akumɔɔɔ amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is mature when the main stem becomes thick and woody, the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and small cracks appear on the soil surface around the base of the plant.
ga: Cassava shɛɔ dalɛ he beni tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ tso. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up bent into weird shapes and small instead of straight and large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee naakpɛɛ ni eyɛ bibioo moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ kɛ agbo lɛ?

english: Yams bend and stay small when the soil is hard, stony, or compacted. Loose, deep soil or high raised mounds allow the yam tubers to expand downward smoothly without obstruction.
ga: Sweet potatoes baabɔle ehe ni ebaafee bibioo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that spread sideways near the topsoil rather than deep underground. Heavy rain softens the soil, making it easy for wind to tip over heavy fruiting plants.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa sɛɛgbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa tsei ni woɔ yibii ni tsii lɛ amɛshwie shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves burn and turn brown when I clear all the trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are soft and sensitive to high heat and direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains around them to block the intense mid-day sun, the leaves lose water too fast and burn up.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ darako ni amɛnuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii bɛ he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Koni ekɛtsi hulu la lɛ naa yɛ gbi lɛ mli Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya tsɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means the soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its old lower leaves up to the young top leaves to survive, showing that the farm needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Etsɔɔ kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is Black Pod Disease, caused by a small water mold that spreads easily in cool, damp weather. When rainy seasons stay wet and air cannot flow through overcrowded branches, the mold grows quickly on the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nu mli ŋmei bibioo ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ kɛ fɛ̃i mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ, Fɛ̃i lɛ daa oya yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my cassava have tall, bushy stems with leaves but very thin roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai yɔɔ mli shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen compared to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and branches above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eniji lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if the ground has enough moisture to plant my maize seeds when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛdu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should wait until the rain wets the soil deep enough that you can squeeze a handful of earth from a small hole and it holds together in a soft ball without crumbling right away.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ sũ lɛ nɔ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛmimɔ sũ ko kɛjɛ bu bibii lɛ amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ amɛ afee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo. ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak without bearing much fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe waaa shi amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots fight over water and food in the soil, causing them to stretch tall for light instead of producing fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni ekɛ la lɛ awo mli moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why does my farm yield less harvest every year even though I use the exact same land and seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Every crop harvest removes goodness and nutrients from the earth. If crops are grown on the exact same spot every season without resting the soil, adding manure, or rotating crops, the soil becomes hungry and exhausted.
ga: Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ jieɔ kpakpafeemɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei yɛ he kome daa be mli ni aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he, loo atsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before growing into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by sudden hot dry weather, lack of water, or when helpful insects like bees are not around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni edɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ ji koni akɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing green and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting clean, disease-resistant stem cuttings stops the sickness from appearing.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ adu tsei niji ni he tse ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela akamɔ bo.

english: Why did many of the maize seeds I buried in the soil fail to shoot up out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mifuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to come up if they were planted too deep in the soil where air cannot reach them, if the ground was too dry, or if insects and birds ate them before they could sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi ye lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and the plants staying very short this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ hu miifee kuku yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves and stunted growth usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for the crop. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the maize plants the energy they need to grow tall and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer fata he lɛ, ebaaha o-corn tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing lots of tall green leaves but giving me tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too tightly, the cassava plant puts all its strength into leaf growth above ground instead of expanding its tubers below. Loose soil with balanced nutrients helps tubers grow thick.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbala yitso lɛ shishi lɛ, Loamy shikpɔŋ ni niyenii ni ja yɔɔ mli lɛ haa bulbs ni mli wa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do I get a smaller total harvest when I plant my maize seeds very close together to squeeze more onto my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibiiwoo fɛɛ nɔ bibioo nɔ beni miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni mikɛmiimi babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight each other for food and water in the soil, and their leaves block sunlight from neighboring plants. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets full sunlight and food to make large ears.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha etoi lɛ adara.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce small, light bunches when many young shoots grow around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: The extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main mother plant. Removing most of the extra shoots leaves the mother plant with enough energy to build a heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Tso krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plant roots rot and the leaves droop whenever heavy rains flood my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ ni naa wa baaha miŋmɔ lɛ mli afua gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water sits in the soil for too long without draining, roots drown, stop taking in nutrients, and begin to rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛkpaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before turning into fruits during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High heat combined with dry soil stresses the plant, forcing it to drop its flowers to save energy and stay alive. Keeping the soil cool with mulch and watering regularly preserves the flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni fata shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwie shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ, ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree during the wet months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that loves wet, shady conditions. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air flow through the farm dries out the trees and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungs ko ni sumɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Kɛ́ atsake tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce very small harvests even if I water my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm; their fast-growing roots suck up the fertilizer and moisture meant for your crops, leaving your crops weak and starving.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Eshishifãi ni daa oya lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye bo.

english: Why do seeds I save from my previous harvest grow weaker crops than certified seeds bought from an agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ wo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their natural vigor and carry over hidden diseases from previous seasons, while certified seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests and produce uniform, high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni amɛtsɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why do my cassava stalks grow better when I plant them at a slanted angle instead of flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slant buries multiple growth nodes under the soil while leaving others open to air, allowing deep roots to form easily while stems sprout quickly toward sunlight.
ga: Yucca tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ fuɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni miida lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ be mli ni eshiɔ hei krokomɛi ni kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ hulu la mli.

english: Is it necessary to completely clear all old food crops from my land before planting new ones?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ajie niyenii tsei momoi fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu eheei?

english: Clearing old crops helps remove pests and diseases that might be hiding in leftover stems. It also cleans the field so new crops do not have to fight old plants for water, sunlight, and nutrients.
