ga: Nibii ni egbɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni ekolɛ amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ amli lɛ. Etsuɔ he lɛ hu he nii bɔni afee ni ehe ehiaaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii heei kɛ tsei momoi awuu koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil is the reason my crops are growing poorly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your plants have yellow leaves, grow very slowly, or produce small roots despite good rainfall, the soil is likely low in nutrients. Weak soil needs compost, manure, or fertilizer to help crops perform well.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ, edaa blɛoo waa, loo eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo. Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I leave my farmland to rest for a season if my harvest keeps getting smaller?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi be ko kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiba shi?

english: Yes, leaving land to rest—known as fallowing—allows the soil to naturally rebuild its nutrients and organic matter, leading to a much better harvest when you plant again.
ga: Hɛɛ, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe. Ale lɛ hu akɛ shigbeemɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee niyenii heei kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmaa kpakpa kwraa kɛji odu ekoŋŋ.

english: Officer, why am I harvesting very small cassava tubers even though I planted on time?
ga: Official Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmei shishifãi bibii toɔ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ be naa moŋ?

english: Small tubers usually happen when the soil is too hard for roots to expand, or when weeds steal the crop's food. Loosening the soil into mounds and weeding regularly gives the tubers space to grow big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. aloo be mli ni jwɛi juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ gɔji ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ daa lɛ baaha bulb lɛ aná he ko ni da.

english: What farm practices can I do to turn around a poor cassava crop and get a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mawo ŋmei tsei ni ehiii lɛ shi ekoŋŋ ni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: You can improve yield by planting high-quality stems, making high soil mounds for loose earth, weeding during the first four months, and applying compost or fertilizer early in the season.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Feemɔ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛha shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji ejwɛ lɛ mli. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: If my cassava crop looks weak halfway through the farming season, can I still save it?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ fã mli lɛ Ani manyɛ makwɛ nɔ lolo?

english: Yes, clearing surrounding weeds immediately and heap loose soil around the bases of the plants (earthing up) can give the cassava the boost it needs to feed and enlarge its tubers before harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ. Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni abua naa yɛ tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ nɔ) lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha ŋmei lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekɛ bulbs lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ aya hiɛ dani akpa.

english: Does the quality of the cassava stem I choose to plant affect my final harvest?
ga: Ani bɔ ni ŋmeii ni mihala akɛ makwɛ lɛ hi ha lɛ baaná naagbee ŋmaa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, taking stems from healthy, mature plants with no disease spots gives your crop a strong start, resulting in faster sprouting and bigger cassava tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda ni hela bɛ he lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha onibii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ wuji.

english: Why do some food crops fail when I plant them too close together on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii tsei komɛi shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight for the same soil food and water, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other, causing weak growth and low yields.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa.

english: What can I put on my land to help food crops grow well if I don't have money for chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua niyenii ni eda jogbaŋŋ kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: You can add decomposed poultry manure, cow dung, or composted plant leaves to your soil. Organic manure improves soil structure, holds water, and releases nutrients over time.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kooloi ashishifã ni egbo, tsina ashishifãi, loo tsei ahe baai afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Organic fertilizers haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo, ehiɛɔ nu mli, ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do cassava tubers sometimes rot underground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Underground rot is often caused by excess water pooling around the roots in heavy soil. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps drain excess water away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔleɔ shishifãi ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi fitemɔ baa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli, ni ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the base will help restore nutrient levels.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ jɛɛhe titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do groundnut plants help make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Te ŋmei tso baafee tɛŋŋ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants are legumes, meaning they work with helpful bacteria in their roots to take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When the plants decompose, that nitrogen stays in the soil as free fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Peanut tso lɛ ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛkɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ fite Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth. Rotating pepper with crops like maize or beans keeps the soil balanced and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ je lɛŋ. Pepper ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni atsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa helai lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ani okɛ ohe ewo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which feed on tender young maize leaves inside the central whorl. Inspecting leaves early and applying appropriate organic or approved sprays in the early morning helps prevent total crop loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni oookwɛ baai lɛ amli mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni sa loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii leebi lɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot because waterlogged soil starves the roots of air and creates ideal conditions for fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. ni efee shihilɛ ni sa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when planted in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate roots and thin leaves that easily burn and dry out under strong sun heat. They require shade crops like plantains or cassava to create a cool, moist canopy until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo yucca koni amɛfee ŋwɛitsu ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ. Kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and regular watering helps the plant retain its flowers and produce tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli trukaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũu be fɛɛ be, ni afɔ lɛ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ tomato.

english: Why should I remove some of the small shoot suckers growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ Ajieɔ.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain stem for water, sunlight, and soil food. Pruning off the excess suckers and leaving only one or two allows the main plant to put all its energy into producing large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwo ŋmeii agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high up into the sunlight so their leaves can produce food for the root underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot, damp soil where fungal rot can infect the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni hulu la ashɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii aha amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ baanyɛ atswa tso lɛ hela.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my cultivated crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have naturally adapted to aggressively absorb water, sunlight, and soil food much faster than domesticated crops. Clearing weeds early in the season prevents them from stealing vital nutrients away from your farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: If I cut down all the trees and bush off my land before planting, will my crops grow better?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mifolɔ tsei kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ dani midu hu? Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaya hiɛ?

english: Clearing heavy bush gives young seedlings sunlight and removes weeds, but cutting down all large trees leaves the soil naked to hot sun and heavy rain. Leaving some canopy trees or planting temporary shade crops keeps the soil moist and protects tender young plants.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei bibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ aná hulu la, ni ebaaha jwɛi lɛ akashɛ amɛhe. Shi tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ loo odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Should I remove old tree stumps from my farm before planting new crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tsei momoi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani madu tsei heei?

english: Yes, removing old decaying stumps is good because pests like termites and diseases like root rot often live inside dead wood. Clearing them out prevents these diseases from spreading to the roots of your fresh seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei akutsei ni egbɔ ni egbo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai tamɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ hiɔ tsei ni egboi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã odumɔwui heei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I measure and plant my crop seedlings in straight lines instead of scattering them across the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu ni madu tsei ahe dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛ mashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight, measured rows makes sure every plant gets equal space, soil nutrients, and sunlight. It also makes it much easier for you to walk through the farm to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest without stepping on young plants.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni asusu he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo hu kɛhaa bo akɛ oootsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oyajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa ni okɛ onaji akashɛɛɛ tsei bibii anɔ.

english: What happens if I plant thousands of my seedlings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seedlings are crowded together, their roots fight under the ground for water and food, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other. This causes the plants to grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in a very poor harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa, amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my young seedlings wither and die shortly after I move them from the nursery into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by transplant shock, where young roots dry out or get damaged during moving. Transplanting during cool weather (early morning or late afternoon) and watering the plant immediately helps the roots establish quickly in the main field.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi loo amɛbaafite yɛ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ (leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli) kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ saatso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do young tree crops take several years before they start producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani tsei bibii woɔ yibii lɛ?

english: During their first few years, tree crops focus all their energy on growing deep root systems and strong trunks to support heavy harvests later. They need time to mature before they can hold flowers and fruits.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ Tsei tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdaraa kɛ tsei akutsei ni wa lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛye amɛbua ŋmaakpamɔi wuji ni baa sɛɛ mli lɛ. Be he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara dani amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Can I plant short-term food crops like cassava or plantain in between my newly planted tree crops?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Ani ebaanyɛ ehi tsei kɛ tsei ni adu etsɛko lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, during the first few years while tree crops are still small, growing food crops between them gives you quick food and income. Plantains especially provide helpful shade for young trees while they are establishing.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli beni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Niyenii ni ooodu yɛ tsei nɛɛ ateŋ lɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛ shika oya. Plantains haa tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, titri lɛ, be mli ni amɛto amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english: What causes my young crops to fall over after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni haa mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Crops fall over when their root systems are shallow or when heavy rain washes away the soft topsoil supporting the base of the plant. Heap up soil around the stem base (earthing up) to give the plant a firm anchor against strong winds.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ. Okɛ sũ abɔle tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ) koni eha tso lɛ aná ŋwɛi ŋta ni ma shi shiŋŋ ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why do seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in hard, unworked soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need loose, soft soil so their delicate young roots can easily push downward and absorb air and moisture. Hard, unworked soil acts like a wall that traps seeds, causing them to dry out or suffocate before they can emerge.
ga: Dumɔwui hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shi oya ni amɛŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuuu he nii lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo ni mɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbiɔ loo amɛmuɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How can I tell if my land soil has enough strength to support long-term tree crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ akwɛmɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Fertile land usually has dark, crumbly soil rich in decomposed leaves and soft earth. If soil is light, dry, or sandy, plants will grow slowly and turn yellow early unless you add organic manure or compost before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai ni egboi eyi mli obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse, egbi, loo ŋã yɔɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he dani odu.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my land is not suitable for the crop I am planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ esaaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: If soil is not suitable for a crop, the plants may show stunted growth, yellowing leaves, poor root development, or fail to produce good yield even when cared for properly.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ esaaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii Tsei lɛ baanyɛ ajie dalɛ ni egbɔjɔ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, shishifãi ni eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kpo. aloo enyɛŋ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ po

english: Why do my crops grow well in one part of my farm but fail in another section?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli shi amɛshwereɔ yɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil composition and drainage can vary across the same farm. Some crops dislike heavy or poorly drained soil, which can cause them to struggle or rot in certain areas.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli. Tsei komɛi sumɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nu shwieee nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbo yɛ hei komɛi.

english: Can heavy rain actually destroy my crops even if they grew very well during a drier season?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po?

english: Yes, many crops prefer moderate or low water conditions. Heavy rains can waterlog the soil, suffocate root systems, and rot plants that do not tolerate excessive moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei babaoo sumɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ loo nɔ ni baa shi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha nu akpa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. kɛ tsei ni egboi ni ŋmɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why did my crops produce a better harvest during the year with less rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpaɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certain crops thrive in drier conditions because their roots need air and are easily damaged by excess water. For these crops, lower rainfall prevents root rot and disease.
ga: Tsei komɛi yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni hulu enyɔ shi yɛ lɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia amɛshishifãi lɛ, ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. kɛha tsei nɛɛ Nugbɔ ni baa shi lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛ helai akafee nɔ ko.

english: How do I know if a crop I want to plant needs a lot of water or very little water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ni misumɔɔ ni makwɛ lɛ he miihia nu babaoo loo nu fioo ko pɛ?

english: Different crops have unique water requirements. Asking an extension officer or observing how the plant responds to wet weather helps you avoid planting water-sensitive crops during heavy rain seasons.
ga: Nu he hiamɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ahe. Bi mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ loo kwɛmɔ bɔ ni tsei lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ tsei ni nu sumɔɔ waa lɛ adumɔ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: What should I do on my farm when heavy rains leave too much standing water around my plants?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu babaoo ebɔle tsei lɛ ahe?

english: You should dig simple drainage channels to help water flow away from the farm, as standing water damages root systems for crops that cannot tolerate flooded conditions.
ga: Esa akɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ. Koni eye ebua nu ni ejɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Enɛ ji akɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ baafite tsei ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ nu afua shihilɛi anaa lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds or roots too deep into the ground?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui loo shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Planting too deep can prevent stems from reaching sunlight, suffocate roots, and cause plants to develop yellowing or sickness because the underground environment is too dense or wet.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ tso lɛ yitso lɛ naa koni hulu la akashɛ enɔ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. ni ehaa tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo hela mɔɔ amɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shihilɛ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ.

english: My crop leaves are turning pale and looking weak; what causes this crop 'fever'?
ga: Mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Mɛni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ ‘atridii’ baa?

english: Crop yellowing or 'fever' is usually a sign of stress caused by root suffocation, planting too deep, excess moisture in the soil, or unfavorable soil conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei amli ŋmɔlɔ loo ‘atridii’ ji haomɔ ni shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. dumɔ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ Fɛ̃i babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. loo shikpɔŋ shihilɛ ni ehiii

english: Is it safe to plant a new crop on land where I just uprooted an old, failed crop?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii heei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mijie ŋmɔshi nibii momoi ni efite lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: It depends on the crop. If the previous crop failed due to soil issues or disease, planting immediately without treating the soil or changing the crop type can cause the new plants to fail as well.
ga: Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ he naagbai loo hela hewɔ Dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni asaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo atsakeee tso henɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha tsei heei ŋmɔ.

english: If heavy rain ruins my crops mid-season, should I leave the field and wait for next season?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fite miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ Ani esa akɛ mashi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mamɛ kɛyashi be kroko?

english: If a crop is completely ruined by water, it is best to clear the dead plants to prevent pest and disease buildup, let the soil dry out, and plan for a crop better suited for the next weather condition.
ga: Kɛji nu fite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwraa Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie tsei ni egboi lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai akabua amɛhe naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. ni ato gbɛjianɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to sunlight so they can make food efficiently. Sunlight gives the plant the energy it needs to send nutrients down into the soil to grow big, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Hulu la haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt during the hot afternoon even when I water them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In the hot sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Watering deeply in the early morning and placing dry grass around the base of the plant (mulching) keeps the root area cool and retains water.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli waa leebi ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi fɔ̃ɔ shishigbɛ (mulch) lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi.

english: How do I know if my cassava stem cuttings are actually growing underground after I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi diɛŋtsɛ? Beni midu sɛɛ?

english: Within two to three weeks after planting stem cuttings, you will see fresh green shoots breaking through the soil surface. This tells you that roots have successfully formed underneath to draw nutrients and anchor the plant.
ga: Yɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ mli beni adu tsei lɛ Obaana tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni miifo kɛmiitsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ bo akɛ shishifãi ebɔi shishigbɛ koni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛha tso lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key plant food needed for healthy green growth. It can also happen when soil stays too waterlogged, so applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea on moist soil will help it recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea wo shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ afee fɛo.

english: Does planting cowpea or groundnuts really improve the soil for my next crop of maize?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpea and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants rot after harvest, they leave natural fertilizer in the ground that feeds the next crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Tsei shiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni haa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaf surface. Spraying with neem oil solution or recommended organic pesticides helps eliminate these insects so new leaves grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ ohe. koni baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ waa

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a shortage of calcium inside the growing fruit, which usually happens when soil moisture goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping soil moisture consistent prevents the fruit bottoms from turning black.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛtee nɔ ni mli edɔ waa nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsi aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔii ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or damage from insects like mirids (akate). Providing adequate shade trees and protecting the farm from insects helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids (akata) lɛ fiteɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo ni sa ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cabbage seedlings fall over and die suddenly a few days after transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden dying is usually 'damping-off' caused by soil fungus in overly wet soil, or shock from hot direct sunlight. Transplanting late in the afternoon and avoiding overwatering protects fragile young stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ trukaa gbele nɛɛ ji ‘damping’ ni sũ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ ni mli efɔ fe nine lɛ kɛbaa. loo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he gbeyeishemɔ Kɛ́ atsake tsei lɛ yɛ shwane mli ni ajie nu fe nine kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How long does a new plantain sucker take from planting until the bunch is ready to harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani dumɔwui heei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: A plantain sucker typically takes between 12 to 15 months to mature and yield a harvestable bunch, depending on soil fertility and rainfall. Removing extra shoots around the main plant gives it maximum energy to fruit faster.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ heɔ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 dani amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa. Edamɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ fɛo ha kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ nɔ. Nibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ he lɛ baaha hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwo yibii oya.

english: If I plant other crops together with my cocoa trees, won't those extra plants steal all the food from the soil and weaken my cocoa?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ kookoo tso lɛ du tsei krokomɛi lɛ, Ani nakai tsei krokomɛi lɛ ejuŋ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni eha mikookoo lɛ agbɔjɔ?

english: Not all plants steal food from cocoa. Certain crops and trees can live peacefully alongside cocoa without draining its strength or reducing your harvest, as long as they do not directly block all its sunlight or overcrowd its roots.
ga: Jeee tsei fɛɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kookoo mli. Nibii ni aduɔ kɛ tsei komɛi baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ toiŋjɔlɛ mli yɛ kookoo masɛi ni amɛhewalɛ baaa shi loo amɛbaaa yibiiwoo nɔ. Shii abɔ ni amɛtsiii hulu la naa tɛ̃ɛ loo amɛhaaa amɛshishifãi lɛ ayi obɔ lɛ,

english: Is it bad for my cocoa trees if I leave some naturally growing wild plants mixed in on the farmland?
ga: Ani nɔ ko ni ehiii baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ ni akɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Leaving selected non-aggressive plants mixed in with cocoa does not drain the soil's strength. Some naturally occurring plants actually keep the land cool, hold soil moisture, and protect the cocoa trees.
ga: Tsei ni ahala ni bɛ basabasa ni akɛfutuɔ kookoo mli lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ aba shi. Tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo tso lɛ he

english: How can I tell if a neighboring crop is taking away the soil's strength from my main crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ miihe shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ amli?

english: If your main crop turns pale yellow, develops thin stems, or grows very slowly while the neighbor crop thrives wildly, they are competing for soil strength and nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso titri lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, eyɛ ŋmeii bibii, loo edaa blɛoo waa yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ daraa oya. Amɛmiitswa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava or plantain together with my cocoa without harming the cocoa's growth?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kookoo adu ŋmei loo plantain ni mifiteee kookoo lɛ dalɛ?

english: Yes, planting food crops alongside cocoa is fine and can even protect young cocoa from harsh heat, provided you space them properly so they do not compete heavily for root space.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ hi, ni ebaanyɛ ebu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Esa akɛ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni amɛkatswa akaŋ koni amɛná shishifãi babaoo.

english: How do I know which plants are safe to leave growing near my cocoa roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni esa akɛ adu yɛ mi-kokoo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Safe plants generally have shallow roots or different nutrient needs than cocoa. They feed on different layers of the soil, meaning they will not take away the food your cocoa trees need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo amɛyɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa fe kookoo. Amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ fãi babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛheŋ niyenii ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei lɛ.

english: Does growing multiple types of plants in one field make the land tired faster than growing just one crop?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii kome ni aduɔ?

english: No, mixing the right crops can actually keep the land healthy. Different plants feed differently and return useful organic matter back into the earth, preventing the land from losing its strength.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha he ko ahi shi jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. Tsei srɔtoi yeɔ niyenii srɔtoi ni amɛkɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akafite hewalɛ

english: I have a large piece of land, but I can only plant a small portion this season. Will the unplanted land lose its richness if left alone?
ga: Miyɛ shikpɔŋ agbo ko. Shi midu fã bibioo ko pɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli. Ani shikpɔŋ ni aduko nɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ baafite nibii ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Leaving part of a large farm unplanted will not ruin the soil. Resting land allows natural foliage to grow and restore nutrients, making the ground rich and ready for future planting.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔ agbo ko fã ko ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ, eyeŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ awui. He ni ajieɔ hejɔɔmɔ yɛ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii, ni efee klalo kɛha nidumɔ nii wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do some trees on the farm seem to grow fine alongside crops while others cause nearby plants to wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Some trees have aggressive root systems and heavy leaf cover that starve nearby crops of sunlight and water, while friendly tree species share soil peacefully without draining crop strength.
ga: Tsei komɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛ baai ni mli wa ni haaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anaaa hulu la kɛ nu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo lɛ baajara shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ toiŋjɔlɛ mli ni amɛfiteee tso lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Is it normal for a cocoa farm to produce a good harvest even if it isn't cleared completely bare?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ ajieee amɛ po?

english: Yes, cocoa naturally thrives in forest-like conditions. Having a controlled mix of shade trees and mixed vegetation keeps the environment humid and balanced without hurting farm production.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni tamɔ koo mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ tsei ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni akudɔ amɛ lɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni enaaa ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do wild plants grow back so fast on my farmland even after I clear the land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei miida oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ moŋ.

english: Wild plants are naturally adapted to the local soil and quickly grab water and sunshine. Managing them early keeps them from growing out of control and competing with your crops.
ga: Koo mli tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eŋɔ nu kɛ hulu la oya nɔkwɛmɔ kɛjɛ egbekɛbiiashi Enɛ baaha amɛnyɛŋ amɛye nɔ ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabɔ akaŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or adding well-decomposed animal manure gives the plants the strength to green up and grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK tsu nii loo akɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni fiteɔ waa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop produce huge leafy branches above ground but tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ niji wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves instead of roots. Using balanced organic compost or potassium-rich fertilizer encourages the plant to direct its food down into expanding the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ faaa lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni eye nii koni ekwɛ̃ bulbs.

english: What will happen if I plant my cassava sticks too close to each other on the ridges?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ yɛ ŋmei ko nɔ?

english: Planting cassava too close forces the roots to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to spread its roots and produce thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa ni efeɔ bulbs ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: How do I know if my soil is loose enough to plant root crops like yam?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmeii?

english: Root crops like yam need soft, deep soil so the tubers can expand easily without bending or stopping growth. If you push a stick into the mound and it goes down smoothly without hitting hard clay or rocks, the soil is well-prepared for healthy yam growth.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi, tamɔ sweet potatoes lɛ, he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛkuuu amɛhe loo amɛkpaaa amɛdalɛ. Kɛji otsi tso nine lɛ kɛtee gɔŋ lɛ mli ni eya shi mlɛo ni etswaaa shikpɔŋ loo tɛi lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha sweet potato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers during the hottest weeks of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air put stress on tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to save energy and water. Mulching the base of the plant with dry grass and watering consistently in the early morning helps keep the soil cool so flowers can set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi ni awo nɔ nu daa leebi maŋkpa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and drying at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling happens when the plant loses water faster than its roots can pull from the soil during dry spells, or when tiny pests like thrips suck sap from the leaves. Checking under the leaves for pests and keeping the soil moist helps leaves stay flat and healthy.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Aloo beni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ mli, ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that thrives in cool, overly shaded, and wet conditions. Pruning tall shade tree branches and clearing weeds allows air and sunlight to dry the farm, stopping the fungus from destroying the pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Shade babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ ni edɔ. Niji ni kɛlɛ ni afoɔ Shade ni akɛhaa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni ekpaa ŋmeii lɛ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ

english: What is making big, round holes in the leaves of my cabbage crops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bulɛi wuji ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars feeding on the crop at night. Spraying the leaves early with neem seed extract solution acts as a natural repellent that stops caterpillars from eating your leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu lɛ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ mra. Ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni tsiɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye obaai lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting after just a few weeks in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ ni mikɛhi mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they get cut or bruised during harvest, or if stored in hot places without air circulation. Gentle handling during harvest and storing yams in a well-ventilated, shaded barn keeps them fresh for months.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ Okɛtsu nii blɛoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli ni okɛ sweet potato ato ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do small insects ruin my harvested maize grains after I seal them in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ beni mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize grains often hold small weevil eggs or moisture if bagged before drying completely in the sun. Drying maize thoroughly until the grains are hard, and using airtight storage bags, suffocates pests and prevents insect damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmeii hiɛ ŋmeii bibii bibii. Aloo ŋmɔtɔ baaba kɛji akɛ awo kotoku lɛ mli dani egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Abɛi ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli baafee shiŋŋ ni akɛ vacuum storage bag atsu nii Ebaaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop is running out of nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to build green leaves, so when soil nutrients run low, the plant moves what little it has left to its newest top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa hee fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying early with neem oil or targeted insecticide helps protect the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing heart of young maize plants. Detecting them early and applying recommended controls before the plant flowers prevents major crop loss.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ atsui lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni oooyɔse amɛ mra Ni okɛ nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔ amɛ lɛ atsu nii dani amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a field with direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains nearby gives young cocoa plants the gentle shade and humidity they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli jɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to place tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight. Staking gets the leaves off the hot ground where diseases spread, allowing the leaves to collect maximum sunlight and manufacture food to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Staking baajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni edɔ yɛ ni hela lɛ egbɛ eshwa lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain causes water to sit around roots, cutting off oxygen and allowing rot-causing soil organisms to attack the cassava tubers. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets heavy rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu feɔ ekome kɛbɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ mli, ni ehaa sũ mli nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the hot afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: On very hot afternoons, water evaporates from leaves faster than roots can drink it from the soil. Spreading dry grass mulch around the base of your plants keeps soil cool and retains moisture longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Tsei ashishi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans on my field help my maize grow better next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans work with beneficial soil microbes to pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the bean roots decay, they leave behind rich natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans Ekɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbo Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛha onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before turning into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings sharply between very dry and very wet. Keeping soil consistently moist helps flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya yɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ waa teŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra small shoots growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantain baai lɛ ahe

english: Too many shoots around one plantain tree compete for water, sunlight, and plant food. Pruning extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, allowing the parent tree to produce a much bigger, heavier bunch.
ga: Tsoi bibii babaoo ni bɔle dumɔwu kome he lɛ kɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ tso niyenii he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afo tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ aba ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ awo niji ni dara ni tsii kwraa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, strong sunlight because their leaves lose water faster than their small roots can absorb it. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava to protect them until they mature.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Akɛni baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. Koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ

english: How long does it usually take after planting cassava before I can harvest the tubers?
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani anyɛɔ akpaa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Most standard cassava varieties in Ghana take between 9 to 12 months to mature, though some improved fast-growing varieties can be ready for harvesting in 6 to 8 months.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛdaraa, eyɛ mli akɛ cassava henɔi komɛi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 mli moŋ.

english: How can I tell that my yams are fully mature and ready to be dug up from the mound?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei ko ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa kɛjɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines start turning yellow and drying up naturally at the end of the rainy season, showing that the plant has stopped growing and stored all its energy in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is essential for plant growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or urea can help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my farm if I plant cassava on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Cassava takes a lot of nutrients out of the ground. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil completely, leading to smaller harvests and a buildup of soil-borne diseases over time.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without producing any actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to extreme heat stress, insufficient water, or insect pests attacking the blossoms. Ensuring regular watering and controlling pests helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: What causes tiny holes in the leaves of my cabbage plants and how does it hurt the crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-cabbage lɛ baai lɛ anɔ Ni te eyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are caused by caterpillars or beetles feeding on them. This damages the plant's ability to absorb light and make food, preventing the cabbage from forming a solid, full head.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ kaabeji baai amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛmɔɔ la ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, kaabe lɛ mli waŋ kwraa.

english: How do I know when it is safe to start planting my maize during the major rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: You should plant your maize right after the first two or three heavy rains have thoroughly soaked the soil, ensuring there is steady moisture for the seeds to germinate without drying out.
ga: Esa akɛ odu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do weeds harm my pepper plants even after the pepper plants have grown tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitutua mi-pepper tso lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ekwɛ momo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential food, water, and sunlight directly from the soil that your pepper plants need. Even tall plants will produce fewer and smaller peppers if weeds are competing with them.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni o-pepper tsei lɛ taoɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ po woɔ ŋmeii fioo ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛji jwɛi kɛ amɛ miitswa akaŋ.

english: Why do my newly transplanted plantain suckers take a long time to sprout fresh leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-banana tso ni midu ehee lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ baai heei lɛ?

english: If plantain suckers are planted too deep, or if the roots were damaged without trimming the old leaves, the plant spends extra energy recovering its roots before it can push out new growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ efite ni afooo baai momo lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ kroko baatsu nii ni ekɛku esɛɛ eshishifãi lɛ dani dalɛ hee abaje shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural shade, protecting young cocoa plants and keeping the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad to burn my field after clearing bushes and weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mashã miŋmɔ lɛ beni ajie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and kills beneficial organisms in the soil, leaving the earth dry, weak, and less capable of holding nutrients for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ ahiɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ato kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and bent inside the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni amɛbɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam roots need soft, loose soil to expand easily. If planted in hard or rocky soil without raised mounds, the growing tubers get crushed and distorted as they struggle to push through the dirt.
ga: Sweet potato shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛsaa nɔ ni gɔŋji bɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni miida lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I leave distance between my maize seeds instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abɛi dumɔwui lɛ abɔ he moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small, poor cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni ŋmeii lɛ hu yɛ bibii.

english: Why does my cassava crop take longer to mature when planted on weak soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stores extra energy to build heavy root tubers. If the soil lacks nutrients, the plant uses its limited energy just to stay alive, delaying tuber growth.
ga: Cassava kɛ hewalɛ kroko toɔ koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni tsii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ. Yitso dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and curl up in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow, curled cassava leaves are often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or green mites, which thrive in dry conditions and spread leaf viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo green mites ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa ebaai lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if caterpillars or armyworms are destroying my maize leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii loo asraafoi amli ŋmeii miifite mi-abele baai lɛ?

english: Armyworms leave rough, jagged holes on leaves and drop powdery, sawdust-like waste inside the center shoot of the maize plant, unlike normal leaves chewed smoothly along the edges.
ga: Cutworms lɛ shĩɔ bu ni mli edɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ baai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ashɛreɔ blɛoo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a heat surge and dry weeks before main rains start. Planting too early can dry out and kill new seedlings before regular rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ kɛ hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ otsii babaoo dani nugbɔ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering, as the plant sacrifices flower production to save water and protect itself from stress.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei kɛ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeɔ lɛ ashã afɔle koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔ he.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop in the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon sun, pepper leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can absorb it. Drooping is a temporary defense mechanism to reduce sun exposure until the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Drooping ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he yɛ be kukuoo mli koni hulu la ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at a slant instead of burying them flat in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a 45-degree angle encourages roots to grow downward and spread evenly, resulting in larger tubers that are much easier to dig up during harvest.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ 45 degree angle mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shi ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni eyɛ mlɛo kwraa akɛ abaakumɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Yam plants need direct sunlight on their leaves to generate food, which is then stored underground to form big tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light and preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee bulb agboi. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛwo la mli ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep dropping off the tree without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack proper soil nutrients, or lack tiny pollinating insects in the soil. Maintaining shade and moist soil helps flowers develop into full pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ baa ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a vital soil nutrient. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen away from root systems, requiring additional fertilizer or compost to restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he koni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before they even get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo dani eshɛ po lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom end rot, which happens when the tomato plant cannot absorb enough calcium. Irregular watering or dry soil prevents the roots from taking up calcium from the ground.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the center leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni muji tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ateŋ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf funnel of maize plants and eats the young leaf tissue before it expands.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baa bibii lɛ amli fãji dani amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ.

english: How do I know if the very first rain of the season is enough for me to start sowing my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Sowing after just one rain can ruin seeds if a dry spell follows. You should check if the soil stays moist at a depth equal to the length of your finger for a couple of days before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui lɛ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛyashɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ onine lɛ kɛlɛ yeɔ egbɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani odu.

english: Why shouldn't I apply all my chemical fertilizer on the farm on the exact same day I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbi kome nɔ ni aduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds and young sprouts do not have developed root systems to absorb heavy nutrients yet. Applying all fertilizer at once can burn young plants or get washed away by rain before the crop can use it.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ tsei bibii lɛ enáko shishifãi ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsii lɛ lolo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli shikome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei bibii lɛ ashã loo nugbɔ atsɔ amɛnɔ dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why does spreading dry bush grass or leaves around the base of my crops help them stay alive in dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, known as mulching, blocks direct sunlight from hitting the soil. This keeps the root zone cool and prevents moisture from evaporating rapidly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la lɛ akatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why is it so difficult to get a high yield when I grow rice on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ maná yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice requires very precise conditions to thrive. Without proper water control, timely fertilizing, and good field preparation, the plant cannot produce its full potential of grain heads.
ga: Shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. Kɛji nu he gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa bɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ saamɔ kpakpa Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui ayitsei kɛyashɛ he ni ebaanyɛ eshɛ.

english: What causes some of my rice plants to produce empty grains with no rice inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni ŋmãa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty grains usually happen when the plant suffers from lack of water or insect attacks during its flowering stage, preventing the grain from filling up properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo kooloi bibii tutua amɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ ayi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young crop leaves turn yellow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the crop is starving for nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe and absorb food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ nitrogen, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu ni amɛhe niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why does rice need so much flooded water compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in wet soil, and keeping water on the field helps regulate soil temperature while naturally drowning out competing weeds.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Ni nu ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does leveling my farmland help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔ lɛ ni mikɛbaafee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Level ground ensures that water and fertilizer spread evenly to every single plant, so no part of your farm dries out while another part gets flooded.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jaa tsei lɛ fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔ lɛ fã ko bɛ ni egbi yɛ be mli ni nu eyi fã kroko nɔ.

english: How do I know if my piece of land is suitable for growing rice?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Land that is good for rice retains water well, such as clay-rich soil found in low-lying valley areas that do not dry out quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni anaa yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ. ni gĩii oya lɛ

english: Why is weed control more critical when growing rice than with other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ he hiaa waa yɛ ŋmãa mli fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Rice seedlings grow slowly at first and easily get choked out by fast-growing weeds that steal sunlight, water, and nutrients needed for a good harvest.
ga: Omɔ dumɔwui daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ haa amɛhe oya. Enɛ juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha kpamɔ kpakpa.

english: Why should I spend money on certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika yɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahe? Mohu ɔ, nyɛ heɔ wuhi nɛ a je nyagbe ní kpami be ɔ mi ɔ yi wami.

english: Certified seeds are specially selected to sprout reliably, resist diseases, and produce higher yields, whereas saved seeds lose their strength over generations.
ga: Ahala dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli.

english: Is there a strong market demand if I decide to start farming rice in Ghana?
ga: Kɛji mikpɛ miyiŋ akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ Ghana. Ani jarayeli nibii babaoo baaba?

english: Yes, rice is a daily staple in almost every Ghanaian household, meaning local demand is high and growing every year.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, omɔ ji daa gbi niyenii yɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ Ghana shia fɛɛ shia mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, nibii ni ataoɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ fa babaoo ni eyaa hiɛ daa afi.

english: What main resources do I need to clear and prepare before I start commercial rice farming?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafo mli dani mabɔi jarayeli okwaayeli?

english: Beyond having suitable land, you need investment for field bunding, quality seeds, fertilizers, weed control, and dedicated labor for planting and harvesting.
ga: Kɛfata shikpɔŋ ni sa ni oyɔɔ lɛ he lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ shika awo mli lolo kɛha shikpɔji ni akɛaafee ekome lɛ. Dumɔwui ni hi, ŋmɔshi nibii, jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ. kɛ nitsumɔ ni akɛhaa dumɔwui kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ

english: Why am I finding small holes in my young maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hidden inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee ŋmãa lɛ shishi lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that feeds on young maize leaves and growing points. Detecting them early allows you to treat the crop with recommended pesticides or neem extracts before they destroy the whole yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. mra mli ni anaa Ehaa okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsuɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe nii dani okpãtãa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Why are the green leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing bright yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kpɛɔ lɛ?

english: Your cassava plants likely have Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. This disease prevents the plant from growing large tubers, so removing infected plants and using disease-resistant cassava stems for planting next season is best.
ga: Ekolɛ o-yucca tso lɛ yɛ yucca mosaic hela. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei akwɛ bulbs wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akɛ ŋmeii ni hela nyɛɔ emɔ amɛ lɛ atsu nii kɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves in a V-shape indicate that your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea around the plants will help them regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii yɛ Tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli su lɛ mli ni eda waa.

english: Why should I stop burning the bush on my land before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Burning kills useful organisms in the soil and destroys organic matter that holds moisture. Clearing without burning leaves organic materials to decay naturally, making the soil richer and more fertile for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ toɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ashãaa lɛ, ebaaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ afite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmeii lɛ agbe naa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Rotating them with heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores soil fertility without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni akɛduɔ nibii ni ji kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa protects them from sun scorch and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot, when there is irregular watering, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Ensuring consistent moisture and avoiding excessive leaf-growing fertilizers during flowering helps fruits form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Be mli ni nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be fɛɛ be, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai aba.

english: Why do I need to put up tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high enough to capture maximum sunlight for making food. The more sunlight the leaves get, the larger and healthier the yam tubers beneath the ground will grow.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato lɛ baai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha nihoomɔ. Babaoo ni hulu la kpɛɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, Babaoo ni shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato tubers lɛ baafee wuji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot suckers growing around my main plantain stool?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Plantain sɛi wulu lɛ je kpo.

english: Too many suckers compete directly with the main plant for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Removing extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong ones ensures the main plant produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ahi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.
