english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning instead of during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning gives the plant roots time to absorb moisture before heat builds up. Watering under hot afternoon sun causes most of the water to evaporate quickly and can heat up wet leaves, causing stress to the crop.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛjieɔ nu dani latsaa lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ oya ni ehaa baai ni efɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I keep replanting seeds saved from my previous year's yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui heei, ni mikɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ toɔ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds gradually lose their vigor over multiple generations and can carry hidden diseases from previous seasons. Using certified fresh seeds ensures uniform growth, stronger disease resistance, and maximum yield potential.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ baalaaje fiofio. Ehewalɛ fite yɛ yinɔi babaoo mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ bei ni eho lɛ amli lɛ aba. Dumɔwui heei, ni ana he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ naa dalɛ daa. Helai ahewalɛ ni mli wa kɛ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ ahewalɛ ni fe fɛɛ

english: Are old traditional seed varieties always better to plant than the new hybrid seeds?
ga: Ani kusum mli dumɔwui momoi lɛ hi fe dumɔwui heei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ adumɔ be fɛɛ be?

english: Traditional seeds are well-adapted to local conditions, but improved hybrid seeds are specifically bred to mature faster, withstand modern pest pressures, and yield significantly more food on smaller land areas.
ga: Kusum dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛshwere oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. ni amɛfeɔ niyenii babaoo kwraa yɛ he ko bibioo.

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale yellow and stop growing even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate that your crops are starving for essential soil nutrients, particularly nitrogen. Rain supplies water, but plants also need fertile soil or added organic manure and fertilizer to grow green and strong.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. titri lɛ nitrogen Nugbɔ ji nu jɛɛhe. Shi tsei hu he miihia shikpɔŋ ni baa nii loo humus kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth. Rotating with crops like beans or peanuts restores soil fertility and breaks insect life cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ je lɛŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ kooloi ashihilɛ.

english: What main factors affect whether my crops give a full harvest or completely fail?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii titrii ni saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛji eshɛɔ ŋmaa ni yeɔ emuu loo eshɛɛɛ he kwraa?

english: Crop success relies on five major factors: healthy seed selection, nutrient-rich soil, reliable moisture, adequate sunlight, and protection from pests or diseases. A failure in any one of these causes total crop yield to drop.
ga: Nibii titri enumɔ ni baahã ŋmɔshi nibii aye omanye: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ahalaa. shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ Kɛji enɛɛmɛi ateŋ eko nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick green leaves but produce small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai eŋɔlii ni mli tse, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages plants to focus energy on growing top leaves and stems rather than developing roots. Balancing the soil with phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to store energy in big tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ ama baai kɛ ŋwɛi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium to shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ bulb agboi amli.

english: Why did my young crops wither and burn shortly after I applied chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo mli lɛ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer or placing it directly against crop stems causes chemical burn by pulling moisture out of the roots. Fertilizer must be applied in correct small amounts at a safe distance from the stem in moist soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ shishi loo okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ashã tso lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni sa lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms before forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Blossom drop happens when crops experience severe stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or sap-sucking insects. Mulching to retain soil moisture and providing protection against pests helps flowers develop into fruit.
ga: Blossom drop baa kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ miigba tsei anaa waa. Mulching ni akɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings drying up and dying during their first dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow root systems and delicate leaves that burn under full sun and hot harmattan winds. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides shelter and retains soil moisture during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu ni naa wa kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa mɔ náa wɔɔhe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: How do I decide the best time to sow seeds when the rains are unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ he?

english: Rather than relying strictly on traditional calendar dates, wait until the soil receives consecutive days of deep rainfall so seeds have sustained moisture to germinate and establish strong root systems.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ kusum kalanda gbii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛma shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields after I farm on the same piece of land for two or three consecutive years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni mikɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ etsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the soil every season to grow. If you plant on the same soil repeatedly without giving it a break or feeding it, the soil becomes exhausted, causing your harvest to shrink over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ Ni okɛ nɔ ko akawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo okɛ niyenii haaa lɛ, egbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why did our grandfathers used to abandon their farmland after a few years and move to a new forest plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔtsɛkwɛ̃ lɛ shi eŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ ni efã kɛtee koo hee ko mli lɛ?

english: Our elders practiced shifting cultivation because leaving land unfarmed—or fallow—allows trees and wild plants to grow back. Over time, decaying leaves naturally refill the soil with nutrients so it can support healthy crops again.
ga: Wɔ onukpai lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ—loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ—ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ koo mli tsei kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, baai ni fiteɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni enyɛ ekwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ

english: How long does a tired piece of land need to rest before the soil becomes fertile again?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ lɛ jɔɔ ehe dani ebafeɔ nɔ ni baa nii ekoŋŋ?

english: Naturally, land usually needs at least 3 to 5 years of rest for trees and bush plants to regenerate the soil, though adding compost or planting special leguminous plants can speed up this process.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, ehe baahia ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe afii 3 kɛyashi 5 koni tsei kɛ tsei bibii anyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ehee. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he loo ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya oya moŋ, shi.

english: Is it possible for me to keep farming on the same plot every year without moving to a new location?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ matsu ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he nii daa afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo he ko hee?

english: Yes, you can farm the same land continuously if you care for the soil by adding organic manure, using commercial fertilizers, rotating your crops, and leaving crop remains to decay back into the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oya nɔ otsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ kɛji okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii ni oha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do crops grow so much stronger on freshly cleared forest land than on land that has been farmed recently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ waa yɛ koo mli shikpɔŋ ni agbele ehee lɛ nɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Forest land has accumulated years of fallen leaves, dead roots, and natural compost, creating rich topsoil packed with natural plant food that gives new crops a massive boost.
ga: Kooi amli hei ebua baai ni egbee shi lɛ anaa. shishifãi ni egboi kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii afii babaoo Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: What can I do to keep my land fertile so our community can remain a major food producer?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii bɔni afee ni wɔ akutso lɛ aya nɔ afee niyenii babaoo?

english: To maintain high food production, you should protect topsoil from rain washing it away, rotate feeding crops like maize with soil-building crops like beans, and consistently feed the soil with compost or manure.
ga: koni niyenii ni anáa lɛ ahi shi babaoo Esa akɛ obu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii kɛ tsei ni maa shikpɔŋ tamɔ ŋmãa. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ daa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize turn yellow and stay small when planted on an old field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ bibii kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves and stunted growth are signs that the soil has run out of vital nutrients like nitrogen. Old fields often lack nitrogen because previous crops have used it all up.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni egbɔ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu tsutsu lɛ efite.

english: Why do weeds seem to take over my farm much faster in the third year of planting than in the first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ oya kwraa yɛ afi ni ji etɛ ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ mli fe klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: As soil loses its nutrients, your planted crops grow weaker and cannot fight for space. Tough wild weeds that tolerate poor soil take advantage of this weakness and quickly overcrowd your field.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fite lɛ Tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye he ko he akaŋ. Koo mli jwɛi ni wa ni kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ naa lɛ baaŋɔ bɔjɔmɔ nɛɛ he sɛɛ ni amɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ eyi oya.

english: Can planting groundnuts or cowpeas help fix soil that has grown weak from growing cassava or maize?
ga: Ani ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni asaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei loo ŋmei dumɔ egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, plants in the bean and pea family are special because they trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil for other crops planted after them.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ji nɔ ko krɛdɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa tsei krokomɛi ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Does burning the bush on my land before planting help or hurt the soil in the long run?
ga: Ani tsei bibii ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ awui yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Burning provides a quick layer of ash that feeds crops for one season, but it destroys natural organic matter and beneficial soil organisms, causing the soil to lose its fertility much faster in the years that follow.
ga: Shãa oya lɛ haa sũ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ hewalɛ kɛyashiɔ be ko mli lɛ baa. Shi efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya kwraa yɛ afii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape pattern, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older lower leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the rains to set in properly before planting my maize seeds instead of planting after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui moŋ fe klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain only wet the surface soil. If you plant immediately, the seeds will sprout, but a hot dry spell usually follows, which will dry up the young roots and kill the seedlings before the main rains arrive.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nuɔ pɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ he okadii baa. Enɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛfite dumɔwui lɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa aba.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Beni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ enáa hulu la lɛ fɛɛ lɛ,.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers but only a few of them turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi fioo pɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni etsɔɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop flowers that are not visited by tiny pollinating insects. Rainstorms or extreme heat can also cause unpollinated flowers to drop off so the tree can save its energy for the pods that successfully set.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ loo latsaa ni naa wa baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollen lɛ agbo. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ anyɛ ato hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli lɛ.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees easily fall over when the fruit bunch becomes heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akutsei lɛ amli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots like oak trees; they have shallow roots near the soil surface. As the bunch grows heavy, it pulls the plant's center of gravity forward, causing the shallow roots to snap or slip out of the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ odum tsei. Eyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji kuu lɛ da Egbala tso lɛ teŋgbɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛyaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ fãa loo amɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is heavy rainfall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain fills all the empty air spaces in the soil for days, the roots suffocate from lack of oxygen and decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ kɛ fitemɔ hewɔ.

english: Why do I need to lift and stake the vines of my yam plants off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mi-sweet potato tso lɛ wain tsei lɛ anɔ ni mikɛ amɛ abɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the light and prevents soil-borne diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ la ni mli tse mli, ni ehaaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akatutua baai lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl upwards during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon is a natural defense mechanism. The tomato plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sun, helping it trap moisture and avoid losing too much water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants drop off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience temperature stress from extreme heat or when the plant does not get enough water. Shedding flowers prevents the plant from exhausting itself when conditions are poor.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be mli loo kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Fɔfɔi ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekagbɔjɔ kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ ehiii kwraa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans together with my main crops help the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful bacteria in the soil to catch nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots, acting like a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ amɛwo shishifãi lɛ amli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: How many years can an oil palm tree continue to give me good palm nuts after planting?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu mu tso ko lɛ, ebaanyɛ eya nɔ ewo ŋmei yibii kpakpai?

english: Oil palm trees have a very long productive lifespan, usually yielding good harvests for 25 to 30 years before their output slows down and they grow too tall for easy harvesting.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ hiɛ wala be kakadaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii. Bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai afii 25 kɛyashi 30 dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛfeɔ shwiili tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akpa amɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do the palm nut bunches on my older trees become smaller over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso momo lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee bibii yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ?

english: As palm trees grow very tall over many years, nutrients take longer to travel up the trunk, and the soil loses minerals, which causes the fruit bunches to shrink unless fertilizer is added.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tɛŋ tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ waa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani eyaa tso lɛ nɔ. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ minerals Enɛ haa aduawai akuu lɛ shwieɔ shi ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field with no trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are fragile and burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops next to them creates a protective shield against intense heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa nɔ ko tsiɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava on the same land where I just planted young tree crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tso ko, tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu tso bibioo ko nɔ amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting food crops alongside young tree crops helps maximize your land use and provides food while the main trees grow, as long as the food crops do not block sunlight from the young trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooodu yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii babaoo. ni ekɛ niyenii aha be mli ni tso titri lɛ miida Be fɛɛ be ni niyenii tsei lɛ tsiii hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: How do I know the best time to dig up my cassava tubers from the ground?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie ŋmei shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava roots are usually ready to dig up between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping, showing that energy has moved into the underground roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afeɔ klalo akɛ abaakumɔ ŋmei shishifãi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hewalɛ efã kɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and short instead of deep and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni yɔɔ kuku yɛ nɔ ni mli kwɔ ni kɛlɛ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Tubers need loose soil to expand downward easily. If the ground is hard or not dug deep enough when making mounds, the roots cannot push through and will stay small and shallow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse he miihia bulb lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa kɛya shi oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo otsako shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ ofee gɔŋ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli ni amɛfee bibii ni mli ekɔɔɔ.

english: Why does my farmland yield less food now compared to when I first cleared the land years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe beni mijie mli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa afii ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Plants pull food out of the dirt every season. Digging up crops continuously for many years empties the natural nutrients from the soil unless you add manure, compost, or rest the land.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Tsei ni atsaa yɛ afii babaoo mli be fɛɛ be lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo sũ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ fata he.

english: Why does the soil around my farm become so hard that water just runs off the surface?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ mli wa waa akɛ nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Direct heavy rain and hot sun bake bare soil into a hard crust. Adding organic material like dead leaves or crop waste keeps the soil soft and helps water soak down to the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ fata he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa nu boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do the fruit bunches on my oil palm trees drop off before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-mu tsei lɛ anɔ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Palm nuts drop early when the tree suffers from severe water stress during dry spells or lacks key nutrients like potassium needed to hold heavy fruit.
ga: Palm ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ ni naa wa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo ebɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ potassium ni he hiaa koni ekɛhiɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily during strong rains and winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the surface. When the heavy soil becomes soaked with water, the roots lose their grip, especially if the plant is carrying heavy fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ amɛhe. Titri lɛ kɛji tso lɛ woɔ yibii ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow big. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: What is making small holes in my maize leaves with tiny dark droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-abɛi lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii lɛ miifee? Ni ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the growing center of maize plants and eat the young leaves unless controlled early with recommended insecticides or neem extracts.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. ja akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ akudɔ lɛ mra.

english: Why do my maize cobs stay small and incomplete even though I planted on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo ni amɛyeee emuu eyɛ mli akɛ adu amɛ yɛ be naa moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize cobs fail to fill up completely if the crop lacks water or nutrients during the flowering and silking stage, which prevents all the grain seeds from pollinating properly.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ aha ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ awo mli kwraa kɛji akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ siliki shweremɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings dying when the hot dry season comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, strong sunlight because their leaves burn and dry out quickly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them keeps the plants shaded and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall down when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily if tiny underground pests like nematodes or plantain root weevils eat away their roots, weakening the tree's support in the soil.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo plantain weevils ye amɛshishifãi lɛ. Ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ asɛɛfimɔ baa shi.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to turn soft and rot underground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa?

english: Cassava roots rot underground mainly when heavy rainfall pools in soil that does not drain well, or when root-rot diseases attack the plant in waterlogged fields.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo beni shishifãi ni egbo lɛ tutuaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why are my yam vines drying up and turning black long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ediŋŋ be saŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: This blackening is usually caused by a fungal leaf disease called anthracnose, which spreads fast during wet periods and kills the foliage before tubers can mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ diŋ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni egbeɔ baai lɛ dani bulb lɛ daa kwraa.

english: Tomatoes shed flowers when temperatures are too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is insufficient breeze or insects to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up into small cups and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? Ni akpa tso lɛ dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids transmitting leaf curl virus while feeding on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni gbɛɔ leaf curl hela lɛ amɛshwãa be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland needs manure before I plant my next crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu miŋmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If your previous harvest gave lower yields, or if weeds and past crops showed pale yellow leaves and stunted stems, it indicates the soil nutrients are low and need manure or compost.
ga: Kɛji okpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ wo yibii ni baa shi Aloo kɛji akɛ jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do the outer edges of my maize leaves turn yellow and look burnt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã lɛ?

english: This leaf scorching is a common sign of potassium deficiency. Potassium helps crops regulate water and strengthen leaf tissues; when soil lacks it, the edges of older leaves dry out and die early, reducing overall yield.
ga: Nɛkɛ baa ni shãa nɛɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ potassium faaa. Potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛɔ nu nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewajeɔ baa fãji lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ bɛ lɛ, baai momoi lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ nɔbaa.

english: How does adding potassium fertilizer help my cassava and yam tubers grow bigger?
ga: Te potassium ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa mi-cassava kɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Potassium acts as a transporter inside the plant, moving sugars produced in the leaves down into the underground roots. This food transfer is what allows tubers like cassava and yam to expand, thicken, and become heavy.
ga: Potassium tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni kɛ nibii yaa tsei amli. Kɛtsɔ sugar ni ajieɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii ni akɛyaa he kroko nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi, tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei, ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits small, soft, and ripening unevenly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ ji bibii, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni eshɛɛɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Tomatoes need sufficient potassium during the fruiting stage to build solid fruit walls, produce even red color, and maintain firmness. Without it, fruits stay light, watery, and spoil quickly after harvest.
ga: Tomato he miihia potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli koni ekɛfee yibiiwoo gbogbo ni wa. Ha efee su tsuru ni yɔɔ ekome. ni ehaa aduawai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Kɛ́ ebɛ lɛ, aduawai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ mlɛo, amɛfeɔ nu, ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛ́ akpa amɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily when a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Stalks become weak and brittle when plants lack essential nutrients like potassium or when roots remain shallow. Proper balanced nutrition strengthens the stem structure so crops can stand firm against weather.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ tso lɛ mli, loo kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Niyenii ni sa jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ tsitsi lɛ mli hewalɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ anaa.

english: Flower drop occurs when crops face stress from heat, irregular watering, or nutrient shortfalls. Ensuring plants have proper soil moisture and balanced plant food keeps flowers attached so fruits can form.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Kwɛmɔ ni tsei lɛ aná shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni sa kɛ tsei niyenii ni ja lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe koni aduawai anyɛ afee.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves curl up and dry out quickly during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds cause plants to lose water rapidly through their leaves. Young or unshaded cocoa trees dry out easily because their root systems cannot pull up water fast enough to match the moisture lost from leaf surfaces.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Cacao tsei bibii loo ni bɛ hulutsoo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu oya bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔtɔ ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is suffering from nutrient starvation instead of a pest attack?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he hɔmɔ miipiŋ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutua amɛ?

english: Nutrient shortages usually show up as widespread, balanced patterns like leaf yellowing or stunted growth across many plants. Pest attacks usually leave clear physical damage like holes, bite marks, or sticky residue on specific spots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo yɛ gbɛi ni gbɛ eshwa ni ja nɔ, tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo tsei srɔtoi babaoo ni edaaa lɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shiɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, tamɔ bu, ŋmei okadii, loo nibii ni kpɛtɛɔ he. yɛ sane pɔtɛɛ ko he

english: Why should I talk to an agricultural extension officer before planting instead of waiting until crops show problems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko agba sane dani madu nii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni tso lɛ aná naagba ko lɛ?

english: Getting advice before planting helps you select the right seeds, test your soil, and apply the correct fertilizers early. Preventing problems before planting is much cheaper and more successful than trying to save damaged crops later.
ga: Kɛ́ ona ŋaawoo dani odu lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohala dumɔwui ni sa, oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa awo mli mra. Naagbai ni abaatsi naa dani adu lɛ jara waaa ni eyeɔ omanye fe bɔ ni abɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ahere ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ ayiwala yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops perform poorly even though I use the exact same seeds and fertilizer as my neighbor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ mikutsoŋbii lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Soil composition, water retention, and land history differ from one field to another. A practice that works for a neighbor might fail on your land if your soil lacks different nutrients or requires a different management approach.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ nu ni akɛhiɛɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ yinɔsane yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Nifeemɔi ni tsuɔ nii ehaa okutsoŋnyo lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii srɔtoi loo ebiɔ gbɛ kroko ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nɔ.

english: Heavy rains wash away loose fertilizer from the soil surface before crop roots have time to drink it in. This wastes your investment and leaves the crops hungry despite your hard work.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Enɛ baafite shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ ni hɔmɔ baaye onibii kɛji otsu nii waa po.

english: Why are the leaves on my coconut trees turning bright yellow and dropping all their fruits suddenly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ akokoso tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa ni enɔ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a deadly infection called Lethal Yellowing disease. It attacks the tree's internal food supply, causing the flowers and young nuts to drop early before the leaves turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji hela ko ni naa wa ni atsɛɔ lɛ wala hela. Etutuaa niyenii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Ha fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ agbo oya dani baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: How do I know if my coconut leaves are turning yellow because of poor soil or because of a tree disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo tso hela hewɔ ni ŋmeii baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Soil deficiency usually turns leaves light green or yellow slowly across your entire farm, whereas Lethal Yellowing disease attacks specific trees rapidly, making leaves turn intense golden-yellow while flowers and nuts fall off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni bɛ lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ fiofio. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tutuaa tsei komɛi oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ shika tsuru ni mli kwɔ beni fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why can a crop look healthy on the outside even when it is actually sick inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ kponɔgbɛ eyɛ mli akɛ hela mɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ mligbɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Many plant diseases take time to build up inside the plant's tissue. During this early stage, the plant functions normally, but internal damage is happening long before yellow leaves or rotting show up on the outside.
ga: Tsei ahe helai babaoo heɔ be dani amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ tsei amli fãji amli. Yɛ shishijee be nɛɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi mligbɛ fitemɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ dani baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni fiteɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why is it so hard to tell what sickness my crop has after the leaves start drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ male nɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe beni baai lɛ je shishi amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Once severe symptoms like drying leaves appear, other secondary pests and fungi often move in on the weakened plant. This makes it difficult to tell what original disease caused the problem without expert testing.
ga: Kɛji hela lɛ he okadii lɛ mli wa waa, tamɔ baai ni egbi, tsɛŋemɔ helai krokomɛi ni ji enyɔ kɛ ŋmeii. Bei pii lɛ ebaa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaale hela ni yɔɔ shishi ni kɛ naagba lɛ baa lɛ kɛji ŋaalɔi ekaaa lɛ akwɛɛɛ.

english: What does it mean when my plant stops bearing fruit even though the leaves still look fine?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ mitso lɛ kpa yibiiwoo eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ lolo moŋ?

english: This usually means an internal disease or nutrient blockage is developing silently. The plant diverts its remaining energy away from growing fruit to keep itself alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni yɔɔ mli loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ mɔ naa lɛ miiya nɔ yɛ dioofeemɔ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli koni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli.

english: Can tiny germs like bacteria really kill a whole mature tree like a coconut palm?
ga: Ani helai bibii tamɔ bacteria baanyɛ agbe ŋmei tso muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛɛlɛŋ?

english: Yes, certain microscopic bacteria can multiply inside the tree's water and nutrient channels, blocking them completely until the tree starves and dies from the inside out.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai bibii komɛi ni anaaa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ́ yɛ tsei lɛ amli nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ gbɛi lɛ amli. Ekɛ amɛ kpaa gbee kwraa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ni egboɔ kɛjɛɔ emli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Are crop diseases caused mainly by insects or by something else I cannot see?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii loo nɔ kroko ni minaaa lɛ ji nɔ titri ni kɛ tsei ahe helai baa?

english: While insects cause visible bite damage, severe tree diseases are often caused by invisible germs like bacteria or viruses. However, sap-sucking insects frequently carry these germs from sick plants to healthy ones.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ fiteɔ nii moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, helai ni anaaa, tamɔ bacteria loo virus lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsei ahe helai ni naa wa baa. Shi kɛlɛ, bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ kɛ helai nɛɛ yaa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Is this disease killing coconut trees only happening on my farm in Ghana, or is it in other places too?
ga: Ani hela ni gbeɔ akokoshi tsei nɛɛ baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli pɛ yɛ Ghana loo he kroko?

english: Lethal Yellowing disease is a global problem found in many coconut-growing regions around the world. It spreads easily when insects fly between farms or when infected planting materials are moved.
ga: Yellow leaf hela ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ji jeŋ muu fɛɛ naagba ko ni anaa yɛ hei babaoo ni aduɔ ŋmeii yɛ yɛ je lɛŋ he fɛɛ he lɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ kooloi bibii fo kɛtee ŋmɔji ateŋ loo kɛ́ ajie dumɔ nii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ he kroko.

english: Why do some of my trees die completely within just a few weeks of showing sickness?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ekomɛi gboiɔ kwraa yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ mli beni amɛjieɔ hela lɛ he okadii lɛ akpo lɛ?

english: Lethal bacterial diseases rapidly clog the plant’s pipelines. Once the blockage becomes total, water and nutrients can no longer reach the leaves and roots, causing the tree to collapse very quickly.
ga: Helai ni muawai ni woɔ mɔ wala he gbeyei kɛbaa lɛ tsiɔ tsei amli gas paipii lɛ anaa oya. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ko tsi gbɛ lɛ Nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe dɔŋŋ. Ehaa tsei shwieɔ shi oya waa.

english: How can I protect my coconut trees from getting sick if I cannot see the sickness early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi ŋmei tso lɛ naa koni hela akamɔ mi kɛji hela lɛ enaaa oya?

english: The best protection is planting disease-resistant coconut varieties, controlling plant-hopping insects that spread germs, and removing and destroying any infected trees immediately to protect the healthy ones.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa ji ni adu ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ shi ni gbɛɔ hela amɛshwaa lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ ni ajieɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni akpataa amɛhiɛ koni akɛbu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: Sir, should I apply new fertilizer to the soil around my plantain plants after I harvest the main bunch?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hee afata shikpɔŋ ni bɔle dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ he?

english: Yes, after you harvest the main stem, the young suckers left behind need fresh nutrients to grow into strong plants for your next harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni okpa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ sɛɛ. Nibii heei he miihia gbekɛbii ni eshwɛ lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha okpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What can I do to feed my crops when chemical fertilizer is scarce or too expensive for me to buy?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mikɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ namɔ wa loo ejara wa tsɔ akɛ abaanyɛ ahe?

english: You can use well-rotted animal manure, compost, or decayed crop waste around the base of the plants to supply nutrients naturally without buying expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei ni egboi ni etse amɛhe lɛ abɔle he. Tso lɛ shishi haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my plantain crop is not getting enough nutrients from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantains lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves often turn yellow instead of dark green, their stems stay thin, and they produce small or weak bunches of fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ Bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ, eshishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni ewoɔ aduawai bibii loo ni yɔɔ blɛoo.

english: Should I mix fertilizer into the soil before I put a new plantain shoot into the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui heei?

english: Yes, putting compost or manure into the planting hole gives the young root system immediate food, helping the new crop settle and grow much faster.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔ bu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi bibii lɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei heei ni amɛtoɔ amɛhe shi ni amɛdaraa oya kwraa.

english: Do I need to keep watering my plantain field after I have finished cutting down the mature fruit?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni maya nɔ mawo mi plantains lɛ nu beni mifo aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, plantains need continuous moisture because the young shoots remaining in the ground depend on wet soil to grow and take over as the next crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔtɔ he miihia plantains be fɛɛ be ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni akɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How often do I need to water my young plantain plants during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe hiaa ni mawo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young plantains have broad leaves that lose water quickly, so watering them deeply two to three times a week during dry months keeps them healthy and growing.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu waa shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni eda.

english: My plantain plant has produced too many young shoots around its base; do I need to remove some of them?
ga: Mi plantain lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo tsɔ ni ebɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he. Ani ehe miihia ni majie fãi komɛi?

english: Yes, too many shoots or 'children' will fight each other for food and light. You should trim them so only two or three strong shoots remain per plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii loo ‘bii’ babaoo tsɔ baatswa niyenii kɛ la he akaŋ. Esa akɛ ofo tso lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ mli ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi yɛ tso kome mli.

english: How does a plantain crop continue to produce fruit after the main tree has been cut down?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantain tsei yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii beni afo tso titri lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plantains grow from an underground root base that stays alive and continues to sprout new side-shoots (suckers) after the parent stem is harvested.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishitoo ni hiɛ ka mli ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii heei (ŋmeii) beni akpa fɔlɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves on my plantain plant turn brown and dry, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ mafo mli?

english: Older leaves dry out naturally as the plant grows; pruning dry brown leaves stops pests from hiding in them and helps direct energy to new growth.
ga: Baai ni egbɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Baai ni egbi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akatee baai lɛ amli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsɔɔ hewalɛ gbɛ kɛyaa dalɛ hee nɔ.

english: Sir, can I feed my plantains using the exact same fertilizer I use for my maize?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛfeɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔŋŋ aha mi plantains lɛ niyenii?

english: While both need basic food, plantains require higher amounts of potassium to develop large bunches, so fertilizers rich in potassium or wood ash suit plantains best.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ niyenii titri he miihia amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ moŋ. Shi potassium babaoo he miihia plantains koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium loo tso mli sũ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui.

english: How do I properly collect soil from my farm to test if the land is good for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabua shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ koni maka kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii loo ehiii?

english: You should take small amounts of soil from several different spots across your field in a zig-zag pattern, mix them together in a clean bucket, and take a sample of that mixture so it represents the whole farm.
ga: Esa akɛ oŋɔ shikpɔŋ bibii kɛjɛ hei srɔtoi. kɛtsɔ oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ zigzag gbɛ nɔ Futumɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ baagi ni mli tse mli. ni obua nakai futumɔ nii lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii anaa koni efee ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔ

english: Why can't I just take soil from one spot near my farm hut to test my entire field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ maŋɔ shikpɔŋ kɛjɛ he kome ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ mli tsũ lɛ ni maka mihe fɛɛ he lɛ makwɛ?

english: Soil changes across your land depending on slopes, shade, and past crop use. Testing only one spot gives an inaccurate picture, as other areas of your farm may have different nutrient levels.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ, shade, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Nɔ kome pɛ ni akaa lɛ akwɛɔ lɛ haa anáa mfoniri ni ejaaa. Ejaakɛ hei krokomɛi Ekolɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi srɔtoi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How deep should I dig when taking soil samples for my crops?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mibua shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔnii anaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You should clear the top leaves and dig about 15 to 20 centimeters deep—roughly the length from your wrist to your elbow—because that is the zone where crop roots draw most of their food.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni otsa aaafee sɛntimita 15 kɛyashi 20 (aaafee elɛɛmɔ kɛjɛ nine nɔ kɛyashi etsitsi nɔ), ejaakɛ jɛmɛ ji he ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbalaa amɛ niyenii lɛ babaoo yɛ.

english: Is it okay to take soil samples for testing right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ ko ni aka lɛ akwɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni awo mli ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, testing right after applying fertilizer gives fake high readings. It is best to take samples before planting or long after harvest so you get a true measurement of the soil's natural condition.
ga: Dabi, kaa ni afeɔ yɛ fɔmɔ kotoku mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baaha akanemɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni ji amale. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaabua nɔkwɛmɔnii anaa dani adu loo be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ osusu bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very well in the low flat areas but struggle on the hillsides of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ shi amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ gɔji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater washes topsoil and nutrients down from the slopes into the low areas, leaving hilltops drier and poorer in nutrients while low flat lands stay rich and moist.
ga: Nugbɔ nu hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ gɔŋji lɛ amli kɛyaa hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa gɔji lɛ ayitsei lɛ agbiɔ, ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does the layout of my land affect how much fertilizer I need to buy?
ga: Te bɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe hiaa ni mahe lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Sloped or eroded parts of your land lose nutrients quickly and may need more organic matter or fertilizer, while low spots that accumulate washed-down soil often need less.
ga: Hei ni shwieɔ shi loo hei ni efite lɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ oya, ni ekolɛ ehe baahia ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mli. yɛ be mli ni hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni buaa sũ ni afɔ lɛ naa lɛ fɔɔ nɔ ni biɔ fioo.

english: Why do crops near stream beds and valley bottoms stay green longer during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ faai kɛ jɔɔ lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Valley bottoms naturally retain moisture longer under the ground and collect rich soil washed down from higher land, allowing plants to access water even when the rains stop.
ga: Jɔɔ lɛ shishi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ. ni ebua shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa nu kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ekpa po.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce large roots in sandy spots but small roots in hard clay spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miiwo shishifãi wuji yɛ ŋã he lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ sũ mli hei ni wa.

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to expand easily. Hard clay soils tightly compact the roots, making it difficult for them to swell into large tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ sũ fee lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaafu ni amɛtsɔ yitsei wuji.

english: Why do crops grow much taller in spots on my farm where I burned clearing brush in the past?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ ni mishã vetiver jwɛi yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Burning leaves ash, which temporarily adds potassium and lime to that specific spot, but this effect fades quickly and burning can damage the healthy organisms in the rest of your soil.
ga: Shãa ni shãa, ni kɛ potassium kɛ lime fataa he lɛ he yɛ be kukuoo mli Shi nɛkɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni shãa baanyɛ akpata nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ.

english: What causes my maize leaves to turn pale yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa po sɛɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen—a key food plants need to stay green—or the soil is too packed and waterlogged for the plant roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ tsɔ ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ amu.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa plants drying up and turning brown in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily scorch in direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa from sun damage and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ adumɔ. Amɛ fɛɛ amɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need to be trained onto wooden stakes to yield well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsɔse sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce large tubers underground by collecting solar energy through their leaves. Lifting the vines off the ground with stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and air, while preventing fungal rot that happens when leaves lie on damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji kɛtsɔ hulu hewalɛ ni amɛbua naa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa kɛji akɛ akɛ baai wo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ? Dumɔ be

english: Growing maize in the same spot continuously exhausts specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the earth. Rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsu nii yɛ ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the tips of lower leaves usually means the soil is low in nitrogen. Nitrogen is the primary nutrient crops use to make leaves green and grow strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu awa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and look pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil that your main crops need. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients required for healthy growth.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni otsei titrii lɛ taoɔ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying suddenly even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden collapse is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne organism that clogs the water pipes inside the plant stem, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves even if there is plenty of moisture in the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa lɛ. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and showing green and yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This pattern is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insect pests called whiteflies. The virus prevents the plant from converting sunlight into food efficiently, resulting in smaller root tubers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkatsake hulu la lɛ amɛfee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifã lɛ yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Why do tiny green worms eat holes in the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Koni amɛye bu ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These worms are usually fall armyworms that hide in the growing center of the maize plant to feed on tender young leaves, which slows crop development if not managed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji asraafoi ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ mra.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates high air moisture that helps fungal spores grow and spread quickly between cocoa pods through splashing rain droplets, causing the Black Pod disease.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i babaoo baa, ni no haa ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ kɛtsɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛ black pod hela baa.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular water supply, or a lack of essential soil minerals needed to support fruit development.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. aloo minerals ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai adalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli

english: Why do my crops give smaller yields every year when I plant on the same farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Continuous planting on the same piece of land without resting it or adding organic manure drains the soil of essential food. Just like a person needs food to work, soil needs nutrients replenished to feed new crops.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni akɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. Taakɛ niyenii he hiaa wɔ koni wɔtsu nii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu he miihia ni akɛ niyenii afata he koni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii heei.

english: Why does my soil seem to lose its strength so quickly after growing heavy crops like maize or yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ he waaa oya beni midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops like yam and maize are heavy feeders that draw large amounts of nutrients out of the earth. Rotating them with legumes like cowpeas helps put nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ji niyenii wuji ni jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What can I add to my soil to help my crops grow strong when I cannot afford chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni mikɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ be mli ni minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can mix animal manure, dried leaves, and compost into the soil. This natural food improves the soil structure and slowly feeds your plants over a long period.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, baai ni egbi, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tsei niyenii fiofio yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and thin instead of fat and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee fɔ kɛ kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep, and well-aerated soil to expand easily. If the soil is hard, compacted, or lacks nutrients, the tuber cannot force its way through the dirt to grow thick.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ, Yitso lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I store my harvested yams so they do not rot quickly during months when food is scarce?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ekafite oya yɛ nyɔji babaoo ni niyenii faaa lɛ amli?

english: Construct a traditional raised yam barn with good shade and air circulation. Keeping the tubers dry, elevated off the ground, and protected from hot sunlight stops rot and pest damage.
ga: Feemɔ kusum naa sweet potato ŋmɔ ni awo nɔ ni haa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ŋmeii ni awó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbimɔ ni atsĩ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa Baakpa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my crop plants stay small and stunted for months without making progress?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee bibioo ni egbɔjɔ nyɔji babaoo ni nɔ ko nɔ ko eyaaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Stunted growth usually happens when plants lack key soil nutrients, suffer from root pests, or do not get enough water. Checking for root damage or adding compost can kickstart their growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ adalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa kɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shishifãi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe piŋmɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni anáaa Shishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ awo dalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops have green leaves but fail to produce fruit or good harvests at the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa eŋɔli shi ewooo yibii kpakpai loo ewooo yibii kpakpai yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen makes plants put all their energy into big green leaves instead of food production. Plants need phosphorus and potassium to form heavy fruits, tubers, and seeds.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ niyenii ni amɛbaafee lɛ najiaŋ. Tsei he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛwo aduawai ni tsii, ŋmeii, kɛ dumɔwui.

english: Why do some crops on my farm grow very well while the plants right next to them yield nothing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni mɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ daaa lɛ? Ani ejieee nɔ ko kwraa kpo?

english: Uneven soil, weeds stealing water, or pest attacks in specific spots cause unequal growth. Spacing plants properly ensures each plant gets its fair share of sunlight, water, and nutrients.
ga: shikpɔŋ ni ejaaa Jwɛi juɔ nu loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa yɛ hei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni kɛ dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee baa Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ateŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni sa.

english: How can I protect my food crops when the rains stop earlier than expected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass or leaves—called mulching—traps moisture in the soil, keeping plant roots cool and hydrated during dry periods.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ŋmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: What is the best way to prepare my land before the rainy season starts so my crops grow fast?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi koni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ oya?

english: Clear weeds early, loosen the topsoil without exposing it to harsh sun, and build mounds or ridges. This helps rainwater soak deep into the soil where roots can reach it.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa akashɛ enɔ. ni amɛmaa gɔji loo ŋmeii Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant is hungry, usually lacking nitrogen. Heavy rains can wash nutrients deep into the ground where young roots cannot reach, showing that the soil needs compost or fertilizer to help the plant regain its strength.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the tall trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under full, hot sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains creates living umbrellas that protect the cocoa from heat and keep the soil moist while the cocoa grows.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaha ŋwɛi ŋta ni baabu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ latsaa he lɛ aba. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing light green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on cassava are usually a sign of mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from capturing sunlight properly, leading to small, poor-quality tubers under the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ yucca nɔ lɛ ji mosaic hela he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni ehiii lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why is it dangerous to plant my maize immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry spell. If you plant too quickly, the seeds will sprout, but the hot sun will dry up the young shoots before the main rainy season fully settles in.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ agbi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme dry conditions. Without steady water and cooler soil, the plant drops its flowers to save energy so the main stem can stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ bɛ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: How do I know that my yams under the soil are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: When the leaves and vines above the ground turn yellow and dry up naturally, the yam is ready. This drying shows that the plant has finished transferring all its food energy from the leaves down into the underground tuber.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ eshɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava cuttings very close to each other so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni anyɛ adu shikpɔŋ babaoo?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of getting many big roots, you end up with tall, thin plants that produce very small tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehiɛ shishifãi wuji waa Ebatsɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my harvested maize produce smaller crops than the certified seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni miheɔ lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields in their first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their high-yielding properties in the second generation, leading to uneven growth and smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee jarayeli nibii krokomɛi lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ yibiiwoo babaoo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop in the middle of the afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can drink it up from the ground. The plant droops temporarily to conserve moisture and will recover as the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni ebaahe ejɔ lɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why should I remove the extra shoot suckers growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers steal water and nutrients away from the main mother plantain tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets full nourishment to produce a heavy, large bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni tsii baa.

english: How long will it take after I plant a plantain sucker before I can harvest my first bunch?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe beni midu plantain lɛ sɛɛ dani makpa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees generally take between 9 to 12 months to flower, and another 3 to 4 months for the fruit bunch to mature fully for harvest, depending on soil fertility and rainfall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, ni amɛheɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi hu dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ kɛha kpamɔ. Edamɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ fɛo ha kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ nɔ.

english: Can I leave my cassava roots in the soil if I am not ready to harvest and sell them yet?
ga: Kɛji ofeee klalo akɛ obaakpa ni ohɔ̃ɔ Ani abaanyɛ ashi ŋmei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cassava is a very forgiving crop. Mature roots can stay safely underground for several months without spoiling, allowing you to harvest them only when you are ready to use or sell them.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ji tso ko ni kɛ eshai keɔ waa. Shishifãi ni eda lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo ni amɛgbooo. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii lɛ pɛ kɛji ofee klalo akɛ okɛbaatsu nii loo okɛhɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why does a mango tree take so much longer to produce fruit compared to plantains or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii fe plantain loo cassava lɛ?

english: Mangoes are permanent tree crops that spend their first 3 to 5 years building deep root systems and strong trunks before they can produce fruit, whereas plantain and cassava grow rapidly and complete their cycles much faster.
ga: Mango ji tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni amɛheɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Yɛ be mli ni plantain kɛ cassava daa oya ni sɛɛkuu lɛ gbeɔ naa oya kwraa lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava and plantains together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and plantain works well because cassava tubers grow underground while plantains grow tall above ground, allowing them to share the land efficiently without crowding each other out early on.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmei shishifã lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Enɛ haa amɛjaraa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsiii amɛhe mra.

english: What simple things can I do to keep my farm soil rich and healthy for my crops year after year?
ga: Mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Mibaanyɛ mafee ekomɛi koni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa afi.

english: You can add decomposed animal manure or compost, leave crop leftovers to decay naturally on the field, and avoid burning farm clearings so the natural organic nutrients stay in the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he. Ha ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ agbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni agbele yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ni oooshã lɛ he koni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that the mangoes on my tree are mature enough to be plucked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mango ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie?

english: Mangoes are ready when the fruit shoulders widen and turn full, the skin color shifts from dark green to a lighter green or yellow, and the fruit yields slightly to gentle pressure.
ga: Mango lɛ efee klalo akɛ ayeɔ kɛ́ tsitsii lɛ mli etse ni aduawai lɛ eyi obɔ. Hewolonɔ su tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛyaa eŋɔli ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ. ni nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji nɔnyɛɛ fioo

english: Why do the outer leaves of my plantain trees dry up and turn brown during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that evaporate water quickly. During the dry harmattan winds, the plant naturally drys off its lower leaves to conserve water in its main stem and survive until the rains return.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni haa nu shwieɔ shi oya. Yɛ Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli Tso lɛ baagbi eshishigbɛ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ehiɛ nu yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ mli ni ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stems to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni sa ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from plants that are 8 to 12 months old, ensuring the stems are free from diseases or insects, and cut them into sections with at least 3 to 5 clear buds.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ amli tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ hela loo kooloi bɛ tsei lɛ amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli fãi bibii. kɛ hoo lɛ, ŋmeii 3 kɛyashi 5 ni mli tse.

english: If small-scale illegal mining has damaged a part of my land, can crops still grow there?
ga: Kɛji shika bibii ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ kɛ fitemɔ ba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lolo?

english: Mining strips away the fertile topsoil and packs the ground tight. To grow crops there again, the land must be leveled, deep-plowed to loosen the earth, and enriched with plenty of organic matter like compost over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni tsei akwɛ yɛ jɛmɛ ekoŋŋ Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.
