Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mli yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli.

english: Is it better for a beginner farmer like me to plant only one crop or mix different crops like plantain, cassava, and fruit trees?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ okwaafonyo hee tamɔ mi baadu ŋmɔshi nibii kome loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutu tamɔ plantains, cassava kɛ aduawai tsei?

english: Mixing crops is usually better for beginner farmers because it spreads your risk. Quick crops like cassava provide early food and income while you wait for longer-term trees like mangoes to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha okwaafoi heei ejaakɛ ehaa oshara ni oyɔɔ lɛ feɔ srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ oya tamɔ ŋmei haa niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ tsei ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ mango lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do young baby cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before growing into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa kwraa lɛ?

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' which is the cocoa tree's natural way of self-thinning when it carries more fruits than it can feed, though it can also be caused by sap-sucking insects or a lack of soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ ‘cherelle wilt’, ni ji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa ehe feɔ mlɛo kɛji ewo yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye. Eyɛ mli akɛ cacao hu baanyɛ ajɛ kooloi ni nuɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli aba moŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and wither when left under full direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that cannot handle high heat and direct sun rays, so they need shade crops like plantains to shelter them until their canopy develops.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains lɛ anɔ koni amɛha amɛhe nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni hulutsoo be ko baaje kpo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient roots pull from the soil to keep leaves green and grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii mli shishifãi ni he hiaa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall, weak, and thin with tiny cobs when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe tseee ni amɛmli ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients while their leaves block each other's light, forcing the stalks to stretch upward instead of growing thick and strong.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe la lɛ naa Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe wa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without turning into green tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress, as the plant tries to save water and energy rather than making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and get crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking juices from the undersides of young leaves, or transmitting viruses that distort leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo egbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ eshwaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting beneath the ground after long periods of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe; when water stays trapped around the roots for too long, it suffocates them and allows soil fungi to cause tuber rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu ŋmɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaafo ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why do yam vines need to be trained on tall wooden stakes to yield bigger tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsɔse sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ koni amɛwo bulbs wuji lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce the food energy required to expand big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi yɛ hulu la mli koni amɛná niyenii hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, draw away water and nutrients from the mother plant, so keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem yields a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi loo suckers lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 1 loo 2 pɛ ahi shi koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmeii agbo ko yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does growing cowpeas or groundnuts in my field make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas work with friendly soil bacteria on their roots to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ su tsuɔ nii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli, he ni eji tsei aniyenii ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I add manure or compost into the hole before planting my plantain sucker?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo bu lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Organic matter like manure acts like a sponge and a food source. It provides young plantains with essential nutrients to grow fast and keeps the soil around the roots moist so the sucker does not dry out.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji kɛ niyenii jɛɛhe. Ehaa plantains bibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni suckers lɛ akagbi.

english: Why is it necessary to pour water directly into the planting hole when putting the plantain inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔse nu awo dumɔ bu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ adu plantains lɛ?

english: Pouring water directly into the pit settles the soil firmly around the roots, removes dry air pockets, and gives the fresh sucker the immediate moisture it needs to start sprouting right away.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo bu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli awa. Ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kotokui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii heei lɛ naa nu ni he hiaa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend digging deep pits for plantains rather than small, shallow holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ atsa bu ni mli kwɔ koni akɛdu dumɔwui yɛ bu bibii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Plantains have spreading roots that need soft, loose soil to grow easily. A deep pit allows you to mix in good soil and manure, giving the plant space to anchor firmly against strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ekwɛ̃ oya. Bu ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efutu jogbaŋŋ lɛ futuɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa.

english: Why do I need to mix organic matter into the pit soil instead of just scattering it on top of the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli futuɔ bu lɛ mli sũ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mikɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mixing manure deep into the pit places nutrients right where the new roots are growing. If left on top of the ground, heavy rains can wash the manure away before the plantain roots can reach it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu bu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ahi he ni shishifãi heei miida lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ aya dani plantain shishifãi lɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why is it important to cover the plantain sucker completely with soil after putting it in the watered hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ sũ aha dumɔwu lɛ nɔ kwraa beni akɛ nu ewo bu lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Covering the sucker fully protects the delicate root area from harsh sunlight, traps moisture inside the pit, and holds the young plant upright so it can grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ oha tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ bu lɛ mli lɛ ni ehiɛɔ tso bibioo lɛ mli koni enyɛ eda waa.

english: How does a plantain sucker cut from an old plant manage to sprout into a brand new crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni plantain tso ni afo kɛjɛ tso momo ko mli lɛ atsɔ tso hee?

english: The base of a plantain sucker contains stored food energy and tiny growth buds. When buried in moist, nutrient-rich soil, these buds awaken to produce new roots below and fresh leaves above.
ga: Hewalɛ ni ato kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ plantain sucker lɛ shishi. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi heei yɛ shishi kɛ baai heei yɛ ŋwɛi.

english: What will happen to my plantain sucker if I plant it in a dry pit without adding water first?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantain sucker lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛdu yɛ bu ko ni egbi mli ni mikɛ nu fataaa he klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: If planted in dry soil without water, the sucker will lose its internal moisture to the dry dirt, which slows down growth and can cause the young plant to dry up and die.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ Vacuum lɛ laajeɔ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Enɛ haa dalɛ baa shi ni ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why is it helpful for farmers to work in small groups when planting plantains on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ okwaafoi baatsu nii yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting plantains involves multiple steps—adding manure, watering the pit, setting the sucker, and covering it. Working together ensures the sucker is planted and watered quickly before the hot sun dries out the open hole.
ga: Plantain dumɔ biɔ nibii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, nu ni akɛwoɔ bu lɛ mli, sucker lɛ ni atoɔ he gbɛjianɔ, kɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ. Nitsumɔ ni akɛ ekomefeemɔ tsuɔ lɛ haa aduɔ su lɛ ni awoɔ nu oya dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa egbiɔ kɛjɛɔ bu ni agbele lɛ mli.

english: How long does it usually take for a newly planted plantain sucker to sprout its first green leaves?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani plantain tsei ni adu ehee lɛ kwɛɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ baai ni ji eŋɔli lɛ?

english: When planted in moist, rich soil, a healthy plantain sucker usually starts pushing out its first green shoots within two to three weeks as its roots take hold.
ga: Kɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ nɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, plantain suckers ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shishi yɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ mli kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ emɔ shi.

english: How does having wet organic matter at the bottom of the pit help my crop survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ bu lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Organic matter holds onto moisture deep underground like a reservoir. During short dry spells, the plantain roots can still draw water from this damp soil layer to keep growing without wilting.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ toɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ tamɔ nutoohe. yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ Plantain shishifãi hu baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɛɛ nɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara ni amɛgbooo.

english: What does mechanization actually mean for my farm, and why are other farmers switching to it?
ga: Mɛni ji tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi No hewɔ lɛ otsake kɛtee tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ anɔ?

english: Mechanization simply means using machines like tractors, planters, and harvesters instead of doing all the heavy work by hand with hoes and cutlasses. Farmers switch to it because machines allow you to farm larger areas of land much faster, leading to higher efficiency and better overall profits.
ga: Mechanization tsɔɔ tsɔnei tamɔ traktɔi, nibii ni akɛduɔ nii, kɛ nibii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni Okwaafoi kɛ amɛdɛŋ baatsu nitsumɔi ni wa lɛ fɛɛ kɛ shɔvel kɛ dade lɛ, amɛmiitsake kɛmiiya nɔ ejaakɛ tsɔnei haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ okwaayeli yɛ hei wuji oya kwraa. Enɛ kɛ nitsumɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: Will hiring a machine service to help plant my crop fields really bring me more money in the long run?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ahe nitsumɔhe ko ni mikɛbaatsu nii koni eye ebua mi ni mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ baaha maná shika babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, because machines prepare the soil deeper and plant seeds uniformly at the right spacing. This leads to healthier crops, less seed waste, and higher crop yields that easily cover the cost of paying for the machine service.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsɔne lɛ baasaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni edu dumɔwui lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ he ni sa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa. Dumɔwui ni afiteɔ fioo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa babaoo ni haa tsɔnei ahe nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo lɛ he nyɔmɔ mlɛo.

english: Why is it so difficult for me to clear and plant my farm using only hired farm workers during the main planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa mi akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi ni aŋɔ amɛ pɛ baatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ amli ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Because when the rains start, every farmer is looking for labor at the exact same time. This makes manual labor scarce and expensive, whereas using tractor services allows you to finish land preparation and planting on schedule without depending on large labor crews.
ga: Ejaakɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ Okwaafonyo fɛɛ okwaafonyo miitao nitsumɔ yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa nitsulɔi faaa, ni ejara hu wa. Yɛ be mli ni traktɔ nitsumɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa onyɛɔ osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ogbeɔ dumɔwu lɛ naa yɛ be naa ni okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔɔ nitsumɔ babaoo nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my farm work become so much harder and stressful when my crops produce a very heavy yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ wa ni ehaa mɔ haoɔ waa yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ?

english: A bumper crop harvest requires much more time, labor, and transport to gather, dry, and protect before it spoils in the field. Without proper planning or mechanical equipment to help, processing a high-yielding crop manually can easily overwhelm a farmer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akpamɔ heɔ be babaoo, nitsumɔ, kɛ gbɛfaa babaoo koni akɛbua naa, agbi, ni abu he dani amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Kɛ atooo gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ loo akɛ tsɔnei ni sa tsuuu nii lɛ, Nibii ni akɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha okwaafoi lɛ aye amɛhe oya.

english: Why do some of my crops rot or spoil in the field even when I have had a very successful growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi miifite loo miifite yɛ ŋmɔji amli eyɛ mli akɛ miná ŋmɔshi nibii ni ye omanye waa lɛ?

english: When crops produce abundantly, manual harvesting often takes too long. If crops stay in the field past their peak maturity while waiting to be picked by hand, rain, insects, and humidity will cause them to spoil before you can harvest them.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fa babaoo lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tee nɔ amɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkpa lɛ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni akɛ niji akpa amɛ lɛ, nugbɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ hulutsoo baaha tsei lɛ agboi dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Is it true that planting my crop seeds very close together will give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha maná yibii babaoo?

english: No, crops need personal space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong. When planted too close together, crops compete against each other, leading to weak, thin plants with very small yields.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ he, hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara waa. Kɛji adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe baatswa akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow unevenly across my field when I plant seeds by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ beni mikɛ minine duɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Hand planting makes it hard to keep every seed at the exact same depth and distance. Seeds planted too deep take longer to germinate, while seeds planted shallow grow faster, causing uneven crop growth across your field.
ga: Nine ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaaha dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu ahi shi yɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ kome mli. Dumɔwui ni adu mli tsɔ lɛ baahe be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ daa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei daaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Why do my crops start yielding less after a few years of giving me very heavy harvests on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi yibiiwoo fioo yɛ afii fioo komɛi ni mikɛtsu nii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crops consume minerals and nutrients from the soil to produce heavy harvests. If you do not replenish the soil with fertilizers, manure, or crop rotation, the soil becomes tired and depleted, causing future crop yields to drop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ sũ mli nibii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo nibii babaoo. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast and aggressively in fields where my crops are growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa yɛ ŋmɔji ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Good soil, rain, and fertilizer nourish weeds just as much as your crops. Because weeds are naturally tough, they will quickly overrun your crops and steal their food unless you prepare the land properly before planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa, nugbɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa jwɛi lɛ hewalɛ tamɔ bɔ ni jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii Enɛ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ ji nɔ ni wa kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli. Amɛbaatutua onibii oya ni amɛbaaju amɛ niyenii. Ja osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani odu.

english: How does deep soil plowing with a tractor help my crop roots grow better compared to using a hand hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ trakta ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni mli kwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋtayaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he?

english: Tractors plow deep into hard ground to loosen compacted soil, making it soft and full of air. This allows young crop roots to spread easily, reach deeper water reserves, and anchor the plant firmly against strong winds.
ga: Trakta ko shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ekɛjie shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyi mli obɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ashishifãi ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo. Nu jɛɛhei ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe nine shɛɔ nɔ ni emɔɔ tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: How long does it take for a plantain sucker to start bearing fruit after I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mamɔ plantain koni mabɔi yibiiwoo beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plantains usually take about 9 to 12 months to produce flowers and another 3 months for the fruits to mature and be ready for harvest, depending on soil quality and regular rainfall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ dumɔwui lɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, ni eheɔ nyɔji 3 krokomɛi hu dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ. Edamɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hi ha kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my main plantain tree die after producing just one bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ gbo beni ewo yibii akuu kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The main plantain stem is designed to produce fruit only once in its lifecycle. After fruiting, it naturally dies back to allow its side shoots, called suckers, to take over and become the next generation of fruiting plants.
ga: Afee plantain tso titri lɛ koni ewo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ ewala be mli. Kɛ́ ewo yibii sɛɛ lɛ, egboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ gbɛ aha sɛɛ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ. Eheɔ egbɛhe ni ebafeɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I grow plantains under large shade trees, or do they need full sunlight?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ shade mli? Aloo oosumɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa?

english: Plantains require full sunlight to build the energy needed for thick stems and heavy fruit bunches. Planting them under deep shade makes them grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in smaller bunches.
ga: Hulu ni fa babaoo he miihia plantains koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ aba. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be mli kwɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee shɔŋŋ, amɛhe afee mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni no baaha amɛfee bibioo.

english: Why do all my plantain crops seem to mature at the exact same time during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni midumɔwui lɛ daa yɛ be kome mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains respond heavily to water availability. When the rains start, plants across the region grow rapidly and flower together, leading to a simultaneous harvest season.
ga: Plantains lɛ tsuɔ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ he nii waa. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ je shishi Tsei ni yɔɔ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be kome mli. kɛ mɔ yaa kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli ekomefeemɔ mli

english: What happens to my plantain plants during a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and broad leaves that lose moisture quickly. During dry weather, leaf growth slows down, leaves turn yellow, and the resulting fruit bunches become much smaller.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo. baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ Ni nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: Why do strong winds easily blow down my heavy plantain plants right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ mlɛo dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Plantains do not have strong woody roots or a solid tree trunk; their stems are made of tightly packed leaf sheaths. When a heavy fruit bunch develops, the plant becomes top-heavy and vulnerable to wind.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni wa loo tso shishifãi ni wa. Akɛ baai ni akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ fee tso lɛ shishi. Kɛji aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atswa lɛ oya.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen and spoil so fast before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni egboɔ oya dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, plantains release a natural ripening gas called ethylene. Heat and direct sunlight speed up this gas release, causing the fruit to soften and spoil quickly if kept in a warm area.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa Plantains lɛ, ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo. Dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ jeɔ kpo oya. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa.

english: Why do traders travelling from far places prefer buying green plantains instead of ripe ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi ni fãa gbɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ yaheɔ plantains ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji moŋ fe nɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Green plantains are firm and less easily bruised during long journeys on rough roads. Ripe plantains are soft, bruise easily, and spoil fast before reaching distant buyers.
ga: Plantains eŋɔli lɛ mli wa ni ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ fioo yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Plantains ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, efiteɔ oya, ni efiteɔ oya dani eshɛɔ mɛi ni heɔ yɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: What kind of soil do I need to get big, heavy bunches of plantain?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ he hiaa mi koni maná dumɔwui wuji ni tsii?

english: Plantains need deep, rich, well-draining soil filled with organic matter like compost. Their roots rot quickly in heavy clay or standing water, which prevents them from feeding the plant properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia plantains. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ sũ loo nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa amɛha tsei lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain plant turning yellow and drying up from the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by fungal leaf spot diseases that thrive in warm, humid conditions. These spots destroy the leaf surface, reducing the plant's ability to create food for the growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fungal leaf spot ni shwereɔ yɛ hulutsoo, fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa aduawai ni miida lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, so adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: What makes my groundnut plants produce empty pods with no seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods happen when the soil lacks calcium or moisture while the pods are swelling underground. Adding agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil before planting provides the calcium needed for full seeds to form.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ calcium loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo tso sũ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he dani adu lɛ, ebaaha calcium ni he hiaa koni dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aná.

english: How does leaving dead leaves on top of my soil help my crops survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egboi ni mishiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Covering your soil with dead leaves or grass acts like a protective blanket called mulch. It shades the soil from the hot sun, traps moisture so you water less often, and slowly rots into plant food.
ga: Nibii ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo pɛ awo mli ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up into tight little cups instead of opening broad and flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbele ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites living underneath the leaves. Spraying the undersides of the leaves with soapy water or neem oil helps clear these pests so new leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ. koni baai heei anyɛ akwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when they experience irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting tall crops nearby to provide partial shade during the hottest afternoon hours helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu tsei kakadaji yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ koni ekɛ hulutsoo be fioo aha yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall sticks instead of trailing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakpã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight, which provides energy to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off damp ground, protecting the plant from fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni ji hewalɛ ni akɛkwɛɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I plant them in an open field with no trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and burn under direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates living umbrellas that shelter the seedlings until they grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to dig up from the farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the main stem begins to crack as the tubers swell beneath the soil surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants grow lots of tall green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi bean pods fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes bean plants to spend all their energy growing stems and leaves instead of flowers. Avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizers encourages the plant to start flowering and setting pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛje fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my cabbage heads splitting open in the middle before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ teŋgbɛ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads split when heavy rains or sudden over-watering follow a dry spell, causing the inside to grow faster than the outer leaves can stretch. Maintaining steady, regular watering prevents this sudden growth spurt.
ga: Kaabeji yitsei lɛ baatswa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni hoɔ fe nine trukaa. Enɛ haa mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa ni afeɔ lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ trukaa dalɛ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and burning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiishã lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade from direct sunlight during their first few years. Without shade trees or plantains nearby, the intense heat scorches their delicate leaves and dries out the plant.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha tso lɛ agbi.

english: Why are my young maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a vital plant food. Applying the right fertilizer at the right time helps the leaves turn green so the plant can grow tall and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli. Kɛkɛ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ ada ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Which direction should I plant my cassava stick when putting it in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings must be planted with the growth buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems struggle to grow properly, resulting in poor root and tuber formation.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni ŋmeii wuji lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaná naagba yɛ edalɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots at the bottom of tomatoes are called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering during fruit development.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso ama sweet potato tso masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to stretch upward toward sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground to catch more light and prevents soil-borne diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ miikwɔ wain tso ko ni ehe hiaa ni akpã mli koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ akpee lɛ nɔ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná la babaoo ni ekɛtsi helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua baai lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience heat stress or prolonged dry weather. Keeping the soil moist around the roots during flowering prevents the blossoms from drying up and falling.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli edɔ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ lɛ, ebaatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa ni amɛkagbi ni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small ears when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ toi bibii waa kɛ midu amɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to form full, healthy ears.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and hard while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads quickly in damp, dark, and overly humid farms. Pruning excessive foliage and clearing weeds allows air and sunlight to dry out the field and reduce the fungus.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ tsɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Baai ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants look twisted, yellow, and crumpled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite, eyɛ ŋmɔŋ, ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted and yellow-patterned leaves are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant stem varieties is the best defense against this problem.
ga: Baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Adumɔ tso henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why should I cut away the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra shoots, known as suckers, drain water and nutrients away from the main plant. Pruning them away leaves only the strongest sucker to grow while allowing the main stem to produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, jieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ adara. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha tso lɛ yitso lɛ afee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is an essential food they need to grow strong and green. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost early in the plant's life usually solves this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, etsuɔ ​​naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: How do I know if fall armyworms are destroying my corn field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ fall cutworms lɛ miifite mi-ŋma ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: You will notice ragged holes on the leaves and a sticky, sawdust-like dirt inside the center of the young plant shoot. If you open the shoot, you will often find small caterpillars hiding inside.
ga: Obaana buji ni etse ehe yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ. Kɛji osu mfonirifeemɔ Bei pii lɛ obaana ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee mli.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my crop leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and humidity during the rains create the perfect conditions for fungal diseases to spread on plant leaves. Clearing weeds around the plants helps air flow freely and reduces leaf moisture.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa ŋmeii helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ahe baai lɛ anɔ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Tsei haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa baai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ baa shi.

english: Why are my corn cobs not fully filled with grains at the very top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Empty cob tips usually happen when the plant does not get enough water or fertilizer right when the corn silks are appearing, which prevents proper pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu loo ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ beni ŋmeii siliki jeɔ kpo lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ pollination ni sa naa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant corn on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that love that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts restores soil fertility.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn plants stay thin and small when I put many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each seed enough space allows every plant to grow thick stems and large ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni enáa tsitsi ni mli tse kɛ toii wuji.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant cowpeas or beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and drop it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the soil and helps neighboring maize crops grow better.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up tightly like tubes on hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss through its leaves when the sun is extremely hot and the ground is dry.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize completely before putting it into storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ kwraa dani mikɛwo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Damp or wet maize rots quickly and attracts insects like weevils. Thoroughly drying your grain prevents dangerous mold growth and keeps the corn safe to eat for months.
ga: Abɛi ni mli efɔ loo efɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya ni egbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa ŋmãa ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aya hiɛ, ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ayeɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do my crops wilt easily even when the soil still looks slightly wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ fioo moŋ lɛ?

english: If the plant roots are damaged by underground pests, flooded with standing water, or infected by root diseases, the plant loses its ability to drink water from the soil, causing it to wilt.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai fite tsei ashishifãi, nu shwie shi loo shishifãi helai emɔ amɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛnu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ha egbi

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them provides living umbrellas that give young cocoa the shade and moisture needed to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaha kookoo bibioo lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help your maize regain its green color and produce good ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ okɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛ toi kpakpai.

english: Is it good practice to burn dry weeds and bushes on my farm before planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni egbi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu?

english: Burning clears the land quickly, but it destroys important nutrients in the soil and kills beneficial living organisms that help plants grow. Leaving the cleared weeds to rot naturally into the soil acts as free organic fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Shi efiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ oha jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ onibii amli ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil. Beans and groundnuts are special because they take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth through their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beans kɛ peanuts ji nɔ ko krɛdɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and develop light green and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The best way to prevent this is by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties obtained from certified extension agents or research centers.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ atsĩ enɛ naa ji ni adu ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni anáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli loo niiamlitaomɔ he ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars inside the center leaves of my young maize eating tiny holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ bu bibii kɛtsɔɔ amɛmli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the central growing tip of young maize plants. Inspecting your farm early and using recommended organic controls, like neem leaf extracts, or approved sprays can stop them before they ruin your farm.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem baa mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ atsu nii. loo spray ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ Baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and thin when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When yam mounds are placed too close together, the roots fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Giving each mound enough space allows the roots to expand freely into big, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii ni abua naa lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baatswa nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ Kɛ́ aha ŋtayaa fɛɛ ŋtayaa he gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshwereɔ amɛfeɔ ŋtayaai wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight rows rather than scattering seeds randomly across the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines makes it much easier to walk through your farm, clear weeds, and apply fertilizer without damaging plants. It also ensures every crop gets an equal share of sunlight and root space.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ aaatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ajie jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afiteee tsei lɛ. Ehaa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa hu.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without forming any fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and prevents their blossoms from producing fruit. Watering your tomatoes at the roots early in the morning and leaving some shade can protect the delicate flowers during very hot days.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa amɛwo fɔfɔi loo amɛwo yibii. Kɛ́ afɔ tomato nɔ nu yɛ shishigbɛ leebi ni aha ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: How can I keep my soil damp for longer during the dry season when rain is scarce?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo lɛ?

english: You can cover the bare ground around your crops with dry grass or fallen leaves, a practice called mulching. This acts like a blanket, trapping moisture in the soil and preventing the hot sun from drying it out quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ nibii ni jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egbee shi yɔɔ mli. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaaa egbi oya kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very soft leaves that burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living shade that cools the young trees and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baada waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to clear the grass around the base of my young tree crops every few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ daa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds and grass compete directly with young crops for water, fertilizer, and sunlight. Clearing the ground around the base of your plants ensures that all the nutrients in the soil go straight to your crop's roots instead of feeding unwanted grass.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la. He ni ebɔle he lɛ mli ni ajieɔ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ ni oooha lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and dry from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food needed to make leaves green and healthy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the plants helps restore their bright green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa. Eji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛbaabɔle Tsei ahe lɛ baaye abua ni eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny, empty cobs when I plant three or four seeds very close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ? Be ko lɛ, miduɔ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, root space, and soil nutrients. Spacing plants properly gives each stalk enough food and water to grow thick stems and full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawuu koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shishifãi ahe he, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii. Gbɛ ni kã tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rain falls for many days in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy, but standing water drowns the roots and causes rot-producing germs to grow. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away safely from the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shi nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa helai ni fiteɔ lɛ daa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting at the right time of year prevents heat stress from killing the blossom buds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo be ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ akagbe ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of green leaves but fail to make any seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi enyɛɛɛ efee pods lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much rich nitrogen fertilizer causes them to put all their energy into making thick green leaves instead of flowers. Tiny insects like thrips can also destroy invisible flower buds, so protecting early flowers helps pods form.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips hu baanyɛ afite ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe yɛ shishijee mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni eyɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck the sap out of new leaves and spread plant viruses. Sprays made from neem seed extract or recommended crop remedies can protect the leaves from these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ baai heei amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe ŋaa lɛ baanyɛ abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when a moderate wind blows, even before the fruits mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fioo mli lɛ? Dani aduawai lɛ po baakwɛ̃?

english: Plantain trees fall over when invisible pests like root nematodes or weevil larvae eat and weaken the roots underground. Using clean planting suckers and keeping the base of the plant free of decaying stems builds strong roots that keep the tree anchored.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi ni anaaa amɛ tamɔ shishifãi ni atsɛɔ amɛ root nematodes loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ye ni amɛgbɔjɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ sucker ni he tse tsu nii ni aha shishitoo lɛ akafee nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni mli wa ni haa tso lɛ ahi shi lɛ aba.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for growing big tubers. Staking also keeps the leaves dry and away from soil diseases that thrive on wet leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baa ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: Can I use salty well water to irrigate my vegetable crops like tomatoes?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni mli edɔ yɔɔ nubu mli nu lɛ afɔ aduawai tamɔ tomato nɔ?

english: Salty water draws moisture out of plant roots instead of hydrating them, which burns the root tips, stunts plant growth, and causes the leaves to dry up even when the soil appears wet.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛmli nu. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashã. Ehaa tsei kpaa dalɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off when heavy rains flood my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Flooded soil starves plant roots of air, preventing them from taking up nutrients, which causes the lower leaves to turn yellow and drop off as the plant struggles to survive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye tsei shishifãi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi be mli ni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni ehi shi lɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil with dry grass around my vegetable crops stop them from drying out quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo he ni ebɔle he lɛ? Te mafee tɛŋŋ mitsei lɛ atsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkagbi oya?

english: Covering bare soil with dry grass creates a protective shield that blocks direct sunlight, reducing water evaporation from the ground and keeping crop roots cool during hot days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ha nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings get scorched and die when I clear all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ pɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full tropical sun; they require shade trees to reduce heat stress and keep the air humid around them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves into thin tubes to reduce the leaf area exposed to hot sun and wind, which helps them save water until temperatures cool down.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli amɛfeɔ tsɔnei bibii. Koni akɛba he ni baai lɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the stems of my pepper plants becoming weak, hollow, and snapping easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, amɛhe ewo muji, ni amɛkumɔ oya lɛ?

english: Pest larvae known as stem borers hatch from eggs laid on the plant and burrow inside the stem to eat the soft tissues, leaving the stem hollow and fragile.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, ni atsɛɔ amɛ stem borers lɛ, fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ wɔji ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ amli ni amɛfoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Shi tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli ewo muji ni egbɔjɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are turning pale green because the soil lacks nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ eŋɔli ejaakɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Healthy crop leaves are usually deep green; when leaves turn pale green or light yellow starting from the lower leaves, it shows the soil has run out of essential plant food like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Why do my oil palm trees drop small green fruits before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palms drop immature fruits when the tree experiences severe water shortage during dry periods or when the soil lacks potassium to feed the growing fruit clusters.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ jieɔ yibii ni eshɛko kɛji nu he miihia tsei lɛ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium ni baaha aduawai akui ni miida lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Garden egg flowers drop off without setting fruit if the weather is extremely hot and dry, or if there are no pollinating insects like bees around to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Eggplant ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baagbee shi ni ewooo yibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii ebɔle amɛhe koni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ fɔmɔ nii.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot and spoil quickly when stored inside a hot, enclosed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested yams are still living tubers that breathe; storing them in a hot, unventilated room creates heat and moisture trapped around them, allowing rot fungi to grow quickly.
ga: Yams ni akpa lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo, ni amɛmiimu. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ abɔle amɛhe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ daa oya.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy green growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green leaves and improves crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai eŋɔli lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha tsei lɛ ayibii aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts in the same field as my maize help the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that can pull nitrogen out of the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds the maize without needing extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele masɛi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha abele atsɔsemɔ ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, hot sunlight and burn easily. Keeping or planting shade trees like plantains shields young cocoa plants from heat stress and holds moisture in the soil.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ni amɛshãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ akwɛmɔ loo adumɔ baaye abua ni ebu cocoa tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes through the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu kɛmiitsɔ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds inside the leaves and growing point of maize. Detecting them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or chemical controls prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ baai kɛ ŋmãa hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ amli. Ni aaana amɛ mra Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo tsofai ni akɛbuɔ he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: If I plant my maize seeds closer together, will I harvest more corn?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani makpa ŋmãa babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes crops to fight over sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny cobs. Giving each plant proper spacing allows it to grow larger and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to prop up my yam vines with long bamboo poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ ŋmei tsei kakadaji tsuɔ nii kɛfiɔ ŋmei wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight for their leaves to produce food. Lifting the vines off the ground allows maximum sunlight exposure, which directly helps build large tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛbaai lɛ afee niyenii. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha ená hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tɛ̃ɛ ni afeɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in soggy soil for too long. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rain and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and top-heavy fruit bunches, making them vulnerable to strong winds. Propping the stems up with sturdy wooden sticks or planting them in blocks reduces wind damage.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni wa damɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo odu yɛ blɔki mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping soil moist through regular watering and applying organic mulch keeps roots cool and encourages flowers to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and weak even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from the soil before your crops can absorb them. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your crops receive all the food and water they need.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and fall off during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds and low soil moisture cause extreme water loss. Cocoa trees shed their leaves to conserve moisture and protect themselves from drying out completely during the dry stretch.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo lɛ haa nu fiteɔ babaoo. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he, ni amɛtsi amɛhe gbɛ koni amɛkagbi kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without ever turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed to ensure pollination. Factors like poor insect pollination, dry weather, or lack of soil nutrients cause the tree to shed the excess flowers it cannot support.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ koni amɛkwɛ koni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nibii tamɔ kooloi bibii ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the roots underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are planted too close together, cassava puts its energy into leafy growth above ground instead of storing food in the roots. Proper spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourage tuber growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei baato niyenii yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewalɛ. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ haa tuber lɛ daa.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has become tired and needs fertilizer or a rest period?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ etɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo mi ŋmɔshi nibii loo hejɔɔmɔ?

english: Tired soil shows clear signs such as pale or yellow leaves, stunted plant growth, slow recovery after rain, and lower harvest yields year after year even when the weather is good.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baatsɔɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, tamɔ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. dwarf plant growth Nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ fiofio Ni kpamɔ lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ hi po.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans helps improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have small nodules on their roots containing helpful bacteria. These bacteria pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi ni helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ Helai nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do I see ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ? ni akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. The moths lay eggs on young maize leaves, and the hatched caterpillars eat their way into the plant funnel, requiring early detection and treatment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ni woɔ ŋmãa baa bibii anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ŋmeii ni baa lɛ baaye nii kɛbote tso lɛ gbɛi lɛ amli. Enɛ biɔ ni ana mra ni atsa lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my planted crops right after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in large numbers in the soil and are adapted to sprout rapidly at the slightest moisture, competing for sunlight and soil nutrients before young crops can fully establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui babaoo ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ shishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young suckers growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to compete with the main plant for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers leaves only strong stems that produce larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Kpojiemɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ panicles wuji pɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do I need to clear tall grass and stake my yam vines with sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kakadaji ni madu sweet potato tsei ni niji yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to manufacture food that grows the tuber underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, maximizing light exposure and keeping leaves away from moist soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ́ akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Ha nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni obu baai ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants wither and drop off when the sun gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes heat stress and damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. When pollination fails, the plant naturally sheds the flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa ni efiteɔ pollen ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaaa enyɛŋ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are small black insects eating my stored corn, and where do they come from?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi diji bibii miiye mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ? Ni nɛgbɛ amɛjɛɔ?

english: These are maize weevils. Female weevils often lay tiny eggs inside the corn kernels while the crop is still standing in your field, and once you harvest and bag the corn, those eggs hatch and multiply quickly inside the warm storage.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmãa ŋmeii. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii yei fɔɔ wɔji bibii. yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ nyɛŋmɔji lɛ amli lolo lɛ. Ni kɛ́ okpa ŋmãa lɛ ni okɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ Nakai ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ni eshwereɔ oya yɛ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I stop insects from destroying my maize after I harvest and bag it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa lɛ beni mikpa ni mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You must make sure the corn is completely dried until the grain is hard, clean your storage area of old grains, and use airtight storage bags (like PICS bags) or approved grain-protectant dusts to suffocate any pests.
ga: Osumɔɔ ni okwɛ koni ŋmãa lɛ agbi kwraa kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsumɔ he ni akɛ ŋmaa toɔ momo lɛ. Ni okɛ vacuum storage bag (tamɔ PICS kotoku) loo sũ ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛmu tsɛŋemɔ helai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weevils seem to multiply much faster in my barn during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ oya yɛ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weevils love moisture and warmth. High humidity in the air during the rainy season makes stored corn softer and slightly damp, which creates the perfect conditions for weevils to lay more eggs and hatch faster.
ga: Beetles sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa ni ato lɛ feɔ blɛoo fioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmei lɛ awo wui babaoo ni efɔ oya.

english: Is it safe for my family to eat maize that was treated with pest powder to keep insects away?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ miweku lɛ baaye ŋmãa ni akɛ powda ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi amli lɛ efutu mli koni akɛshwie kooloi?

english: It is safe only if you use approved, food-safe grain protectants recommended by extension officers, observe the required waiting period before eating, and wash or winnow the grain thoroughly before cooking.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe pɛ kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni niyenii he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ko wo he ŋaa lɛ tsu nii. Kwɛmɔ be ni ataoɔ ni akɛmɛ dani aye nii. Ni ofɔ loo ofɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ dani ohoo.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my corn so pests do not attack it in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akatutua ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvest your maize when the leaves turn yellow-brown, the cob husks dry up, and the silk turns completely black; leaving dry corn on the stalk too long exposes it to rain, birds, and field insects.
ga: Kpaa ŋmãa kɛji baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ. Cob bark ni egbi ni siliki lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni egbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaagbala nugbɔ, okpoi kɛ kooloi bibii kɛba ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my corn spoil or attract bugs even after I dry it in the sun for two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ efite loo egbalaa kooloi? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ gbii enyɔ ehi hulu lɛ mli bianɛ moŋ.

english: Two days of sun drying is usually not enough, especially in humid weather. If moisture remains trapped inside the kernel, fungi will grow and insects like weevils will easily bore into the soft grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii enyɔ ni ayeɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ faaa. Titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ehi dumɔwu lɛ mli lolo Fungus baakwɛ̃ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii baabote dumɔwui bibii lɛ amli mlɛo.

english: Can I mix clean wood ash or dried hot pepper with my stored corn to keep bugs away?
