ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tso sũ ni he tse loo chili ni egbi afutu ŋmãa ni ato koni mikɛbu he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe?

english: Yes, mixing clean wood ash or crushed dry pepper with stored grains is a traditional method that deters insects by blocking their breathing pores and making it hard for them to move and lay eggs.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso sũ ni he tse loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ ji kusum gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ kooloi anaa kɛtsɔ amɛmumɔ buji ni tsiɔ amɛnaa lɛ nɔ. Ni enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaafã kɛya ni amɛwo wɔji.

english: How can I test my corn at home to see if it has hidden insects before taking it to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka ŋmãa lɛ makwɛ yɛ shia koni mana kɛji eyɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ dani mikɛba jara nɔ?

english: Place a handful of corn kernels into a bowl of clean water; kernels that have been hollowed out by hidden weevils or larvae will float to the top, while healthy, solid grains will sink.
ga: Okɛ ŋmãa ni mli tse ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ awo nu ni mli tse mli. Dumɔwui ni kooloi loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ tswaa kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Beni dumɔwui ni wa ni he wa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn plants showing big holes and looking chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plants lɛ baai lɛ yɛ buji wuji ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛye lɛ?

english: Holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the green leaves, which weakens the young plant and prevents it from growing strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ, ni no haa tsei bibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ adara waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant the corn seeds I saved from my own harvest from last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds, especially hybrid varieties, lose their natural strength and yield potential over generations, resulting in weaker plants that get attacked more easily by pests and produce smaller cobs.
ga: dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ Titri lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ Efiteɔ ebɔɔ su hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni eyɔɔ lɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛtutuaa amɛ oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why are the seeds I planted not coming out of the soil at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if they were damaged, old, planted too deep in the soil, or if the soil was too dry or flooded with too much water.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛfite, amɛgbɔ, loo adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ

english: How can I tell if the crop seeds I am buying from the seller are high quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ nihɔɔlɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good quality seeds are usually uniform in size, free from holes or mold, and come in sealed packages from certified agricultural dealers rather than open bags at food markets.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe. Ebɛ bu loo ŋmɔtɔ. ni ebaa yɛ tsɔnei ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbele kotokui yɛ niyenii ajarayelihe lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize grain bought from the food market instead of proper planting seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ niyenii ajarayelihe lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Food market grain is meant for eating and often lacks the strong growth traits, disease resistance, and high germination rates of properly treated planting seeds.
ga: Afee ŋmaa ni yɔɔ niyenii jarayelihe lɛ koni aye ni bei pii lɛ, ebɛ dalɛ sui ni mli wa. Helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai kɛ dumɔwui ni adu jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni fa babaoo.

english: How should I store my leftover seeds at home so they do not spoil before the next season?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ ato shia koni amɛkafite dani be ni baa lɛ aba?

english: Store your seeds in clean, airtight containers in a cool, dry place off the ground to protect them from moisture, heat, and insect attacks.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui awo tsɛnsi ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ, dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi srɔtoi ahe.

english: Is it safe for me to bring crop seeds from my home village in another region to plant here?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maŋɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ mimaŋ akrowa ni yɔɔ kpokpaa kroko nɔ lɛ mli ni madu yɛ biɛ?

english: Seeds from another region may not grow well because they are used to different weather and soil, and they can also introduce new pests or diseases to your farm.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ edaŋ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ bɔ ni amɛle kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ lɛ. Ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ kooloi loo helai heei hu aba. baanyɛ aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Can I still plant seeds that I bought two years ago and kept in my house?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui ni mihe afii enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ lolo ni mikɛto shĩa?

english: Seeds lose their vigor over time, so older seeds will have low germination rates, sprout weakly, or fail to grow completely.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli, no hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui ni eda lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ fioo, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ fioo, loo amɛdaraaa kwraa.

english: Does it matter how deep I push my seeds into the soil when planting?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ mihaa beni miduɔ nii lɛ he hiaa mi?

english: Yes, planting seeds too deep makes them exhaust their food reserves before reaching light, while planting them too shallow exposes them to sun damage and birds.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baaha niyenii ni ato lɛ afite dani amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ okpoi aná amɛ.

english: Will pouring a lot of water on my newly planted seeds make them sprout faster?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ni oooha amɛ nu lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: No, excessive water deprives the seeds of air in the soil, causing them to rot underground before they can sprout.
ga: Dabi, nu babaoo baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How can I test my seeds to know if they will sprout before planting them on my big farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka midumɔwui lɛ makwɛ kɛji amɛbaakwɛ̃ dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ agbo lɛ mli?

english: Place ten sample seeds on a damp cloth in a warm place for a few days; if at least eight sprout, your seeds are healthy and good for planting.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui 10 ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ awo mama ni mli efɔ nɔ. yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ gbii fioo komɛi Kɛji kɛ hoo lɛ tsei kpaanyɔ kwɛ̃ Odumɔwui lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni amɛhi kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why are insects eating my seeds underground before the plants can even grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye midumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ adara lɛ?

english: Soil pests are attracted to the nutrients inside soft, moist seeds, which is why seeds are often treated with safe protective chemicals before planting.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli efɔ lɛ amli lɛ gbalaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi. Enɛ hewɔ ni bei pii lɛ akɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsuɔ dumɔwui ahe nii dani aduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well as soon as the rain stops in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpaa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ Ghana pɛ?

english: Crops rely on steady soil moisture to absorb nutrients from the earth. Once the rainy season ends and the soil dries out, plants cannot take up food properly, causing their growth to slow down or stop completely.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ Tsei nyɛɛɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ. ni haa dalɛ baa shi loo ekpaa kwraa

english: How much water do my bean plants actually need to produce good pods?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa mi-bean tso lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii kpakpai?

english: Bean plants need continuous moisture, especially when they start flowering and forming pods. If they don't get enough water during pod formation, the pods will be small, flat, or empty.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ eje fɔfɔii ashishi ni efee pods. Kɛji akɛ anáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni afeɔ pod lɛ, pod lɛ baafee bibioo, ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why are my bean pods small and empty when the weather gets dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea pods lɛ feɔ bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ?

english: When the soil loses moisture, bean plants don't have enough water energy to fill the seeds inside the pod, so the plant leaves the pods empty to save its own life.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fite lɛ Bean tsei lɛ bɛ nu hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ dumɔwui awoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shiɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ efolo koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Can giving my crops too much water hurt them just as badly as a drought?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ awui tamɔ hɔmɔ hu?

english: Yes, too much water drowns the roots by filling all the tiny air spaces in the soil. Without air, the roots begin to rot and the leaves turn yellow, making the crop look sick.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ ni baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ lɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds late, near the end of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ sɛɛ mli beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Crops planted late won't have enough time to grow deep roots before the dry season starts. Once the rains stop, their shallow roots dry up quickly and the crop will wilt before harvest.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ bɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani akpaa.

english: Why do crops planted right at the start of the first rain yield better than late ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa yibii kpakpai fe be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Early planting gives crops full access to weeks of natural rain, allowing them to establish strong root systems and healthy stems before dry weather sets in.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ehaa tsei lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ otsii babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ baa.

english: Why is it difficult for me to grow crops during the dry season without an irrigation pump?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa mi akɛ makwɛ tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni nu pɔmp bɛ mihe lɛ?

english: Most farming in Ghana depends entirely on rain to moisten the soil. In the dry season, the hot sun evaporates groundwater, so crops cannot survive on dry earth alone without added water.
ga: Okwaayeli nitsumɔi babaoo ni yaa nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ damɔ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ nu fataaa he lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi pɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm crops are suffering from lack of water before they completely die?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu efo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli dani amɛgboi kwraa?

english: Plants show early stress by curling or dropping their leaves during the hottest part of the day, looking dull green instead of bright green, or dropping their young flowers.
ga: Tsei jieɔ haomɔ kpo mra kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe eŋɔli ni mli tse. loo eha fɔfɔi bibii lɛ agbo

english: Is it better to give my crops a little water every day or a lot of water once a week?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nu fioo daa gbi loo nu babaoo shikome yɛ otsi mli?

english: Watering deeply less often is better because it forces roots to grow deep into the soil searching for water, making the plant stronger during dry days than shallow daily watering.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fioo lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ enyɛɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao nu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli waa yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli fe kɛji akɛ afɔ lɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ daa gbi.

english: How can I keep moisture in the soil longer so my crops don't dry out so fast?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi oya nɛkɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your plants with dried grass or leaves (mulching) shades the soil from the hot sun, preventing water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ, ni okɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help them regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller crop yields when I plant maize on the exact same land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ baa beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot continuously exhausts specific nutrients from the soil and builds up pests. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nutrients back into the soil and restores crop yields.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ be fɛɛ be ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when heavy rains fall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because they cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my tomato plants dry up and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop lower leaves during dry heat to save water for their survival and upper stems. Mulching around the roots with dry grass helps hold moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛshishi baai lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛha wala kɛ ŋwɛi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the plant sap and spread plant diseases. Spraying neem seed water or recommended insecticides keeps these insects away so leaves stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tso helai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ ohe. Koni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small flowers before any pods start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani pods lɛ baaje shishi eda?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, lack of moisture, or insect attacks like mirids. Maintaining good shade trees and protecting the farm from sucking insects helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Fɛ̃i ni bɛ loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ, tamɔ hulu la. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni abu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni nuɔ amɛ lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and provide living shade umbrellas that keep the seedlings cool and moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛhaa hulutsoo ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe jɔɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and bigger than my crops even when they start growing at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya ni amɛdara fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛbɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to steal water, light, and soil food faster than crops can. Clearing weeds early in the first few weeks gives your crops the space and food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsɔ amɛhe ni amɛju nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni tsei baanyɛ afee. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when they start producing large bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ebɔi yibii babaoo womɔ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, making the tree top-heavy when a big bunch grows. Supporting the main stem with sturdy bamboo forks or wooden poles prevents strong winds from pushing them down.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ tsiimɔ kɛji aja mli awo kui wuji amli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fĩ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekatswa lɛ shi.

english: Why do some of my planted yam seed tubers take a very long time to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural sleeping period called dormancy after harvest. Storing seed yams in a cool, dry place until small buds naturally appear ensures they will sprout quickly once put into the soil.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔ be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi kɛyashi ŋmeii bibii baaje kpo. Bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Can diseases on my crops make my family or me sick if we touch or eat them?
ga: Ani hela ko ni yɔɔ midumɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ baaha miweku lɛ loo mihe afee shoo kɛji wɔta he loo wɔye?

english: Yes, certain plant diseases, especially molds like aflatoxins on maize and groundnuts, produce toxins that can cause severe stomach illnesses or long-term health issues in humans if consumed.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai komɛi Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ aflatoxins ni yɔɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ ahe. Ejieɔ tsofai fɔji ni baanyɛ aha mɔ aná musu hela ni naa wa. loo gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ he naagbai ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ adesai amli kɛji akɛ aye

english: How do crop diseases spread from one side of my farm to another so quickly?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome kɛyaa fã kroko lɛ nɔ?

english: Diseases travel through invisible fungi spores or bacteria carried by wind, splashing rain, insects, or even on your boots, cutlasses, and clothing as you work through the fields.
ga: Helai tsɔɔ ŋmeii loo helai ni anaaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛbaa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ o-boots, o-daggers, kɛ otadei po anɔ beni otsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Is it safe to harvest and eat my vegetables immediately after spraying them with agrochemicals?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makpa mi-aduawai lɛ ni maye amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ agrochemicals efɔ amɛnɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, every chemical has a specific waiting period before harvest. Eating crops too soon after spraying leaves toxic chemical residues that can make you and your customers very sick.
ga: Dabi, tsofai fɛɛ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛmɛɔ dani akpaa amɛ. Kɛ́ oye ŋmɔshi nibii mra tsɔ beni okɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ, eshiɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni baanyɛ aha bo kɛ mɛi ni baahe nii yɛ odɛŋ lɛ aná hela ni naa wa.

english: Why do you advise me to dig up and burn sick crops instead of leaving them in the soil to rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli ni mashã amɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛgboi lɛ?

english: Leaving diseased plants in the farm allows the germs to hide in the soil or plant debris, where they will multiply and attack your healthy crops in the next planting season.
ga: Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa helatsɛ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ loo tsei amli sũ mli. Amɛbaafee babaoo ni amɛbaatutua onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is starving for key nutrients like nitrogen, or the ground is so waterlogged that the roots cannot breathe and absorb food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛmɔmɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before growing any actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by sudden heat, insufficient water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, causing the plant to save energy instead of fruiting.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo bɛ Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ toɔ yibii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my farm at the same exact time every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Insects follow natural seasonal cycles timed with the weather; pests hatch during the rains when young, tender leaves are abundant for their offspring to feed on.
ga: Kplukai nyiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli be mli nibii ni damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ́ baai lɛ tsɔ bibii ni amɛdara lɛ, niyenii babaoo baahi shi ni seshibii lɛ baaye.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn black and rot underground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa?

english: Cassava root rot is caused by water-loving fungi in heavy or poorly drained soil, especially when infected stem cuttings are planted during heavy rainy periods.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fitemɔ jɛɔ ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn powdery and get full of tiny holes in the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ tsɔɔ ashikishaŋ ni eyɛ bu bibii yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils bore into the grain to lay eggs; if maize is stored before drying completely or without proper protection, these insects multiply and destroy the harvest.
ga: Picker kooloi tamɔ weevils shwieɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli koni amɛwo ŋmeii. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa to dani egbi kwraa loo abuuu he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baafa babaoo ni amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do some varieties of crops survive dry spells better than others on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yeɔ wala yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Drought-hardy varieties have deeper root systems that pull water from far below the surface, as well as leaf features that prevent moisture from evaporating too quickly in the hot sun.
ga: Tsoi srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Nakai eji yɛ baai lɛ ahe nibii ni tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, a vital nutrient in the soil. When soil loses nutrients from continuous farming, the plants cannot make food properly, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow starting from the tips.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli. Tsei nyɛŋ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ naagbee.

english: How does applying fertilizer actually help my crops grow bigger and yield more?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for your plants by restoring essential nutrients—like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium—that crops take out of the soil. When plants get these missing nutrients, they build stronger roots, bigger leaves, and more fruit.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa otsei lɛ kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium ni ekɛbaa ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei gbalaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ tsei lɛ ná niyenii ni elaaje lɛ Amɛbaawo shishifãi ni wa, baai wuji kɛ aduawai babaoo.

english: Why does my farm land dry out so fast just two days after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Bare soil exposes moisture directly to the hot sun, causing it to evaporate quickly. Covering the soil with dried leaves or grass (mulching) or adding manure acts like a sponge, holding rainwater in the dirt so plant roots can drink over a longer period.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. evaporate quickly Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulching) loo ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they get stressed, usually due to extreme afternoon heat or erratic watering. If the plant feels it lacks water or energy to sustain a full fruit, it sheds the flower to protect itself.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ shwane mli loo nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛji tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ebɛ nu loo hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ eyibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebaafɔse efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu ehe.

english: Why are my cassava roots remaining thin like sticks instead of swelling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ moŋ fe ni eeefu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot expand if the soil is packed too hard or lacks potassium. Soft, well-loosened soil allows the tuber roots to push outward easily, while good soil nutrients provide the energy needed to store starch inside the root.
ga: Kasava shishifãi nyɛŋ alɛɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa bulb lɛ shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, sũ mli niyenii kpakpai haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛto ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bent and twisted instead of smooth and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downward by pushing through the soil. If the ground is hard, rocky, or filled with uncleared tree roots, the tuber is forced to bend around these obstacles as it expands.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyaa shi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo tsei shishifãi ni bɛ faŋŋ eyi mli obɔ lɛ, anyɛɔ yitso lɛ nɔ ni ebɔleɔ gbɛtsii nibii nɛɛ ahe beni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that spread sideways near the top of the ground rather than digging deep into the dirt. When the fruit bunch gets heavy, the top-heavy weight easily pulls the roots out of wet, soft soil during high winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa sɛɛgbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ Muji ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ gbalaa shishifãi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into tight cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ kɔɔpoo ni mli wa ni ekpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites underneath the leaves. As they suck the sap, they damage the leaf cells and can spread viruses that cause the plant leaves to deform and stunt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. be mli ni amɛnuɔ mliki lɛ Efiteɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli wala yibii ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni fiteɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ni ehaa amɛhe feɔ shoo lɛ eshwa.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal disease that thrives in wet, overly shaded farms. During the rainy season, water drops splash the fungus from the ground or infected leaves onto the pods, where high humidity allows it to spread rapidly.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, nu mli ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo ni haa ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally adapted to the local environment and can lie dormant in the soil for years. When rain falls, these native seeds sprout immediately and suck up available water and nutrients much faster than introduced farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nɛkɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ dumɔwui nɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛba lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves whatever food it has to the new leaves at the top, leaving the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and wither.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny bumps on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the plants die, this nitrogen stays in the dirt as free fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa tso fɛɛ tso ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants stretch upward to compete for sunlight while fighting each other for nutrients and water in the soil. Because no single plant gets enough food, they grow thin and weak and cannot produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shwereɔ koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ amɛteŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛkɛ lɛ tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ. ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba

english: If too many young shoots grow around the main plantain trunk, they steal water and nutrients from the main tree. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the main plant gets enough food to grow big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain tso wulu lɛ he lɛ Ebaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ aba ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to clear small trees to plant cocoa, but still keep some big trees on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie tsei bibii ni akɛdu kookoo shi tsei wuji ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun and need tall shade trees to protect them from harsh heat and strong winds. However, too many shade trees block sunlight completely, so keeping just a few big trees gives the cocoa the right balance of shade and sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei kakadaji ni baaha amɛná hɔnɔ ni baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Shi kɛlɛ, hulutsoo be babaoo baanyɛ atsĩ hulu lɛ naa kwraa, no hewɔ lɛ tsei wuji fioo komɛi pɛ ni Cocoa yɔɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo be kɛ hulu la lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch enough sunlight to make food for growing tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off wet soil, preventing diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking hu woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ koni helai akatutua baai lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under the leaves and suck out the plant's juices. This insect damage causes the young leaves to grow deformed and twisted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ sito tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloo nɛɛ fiteɔ lɛ haa baai bibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhe feɔ shoo.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by dry weather, poor soil moisture, or insect attacks. If tiny insects do not pollinate the flowers or if the tree lacks water, it sheds the flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao tso lɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo kooloi tutuamɔ Kɛji kooloi bibii Kaawo fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ loo kaaaha tsei amli nu akafee nɔ ko. Amɛbaashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the blossom ends of my growing tomatoes turning black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni miduɔ lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit while it forms, usually due to irregular watering. When soil moisture goes up and down, the plant cannot move calcium from the soil into the developing tomato.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni efeɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tee hiɛ ni eba shi lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya tomato ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are ready to harvest since I cannot see them under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ejaakɛ anaaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves of the plant turn yellow and fall off, leaving a cluster of green leaves at the top, and the main stem turns dark greyish-brown. This usually happens around 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi baai eŋɔli kuu ko yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. ni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Can using dirty tools on my crops cause them to catch bad diseases?
ga: Ani nibii ni he tseee ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba?

english: Yes, farming tools like cutlasses and pruning shears can carry fungi and bacteria from infected plants to healthy ones. Cleaning your tools after working on sick crops prevents diseases from spreading across your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli nibii tamɔ dadei kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Kɛ́ otsumɔ odɛŋdadei lɛ amli beni okɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops get sick even when I give them enough water and fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Plants can still get sick if they are planted too close together or if improper handling harms their stems. Poor airflow and tiny wounds on the plant give fungal and bacterial diseases an easy path to enter and grow.
ga: Tsei hu baanyɛ aná hela kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ akɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ awui. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ pilamɔi bibii Yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ abote mli ni amɛdara oya.

english: What is the best way to keep a crop disease from destroying my whole field?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ atsĩ tsei ahe helai anaa koni amɛkafite miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: The best way is to spot sick plants early, remove and burn them away from the farm, use clean planting materials, and avoid working in wet fields where diseases spread easily on your clothes and tools.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooona tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Jiemɔ amɛ ni oshã amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ dumɔ nibii ni he tse atsu nii. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ nitsumɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã otadei kɛ onitsumɔ dadei anɔ oya lɛ amli.

english: What is the benefit of planting fast-maturing crops like 'amankwaatia' varieties on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ‘amankwatia’ ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Fast-maturing crop varieties reach harvest time quickly, allowing you to produce food and earn income faster while escaping severe late-season dry spells and pest outbreaks.
ga: Akpaa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni ofeɔ niyenii ni onáa shika oya. yɛ be mli ni etsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ be lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa ni baa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ hu he.

english: Why do some crop varieties handle diseases better than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ helai ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Some crop varieties are bred with natural defenses that help them resist common local pests and diseases, while older or unselected seeds easily fall sick under bad weather or poor soil conditions.
ga: Akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni egbɔ loo ni ahalaaa lɛ hela mɔ amɛ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii shishi.

english: How can I protect my crops from diseases if I don't have enough time to spend on my farm every day?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe? Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaatsu okwaayeli daa gbi hu?

english: You can save time by spacing your crops correctly during planting and using clean, disease-free seeds. Proper setup reduces the need for constant spraying and doctoring later in the season.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ be ato kɛtsɔ tsei ni oookɛ amɛ aaabɔ he jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni oduɔ nii lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ni oookɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ daa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I delay weeding because I am busy with other farm work?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ shwie shi ejaakɛ mikɛ mihe ewo ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi krokomɛi amli?

english: When weeds stay too long, they steal water, light, and nutrients from your crops. Weakened crops become easy targets for diseases and insect attacks, which drastically reduces your final yield.
ga: Kɛ́ jwɛi hi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nibii ni aduɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ bafeɔ hei ni helai kɛ kooloi tutuaa amɛ oya. Enɛ baaha onaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi waa.

english: How can I tell if my crop is suffering from a disease or just lacks water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii loo nu efo mli?

english: A thirsty plant will wilt during hot hours and recover when watered or in the evening. A diseased plant often shows dark spots, yellow patches, rotting stems, or wilting that does not improve after rain.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ gboɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni ebaatsa kɛji akɛ afɔ lɛ nu loo gbɛkɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji. Ayɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. tso ni egbo loo ŋmɔtɔ ni eyaaa hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do crop stems rot in the ground shortly after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stems rot when planted in waterlogged soil without proper drainage or when contaminated planting cuttings are used. Fungi in wet soil attack the soft cut ends before the plant can form roots.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ loo kɛ akɛ tsei ni mli ewo muji tsu nii. Fung ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii bibii ni afoɔ lɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow and dropping before the harvest period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Early yellowing is usually a sign of nutrient deficiency in the soil, root damage caused by pests, or a fungal infection preventing the plant from drawing up food and water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni baa mra lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Shishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu ato lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods growing large while others on the same tree turn yellow and shrivel up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ ekomɛi daraa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ lɛ?

english: When a tree carries more pods than its roots can supply with water and nutrients, it naturally sacrifices the younger pods—a process called cherelle wilt—to save energy for the healthier, mature ones.
ga: Beni tso ko yɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe shishifãi ni baanyɛ aha nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Taakɛ eji lɛ, ekɛ pods ni darako lɛ shaa afɔle. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherel wilt. Koni akɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves that form a 'V' shape at the tips usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed its newer top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ‘V’ yɔɔ amɛhe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛyaha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without producing any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: High temperatures and dry air dry out the pollen inside the flowers, preventing pollination. When a flower is not pollinated, the plant sheds it to conserve moisture.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ. Tsi pollination naa Kɛji fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ pollination Tsei jieɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and skinny with very few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete for limited sunlight by growing tall quickly rather than branching out. Less branching means fewer flower sites and fewer peppers.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa ni amɛyaa oya yɛ niji ni amɛaaje kpo lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ. Niji ni faaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔfɔi jɛɛhei fioo kɛ ŋmeii fioo.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into narrow tubes during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, which traps moisture and keeps the plant from drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ba hulu la ni shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso lɛ mli ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbi.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees get brown spots and drop off during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain and cool, humid air allow fungal diseases like Black Pod to spread quickly through water splashes from the soil and neighboring leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ baai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli ni ashwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, cracks form in the soil around the base of the plant, and the main stems turn light brown.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Gbɛjegbɛi jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. ni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen and turn soft so quickly before I can get them to the buyers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya dani eshɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains release a natural gas called ethylene after harvest. Direct heat, bright sunlight, and physical bruising make the crop release more gas, speeding up the ripening process.
ga: Feemɔ ekãa ni ojie adebɔɔ mli la ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ fãji haa ŋmɔshi nibii jieɔ gas babaoo kpo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ oya.

english: Why is it necessary to ferment cocoa beans for several days instead of drying them immediately after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ afeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ gbii babaoo moŋ fe ni aaaha amɛgbi kɛji akpa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fermentation kills the bean seed to stop it from sprouting and triggers the essential chemical reaction needed to develop the true chocolate flavor and rich brown color desired by buyers.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ehaa tsofai ni he hiaa koni aná anɔkwa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ su ni mli kwɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains rot or turn moldy when stored in sacks inside my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ akɛto kotokui amli yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: If maize is packaged before it is fully dried, the trapped moisture creates a warm, damp environment that allows mold spores and fungi to grow rapidly inside the sack.
ga: Kɛji akɛ awo ŋmãa lɛ mli dani egbi kwraa Fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ daa oya yɛ kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide essential shade and keep the soil cool while the cocoa plants mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rains and winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not sink deep into the ground. When heavy rain softens the soil and the fruit bunch grows heavy, wind can easily pull the roots out of the earth.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni aduawai akui lɛ feɔ shwiili. Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ajie shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to make green leaves. Adding fertilizer or animal manure restores this nitrogen to the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves of my maize and eating holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mli lɛ?

english: These pests are Fall Armyworms. They target the tender inner leaves of maize plants, and controlling them early with safe treatments protects the plant's growing point.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms. Amɛtutuaa ŋmãa tsei amli baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. kɛ amɛhe nɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ tsofafeemɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe nɔ lɛ ebuɔ tso lɛ dalɛ hei lɛ ahe.

english: When heavy rain creates standing water around cassava roots, it starves the roots of air and allows soil fungi to breed, which causes the tubers to decay.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ he fɛɛ he. cassava root Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. ni oha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afɔ ni haa yitso lɛ fiteɔ

english: Why do I need to put long sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei kakadaji lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on sticks so their leaves can catch direct sunlight. Leaves use sunshine to make food, which travels down to swell the underground tuber.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and turning small and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaves, which can also spread plant viruses that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ hu baanyɛ agbɛ tsei amli helai ni tsiɔ amɛdalɛ naa lɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my tomato flowers drying up and dropping off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when the soil lacks nutrients, preventing the flower from successfully forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, which feeds the soil and helps nearby crops like maize grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele, ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why is it harmful to plant the exact same crop on the same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ abaadu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain plants grow fast and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and retain soil moisture, protecting the young cocoa trees until they grow stronger.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: Planting cassava on raised mounds loosens the earth so the roots can expand easily into large tubers. It also prevents heavy rainwater from pooling around the roots and rotting them.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ bulbs agboi. Ehaa nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves off the ground toward sunlight. Exposure to sunlight helps the leaves make food, which travels down to grow bigger and healthier tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant moves available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves and young corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during hot afternoons to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and hold onto water. If they recover in the cooler evening, the plant is simply protecting itself from heat stress.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛ nu ahi mli. Kɛji amɛhe wa amɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛmiijɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛkɛ.

english: Pepper plants often drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when they receive unpredictable amounts of water. The plant sheds flowers to save energy and protect itself during times of stress.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛná nu babaoo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe yɛ haomɔ bei amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same spot exhausts the same soil nutrients every season and allows maize pests to multiply in the soil. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans helps rebuild soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa shi daa be. ni ehaa ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ saa ehe yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does spreading dry leaves around the base of my plants help keep the soil moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves creates a protective blanket called mulch. This layer blocks direct sunlight from drying out the ground, keeps the soil cool, and slows down water evaporation.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi blɛoo

english: Why do my cowpea crops stay green even when there has been no rain for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko otsii babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have deep root systems that reach far down into the earth to draw hidden underground water. They are naturally adapted to dry conditions and use water very efficiently.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ejie shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. Amɛhe yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛkɛ nu tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa.

english: Why do black spots appear on my cocoa pods when the rainy season is very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ ŋmɔji diji yɔɔ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa lɛ?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods during wet periods are usually black pod disease, caused by a water-loving fungus. The high humidity and splashing rain spread fungal spores easily from pod to pod.
ga: Nibii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii diji hela ji no. Fungi ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ kɛbaa Fungi ni mli edɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ gbɛɔ fungal spores lɛ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and tender roots that burn easily under intense heat. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to shield them from direct sunlight and keep the soil moist while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ amɛyiteŋ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines that need to lift their leaves off the damp ground to reach sunlight and avoid soil-borne fungal diseases. Climbing allows the leaves to trap solar energy, which the plant uses to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni shwieɔ shi ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ hulu hewalɛ. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: If too many sucker shoots grow at the base, they steal water and food from the main plant. Trimming away extra suckers leaves only the main stalk and one strong replacement shoot, ensuring you get large, healthy bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tso titri lɛ kɛ tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ. Enɛ baaha onine ashɛ plantains wuji ni mli wa nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plants lack nitrogen, a essential nutrient needed to make food and grow strong leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha niyenii feemɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akwɛɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting beans or groundnuts together with maize helps the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that can trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. Maize planted nearby feeds on this extra nutrient, making the soil richer without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsake lɛ efee tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaye niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa nɛɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why should I apply my fertilizer only when the soil is wet after a rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can draw it up safely. Applying dry fertilizer to dry soil can burn and destroy the plant roots or cause the fertilizer to wash away as dust before the crop can use it.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ajie lɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ sũ dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars chewing holes into the leaf center of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ŋmɔɔ bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the central growing funnel of corn plants to eat tender foliage. Catching them early and applying approved insecticides or ash mixes prevents them from ruining the stalk before ears form.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo sũ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ atsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ shishi dani toi lɛ adara.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem before growing into actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani amɛmiitsɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. When soil dries out too quickly or temperatures rise too high, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy and save itself from dying.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya tsɔ loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhere amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele mli.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my farm reduce the final harvest of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa minaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal sunlight, soil moisture, and plant nutrients directly from your crop roots. Keeping the farm clear of weeds ensures all the water and soil goodness goes straight into growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. shikpɔŋ mli nu kɛ tso mli niyenii ni jɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa nu kpakpa kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa yaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn to dust and get small holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ sũ ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Insects called weevils burrow inside dry maize kernels to lay eggs and feed on the inner food store. Drying maize thoroughly and storing it in airtight bags or treating it with storage dust keeps these insects out.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli koni amɛwo ŋmãa ni amɛye niyenii ni ato yɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo okɛ sũ awo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Why does my farm soil dry out so quickly after I clear away all the weeds and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clearing all plant cover exposes the bare soil directly to the hot sun, causing moisture to evaporate rapidly. Leaving dead leaves as mulch keeps the soil cool, retains water, and feeds beneficial organisms.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ aná hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya Eshiɔ baai ni egboi akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa nu hiɔ shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or farmyard manure helps the plant build strong green leaves again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight during their first couple of years. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby creates living umbrellas that shelter the young cocoa from harsh sun and retain soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same piece of land without them competing?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe akaŋ akaŋ?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving the field clear for the slower-growing cassava to expand later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Ha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ afee faŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ anyɛ afɔ sɛɛ mli.

english: What is eating small ragged holes into my young maize leaves, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni ji nakai buji bibii ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli lɛ ayeli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the center of the plant. Applying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening targets the caterpillars when they come out to feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ekɛ ehiɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛje kpo amɛmiitao niyenii.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up with yellow patches and producing small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Yellow ni eyɛ shishifãi bibii?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or spread by using infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension agents prevents this issue.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my previous hybrid maize harvest produce smaller yields when planted again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds lose their high-yielding strength in the second generation. To get maximum yields every season, it is best to buy fresh certified seeds rather than recycling harvested grains.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ ni haa yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni oná yibii babaoo yɛ be fɛɛ mli Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ dumɔwui ni akpa momo lɛ baatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to sow my seeds at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should wait until two or three heavy rains have soaked deep into the ground. Sowing seeds into soil that is dry just below the surface causes seeds to rot or sprout and die early.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow big leaves but very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ baai dara shi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants put all their energy into leaves instead of fruit. Pruning extra side shoots and using balanced fertilizers encourages plants to produce flowers and tomatoes.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ aduawai lɛ najiaŋ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛbaakpa tso lɛ he kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ awo fɔfɔi kɛ tomato.

english: How can I get improved crop seeds and planting methods developed by agricultural university researchers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii ni okwaayeli he yunivɛsiti mli niiamlitaolɔi lɛ fee lɛ?

english: Agricultural extension officers work directly with university researchers to bring tested seeds and modern techniques to local farmers. You can request these improved varieties through your district extension office.
ga: Okwaafoi agbɛjianɔtoo he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ univɛsiti niiamlitaolɔi tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkɛ dumɔwui ni aka amɛ akwɛ kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai aba maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi lɛ aŋɔɔ. Obaanyɛ obi nɛkɛ tsofai srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ kɛtsɔ okpokpaa nɔ nitsumɔhe ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when the soil becomes hard and heavy like clay after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni etsii tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy clay soil holds a lot of water and becomes sticky when wet, then bakes hard when dry. This suffocates plant roots by cutting off air and making it hard for roots to expand. Adding compost or well-rotted manure softens clay soil and improves drainage.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ sũ fee lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo. ni ekpɛtɛɔ he kɛji edɔ ni ewaa kɛji egbi Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee blɛoo, ni ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do older farmers cover the soil around their yam mounds with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko kɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle e-sweet potatoes ni ekɛto lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from direct heat, keeps the soil cool and moist, reduces water evaporation, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni otsi jwɛi ni shwereɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight and intense heat. Leaving mature trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides shade and retains ground moisture, acting as a shield for young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni eda lɛ ni ajieɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko kwraa lolo?

english: During extreme heat, leaves lose water faster through evaporation than the roots can pull from the ground. Drooping or curling leaves is the plant's natural way of reducing leaf surface area exposed to the sun to conserve water until evening.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni shwieɔ shi loo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebaa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni ekɛto nu he kɛyashi fɛ̃i baa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or decomposed animal manure restores nutrient levels and turns leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmei ni efite fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Will removing the lower branches and extra shoots from my pepper plants give me better fruit?
ga: Ani niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni jɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ mli lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha maná aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, trimming weak lower branches and extra non-fruiting shoots allows the plant to redirect its energy, water, and soil nutrients into growing larger, healthier peppers.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afolɔ kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni wooo yibii lɛ haa tso lɛ tsakeɔ hewalɛ, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Will planting my crops very close together help me get a bigger harvest from my small farm?
ga: Tsei ni mikwɛɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaye abua mi ni makpa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: No, planting too close forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed and grow full, heavy produce.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ abɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can dry out and kill freshly germinated seeds. Waiting until the rains become regular ensures young plants have steady moisture to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ amɛmɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ aná nu ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛhi shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees. Keeping soil moisture consistent and avoiding over-use of harsh chemicals helps protect flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my vegetable leaves during the humid wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: White spots are usually caused by fungal diseases that thrive in warm, humid air with poor wind circulation. Giving plants proper distance from each other and watering the soil instead of the leaves reduces fungus growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa, ni okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni oooha amɛ nu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why am I getting only three bags of cocoa from my farm while other farmers get over fifteen bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛ kookoo kotokui etɛ pɛ nɔ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, okwaafoi krokomɛi hu nine shɛ kookoo kotokui ni fa fe nyɔŋma kɛ enumɔ nɔ.
