english: Low yields usually happen when trees do not get enough nutrients, are overcrowded, or are damaged by pests and shade issues. By properly pruning trees, applying the right fertilizer, and clearing weeds, your farm can produce significantly more pods on the same acreage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpa, amɛyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii kɛ hulutsoo naagbai efite amɛ. Kɛtsɔ tsei ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa awo mli ni ojie jwɛi Oŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Flowers also need tiny insects called midges to pollinate them, which require moist organic litter on the soil floor to breed and do their work.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ latsaa he, nu bɛ mli, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii kpakpai bɛ mli. Fɔfɔi hu he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli. Enɛ biɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni enyɛ efɔ ni etsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa provides living shade that cools the plants and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe. Ehaa hɔɔŋ ni haa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do agricultural officers keep telling me to cut off branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafolɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ aniji lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-productive branches that steal nutrients from the main trunk. Opening up the canopy lets sunlight in and lowers humidity, which prevents destructive fungal diseases from growing on your pods.
ga: Niji ni wooo yibii ni juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ niji lɛ. Kɛ́ agbele ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa lɛ, hulu la boteɔ mli ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akakwɛ̃ yɛ o-pods lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and rot before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: This rot is called Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, overly dark, and damp farm conditions. Keeping weeds low, pruning excess tree branches, and removing affected pods quickly stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ akɛ blackpod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, duŋ tsɔ, kɛ hei ni efɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Ni aaaha jwɛi lɛ ahi shi Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ Kɛ ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ oya lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know if my soil is tired and needs fertilizer to help my crops grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Tired soil shows in slow tree growth, small yellowing leaves, and a declining harvest each season. Adding organic compost or recommended fertilizers restores vital nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus back to the land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ miida blɛoo. baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer pods than they used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo fe afii komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past twenty years, their internal transport systems slow down and they become weaker. Rejuvenating old farms by grafting improved branches onto old trunks or replanting with high-yielding varieties restores full production.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tso ko ye afii 20 lɛ, gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ emli lɛ baa shi ni egbɔjɔɔ. Gbɛjegbɛi momoi ni abaaku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni asaa amɛhe lɛ ni akɛaawo tsei momo lɛ anɔ loo ni akɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo baadu ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo aba jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does letting weeds grow tall under my crops reduce my final harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mihaa amɛdaraa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ashishi lɛ haa minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. They also hide harmful insects like capsids (mirids) that bite young cocoa shoots and destroy pod development.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids (mirids) ni ŋmɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni fiteɔ pod lɛ shweremɔ lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods shrivel and dry up on the branch during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So mine lɛ gboɔ ni egbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Dry Harmattan winds suck moisture out of tree leaves faster than roots can draw water from dry soil. Leaving cut leaves as mulch around the base of the trees traps soil moisture and protects roots during dry spells.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi baai ni afo lɛ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: What is the benefit of buying hybrid seedlings from research institutions instead of planting seeds from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ ahemɔ he kɛjɛ niiamlitaomɔ he ko moŋ fe ni ooodu dumɔwui kɛjɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli?

english: Hybrid seedlings developed by agricultural researchers are bred to start bearing fruit in just two to three years instead of five, resist local diseases better, and naturally yield many more pods per tree.
ga: Atsɔse dumɔwui ni akɛfee tsofai ni okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi fee lɛ koni amɛje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ mli, shi jeee afii enumɔ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔi babaoo baa tso kome nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my tomato plants with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops after the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants naturally adapted to the soil, so they absorb nutrients and water much faster than cultivated seeds. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ niyenii kɛ nu oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or that the soil is overly waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli tsɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight for their leaves. More sunlight helps the plant manufacture energy, which directly feeds the big yam tuber growing under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava stem cuttings when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava niji lɛ abɔ he shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ miidu nii?

english: Planting cassava cuttings about one meter apart gives each root enough space to expand into large tubers and ensures the leaves do not fight each other for sunlight.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei niji ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa shishifã fɛɛ shishifã naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ ŋmei agbo. ni etsĩɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la.

english: What causes small holes in my young corn leaves with small caterpillars hidden inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ. ni akɛtee mli

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. They feed inside the central leaves of young corn, and identifying them early allows you to apply recommended treatments before they ruin the harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji Fall Armyworm lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa, ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe baai. kɛ amɛyoomɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii lɛ tsuɔ nii dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmaa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and stopping the fruits from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by extreme heat and uneven watering stress, which stops the plant from growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to build up and ruin future harvests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai toɔ wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: How do I know the best time to sow my seeds right after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rain has soaked the ground thoroughly across several consecutive days, ensuring the soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate without drying out.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow when they are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni eyɛ kuku lolo?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen or the roots are sitting in too much water. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or urea helps the leaves turn deep green and support strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet and overly shaded farms. Pruning thick tree branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods early helps protect the rest of your harvest.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji ni mli tse lɛ afolɔ Ha hulu la babaoo aba ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning yellowish-green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are a common sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using certified disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings for planting is the most effective way to prevent it.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ cassava mosaic hela he. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛji woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmei ni afolɔ ni helai nyɛɔ eyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ baatsu nii beni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil becomes too dry, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the roots helps the plants set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers near my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the young cocoa trees from heat and retaining soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How deep should I bury my yam setts when planting them on mounds?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu sweet potatoes lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ?

english: Yam setts should be buried about 10 to 15 centimeters deep inside the mound. Planting too shallow causes the seed to dry out in the hot sun, while planting too deep makes it difficult for shoots to push through.
ga: Esa akɛ adu sweet potatoes ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15 yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛaabote mli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water rapidly in dry weather. Spreading a thick layer of dry grass or plant waste around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and holds moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nɔ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly and choke my crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds resting in the soil sprout faster than most crops when rains fall because they are adapted to steal water and light. Clearing weeds within the first three to four weeks gives your crops a head start to shade out weeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe tsei babaoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛju nu kɛ la. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aje jwɛi lɛ ashishi kwraa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help improve my soil for the next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the plant roots decay after harvest, that stored nitrogen enriches the soil naturally for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tso shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my okra pods become hard and woody before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ mli wa ni amɛfeɔ tsei dani mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Okra pods mature very rapidly and harden once the plant starts putting energy into seed development. Harvesting pods every two to three days while they are still short, tender, and snap easily prevents them from becoming woody.
ga: Roselle ŋmeii lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwaa beni tso lɛ jeɔ shishi ekɛ hewalɛ fataa he koni ekɛdumɔwui aba lɛ. Pod fɛɛ pod ni oookpa Gbii enyɔ loo etɛ be mli ni amɛji kuku lolo, amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkumɔ lɛ baatsi pod lɛ naa koni amɛkatsɔ tso.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when there is strong sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sun. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby provides a natural umbrella that keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce small ears when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ toi bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops are forced to fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to develop large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, anyɛɔ Dumɔwui anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo tso agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whitefly insects. Using disease-resistant planting cuttings stops the virus from taking over your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil lacks the nutrients my crops need to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Soil lacking nutrients usually shows in the crops—plants remain short, leaves turn pale green or yellow instead of deep green, and harvest yields drop. Adding compost, manure, or the right fertilizer restores those missing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Tso lɛ hiɔ shi kuku. Baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds grow very fast and strong on my farm even when my planted crops are struggling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miida oya ni amɛhe wa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mi tsei lɛ miina naagbai moŋ.

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep root systems that quickly steal water, space, and fertilizer before your planted crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early gives your crops a chance to drink and feed properly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni juɔ nu, ŋwɛi, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya dani otso lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛnu nu ni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the soil when I plant right after the very first small rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain after a long dry season often wets only the top surface of the ground. If seeds absorb a little moisture and then the soil dries up completely, the seeds stop growing inside and rot before full rains arrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ ŋɔ nu fioo ko pɛ lɛ, no lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa. Dumɔwui lɛ kpaa amɛkwɛ̃mɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ.

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen food out of the air and put it back into the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow green and strong, so planting them together naturally feeds the maize.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa ŋmãa niyenii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many flowers, but the flowers fall off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plants experience extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of pollination by insects. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay on the plant long enough to turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni bɛ pollination Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I save hybrid maize seeds from my harvest to replant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ hybrid corn dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields in their first generation only. Replanting seeds harvested from hybrid crops results in weak, mixed plants that yield much less corn than the original seed.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa fioo pɛ baa fe shishijee dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody if I leave them in the soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are storage organs that build up tough starch fibers as the plant gets older. If left unharvested past full maturity, the soft edible starch converts into hard wooden fiber, making the cassava tough to cook and eat.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe ni feɔ starch fibers ni wa be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akpaaa ŋmei lɛ kɛyashi eshɛreɔ kwraa. Atsakeɔ starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ayeɔ lɛ awoɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa mli. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaahoo ŋmei ni ayeɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees failing to grow well on my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees require deep, rich soil, consistent moisture, and proper shade. If your land is too dry, has poor soil, or gets too much direct sunlight, cocoa trees will struggle and fail to thrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii babaoo he miihia koko tsei. hulutsoo ni tamɔ ekome kɛ hulutsoo ni sa Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii, loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fa babaoo. Kookoo tso lɛ baaná amanehulu ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ̃.

english: Can I plant cashew nuts on land where my cocoa trees failed to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cashew ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, cashew trees are much hardier than cocoa trees and can thrive in drier, less fertile soils. Switching to cashew is a smart way to make good use of land where cocoa struggles.
ga: Hɛɛ, cashew tsei lɛ wa kwraa fe cacao tsei lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ eda yɛ shikpɔji ni egbi ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ Tsakemɔ kɛmiiya cashew ŋmeii anɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni kookoo ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why do cashew trees survive in dry conditions where cocoa trees wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew tsei hiɔ shi yɛ hei ni egbi ni cacao tsei lɛ gboi yɛ lɛ?

english: Cashew trees have deep taproots that reach underground water and require less moisture, whereas cocoa trees have shallow roots and need rich, moist soil with plenty of shade.
ga: Cashew tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he, ni ehe ehiaaa ni ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ ahi mli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: What happens to my soil if I leave my field empty after my crops fail?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi miŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni ŋmɔshi nibii efo mli sɛɛ?

english: Leaving land bare exposes the soil to hot sun and heavy rains, which washes away valuable topsoil nutrients, causes erosion, and makes the land deteriorate over time.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ, ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa nɔ. Enɛ baajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Is it better to abandon land that isn't producing well or try planting a different crop?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooshi shikpɔŋ ni wooo yibii loo oooka ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi adumɔ okwɛ?

english: It is much better to plant a different, hardier crop because keeping the soil covered prevents erosion, maintains land value, and can gradually rebuild soil fertility.
ga: Ebaafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu tso kroko ni wa fe no kwraa. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ naa. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ jara nɔ ni otswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekoŋŋ fiofio.

english: How does changing the type of crop I grow help improve my land?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Different crops take and give back different nutrients to the earth. Changing crops helps break soil pest cycles, balances nutrient levels, and prevents the land from becoming exhausted.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi lɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii srɔtoi anɔ ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaato he jogbaŋŋ ni atsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do some crops grow very well on one part of my land but fail on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko nɔ shi amɛkwɛɛɛ yɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil composition, water drainage, and sunlight vary across different sections of a farm, meaning one spot might be perfect for cocoa while another spot is better suited for hardier crops like cashew.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii, nu ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ hei srɔtoi, ni tsɔɔ akɛ he kome baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ. yɛ be mli ni he kroko lɛ sa kɛha tsei ni wa tamɔ cashew ŋmeii.

english: What should I do first when my young cocoa seedlings start dying on my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ́ kookoo tsei bibii je shishi amɛgboi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Check if the seedlings have adequate shade and water, examine them for pests or disease, and seek advice from an extension officer to determine if the soil is suitable before replanting.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kwɛmɔ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai komɛi yɛ mli. ni otao ŋaa kɛjɛ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛna kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hi loo ehiii dani amɛdu ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has deteriorated too much for cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite tsɔ ni esaaa akɛ afeɔ kookoo?

english: If the soil is hard, dry, washes away easily during rains, or if cocoa leaves constantly turn yellow and drop off despite caring for them, the soil has likely lost the nutrients cocoa needs.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi lɛ, ewaaa akɛ abaafɔ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be fɛɛ be ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ahaa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu baanyɛ afite niyenii ni he hiaa kookoo lɛ.

english: Who can I ask for guidance when my crops keep failing on my field?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ mabi ŋaawoo ehã mi kɛ́ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ehiii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can reach out to local Agricultural Extension Officers or experienced lead farmers in your community who can inspect your farm soil and recommend the best alternative crops for your area.
ga: Obaanyɛ oya okwaafoi anitsumɔ mli shweremɔ he nitsulɔ loo okwaafoi ni hiɛ niiashikpamɔ ni yɔɔ oakutso lɛ mli lɛ aŋɔɔ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ohala kɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I keep planting seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest over and over again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ fioo shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Reusing hybrid seeds from previous harvests leads to weaker crops and lower yields because the plants lose their vigor over generations and become more vulnerable to local pests and diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ tsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. ni amɛhe yɔɔ oshara waa kɛha he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai.

english: Why shouldn't I plant sweet cassava right next to bitter cassava varieties in the same small farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni mli edɔ lɛ masɛi yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting different varieties too close together can lead to cross-pollination or mix-ups during stem cutting selection, which can alter the taste and processing quality of future harvests.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha cross-pollination loo hybridization aba yɛ be mli ni ahalaa ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsake bɔ ni wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ ŋɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni atsuɔ he nii ahaa lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce very little maize now compared to when I first cleared the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miiwo ŋmãa fioo pɛ kɛ akɛto be mli ni mijie brɔshi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the soil every harvest. Without adding manure, compost, or fertilizer to replenish the earth, the soil gets tired and hungry, leaving no food for new plants to grow strong.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa amɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fataaa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ hu baaye lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii ko eshwɛɛɛ ni tsei heei lɛ baanyɛ adara waa.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant leguminous cover crops like mucuna during the off-season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ quince yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Cover crops protect topsoil from heavy rains, suppress weeds, and naturally pump nitrogen back into the soil to restore fertility for your next main crop.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa he, ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops get sick if I plant tomatoes in the exact same spot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela mɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji midu tomato yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting crops from the same family in the same soil year after year allows soil-borne diseases and specialized pests to build up in that spot, making every new plant sick faster.
ga: Tsei ni jɛ weku kome mli ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ jɛmɛ. Ehaa tso hee fɛɛ tso hee hela mɔɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce small cobs when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing all of them to stay weak and undersized.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa tsɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding young cocoa from the heat while keeping soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crop yield even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal fertilizer and soil nutrients directly from your crops' roots, starving your plants even if water is plentiful.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ kɛji amɛyɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Why shouldn't I collect runoff water from a neighbor's flooded farm to water my own crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mibuaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mikutsoŋnyo ŋmɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni mikɛha mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nu?

english: Water flowing from another field can carry invisible fungal spores, bacteria, and weed seeds that will quickly infect your healthy land and crops.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji krokomɛi amli lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ fungal spores ni anaaa, bacteria, kɛ jwɛi dumɔwui. Enɛ baagbɛ eshwa oshikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ onibii amli oya.

english: Why should I cut off yellow or spotted leaves from my garden eggs and tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ tomato tsei amli lɛ?

english: Pruning diseased leaves prevents fungal spores from spreading to the rest of the plant and helps the crop send its energy into growing clean, healthy fruit.
ga: Baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tso lɛ fãi krokomɛi amli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ gbɛ kɛyaa tso yibii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains on the same land where I am planting young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũuɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant cassava too close to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ lɛ ji nɔ fɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a heavy feeder that aggressively draws nutrients and water from the soil, and its thick leaves block sunlight, which can choke and starve delicate young cocoa plants.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii ni tsii ni jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa. ni ebaai ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha cacao tso bibioo lɛ agbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ aye lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow better on one of my farmland locations than on another land I own in a neighboring village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔji lɛ eko nɔ fe shikpɔji krokomɛi ni miyɔɔ yɛ akrowai ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Soil quality varies from place to place. One piece of land may have richer organic matter and better water retention, while land in another area might be sandy, eroded, or depleted from years of continuous farming.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha yɛ he fɛɛ he. Shikpɔŋ bibioo ko baanyɛ aná nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo kɛ nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hei krokomɛi lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋã, ni efite loo efite kɛjɛ afii babaoo ni akɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster on my cleared land than the crops I carefully plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to immediately seize bare land, open sunlight, and surface soil nutrients, whereas cultivated crops take longer to settle their roots and start growing.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛye shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. hulu la ni agbeleɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ Tsei ni adu lɛ, yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛjeɔ dalɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves, but give me very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of swelling its tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e yi ɔ fĩɔ ngɛ zugba sisi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but most of them fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee pods?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or when the tree is stressed by dry weather and lacks the nutrients needed to support pod development.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ebɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha pod lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees stop yielding as many pods as they did when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ ekpa yibii babaoo womɔ tamɔ bɔ ni ewo beni eji gbekɛ fioo lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees pass 20 to 30 years of age, their inner systems slow down and struggle to carry nutrients to the top branches, especially if the soil nutrients have been depleted over time.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tsei eye afii 20 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, amɛmli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ baa shi ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and rot when the tree branches grow too thick and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ niji lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Overly dense branches block sunlight and airflow, creating a dark, wet atmosphere where black pod fungal disease thrives and spreads rapidly from pod to pod.
ga: Niji ni tsii fe nine lɛ tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ duŋ ni edɔɔ. Black pod fungus hela lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains require a lot of water to hold up their massive leaves. In dry weather, the plant naturally drops its outer leaves to reduce water loss and protect its stem from drying out completely.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ amɛbaai wuji lɛ. yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛtsi amɛshishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain shoots produce smaller bunches when I keep planting them in the exact same hole year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ bu kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Replanting in the exact same spot exhausts specific soil nutrients and allows soil pests like nematodes and root diseases to build up in the ground, weakening new shoots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes kɛ shishifãi helai ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii heei lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to produce green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away nutrients or leave the soil too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients. Supplying steady water during dry spells and keeping the soil nourished helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tight during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a self-defense mechanism where the tomato plant rolls its leaves to reduce surface area, preventing water from evaporating too quickly in intense heat. If the leaves unfold when the sun goes down, the plant is simply protecting itself.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he. Tomato tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the large shade trees from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Without shade trees or temporary shade crops like plantains to block harsh heat and trap air moisture, tender seedlings dehydrate quickly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ tsei loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, bɛ koni akafee hulutsoo ni naa wa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli nu faaa oya.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra suckers growing around the base of my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: If too many suckers grow from the same root, they compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one main plant and one or two strong suckers directs energy into producing larger, heavier bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ni jɛɔ shishifã kome mli lɛ fa babaoo lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tso titri kome pɛ kɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my field help the maize crop I plant next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize on that same field later, the maize feeds on this stored nitrogen and grows much better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ sɛɛ mli lɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, ŋmãa baaye nitrogen ni ato lɛ ni ebaada jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight for growth. Staking also keeps the leaves dry and clear of wet soil, preventing leaf rot and allowing the plant to build bigger underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo koni amɛshwere. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni sũ ni mli ewo fɔ bɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ agbo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my vegetable plants with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Tsoi ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the ground, or mulching, acts like a protective blanket that keeps soil cool and prevents water from evaporating under the sun. It also blocks weed seeds from receiving sunlight and stops topsoil from washing away in heavy rains.
ga: Mulching, loo mulching, tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. Agbɛnɛ hu, etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ, ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ hu shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 8 to 12 months after planting. You will know they are ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack as the tubers swell underground.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo baahi shi aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ amɛfee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to apply granular fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ granular fertilizer baawo mli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash fertilizer off the surface of the soil before plant roots have time to drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is moist but no heavy storms are expected so the nutrients stay near the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi akpaaa ahum ni naa wa ko gbɛ ni baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii abɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my maize when the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the ground might dry out again. Wait until you get two or three steady rains that soak deep into the soil so your seeds have enough water to germinate and stay alive.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ekoŋŋ. Mɛɛ ni oná nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nɛɔ daa ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava turning yellow and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry weather to save water and protect their tubers underground. As long as the stems stay green inside, the crop will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafee eŋɔli yɛ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the tall trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight because their roots are short and leaves are delicate. Leaving large shade trees or planting plantains around them keeps the soil cool and moist while they grow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Enɛ jɛɔ eshishifãi kukuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ hewɔ. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant many maize seeds very close together in one hole?
ga: Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Planting too many seeds together causes the plants to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to thin stems and tiny cobs. Planting one or two seeds per hole with proper spacing yields larger, healthier cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ yɛ bu kome mli ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes rapidly from dry to flooded. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch around the base helps flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa nu afua mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛmaa shi tamɔ tomatoi.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the maize. Checking your field early and applying recommended treatments into the funnel before the caterpillars grow large protects the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo ŋmei lɛ nɔ dani ŋmei lɛ mli alɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmei lɛ he.

english: Why should I clear weeds from my farm before I put fertilizer near my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will steal the fertilizer nutrients from the soil before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds first ensures your crop gets all the nourishment from the fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ebaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abashɛ. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haa onibii lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they catch maximum sunlight and avoids leaf rot.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ, ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: In hot afternoons, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the soil. As long as the plant recovers and looks firm again by morning, this is normal heat defense behavior.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni wa ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ. Enɛ ji hulutsoo hebuu subaŋ ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea plants die and decompose, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji cowpea tso lɛ gbo ni egbo lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Which way up am I supposed to plant my cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ madu ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Always plant cassava stems with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots struggle to reach the surface, resulting in weak plants and very small tuber yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cassava tsei ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji okɛ tsei shwie shi lɛ Shoots baaná naagba ni ekɛshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do I need to make high mounds of earth before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow long and need soft, loose soil to expand easily without hitting hard ground. High mounds also keep the roots well-drained so water does not sit around them and cause the yams to rot.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ daa ni amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ haa nu kpakpa tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ nu bɛ jɛmɛ. kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo

english: It is better to wait until the rains become steady and regular. The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell, which will scorch and kill the newly sprouted seeds before the real wet season begins.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ anɛ daa kɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baashã ni ekpata dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahiɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: This yellowing means your maize crop is lacking nitrogen fertilizer. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves its remaining food to the new top leaves, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: What is eating ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark waste in the stems?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ekumɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ nibii diji ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center whorl of the maize plant. They chew through tender leaves and can destroy your crop if not treated early with recommended control measures.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite onibii kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra yɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ he lɛ naa.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit when water supply is uneven. Giving your tomato plants a steady, regular amount of water helps them draw calcium properly from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ daa kɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from stress, such as hot dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or insect attacks. Keeping the tree roots moist and shaded helps flowers stay attached and turn into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛha hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die if there are no big trees growing near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji tsei ni eda ko bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn quickly under intense direct sunlight. Planting tall shade crops like plantain or shade trees keeps the soil cool and creates a moist environment that protects tender seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe lɛ baa.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally enriches the soil with food for your maize crop. Their leafy vines also shade the ground, slowing down weed growth and saving soil moisture.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii ni ekɛbaakwɛ o-corn lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Wein tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo he ni ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ ni jwɛi kɛ baai yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the hot sun from evaporating all the soil moisture. It also slows down weed growth and turns into rich natural fertilizer as it rots into the soil over time.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ atsɔ la. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ hu shwereɔ fioo ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa beni efiteɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ.

english: How long can I expect tree crops like cocoa or citrus to keep giving a strong harvest after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ tso ko, tamɔ kookoo loo sitrus baawo yibii ni mli wa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Perennial tree crops take 3 to 5 years to start producing, but once mature, they can give you heavy, strong harvests for 15 to 20 years or more if you prune them and keep the soil healthy.
ga: Tsoi ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi kɛ́ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ebaanyɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ afii 15 kɛyashi 20 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛji ofolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni owo mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops give a very big harvest in the first few years but then start yielding less later on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli shi no sɛɛ lɛ ebɔi yibii fioo kowoo lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the soil every time they produce fruit. If you do not feed the soil with compost, manure, or fertilizer, the land becomes tired and crop yields will drop over time.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaawo yibii. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Do I need to plant new seeds every year, or are there crops that stay in the soil and produce for many years?
ga: Ehe miihia ni adu dumɔwui heei daa afi. Aloo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ni shwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ewoɔ yibii afii babaoo?

english: Crops like maize, rice, and tomatoes are annuals that die after one season and need replanting. Crops like plantains, cocoa, and oil palm are perennials that stay in the ground and yield fruit for many years.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ tomato ji afi mli tsei ni gboiɔ yɛ be kome sɛɛ ni ehe hiaa ni adu ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ plantains, cocoa, kɛ oil palm ji tsei ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii afii babaoo.

english: Is it better to clear and plant my entire piece of land all at once or plant it section by section over time?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majie mishikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ni madu shikome loo madu fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Planting section by section helps you manage labor and costs easily. It also spreads out your harvest times so you can have steady income instead of doing all the hard work at once.
ga: Nibii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ fãi amli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ nitsumɔ kɛ shika nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Egbɛɔ okpamɔ be lɛ hu eshwaa koni eha oná shika ni yaa nɔ daa moŋ fe ni oootsu nitsumɔi ni wa lɛ fɛɛ shikome.

english: Why does it take so many months after preparing my land before tree crops start showing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ nyɔji babaoo yɛ be mli ni misaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ dani tsei lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Tree crops use their first few years to build deep root systems and strong trunks. This early growth period is necessary so the tree is strong enough to hold heavy fruit in later years.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Nɛkɛ mra be mli dalɛ nɛɛ he miihia koni tso lɛ aya nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ewo yibii ni tsii yɛ afii ni baa lɛ amli.

english: How long should I leave my farmland to rest before planting crops on it again?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ koni mihe ajɔɔ mihe dani manyɛ madu nii ekoŋŋ?

english: Leaving farmland to rest for 1 to 3 years allows wild plants to grow and die back, which naturally puts organic matter and nutrients back into the soil so it becomes fertile again.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi he ni adu lɛ yɛ lɛ mli afii 1 kɛyashi 3 lɛ, ebaaha koo mli tsei lɛ adara ni amɛgboi. Enɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛha sũ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some crops like maize mature in a few months, while crops like yam take almost a whole year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ abele lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ sweet potatoes hiɔ shi yɛ afi lɛ mli bei babaoo mli lɛ?

english: Fast crops store their energy in simple seeds or fruits on top of the ground, while slow crops like yam need many months to build up and store heavy food underground in their tubers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ oya lɛ kɛ hewalɛ toɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli, yɛ be mli ni nibii ni aduɔ blɛoo tamɔ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii ni tsii ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii amli.

english: How can I tell when my crops have stopped growing and are ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpa shweremɔ ni esa akɛ makpa?

english: Crops show physical signs when mature, such as leaves turning yellow and drying up, stalks dropping, or fruits changing color and easily coming off the stem.
ga: Tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii akpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ, amɛshishifãi ni shwieɔ shi, loo aduawai ni tsakeɔ amɛhe su ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifã lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds very close together so I can get more crops on my field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If crops are planted too close, their leaves block each other from sunlight and their roots fight for water and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak plants with small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai lɛ abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops slow down their growth during the dry harmattan season even if I try to water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ harmattan be ni nu lɛ egbi lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mibɔ mɔdɛŋ akɛ mawo nɔ nu moŋ

english: In the hot, dry season, the dry air makes plants lose moisture very fast through their leaves, so the plants slow down their growth to save water and protect themselves from heat.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei haa amɛdalɛ baa shi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and die when I clear all the tall trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Large shade trees protect young cocoa from scorching sun and help keep the soil moist until the cocoa canopy matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the fruit is even ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani aduawai lɛ po shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that cannot support the heavy weight of a maturing bunch, especially during strong winds. Supporting them with wooden props helps carry the weight until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ tsei niji ni eda lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Tsoi ni akɛfiɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ muji lɛ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to grow green leaves and healthy stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa lɛ aná baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why does my land become dry and hard like rock shortly after the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni efee tamɔ tɛi beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil left bare without shade or mulch loses its moisture very quickly to the hot sun. Adding dead leaves, grass, or crop residues on top of the soil helps retain water and keeps the ground soft.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ashi ni hulutsoo be loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai, jwɛi, loo tsei ni egboi fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ ahi shi ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the soil when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing fungal root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ebaanyɛ eha fungal shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do black spots appear on my tomato leaves right after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ diji yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain splashes fungal spores from the soil onto lower leaves, and the wet conditions allow leaf spot diseases to spread quickly across the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ haa baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Why am I finding small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs on corn leaves. The hatched caterpillars crawl into the central leaves (the whorl) to feed on the tender young tissue.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa baai anɔ. Kplukai ni afɔ lɛ shwieɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ (whorl) koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil, as the plant tries to save energy and water rather than nourish new fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pepper tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ato moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ aduawai heei.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to feed the plant, which allows the tuber underground to grow larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni ekɛfi tso lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: If I plant my crop seeds very close together, won't I get a larger harvest from my small land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and very small yields overall.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni baa lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crop turning yellow while the plants are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Leaves usually turn yellow from the bottom up when the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is like the main food that keeps crops green and strong, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea will help fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ ŋmãa tsei he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen tamɔ niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my pepper plants without turning into any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by sudden heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist and shaded during peak heat helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna haomɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ plantains yɛ mi-kokoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that create a living canopy, giving the young cocoa the shade and cool moisture it needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the earth. It traps water in the soil longer, stops weeds from growing, and slowly rots to feed the ground.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛtsɔ nu ni ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni egboɔ fiofio koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows maize pests to live in the ground permanently. Swapping your plot with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ebaafite niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa ŋmãa mli ŋmeii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa. Otsakemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaaku ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli.

english: What is causing the leaves in the center of my young maize plants to look like they were chewed up overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre amɛ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day and feed on the fresh leaves at night. Applying recommended control products into the central leaf funnel early in the morning or late evening stops them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli, ni amɛyeɔ baai heei gbɛkɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛkwɛɔ hela lɛ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha enɛ akpa.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering or a lack of calcium in the soil. When the plant does not get steady water, it cannot transport calcium to the tip of the growing fruit, causing the bottom to collapse and turn dark.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ calcium aya aduawai lɛ ashishi ni miida lɛ naa Ehaa shishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ duŋ.

english: Should I plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the major season comes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni he hiaa yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ eba lɛ?

english: It is safer to wait for two or three heavy rains so the soil gets wet deep down. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout, only to dry up and die if a dry week follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Be kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi ebaagbi ni egbo kɛji otsi ni mli egbi nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do I have to train my yam vines onto tall wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on wooden poles allows the leaves to catch maximum sunshine to manufacture food for the crop, while keeping the leaves off the damp ground where diseases easily attack them.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai srɔtoi baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooopila.

english: Cassava is generally ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves yellow and fall off, and the base of the stem causes the surrounding soil to crack as the tuber roots grow large underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ fee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli gbalaa beni tuber lɛ shishifãi lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: If a strong wind blows down my young cocoa tree, is it dead, or can I salvage it?
ga: Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko tswa mikookoo tso bibioo lɛ, Ani ebaagbo loo manyɛ mahere lɛ yiwala?
