english: Young cocoa trees around 18 months old are tender and flexible. If they get knocked over, you can gently lift them back up, support them with a wooden stake, and pack soil tightly around the roots so they can continue growing.
ga: Aaafee nyɔji 18 lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo. Kɛ amɛgbee shi Obaanyɛ owó nɔ ekoŋŋ fiofio Kɛtsɔ tso ni okɛbaafi esɛɛ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle eshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ afee ekome koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara

english: How sensitive are my young cocoa trees compared to the older trees on my farm?
ga: Te mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto cacao tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Young cocoa trees under two years old are still tender and soft. Unlike mature trees with deep roots and thick trunks, young trees are easily shaken by wind and heat, requiring extra care and physical support when damaged.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii ni eyeko afii 2 lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ lolo. Esoro lɛ kwraa yɛ tsei wuji ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ latsaa hosoɔ tsei bibii oya. Akɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ yelikɛbuamɔ he miihia kɛ́ efite.

english: What is the correct way to lift a young fallen cocoa tree without breaking it?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ awóɔ cacao tso ni egbee shi lɛ nɔ ni akuuu mli?

english: You should lift the main stem carefully while supporting the base where the roots meet the ground. Once upright, tie the stem loosely to a sturdy stake and heap fresh soil around the base to steady the roots.
ga: Esa akɛ owó tso titri lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ofiɔ shishitoo lɛ sɛɛ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ema shi lɛ Fimɔ tso lɛ shishi. kɛ akulashiŋi ni wa kɛ muji heei ni ato he fɛɛ he koni shishitoo lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ

english: At what age does a young cocoa tree start becoming strong enough to withstand harsh conditions?
ga: Mɛɛ afii amli kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ mɛi ni he wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai anaa?

english: Around 18 months to two years, cocoa trees begin developing a stronger main stem and deeper taproot, but they remain tender enough that physical damage from winds can still be corrected easily by hand.
ga: Aaafee nyɔji 18 kɛyashi afii enyɔ Cacao tso lɛ baaje shishi ená shishifã titri ni mli wa kɛ shishifã ni mli kwɔ. Shi eyɛ blɛoo lolo bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ enine baanyɛ asaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ nibii ni kɔɔyɔɔ efite lɛ mlɛo.

english: When the sky becomes very cloudy and strong winds blow, how does that affect my young crops?
ga: Be ni ŋwɛi ewo atatu ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ. Te ebaaná midumɔwui lɛ anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Strong winds during stormy weather can push over tender young crops and dry out their fresh leaves. It is important to inspect your farm after strong winds to upright any plants that have tilted or fallen.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa yɛ ahum be mli lɛ baanyɛ atswa tsei bibii kɛya ni eha baai heei agbi. Ehe miihia ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ koni okɛjaje tsei fɛɛ ni shwieɔ shi loo ni miigbee shi lɛ.

english: Why is it important to keep big forest trees on my farm alongside my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ koo mli tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛfata kookoo lɛ he lɛ?

english: A good forest canopy acts as a natural windbreak and shield. It protects delicate cocoa trees from severe winds that knock them over and shelters them from harsh weather that causes leaves to wither.
ga: Tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Ebuɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni shwieɔ amɛ shi lɛ he, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ahe.

english: What should I look out for on my cocoa farm right after a windy storm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ mihe yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ahum ni naa wa ko sɛɛ?

english: Immediately check your young crops to see if any tender trees have been blown flat to the ground or tilted. Lifting them back up quickly prevents the roots from drying out and dying.
ga: Kwɛmɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ona kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ komɛi efo shikpɔŋ loo etsɔ ehe. Kɛ́ owó nɔ ekoŋŋ oya lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees withering and turning dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Leaves wither when the tree loses moisture faster than its young roots can absorb water, often caused by strong winds or hot sun. Reducing direct wind exposure and keeping root soil moist helps prevent this.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ fite oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ enɛ baa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ni aaatsi kɛ shishifãi lɛ ni afee ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Can a cocoa tree that looks like it is withering and dying actually be saved?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ahere kookoo tsei ni tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiigboi ni amɛmiigboi lɛ ayiwala diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, young cocoa trees are resilient. As long as the root system and main stem remain intact, relieving weather stress and providing proper support can rescue a withering tree and bring it back to good health.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cacao tsei bibii baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Shii abɔ ni shishifã lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baahi shi shiŋŋ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he haomɔ ni ajieɔ kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei ni egbi lɛ ni eha amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I be scared when my young cocoa farm gets hit by bad weather and trees tilt over?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashe gbeyei beni kɔɔyɔŋ gbonyo ba Mine kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo ko nɔ ni tso ko gbee nɔ lɛ?

english: There is no need to panic. Young cocoa plants are flexible, and most common issues like fallen or leaning stems can be quickly fixed by manually propping them back up and securing their soil.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni oshe gbeyei. Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe. Ni naagbai ni afɔɔ naa waa lɛ ekomɛi ji tsei ni gbeeɔ shi loo amɛtsiɔ amɛhe. Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ oya kɛtsɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ ni ooofi kookoo tso lɛ sɛɛ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ama shi shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my tree seedlings in May or June instead of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ May loo June mli moŋ fe hulutsoo be lɛ?

english: May and June mark the start of the primary rainy season in southern Ghana. Planting during this window ensures your young seedlings get continuous water to build strong root systems before the heat and dry spell set in.
ga: May kɛ June ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee yɛ Ghana wuoyigbɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ samflɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa nu ni yaa nɔ koni amɛto shishifãi ni mli wa ama shi dani hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛbaa.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is ready before my new crop seedlings arrive for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo dani dumɔwui heei aba koni adu?

english: Your soil is ready when it is moist, cleared of heavy weeds, and dug into loose planting holes. Loose, damp soil allows the soft roots of young seedlings to spread easily and drink water immediately.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ edɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni tsii ni okɛfo dumɔ bu lɛ mli mlɛo Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni mli efɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo ni amɛnuɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What makes a hybrid rubber seedling better than the seeds I pick from old farms?
ga: Mɛni haa rɔbɔt dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seedlings are specially bred to combine the best traits of strong parent plants. They grow faster, resist common tree diseases better, and produce much higher amounts of latex than random wild seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofa kroko fee lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni akɛ fɔlɔ tso ni he wa lɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ afata he. Amɛ daa oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ latɛs babaoo baa fe koo mli dumɔwui ni afee amɛ trukaa lɛ.

english: Why must I remove the black plastic nursery bag before putting the seedling into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ojie plastic kotoku diŋ lɛ dani okɛ dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The plastic bag holds the soil together during transport, but if left on in the ground, it stops the roots from growing outward into your farm soil. The roots will wind around themselves and choke the plant.
ga: Plastic kotokui lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ Enɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ bɔleɔ amɛhe ni amɛhaa tso lɛ muɔ.

english: How long will a newly planted rubber tree take before I can start tapping it for latex?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani rɔbɔt tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ rɔbɔt tswaa shishi?

english: With good care and weeding, a hybrid rubber tree usually takes about 6 to 7 years to mature and develop bark thick enough for safe latex tapping.
ga: Kɛtsɔ jwɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ejiemɔ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa ŋmeii ni mli tse bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atswa ŋmeii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do some of my young seedlings wilt and die shortly after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock. When tender plants are moved from shaded nurseries into harsh sunlight without enough initial soil water, they lose moisture faster than their roots can draw it up.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Beni ajieɔ tsei bibii kɛjɛɔ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ.

english: Why do rubber trees shed all their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ rɔbɔt tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf shedding is a rubber tree's natural way of saving water. By dropping its leaves when the ground is dry, the tree stops water from evaporating into the air through the leaves.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni rɔba tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he. Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi Tso lɛ tsiɔ nu ni tsɔɔ ebaai lɛ amli kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crop turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellow, curling leaves usually indicate crop stress—often caused by a lack of plant nutrients in the soil, too little water, or tiny insects sucking sap from the leaf undersides.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ haomɔ. Tse niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. nu fioo tsɔ loo kooloi bibii Emuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to leave wide spaces between rubber trees when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔshi he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ yɛ rɔbɔt tsei ateŋ kɛ́ wɔmiidu nii lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough direct sunlight for its canopy and enough soil space for its roots to gather water and nutrients without fighting neighboring trees.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋwɛitsu lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ abua nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ awuu.

english: Should I put chemical fertilizer directly into the hole right when I drop the seedling in?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu dumɔwui lɛ, ani esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo bu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, putting raw fertilizer directly against fresh seedling roots can burn and destroy them. It is safer to let the seedling settle for a few weeks first or mix well-rotted manure into the soil.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔŋ wo dumɔwui heei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã amɛ ni efite amɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oooha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi otsii fioo komɛi klɛŋklɛŋ loo okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an important food nutrient in the soil that helps plants build strong, green leaves and produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛ woɔ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. ni owo toi lɛ hewalɛ

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans in the same field where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have special bacteria on their roots that take food from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally feeding the maize plants growing next to them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ekɛ niyenii haa ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer right against the main stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso titri lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is strong like salt; putting it directly against the stem burns the plant's skin and roots. It must be placed a short distance away in a ring so the plant's outer roots can safely drink it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ ŋmei. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛwo ŋwɛi ŋtayaa ko mli kɛyashɛ he ko kuku. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ shishifãi lɛ anu nu shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikpaa cacao tsei wuji lɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and their young roots cannot reach deep soil water; they need overhead shade trees to keep them cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ nu he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔ.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high in the sunshine to catch light and make food for the plant, and lifting them off the ground prevents wet soil from rotting the leaves and stems.
ga: Esa akɛ agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni la aba ni eha tso lɛ niyenii. Ni kɛ́ owó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaaha baai kɛ tsei lɛ agbo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small tubers and thin stalks even when it rains well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ bulbs bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, light, and soil food away from your crops before the crop roots can reach them, leaving your main crops starving even in good rain.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii titrii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kpakpa po mli.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to come out of the soil when I bury them very deep in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii dumɔwui lɛ ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni mifuɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: A seed carries only a tiny pocket of stored energy; if planted too deep, it wastes all its energy trying to push up through the heavy dirt and dies before its shoot reaches sunlight.
ga: Hewalɛ ni ato lɛ kotokui bibii pɛ yɔɔ dumɔwui amli. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli tsɔ Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ mli. ni egbo dani hulu la lɛ shɛ ehe.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the afternoon sun becomes too hot or when the plant goes too long without water, dropping the flowers to protect itself from dying of stress.
ga: Tomato tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ ashi tomato tsei ni nu bɛ amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ. Okɛ nu awo mli koni obu ohe kɛjɛ gbele he haomɔ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground when wet water stays on the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need space in the dirt to breathe air; when rain stays flooded on top of the ground, the roots choke, drown, and rot from small organisms in wet soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ gbɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa, amɛshwieɔ nu mli ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the middle leaves of my young maize during warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, called Fall Armyworms, hide inside the tight, hidden leaves at the top of young maize plants where it is tender and moist, allowing them to eat safely away from birds and hot sun.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ amli, ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ, he ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ nii shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni okpoi kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my cashew trees before any nuts start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ cashew tsei anɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cashew flowers often drop due to insect attacks like thrips, prolonged dry spells, or a lack of soil nutrients. Spraying approved insecticides during early flowering and keeping soil moist helps the tree hold its flowers and form nuts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew nut fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kooloi tamɔ thrips, be kakadaŋŋ ni nu bɛ lɛ ahewɔ. loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii amli mra kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: What causes my young cocoa pods to turn black and dry up right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads in cool, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning dense branches to let in sunlight and spraying recommended fungicides during the rainy season helps stop the fungus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ duŋ kɛbaa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa koni hulu la aba mli kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akpa.

english: Why did my mango tree give a massive harvest last year but has almost no fruit this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ wo yibii babaoo yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ? Shi afi nɛɛ, eshwɛ fioo ni nɔ ko kwraa bɛ ni baajɛ mli aba?

english: Fruit trees like mangoes often experience alternate bearing, where producing a massive crop uses up all their stored energy, requiring a year to recover. Pruning and applying fertilizer right after a heavy harvest helps the tree produce fruit every year.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni woɔ yibii tamɔ mango lɛ naa yibii ni tsakeɔ amɛhe. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni anáa lɛ nɔ lɛ, hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii. Ehe afi dani ehiɛ ba ehe nɔ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni wa sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody instead of swelling up big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛfuu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin when the soil is too hard for the tubers to expand or when plants are crowded together. Loosening the soil into mounds or ridges and leaving adequate space between plants lets the roots grow thick.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. aloo beni tsei ebua amɛhe naa babaoo ni amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛfeɔ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni amɛshiɔ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my harvested yams starting to sprout leaves in the barn before planting season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Yams sprout early when stored in warm, humid, or bright spaces because warmth signals to the tuber that it is time to grow. Keeping your yam barn shaded, cool, and well-ventilated keeps the tubers dormant longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ, loo he ko ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ o-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ to he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves, so applying urea or NPK fertilizer near the roots restores full leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ urea loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná su fɛɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my rice seedlings after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds naturally germinate faster and absorb ground nutrients quicker than cultivated rice. Clearing your land early, flooding the field to proper water levels, or planting in straight lines helps you weed before the rice gets choked.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmãa ni aduɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ mra Gbɛjianɔtoo ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nu ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ooofee Loo ni ooodu yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ baaye abua bo ni ojie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ ohe dani amɛfo ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and slowing fruit growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ehaa aduawai lɛ daa blɛoo lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading viruses, or by extreme sun heat. Using insect traps, spraying neem oil solutions, and keeping the soil evenly moist prevents leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ahe tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop down and fold during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves fold during peak heat to protect themselves from harsh sunlight and conserve internal water. This is a natural protective behavior, and the leaves unfold once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni ekɛbu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu su. Ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni hulu lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers without making any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when soil nitrogen is too high compared to phosphorus, or when plants suffer from irregular watering. Switching to balanced fertilizers and maintaining regular watering encourages the plant to retain flowers and form pods.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fa tsɔ kɛ akɛto phosphorus he. aloo be mli ni tsei kɛ naagbai ni kɔɔ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ kpeɔ Kɛ́ atsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja nɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmeii.

english: How do I know if a new spray being sold in our market is safe to use on my maize farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa hee ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ wɔ jara lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Safe farm chemicals are tested and registered by agricultural officers to make sure they harm pests without destroying crops or soil. Unapproved chemicals can burn your crops, so you should always check with an extension officer before trying any new input.
ga: Okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kaa ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛŋmalaa amɛwoɔ wolo nɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛyeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii awui ni amɛfiteee ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã onibii. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ agba sane dani oka akɛ okɛ saji heei awo mli.

english: Why didn't the chemical spray I bought stop the insects from eating my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ shi ni mihe lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ akaye mi-cabbage baai lɛ?

english: Different farm chemicals perform specific jobs—an herbicide kills weeds, while an insecticide kills bugs. If you use the wrong chemical or apply it in the wrong amount, the pests will continue to feed on your crops.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nitsumɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ gbeɔ kooloi. Kɛji okɛ tsofai ni ejaaa tsu nii loo okɛ falɛ ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baaya nɔ aye onibii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is very intense, crops curl their leaves to reduce water loss and protect themselves from heat. If the soil has enough moisture, the leaves will usually bounce back once the evening cools down.
ga: Kɛ hulu la lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Baai lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji amɛhe jɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up even after I spray them with liquid fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ moŋ?

english: Strong sun without sufficient shade will scorch young cocoa leaves regardless of fertilizer. Chemical inputs cannot replace the protective cover and moisture that shade trees provide against harsh weather.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli lɛ baashã kookoo baai bibii lɛ ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ aye nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsei haa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why are my maize plants turning light green instead of deep green during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need rainwater to dissolve soil nutrients like nitrogen and carry them up into the stem. When there is a drought, the plant cannot feed properly, causing the leaves to lose their healthy green color.
ga: Tsei hia nugbɔ nu koni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni ekɛ amɛ aya ŋwɛi tso lɛ shishi. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa baa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amɛ su kpakpa ni ji eŋɔli lɛ.

english: If I spray fertilizer on my vegetables right before it rains, will it help them grow faster?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwie aduawai anɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ani ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara oya?

english: Heavy rains will wash away the fertilizer into gutter streams before the soil can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is slightly damp and heavy rainfall is not expected immediately.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa nubui amli dani shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo ni akpaaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings rot in the ground when I plant them immediately after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil deprives plant roots of air and encourages fungus growth, causing stem cuttings to decay. Waiting a short while for excess rainwater to drain ensures healthier root development.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yibii ni afo lɛ fiteɔ. Mɛɛ minitii fioo komɛi ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Extreme sun and heat cause stress to pepper plants, making them drop flowers to save energy for survival. Giving them steady water and partial shade helps them hold onto flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine kɛ dɔlɛ kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Ha fɔfɔii ada koni akɛ hewalɛ ni akɛhi shi lɛ ato. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be fioo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Can I use chemical fertilizer to save my crops from drying up when the rain stops early?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii koni eye ebua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra?

english: Fertilizer acts as food for plants, not water. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil during a drought can scorch plant roots because moisture is needed to safely dilute and transport the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei aniyenii, shi jeee nu. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehe miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli koni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛya shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does black pod disease spread faster on my cocoa farm during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: The fungus causing black pod thrives in dark, damp conditions and travels through rain drops splashing on pods. Pruning tall branches allows sunlight and dry air into the farm to stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Fung ni haa ŋmeii diji baa lɛ shwereɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ni etsɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pod lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ni efolɔ tsei niji kakadaji lɛ Enɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to stay green, build strong stems, and grow quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Bɔɔ tso ni mli wa ni edaa oya

english: Why does putting extra fertilizer on my crop make the leaves turn brown and burn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Applying too much draws water out of the plant's roots instead of feeding them, causing the leaf tips to dry up and burn.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my tomato plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or water is irregular. When stressed by heat or drought, the plant drops flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ kpe Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do government-approved seed varieties produce higher yields than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni nɔyeli lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Approved seeds are specially bred for strength and disease resistance. Replanting saved seeds over multiple seasons causes them to lose their vigor, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛhe. Dumɔwui babaoo ni ato lɛ adumɔ Bei haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why are my cassava roots staying thin and woody instead of swelling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee mlɛo ni amɛfee tamɔ tso yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛfuu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to swell if the soil is too hard for tubers to expand or if the soil lacks potassium, which is the nutrient needed to build starch inside the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni afee starch yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my cabbage plants more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-cabbage tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many crop pests reproduce faster in hot, dry conditions, whereas heavy rains naturally wash insects and their eggs off plant leaves before they can cause heavy damage.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo fɔɔ oya yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛwui kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa dani amɛfiteɔ nii waa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of big leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or receives excessive water, the crop focuses all its energy on growing thick stems and leaves rather than forming flowers and pods.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo enine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa tsei kɛ baai ni mli tse ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: Why do all the tomatoes in my field ripen at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Crops of the same seed variety planted on the same day follow identical biological clocks, causing them to reach maturity and ripen together under uniform weather conditions.
ga: Tsei ni adu dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ. Ha amɛdara ni amɛfee ekome yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ shishi.

english: Why does my stored maize turn into dust and get full of tiny holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikɛto lɛ mli eyi kɛ sũ ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Ani ebaayi obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Grain weevils or their hidden eggs enter the maize while it is still in the field, and once in storage, they multiply and eat the grain from the inside out.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ boteɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. ni kɛ́ akɛto he lɛ Amɛfɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves regain their deep green color and feed the growing ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua toi ni miida lɛ.

english: How does adding dried farm manure help my soil hold water longer during hot days?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: Dried manure acts like a sponge in the dirt. It binds soil particles together so rainfall stays in the root zone longer instead of sinking straight down or evaporating in heat.
ga: Nibii ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii bibii lɛ feɔ ekome bɔni afee ni nugbɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaagbee shi tɛ̃ɛ loo ebaatsɔ la yɛ latsaa mli lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees or planting plantains beside them shields young cocoa from heat stress until their leaves mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni baai lɛ daraa kwraa.

english: Why should I wait until the rains are steady before sowing my main maize seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui titrii lɛ?

english: Planting too early after the very first rain is risky because if the rain pauses for a week or two, the newly sprouted seeds will dry up and die in the hot soil.
ga: Ni ooodu nii mra tsɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome loo enyɔ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam plants produce bigger tubers when I stake their vines on tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji kɛ mikɛ wain tso lɛ fɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up into the air so they can catch maximum sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves catch, the more energy the plant sends underground to swell the yam tuber.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛwo sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn soft and rot underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Underground root rot is usually caused by heavy waterlogging in poorly drained soil, which suffocates roots and allows fungal rot to attack. Planting on raised soil ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and preventing fruit growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni etsĩɔ yibii lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that spread plant viruses. Spraying neem oil solution on the undersides of leaves helps keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do flowers drop off my tomato plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi tomato tso lɛ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or erratic watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots helps flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds grow faster when I plant my crops too far apart from each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ? Beni miduɔ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Wide gaps between crops leave open soil exposed to direct sunlight, which gives wild weeds the light they need to grow. Proper spacing lets crop leaves touch and shade out weed growth naturally.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa koo mli jwɛi lɛ náa la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Gbɛ ni sa haa tsei baai lɛ taa ni amɛhaa jwɛi ni eda lɛ he shade.

english: Why should I cut down extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: When too many suckers grow around a plantain mat, they steal water and plant food from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures maximum food goes into producing a heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii babaoo aba yɛ ŋmeii ni tsii amli.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds from my cocoa farm so that my trees can grow well?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni tsei lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeding should be done about three to four times a year, especially during the rainy season, so that weeds do not steal water, light, and nutrients away from your young cocoa trees.
ga: Esa akɛ atsu jwɛi ahe nii aaafee shii 3-4 yɛ afi mli, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Enɛ baaha jwɛi akaju nu, la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-cacao tsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight because their roots are small and cannot pull up water fast enough, so they need shade crops like plantains to shelter them.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala nu oya bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei lɛ aná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from hot weather by reducing the amount of moisture that escapes from their leaves into the air.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛbaa shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without growing into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani mɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers if they lack water or nutrients, and flowers will also drop if tiny pollinating insects do not visit them.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi titri kɛji nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli. Ni fɔfɔii hu baagbee shi kɛji kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollen lɛ fee nakai. Kaaba amɛsaramɔ.

english: What causes the cocoa pods on my trees to turn black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Black pod is a disease caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions, which happens when a farm is overgrown with weeds or has too much shade.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ jwɛi eyi ŋmɔ ko mli loo eyɛ hulutsoo babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the plant from producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves, which weakens the plant and stops normal fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ daamɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully grown and ready to dig up from the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akumɔ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil surrounding the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso titri lɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa.

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same piece of land without damaging either crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee ŋmãa enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop maize and cassava because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving plenty of room and nutrients for the cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, abele daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Enɛ haa gbɛ babaoo kɛ niyenii babaoo ni haa ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra side branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches allows fresh air and sunlight to pass through the tree canopy, which reduces disease growth and helps the tree focus its energy on growing pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la boteɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa helai baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm turn very hard and dry out quickly after the rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Soil becomes hard when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves or compost, which act like sponges to hold moisture in the soil for your crop's roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni wa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo bɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ahi otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I clear all the big shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh, direct sunlight to survive. Leaving tall shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantain creates a cool microclimate, keeping the soil moist and protecting tender leaves from burning.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko aba. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã.

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground based on how much sunlight their leaves can catch. Staking lifts the vines off the hot ground, exposing leaves to sunlight and air while preventing soil-borne leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii yɛ hulu la ni baai lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ naa. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni edɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ sũ mli tsei ahe helai anaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning pale yellow from the tips downwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for healthy green growth. Adding organic manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen from the air into the soil. When the crop finishes, that leftover nitrogen fertilizes the soil naturally for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji agbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa lɛ Nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to apply chemical fertilizer right when a heavy rainfall is starting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away fertilizer from the topsoil before plant roots can drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is moist but not during intense rain to avoid wasting your money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi otsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he koni akafite shika.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when rain falls continuously for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: When soil stays flooded with water, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing cassava roots to drown and fungal diseases to spread. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ŋmei helai gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the soil around pepper plants with dried grass or husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dried leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the ground cool, slows down water evaporation during dry heat, and stops weeds from stealing moisture from your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaju nu ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra small stems growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ fãi krɛdɛɛi komɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Extra shoots compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients. Leaving only two or three strong shoots allows the main tree to devote its energy to producing big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsobii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ashi niji enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I find tiny holes in my young maize leaves with small worms hidden inside the stem funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yɛ. Akɛtee trunk cone lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the plant core to eat young leaves. Catching them early and applying organic neem extract or recommended treatments directly into the leaf funnel stops them before they destroy the stem.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni aaamɔ amɛ mra Ni akɛ organic neem extract loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ awo tso lɛ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. baatsi amɛnaa dani amɛbaakpãtã tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani etsɔɔ etsuru po lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often made worse by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady and adding calcium (like agricultural lime or wood ash) prevents this rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ mli baa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ haa enɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii kwraa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium (tamɔ lime loo tso sũ) ni akɛfataa he lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantains planted next to them when I set up a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu kookoo tsei bibii ni dumɔwui awo amɛmasɛi lɛ? Be ni mima ŋmɔ hee lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct hot sun. Planting plantains alongside them provides natural shade and keeps the air and soil humid while the cocoa stems grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava crop is suffering from cassava mosaic disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kasa tso lɛ yɛ cassava mosaic hela?

english: Look closely at the leaves. If they appear twisted, curled, and covered in patches of yellowish-green color instead of smooth dark green, the plant has cassava mosaic disease, which is carried by whiteflies.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni etsake, ebɔle ehe, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii yɛŋ woɔ lɛ

english: What happens to my pepper plants if I put the seedlings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes their stems tall and weak, produces smaller peppers, and allows leaf diseases to spread rapidly between plants.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ bafee ekome lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Ehaa chili ŋmeii bibii baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa foliar helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ tsei ateŋ.

english: Why is it better for me to buy certified seeds instead of using seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to fight off local diseases and yield bigger crops. Seeds saved from past harvests lose their vigor over time, leading to weaker growth and lower harvest quantities.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛ maŋ lɛ mli helai awuu ni ewo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ baa shi ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates sharply between very dry and very wet. Keeping soil moisture balanced with mulching helps fruits form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya yɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ waa teŋ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ja ni akɛ mulching baakwɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ewo yibii.

english: Is it beneficial for my farm if I plant cowpeas together with maize in the same plot?
ga: Ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsina ŋmãa fata ŋmãa he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil as natural fertilizer. This feeds the maize plants growing alongside them and improves your overall harvest from one field.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni miida yɛ amɛhe lɛ niyenii ni ebaaha okpamɔ fɛɛ ni jɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to dig up my yam tubers from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie sweet potato ŋmeii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines stop growing, turn yellow, and begin to dry up. This signals that the plant has stored all its energy inside the bulb and is ready to harvest.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ kpa dalɛ. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔi gbimɔ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto bulb lɛ mli ni efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa.

english: Why do weeds sprout up faster than my main crops immediately after I clear my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie asleep in the soil for years. Clearing the bush lets direct sunlight and rainfall reach these dormant seeds, causing them to germinate quickly before your planted crops can take root.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Tsoi bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɔ dumɔwui ni ekã shi nɛɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ shishifãi.

english: Why should I cut off extra sucker stems growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo suckers krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Removing extra suckers ensures that all the water and nutrients in the soil go directly to the main mother tree. This helps the plant produce one large, heavy bunch of plantains instead of many tiny ones.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ plantain agbo kome ni tsii, moŋ fe bibii babaoo.

english: Why do crops like cassava and cocoa take many months or years to yield, unlike fast vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei heɔ nyɔji loo afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ ŋmãa lɛ? Jeee tamɔ aduawai ni yeɔ oya?

english: Crops build their roots, stems, and fruits slowly by gathering nutrients and sunlight over time. Tuber and tree crops need to store massive amounts of energy to produce high yields, which cannot be rushed.
ga: Tsei shwereɔ shishifãi, ashishifãi, kɛ aduawai fiofio. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la ni abua naa yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmeii kɛ tsei ato hewalɛ babaoo he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛná yibii babaoo, ni anyɛɛɛ afee oya.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves helps the plant manufacture food efficiently and send energy down to grow a bigger underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛ́ awo tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when left in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are tender and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains around them acts as a canopy umbrella, keeping the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ ehe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ŋwɛi ŋta. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ maa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Leaf curling in hot weather is a plant's natural defense to save water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to keep from drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ akagbi.

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of a maize plant are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant moves the remaining nitrogen to its younger top leaves to keep growing, leaving the older lower leaves without food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi, ni ji bibii lɛ anɔ koni eha baai lɛ aya nɔ ada. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ ni niyenii bɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai komɛi aba. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, poor watering, or lack of pollination. Without moderate temperature, balanced soil moisture, and insects to move pollen, the flower cannot set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. nu ni ehiii loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛji sũ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni ja kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛjieɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why do plantain suckers take a long time before they start showing a bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛjieɔ ŋmeii lɛ akpo lɛ?

english: A plantain sucker must first grow a massive underground root system and produce over 30 large leaves to store enough food energy before it can push out a single fruit stem.
ga: Esa akɛ plantain suckers lɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifã agbo ko klɛŋklɛŋ. ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni fa fe 30 ni ekɛtoɔ niyenii hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa he dani enyɛɔ eshɛɔ aduawai tso kome pɛ kɛjeɔ kpo.

english: What is eating small holes in the center of my young maize leaves, and why does it spread so fast?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa gbekɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ Ni mɛni hewɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa oya nɛkɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of young maize plants. They feed rapidly on tender growing leaves and move quickly across nearby plants if not caught early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ, ni amɛfoɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli oya kɛji akɛ amɔmɔɔɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do my cassava leaves develop yellowish mosaic patterns and become twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ mosaic mfoniri ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: This pattern is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. The virus disrupts how the leaf makes food, causing distortion and reducing the size of the roots harvestable below ground.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ. Virus nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ, ni egbaa bɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ niyenii lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ shishigbɛ nibii amli ni amɛbaa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to harsh sunlight and heat. Without shade crops like plantain trees to shield them, their leaves burn and dry out before their root systems can fully establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shade tamɔ plantains ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Amɛbaai lɛ baashã ni amɛbaagbi dani shishifãi lɛ baaje shishi kwraa.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam plants create food for their tubers through sunlight caught by their leaves. Lifting the vines on stakes spreads out the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and prevents diseases caused by lying on damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ hulu la ni tswaa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ owó wein tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo, ni ebaatsi helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni akɛkãa lɛ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to stay green and grow fast. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients out of the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour my fertilizer directly against the stem of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer placed directly on the stem acts like a chemical burn to the plant skin and roots. It should be buried a few inches away from the stem so the spread-out roots can absorb it safely.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa ni shãa tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ afu lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep falling off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fail to form pods if there are not enough tiny pollinating insects in the field, or if the tree is experiencing water stress or natural pod loss (cherelle wilt) due to nutrient shortages.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee pods yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ. Eshɛɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli loo kɛji tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu he haomɔ loo adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni elaaje (ni egboɔ) yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the underside of leaves or spreading leaf-curl viruses into the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away quickly. Excess water suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungus to attack and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli oya. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbe amɛ.

english: Why do my seeds dry up and fail to grow if I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ egbi ni amɛkwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often only wets the top layer of dry soil. If another rain does not fall soon after, the seeds sprout briefly and then quickly die from heat and lack of deep moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ pɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ be kukuoo mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, egboɔ oya yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant does not get enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil swings between very dry and very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ.

english: How do weeds actually reduce my harvest if there is plenty of soil for everything?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha mikpamɔ lɛ aba shi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Even if there is enough space, weeds drain the resources your crops need to produce heavy fruits and grains.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni naa wa Eyɛ mli akɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ moŋ, shi jwɛi hu baajie nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛwo aduawai kɛ ŋmaa babaoo lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize crops very close together, will I harvest more cobs?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ he waa Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmãa babaoo?

english: When you plant maize too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of getting more yield, you will end up with thin, weak stalks that produce very small or empty cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ ohe tsɔ Tsei baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ moŋ fe ni ooona yibii babaoo. Obaagbe naa kɛ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmei agbo ni mli wa baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow tall and skinny without bearing much fruit when planted under trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ashishi lɛ?

english: Vegetable crops need direct sunlight to make their own food and produce fruit. When planted under shady trees, they stretch upward searching for light, making them tall and weak with very little energy left to produce vegetables.
ga: Aduawai tsei hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaakpã mli kɛya ŋwɛi koni ena la. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛɔ, amɛgbɔjɔ ni hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ ni amɛkɛbaafee aduawai.

english: Why should I cut away the extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water and plant food away from the main mother plant. By leaving only one strong sucker alongside the main plant, all the nourishment goes into producing a single large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Ni ashiɔ tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ tso titri lɛ masɛi. Niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ baaha plantains ŋmɔ kome ni da ni tsii aba.

english: Why do all my tomato plants ripen their fruits at the exact same time instead of bit by bit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ shikome moŋ fe ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ fiofio lɛ?

english: Certain tomato varieties are naturally programmed to flower and set fruit all together so they mature at once. If you want to harvest tomatoes continuously over several weeks, you can plant small batches two weeks apart or plant different varieties.
ga: Afee tomato henɔi komɛi ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai shikome. Kɛji oosumɔ ni okpa tomato be fɛɛ be otsii babaoo. Obaanyɛ odu yɛ kui bibii amli. Ha amɛteŋ otsii enyɔ loo dumɔ srɔtoi srɔtoi.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers onto the ground before pods can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by hot sun, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. Keeping shade trees on your farm and mulching around the roots helps retain moisture so the flowers can turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa amɛnɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi.

english: Why are my cowpea plants covered in big green leaves but growing very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ahe lɛ? Shi pods fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Giving cowpeas too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the crop put all its energy into growing thick foliage instead of flowers. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen, so using fertilizers high in phosphorus will help them bloom and form plenty of pods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai ni mli tse. yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ lɛ, Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛná ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stems down into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have a unique way of growing. Once the flowers are pollinated above ground, the stems bend downward and push into the soil so the actual groundnut pods can grow and mature safely underground.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛdaraa. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural way for cassava plants to protect themselves during dry spells. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss and keeps its energy stored safely in the underground roots until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni ŋmei tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baaha nu ni efiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my fresh pepper fruits spoil so quickly after I harvest them in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai heei lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikpa amɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Harvesting peppers in the hot afternoon sun leaves heat trapped inside the fruit, which makes them soften and decay quickly. Harvesting early in the morning when the air is cool keeps the peppers fresh for a much longer time.
ga: Chili ni ajieɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa chili lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting shoots inside the barn long before I re-plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ dani mikɛ amɛ du ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that rest for a few months after harvest. Once that resting period ends, heat and moisture in the barn signal to the yam that it is time to grow, causing new shoots to break through the skin.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni baajɔɔ amɛhe nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Beni hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ haa ŋmeii heei tsɔɔ hewolo lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants produce smaller cobs when I plant the seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they compete for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop strong roots and broad leaves, resulting in larger, fully filled cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii wuji kɛ tsei ni eyi obɔ.
