english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn yellow and start curling during dry hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are a defense mechanism against heat and drought. The curling reduces leaf surface area to save water, while yellowing usually means the plant lacks nitrogen or water required to stay healthy.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he. Curling haa baa lɛ hiɛ he lɛ baa shi koni ekɛbu nu he. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do groundnuts form under the dirt when their flowers grow above the ground?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi beni amɛfɔfɔi lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, small stems called 'pegs' bend down and grow directly into the soil. Once underground, the tips of these pegs swell and develop into groundnut pods.
ga: Beni ajie ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, tsei bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. kɛji akɛ eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ anaagbee lɛ fũuɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting groundnuts helps improve soil fertility for other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei dumɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that collect nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant roots decay after harvest, this natural nitrogen stays in the soil and fertilizes future crops.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa ko ni buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa wɔsɛɛ tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my stored groundnuts get a bitter taste and moldy coat if I harvest them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ mli ŋɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji mikpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut pods need dry ground to mature properly. Excess moisture during harvest encourages damp fungi to grow, which produces harmful mold toxins (aflatoxins) that spoil the taste and safety of the nuts.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi he miihia ŋmei ŋmeii koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Enɛ haa mycotoxins ni yɔɔ oshara baa. (Aflatoxin) ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ.

english: Why does rice need so much water or flooded ground to grow compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu loo nu afua babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in waterlogged soil because their roots are adapted to pull oxygen even underwater, while standing water smothers competing weeds that would normally starve the rice plants.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ nu shishi po. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni kulɛ ebaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmãa tsei lɛ.

english: Why should I nurse my rice seeds in a small plot first before transplanting them into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ lɛ? Dani obaafã kɛya ŋmãa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Nursing rice seeds gives young seedlings a protected environment to grow strong root systems safely away from birds, pests, and heavy weeds, resulting in higher survival rates when moved to the main field.
ga: Omɔ dumɔwui ni atsa amɛ lɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa he ko ni abuɔ he koni shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ adara shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ okpoi, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ jwɛi ni tsii lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa wala yibii babaoo baa kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, causing reduced harvests over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I grow tall crops like maize together in the same field with low crops like groundnuts?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kakadaji tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kukuji tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, tall maize and low-lying groundnuts complement each other well. Maize grows high to catch upper sunlight, while groundnuts cover the ground surface to prevent soil erosion and stop weed growth.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa kakadaŋŋ kɛ ŋmãa kukuji feɔ ekome jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ naa ni ekpa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack the hidden center whorl of my young maize plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm target the tender, hidden center whorl of young maize plants because it offers soft, nutrient-rich leaves and shelter from hot sun and predators.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛhaa baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli, kɛ he ko ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no big trees growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong, direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and overheats their roots. Planting shade trees or temporary shade crops like plantains creates a cool environment and retains soil moisture, helping the young cocoa survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni eha amɛshishifãi lɛ adɔ fe nine. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lolo lɛ feɔ blɛoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable plants dry out so fast during the dry harmattan season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ harmatta be ni egbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: The dry harmattan wind strips moisture directly from plant leaves faster than roots can absorb water from the soil. Covering the soil around your plants with dry leaves or grass (mulching) helps trap moisture in the soil and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tips usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts on my farm makes the soil better for other crops later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the groundnut crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays behind to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei tsei Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I not apply chemical fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer off the top of the soil and down the slope before the plant roots have a chance to soak it up. This wastes your money and deprives the crops of food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ oshika ni ehaa ŋmɔshinii lɛ náaa niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle of my young corn plants and leaving dark dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ waa yɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the central growing tip (the whorl) of maize plants. Checking your farm early and applying organic mixtures like neem seed extract or approved control sprays can kill them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tso lɛ naagbee ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ (ring) lɛ mli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ agbe ŋmɔji dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rain falls for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when soil stays completely flooded with water because the roots cannot breathe and become vulnerable to fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and small even when I water the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni sũ lɛ yɔɔ kɛha otsei lɛ waa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need their leaves high up in full sunlight to process solar energy efficiently. Exposing the climbing leaves to maximum sunlight allows the plant to send more food underground, resulting in larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ taoɔ baai kakadaji kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔni afee ni amɛtsu hulu hewalɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni kwɔɔ lɛ wo hulu la ni fa babaoo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii babaoo majeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafee wuji.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field. Rotating with different crops breaks disease cycles and keeps the soil balanced.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: Why is the government telling us to cut down our old cocoa trees even when some of them still have pods on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ miikɛɛ wɔ akɛ wɔfo wɔ kokoo tsei momo lɛ? Tsei komɛi yɛ ŋmeii lolo?

english: Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease spreads quickly from tree to tree and cannot be cured with chemical sprays. Cutting down infected trees is the only way to stop the virus from spreading and destroying the rest of your farm and neighboring farms.
ga: Cocoa bud virus hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. ni anyɛɛɛ atsa kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ afomɔ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni efite oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ kɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ.

english: How long do I need to wait before planting new cocoa seedlings on land where old diseased trees were cut down?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Once old diseased trees are removed, you can plant plantains for temporary shade right away and introduce new disease-resistant cocoa seedlings within the same farming season once the site is properly cleared.
ga: Kɛji oojie tsei ni egbɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni eha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko aba. kɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛaaba yɛ shweremɔ be kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli beni ajie jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight and burn easily. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their leaves from sun damage and keep the soil moist while their roots grow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei, koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees during the dry season, and how can I help them survive?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua cacao tso lɛ ni ehi shi?

english: During the long dry season, cocoa trees drop leaves to reduce water loss. You can help them retain soil moisture by keeping shade trees on the farm and spreading a layer of dry leaves or straw around the base of each cocoa tree.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Obaanyɛ oye obua amɛ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi afɔ nɔ. Ebɔle kookoo tso fɛɛ tso shishi

english: Can I plant cassava alongside my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ masɛi?

english: It is not recommended because cassava grows aggressive roots that steal water and nutrients from young cocoa plants. Planting plantain or cocoyam is better because they provide shade without starving the cocoa roots.
ga: Akɛ enɛ etsɔɔɔ ejaakɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli. Plantain loo kookoo ni aduɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ehaa hulutsoo be ni hɔmɔ yeee kookoo shishifãi lɛ.

english: How do I know if the land I am renting from a landlord is suitable for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mihaa mishikpɔŋtsɛ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Good cocoa soil is dark, deep, well-drained, and rich in organic matter. Avoid rocky land or land where water sits stagnant after heavy rains, as waterlogged soil rots cocoa roots.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli Tsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni tɛi yɔɔ loo hei ni nu damɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: If I cut off branches from my cocoa tree, won't that reduce the number of pods I get?
ga: Kɛ mifo kookoo nine lɛ Ani ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ ayibɔ baaa shi?

english: Pruning actually increases your harvest. Removing extra or unwanted branches allows sunlight and fresh air into the tree canopy, which reduces disease and directs the plant's energy into growing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsei lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni ataooo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa helai baa shi ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do all the small flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi koko tso lɛ nɔ koni egbee shi ni etsɔko pod?

english: Flowers fall off when the tree experiences stress from dry weather, poor nutrients, or lack of pollination. Keeping soil moist with shade and leaving organic mulch on the ground helps beneficial insects pollinate the flowers successfully.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. niyenii ni ehiii loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ashiɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and hard before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, overly shaded, and humid conditions. Regular pruning to improve air circulation and removing infected pods early stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli Shade babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Afolɔ tso lɛ mli daa koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do trees on my neighbor's farm produce more cocoa pods than mine even though we share the same boundary?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔyɛ ŋmɔ mli tsei kome moŋ?

english: Higher yields depend on using improved hybrid cocoa seeds, regular weeding, timely pruning, and applying proper fertilizer to feed the soil, rather than just relying on the land's natural condition.
ga: Nibii ni anáa babaoo lɛ damɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa Jeŋ ni afoɔ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ shihilɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help keep the leaves healthy and improve your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni eha okpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests that attack corn to build up in the soil. Switching to legumes like beans or groundnuts for a season puts food back into the soil and starves out those pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɛi lɛ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and yield small cobs when I put many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii beni mikɛ ŋmeii babaoo feɔ bu kome lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted together, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Spacing seeds properly gives each maize plant enough space to feed well and produce larger, fuller cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo ŋmãa wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rains flood my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air to breathe and will rot if they sit in standing water for too long. Planting cassava stems on raised dirt mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away from the roots, keeping the tubers safe.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Ni ebaagbo kɛji eta nu ni mli ejɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Koni oyitso ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why does covering the soil around my crop roots with dry grass help them survive sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo gbii amli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as a blanket or mulch that shades the dirt from direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly, ensuring your crop roots stay wet even during dry spells.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ blanket loo ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ muji he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha nu lɛ akaho oya. Ehaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli po.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their blossoms without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when they suffer heat stress or when soil switches quickly from very dry to soaked. Watering your plants regularly and keeping the soil evenly moist prevents the plant from dropping its flowers.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo miigba amɛnaa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ baai lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear away all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn under full direct sunlight. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains next to young cocoa creates a safe canopy that protects the young trees from hot sun and wind.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ koni akɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Koo tso lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni buɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he.

english: Curled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites hidden under the leaf sucking out the sap. Spraying your crops with mild soapy water or neem oil destroys these pests so clean leaves can grow back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛmu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaakpata nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahiɛ. Bɔni afee ni baai ni he tse lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to set up wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa tso ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to create energy that feeds the underground tuber. Staking lifts the vines off the wet ground where leaves would otherwise catch fungal diseases and rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe koni ekɛfee hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Baai lɛ baanyɛ aná tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ.

english: Why should I pick narrow 'sword' suckers instead of broad-leaf suckers when expanding my plantain farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala ‘klante’ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ fe tsei ni yɔɔ baa ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ beni mikɛ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Sword suckers have strong bases attached to large food reserves that power fast growth and heavy plantain bunches. Broad-leaf suckers draw more energy into early leaf growth instead of building strong roots, leading to weaker plants.
ga: Sword sucker lɛ yɛ shishitoo ni wa ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ niyenii agbo ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni haa edara oya kɛ plantain tsei ni mli tse lɛ ahe. Broadleaf suckers lɛ gbalaa hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa baai lɛ adalɛ mli mra moŋ fe ni amɛaafee shishifãi ni wa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates living shade to protect the young trees, keep the soil moist, and help them survive their early stage.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and sticky dirt inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ ni muji ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the tender foliage. Checking your fields early and applying appropriate control methods into the plant's leaves before flowering protects the yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmɔji amli mra Kɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ tso lɛ baai dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and moldy during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and shaded environments. Pruning excess tree branches allows air and sunlight to dry the farm canopy, which slows down the fungal growth.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋwɛitsu lɛ gĩɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the earth, naturally enriching the soil to feed the maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmãa.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm make my crops grow better over time than relying only on chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli kooloi ashishifãi ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ

english: Animal manure improves the overall soil structure and helps the ground hold water longer, while releasing balanced nutrients slowly over several seasons.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ fɛo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. kɛ niyenii ni ja ni ajieɔ lɛ fiofio yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ fata he

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the heavy rains stay for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped water deprives them of air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away, protecting the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni emɔ mli lɛ ha kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ, ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How does spreading dry grass over my vegetable beds help my plants during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ aduawai asa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from direct sun, prevents moisture from evaporating, and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why do hybrid seeds bought from the store yield better than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Store-bought certified hybrid seeds are bred for high vigor and uniform growth in their first planting generation. Reusing seeds saved from hybrid plants results in lower yields and variable plant growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛdara yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ adalɛ tsakeɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crowded crops compete with one another for soil nutrients, groundwater, and light. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to grow large, healthy produce.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ babaoo lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ la mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil is well watered?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is often bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks water transport inside the plant stem. Rotating tomatoes with non-susceptible crops like maize prevents the disease from accumulating in the field.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, bacteria wilt kɛbaa Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsiɔ nu ni tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni nyɛɛɛ atswa, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ tsake tomato lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akabua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil or have waterlogged roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or improving field drainage helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo amɛshishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he loo aha nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Will planting cowpeas between my rows of maize slow down how fast my maize grows?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaha mi ŋmãa lɛ adara blɛoo?

english: No, cowpeas actually help maize by capturing nitrogen from the air and enriching the soil. They also cover the ground to conserve soil moisture and suppress weeds that would otherwise choke your maize.
ga: Dabi, cowpea yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni emɔɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ. Amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii hu koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko ni amɛgbeɔ jwɛi ni baanyɛ agbe o-abele lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with lots of leaves but only producing tiny tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or the crop gets excessive shade, cassava puts its energy into growing top leaves instead of roots. Giving plants full sunlight and avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizers encourages larger tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa shwereɔ yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ hulu la ha tso lɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ bulbs wuji.

english: Does lifting up my yam vines onto wooden stakes really help the tubers grow bigger underground?
ga: Ani mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ni miwoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yes, staking lifts the leaves into the sunlight so they can produce more energy for the plant. That energy travels down to feed the underground tuber, helping it grow larger than an unstaked plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking haa baai lɛ jeɔ hulu la mli bɔni afee ni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo amɛha tso lɛ. Nakai hewalɛ lɛ yaa shi koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Ye obua ni eda fe tsei ni atswako amɛ.

english: What causes my small cocoa pods to turn black and shrivel up before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo dani eshɛ dalɛ he.

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, shady conditions. Pruning overgrown branches to allow sunlight and airflow through the farm helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Tsei ni edara fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves burn and dry up when I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Retaining scattered canopy trees provides natural shade, retaining soil moisture and protecting young cocoa from intense heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kpoji ni mli tseee lɛ akwɛmɔ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain trees drooping and turning brown during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are large and lose water quickly in hot weather. Drooping is the plant's natural defense to reduce sunlight exposure, but covering the ground around the base with dry mulch helps trap moisture and keep the tree healthy.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ dara ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Defoliation ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛba hulu la ni ekɛkpeɔ lɛ shi. Shi kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi tso lɛ mli ni eha tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when air temperatures get too hot, when soil moisture fluctuates wildly, or when pollination fails. Regular watering and mild shade during extreme afternoon heat help fruit set successfully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ waa loo be mli ni pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli hulutsoo be lɛ ye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛwo omanye.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the underside of the leaves, or by viruses they spread. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ mli Kɛ́ akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite tsei ahe tsei lɛ.

english: Why are my okra plants growing very bushy with thick stems but taking a long time to produce pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa ŋmɔ mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ? Shi ani eheɔ be babaoo dani anyɛɔ afeɔ pods lɛ?

english: Okra focuses on stem and leaf growth when given excessive water or high-nitrogen fertilizer early in its life. Moderate watering and full sun exposure trigger the plant to shift its energy into flowering and producing pods.
ga: Okra kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tso lɛ yitso kɛ ebaa lɛ dalɛ nɔ kɛ́ enine shɛ nu babaoo loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo nɔ yɛ eshihilɛ mli mra. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ kɛ hulu la babaoo baaha tso lɛ atsake ehewalɛ lɛ ni etsɔ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to grow well if I plant too many of them in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many maize seeds are planted in one hole, the young plants compete heavily for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in thin, weak stalks and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Tsei bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ, ni no haa ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa baa.

english: How do I choose the best stem cuttings when I am preparing to plant cassava on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei niji ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ́ miisaa mihe koni madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best cassava cuttings come from the middle portion of healthy, mature plants that are 8 to 18 months old, as these stems contain enough stored nutrients and strong buds to sprout reliably.
ga: Yucca ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ jɛɔ tso ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18 lɛ teŋgbɛ, ejaakɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ato kɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers always advise me to plant beans or cowpeas on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a free natural fertilizer that improves soil health for future crops like maize.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛsu mli amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die so quickly if I clear all the big trees from my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo oya nɛkɛ? Kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight and need shade trees above them to lower the heat, retain soil moisture, and protect their delicate leaves during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. ni ehe miihia tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo yɛ amɛyiteŋ koni ekɛba dɔlɛ shi lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ebuɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground using stakes allows the leaves to catch more sunlight to produce food for the plant, which results in larger and healthier yam tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei tsu nii kɛwo sweet potato wain tsei anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni ekɛ niyenii aha tso lɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without forming fruits during periods of intense heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When pepper plants suffer from extreme heat and water stress, they drop their flowers as a survival response to save water and energy rather than attempting to support fruit growth.
ga: Taakɛ pepper tsei lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ lɛ. Amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii amɛshwieɔ shi akɛ wala yiwalaheremɔ hetoo koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Mohu ɔ, bɔɔ mɔde kaa o maa ye bua tso yiblii ɔ wami.

english: Why do the leaves on my garden eggs and tomato plants turn yellow and spotty during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water and high humidity during the rainy season create ideal conditions for fungal and bacterial diseases to infect leaf surfaces, causing yellowing, spots, and leaf loss.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha fungal kɛ bacteria helai ni baanyɛ atswa baa lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, ŋmeii kɛ baai ni laajeɔ.

english: Why does allowing weeds to grow around my crops reduce my final harvest so drastically?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ha minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ nɔ ba shi kwraa.

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and aggressively steal vital soil nutrients, fertilizer, water, and root space that your crops need to develop fully.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. ni ejuɔ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni he hiaa, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ shishifãi ni he hiaa ni otsei lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid applying dry chemical fertilizer onto my fields when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so roots can absorb it; placing it on bone-dry soil can cause root burn or cause the fertilizer to sit unused until heavy rains wash it away.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi tamɔ wu nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahi shi ni akɛtsuuu nii kɛyashi nugbɔ ni naa wa baaho lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil or attract insects so quickly when I put them into bags right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ loo egbalaa kooloi oya kɛji mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli beni mikpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains high levels of moisture that cause fungal mold to grow and attract insect pests; drying grains thoroughly in the sun before bagging keeps them safe for storage.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ amli nu babaoo yɛ mli, ni no haa ŋmɔtɔ daa ni egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmaa lɛ kwraa dani awo kotoku mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni akɛtoɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal sickness that thrives in wet and dark conditions. The fungus attacks the pod skin and quickly moves inside, destroying the beans if the pod is not removed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Fuŋ lɛ tutuaa pod lɛ hewolo lɛ ni eboteɔ mli oya. Kpatamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ kɛji ajieee ŋmeii lɛ mra.

english: If one of my cocoa trees gets sick, can the sickness spread to the healthy trees nearby?
ga: Kɛji hela mɔ kookoo tsei lɛ eko Ani hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, many crop sicknesses spread through rain splashes, wind, insects, or infected harvesting tools. Removing infected leaves or pods quickly helps protect neighboring healthy trees.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ahe helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi, kɔɔyɔɔ, kooloi bibii, loo nibii ni akɛkpaa nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Baai loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are turning yellow from a disease versus just hot dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hela kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be pɛ hewɔ?

english: Dry weather causes leaves across the whole tree to dry up evenly and drop during drought, whereas disease usually causes dark spots, patchy yellowing, or swollen branches even when rain is falling.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo tsei niji ni efu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po

english: Is it fine to leave sick, rotten cocoa pods on the ground inside my farm after I pluck them?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii ni efite lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mifolɔ amɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, leaving rotten pods on the farm floor keeps the disease spores alive in the soil. When rain drops fall, they splash those sickness spores back up onto healthy pods and trees.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa hela lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ekɛ hela lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa pods if land disagreements force me to delay harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ béi ha mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ fo?

english: If pods are left on the tree past their ripe stage, the seeds inside will start to sprout and fungi will invade, causing the entire yield to rot and lose market value.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛho amɛshweremɔ be lɛ he lɛ, Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ ni ŋmeii baatutua amɛ. Enɛ haa nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ ni jara ni eyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pluck my cocoa pods so they don't spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛkafite?

english: Cocoa pods are ready to harvest when their color changes completely—usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from red to orange. Harvesting at this stage ensures the beans inside are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhe su etsake kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. loo kɛjɛ tsuru mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can pulling cocoa pods off the tree by hand damage my future harvests?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmeii ni akɛ niji gbalaa kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ baanyɛ afite miwɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, ripping pods off damages the flower cushion on the tree trunk where future pods grow. Using a sharp tool prevents damaging this spot so the tree can flower and produce again next season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baafite fɔfɔii akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi ni wɔsɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ baajɛ mli aba lɛ. Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akafite nɛkɛ nii nɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ afɔlɔ ni amɛwo yibii ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the beans inside my cocoa pod ruined even when the outside pod looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ efite eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔji lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Tiny insects often pierce the outer shell to feed, creating small hidden punctures. Fungal sickness enters through these tiny holes and rots the beans inside long before the skin shows full decay.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tsɔɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ tsitsii lɛ amli koni amɛna niyenii. Enɛ haa bu bibioo ko ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ baa. Fungal helai boteɔ bu bibioo lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi haa kɔfi yibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ dani ehewolo lɛ fiteɔ kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but many of them fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers than they can feed, but heavy flower drop usually means the tree lacks shade, water, or nutrients, or is being attacked by tiny insects.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye. Shi bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ babaoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ hulutsoo, nu loo niyenii, loo kooloi bibii miitutua lɛ.

english: Why should I cover my harvested cocoa beans with plantain leaves instead of putting them straight in the sun to dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ plantain baai aha mi-cocoa yibii ni mikpa lɛ ahe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makɛ amɛ awo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli?

english: Fresh cocoa beans need to ferment first to develop chocolate flavor and kill the seed inside so it stops growing. Covering them with plantain leaves traps the heat needed for proper fermentation.
ga: Esa akɛ afee cocoa ŋmeii heei lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛná tsokolate lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ baai ha plantain lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha dɔlɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava stems need to be planted at an angle instead of straight up or flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmei tsei yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo ŋmei lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stem cuttings at an angle (around 45 degrees) helps the plant form deeper, stronger roots that absorb water better while making it easier for new shoots to sprout above the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ (aaafee digrii 45) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa. ni shwieɔ nu jogbaŋŋ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii heei baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is rich enough to plant maize without adding fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni mikɛ ŋmãa wooo mli?

english: Good, fertile soil is usually dark in color, crumbly to touch, retains moisture well, and has earthworms present; pale, sandy, or hard-packed soil lacks nutrients and will need manure or fertilizer to produce healthy maize.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi ni baa nii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efoɔ kɛji ata he Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋã, loo ewa. Ebɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ebaabi ni ekɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei awo mli koni ekɛ ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high, when there is a sudden dry spell, or when insects fail to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies feeding on the sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yeɔ tsofa lɛ mli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the trunk before maturing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, damp, and overly shaded environments during the rainy season.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during heavy rains and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy; waterlogged soil loosens the roots, so supporting the trees with wooden props helps keep them upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baajie shishifãi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsei fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi jaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil is still damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: Cowpeas temporarily wilt or curl their leaves in intense heat to prevent water from evaporating too quickly, which is a natural defense mechanism to survive the midday sun.
ga: Cowpeas baagbɔjɔ loo ebaabɔle amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni nu akatsɔ oya tsɔ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ayeɔ wala yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are ready to be dug up from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are ready to harvest when the leaves start turning yellow and drying, and when the inside of a freshly sampled shell shows dark brown markings and plump seeds.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Ni beni ŋshɔŋloo hee ni ajie lɛ mli lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni mli edɔ lɛ,

english: Why are caterpillars eating big holes in my cabbage leaves and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Moths lay eggs on cabbage leaves that hatch into hungry caterpillars; checking leaves regularly to crush eggs, using insect netting, or spraying organic neem leaf extracts will protect the crop.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ amli daa koni akɛkumɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii atsu nii Loo akɛ organic neem tso mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baabu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Which crops can I plant in Ghana to get quick food and income while waiting for my main tree crops to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana koni maná niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni yeɔ daa lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Short-term food crops like maize, cowpea, plantain, and vegetables can be harvested within three to six months. Planting them alongside slow-growing cash crops gives you food and income during the years before your main trees start producing.
ga: Abaanyɛ akpa niyenii ni akwɛɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ aduawai yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni oookwɛ yɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ ahe lɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛ shika yɛ afii ni tsɔ otsei titrii lɛ abɔi yibiiwoo lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the shade trees from my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and high heat. They need temporary shade from plants like plantains or bananas to keep the soil cool and moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo bananas adɛŋ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: How can I make my soil fertile again if I cannot afford expensive chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ? Akɛni minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hewɔ lɛ?

english: You can naturally enrich your soil by planting leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas, which feed nitrogen back into the earth, and by mixing dry organic materials or farm manure into the soil before planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. ni haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nibii ni egbi loo ŋmeii ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani aduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing huge leaves and stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and lacks potassium, the cassava plant directs all its energy into growing upper green leaves instead of expanding its underground roots into thick tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai eŋɔli ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli etsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow right after heavy rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kpa pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes essential plant nutrients like nitrogen deep into the soil beyond the reach of maize roots. Yellow leaves indicate the plant is hungry and needs a top-dressing of fertilizer or manure to recover.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni ŋmãa shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he. Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛha ehi shi ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from water stress during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu he haomɔ he yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: During Harmattan, crops show stress by curling their leaves, dropping flowers early, or wilting in the heat of the afternoon. Mulching the base of plants with dry grass helps keep moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii jieɔ haomɔ kpo kɛtsɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya loo amɛgboɔ yɛ shwane mli Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites that transmit plant viruses. Early spraying with soapy water or appropriate farm sprays keeps these pest populations low.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni hiɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛ samla loo ŋmɔ mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when soil moisture changes rapidly from wet to dry, or when heat is too intense. Regular watering and mulching keep soil temperatures stable so flowers can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo be mli ni latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to come up out of the soil after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if planted too deep where air cannot reach them, if planted in completely dry soil, or if birds and insects eat them. Planting at a depth about twice the size of the seed usually yields the best results.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ loo kɛji akɛ okpoi kɛ kooloi ye dumɔwui lɛ Bei pii lɛ, adu yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ toi enyɔ haa nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: What happens if I plant my crops very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak stems and low yield. Proper spacing allows good airflow and healthy plant growth.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni tsei lɛ hu daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe and absorb nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpea or groundnuts on my land make the next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leguminous crops like cowpea and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young plants with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, stops heat from drying out the ground, keeps moisture in the soil longer, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa la ni tsoɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and twisting tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from the underside of the leaves or spreading a virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa.

english: Why do my fresh tomatoes develop dark, rotten spots at the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato hee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni egboɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often triggered by irregular watering during fruit formation.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Cassava roots rot in the ground when the soil retains too much water without proper drainage, creating a wet environment where fungal diseases thrive.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small young pods before they can fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miishwie amɛbii bibii lɛ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Small cocoa pods often wilt and fall (cherelle wilt) when the tree experiences stress from drought, poor nutrition, or when it self- thins to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi. (Cherelle wilt) beni tso lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ kpeɔ lɛ. niyenii ni esaaa Aloo be mli ni egbɔjɔɔ koni ehi shi

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over whenever a small wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko baa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when their root systems are weak or damaged by microscopic soil worms called nematodes, or if planted in shallow soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ efite amɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɔ

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown crops fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients, resulting in thin plants and small harvests.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkpaaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green sprouts before I take them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃mɔ dani mikɛwo jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams sprout naturally after their resting stage ends, especially when kept in warm, damp, or poorly ventilated storage spaces.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri kɛji akɛ akɛto he ni edɔ, fɛ̃i yɔɔ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ.

english: Which crops can I plant in Ghana that will be ready for harvest in just three months?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana ni baafee klalo kɛha nikpamɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli?

english: Crops like maize, cowpeas, tomatoes, and cucumbers usually mature within 90 days (three months). They allow you to harvest quickly and plant multiple times in a single rainy season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, tomato kɛ kukumba shwereɔ yɛ gbii 90 mli (nyɔji etɛ), ni no haa anyɛɔ akpaa oya ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, preferably early in the morning or late afternoon after light rain. Always cover or lightly mix the fertilizer into the soil so heavy rainfall does not sweep it off the field.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Esa akɛ awo lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. Yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ha loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu mli fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Does it matter which way I point a cassava stem when planting it in the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko beni mikɛ amɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, the small growth buds on the stem must point upwards toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down forces the buds to grow downwards first, which weakens the plant and reduces tuber yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Cassava ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ shi klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small fruits when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ aduawai bibii beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough air, light, and food to grow strong and produce large yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa kɔɔyɔɔ, la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving some taller shade trees or planting plantains next to young cocoa creates a safe microclimate that protects them from scorching.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ oha tsei lɛ ha hulutsoo ni nɔ kwɔ Loo dumɔwui ni adu yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe aba ni ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa? yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing whorl of the maize plant. Inspecting fields early and applying botanical sprays like neem solution can help control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni oookwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa nɔ tamɔ neem solution lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their flowers before turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ pepper yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop flowers due to heat stress or sudden dry conditions. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the plants hold onto their flowers and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my harvested yams begin to rot so quickly when stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot when exposed to heat, high humidity, and poor airflow. Storing them on raised wooden racks in a cool, well-shaded, and airy barn keeps them dry and prevents rotting.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛji akɛwo dɔlɛ, latsaa babaoo, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛto tsei ni awó nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkagbi ni amɛkafite.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and strong. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps them regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpaa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava rot usually happens when excess water gets trapped in heavy soil around the roots during heavy rains, allowing fungal infections to build up. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps surplus water drain away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei fitemɔ baa kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli. Shishifãi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli Baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they face heat stress from extreme dry weather, lack of shade, or when tiny pests attack the stems. Keeping adequate shade trees and protecting the crop during flowering helps pods set properly.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni jɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa mli baa, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo kɛji kooloi bibii tutua tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni sa mli, ni abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are black spots forming at the bottom of my tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji yɔɔ tomato aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: This black spot is blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often because of irregular watering during fruit development.
ga: Nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ ji he ni egbo ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishi. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil naturally. They also cover the bare ground, which reduces weed growth and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa hei ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ hu nɔ, ni no haa jwɛi lɛ daalɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I keep my cut seed yams from rotting in the ground after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni ŋmeii ni afo lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cut seed yams rot when soil bacteria and fungi enter the open cuts. Coating the cut surfaces with dry wood ash seals the wound and protects the yam piece while it establishes roots.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ sweet potato dumɔwui ni egbo lɛ kɛji helai ni yɔɔ sũ mli kɛ ŋmeii bote he ni agbele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso sũ ni egbi wo he ni afo lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi pilamɔ lɛ naa ni ebu sweet potato fãi lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong winds just when the heavy bunches are forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli yɛ be mli pɛ ni jwɛi bibii lɛ miifee lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that microscopic soil pests (nematodes) can destroy, weakening their anchor in the soil. Supporting heavy trees with sturdy wooden Y-props prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni sũ mli kooloi bibii ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛ. (nematodes) baanyɛ afite egbɔjɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli ŋshɔ lɛ mli Tsei ni tsii ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Leaf curl in pepper is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies that transmit plant viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy so the plant can feed its fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ awo yibii.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable farm in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Okɛ nu awo aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli shwane mli. Aloo ani leebi hi fe no?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the plants absorb moisture before the day gets hot. Afternoon watering causes water to evaporate quickly in the sun and can invite fungal diseases on hot wet leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baaŋɔ nu dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu la mli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba baai ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even when I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii moŋ.

english: Crops remove nutrients from the ground every season. Without adding organic matter, rotating crops, or letting the land rest, the soil becomes depleted, leading to smaller yields over time.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji akɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ mli loo kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ, ebaagbɔjɔ, ni no baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and scorching?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains. Full sunlight scorches their young leaves and dries out the topsoil before their root system is fully established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ. Hulu shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ dani shishifãi lɛ gbeɔ naa.

english: Can I plant cassava together with my young cocoa trees on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛfata kookoo tsei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?
