english: It is best to avoid planting cassava directly beside young cocoa. Cassava grows aggressive root systems that compete heavily for water and soil nutrients, which can stunt the growth of young cocoa trees.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he yɛ ŋmei bibii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni kɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii he akaŋ waa lɛ mli. ni baanyɛ atsĩ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ naa

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many small flowers but end up dropping most of them without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but many drop if there are not enough tiny midges to pollinate them, or if the tree experiences water stress and nutrient shortages during flowering.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi fɔfɔi babaoo baagbee shi kɛji akɛ cacao tsei ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ naa nu he haomɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect the plant from losing too much water through evaporation during high heat. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to survive dry conditions.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni tso lɛ akafite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and airflow to dry out the canopy and reduce fungal growth.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ fɔ́ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes the small, dark, sunken spots on my cocoa stems and young pods?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ baa? Sui ni tsuɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ kɛ mi-pods bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: These spots are caused by mirid (capsid) insects that feed on the soft tissue of the tree, injecting sap-damaging toxins that cause the shoots and young pods to wither and die.
ga: Mirid (capsid) kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. kɛ nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei akutsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the water sprouts or chupons growing at the base of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafo nu mli dumɔwui loo chapons fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Chupons consume energy, water, and nutrients from the soil that the tree needs to produce heavy pods. Removing them directs all energy back into pod production.
ga: Chupon kɛ hewalɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ etsitsii ni tsii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa pod feemɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is losing its fertility without taking it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiɛ edɔ ni mikɛyaaa laboratori?

english: If your crops show weak stems, pale or yellowing leaves, slow growth, and noticeably lower yields compared to previous years, the soil is likely depleted of key nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ Pale loo yellow baai, edaa blɛoo, ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color completely from green or dark red to a bright yellow or orange-yellow, and make a hollow sound when tapped lightly with your knuckles.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni efeɔ gbɛɛmɔ ni mli ewo muji kɛ́ okɛ onine tswa fioo.

english: Why do I need to heap my fresh cocoa beans under plantain leaves for a few days before drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii heei toɔ plantain baai ashishi gbii fioo komɛi dani mikɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Heaping cocoa beans under leaves creates heat for fermentation. This crucial process kills the seed bean, changes its color from purple to dark brown, and develops the rich chocolate flavor buyers look for.
ga: Okɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ato baai lɛ ashishi koni ekɛ dɔlɛ aba kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Gbɛ ni he hiaa nɛɛ gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Tsakemɔ su kɛjɛ purple kɛya brown ni mli edɔ ni oná tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from taller plants like plantains or shade trees to survive their first few years. Without shade, direct sunlight and heat stress burn the leaves and dry out the roots, causing the leaves to yellow and drop.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni ohi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and soft right on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads rapidly in high humidity and excess shade. Pruning overhead branches and weeding the farm lets sunlight and air dry out the pod canopy, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ kookoo diji baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fe nine mli lɛ. Nibii ni afoɔ yɛ yiteŋ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛyaa ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Why do my maize plants remain short and turn light green or yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ efee kuku lolo ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize plants usually suffer from a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow tall and green. Applying fertilizer or well-composted manure early in the plant's life provides the necessary nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni ji yellow lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha ená nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there small holes and chewing marks in the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni chew okadii yɛ?

english: Holes in the central leaf whorl of corn plants are a classic sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Finding them early and applying approved controls directly into the leaf center prevents them from destroying the growing point of the plant.
ga: Buu ni yɔɔ ŋmã tso ko baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi. Ehe miihia ni ona amɛ mra. Ni kɛ akɛ nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akudɔɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much standing water for long periods, starving the roots of oxygen. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu ni ekã shi babaoo be kakadaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do my seed yams start sprouting inside my storage barn before the planting season even starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ po jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Seed yams sprout prematurely when stored in warm, bright, or humid conditions, which tricks the tuber into thinking it is in the soil. Storing yams in a cool, dark, and well-ventilated shade barn keeps them dormant longer.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ mra kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ, loo he ko ni mli edɔ, ni no baaha ŋmeii lɛ asusu akɛ amɛyɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes wo he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop to the ground without developing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsɔko pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat stress or dry soil during flowering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering or mulching helps the plant retain its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛna piŋmɔ yɛ latsaa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ewo yibii.

english: Why does the soil in my tomato patch dry out and form hard cracks just a day after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ mli egbi ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ gbi kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil cracks quickly when it lacks organic matter and is left bare under direct sunlight. Covering the soil with a layer of dry grass or leaves (mulch) shades the ground, traps moisture, and stops the soil surface from hardening.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli, ni ashi lɛ yɛ he ko ni hulu la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (Mulch) Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaaa sũ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my primary crop help my farm produce more yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that collect nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This enriches the soil naturally, feeding the neighboring crops without relying entirely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ niyenii ni okɛ ohe akafɔ̃ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: Why are my plantain stalks growing very thin and producing small, light bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Plantain stems grow thin when too many sucker shoots sprout around the mother plant and compete for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers to leave only one strong stem per mat yields much larger bunches.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe. Amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ amli bɔni afee ni tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ashwɛ yɛ mat kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei babaoo aba.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the sunlight so the plant can make enough food through its leaves, which leads to much larger and healthier tubers underground.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ jeɔ hulu la mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ ekɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa aba. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii ni dara babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know which plantain suckers to leave around the main trunk and which ones to cut off?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male plantain tsei ni esa akɛ mashi yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he kɛ nɔ ni esa akɛ mafo?

english: You should keep 'spear suckers', which have narrow, sword-like leaves, because they grow into strong fruiting plants. Cut off 'water suckers' with broad leaves, as they produce weak stems and smaller bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ‘spear bamboo shoot’ ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ klante lɛ ahi shi. Akɛni edaa ni etsɔɔ aduawai tso ni he wa hewɔ lɛ, shwiemɔ ‘suckers’ lɛ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ejaakɛ enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee blɛoo ni amɛgbala amɛhe amɛwo kui bibii amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which helps leaves stay green and strong. Adding compost or a nitrogen fertilizer early in the growing stage will help them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he mra yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava crop producing very bushy leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Too many leaves with small tubers happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. Nitrogen makes the plant grow top leaves, while potassium is what makes the roots swell into big tubers.
ga: Baai bibii ayitsei babaoo baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Shi potassium lɛ ji nɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my garden vegetables wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil still has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: When the midday sun is strong, leaves lose water faster than the roots can pump it up. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from losing more water, and it usually bounces back by evening.
ga: Kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli wa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre nu lɛ. Tso lɛ baagbo be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni elaaje lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ gbɛkɛ

english: What causes my green tomatoes to turn black and rotten at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tomato eŋɔli lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ shishigbɛ dani ekwɛ̃?

english: This rot is caused by a shortage of calcium inside the developing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering that prevents the plant from taking up minerals properly from the soil.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aŋɔ minerals ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by a virus spread by these same insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ latex ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nɔŋŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the tree during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is black pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let light and air in helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela, ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afolɔ hulutsoo kroko mli koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers fall off the branches without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if the tree experiences stress from dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or damage from tiny pests like mirids that feed on delicate flower stems.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo nɔ ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli.

english: Why are insects attacking my cowpea crop right when the flowers start opening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kɛji amɛbɔi fɔmɔ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar that attracts pests like pod borers and thrips. Protecting the crop during flowering is critical because these insects feed on the flowers and prevent pods from forming.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ nu ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ pod borers kɛ thrips. Nibii ni abuɔ he yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ he miihia ejaakɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmeii ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra shoots growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain tsei lɛ je kpo.

english: If you leave too many shoots around one main plantain stem, they all fight for the same nutrients and water in the soil. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoots, which results in larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oshi ŋmeii ni bɔleɔ he lɛ, tso titri kome lɛ fa tsɔ. Nakai tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ. ni haa anáa plantains wuji

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil. It can also happen if the soil stays waterlogged for too long, which prevents the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aye niyenii.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny brown powders inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni powda fioo ko ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the leaves at the center of the plant during the day and chew through the young shoots, leaving behind small holes and waste.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛtsɔ bu bibioo ko kɛ jwɛi ni amɛshiɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot or when the plant experiences extreme dry stress. It can also happen if you give the plant too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes it grow big leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ ni naa wa waa akɛ ebaagbi. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha otsei lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa baai wuji yɛ yibii najiaŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the underside of the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. They droop to protect themselves from excessive sun, but usually recover by evening when the temperature drops.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛsheɔ gbeyei koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɛɔ shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and cracks begin to show in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni ŋmeii jeɔ shishi amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Staking gets yam leaves off the ground so they catch direct sunlight to produce food for the tuber. It also keeps the leaves off damp soil, which prevents fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Staking jieɔ sweet potato baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Planting maize on the same plot every season drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests to build up in the soil. Rotating with legumes like groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ haa abɛi lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii atsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is blast disease, and how does it affect my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji shãa hela? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Blast disease is a fungal infection that attacks plants like rice and cereals. It creates dark spots on the leaves and stems, causing the plant to dry up, wilt, and die if it is not treated early.
ga: Blast hela ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmaa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsɔi ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: How do crop diseases get into the soil and stay there after harvest?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When infected leaves, stems, or fruits drop to the ground, the germs causing the disease can survive in the soil or crop debris. When you plant new crops in that same soil, the germs jump onto the new plants.
ga: Kɛji baai, tsei ashishifãi, loo aduawai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ Helai ni kɛ hela lɛ baa lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli. Kɛji odu tso hee yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ Helatsɛ lɛ baaju kɛya tsei heei anɔ.

english: What should I do if a severe disease completely ruins my crop field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji hela ko ni naa wa kpata miŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ kwraa?

english: When a disease destroys the whole field, you need to clear away all infected plants, remove weeds, and burn or properly dispose of the debris so you can clear the land and start planting fresh again from the beginning.
ga: Kɛ hela lɛ kpata he fɛɛ he lɛ Ebaabi ni ojie tsei fɛɛ ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ, ojie jwɛi lɛ, ni oshã loo okɛ jwɛi lɛ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni obɔi dumɔ ekoŋŋ kɛjɛ shishijee.

english: How can I protect my food crops from getting disease outbreaks in the first place?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miniyenii ni miduɔ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ni baa lɛ ahe?

english: You can prevent diseases by planting clean, disease-resistant seeds, keeping your farm free of weeds, practicing crop rotation, and consulting extension officers early for recommended sprays or organic treatments.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsĩ hela naa kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni he tse ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Ha jwɛi akafee oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ ni okɛ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ agba sane mra koni onine ashɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni akɛ tsofai fɔji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds and stones from my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie jwɛi kɛ tɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ko mli dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Stones block young crop roots from growing deep into the soil, and weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops. Clearing them gives your plants the best environment to grow strong.
ga: Tɛi tsiɔ tsei bibii ashishifãi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ni jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná shihilɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara waa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops weak and more likely to get sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni hela baa mɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds crowd around your crops and absorb the water and fertilizer meant for your food plants. Weakened crops don't have enough energy to fight off plant diseases and insect attacks.
ga: Jwɛi baabɔle onibii ahe ni amɛbaaŋɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii. Tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawu amɛshi tsei ahe helai kɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my food plants need to produce healthy flowers before giving me a harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi niyenii tsei lɛ awo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers are the part of the plant responsible for making seeds and fruits. Healthy flowers get pollinated by insects or wind, which allows them to swell up and turn into the food you harvest.
ga: Fɔfɔi ji tso fã ni woɔ dumɔwui kɛ aduawai. Kplukai loo kɔɔyɔɔ haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ pollen. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni obaakpa.

english: Why do some of my crops start rotting from the ground up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi miibɔi fitemɔ kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Rotting at the soil level is usually caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial diseases, often triggered when water sits around the base of the plant for too long after heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ mli fitemɔ baa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu hi tso lɛ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: Who can I call to help me understand what is wrong with my crops when I see strange sickness on the farm?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ matsɛ koni eye ebua mi ni manu nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ shishi kɛ́ mina helai ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should reach out to your local agricultural extension officer or trained crop advisors. They have scientific training to inspect your crops, identify the exact disease, and show you how to treat it.
ga: Esa akɛ oya okwaayeli he nitsulɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ŋaawolɔ ni atsɔse lɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ. Amɛyɛ jeŋ nilee mli tsɔsemɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli. Tsɔɔmɔ hela pɔtɛɛ ni otsɔɔ bɔ ni atsaa hela

english: How can I tell if an infected crop can still be saved or if it needs to be uprooted?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji abaanyɛ ahere ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ayiwala lolo loo ehe miihia ni ajie kɛjɛ shishi?

english: If only a few outer leaves have spots, you can usually save the plant by trimming them or using treatment. But if the main stem is rotten or the plant has completely dried up, it is best to remove it to prevent spreading the illness.
ga: Kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ ohere tso lɛ yiwala kɛtsɔ tso lɛ ni ooofo loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishitso titri lɛ egbo loo tso lɛ egbi kwraa. Esa akɛ ajie amɛ koni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is essential plant food. The plant moves nitrogen from old lower leaves to feed the young top leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early helps keep the whole plant green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛɔ shi.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains specific nutrients from the soil and lets pests multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and stops pests from building up.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ehaaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ama shi.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves burn and drop off when I clear all the large forest trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo lɛ baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle mihe lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight without shade. Tall forest trees act as natural umbrellas that lower heat and hold moisture in the air so young cocoa can survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ nɔ kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ amɛhe. Koo mli tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa dɔlɛ baa shi ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and droop during hot afternoons even when the soil isn't completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko kwraa lolo?

english: Cassava plants curl their leaves in intense midday heat to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun. This traps internal moisture and prevents water loss until temperatures cool down.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha nu ahi mli ni nu lɛ akafite kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak if both are receiving the exact same rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ amɛ fɛɛ amɛnáa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ kome pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and aggressively take up the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow tall.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛmɔɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ mli lɛ waa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings very close together so I can fit more crops on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ makwɛ nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots compete underground for space and food, resulting in many thin, useless roots instead of large, heavy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni he ehiaaa lɛ baa yɛ bulb agbo ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Why didn't my maize seeds sprout after I buried them deep underground to keep birds from eating them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni okpoi akaye amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds carry only a small burst of stored energy to shoot upward through the dirt. If buried too deep, the shoot exhausts all its energy before reaching the surface and dies buried in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Tsoi lɛ ahewalɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ dani amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ ni afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the roots of my pepper plants rot and turn soft when rainwater stands on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nu damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans do. Waterlogged soil suffocates the roots, causing root rot and causing the plant to wither and die.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high, water supply is irregular, or bees are not present to pollinate them. Keeping soil moist and providing light shade during intense heat helps set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. Aloo ŋmeii komɛi bɛ ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I cut off extra side shoots from my tomato plants when extra stems could mean more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ? Tso lɛ yibii ni fata he lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Allowing too many stems forces the plant to divide its food among many small branches, resulting in tiny, poor-quality tomatoes. Pruning side stems directs food into growing fewer, larger, and healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii babaoo yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aja eniyenii lɛ ewo tsei niji bibii babaoo amli, ni no baaha ená tomato bibii ni ehiii kwraa. Side pruning baaha tso lɛ adara bibioo, agbo ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant new improved orange varieties instead of saving seeds from local oranges like akutuo?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu citrus henɔi ni atsake lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaabua dumɔwui kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli akutuo tamɔ akutuo mli lɛ,

english: Improved orange varieties are bred to produce sweeter fruit, yield faster, and resist common pests, whereas seeds saved from traditional local fruits often take many years to produce fruit and may not retain the parent tree's quality.
ga: Akwɛ citrus tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni ŋɔɔ fe tsutsu lɛ. Ehaa nibii feɔ oya ni eteɔ shi ewoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli akusum aduawai amli lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii. ni ekolɛ ehiɛɛɛ tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli

english: Why is it better to plant grafted fruit seedlings instead of planting seeds directly into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu aduawai ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Grafted seedlings grow faster and produce fruit much earlier than seeds, and they guarantee that the new tree will produce the exact same high-quality fruit as the mother tree.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya fe dumɔwui. Ni ama nɔ mi akɛ tso hee lɛ baawo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why will my crops produce smaller harvests if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak, thin stems and small, poor-quality fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ aduawai bibii ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why do the leaves on my orange trees turn yellow even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged and preventing the roots from breathing properly.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛmu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young orange fruits keep falling off the tree before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange bibii lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Young fruit drops off early when the tree faces sudden dry spells, attacks from fruit flies or bugs, or a lack of nutrients needed to hold the weight of the fruit.
ga: Yibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo be trukaa. Tso yibii mli ŋmeii loo koolooi tutuamɔ loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tso yibii lɛ tsiimɔ ni bɛ

english: Why do my fruit trees produce plenty of flowers but fail to form any actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ yibii lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii babaoo shi ebɛ yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers fail to turn into fruit if there are no bees or insects around to pollinate them, or if extreme heat and lack of water cause the flowers to dry up and fall off.
ga: Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee aduawai kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii bɛ amɛhe ni baawo amɛmli, loo kɛji latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ ha amɛgbi ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to cut off healthy-looking branches inside my orange tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei amli lɛ?

english: Pruning crowded inner branches lets sunlight and fresh air reach the whole tree, which stops fungal diseases from growing and helps the tree direct energy into growing bigger fruits.
ga: Mligbɛ tsei ni afolɔ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he. Enɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do insect pests appear on my farm in huge numbers right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The rain causes crops to sprout soft, young shoots and leaves, which provide rich food for insects to feed on and reproduce rapidly.
ga: Nugbɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ tsei bibii kɛ baai. Enɛ haa kooloi bibii lɛ náa niyenii babaoo ni amɛyeɔ ni amɛfɔɔ oya.

english: How do weeds actually slow down the growth of my main crops?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha mitso titri lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and space from the soil, starving your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii titrii lɛ.

english: How can I keep my harvested oranges fresh so they do not rot before reaching the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-orange lɛ ahi shi ehee koni ekafite dani eshɛ jara nɔ?

english: Harvesting fruits carefully without bruising them, keeping them in cool shaded areas, and avoiding direct contact with damp soil helps preserve their freshness and market value.
ga: Yibii ni oookpa jogbaŋŋ ni okɛwooo mli Okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ Ebaaye ebua ni eha ehe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi jara nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen nutrients, or there is too much water sitting at the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure helps the leaves turn dark green again so the plant can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nu babaoo ebua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ koni ewo tsei lɛ adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in open land under full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains beside cocoa creates natural umbrella shade, keeping the cocoa cool and moist while it gets established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli shade aba. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully grown and ready for harvest under the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the ground near the base of the plant begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: What is eating small holes inside the middle leaves of my corn plants, and how do I fix it?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ ŋmãa tso ko teŋgbɛ baa mli Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a common pest that hides in the funnel of corn plants. Applying approved pest control or neem leaf extract directly into the center funnel early in the morning kills them off.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli ŋmeii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe amɛ.

english: Will planting cowpea beans between my rows of maize steal food from my maize plants?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaju niyenii kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli?

english: No, cowpea beans actually help maize. Legumes like cowpea pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as free plant food for the maize beside it.
ga: Dabi, cowpea yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to spend time tying my yam vines to tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛfi sweet potato wain tsei ahe yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves onto poles gets them closer to sunlight so the plant can make more food to grow big tubers underground, while keeping leaves off wet soil prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulu la babaoo. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aná niyenii babaoo lɛ, nyɛkwɛa bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni akaye baai lɛ ahe helai.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds while my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop roots are small and weak, so fast-growing weeds will steal their water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, stunt their growth before they can mature.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi dani amɛshɛɔ dalɛ he.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants dropping off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures get too hot, water is uneven, or soil nutrients are lacking, which stresses the plant and prevents it from holding onto the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu lɛ ejaaa. loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoot suckers growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi.

english: Having too many suckers forces the main plantain tree to share its food and water, resulting in small bunches. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem yields big fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋhosomɔi babaoo baaha plantain titri lɛ aja niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji niji bibii Kɛ́ ahiɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ woɔ yibii wuji.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the roots of my vegetables help them grow during dry heat?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te mi shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket that traps moisture in the dirt, protects roots from hot sun, and stops weeds from sprouting.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Buu shishifãi ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning purple and the stalks staying short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ purple ni ŋmeii lɛ efee kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Purple leaves and stunted growth usually mean the soil lacks phosphorus. Phosphorus is a vital nutrient that helps young plants build strong root systems and sturdy stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Fosforo ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans in my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny root nodules that pull nitrogen from the air back into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits rotting and turning black before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifite ni etsɔ ediŋŋ dani etsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often caused by uneven watering or dry spells during fruit development.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo be ni hulu enyɔ shi yɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves on purpose when water is scarce to reduce water loss. The plant goes dormant above ground while keeping the root tubers safe and growing below.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ yiŋtoo ko hewɔ beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baaha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi lɛ. Tso lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛdaraa yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers drop off the branches without producing any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa efeee lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience heat stress, lack of water, or when there are not enough tiny insects called midges in the farm to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji hulutsoo, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds and rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that do not go deep into the ground. When the fruit bunch becomes heavy, the plant easily loses balance in wet, soft soil during heavy storms unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ tsii lɛ Tsei baanyɛ afite amɛhe oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɔ yɛ ahum ni naa wa ko mli. ja tso nibii fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my oil palm trees start drying and turning brown from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miije shishi amɛmiigbi ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Browning leaf tips on oil palms usually indicate potassium deficiency in the soil or severe drought, which prevents the tree from transporting water to the ends of its leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mu tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa eba. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ nu aya ebai lɛ anaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into small cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking leaf sap, or viruses spread by whiteflies. This damages the leaves and prevents the plant from growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ baa mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bent and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers bend and deform when the soil is compacted, hard, or full of stones. The soft growing tip of the yam cannot push straight through hard soil, so it turns around obstacles.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baabɔle amɛhe ni amɛbaafite kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, ewa, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Sweet potatoes lɛ ashishifãi ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ, no hewɔ lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛfo gbɛtsii nibii amli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh soil conditions. Their seeds lie dormant in the soil and react instantly to moisture, growing faster to capture sunlight before cultivated crops can establish.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ. Amɛ dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛ tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ba. Amɛdaraa oya koni amɛná hulu la dani tso lɛ daa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and drying up in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct, harsh sunlight. They need partial shade to keep cool and retain leaf moisture while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi ni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ afee fɛ̃i be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: How do tall plants protect my seedling cocoa from getting damaged by heat?
ga: Te tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahe koni hulutsoo akafite amɛ amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Tall plants with large leaves act like an umbrella, blocking direct overhead sunlight and reducing soil evaporation, which creates a cooler, moister microclimate for young cocoa trees.
ga: Tsei kakadaji ni baai wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ambrela. Etsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛhaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Does mature cocoa need full shade or can it handle direct sunlight?
ga: Ani kookoo ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ he miihia hulutsoo be fɛɛ loo amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ?

english: While young cocoa requires heavy shade to prevent leaf burn, mature cocoa trees need filtered or partial sunlight to produce flowers and healthy pods efficiently without overheating.
ga: Nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo bibii hia hulutsoo ni mli wa koni baa lɛ akashã. Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni atsɔ mli loo fã ko koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdɔɔɔ fe nine.

english: Where is the best spot on my land to plant my plantains so they grow big bunches?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni abaanyɛ adu plantains koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ jwɛi wuji?

english: Plantains thrive best in moist soil where water naturally collects or drains slowly, as their large leaves and soft stems require continuous soil moisture to support heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, he ni nu buaa ehe naa loo ejɛɔ mli fiofio yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai wuji kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni enyɛ eye ebua aduawai ni tsii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants dry out so quickly during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose water rapidly through evaporation. If the soil does not have enough moisture, the plant quickly wilts and struggles to grow.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu lɛ laajeɔ oya yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ewaa akɛ ebaakwɛ̃.

english: Can I plant plantains in the same field alongside my new cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe?

english: Yes, planting plantains with new cocoa is a common practice. Plantains grow fast and provide temporary shade to protect young cocoa from sunburn while giving you food and income before the cocoa matures.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kookoo dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni ebu kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Will planting plantains next to my cocoa steal water away from the cocoa roots?
ga: dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ani mi-cacao tso lɛ baaju nu kɛjɛ cacao shishifãi lɛ amli?

english: When planted with proper spacing in moist soil, plantains actually help keep the surrounding ground cool and retain moisture, which benefits young cocoa plants rather than drying them out.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ gbɛ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, Plantains lɛ baaye abua diɛŋtsɛ ni eha he ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛgbi.

english: Why do extension officers recommend pruning branches from cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or excess branches, allowing air and light to circulate through the canopy. This reduces humidity that causes pod diseases and helps the tree focus energy on pod growth.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la atsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ hela baa tso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ tso lɛ dalɛ he nii.

english: Should I trim off the dead or hanging leaves on my plantain trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo baai ni fĩ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, trimming dead plantain leaves prevents pests from hiding in them, stops the spread of leaf diseases, and allows the plant to send nutrients directly to the stem and growing bunch.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantain baai ni egboi lɛ ni aaafo lɛ tsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe. Kpaa tsei lɛ ahe helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ tsei akui ni miida lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What happens if I leave my cocoa farm untended without pruning or clearing shade?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛtsuuu nii ni mifolɔɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo mijieee ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: If a cocoa farm is neglected, too much shade or overgrown branches will cause high humidity, leading to black pod disease, fewer flowers, and significantly lower cocoa harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aku hiɛ ashwie kookoo ŋmɔji anɔ Shade babaoo loo tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ baaha hulutsoo be babaoo aba. Enɛ haa black pod hela baa, fɔfɔi fioo pɛ kɛ cocoa ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Which side of a cassava stem cutting should face up when I am planting it in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ fã esa akɛ afo ŋmei tso lɛ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ mli?

english: Look closely at the small bumps or buds along the stem where leaves used to grow. Ensure these buds point upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down makes it difficult for roots and shoots to grow, resulting in weak plants and poor yields.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmei bibioo lɛ. loo fɔfɔii bibii ni shwieɔ shi Ebɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishi he ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be ko ni eho lɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa ewaa akɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yam plants need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make food and grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil, exposing the leaves to maximum sunlight while preventing fungal diseases caused by contact with wet ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ amli baa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when many small suckers grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii bibii yɛ lɛ Mɛi pii daa yɛ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he.

english: Too many suckers steal water and nutrients from the main tree. By cutting away the extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones, the mother plant gets enough food and energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso wulu lɛ mli tsei babaoo juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso nyɛ lɛ baaná niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii agboi ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains or leaving forest trees nearby shields the young cocoa from burning heat, keeps the soil moist, and helps them establish safely.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei ni ashi yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kookoo lɛ daa shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without turning into peppers during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing them to drop their flowers to save water and energy. Providing light shade or watering early in the morning helps cool the plants so they can hold their blossoms and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ nyɛɔ pepper tsei anɔ koni amɛgbee shi koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo loo nu wo tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ mli ajɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ abua fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai anaa.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside leaves of my young maize plants, and how do I fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on tender young maize shoot leaves. Checking your farm weekly and applying recommended biological controls or botanical sprays like neem early prevents them from destroying the plant's growing center.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ ahe. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa otsi ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ tamɔ neem awo mli mra. Etsiɔ ŋmɔji anaa koni amɛkafite hei ni tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady with regular watering and adding wood ash or lime to the soil helps the plant absorb calcium properly.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ tso sũ loo lime ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aná calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same piece of land three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows maize pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest life cycles naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ feɔ babaoo. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli wala ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass instead of burning it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni mashã lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) shields it from hot sun, traps soil moisture, suppresses weeds, and breaks down over time into organic fertilizer that feeds your crop roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough moisture for planting maize at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil into a ball in your hand. If it forms a soft ball that holds together without dripping water and crumbles easily when gently pressed, the soil has ideal moisture for seeds to sprout without rotting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu yɛ onine mli. Kɛji akɛ efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ anyɛ nɔ blɛoo lɛ, no lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee.

english: When I harvest my soybeans, is it better to pull the whole plant out of the ground or cut it at the stem?
ga: Soybeans ni akpaa Ani ehi akɛ abaajie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ loo abaafo shishigbɛ?

english: It is much better to cut the stem near the ground rather than pulling the plant out. Cutting leaves the root system intact in the soil, which retains valuable natural nutrients for your field.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ moŋ fe ni oootsi tso lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo lɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. ni buɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jara wa he kɛhaa oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ

english: If I do not own a harvesting machine, how should I manually cut my soybean plants to protect the soil?
ga: Kɛji mibɛ tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi soybean tsei lɛ koni mabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: You can use a sharp sickle or cutlass to cut the stems right above the ground level. This keeps the root system undisturbed in the dirt while allowing you to safely collect the pods.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kakla loo kakla ni naa wa atsu nii. Obaanyɛ ofo tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haaa muji agbala shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ehaa okɛ ŋmeii lɛ toɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Can I use a harvesting machine for my soybean crop, and what benefit does it give me?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-soybean ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii? Ni mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni jɛɔ mli baa?

english: Yes, using a machine speeds up harvesting on large farms and cuts the plant stems precisely above the ground, ensuring the roots stay in the soil to enrich your land.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa nikpamɔ yaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli. ni efoɔ tsei ashishifãi pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ekwɛɔ koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my mature soybean pods dry up and pop open, spilling seeds all over the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean ŋmɔji ni eda lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiitswa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani dumɔwui lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ?

english: This behavior is called pod shattering. When soybean pods become overripe and dry in the sun, they automatically split open to scatter their seeds, which causes heavy grain loss if harvesting is delayed.
ga: Atsɛɔ subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ pod mligbalamɔ. Beni soybean ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ fe nine ni amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Soybean ŋmeii lɛ tswaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛgbɛ dumɔwui lɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ baafite soybean dumɔwui lɛ waa kɛji akɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ fo.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my soybeans so I do not lose my crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa soybeans? Bɔni afee ni miŋmɔshi nibii akafite?

english: You should harvest when the plants turn yellow-brown and mature, but before the pods dry out completely and shatter on their own in the field.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa beni tsei lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara lɛ. Shi jeee dani ŋmeii lɛ agbi kwraa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbee shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What will happen if I leave my ripe soybeans in the field for too many weeks?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi soybeans ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Leaving ripe soybeans in the field too long exposes them to heat, causing the pods to shatter and drop their seeds onto the ground, leaving you with very little crop to sell or eat.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi soybeans ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbálaa ni dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa onáa nɔ ko fioo pɛ ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ loo oye.

english: Why do extension officers say that soybean plants put nitrogen into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ soybean kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soybeans are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the roots remain in the ground after harvest, that stored nitrogen enriches your soil.
ga: Soybeans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ beni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lolo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: If I pull soybean roots out of the dirt during harvest, will my soil lose fertilizer benefits?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajie soybean shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Ani sɛɛnamɔi ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli baa lɛ baaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, pulling out the roots removes the stored nitrogen from the farm. Leaving the root system inside the soil allows it to decay and act as free natural fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishifãi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi shishifãi lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ afite ni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Will leaving my soybean roots in the ground help the next crop I plant on the same land?
ga: Ani soybean shishifãi ni mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, as the buried soybean roots break down, they release natural nitrogen into the soil, which helps feed future crops like maize and reduces the amount of chemical fertilizer you need to buy.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ afu soybean shishifãi lɛ gbee shi. Amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii ni ehaa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli ni esa akɛ ohe lɛ baa shi.

english: Why shouldn't I clear out and throw away the underground parts of my legumes after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mijie mi-legumes lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ shi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Removing the underground roots starves the soil of organic matter and nitrogen. Keeping the root material in the soil maintains soil health and supports long-term farm productivity.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akafee nɔ ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nitrogen. Shishifãi nibii ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa okwaayeli nitsumɔ ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when there are lots of weeds growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni jwɛi babaoo ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. When weeds are present, they steal the food your crops need, causing the plants to grow slowly and stay weak.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Beni jwɛi yɛ lɛ Ebaaju niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: Is it better to burn the cleared bushes on my field or leave the plant debris on the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni ajie yɛ mishia lɛ mli lɛ loo mashi tso lɛ mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving plant debris on the ground as mulch protects the soil from drying out under the hot sun, prevents weed growth, and eventually breaks down to make the soil richer. Burning destroys these valuable natural fertilizers.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ efoɔ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo. Shãa fiteɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa nɛɛ.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds from my farm so my plants stay healthy?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mitsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: You should clear weeds early and regularly, especially during the first few weeks after planting when your crops are young, because young plants are easily choked out by fast-growing weeds.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii mra ni okɛtsu nii daa, titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ beni otsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Ejaakɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ nyɛɔ ejieɔ tsei bibii kɛyaa oya.

english: How do chemical sprays actually help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Chemical sprays protect plants by controlling pests that eat the leaves and killing diseases that weaken the crop. By keeping the plant healthy, the crop can direct all its energy into growing and producing yields.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ buɔ tsei ahe kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ baa lɛ ni egbeɔ helai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui baanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray chemical treatments on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when temperatures are cooler and wind is low, which prevents the liquid from evaporating too quickly or drifting away from the plants.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo shwane mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu waaa lɛ. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ loo ekagbee tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Will applying too much chemical spray help my crops grow faster?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: No, applying too much chemical spray can burn the leaves and damage the root system of your crops, doing more harm than good. It is important to always use the correct recommended amount.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Ekɛ awuiyeli babaoo baa fe kpakpa. Ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofa ni sa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛhaa lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my plants produce smaller crops when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for space, water, and nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough food to produce large fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haaa tso ko bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my young plants turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that your plants are either lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, getting too much or too little water, or being attacked by small insects at the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ loo fioo tsɔ. loo kooloi bibii tutuaa amɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt under the strong sun even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Young seedlings have tender roots that cannot drink water fast enough to replace what high heat dries out from their leaves. Providing light shade or covering the surrounding soil with dry leaves helps keep them cool.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ anu nu oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛkɛto la ni mli egbi ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ. ni haa hulutsoo be fioo Aloo okɛ baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy enough to support good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well, and contains living organisms like earthworms, which help break down organic material into crop food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛgbalaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii.

english: Can I use empty sachet water bags to nurse my crop seeds to save money?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu kotokui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛtsa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni mikɛ shika akafite?

english: Clear or semi-transparent sachet water bags allow light to pass through the sides. Many seeds and young roots cannot grow properly when light reaches them, so clear plastics can stunt or kill your seedlings compared to dark containers.
ga: Saji ni mli tse loo nɔ ni mli tse fioo lɛ haa la tsɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ. Dumɔwui kɛ shishifãi bibii babaoo nyɛɛɛ adara jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni la yɔɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, plastic ni mli tse lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ afee shoo loo egbe amɛ. Kɛ akɛto tsɛnsii ni mli ewo duŋ he

english: Why do agricultural extension officers always recommend black polybags for seed nurseries?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ poly bag diji he ŋaa be fɛɛ be kɛha dumɔwui adumɔ lɛ?

english: Black polybags block all sunlight from passing through the sides. This creates a completely dark environment underground, which protects delicate root systems and encourages strong seedling growth.
ga: Poly kotokui diji tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekabote sɛɛgbɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi shihilɛ feɔ duŋ kwraa. Enɛ buɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ daraa.

english: Can I use clear ice-water plastic bags to raise my oil palm seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ plastic kotokui ni ais ni mli tse yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛdu mu tso dumɔwui?

english: Clear ice-water bags are not good for nursing oil palm seeds because they let light in from all sides. Oil palm roots and kernels need complete shade and darkness to sprout and establish healthy roots.
ga: Ais kotokui ni mli tse lɛ ehiii kɛha mu tso dumɔwui akwɛmɔ ejaakɛ amɛhaa la boteɔ mli kɛjɛɔ he fɛɛ he. Mu tso shishifãi kɛ dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo kɛ duŋ ni yeɔ emuu bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: How does the color of a seedling bag affect how well my crops grow?
ga: Te dumɔwui kotoku lɛ su lɛ saa tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The color determines how much light reaches the soil inside. Dark or black bags completely block out light, which keeps the soil dark and warm for proper seed germination, whereas light-colored or clear bags let harmful sunlight reach the roots.
ga: Su lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ bɔ ni la ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fa ha. Baagi ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ tsiɔ kane naa kwraa. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee duŋ ni edɔ koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kotokui ni mli tse loo ni mli tse lɛ baaha hulu la ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my oil palm seeds fail to sprout when I put them in bright, light-filled conditions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mikɛwo he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palm nuts are sensitive to light during germination. They naturally require dark conditions to trigger sprouting, so exposed light signals harsh conditions and prevents the embryo from developing.
ga: Oil palm ŋmeii lɛ nuɔ la he waa yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛbiɔ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ dani amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, la ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ tsɔɔ shihilɛi ni esaaa, ni ehaaa fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do oil palm nuts sprout much better when buried deep in dark soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni oil palm ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Oil palm nuts prefer complete darkness to germinate. Soil acts as a natural shield against light, providing the dark and steady conditions the seed needs to break its hard shell.
