ga: Oil palm ŋmeii sumɔɔ duŋ kwraa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni tsiɔ la naa. Kwɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ agbala amɛ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ amli yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ duŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Will light passing through the sides of my seedling containers harm my young crops?
ga: Ani la ni boteɔ dumɔ nii lɛ afãi lɛ baaye mi tsei bibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, light penetrating the sides of a container tricks the plant roots into growing incorrectly and can scorch tender new shoots before they emerge above the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, la ni boteɔ tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ lakaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ni ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii heei ashã dani amɛje kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do plant roots always grow down into dark soil instead of towards the light?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi daa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be moŋ fe ni amɛaaya la he lɛ?

english: Roots naturally avoid light to protect themselves from drying out. They are programmed to search for dark, moist areas underground where they can safely anchor the plant and absorb nutrients.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ la he koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he. Afee amɛ gbɛjianɔtoo koni amɛtao hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni edɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: What happens to young crop roots when sunlight hits them through transparent nursery containers?
ga: Mɛni baa tsei bibii ashishifãi anɔ kɛ́ hulu la kpɛ kɛtsɔ tsei akwɛmɔhe ko ni mli tse mli?

english: Direct sunlight hitting exposed roots burns the delicate root tips, stops them from absorbing water properly, and can cause the entire seedling to wither and die.
ga: Hulu la ni tswaa shishifãi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Etsiɔ enaa koni ekaŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. ni ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why is it important for the container around my crop's roots to be completely opaque?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsɛnsi ni bɔle Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni mli tseee kwraa lɛ.

english: An opaque container ensures no light can reach the soil from the top, middle, or sides. This mimics natural deep-soil conditions, allowing roots to spread evenly throughout the whole container.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni hulu bɛ mli lɛ haa kane ko jɛɔ ŋwɛi, teŋgbɛ, loo sɛɛgbɛ kɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ kaseɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsɛnsi lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect them from harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade plants like plantains or shade trees, the intense sun scorches their leaves and weakens the young plant.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo be koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo hulutsoo tsei bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha tsei bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow starting from the bottom when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ shishifã lɛ ji bibioo lolo po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or proper fertilizer early in the season fixes this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when we get heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the soil cannot drain. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps the extra rain flow away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: If I cut off excess branches from my cocoa trees, won't that reduce the number of pods I harvest?
ga: Kɛ mifolɔ niji ni eshwɛ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ani no haŋ ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: Pruning actually increases your yield. Removing unnecessary branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the trunk and remaining branches, encouraging more flowers to turn into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kpojiemɔ baanyɛ aha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ niji ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi babaoo tsɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat or sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil regularly moist and adding dry leaf mulch around the base keeps the plants cool enough to hold their flowers.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa lɛ ye amɛnɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo ehe. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni enyɛ emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows maize pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with beans or groundnuts restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi damɔ nɔ lɛ ni eye ebua abɛi mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to develop black spots and rot completely during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboiɔ kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, cool, and dark environments. Clearing weeds and pruning thick tree branches lets airflow and sunlight in to dry out the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ duŋ. Niji ni mli tse lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together so I can get more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for light, water, and soil food, resulting in small, weak plants. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkpaa babaoo.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my crops with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Nibii ni aduɔ ni baai egbi loo jwɛi?

english: Covering the ground, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the soil too quickly, reduces weed growth, and gradually turns into natural plant food as the leaves decompose.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha hulu lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni fiofio lɛ etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii be mli ni baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young maize plants and leaving small holes?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ bu bibii?

english: That damage is typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm that hide inside the growing center of the plant. Checking fields early allows you to control them before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ baa. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ lɛ dani efiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a critical food for growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves back their dark green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloi ashishifã ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aku sɛɛ afee eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni ebaaha dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer, making the soil richer for maize planted nearby.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes right through the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that burrows into the growing center of corn plants. Applying recommended organic or chemical pest control early in the morning or late evening destroys them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsu nii ni akɛwo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakpata amɛhiɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly and turn yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by the Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies with insecticidal soaps or neem oil and keeping plants watered helps protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛ́ akɛ samla loo neem fɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ye whiteflies lɛ anɔ, ni akɛ nu wo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil traps too much water, causing fungal rot diseases. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rain to drain away quickly so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ fungal rot hela aba. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking holds leaves up to catch light and prevents fungal diseases that live on damp ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni eha niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ koni amɛha la abote mli ni amɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees next to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil cool for young cocoa.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛha kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers fall off without growing into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the trees lack water, suffer from poor soil nutrients, or lack tiny insects called midges that pollinate the flowers. Keeping trees properly fed and avoiding chemical sprays that kill good insects helps pods form.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu bɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni anáaaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni bɛ lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ pollinating hemorrhoids. Kɛ́ oha otsei lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kpakpai lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Watering regularly and feeding the soil helps the plant hold onto its flowers and turn them into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he ko ni dɔɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium bɛ. Nu ni awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does covering the soil around my garden plants with dry grass help them grow in dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, acts like a protective shield. It traps moisture in the dirt so water doesn't evaporate fast in the sun, keeping root systems cool and hydrated.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ muji lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ hulu la kpɛ nu lɛ, efooo oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, their roots and leaves compete with each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to form full, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to give me bigger tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ koni bulbs wuji lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food that feeds the underground tubers. Lifting the vines on stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight while protecting them from ground pests and diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field help my maize crop grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize after groundnuts, the maize feeds on this leftover natural nitrogen.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ ŋmãa baaye nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni eshwɛ nɛɛ.

english: Why am I supposed to place fertilizer a few centimeters away from the plant stem instead of touching it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai 2-3 moŋ fe ni mata he?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the tender plant tissue and roots. Keeping it a short distance away allows soil moisture to dissolve the nutrients safely for the roots to reach.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ fãji kɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. He ni jɛkɛmɔ kuku ni aaakwɛ nɔ Enɛ baaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ niyenii mli nibii amli shweshweeshwe bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool air it needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruit during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages tomato pollen, preventing the flowers from getting fertilized. When temperatures get too high, the plant drops unfertilized flowers to conserve moisture and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Ehaa fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awoko mli lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why are small caterpillars feeding inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye nii yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft, tender leaves inside the central whorl of young maize plants where it is dark and moist. Identifying them early helps you apply control measures before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni edɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ. mra be mli ni ayɔseɔ lɛ Ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ gbɛjianɔtoi akudɔ dani efite he ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when I give my farm enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida fiofio eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa miŋmɔ lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and light meant for your crops. Clearing weeds ensures your main crops get full access to all the nutrients in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ haa otsei titrii lɛ náa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, the stems turn woody, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open from the swollen roots beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ tsɔɔ tso. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest produce weaker plants than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ahereɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ mi tsutsu ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ni woɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose their strength and uniformity in the second generation, leading to smaller yields. Certified seeds are specially produced to guarantee high germination and disease resistance.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛha amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ.

english: Officer, why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow from the bottom of the plant going up?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting at the bottom, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil food. Giving the crop nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves stay green so they can make food for large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ha tsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii wuji ni he wa lɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help make my soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dumɔ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny natural powerhouses on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant harvest is done, that left-behind nutrient feeds the next crop you plant there.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli. Egbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbe naa lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings drop their leaves and die when there are no bigger trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily dry out under full, direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain or shade trees shields the young cocoa from hot sun and keeps the air humid so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does spreading dry grass on top of my soil keep my vegetable crop alive during hot dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa mitsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, acts like a blanket over the earth. It stops the sun from evaporating the water in the ground, keeping the soil cool and moist for the crop's roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa tsei shishifãi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if heavy rains leave water standing in the field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shi nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air to stay healthy just like human beings do. When heavy water sits on top of the soil for too long, it drowns the roots and creates the right environment for dangerous soil fungi to attack and rot the cassava.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji muji lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ koni amɛtutua ŋmei lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes when the hot sun is very fierce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when intense heat causes them stress. Extremely high temperatures damage the pollen inside the flower, so the plant sheds the flower to save its energy until weather conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ haomɔ ba. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my plantain stand give smaller fruit bunches when I leave all the shoot suckers growing around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii bibii beni mikɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ shwieɔ lɛ?

english: All the suckers attached to the main plantain tree compete for the same food and water in the ground. Leaving too many suckers steals energy away from the main stalk, resulting in small and weak bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei fɛɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaju hewalɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei niji lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my crops seem to stop growing tall once they start showing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kɛji ebɔi fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: When a crop flowers, it switches its energy away from making new stem and leaves to focus entirely on developing seeds, fruits, or cobs. Height growth slows down naturally so the plant can feed the upcoming harvest.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ Eshiɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai heei ni efeɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama dumɔwui, aduawai, loo ŋmeii muu fɛɛ ni baa lɛ nɔ. Akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and bigger than my crops even though I planted them around the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya ni amɛdara fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Nɛgbɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally aggressive at taking water, sunlight, and food from the earth. Because they adapt faster than cultivated crops, they will crowd out your farm crops if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa, ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛfeɔ basabasa ni amɛnuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛbaaye oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji ajieee mra.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small wrinkled cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding underneath the leaf and sucking out the plant sap. This feeding damages the leaf growth and can spread viral diseases to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Niyenii nɛɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ agbɛ ashwã tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my maize crops are producing as many bags as my land can support?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ miiwo kotokui babaoo bɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ?

english: Crops yield best when planted with proper spacing and adequate nutrients. If your crop plants are healthy with dark green leaves and produce well-filled cobs across the whole field, your land is performing at its full potential.
ga: Tsei woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii. Etsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I am delayed in harvesting them when they mature?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛkpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ beni amɛshɛ shweremɔ he lɛ?

english: Leaving mature crops in the field for too long exposes them to pests, mould, and birds. Grains can fall off the stalks onto the ground, and root crops can rot, leading to severe loss in harvest quantity and quality.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai, ŋmeii, kɛ okpoi baanyɛ aye amɛ oya. Dumɔwui baanyɛ ajɛ tsei lɛ amli agbee shikpɔŋ. ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ agbo. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ falɛ kɛ bɔ ni ehi ha lɛ laajeɔ waa.

english: Why do my crops suddenly dry up and fail before reaching harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gĩɔ trukaa ni amɛfiteɔ dani kpamɔɔ be shɛɔ lɛ?

english: Crops usually collapse early because of depleted soil nutrients, sudden droughts, or diseases attacking their root systems. When roots are weak or diseased, the crop cannot draw water or food from the soil to stay alive.
ga: Tsei lɛ fɔɔ gbee oya be mli ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ. hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa loo helai ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ Beni shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ ajie nu loo niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my farmland produce fewer bags of crops each year even when I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotokui amli lɛ faaa daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ.

english: Crops remove nutrients from the ground as they grow. If you do not replenish the soil with organic manure or fertilizers after each harvest, the soil becomes exhausted and produces smaller yields over time.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my planted crops and slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally aggressive at taking water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. If they are not cleared early, they steal essential food away from your crops, causing your crops to grow slowly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ajieee mra Amɛbaaju niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ onibii amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, onibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio.

english: Why do my crop plants grow tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete fiercely for sunlight. The plants spend all their energy growing upward to reach the light instead of using energy to produce heavy fruits or large grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ waa. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii beni amɛdaraa lɛ koni amɛná la, moŋ fe hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ aduawai ni tsii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why do my crops require more water when they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji ebɔi fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Flowering is the most critical stage of crop development. Plants require extra water to carry food from the roots to form healthy seeds, pods, or fruits. Lack of water at this stage causes flowers to drop off.
ga: Fɔfɔii ni shwereɔ lɛ ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Tsei hia nu kroko koni amɛkɛ niyenii ajɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛfee dumɔwui, ŋmeii, loo aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni bɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo.

english: Why are some crops on the same piece of land ready for harvest while others are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ ŋmɔji lolo lɛ?

english: Uneven crop growth happens when seeds are planted at different depths or when parts of the farm have richer soil and moisture than others. This causes individual plants to develop and mature at different speeds.
ga: Tso lɛ dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. Aloo kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo fe hei krokomɛi. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa ni edaa yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli.

english: Why do cassava roots spoil quickly if left in the ground too long after maturing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ ashi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava reaches full maturity, its roots stop growing and begin to lose starch. If left in wet soil past maturity, the roots quickly attract soil fungi and rot underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ baakpa dalɛ ni amɛbaabɔi ŋmei lɛ shwiemɔ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ fe be ni ato lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ gbalaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it good to plant legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas along with my main crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes have unique roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil food. Planting them alongside major crops enriches the soil naturally and helps your main crop grow stronger.
ga: Legumes yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ srɔto ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ du nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient the crop needs to grow green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores this nutrient to the soil.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for next season's maize?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in their roots. When the roots decay in the ground, they feed natural nitrogen into the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛhaa nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa plants burn under direct, strong sunlight. Leaving canopy trees or planting plantains alongside them provides shade and holds moisture in the ground until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ baashã yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Ni ajieɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Yam leaves need to capture sunlight off the hot ground to manufacture food. Staking keeps leaves away from ground pests and diseases, allowing the plant to direct its energy into growing big underground tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my cassava produce tall stems with many leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi ŋmei bibioo ko yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending food down to expand the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala yitso lɛ mli

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat, dry spells, or overwatering. The plant sheds flowers to conserve energy so it can survive the harsh weather.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hulutsoo be, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ fe nine lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why does planting egusi melon between my crops stop weeds from invading my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Egusi melon ni miduɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haaa jwɛi akabote miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Egusi melon vines spread wide across the ground with big leaves. This creates a leafy cover that blocks light from weed seeds in the soil, stopping them from growing.
ga: Egusi melon wain tsei ni gbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ baai wuji. Enɛ haa baa ni haa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkadara

english: Why do armyworms gather inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miibua amɛhe naa yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: The center funnel of the maize plant is soft, moist, and offers shade from the hot sun, making it the perfect protected spot for caterpillars to feed undetected.
ga: Abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa ehiɛɔ ehe. Enɛ haa efeɔ he ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni abuɔ he kɛhaa ŋmeii ni amɛtaoɔ niyenii ni mɔ ko mɔ ko enaaa amɛ.

english: This rot happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium due to irregular watering. Consistent moisture allows the roots to steadily draw up calcium into the developing fruit.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛgbalaa calcium kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my hybrid maize harvest give smaller yields when I plant them again next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent lines to give high yields only in the first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, producing weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi srɔtoi enyɔ amli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade trees or fast-growing food crops like plantains to block the hot sun and keep the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa plants develop strong roots.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni wa yɔɔ.

english: No, planting crops too closely causes them to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed and grow strong, resulting in bigger ears of maize and a better overall yield.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni edaa jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ wuji ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put stakes or wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso loo tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible to make energy for growing large tubers. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛwo bulb agboi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ foliar hela kɛ fitemɔ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed animal manure will help the plant turn dark green and grow vigorously.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning black and rotten before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This problem, called blossom-end rot, is caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, often due to dry soil or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant take up soil calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops at the exact same time I place the seeds in the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli yɛ be kome too mli ni dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, seeds already carry enough internal food to sprout. You should wait until the seeds germinate and grow their first leaves before applying fertilizer, so the roots are developed enough to absorb the nutrients.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwu lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ emli koni ekwɛ̃. Esa akɛ omɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni klɛŋklɛŋ baai lɛ aba dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ aná shweremɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around them for too long because the roots drown without air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: What is making holes in the center leaves of my maize plants and leaving behind dirt that looks like sawdust?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miifee bu yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni amɛshiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing point of the maize plant. Applying recommended biopesticides or putting clean ash or sand into the central leaves early in the morning can help control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he akɛ akɛtsu nii loo akɛ sũ ni he tse loo ŋã fata baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to weed my farm within the first few weeks after my seeds sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crop seedlings and will quickly steal the available water, light, and soil food. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crops get all the resources they need during their critical growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei bibii lɛ ana nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me not to plant maize on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛkadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and soil diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores fertility to the soil and stops pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the tall trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and lose moisture too fast. Tall shade trees act as natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa from heat stress until the plants grow strong enough to endure more sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la babaoo gbɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to grow up tall wooden stakes to produce big tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves make food for the plant using sunlight. Staking lifts the vines high off the wet ground so all the leaves get full sunlight and air circulation, allowing the plant to make maximum energy and send it down to swell the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips on maize are usually a sign of nitrogen hunger. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for deep green, healthy leaves; when the soil lacks it, the plant steals nitrogen from older lower leaves to keep new top leaves alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji nitrogen hɔmɔ he okadi. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwie shi lɛ, tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ aná hegbɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my land make the maize crop grow better the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground. When you harvest them, that trapped food stays behind in the soil as free natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Niyenii ni ekã lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my granular fertilizer on the soil right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji granular lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away loose fertilizer from the topsoil into water paths before the plant roots get a chance to drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist or before a light drizzle so it melts directly into the root zone.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nu gbɛi amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo dani nugbɔ fioo ko baanɛ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ shishifã lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the small sucker shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: When too many suckers grow around the mother plantain stem, they steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight from it. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong followers, ensuring the main stem grows big, healthy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu lɛ tso lɛ he lɛ Amɛbaaju nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ nakai tso lɛ mli lɛ Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni he wa koni ekwɛ akɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ daa ni etsɔ aduawai akuu agbo ko ni he wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and twisting into tiny shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites that feed on leaf juices and spread plant viruses. Spraying appropriate organic or chemical controls early prevents them from stopping plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni yeɔ baa mli nu ni egbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛbuɔ helai ahe lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akakpa edalɛ.

english: Why do the blossom flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot, water is too scarce, or insects fail to pollinate them. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for survival rather than spending it on developing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo kooloi nyɛŋ afee pollination. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaafite shika yɛ aduawai lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mli lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil during periods of excessive rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains flood waterlogged soil with poor drainage, the roots suffocate from lack of oxygen and decay due to rot-causing fungi.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ, ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ kɛ fitemɔ hewɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become tough, woody, and hard to cook if I leave them in the ground past maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa, amɛfeɔ tsei, ni kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛdara lɛ, ehoomɔ wa lɛ?

english: As cassava plants grow past their peak harvest period, they stop storing food starch in the roots and start converting that starch into tough structural fibers, making the tubers hard and unpalatable.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ dara kɛho amɛkpamɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he lɛ Amɛkpaa niyenii ŋmei ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛtsakeɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishitoo ni wa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ wa ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth, or that the soil is waterlogged. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off before growing into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree suffers from water stress, lacks nutrients, or when natural pollinators like tiny midges are absent. High heat and dry winds can also cause the tree to drop flowers to protect its water supply.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa fɔfɔii tamɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ laaje. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baanyɛ aha tsei ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu jɛɛhei ahe.

english: Why does my cassava farm produce tall plants with huge leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ tsei kakadaji ni baai lɛ dara shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant directs its energy into leafy stem growth above ground instead of storage roots below. Cassava needs soil rich in potassium to produce large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛyaa tso ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia cassava koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant plantain suckers alongside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ kookoo dumɔwui duɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that provide living shade and keep the air moist, protecting cocoa plants during their fragile first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei ni waaa lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my seed yam pieces rot in the soil before they even sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam pieces rot when planted in heavy, waterlogged soil that lacks good drainage, or when the raw cut surfaces of the seed yam are not allowed to dry properly in shade before planting, making them vulnerable to soil fungi.
ga: Sweet potato fãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ waa ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. aloo be mli ni aŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni etse lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani adu. Enɛ haa ŋmeii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: This leaf damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the funnel of the maize leaf during the day and feeds at night. Inspecting the center whorl early and applying suitable treatments stops the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli ni amɛtaoɔ niyenii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofafeemɔ ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha nɔ ni efite lɛ akpa.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually triggered by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites, or a virus transmitted by whiteflies. Controlling these tiny pests early prevents the disease from spreading across your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. small pest control Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is caused by bacterial wilt or fungal root rot living in the soil. These germs block the inner water channels inside the plant stem, preventing water from reaching the upper branches.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ mli shwiemɔ trukaa lɛ baa ji helai ni shwieɔ shi loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ tsiɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ amli lɛ anaa. Tsĩ nu naa koni ekashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: Growing maize on the same soil repeatedly depletes specific soil nutrients and lets maize-focused pests and diseases multiply in the ground. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts rebuilds soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi baa shi. ni eha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni ŋmãa kɛbaa lɛ ayi afa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds early when my crop is still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, shallow root systems that cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Weeding early eliminates this competition so your crop gets full strength during its initial growth.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ ashi akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa akaŋshii nɛɛ baa shi koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo yɛ amɛ shishijee dalɛ be mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the large shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need partial shade to survive. Clearing all the surrounding forest trees exposes the tender plants to direct scorching sun and dry winds, which burns the leaves and deprives the plant of moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ koo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ yeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ ashã ni ebaaha tso lɛ aná nu.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt completely in the afternoon sun but look fresh again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kwraa yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli shi amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ leebi lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than their roots can take it up from the soil. Overnight, as temperatures drop, the roots absorb enough moisture to restore the plant's leaves.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ baai lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build green leaves. Applying organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their healthy color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do extension officers tell me that planting beans or cowpeas makes my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔ ko kɛɔ mi akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have tiny organisms on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, leaving free nutrients behind for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eshiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is heavy rainfall for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the field without draining away, it drowns the roots and causes rot-causing fungi to multiply.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbee ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before turning into fruits during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms as a defense mechanism when they experience heat stress or lack water. Consistent watering during dry spells helps the plant hold onto flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ hebuu gbɛ kɛji amɛkɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ loo nu ni faaa kpe. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when heavy wind blows during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa waa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems. When soil gets soft from rain and the plant grows a heavy fruit bunch, wind easily topples it unless you prop it up with strong wooden poles.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli ni tsei lɛ fee aduawai akui ni tsii Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa lɛ oya. Ja okɛ tso ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high up to capture sunlight for food creation while keeping leaves off hot soil, which prevents leafy fungal diseases and results in larger tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni emɔ hulu la ni ekɛfee niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Enɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa, ni ebaaha bulbs lɛ afee wuji.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing the center leaves inside my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiye teŋgbɛ baai ni yɔɔ mibii bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms that target the soft central whorl of young maize plants where it is moist. If left unchecked, they eat the emerging leaves and reduce your crop yield.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli efɔ lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛbaaye baai ni miiba lɛ ni amɛbaahã onibii ni oooha lɛ aba shi.

english: Can I plant cassava close to my young cocoa trees, or will it affect how the cocoa grows?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe? Aloo ebaana kookoo lɛ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ loo enaŋ?

english: Cassava roots grow very quickly and spread wide, which means they will compete with young cocoa trees for soil nutrients and water. It is better to plant plantain for shade instead of cassava.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa he fɛɛ he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛkɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Ehi akɛ ooodu plantains kɛha hulutsoo yɛ ŋmei najiaŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily scorch under direct, strong sunlight during the dry season. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside young cocoa protects them from harsh heat and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ lɛ nu leebi moŋ?

english: Pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up under intense heat. Putting dry leaves or straw around the base of the plant (mulching) keeps the roots cool and preserves soil moisture throughout the hot afternoon.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ shwane mli hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the middle leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves from the tip inward usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow dark green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛyaa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baai ni tsuɔ waa lɛ akwɛ̃. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ, eŋɔli dalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do older farmers say that planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my farm makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural nodes on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: What is the benefit of adding dark compost manure to my field if I can just buy synthetic fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he? Kɛji manyɛ mahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ

english: While chemical fertilizer gives quick plant food, natural compost acts like a sponge that improves the soil's ability to hold water and keeps the soil soft so roots can spread easily, keeping land healthy for many seasons.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya moŋ, shi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii hu tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni ehaa sũ lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ bei babaoo mli.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoot suckers growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ

english: If too many small suckers grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from the main tree. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main tree to make large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni miida yɛ he lɛ Plantain kome fa tsɔ. Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwɛɔ, ni no haa tso titri lɛ woɔ yibii ni tsii ni dara.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants make food in their leaves using sunlight to grow big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground away from pests and spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ feɔ niyenii, ni amɛkɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ekɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ, ni egbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo.

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no insects around to pollinate them. Consistent watering and planting flowering herbs nearby to attract insects helps fruit form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bɛ ni ebɔle he ni baawo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, nu ni oooha daa kɛ tsofai ni woɔ fɔfɔi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Koni agbala kooloi lɛ baaye abua ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing a white powdery substance under them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni nɔ ko ni tamɔ powda yɛŋ yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with white powder are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects called mealybugs. Using clean planting sticks free of pests and letting natural helpful insects eat them keeps your cassava farm safe.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ powda yɛŋ ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ kɛbaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni he tse ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii, ni oha adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ aye amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni o-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does low-land rice grow better in fields that hold shallow standing water compared to dry hillside soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ mli lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ́ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Low-land rice varieties are suited for wet conditions where standing water stops harmful weeds from growing and keeps the roots constantly nourished and hydrated for higher yields.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ hi kɛha shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli koni jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui akakwɛ̃. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle strong direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi cacao tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize relies on for healthy foliage growth. Adding manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the crop regain its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele damɔ baai ni mli wa lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni onibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm help feed other crops I plant later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in little nodules on their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil, natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes, tamɔ ŋmei, gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ kui bibii amli kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo. Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my granular fertilizer right when a heavy rain starts falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ granular fertilizer wooo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash fertilizer off the topsoil or push it too deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach it. Applying fertilizer when the soil is damp, rather than during heavy downpours, ensures the plant absorbs the nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eshɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava sticks too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the stems compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall and thin with small, watery tubers instead of big, healthy roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ, ni eyɛ shishifãi bibii ni nu eyi mli obɔ yɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli wa najiaŋ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajie mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main mother plant. Pruning them so only two or three strong shoots remain allows the mother plant to produce a much larger bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni eshi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2-3 pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ awo tsei babaoo.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop to the ground before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress, dry soil, or uneven watering. Mulching the base of the plant to keep the soil cool and watering consistently early in the morning helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper blossom gbee shi ji dɔlɛ haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ha tso lɛ shishi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni awo nɔ nu daa leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, which often happens when watering is uneven. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots draw calcium up from the ground into the fruits.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbalaa calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight and make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, reducing disease and allowing maximum food to travel down into the growing yam tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛhoo nii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ha helai aba shi ni oha niyenii babaoo atsɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do dark or white spots spread across my crop leaves during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji loo eyɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi tsei lɛ ahe fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and wet leaves create the perfect environment for fungal diseases to multiply. Spacing plants far enough apart allows wind to blow through and dry the leaves faster, preventing fungal growth.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni ebaaha baai lɛ agbi oya. Etsiɔ fungal dalɛ naa

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides shade and maintains soil moisture, protecting young trees while they mature.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Buu tsei bibii ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?
