english: Yellow leaves on maize plants usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or urea helps the plants regain their deep green color and produce strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa su ni mli kwɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting due to excessive heat, irregular watering, or insect pests like thrips. Ensuring consistent soil moisture and protecting plants during intense dry heat preserves the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ thrips, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ahebuu yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: What happens if I leave my cassava roots in the ground past their maturity time?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe be ni ataoɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots left in the ground too long become tough and woody, losing their starch content and soft cooking quality. In heavy rainy conditions, delayed harvest can also lead to root rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee tso. Enɛ haa ashikishaŋ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ kɛ bɔ ni ahoɔ nii blɛoo lɛ. Yɛ shihilɛi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa mli lɛ, ŋmaakpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afite.

english: How deep into the soil should I push my maize seeds during planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kɛya shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ yɛ dumɔ be mli?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep. Planting too shallow makes seeds easy targets for birds and dry air, while planting too deep prevents young shoots from pushing out of the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimita 3 kɛyashi 5. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ haa okpoi kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ baatsi ŋmeii bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does letting grass grow around my cassava farm lower my final yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ahaa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ebɔleɔ he lɛ? Ani mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ miiha mi naagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiba shi?

english: Weeds and grass steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your cassava plants. Clearing weeds early ensures all the soil goodness goes into developing big cassava tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ o-cassava tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni baa lɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the earth through their roots. Planting them after heavy feeders like maize naturally restores soil fertility without buying chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend staking my yam vines with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tsei kakadaji awo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight and off the humid ground, boosting leaf growth while preventing fungal diseases. Sunlight helps the leaves produce energy to grow large yam tubers underground.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ daalɛ yaa hiɛ ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Should I plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the year arrives?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until rains become regular. The very first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch, which can dry out newly germinated seeds and kill young crop seedlings.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni omɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi ni efite dumɔwui bibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into small tight bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee ŋmeii bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from underneath the leaves. Spraying with neem seed extract or appropriate organic solutions helps control these insects and encourages healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ko ni sa ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni eha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as essential food for the plant leaves. Adding fertilizers like urea or well-rotted manure gives the crop the nutrients it needs to regain its rich green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni haa tso baai lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge, bushy leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or receives excessive moisture without balanced nutrients like potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing foliage above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni niyenii mli nibii ni sa, tamɔ potassium bɛ mli lɛ, yucca tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do the blossoms fall off my tomato plants without turning into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollination. Keeping soil moisture steady and protecting plants during very hot dry spells helps the blossoms set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ahebuu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with weak stems when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ waa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete intensely for sunlight. The plants stretch upward as fast as possible to reach the light, which makes their stems thin and fragile instead of thick and sturdy.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ hulu la he akaŋ waa. Tso lɛ baajie ehe kpo oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ la lɛ awo mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly wet conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and fresh air into the farm, keeping the pods dry and reducing rot.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛ nakai baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes the leaves of my young corn to look chewed up with ragged holes overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-baby corn baai lɛ fee tamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii yɔɔ mli nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that crawl into the central leaves of the plant to feed. Checking the leaf funnels early and applying appropriate biological or chemical controls can protect young shoots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli koni amɛtao niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa tsuɔ nii kɛbuɔ tsei bibii ahe.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for the developing tuber underground. Staking raises the leaves into the air for better light exposure and prevents soil-borne fungal diseases from spreading onto wet leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi koni amɛná la jogbaŋŋ. ni etsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoot suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra suckers steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from the main stem. Leaving only two or three strong suckers allows the main mother plant to focus its energy on growing a large, heavy bunch of plantain.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains tsei wuji ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ nɔ.

english: How do I know if the ground has received enough rain for me to safely sow my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui shweshweeshwe?

english: Planting after only a light rain can cause seeds to dry out if the soil beneath is still dry. It is best to dig slightly and check that the top layer of soil is moist to at least the depth of your hand before planting.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofo fioo ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ mli edɔ kɛyashɛ kɛ hoo lɛ onine mli dani odu.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions with very little water or food. Because they naturally absorb nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, clearing them early prevents them from starving your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli kɛtsɔ nu loo niyenii fioo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni hɔmɔ akaye otsei titrii lɛ.

english: How do I know which way to put a cassava stem into the ground when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole bɔ ni aduɔ ŋmei tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small buds along the stem. Plant the stem with those buds pointing upward toward the sky so the green shoot can grow up easily while roots develop below.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Nyiɛmɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ Dumɔ tso lɛ ni fɔfɔii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃ oya yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants burning and turning brown in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, intense heat from the sun. They need shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees planted nearby to act as living umbrellas until they grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that can dry out the topsoil. It is best to wait until the rains become steady so your young seeds do not dry up and die right after sprouting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa koni odumɔwui bibii lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning yellow while the plant is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or the ground is overly soaked with water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or manure and improving field drainage will help the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔtɔ wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni aha nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How does mixing animal manure into my farm soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛfutuɔ sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure acts as natural plant food, feeds the soil, and helps the ground hold onto moisture during dry periods so plant roots can absorb nutrients easily.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ Koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller fruits and lower yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital resources from your crops, including water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil. Removing weeds regularly leaves all those nutrients for your crops to grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nibii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli, ni nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fata he. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi daa lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ afite koni onibii lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when there is enough water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by a soil disease called bacterial wilt, which blocks water from moving inside the stem. Removing infected plants and planting crops like maize or cassava in that spot next season helps clean the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ bacterial wilt lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haaa nu aya tsɔne lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni adu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ nakai he lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to soaked too quickly. Mulching the soil with dry leaves helps keep moisture steady so the plants hold their flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi daa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my maize is completely ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready when the outer leaves wrapping the cob turn completely brown and dry, and the kernels feel hard when you try to press your thumbnail into them.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo beni kponɔgbɛ baai ni bɔleɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni amɛgbi lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ he waa kɛ́ obɔ mɔdɛŋ ni onyɛ mfoniri bibioo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny insects eating holes in my stored beans inside the bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-kɔfi ŋmeii ni mikɛto kotoku mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These insects are bean weevils, which hatch from eggs laid on the beans before or during storage. Drying your beans thoroughly in the sun and storing them in airtight containers stops these insects from surviving.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji ŋmeii. Amɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii anɔ dani akɛtoɔ loo yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbi o-beans lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akahi shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for growth and deep green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the base of the plant will help it recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ kɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ baafata he Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the tips of my pepper leaves turning brown and looking scorched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã lɛ?

english: Scorched leaf tips often mean the soil lacks potassium or the soil is too dry for roots to take up nutrients. Regular watering and adding balanced fertilizer helps the leaves stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishifãi ni shã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled cassava leaves with light yellow spots are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant stem cuttings prevents this problem in future harvests.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse. Cassava mosaic hela ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa Niji ni nyɛɔ helai ahe lɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa yɛ wɔsɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔi amli.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ anɔ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on young crops. Inspecting fields early and applying neem oil or recommended insecticides keeps them from destroying the farm.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra kɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔ lɛ akafite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from extreme heat or dry soil. Giving the plants consistent water and shade during very hot weather helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed many of their leaves during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry seasons to protect themselves from losing too much water. Planting temporary shade trees like plantains protects young cocoa trees from drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: How can I tell if my vegetable farm is getting too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ?

english: If your plants look pale yellow, wilt even when the ground is wet, or show rotting stems near the soil, the field has too much water and needs better drainage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ Egboɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. aloo tsei ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo lɛ?

english: Black rotten bottoms on tomatoes are caused by blossom end rot, which happens when soil water levels fluctuate unevenly. Watering your crops regularly prevents this rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni fiteɔ yɛ tomato nɔ lɛ jɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Nu ni oooha tso lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni akafite nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ.

english: Why did some of the crop seeds I planted in the soil fail to germinate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if planted too deep in the soil, if the soil is too dry, or if insects eat them before they sprout. Planting at the right shallow depth in moist soil ensures good sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji kooloo lɛ ye lɛ dani ekwɛ̃. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ haa ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds in my field grow much faster than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster because they are wild plants adapted to steal food, water, and sunlight from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops a fair chance to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ejaakɛ amɛji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow strong. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK, or adding well-rotted animal manure, will help restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa Kɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo NPK, loo kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baatsu nii. Ebaaye ebua ni aku sɛɛ aha su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli awa.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies that suck the sap out of young leaves. Spraying your plants with neem oil or a recommended organic insecticide helps clear these pests and keeps new leaves growing straight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ ni eha baai heei akwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any fruits start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Water your tomato plants consistently at the base early in the morning to help them hold onto their flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Okɛ nu awo otomato tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli daa leebi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain or cassava next to cocoa gives the young trees the canopy protection and moisture they need until they grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantain loo cassava, yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ náa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ amɛhe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks next to my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ masɛi beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam is a vine plant that naturally climbs upward to spread its leaves toward the sun. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground to prevent diseases and ensures the plant catches enough sunlight to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni jɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli amɛkwɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ he. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rains and winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy bunches of fruit during storms. Digging deeper planting holes and using strong wooden poles to prop up fruiting stems will keep your trees standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ yɛ ahum be mli. Tsɔɔmɔ dumɔ bu ko ni mli kwɔ ni okɛ tso ni wa atsu nii ni okɛfi yibiiwoo tso lɛ sɛɛ koni otso lɛ ahi shi.

english: How do I know how much distance to leave between my crops when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he kɛji midu nii?

english: Proper spacing prevents plants from competing for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. For example, maize is usually spaced about 75 cm between rows so each plant gets adequate room to grow strong ears.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei ahe lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa shĩɔ ŋmãa ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee 75 cm koni eha tso fɛɛ tso aná gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy, soggy soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: What can I do to make my soil rich if I cannot afford chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: You can enrich your soil by mixing in decomposed crop waste, dried leaves, and animal manure, or by planting leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts. These natural methods feed the soil with nutrients without cost.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi ni eshwɛ, baai ni egboi kɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni ooofutu mli lɛ nɔ, loo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni eheee nɔ ko.

english: How can I stop small insects from eating my harvested maize while it is stored in my barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils thrive in grains that still hold moisture. Thoroughly drying your maize in the sun until the kernels are very hard, and storing them in airtight bags or sealed containers, starves pests of air and moisture so your harvest stays safe.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔwui ni mli edɔ lolo lɛ amli. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. ni okɛto vacuum bag loo tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa mli. Ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli Koni okpamɔ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on the same farm with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight can scorch their delicate leaves and dry out the soil. Planting plantains provides fast-growing shade and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Shade tso dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ adumɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ he wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulutsoo tso lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to put wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso he hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to produce energy. When the leaves get enough sun on stakes instead of lying on the hot ground, the plant directs more food into growing larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Beni baai lɛ náa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakã shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo baaba koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nutrients, especially nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color so the plant can grow heavy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tsei lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay very thin even when the stems grow very tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ eshishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or receive too much leaf-growing nutrients, they spend all their energy growing tall branches instead of roots. Proper spacing gives the roots enough room and sunlight to expand into thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo enine shɛ niyenii babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji ni kwɔlɔ mli yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulu la ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil consistently damp by watering regularly and mulching prevents the plant from getting stressed and dropping its blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ loo ŋmɔlɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekahao ni eha efɔfɔi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do the bottom ends of my pepper fruits turn black and rot before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black rot at the tip of pepper fruits is caused by uneven watering, which stops the plant from absorbing enough calcium from the soil. Watering your crops regularly helps the plant transport nutrients evenly into the growing fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ashishi lɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo otsei lɛ amli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa aduawai ni miida lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dried grass or leaves, known as mulching, protects the soil from drying out under the hot sun. It keeps the roots cool, stops weeds from growing easily, and eventually rots into valuable organic food for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni jara wa ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds when my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and aggressively steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Removing weeds early ensures your young crops do not get choked or starved during their most critical growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa otsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo hɔmɔ akaye amɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize-loving pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans rebuilds soil fertility and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots and thick branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mikoo tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi kɛ tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Pruning excess branches allows sunlight and air to pass freely through the tree canopy. This keeps the tree dry to prevent fungal diseases like black pod and ensures the tree sends its strength into growing cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni egbiɔ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃ cocoa tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do extension officers completely clear all undergrowth beneath cocoa trees instead of just trimming it with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ dade baafolɔ tsei lɛ?

english: Thoroughly clearing undergrowth prevents weeds from stealing water and nutrients from cocoa roots, while also reducing hiding places for pests like mirids and diseases like black pod.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hei ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Does the grass growing under my cocoa trees actually harm my yield?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mikookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, dense grass creates high humidity around the lower parts of the tree, which encourages fungal diseases to spread to your cocoa pods, while competing directly with cocoa roots for soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni mli ewo muji lɛ haa hulutsoo babaoo baa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ hei lɛ. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ hewalɛ koni egbɛ eshwa o-cocoa pods lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni kookoo shishifãi yɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: If I clear away all the weeds beneath my cocoa trees, won't the bare soil dry out in the heat?
ga: Kɛ́ mijie jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, Ani shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ egbiŋ yɛ latsaa lɛ hewɔ?

english: Clearing weeds allows you to leave the fallen dead cocoa leaves evenly spread on the ground as mulch. This leaf blanket protects the soil from the sun, keeps moisture in, and rots into free fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ oshiɔ kookoo baai ni egboi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɛkɛ baai nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la he, ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni efiteɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Is it safer for my cocoa trees if I weed with a cutlass or if I spray weedkiller chemicals?
ga: Ani mi-kokoo tsei lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛji mikɛ dagger loo tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie amɛnɔ?

english: Using a cutlass prevents chemical damage to shallow cocoa roots and beneficial soil insects, though it requires more labor than carefully targeted weed spraying.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsofai ni fiteɔ kookoo shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akafite. kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ Enɛ biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo fe jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, shi kɛlɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster under my young cocoa trees than under my old cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishi fe mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have open branches that let in full sunlight, which fuels weed growth. Older cocoa trees form a thick overhead canopy that blocks light, naturally stopping weeds from growing.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ niji ni agbele ni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ. ni haa jwɛi lɛ daraa Kokoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli tse ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: If I have plenty of government-supplied chemical, can I keep applying it to my cocoa trees as often as I want?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miyɛ tsofai babaoo ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa lɛ hu? Ani manyɛ mikɛwo cacao nɔ shii abɔ ni miisumɔ?

english: No, over-applying chemicals can burn cocoa leaves, poison the soil, damage tender feeder roots, and waste valuable inputs without increasing your crop yield.
ga: Dabi, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã kookoo baai lɛ. Ekɛ nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Efiteɔ shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ blɛoo. kɛ nibii ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni afiteɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ eyaaa hiɛ.

english: Are the farm chemicals provided by government programs different from the ones I buy in the local market?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi kɛhaa lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ tsofai ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ he?

english: Government chemicals are official, tested formulations specifically approved for cocoa pests, whereas market chemicals can vary in strength, quality, or intended crop use.
ga: Nɔyeli tsofa lɛ ji tsofa ko ni aka ni akpɛlɛ nɔ pɔtɛɛ aha kookoo tsɛŋemɔ helai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ hewalɛ, bɔ ni amɛhi ha, loo nɔ ni ato akɛ akɛbaatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if I am applying too much chemical spray on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsu nii?

english: Signs of chemical overuse include leaves developing brown burned edges, cocoa trees dropping green leaves prematurely, and leaves turning yellow unexpectedly.
ga: Nɔ ni fata tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ ahe okadii ahe ji baai ni shãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Cacao tsei lɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ fiteɔ mra. Ni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray chemical treatments on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ kookoo ŋmɔ ko nɔ?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is ideal because temperatures are cooler and wind is low, which prevents the chemical from evaporating too quickly or drifting off the leaves.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli Ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu baa shi. Enɛ baaha tsofai lɛ akafo oya tsɔ loo amɛkagbee baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray farm chemicals directly onto the main trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai shwieɔ kookoo tso lɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Direct chemical spraying on the bark can cause chemical burns, damage lower flower cushions where pods grow, and harm delicate roots near the surface of the trunk.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ashã. Kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ashishigbɛ pilɔ lɛ hiɛ, he ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. ni efiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: What does the 'F1' mean on seeds like Demon F1 pepper, and why is it better than saving seeds from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘F1’ shishi yɛ dumɔwui tamɔ Demon F1 pepper lɛ nɔ ni mɛni hewɔ ehi fe dumɔwui ni jɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ ni mahere lɛ?

english: F1 stands for a first-generation hybrid seed, which is bred by crossing two pure plant lines to get strong traits like higher yields, heat tolerance, and disease resistance. Saving seeds from F1 crops doesn't work well because the second generation loses these special traits and yields much less.
ga: F1 damɔ shi kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome. Afɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi enyɔ ni he tse ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛná sui ni mli wa, tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ F1 tsei amli lɛ ehiii kwraa ejaakɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ laajeɔ sui krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why are some chili pepper varieties like Demon F1 much hotter and yield more than traditional local peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi tamɔ Demon F1 lɛ mli edɔɔ waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid chili varieties like Demon F1 are specially bred for commercial production, combining high capsaicin content for extreme pungency with dense fruiting branches, allowing them to produce far more peppers per plant than wild or local varieties.
ga: Atsɔse Hybrid pepper henɔi tamɔ Demon F1 lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha jarayeli nitsumɔ. Ekɛ capsaicin ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛha ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa kɛ niji ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ chili ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ tso kome mli fe chili srɔtoi ni yɔɔ koo mli loo maŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to nurse my chili seeds in a nursery bed instead of planting them directly in the soil on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu chili dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chili seeds are small and fragile. Nursing them in a protected area allows you to control soil moisture, shield young sprouts from harsh sunlight and pests, and ensure only strong, healthy seedlings are transplanted into the main field.
ga: Chili dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. He ko ni abuɔ he lɛ mli saamɔ haa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. Ni dumɔwui ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ akɛ abaadu kɛya shikpɔŋ titri lɛ nɔ.

english: How far apart should I plant my hot pepper seedlings when moving them to the main field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-hot pepper dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ miiwo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Plant your hot pepper seedlings about 50 centimeters apart within a row, with rows spaced 60 to 70 centimeters apart. Good spacing gives plants room to branch out, reduces competition for nutrients, and improves airflow to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Dumɔ chili dumɔwui lɛ aaafee sɛntimitai 50 kɛjɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛkuu mli. Okɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee sɛntimita 60 kɛyashi 70. Gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛjeɔ niji amli. Tsɔɔmɔ akaŋshii ni kɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he lɛ shi ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni akafee tsɛŋemɔ hela.

english: Why are the leaves on my chili pepper plants curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ chili baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites, or a virus passed on by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or recommended sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy so the plant can make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites, loo helai ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ye obua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off before forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Flower drop happens when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which pushes the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit. Regular watering during flower formation helps keep the flowers on the stem.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ fɔfɔii ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ shishi.

english: How often should I water my chili pepper field during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ okɛ nu awo o-chili ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Chili plants need moist but well-drained soil. Water them deeply 2 to 3 times a week at the base of the plant early in the morning, avoiding wet leaves, to keep fruit growing consistently without causing root rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ shi nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia chili tsei lɛ. Nu ni mli kwɔ shii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ otsi mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi leebi. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha aduawai lɛ aya nɔ ada ni ehaŋ shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: What type of soil is best if I want to grow spicy hot peppers in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni madu ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Hot peppers thrive best in loose, well-drained sandy loam soil rich in organic material like compost. Heavy clay soil holds too much water and can drown the roots, while overly dry sand loses nutrients too quickly.
ga: Hot peppers daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni tsii lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ, ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi. yɛ be mli ni ŋã ni egbi tsɔ lɛ baafite niyenii mli hewalɛ oya tsɔ.

english: How do I know the best time to harvest my hot chili peppers for the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa chili ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvest when the peppers turn firm and reach their deep red color, as this is when they have the maximum heat, weight, and market value, although some buyers prefer them harvested green depending on local demand.
ga: Kpamɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli wa ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, no ji be ni chili ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ latsaa, shwiili kɛ jarayeli jara ni fe fɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ mɛi komɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ amɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ mli moŋ, shi enɛ damɔ bɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli bii lɛ sumɔɔ amɛhaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my hot peppers spoil so quickly after I pick them, and how can I make them last longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikpa amɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-chili lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Peppers spoil fast if harvested in the hot sun or kept in airtight plastic bags. Pick peppers early in the morning when it is cool, keep them in breathable crates, and store them in a shaded, well-ventilated space to extend their shelf life.
ga: Chili ŋmɔtɔ baafite oya kɛji akɛ akɛto hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo yɛ plastic kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Okɛto adeka ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli mli. Ni okɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dying in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have weak roots and sensitive leaves that burn easily under full sun. Without temporary shade crops like plantains, the harsh sun dries out the soil and scorches the young leaves, causing them to yellow and drop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ebaashã baai bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Can I plant plantain in the same field as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting plantains alongside young cocoa is very good practice. The broad plantain leaves provide necessary shade to shield fragile young cocoa trees from intense sunlight while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii duɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa waa. Plantain baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo tsei bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Pruning unnecessary branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the main trunk where cocoa pods grow. It reduces disease spread and forces the tree to put its energy into growing pods rather than excess leaves.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ni he ehiaaa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso titri lɛ he ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ baa shi, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai ni fa fe nine baatsu nii.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around the base of my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water and nutrients directly from the soil that your cocoa roots need. Clearing weeds around the base ensures your trees get all the food and moisture, while also removing hiding spots for harmful farm pests.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ ni he hiaa o-cocoa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ajiemɔ Shishitoo lɛ haa tso lɛ nine shɛɔ eniyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ hei ni ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off the tree before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop when the tree lacks essential soil nutrients, doesn't get enough water, or suffers from pest attacks. Ensuring good soil fertility and managing insects helps flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni anáaa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods growing small and deformed instead of big and full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni efite moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Deformed or undersized pods usually happen when insect pests like capsids suck sap from young pod tissue, or when the tree lacks key nutrients during the pod formation stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni efite loo bibii baa kɛji ŋmeii tamɔ capsids miinu nu ni jɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli lɛ. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii yɛ pod lɛ feemɔ be lɛ mli

english: Will I get more harvest if I plant my cocoa trees very close to each other?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu cacao tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: No, planting cocoa too close causes trees to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to small pods. Proper spacing ensures every tree gets enough sunlight and nourishment to produce heavily.
ga: Dabi, kookoo ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. causing small pods He ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkpa nii babaoo.

english: Why do some cocoa farms have thick leafy crowns while mine looks thin with very few leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi yɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni minɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni baai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: A full, green canopy comes from rich soil nutrients, consistent moisture, and protection from leaf-eating insects. Thin canopy growth indicates the tree is under stress from nutrient deficiency, drought, or pest damage.
ga: Niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. hulutsoo ni tamɔ amɛhe kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ ahe Ŋmei bibioo ko ni yaa hiɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, hɔmɔ, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahewɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa pods are rotting because of wet weather or a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo hela hewɔ?

english: Black pod disease starts as small brown spots on pods during humid or rainy weather and rapidly spreads until the pod turns completely black and hard. Removing infected pods immediately prevents it from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jeɔ shishi akɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be loo nugbɔ nɛɔ Ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya aahu akɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my soil needs fertilizer for my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: If your mature trees produce pale or yellowish leaves, drop young pods early, or fail to yield many pods season after season, it is a sign that the soil nutrients have run low and need fertilizer replenishment.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ Shĩ ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ oya. aloo ewooo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be kome mli Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmeii afata he.

english: Why are insects attacking my cocoa pods while they are still growing on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Insects like mirids and pod borers are attracted to the sweet sap and flesh of green cocoa pods. They pierce the outer skin to feed, which leaves dark wounds, stunts pod growth, and allows diseases to enter.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mirids kɛ pod borers lɛ sumɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli nu kɛ amɛmli nu lɛ. Amɛfoɔ hewolo lɛ mli koni amɛna niyenii. ni kɛ pilamɔi ni yɔɔ diŋŋ baa lɛ tsiɔ pod lɛ dalɛ naa ni ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ mli

english: What kind of animals damage cocoa pods and why do they do it?
ga: Mɛɛ kooloo fiteɔ kookoo ŋmeii? Ni mɛni hewɔ amɛfeɔ nakai lɛ?

english: Animals like squirrels, monkeys, and rats chew through cocoa pods to eat the sweet white pulp surrounding the beans, leaving empty, damaged shells hanging on the tree that rot.
ga: Koolooi tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ŋmɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii koni amɛye loo yɛŋ ni ŋɔɔ ni ebɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ, ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni efite lɛ pɛ ni fĩɔ tso ni miifite lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes small holes to appear in the leaves of my young crops?
ga: Mɛni haa buji lɛ feɔ bibii? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by chewing insects like beetles, caterpillars, or grasshoppers. Eating the leaves weakens the plant because it reduces its ability to catch sunlight and make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni yeɔ nii, tamɔ ladybugs, caterpillars, loo ŋmeii kɛ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli baa. Baai lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛtsɔ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaashɛ hulu la ni ekɛfee niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if ants on my cocoa farm are harming my crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Ants themselves don't always eat crops, but they often protect harmful insects like mealybugs that spread the cocoa swollen shoot disease. If you see ants clustered around white powdery spots on stems or pods, they are helping harmful pests.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛbuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ mealybugs ni gbɛɔ cocoa bud swelling hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ahe. Kɛji ona ŋmeii ni miiho kɛmiibɔle ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ miiye amɛmiibua kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods turn black due to Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and poorly ventilated conditions, especially during the rainy season.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Cocoa trees drop yellow leaves during dry spells to protect themselves from losing too much water. Providing permanent shade trees helps keep the soil cool and prevents leaves from scorching and dropping.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be hiɔ shi daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛkagbeeɔ shi.

english: Poor fruit production after flowering usually happens when there are not enough natural pollinators, such as tiny midges, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients needed to turn flowers into healthy fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni ehiii ni baa yɛ fɔfɔii asɛɛ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi, tamɔ midges lɛ faaa, loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to leave rotten or dried pods hanging on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaashi ŋmeii ni egbo loo egbi yɛ cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving old or diseased pods hanging on the tree acts as a breeding ground for fungi and pests, which will easily spread to young, healthy pods during the next growing cycle.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni egbɔ loo hela emɔ amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, eji he ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ. Enɛ baagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check on my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: You should inspect your farm at least once a week. Regular visits help you spot insect infestations, disease outbreaks, or animal damage early enough to stop them before they spread to the whole farm.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli. Saramɔi ni ooofee daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ. hela ni baa loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii oya bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa dani egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What makes mature crop leaves curl up and dry out suddenly?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ?

english: Leaves curl up and dry out when sap-sucking insects drain the plant's juices, or when fungal diseases attack the roots, stopping the crop from absorbing water from the ground.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni koolooi ni nuɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ tutua shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which acts as essential food for leaf growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea will help the leaves turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa ni tsuɔ nii waa.

english: Why does leaving dry leaves and cut grass on top of my farm soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mishi baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ni afo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps moisture trapped in the soil, prevents weed growth, and gradually turns into natural fertilizer as it rots.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni fiofio lɛ etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni egboɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so well when I mix dry chicken manure into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛdu lɛ?

english: Chicken manure is packed with natural nutrients that feed plants and improves the soil's ability to hold water, making it an excellent organic food source that keeps the land healthy.
ga: Akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa tsei niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli lɛ eyi wuɔ ŋmɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsina ŋmei feɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees alongside my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under the harsh sun. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil damp while the cocoa plants build strength during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ maa hewalɛ emaa shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ,.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny ears when I plant four or five seeds together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ toi bibii beni mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ ebɔ he yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing stalks fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to produce large, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha toi lɛ adara ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to create energy, which the plant sends down to grow tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the sun and off the damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ. Abaatsu tsei lɛ kɛba shi koni amɛyadu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ejɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Why are small worms crawling into the leaves at the center of my maize plants and chewing them to pieces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ bibii bibii lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides in the growing center of the maize plant. Spraying approved neem-based natural pesticides or recommended crop chemicals early in the morning will protect your crop before they ruin the harvest.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ ni neem tsuɔ he nii loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe dani ekpãtã amɛhiɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before turning into green peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of calcium. Keeping the soil evenly watered and adding compost helps the plant keep its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo calcium ni faaa lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains flood my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits around the roots without draining away, it suffocates them and causes fungal rot; planting on raised soil ridges helps extra water drain away easily.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ taraa shishifãi lɛ ahe ni efooo kɛyaaa lɛ. Enɛ baaha mɔ ko agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ agbo. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: How do I know the best time to sow my seeds when the rainy season in Ghana starts late or unpredictably?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adũ dumɔwui? Be ni nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ loo be ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba?

english: It is best not to plant right after the very first rain, as a dry spell often follows that can destroy young sprouts. Wait until you get two or three steady rains that soak deep into the dirt before putting your seeds in the ground.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ baa, ni baanyɛ akpata tsei bibii ahiɛ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani okɛ dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it better for me to go out and plant my crops very early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ maje kpo kɛyadu nii leebi maŋkpa lɛ?

english: Planting early in the morning keeps the seeds and young soil cool, protecting them from the harsh afternoon sun which can dry out sensitive seedlings before their roots settle.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ he. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ atswa shishifãi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I don't plant plantains next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni miduuu plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that give young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture needed during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly allows each plant enough room to build a strong stem and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso ni mli wa kɛ tso agbo.

english: Why do my crops wither during the hot afternoon heat even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In intense sun, leaves lose water faster through evaporation than the roots can suck it up from the ground. The plant temporarily wilts to save water, but usually bounces back as the day cools down.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛfeɔ lasu. Nɔ ni fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei gboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shi esumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe aku sɛɛ aba kɛji edɔ.

english: How does covering the soil around my cassava with dry bush grass help the plant grow?
ga: Mulching around Te mi ŋmei jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with grass or dead leaves acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the ground so water doesn't evaporate quickly, stops weeds from stealing plant food, and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ No hewɔ lɛ nu lɛ efoŋ oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen nutrients in the soil, or heavy rains flooded the ground and stopped the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden sticks to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ekɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight on their leaves. The more sunlight the leaves catch, the more energy the plant sends underground to swell the yam tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la babaoo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛwo sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What causes my tomato plants to drop their flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Extreme afternoon heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer stresses the tomato plant, causing it to drop flowers to protect itself rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Why does cassava take almost a year to harvest while maize is ready in a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa heɔ aaafee afi dani akpaa ŋmãa shi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize grows above ground to produce grain quickly, while cassava spends many months building thick, energy-packed starchy roots deep underground.
ga: Abɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmaa aba oya. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani enáa shishifãi ni mli tse, ni eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the underside of the leaf, which damages the leaf cells and spreads crop diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni fiteɔ baa mli wala yibii lɛ ni egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize roots need air as well as water to breathe. When heavy rains flood the soil, the roots cannot take up oxygen or nitrogen, which causes the leaves to lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Abɛi shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa loo nitrogen. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ amɛ eŋɔli su ni amɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my yam tubers splitting and cracking underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miigba ni amɛmiitswa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers crack when a sudden heavy rain follows a long dry period. The tubers absorb water quickly and expand faster than their skin can stretch, causing the outer layer to split.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Yitso lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. ni haa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ fiteɔ

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall and thin with few tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ebɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: Cassava plants need sunlight to manufacture energy for root growth. When planted too close, they compete for sunlight and use all their energy growing tall to reach the light instead of expanding their underground tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei taoɔ hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛ bulb lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant beans or cowpeas alongside my corn crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants capture nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps the neighboring corn grow stronger.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ waa.

english: Extreme heat causes stress to tomato plants, drying out the flower pollen so it cannot fertilize the bloom. Shading the plants or watering during cool morning hours helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. dry the pollen No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tomato tsei amli. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo ha tsei lɛ loo okɛ nu wo amɛmli yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves and stop flowering during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa fɔfɔi yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds rapidly strip moisture from cocoa leaves. To protect itself from dying of thirst, the cocoa tree sheds leaves and stops flowering until the rains return.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai amli oya. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ kumai he Kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛkpaa fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my green leafy vegetables start producing flowers early instead of growing big leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miibɔi fɔmɔ oya yɛ baai wuji ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: High temperatures and heat stress signal to leafy vegetables that survival conditions are becoming difficult, causing them to rush into flowering and seed production rather than growing broader leaves.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa kɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ tsɔɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ akɛ shihilɛi ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ ebafee nɔ ni wa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nɛkɛ aduawai nɛɛ hoɔ oya kɛyaa fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing new flowers after I pick the first heavy harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpa fɔfɔi heei kwɛmɔ yɛ mi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: After producing a large batch of fruit, pepper plants deplete their stored nutrients. Giving the soil compost or fertilizer and adequate water stimulates the plant to produce new shoots and fresh flowers.
ga: Beni ewo aduawai babaoo sɛɛ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baafite niyenii ni akɛto lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmeii heei kɛ fɔfɔi heei.

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking several months to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers go into a resting phase if planted in dry soil or if cut improperly. They require sufficient soil moisture to initiate root growth before new leaves can shoot up.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baaya shihilɛ mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo afolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia amɛ koni amɛje shishifãi lɛ adalɛ shishi dani baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my harvested onions turn soft and rot right before I take them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water near harvest time allows fungal organisms to soak into the onion bulb. Onions need drying soil as they reach maturity so their outer layers can dry into protective paper skins.
ga: Nu babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ baaha ŋmeii abote ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ehe miihia ni sabolai lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ agbi ni efee wolo hewolo ni buɔ mɔ he.

english: How can I tell if a coconut nursery shoot is good quality before I plant it on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A good coconut shoot will have dark green leaves, a thick and sturdy stem base, and a nut that feels heavy with water when you shake it. Avoid shoots that look pale, thin, or soft.
ga: Kokooshi tsei kpakpai yɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Ni ŋmei lɛ baanu he akɛ eyɛ tsiimɔ kɛ́ etswa nu lɛ beni okpokpo lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ mfonirii ni tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ mlɛo, loo eyɛ blɛoo lɛ ahe.
