english: After my coconut seed sprouts, what signs show that the seedling is bad and should be thrown away?
ga: Beni ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ Mɛɛ okadii yɔɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwu ko ehiii ni esa akɛ ashɛrɛ ashwie?

english: If a sprouted seedling has twisted, yellow leaves, a very weak stem, or signs of rotted roots near the nut, it is unviable and will not grow into a healthy, high-yielding tree.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etsake lɛ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ waa. aloo shishifãi ni egboi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ anyɛɛɛ adu ni edaŋ ni efee tso ni wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I make sure I do not accidentally buy weak seed nuts from the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mikɛ oshara baahe ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ jara nɔ?

english: Choose fully mature nuts from healthy trees, test them by shaking to hear liquid inside, and avoid nuts with cracks, dark rotten patches, or small holes made by insects.
ga: Halamɔ ŋmeii ni eda kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Kaa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ koni onu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ ahe. Dark rot loo eyɛ bu bibioo ko ni kooloi kɛbaa

english: I planted some coconut nuts weeks ago, but none have sprouted—what could be the matter?
ga: Midu ŋmeii komɛi otsii komɛi ni eho nɛ. Shi ŋmei tsei komɛi bɛ jɛmɛ. Mɛni maa ba?

english: Coconuts fail to sprout if the soil is too dry, if the nuts were harvested before maturing properly, or if pests like beetles ate the growing tip inside the husk.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii kwɛŋ. Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ladybugs yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: My young crop leaves are turning yellow right after sprouting. What causes this?
ga: Mibaai bibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: Yellowing leaves in young sprouts usually mean the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are drowning in flooded soil that cannot drain water properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ ekã shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli ni nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops on one side of my farm grow strong while the ones on the other side stay stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fa kome lɛ miida waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fa kroko lɛ mli lɛ miiya nɔ egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Soil condition varies across a farm. Areas with rocky ground, poor water retention, or fewer nutrients will cause crops to remain small and weak compared to rich soil areas.
ga: Esoro shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. He ni shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nu nyɛɛɛ ahi mli jogbaŋŋ Loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ he.

english: What should I look for on my young sprouts to know if insects are attacking them early?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ matao yɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni mana kɛji kooloi bibii miitutua amɛ mra?

english: Look for small holes chewed into tender leaves, sticky liquid on the stem, or small brown and black bugs gathering underneath the leaves.
ga: Taomɔ buji bibii ni akɛ baai bibii shwieɔ mli lɛ. Nu ko ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ediŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ. Abua naa yɛ baai lɛ ashishi

english: What is the best way to care for a coconut seedling immediately after it sprouts in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmeii tsei amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: Keep the soil around the sprouted nut moist but not soggy, clear away weeds around it, and give it enough open sunlight to build a strong main shoot.
ga: Ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. ni oha hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ afee ŋmeii titrii ni mli wa.

english: If my young coconut sprout stops growing during the dry season, how do I know if it is dead or just waiting for rain?
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei ko kpa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ egbo loo eemɛ nugbɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Scrape the outer bark of the shoot lightly with your fingernail; if it is green and moist underneath, it is alive, but if it is dry, brown, and snaps easily, it has died.
ga: Okɛ onineshi tsɔne lɛ atsɔ tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ nɔ blɛoo. Kɛji eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishi lɛ, no lɛ eyɛ wala mli lolo. Shi kɛji egbi, eyɛ asasu, ni ekumɔ oya lɛ, no lɛ egbo.

english: Why is it important to check the condition of my crops regularly during their first month in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha daa yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first month is when crops are weakest. Regular checks let you catch early diseases, pest attacks, or water shortages before the plant dies completely.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ ji be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tso lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni oyɔseɔ helai, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo nu ni faaa mra dani tso lɛ gboɔ kwraa.

english: Is it better for me to burn cleared bushes on my farm or leave them to rot on the land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni he tse ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo maha amɛgbo yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving cleared bushes and weeds to rot on your field acts as natural mulch. It feeds useful nutrients back into the soil and traps moisture, whereas burning destroys those good soil nutrients and exposes the topsoil to heat.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ shia lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Egbalaa niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. yɛ be mli ni la ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli dɔɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare earth around my vegetable plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves stops the harsh sun from drying out the soil too quickly, suppresses weeds from growing, and eventually rots to create rich natural manure for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ Ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, egboɔ koni ekɛfee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist for the young cocoa to survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know which direction to insert cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes along the stem cutting; they must point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down forces the leaves to grow backward, weakening the plant and lowering your harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei ni atsɔ hiɛ awo shishi lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady and consistent. The first rain is often followed by a short heat wave or dry spell, which can scorch fragile new sprouts before their roots establish.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ fiofio ni ebaa shi. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. loo hɔmɔ Enɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui heei ni bɛ hewalɛ dani shishifãi lɛ aba.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main fuel crops use to stay green and grow strong. Applying compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji tsofa titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing holes in my maize leaves with little caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ baa? Ani okɛ ohe ewo tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana. Checking your fields early and spraying recommended organic solutions or pesticides directly into the plant funnel protects your yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Onibii ni odu lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ organic solution loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔse tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nibii ni odu lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by small sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit crop viruses. Spraying your plants with neem oil or insecticidal soap helps clear these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi nɛɛ ajie amɛhe.

english: Why do I have to put tall wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy that builds big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the air and sunlight instead of tangling on the hot, shaded ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants dropping off instead of forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat becomes too intense, when the soil dries out inconsistently, or when there are too few pollinating insects around to turn the flowers into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee loo be mli ni ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ feɔ fɔfɔii lɛ faaa tsɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen or water. During dry spells, the soil cannot deliver enough nutrients to the roots, so the plant moves nutrients from its lower leaves to keep the top growing, which turns the bottom leaves yellow.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa aha shishifãi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli koni eha ŋwɛi baa lɛ adara. Enɛ baaha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up during the hot afternoon even when the soil was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in intense afternoon heat to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun. This natural survival reaction prevents moisture from evaporating too quickly from the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ebaabai lɛ anɔ ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ni haa mɔ hiɔ shi nɛɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but produce very small roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from overly rich soil or excess fertilizer, it puts all its energy into growing stems and leaves above ground rather than storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni ŋmei naa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii fe nine loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Lifting the vines on sticks helps the leaves catch maximum sunlight and keeps them off the damp soil where rot and diseases spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. ni otsi enaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ yɛ he ni egboɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Small shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves more energy for the main plant to produce large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii Ekɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant experiences water stress. High temperatures prevent proper pollination, causing the plant to shed flowers to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Ha tso lɛ afee fɔfɔi koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi.

english: Why is it better to plant my maize in straight, measured rows instead of scattering the seeds randomly across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa lɛ

english: Planting in straight, spaced rows ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors. It also leaves clear pathways for weeding, applying fertilizer, and operating farm tools.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. Ekɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni mli ka shi faŋŋ hu haa kɛha jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry organic matter, called mulching, shades the ground from the hot sun to keep it cool and moist, while also blocking sunlight that weeds need to germinate.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ hulu la ni he hiaa jwɛi koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ naa.

english: Why should I wait until after it rains before putting fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ amɛmɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ dani akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into the soil so roots can absorb it. Placing dry fertilizer on hot, dry ground can burn crop roots or cause the nutrients to evaporate into the air.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo eha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: How can using a mechanical tiller help my soil compared to clearing my land using only a hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni akɛ ŋmei pɛ tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: A mechanical tiller breaks up compacted soil much deeper and faster than a hand hoe. This loosens the earth so crop roots can easily push down deep to reach underground moisture and air.
ga: Mɛkanika ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni eyaa oya fe shɔvel ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient crops use to make food and grow strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why does my land yield less cassava when I plant it on the same farm plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmei fioo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific soil nutrients that crop needs without giving the soil time to rest or rebuild its natural fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ daa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ hoɔ. ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo ekɛsaa ebɔɔ su ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my yam vines grow lots of leafy stems but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages yams to focus all their energy on growing heavy leaves above ground rather than swelling the tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ sweet potatoes hewalɛ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama tsei ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ, moŋ fe ni eeeha bulbs lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants dry up and drop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight and heat; they need temporary shade plants like plantains to shelter them and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛná wɔɔhe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before producing any fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress to pepper plants, making them drop flowers to save water and energy until cooler conditions return.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Dumɔ fɔfɔii koni okɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee fɛ̃i ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I sow seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Seeds planted too closely fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, causing all of them to grow weak and yield poorly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ daaa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow slowly even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your planted crops need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei ni okwɛɔ lɛ koni amɛshwere lɛ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas between my maize rows without harming the maize growth?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ ni mifiteee ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ?

english: Yes, cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which actually helps enrich the soil for your maize while reducing weed growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ kɛhaa o-corn lɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shweremɔ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the field when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to breathe, and standing water starves roots of air, causing rot unless planted on raised soil mounds for drainage.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Ni nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. kɛ fitemɔ baa Ja adu yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, rotten spots at the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots at the bottom of tomatoes occur when plants experience irregular watering, which prevents them from taking up calcium properly while fruit develops.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ tomato shishi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ nu ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná calcium ni sa be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food that builds big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they get full sun and stay safe from rots and fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow fast. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same spot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets maize pests build up. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts restores nutrients to the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ oya nɔ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni oha ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I spread dried leaves or grass around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi ashwã he lɛ? miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishitoo

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, keeps direct sunlight from drying out the earth. It traps soil moisture during hot days and stops weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Enɛ baatsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when tiny insect pests attack the flowers. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps protect the blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck sap from young leaves and spread plant viruses. Spraying neem seed liquid or soapy water helps clear these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Kɛ akɛ neem dumɔwui nu loo samla nu shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: How do I know if the first rain of the season is enough for me to start sowing my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: The soil should be moist at least hand-deep into the ground. If you dig down a few inches and squeeze a handful of soil into a soft ball without water dripping out, there is enough moisture for seeds to sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli inchi fioo komɛi ni okɛmimɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ eko mli ni efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni nu ejɛɛɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nii lɛ leebi loo shwane mli lɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer under strong midday heat can burn plant roots and leaves, and causes the nutrients to evaporate away. Cooler times of day allow the plants to drink up the nutrients safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ la ni naa wa shishi yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛbaai. ni ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi Be ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa tsei nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop, and cracks start forming in the ground around the base of the stem from the expanding roots underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmeii bɔi feemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Stem shishi kɛjɛ shishifãi ni yaa shishi lɛ amli.

english: How does giving extra water to my cocoa trees during the dry season actually help them produce more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu kroko ha mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Cocoa trees need continuous moisture to retain flower buds and develop pods. Irrigation prevents flowers from drying out and dropping off during heat spells, allowing the tree to yield pods year-round rather than just during rainy periods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛkagbee shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Jeee yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli pɛ

english: Is rainfall alone enough for my crops, or will adding an irrigation system really make a noticeable difference in my harvest?
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ pɛ fa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii. Aloo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaha srɔtofeemɔ ko ni kadiɔ mɔ aba mikpamɔ lɛ mli?

english: While natural rainfall works well during the wet season, dry spells cause plant stress and reduce fruit size. Irrigation ensures steady water supply, which can double or triple crop yields compared to relying only on rain.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli moŋ Shi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ ayibɔ baa shi. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu baa daa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ toi enyɔ loo toi etɛ. Kɛ akɛto nugbɔ pɛ nɔ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ he

english: How much cocoa should I realistically expect to harvest from my farm if I rely only on natural rain versus using artificial watering?
ga: Cocoa enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ diɛŋtsɛ akɛ makpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ pɛ nɔ moŋ fe nu ni akɛfee lɛ.

english: Without irrigation, a standard cocoa farm yields a baseline harvest dependent entirely on rainy weather. Adding controlled irrigation creates optimal growing conditions that allow trees to reach their maximum genetic yield potential, often producing significantly higher tonnage.
ga: Kɛji nu shwiemɔ bɛ Kookoo ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ lɛ baaha shishijee yibiiwoo ni damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛi anɔ pɛ. Nu ni akudɔɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa yibiiwoo babaoo baa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa shwiili lɛ tsiimɔ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: How can I test if a new government extension method actually works on my farm without risking all my money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji nɔyeli lɛ gbɛ hee ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsakeɔ be lɛ tsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ mishika fɛɛ wooo oshara mli?

english: You can set up a small demonstration or pilot section on a fraction of your land. By applying the new method on that small section and comparing its yield to your regular plot, you can prove the results before investing fully.
ga: Obaanyɛ oto nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko loo pilot fã ko. yɛ okpokpaa lɛ fã ko nɔ Kɛtsɔ gbɛ hee ni okɛtsuɔ nii yɛ fã bibioo ko nɔ No nɔ ni okɛ yibiiwoo lɛ ato oshikpɔŋ ni okwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ he. Obaanyɛ otsɔɔ nɔ ni jɛ mli ba dani okɛ shika awo mli kwraa.

english: Why do my crop leaves look full and green, but the farm still gives me very few fruits at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ eŋɔli lɛ? Shi yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lolo?

english: Green leaves mean the plant has plenty of nitrogen for foliage growth, but fruiting requires phosphorus and potassium. Without the right balance of flower and fruit-boosting nutrients, the plant focuses on growing leaves instead of crop yield.
ga: Baai eŋɔli tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Shi yibiiwoo biɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium. Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai yaa hiɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ baama baai ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do young cocoa plants prefer shade while mature cocoa trees need direct sunlight to produce plenty of pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii sumɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, cacao tso ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that easily burn and dry out under intense heat. As the tree grows mature roots and a sturdy trunk, it needs full direct sunlight to fuel photosynthesis, which creates the energy needed to form heavy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Beni tso lɛ daa lɛ, eyɛ shishifãi ni edara kɛ tso ni mli wa. Tsei hu taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekanya fotosintɛsis. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee pod ni tsii lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the tiny cocoa pods even begin to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani cacao ŋmɔji bibii lɛ daraa lɛ? Ani ebaaje shishi eda?

english: Flowers drop off as a natural defense mechanism when the tree experiences stress, such as sudden drought, poor nutrients, or heat. Keeping soil moisture stable and feeding the soil stops the tree from shedding its flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛji tsei kɛ nɔnyɛɛ kpe, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa. niyenii ni esaaa loo dɔlɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: What happens inside my crops during a long drought that causes them to stop growing altogether?
ga: Mɛni baa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni haa amɛkpaa dalɛ kwraa?

english: During a drought, plants close the microscopic pores on their leaves to save water. This shuts down their internal food production, causing them to stall growth and drop flowers to conserve energy for survival.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ anaa koni nu akafite. Enɛ haa niyenii ni afeɔ yɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkpaa dalɛ ni amɛjieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why does cutting off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa tree make it produce more pods instead of damaging it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii babaoo baa moŋ fe ni eeefite amɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess branches that steal nutrients and block sunlight from reaching the trunk. Opening up the tree allows air to circulate, reduces fungal disease, and directs the tree's food directly into growing larger cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Tso lɛ ni agbeleɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ gbɛ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: How does spreading dry leaf trash around the base of my cocoa trees help keep water in the ground?
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ amli jwɛi ni ajaa kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Te mi-kokoo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ haa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves creates a natural mulch blanket. This blanket shields the soil from direct sunlight, reducing evaporation so the roots stay cool and wet for a much longer time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɛkɛ tsɔne nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni ehaa la ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ be babaoo.

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like sunshades, keeping the young cocoa cool and preserving moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops yield better when I plant groundnuts on that same plot the season before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ wo yibii jogbaŋŋ beni midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans trap natural nutrients called nitrogen from the air and put them back into the dirt. This naturally enriches the soil, giving your maize more food to grow big cobs during the next season.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa o-corn lɛ náa niyenii babaoo ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii wuji anɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, usually right after a light rain, and when plants are actively growing. Applying fertilizer on dry soil can burn plant roots, while heavy rain right after application can wash the fertilizer away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ. kɛ be mli ni tsei miida Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to get more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I grow maize and cassava together on the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works well because maize grows quickly and is ready to harvest in three months, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the space after the maize has been harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni eshɛɔ he ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow, curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus. Removing infected plants early helps stop the disease from spreading to the rest of your healthy cassava crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa ŋmei tsei ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I prevent the bottoms of my tomato fruits from turning black and rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ediŋŋ ni efite?

english: Black rot at the bottom of tomatoes is usually caused by irregular watering and lack of calcium in the plant. Covering the soil around the plant with dry leaves helps keep soil moisture steady so the roots can absorb calcium properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ Tsei ni baai egbi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi daa. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they might rot and allows them to catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ, ni ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my harvested maize when I store it in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ kɛ́ mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils multiply quickly in stored grain if the maize still contains moisture. Sun-drying your maize thoroughly until it is completely hard before putting it in storage prevents insects from spoiling it.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii babaoo baa oya yɛ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ tee nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ewa kwraa dani akɛto lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi akafite lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. The leaves droop temporarily to protect the plant from heat, and they naturally stand back up once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. ni ebaate shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ gbɛkɛ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Is it better for my vegetables if I irrigate them in the middle of the day when the sun is hottest?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-aduawai lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ yɛ gbi mli be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering in the middle of the day causes most of the water to evaporate in the heat before your crops' roots can drink it. Watering early in the morning or late in the evening allows the soil to absorb the water so the plants can feed efficiently.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ yɛ gbi mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aŋɔ nu koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I use a motor pump to give my crops water every single day, will they grow faster?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsɔne pɔmp tsu nii kɛwo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu daa gbi. Ani ebaada oya?

english: Not necessarily. Crop roots need air just as much as they need water. Over-watering drowns the roots, stops them from taking up essential nutrients, and can cause root rot or yellow leaves.
ga: Dabi, kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa tsei shishifãi tamɔ bɔ ni tso shishifãi he hiaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ nu he hiamɔ Nu ni awoɔ fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni ayeɔ lɛ naatsii ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ shishifãi lɛ agbo loo baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: How do I know if my two-hectare farm is getting enough water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji hectare 2 lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can check soil moisture by digging a small hole about hand-depth near your plants. If the soil at that depth feels dry and crumbles easily in your hand, your crop field needs irrigation.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ ha kɛtsɔ bu bibioo ko ni oootse lɛ nɔ. Aaafee ŋmei tso ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso ko lɛ dalɛ Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nakai shishigbɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi ni efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Does using water pumped from a river affect my crops differently than natural rainfall?
ga: Ani nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ faa lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Rainfall carries natural nitrogen from the air which gives leaves an immediate green boost, but river water is equally good for growth as long as it is clean and provided consistently.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hiɛɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Shi nu ni yɔɔ faa lɛ mli lɛ hu he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha dalɛ nakai nɔŋŋ. Shii abɔ ni nu lɛ mli tse ni akɛhaa daa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to reduce their surface area facing the sun, which slows down water loss. It is the plant's natural defense against heat, but persistent curling into the evening means the crop is stressed and needs water.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ni kwɛɔ hulu la lɛ hiɛ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu. Shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shwie shi be fɛɛ be gbɛkɛ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao ni nu he miihia lɛ.

english: Why do crops planted on high, sloping ground dry out faster than those in the lowlands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ kɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Water naturally flows downhill and collects in lower areas, keeping lowland soil moist longer. Soil on hills drains water quickly and loses surface moisture faster to wind and sun exposure.
ga: Nu lɛ baatsɔ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaabua ehe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ hoɔ oya ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my cassava plants survive long dry spells while my pepper plants die without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep, tuberous roots that store water and reach underground reserves, whereas pepper plants have shallow roots that quickly dry out when surface soil loses moisture.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni toɔ nu ni amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ fo.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to cover the soil around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts as a protective blanket that shields the ground from the sun, reduces water evaporation, keeps roots cool, and prevents soil erosion.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I plant them close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, their roots compete aggressively for the same limited pool of water and soil nutrients, leaving every plant slightly starved and resulting in smaller yields.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei fɛɛ fioo ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo fioo.

english: How does clear-cutting trees around my cropland affect how water stays in my soil?
ga: Tsei ni afolɔ abɔle he lɛ jogbaŋŋ Te he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ saa nu ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Trees provide windbreaks and shade that keep the air cool and reduce evaporation. Removing all trees exposes your crops directly to harsh winds and full sun, causing soil to dry out much faster.
ga: Tsei haa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa la ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ ojie tsei lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ashɛ onibii ahe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen from flower to flower. If there are few insects around, or if heavy rain knocks them away, the unpollinated flowers simply drop off the branch without producing pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen ajɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛji kooloi bibii ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Fioo ko pɛ Aloo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsu amɛ ni amɛfo kɛtee? Fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ baagbee amɛniji lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does hand pollination actually help me get more cocoa pods on my farm?
ga: Te nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná kookoo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Hand pollination involves using a brush or cushion to manually transfer pollen directly onto the flowers. This guarantees that the flowers get pollinated even when natural insects are scarce, resulting in significantly more pods forming on each tree.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ biɔ ni akɛ brɔsh loo kushin atsu nii ni akɛ niji atsu nii ni akɛ pollen lɛ aya fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ, kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anamɔ wa po lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso fɛɛ tso yɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni sa kadimɔ waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade trees or plantains when I first plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantain beni miduɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct, hot sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains creates a cool umbrella over the seedlings, keeping the soil moist and protecting them until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ haa shade ni mli ejɔ baa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my farm regularly to check on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa koni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Crops need constant monitoring just like young children. Inspecting your farm frequently allows you to spot early signs of pests, leaf diseases, or drying soil before the problem spreads and ruins your entire harvest.
ga: Taakɛ gbekɛbii bibii ji lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ oyakwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii abɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai, tsei ahe helai, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he okadi mra dani naagba lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni efite oŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: My cocoa farm is around 20 years old, so why are my trees producing fewer pods than before?
ga: Mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ eye aaafee afii 20, no hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees pass 15 to 20 years of age, their natural productivity slows down and their roots absorb fewer nutrients from the soil. Older trees require heavy pruning, soil enrichment, or gradual replanting with younger high-yielding varieties to restore harvest levels.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko eye afii 15 kɛyashi 20 lɛ, bɔ ni efeɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baa shi. ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baaŋɔ niyenii fioo ko kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei ni edara lɛ biɔ ni afolɔ amɛ waa. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ saamɔ loo ŋmeii srɔtoi ni darako ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ adumɔ ekoŋŋ koni akɛha ŋmaa lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farm produce a massive harvest one season and very little the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ nibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli, ni fioo pɛ yɛ be kroko mli lɛ?

english: When a tree produces a huge crop, it consumes almost all of its stored energy and nutrients. Without adequate fertilizer, proper watering, and pruning, the tree becomes exhausted and needs a season to rebuild its strength before it can yield heavily again.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Ekɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni ekɛto lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa, nu kɛ tso lɛ ŋmɔmɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ he baajɔ ni ehe baahia ni ená be ni ekɛtswa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani enyɛ ewo yibii babaoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off green branches from my cocoa tree when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Pruning removes crowded or unproductive branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach the inner parts of the tree. This airflow dries out damp leaves, preventing fungal diseases like black pod while directing the tree's energy into pod growth.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni mli eyi obɔ loo ni wooo yibii lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ baaha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji anaa yɛ be mli ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ mli.

english: Why do some pests damage my crop leaves at night when I cannot see them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni minaaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Many crop pests, such as night-feeding beetles and caterpillars, hide from the intense daytime heat and predators. They emerge after sunset to feed on cool, fresh leaves, which is why you may see leaf damage without seeing insects during the day.
ga: Nɔ ni fata kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe srɔtoi babaoo ji ladybugs kɛ ŋmeii. Hiɛ ohe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli latsaa ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe. Amɛjeɔ kpo beni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni amɛye baai ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ ehee lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ekolɛ obaanyɛ ona baa ni efite ni onaaa kooloi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does heavy rain sometimes reduce my harvest instead of helping my crops grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: While water is essential, sudden torrential rain can wash away pollen, knock open flowers off the stems, and flood the soil, which rots roots and creates a humid environment where fungal diseases thrive.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu he miihia moŋ Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Ha fɔfɔi lɛ ajɛ tsei lɛ ashishi. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil is losing its power to nourish my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaahã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii?

english: When soil loses its fertility, crop leaves will start turning pale green or yellow, tree growth will stall, and the pods produced will be smaller than usual. Adding organic compost or appropriate fertilizers helps restore soil power.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee. Tso lɛ dalɛ baafee nɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. ni ŋmeii ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo fe bɔ ni eji daa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under bright sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and keeping the soil moist for the cocoa trees to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni cacao tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my plantains turn soft and yellow so quickly after I cut them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ oya beni mifolɔ amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, plantains naturally release a ripening gas called ethylene. Warm temperatures and rough handling speed up this gas release, causing the fruit to soften and ripen rapidly before reaching the market.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa Plantains lɛ, ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. He ni mli edɔ kɛ nitsumɔ ni mli wa haa kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ jeɔ kpo oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize crop lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is essential for healthy leaf growth, or that heavy rains have washed the soil nutrients too deep for roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce thin, small roots when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots compete underground for limited soil space, water, and nutrients, resulting in small roots rather than thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii baa yɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or dry conditions, causing the crop to drop its blossoms to conserve water and energy.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During intense afternoon heat, leaves lose moisture through transpiration faster than the roots can drink from the soil. Drooping is the crop's natural defense mechanism to reduce heat exposure.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ latsaa nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Drooping ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa dɔlɛ ni baa shi lɛ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and turning wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a reaction to tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids, which feed on the leaf underside and often spread leaf-curl viruses.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji hetoo ni akɛhaa kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids. Amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni bei pii lɛ amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bent and short instead of growing long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kuku moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers bend when they hit hard, compacted soil or underground rocks. Raising loose, deep soil mounds allows the tubers to expand downward without resistance.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baakɔ kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ awó gɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ mli shwereɔ kɛyaa shi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii enaa.

english: How can I tell that my green plantains are fully mature and ready to harvest before they start changing color?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-plantains eŋɔli lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa dani amɛje shishi amɛtsake amɛhe?

english: Green plantains are mature when the sharp angular edges on the skin become smooth and rounded, indicating that the fingers are filled with starch.
ga: Plantains eŋɔli lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewolo lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, oniji amli eyi kɛ ashikishaŋ.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or get full of small holes when stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ egbo loo eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Be ni akɛtoɔ kotoku mli?

english: Maize stored with too much internal moisture attracts insects like weevils and encourages mold growth. Drying the grain thoroughly under the sun before bagging protects it in storage.
ga: Abɛi ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ emli lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ daa. Kɛ́ oogbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu mli dani okɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know when my farm land is fully ready for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ he kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Your land is ready when the soil is cleared of deep weeds, loosened slightly so roots can easily spread, and naturally moist at the start of the rainy season.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Gbalamɔ mli fioo koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli

english: Is it better for me to plant my crops in straight lines instead of scattering them?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ tsei ashwã?

english: Planting in straight lines gives every plant equal space and sunlight, while making it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and walk through your farm.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko kɛ hulu la ni tamɔ amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyiɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why are some of my young crops growing tall and thin without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together or under thick shade, they stretch upward searching for sunlight instead of using their energy to grow strong stems and produce fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛtao hulu la moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need plantain trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu plantains abɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct heat. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that shade the cocoa and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot branches growing near the bottom of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main tree. Removing them keeps the main tree healthy and focused on producing large cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaawaje tso titri lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni eeefee lɛ nɔ.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds away from the base of my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi?

english: You should clear weeds every few weeks, especially during the rainy season, so the weeds do not steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight from your crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi fɛɛ jwɛi. otsii enyɔ loo enyɔ Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli Bɔni afee ni jwɛi akaju nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ

english: Leaves turn yellow and fall off when the tree lacks important nutrients in the soil, suffers from extreme dry weather, or has roots damaged by standing water.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa loo nu ni damɔ shi lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: What causes small black spots to spread across my growing cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ baa? Okɛgbɛ ashwã mi-kokoo ŋmɔji ni miida lɛ fɛɛ anɔ.

english: Black spots are usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet and shaded conditions. Clearing bushy growth helps sunlight dry the pods and prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Black Pod hela, ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ amli lɛ, hulu la lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa amɛdara.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm help crops grow better than using no fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli kooloi ashishifãi lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe nɔ ni mikɛwooo mli lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural nutrients that plants consume over time, while also improving the soil's ability to hold water during dry days.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli hu.

english: Why do my crops lose their flowers before those flowers can turn into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifɔlɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by prolonged hot weather, lack of soil water, insect damage, or lack of pollination.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ be kakadaŋŋ, nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, loo fɔfɔi ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ.

english: How many years can my cocoa trees keep producing good pods before they grow too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii kpakpai dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: Cocoa trees usually produce their best yields between 10 to 20 years of age. After around 15 to 20 years, their productivity naturally starts to decline, which is when farmers should consider rehabilitating the farm or replanting new seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ́ amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 20. Yɛ aaafee afii 15 kɛyashi 20 sɛɛ lɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji be ni esa akɛ okwaafoi asusu amɛŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛbaatswa ekoŋŋ loo dumɔwui heei ni amɛbaadu lɛ he.

english: Why do I see small insects gathered on almost every tree in my cocoa farm, and are they bad for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi bibii ni miibua amɛhe naa yɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni ani amɛnáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: Insects like mealybugs or capsids often gather on cocoa trees to feed on the sap of young shoots and pods. Some of these insects carry harmful diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, so seeing them spread across your trees means you need to inspect for damage and take control measures.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mealybugs loo capsids Bei pii lɛ Amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ koni amɛnu nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ekomɛi hiɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ona amɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã otsei lɛ amli fɛɛ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okwɛ kɛji nɔ ko efite ni ofee nɔ ko ni baaha okɛ ohe awo mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in open sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and small roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby creates a microclimate that protects young seedlings from heat stroke and soil moisture loss.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii. ni nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko baa ni buɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ he.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in high humidity and excessive wetness. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm, drying out the tree canopy and reducing the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: What causes the leaves on my maize crops to turn yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are typically a signal that the plant lacks key nutrients, especially nitrogen, in the soil. Adding organic compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores healthy green growth and improves yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa bɛ tso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my cocoa trees before turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from stress, such as prolonged dry weather, lack of nutrients, or insect attack. Proper shade management, mulching, and pest control help trees hold onto their flowers long enough to set pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ haomɔ ko ba amɛnɔ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tutuaa amɛ. Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa, mulching, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee pods.

english: Will cutting branches off my cocoa tree reduce the total harvest I get?
ga: Ani mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha mikpamɔ fɛɛ aba shi?

english: Pruning dead, diseased, or unnecessary branches actually increases your harvest. It directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier pods and reduces hiding spots for pests.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tso lɛ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. ni ajie hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ shi

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava or plantain on the same land as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping with plantains or cassava provides beneficial shade for young cocoa trees while giving you food and income while waiting for cocoa to mature. Just ensure proper spacing so the food crops do not overpower the cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni akɛ plantains loo cassava duɔ lɛ baaha cacao tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ahi mli koni niyenii tsei lɛ akaye kookoo lɛ fe nine.

english: How can I protect my young cocoa farm from drying out during the long harmattan dry season?
ga: Mabu kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ he. Te fee tɛŋŋ ni minɔ lɛ ha egbi yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around the base of young trees with dry leaves, straw, or grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture during the dry harmattan period.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi loo jwɛi (mulch) shwieɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my land has good soil for growing cocoa before I spend money planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni mikɛbaadu kookoo dani mafite shika kɛdu lɛ?

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, dark, rich in organic material, and drains excess water well while retaining moisture. Sandy soils that dry out quickly or heavy clay soils that stay waterlogged are not suitable for healthy cocoa growth.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli. Ni ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni egbiɔ oya loo shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ nɔ ni tsii ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ esaaa kɛha kookoo shweremɔ kpakpa.

english: Why does the government tell us to cut down our cocoa trees when the leaves start turning yellow and swollen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ kookoo tsei beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves and swollen stems are signs of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease. Because there is currently no chemical cure for this virus, cutting down the infected trees is the only effective way to stop the disease from spreading to the rest of your healthy farm.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ kɛ tsei ni efuu lɛ ji cocoa bud virus hela he okadii. Enɛ ji akɛ amrɔ nɛɛ tsofa ko bɛ ni abaanyɛ akɛ tsa hela nɛɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. ni ji oŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads rapidly in high humidity and excess water. When heavy rains come, fungal spores splash from the soil onto the pods, causing them to turn black if the farm is too dark or overcrowded.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo ni nu babaoo hu yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Fungal spores lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa etsɔɔ ediŋŋ kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ tsɔ loo eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi tsɔ.

english: What is causing the young branches and small pods on my cocoa trees to dry up and turn black?
ga: Mɛni kɛ tsei niji bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa? Yɛ mi cacao lɛ nɔ lɛ, egbiɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ.

english: This damage is usually caused by sap-sucking insects called mirids, locally known as Akate. They bite into the green stems and pods to feed, leaving wounds that dry out the plant tissues and prevent proper growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids, ni ale amɛ hu akɛ Akate lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ eŋɔlii lɛ koni amɛye niyenii. Eshiɔ pilamɔi ni haa tso lɛ fãji egbiɔ ni etsĩɔ dalɛ kpakpa naa.

english: Young cocoa trees have very tender leaves that burn easily under direct heat. They require temporary shade trees or plantain plants to protect them from scorching sunlight and keep moisture in the soil until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Amɛmiitao tsei loo plantains ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Can I plant cassava in the middle of my young cocoa farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: It is best to avoid planting cassava close to young cocoa trees because cassava roots spread aggressively and absorb large amounts of water and nutrients, which competes with and starves your young cocoa.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ kɛ o-cocoa ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baabɔ akaŋ ni ekɛ hɔmɔ baaba.

english: Why do many flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support. Flowers also drop if there are not enough tiny insects like midges to pollinate them, or if the tree is stressed by dry weather and lack of soil nutrients.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: How many years will it take for my new cocoa seedlings to start bearing fruits?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start flowering and producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years to start fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Why do my crops slow down their growth during the short dry spell in August?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ fo yɛ August mli nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry periods with less rainfall, crops slow down their growth and conserve water to survive. Their roots absorb less moisture, causing the plant to temporarily pause sending out fresh leaves until regular rains return.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi ni amɛbuɔ nu he koni amɛhi shi. Shishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɛɛ nu fioo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kpaɔ baai heei ni amɛtsuɔ lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa tamɔ bɔ ni efɔɔ feemɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Good cocoa soil should be deep, dark, well-drained, and soft enough for roots to penetrate. If rainwater sits on top of your land like a pond for days without sinking in, the soil has too much clay and may rot cocoa roots.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni mli kwɔ, ni eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyɛ blɛoo bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ abote mli. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ta shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ nubu gbii babaoo ni efoŋ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fa babaoo ni ebaanyɛ eha kookoo shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why is it necessary for me to trim and cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or unproductive branches, allowing sunlight and air to move freely through the tree canopy. This lowers humidity inside the tree to reduce pod diseases and directs the tree's energy into growing bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo ni wooo yibii lɛ ajieɔ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi koni ekɛba pod hela shi, ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ gbɛ koni eda ni etsɔ pod agboi.

english: Why does land that has been left to rest for many years yield better crops than land I farmed continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ashi afii babaoo nɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai fe shikpɔŋ ni mitsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: When land rests during a fallow period, wild vegetation grows and naturally returns essential nutrients, organic matter, and beneficial organisms to the soil, giving it time to rebuild its fertility.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehi shi yɛ fallow be mli lɛ, koo mli tsei baakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa anáa be ni akɛtswaa babaoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same spot drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests and soil diseases that feed on maize to multiply quickly.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa abɛi lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ayi fa oya.
