english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle direct, intense sunlight; tall trees provide essential shade and moisture retention needed to protect the young plants until they are established.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ haa hulutsoo ni amɛhiɛɔ nu ni he hiaa koni akɛbu tsei bibii ahe lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛbaatswa shi.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to leave wide space between my crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and smaller yields.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la fioo, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai ahe akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry while the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, causing it to move its remaining nitrogen to feed the newer growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa eyaa nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy green leaves but yield very small tubers beneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Ani eyɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi eyɛ bulbs bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to put all its energy into growing stem and leaves above ground rather than storing nutrients in the roots below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami ɔ kɛ toɔ sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why is it unsafe to apply fresh animal manure directly around the roots of my growing crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ No hewɔ lɛ tsei ni midu lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Fresh manure produces heat as it breaks down and contains strong salts that can burn crop roots, while also potentially spreading weeds and plant pathogens.
ga: Manɔ hee haa dɔlɛ baa beni efiteɔ lɛ, ni ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha jwɛi kɛ tsei amli helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dry leaves and straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry organic material, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, suppresses weeds, and keeps the root zone cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture for planting right after the first rain falls?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain often only wets the top layer of dirt; you should dig down a few inches to ensure the root layer is damp, avoiding early planting where seeds germinate and dry out during short dry spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ofo shi inchi fioo komɛi koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ shishifã lɛ mli edɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ adumɔ he mra yɛ he ni dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbi yɛ be kukuoo mli ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to cut off some healthy leaves and branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ baai kɛ niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary leafy growth so the plant directs its water and food toward developing bigger, healthier fruits rather than maintaining excess leaves.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ baa ni he ehiaaa ni eda lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei kudɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaahiɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct, harsh sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out their weak roots. Leaving some big trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantain protects young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni egbiɔ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Tsei wuji ni aaashi loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to eat holes inside my young maize leaves, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that lays eggs in the central leaves of maize. You can control them by checking your field early, squeezing the worms by hand if few, or spraying recommended organic extracts like neem leaf juice early in the morning.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. Okɛ onine amɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛji amɛyi faaa. Aloo shwiemɔ nibii ni ajieɔ yi akɛ ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ bɔɔ nii amli tamɔ neem baa mli nu lɛ nɔ leebi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy green leaves but give me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ jwɛi ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks phosphorus and potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of expanding its food-storing roots below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa tsɔ shi fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium bɛ mli lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛbaa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a haa sisifãhi nɛ a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the stems without forming any fruits during the dry hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause stress to tomato plants, preventing successful pollination. Providing light shade and watering regularly at the base of the plant during hot dry spells helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. ehaa pollination nyɛɛɛ aba mli ni ehaa hulutsoo be ni mli tse Ni nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ shishi daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Is it better for me to plant my maize seeds close together so I can harvest more plants from my farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni manyɛ makpa tsei babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting maize too close causes the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each stalk enough room to grow strong and produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ yitso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo tsei agboi ni he wa.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food from the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas put natural nitrogen back into the earth. Rotating them improves soil fertility for your next planting cycle.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha dumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing yellowish green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by small insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems from agricultural officers prevents this problem.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ du ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why is it necessary to cut off the extra shoots growing around the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Too many side shoots (suckers) steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing excess suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the mother plant produces big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Side shoots (shoots) babaoo tsɔ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ woɔ plantain ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale green even when the rain falls heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and absorb the soil nutrients and fertilizer before your plant roots can reach them. Clearing weeds early lets your crops drink up the food they need to stay green and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛheɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ye obua onibii lɛ ni amɛnu niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell that my yams are fully mature and ready to be dug out of the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams are mature when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up. This sign shows that the vine has finished sending all its energy down into the tuber for storage.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaa shi kɛyaa eyitso lɛ naa koni akɛto.

english: Why do my plantains seem to ripen mostly between September and January instead of all year round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-plantains lɛ shwereɔ babaoo yɛ September kɛ January teŋ moŋ fe afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain fruiting naturally follows rainfall cycles. The main harvest period usually peaks toward the end of the year after the major rainy season, leading to high availability between September and January.
ga: Plantains woɔ yibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ naa. Bei pii lɛ, kpamɔ be titri lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa mɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ fa babaoo yɛ September kɛ January teŋ.

english: Why is it so hard to find fresh plantains on the market between February and July?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaana plantains hee yɛ jara nɔ yɛ February kɛ July teŋ lɛ?

english: The period from February to July covers the dry season and early rains. Plantain trees produce much less fruit during these dry months, creating a natural lean period across Ghana.
ga: Be ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ February kɛyashi July lɛ ji be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ mra. Dumɔwui lɛ baawo yibii fioo kwraa yɛ nɛkɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ nɛɛ amli. Enɛ eha be ko eba ni adebɔɔ mli tsei tsuuu nii yɛ Ghana fɛɛ.

english: What month of the year is the best time for me to plant plantain suckers on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting at the start of the major rainy season around April or May gives young suckers enough soil moisture to build strong roots before the drier months arrive.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli, aaafee April loo May lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii bibii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee shishifãi ni wa dani nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ aba.

english: How many months does it usually take for a plantain plant to produce ripe fruit after planting?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: It generally takes between 12 to 15 months for a plantain sucker to grow, flower, form a bunch, and fully mature for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 dani dumɔwui lɛ daraa, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, amɛfeɔ kui, ni amɛdaraa kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How can I keep my plantain plants healthy during dry months like February and March?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi plantains lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ tamɔ February kɛ March lɛ amli?

english: Covering the soil around the base of your plantain plants with dry leaves, grass, or cocoa pods keeps the soil cool and retains moisture during hot, dry spells.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ awo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Is it possible for me to get plantains to harvest in May or June when prices are high?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akpa nii yɛ May loo June mli beni nibii ajara wa lɛ?

english: Yes, if you irrigate your farm during the dry season and apply fertilizer or manure, your plantain trees will continue producing fruit even during the usual off-season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ nu wo oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he. Odumɔwui lɛ baaya nɔ awo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ po.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up early in the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Early-year sun heat and dry soil put stress on the plantain plant. The leaves dry out to save water, which slows down the growth of the fruit bunch.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Baai lɛ baagbi koni nu akafite. Enɛ baaha aduawai akuu lɛ aya hiɛ blɛoo.

english: How can I plan my farm so I have plantains to sell continuously instead of all at once?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni maya nɔ mahɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui shikome moŋ?

english: You can use staggered planting by planting small batches of suckers every one to two months during the rainy season, allowing your crop to mature at different times of the year.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ staggered planting atsu nii kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ooodu daa nyɔji 1-2 yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli.

english: How do I know the right time to cut my plantain bunch before it gets soft?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafo plantains ŋmɔ ko dani amɛfee blɛoo?

english: A plantain bunch is ready for harvest when the individual fingers look full and rounded rather than sharp-edged, and the small flower parts at the tips dry off easily.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni inchi fɛɛ inchi tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ ni eyɛ kokroo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. kɛ fɔfɔii amli fãi bibii Naagbee lɛ baanyɛ agbi oya.

english: What can I do if all my plantains ripen at the same time in December and market prices drop?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛji akɛ plantains lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli yɛ December mli ni jara lɛ ba shi?

english: You can harvest them while green and keep them in a cool shade to delay ripening, or process surplus plantains into dried chips or flour to sell later when prices rise.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa amɛ be mli ni amɛji eŋɔli lolo ni okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ koni ekɛha amɛshweremɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo. aloo afee plantains ni fa fe nine lɛ afee woji ni egbi loo ashikishaŋ koni akɛhɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli kɛ́ jara lɛ tee hiɛ.

english: Why do people say planting legumes like groundnuts or cover crops gives strength back to my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leguminous crops capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they decay, they act like natural plant food, enriching the soil with nutrients that make your next crops grow strong and healthy.
ga: Legumes mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ amɛgboi lɛ Ebaatsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii babaoo ni baaha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing thin and weak instead of standing tall and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadamɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Crops grow thin and fall over when the soil lacks essential nutrients or when seeds are planted too close together. Adding manure or compost builds stem strength so the plant can withstand wind and heavy ears of grain.
ga: Tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaawaje tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dumɔwui atoi ni tsii lɛ anaa.

english: What is liquid fertilizer, and how does it help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ji nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Liquid fertilizer is a concentrated mixture of plant nutrients dissolved in water. When sprayed on leaves or poured near roots, it gives plants a quick, direct boost of food to help weak crops recover fast.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji tso mli niyenii ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni akɛwo nu mli. Kɛji akɛ afɔse ashwie baai anɔ loo afɔse ashwie shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ Ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná niyenii tɛ̃ɛ oya. Koni eye ebua tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ oya.

english: How do I know if my cassava leaves are changing color because of disease or just lack of water?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ hela loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ ni ŋmei baai lɛ etsake amɛhe lɛ?

english: Dry crops wilt evenly during the hot sun and bounce back after rain. Diseases leave distinct spots, yellow patterns, or curling on the leaves, showing that the plant is sick and needs medicine or treatment.
ga: Nibii ni egbi lɛ baagbi pɛpɛɛpɛ. Buu ohe he yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni nyɛku sɛɛ nyɛfo yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse baa. Ayɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ hela mɔ tso lɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ tsofa loo atsa lɛ.

english: Can I use natural medicinal plants like neem leaves to protect my crops from insect attacks?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem baai abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, crushed neem leaves contain natural bitter compounds that repel insect pests and treat plant fungal infections without harming the soil or crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔ ko ni yɔɔ neem baai ni atswa lɛ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni mli wa ni shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ni etsaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ni eyeee shikpɔŋ lɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Why is it important to choose the biggest and healthiest seeds for planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahala dumɔwui ni dara fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ kɛha midumɔ nii lɛ?

english: Big, undamaged seeds contain stored energy and strength inside them. This gives the young shoot the power to break through the soil quickly and resist early pests before its roots are fully formed.
ga: Dumɔwu agbo ni efiteee lɛ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ emli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ mra be mli kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ kwraa.

english: What is Lucerne grass, and why would a crop farmer grow fodder plants?
ga: Mɛni ji lucerne jwɛi? Ni mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni duɔ nii lɛ duɔ kooloi aniyenii?

english: Lucerne is a legume grass rich in protein. Farmers grow it either to feed livestock high-quality fodder or to plow it back into the ground as green manure to restore strength and nutrients to exhausted farmland.
ga: Lucerne ji jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli ni protein babaoo yɔɔ mli. Okwaafoi duɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi loo amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How does adding animal manure to my farm help crops absorb water and food better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure acts like a sponge in the soil. It improves the soil's ability to hold onto rain water while slowly releasing nutrients that crops need to maintain vigor during hot weather.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni fiofio lɛ ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná hewalɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable crops keep getting sick even when I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ yaa nɔ hela mɔɔ mi lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo ha po?

english: Water alone gives moisture, but plants also need balanced food for strength. Too much standing water can actually encourage plant diseases and root rot if the plants do not have proper drainage and nutrients.
ga: Nu pɛ haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ. Shi niyenii ni ja hu he miihia tsei koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baanyɛ awo tsei ahelai kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow faster and stronger than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing them early ensures your crops get all the nourishment needed to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli lɛ mli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and sensitive roots that cannot handle direct harsh sunlight and drying winds. Providing shade plants like plantains creates a cooler microclimate and shields the young cocoa until its roots grow deep enough to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ mli jɔɔ fioo ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when high winds blow during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that hold onto the topsoil loosely. When the soil becomes soft from rain and the fruiting bunch gets heavy, the plant loses balance easily, so propping the stem with sturdy wooden forks is necessary to keep it standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he mlɛo. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ lɛ mli ni yibii ni woɔ yibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo lɛ. Tsei baanyɛ afite amɛhe oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ tso ni mli wa afi tso lɛ sɛɛ koni ehi shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the center vein of older leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen hunger. The maize plant is moving available nitrogen from its lower, older leaves up to nourish the younger growing leaves, showing that the soil needs nitrogen fertilizer or compost.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen hɔmɔ miiye mɔ. Abele tsei miitsi nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛmiijɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛmiiya ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but yield small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing heavy stems and foliage above ground rather than storing food reserves in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi kɛ baai ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní nɛ a to ngɛ tso ɔ sisi ɔ mi ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot away during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which thrives in high humidity and excess shade. Wet conditions allow fungal spores in the soil to splash onto the pods and spread rapidly if branches and weeds block airflow.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine. Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya kɛji tsei tsei kɛ jwɛi tsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting into tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites, or viruses spread by insects. As the insects feed on the soft parts of the leaves, the uneven leaf growth causes curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni baa mɔ mli ni ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmeii yeɔ baai lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Baai ni edaaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔlɔ aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly between bone dry and waterlogged. Extreme stress causes the plant to drop its blossoms to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ wu ni egbi kɛ nu ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ teŋ. Haomɔ ni naa wa haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Yam leaves need direct access to sunlight to feed the plant. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp soil, maximizing sunlight capture for bigger tubers while keeping the leaves dry to prevent leaf spot diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua tso lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ hulu la fataa tubers wuji ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, gĩ baai lɛ koni akaye baai lɛ ahe hela.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have beneficial root bacteria that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next crop cycle.
ga: Bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa mli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Aduawai ni akɛ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ewo mli

english: Covering soil with organic materials, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, reduces water loss through evaporation during hot weather, suppresses weeds, and breaks down into natural plant food over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa shi. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni efiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when exposed to full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves are tender and easily damaged by intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living canopy that protects the young cocoa from heat while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does putting dry grass around the base of my crops help them survive during short dry spells?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the soil so it doesn't evaporate quickly in the sun, and it keeps the soil cool for the plant roots.
ga: Mulching around Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ŋmɔɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ lɛ, efoŋ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛha tsei shishifãi

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyaa shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential plant food. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top, causing the lower ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot every year drains the soil of the specific nutrients that plant loves, and it lets pests and diseases build up in the dirt. Rotating with beans or groundnuts helps put natural nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni tso lɛ sumɔɔ. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer so that the rain does not carry it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni nugbɔ lɛ akajie lɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist, but not right before a heavy downpour. Applying it a few inches away from the plant stem into moist soil allows the roots to absorb it before rain can wash it down the hill.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi esaaa akɛ owoɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii inchi fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔ lɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin, weak, and tall without producing good yield when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops are forced to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving plants proper space allows each stalk to grow thick, strong, and yield larger produce.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ Dumɔwui anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ oha otsei lɛ he ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehe wa, ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and twisted even when the green vines above ground look big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni efite lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni da moŋ,.

english: If the soil mound is too hard or shallow, the expanding yam tuber hits tough ground and cannot grow straight or big. Mounding deep, soft soil gives the tuber the space it needs to swell easily underground.
ga: Kɛji gɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo ekɔɔɔ tsɔ Expanded sweet potato tubers lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni enyɛŋ eda tɛ̃ɛ loo efee agbo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaabɔ he ni mli kwɔ ni efee blɛoo lɛ haa bulb lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo.

english: Why are tiny worms eating holes in the leaves of my young corn and hiding in the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ni amɛmiitee amɛhe amɛwo hoppers amli lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the central shoot of maize to feed on tender leaves. Catching them early and treating the funnel of the plant stops them from destroying the growing point of the corn.
ga: Nɔ ni fɔɔ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei ateŋ koni eye tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okwɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite hei ni ŋmeii lɛ daa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and turn yellowish-green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus stops the plant from making food properly, which reduces the size of the roots underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Virus tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ baa shi.

english: Why are flowers falling off my pepper plants without forming any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper yibii ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely high heat, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently watered helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their tender leaves cannot withstand direct, intense sunlight, which scorches them and stops them from absorbing soil nutrients properly.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛshãa ni ehaaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aná jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I select the best plantain suckers from my farm to start a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for 'maiden' suckers, which are medium-sized shoots with narrow, spear-like leaves, as they establish roots faster and grow into stronger plants than broad-leaved suckers.
ga: Taomɔ ‘maiden’ tsei, ni ji tsei ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ shishifãi oya ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing starting at the lower leaves usually means your soil is low on nitrogen, a nutrient maize heavily relies on to build strong leaves and green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi niyenii damɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji anɔ waa.

english: What is making holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji baa mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that hides inside the central shoot of young maize plants to feed on tender leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni eye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: How do I know if the early rains are enough for me to start planting my crop seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Planting should wait until rain wets the soil deeply—about hand-depth—and the soil stays moist for several days so seeds do not dry out after sprouting.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui amɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa. (Aaafee bɔ ni onine lɛ shɛɔ he lɛ) ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baahi ŋmɔtɔ mli gbii babaoo. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Which part of the cassava stem is best for me to cut and plant for a good harvest?
ga: Kasava tso lɛ fã ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafolɔ ni madu koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: The mature middle section of a healthy stem with clear nodes works best, as the very soft top rots easily and the very woody base takes longer to sprout.
ga: Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nodes ni atsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋwɛi fã ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ fiteɔ oya. Ni tso shishitoo lɛ baahe be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃.

english: Why is it important for me to lift my yam vines onto wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mawo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so they can make food for the tubers while keeping foliage off the wet ground to prevent leafy diseases.
ga: Akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ woɔ hulu lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ ahe koni baa lɛ akaye helai.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same piece of land three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ he?

english: Planting the same crop continuously strips the same nutrients out of the soil every season and gives pests and diseases a permanent home to build up.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa Na he ko ni ohiɔ daa

english: Why do people tell me that planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes my soil better for other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dumɔ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally feeds and fertilizes the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni amɛwoɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers, but the flowers fall off without making fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat is too extreme, water supply is irregular, or weather stops insects from properly pollinating the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. Aloo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ haaa kooloi bibii lɛ aná fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is crop pollination, and why is it important for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei amli ŋmɔtɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Pollination happens when pollen moves from one flower to another, allowing the crop to form seeds and fruits. Without proper pollination, flowers drop off without producing any harvest.
ga: Pollination baa kɛji pollen lɛ je fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛtee ekroko mli. Ha tsei awo dumɔwui kɛ aduawai. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but many of them fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Flowers often fall off if they are not pollinated by insects or human assistance, or if the plant suffers from heat and lack of water. Unpollinated flowers drop naturally to save the plant's energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii loo adesai yelikɛbuamɔ haaa amɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ emli lɛ hewɔ. Fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu tso lɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Is it possible for me to pollinate my crop flowers by hand if there are no insects around?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mikɛ miniji baawo fɔfɔi ni miduɔ lɛ amli? Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii bɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: Yes, manual or hand pollination involves transferring pollen from one flower to another using simple tools or hands. This technique guarantees that flowers turn into healthy pods or fruits even when insects are scarce.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔ ni fata nine loo nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ he ji ni akɛ nibii loo niji ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii ni akɛjie fɔfɔi lɛ kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Nɛkɛ ŋaa nɛɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli po.

english: If only a few flowers survive on my plant, is that enough to give me a good harvest?
ga: Kɛji mitso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi fioo pɛ Ani no fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Yes, every successfully pollinated flower can develop into a full fruit or pod. Even a modest number of well-pollinated flowers can yield a profitable harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi ni yeɔ omanye ni ekɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ aduawai loo ŋmɔtɔ kwraa. Fɔfɔi fioo ko ni awo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ po baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he.

english: What causes crop flowers to dry up during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni haa tso fɔfɔii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause water stress in plants. To protect themselves from drying out completely, crops shed delicate parts like flowers to save moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ baa tsei amli. Koni okɛbu ohe he koni okagbi kwraa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, tamɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: How does supporting flower development help increase the money I earn at harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ ni mikɛyeɔ mibuaa lɛ haa shika ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛ́ mikpaa nii lɛ yaa hiɛ?

english: Protecting and pollinating flowers ensures that a higher percentage of them turn into sellable crops, directly increasing your total harvest weight and market earnings.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni abuɔ ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ oha mlijaa 100 ni fa fe fɛɛ bafeɔ tsei ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ mli tsiimɔ kɛ jarayeli mli shika ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can government agricultural programs support me on my farm?
ga: Te nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Government initiatives often train field workers to assist farmers with specialized tasks like hand pollination, provide subsidized fertilizers, or connect farmers with modern growing techniques.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔyeli lɛ nifeemɔi tsɔseɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi koni amɛye amɛbua okwaafoi kɛ nitsumɔi krɛdɛɛi, tamɔ fɔfɔii ni akɛ niji feɔ lɛ. Ni akɛ shika haa ŋmɔshi nibii loo akɛ okwaafoi kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ ŋaai atsa

english: Why is extra farm labor useful around the time my crops start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ kroko ni fata he lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: Flowering happens quickly and requires timely care like hand pollination, weed management, and pest control. Having extra help during this short window ensures maximum fruit set.
ga: Fɔfɔi baa oya ni ebiɔ ni akwɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ, tamɔ nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ Yelikɛbuamɔ kroko ni fata he yɛ be kukuoo mli Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni aduawai lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long after planting does it usually take for crops to start producing flowers?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ dani ebɔi fɔfɔi?

english: This depends on the crop; short-term crops flower in a few months, while tree crops like cocoa take two to three years to build strong stems before flowering.
ga: Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ Tsei ni hiɔ shi be kuku lɛ baawo fɔfɔi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni ji jwɛi tamɔ kookoo lɛ heɔ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ dani amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Can young people with agricultural training help improve the crop yields on my farm?
ga: Ani oblahii kɛ oblayei ni yɔɔ okwaayeli he tsɔsemɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, young agricultural workers trained in modern techniques—such as hand pollination and proper pruning—can boost your farm's productivity and save you time during critical growing periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, oblahii kɛ oblayei ni tsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ atsɔse amɛ yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai tamɔ nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli kɛ ŋmeii ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ ni ekɛ be akafite yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like mites or aphids feeding on the plant sap, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Managing these insects early prevents the leaves from twisting and stops the plant's growth from stalling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni whiteflies hiɛɔ lɛ nɔ Akwɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe ni ebaatsi tso lɛ dalɛ naa koni ekakpa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant feels stressed or overloaded with leaf growth, it sheds its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli loo eyɛ baai ni eda fe nine Ebaajie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests every year if I plant it in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it good for me to plant beans alongside my maize on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛfata ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very helpful. Beans take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil to feed the maize, while also covering the ground to keep the soil moist and stop weeds from growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the rains become steady—usually after two or three heavy downpours that wet the soil deep down—rather than planting after the very first light shower, which can leave seeds to dry out in the hot soil.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be—bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ sɛɛ—shi moŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ asɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide shade with their broad leaves, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry the farm and reduce the moisture the fungus needs to grow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni eha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ŋmeii lɛ adara lɛ aba shi

english: How can I tell that my cassava is ready for harvesting without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni atsaaa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, the main stem becomes thick and woody, and visible cracks appear in the soil near the base of the plant from the swelling tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso titri lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tsei. Ni ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to place tall sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground exposes the leaves to maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce food, which is sent down to grow bigger, healthier yam tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahe babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. Akɛ enɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing in a V-shape starting from the tip of lower leaves is a clear sign that the maize lacks nitrogen. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help the crop regain its dark green color and vigor.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ V ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená su ni mli edɔ ni mli wa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients out of the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the plant turn green again so it can produce large ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen miiye onibii lɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them with maize acts as a natural fertilizer, helping your maize grow stronger while enriching the ground for next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings need plantains or shade trees growing over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ adu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ amɛyiteŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and preserving soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants make their food through leaves exposed to sunlight. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground so leaves get maximum sunlight, air flow, and protection from ground diseases, which leads to bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei hoɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. koni baai lɛ aná hulu la kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ helai ni tsiɔ mɔ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do people cover the base of their vegetable plants with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai haa aduawai ashishi lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the dirt, prevents weeds from growing, and slowly decays into natural food for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy or flat soil during rainy periods. Building raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without making fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or severe dryness. Giving your plants consistent water and shade during the hottest part of the day helps the flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hulutsoo be mli haomɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo ha tso lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling up and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking juice from the undersides of leaves. Spraying an organic mixture like neem seed oil solution helps control these pests and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem dumɔwui amli fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni ebuɔ baai heei ni daa lɛ ahe.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my farm cause my crops to grow thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Removing weeds early ensures that all the food in the ground goes into making your crops yield well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa yibiiwoo kpakpa.

english: Why is it bad to plant tomatoes on the same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows specific pests and soil diseases to build up in that spot and drains the exact same nutrients every season. Rotating with different crops starves out pests and keeps the soil balanced.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai komɛi abua amɛhe naa yɛ nakai he lɛ ni amɛbaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ mli daa be. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: What is a fungicide, and how does it help my mango farm?
ga: Mɛni ji tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi mango tso yibii lɛ?

english: A fungicide is a special plant medicine sprayed on crops to prevent or kill fungi. Fungi are tiny germs that cause diseases like leaf spots and flower rot on mangoes, so spraying fungicide protects your trees and keeps the fruit healthy.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ji tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ koni akɛtsi ŋmeii anaa loo agbe amɛ. Fungi ji helai bibii. ni kɛ helai srɔtoi tamɔ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ yɛ mango nɔ lɛ baa No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ shwie otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu otsei lɛ ahe ni eye ebua ni aduawai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it insects or something else that causes most of the damage to mango fruits?
ga: Ani kooloo ko loo nɔ kroko ji nɔ ni kɛ mango yibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ?

english: While insects can cause damage, fungal diseases are actually the main threat to mangoes. Fungi cause fruits to turn black, spoil, or fall off early, especially when there is a lot of moisture.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ afite nii moŋ, shi yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ji nɔ titri ni woɔ mango he gbeyei. Fuji lɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, amɛgboiɔ loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya, titri lɛ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: How do fungi harm my mango crop if I cannot easily see them with my eyes?
ga: Te ŋmeii baanyɛ aye mango tso awui aha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ akɛ hiŋmɛi ana amɛ?

english: Fungi are microscopic organisms carried by wind and water drops. Once they land on your mango blossoms or young fruits, they feed on the plant, causing flowers to dry up and fruits to rot before they can grow full size.
ga: Fungi ji nibii bibii ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu mli nu bibii woɔ. Beni amɛshɛɔ o-mango fɔfɔi loo aduawai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ. Ebaaye tso lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ ni aduawai lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa kɛyashɛɔ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Why do my mango trees get dark spots and rotting as soon as the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates a damp environment where fungal germs thrive and spread very quickly. The moisture helps the fungi attack leaves, flowers, and fruits, causing rot if the tree is not protected.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. he ni ŋmei lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ Fɛ̃i haa ŋmei lɛ tutuaa baai, fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ kɛji abuuu tso lɛ he.

english: When is the best time for me to spray medicine on my mango trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afɔ mango tsei anɔ tsofa?

english: The best time to spray fungicide is right at the beginning of the rainy season. This creates a protective shield on the tree before the damp weather allows fungal diseases to start spreading.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baa dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii helai jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Will rain wash away the spray medicine if I spray my mangoes during the wet season?
ga: Ani nugbɔ lɛ baajie tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ kɛji mikɛ mango shwie nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: If you apply the fungicide during dry breaks in the weather, it sticks to the leaves and branches. Once dry, it stays on the plant to fight off fungi even when it rains.
ga: Kɛ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii tsu nii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaakpɛtɛ baai kɛ tsei aniji ahe. Kɛji egbi lɛ, ebaaya nɔ ehi tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmeii awuu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po.

english: Why do I need to take extra care of my mango trees compared to some of my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ mi mango tso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Mango trees are very sensitive to wet-weather diseases during their flowering and fruiting stages. Without proper care like seasonal spraying, fungal diseases can quickly destroy your entire harvest.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ helai yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ yɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ be mli ni akɛ tsofa shwieɔ nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Fungal helai baanyɛ afite onibii fɛɛ oya.

english: Can spraying fungicide on my mango trees help increase the amount of fruit I harvest?
ga: Ani tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛshwieɔ mi mango tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha aduawai ni mikpaa lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, spraying fungicide prevents fungal diseases from destroying the delicate mango flowers and young fruits, allowing more healthy mangoes to stay on the tree until harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii helai akafite mango fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Enɛ haa mango ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa.

english: What basic steps should I take to prevent my mangoes from getting spoiled before harvest time?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee koni mi-mango lɛ akafite dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba?

english: To protect your mangoes, keep the farm clean, prune dead branches, and apply fungicide sprays right before and during the rainy season to keep destructive diseases away.
ga: Koni okɛbu o-mango lɛ he Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ. Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ afɔse dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa kɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa koni helai akabote mli.

english: Why does plant disease spread so fast across my farm when the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater splashing from leaf to leaf and wind blowing during storms spread fungal spores rapidly across the farm. Combined with high humidity, this allows diseases to multiply fast if untreated.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa yɛ ahum be mli lɛ gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛ akɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo fata he lɛ ebaaha helai srɔtoi aba Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji atsaaa lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Taller trees provide essential shade and keep the air and soil humid, which protects young cocoa leaves from burning until the crop matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tso lɛ daa kwraa.

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that shield young cocoa plants from intense sun exposure. They also provide food and income for your family while you wait for your cocoa trees to start bearing fruit.
ga: Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Amɛhaa oweku lɛ niyenii kɛ shika hu yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a key food element in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmei lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to multiply in the ground. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnut refills nutrients naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge top leaves but very small tubers underneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together or given too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to build leaves instead of storing strength underground in large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ bulb agboi amli.

english: Why do I need to erect wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a vine crop that needs to spread its leaves high in the sunlight to make food. Staking raises the leaves off the wet ground, catching maximum sunlight and preventing leaf disease.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulu la mli koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking baajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. koni ená hulu la babaoo ni ekɛtsi baa helai anaa

english: How do I know the right time to sow my crop seeds after the long dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ eho lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until two or three heavy rains have soaked the soil deeply. Planting after the very first light rain can cause seeds to sprout and dry up if dry weather returns.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps soil moisture under hot sun conditions and prevents rain from splashing dirt and diseases onto your tomato leaves.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni otsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ muji kɛ helai srɔtoi ashwã o-tomato baai lɛ anɔ

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow poorly even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil nutrients, sunlight, and water directly away from your crops. Clearing weeds during the first few weeks after planting lets your crops get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: What makes tiny holes appear in the young leaves of my maize plants with light dust inside?
ga: Mɛni haa buji lɛ feɔ bibii? Eje kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ anɔ ni sũ fioo ko yɔɔ mli.

english: Tiny holes and powdery material inside young maize leaves are signs of caterpillar pests like the fall armyworm. Finding them early and treating them with safe pesticides or neem oil stops them from destroying the growing crop.
ga: Buu bibii kɛ nibii ni tamɔ powda ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ ahe okadi. Ni oootao amɛ mra ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem fɔ atsa amɛ. Ehaaa amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ.

english: If I plant beans together with my main crops, will the beans steal all the plant food from the soil?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ du ŋmeii Ani ŋmeii baaju tso niyenii fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, beans actually help feed the soil. They capture nitrogen from the air and convert it into plant food in the ground, which helps neighboring crops grow stronger and healthier.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ. Amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ niyenii kɛhaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees grow so much faster than other crops I plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miida oya fe tsei krokomɛi ni mikwɛɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly because their large leaves capture maximum sunlight to make food, and their roots spread fast to absorb water, giving them a fast growth habit compared to slower crops.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ejaakɛ amɛbaai wuji lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu la lɛ babaoo kɛhooɔ nii. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya koni amɛmɔmɔ nu. Enɛ haa amɛnáa su ni haa amɛdaraa oya kɛ akɛto tsei ni daaa blɛoo lɛ ahe.

english: What is the actual job of crop protector chemical sprays on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nitsumɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni tsofa ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crop protectors act like a shield for your plants. They destroy harmful insects and prevent crop diseases so your plants can grow safely without getting damaged.
ga: Nibii ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ otsei lɛ ahe. Amɛfiteɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, ni amɛtsiɔ tsei ahelai anaa koni otsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee amɛ.

english: How do I know when my bean plants are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-bean tsei lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Bean plants are ready to harvest when the leaves turn yellow and drop off, the pods turn dry and brown, and you can hear the seeds rattling inside when you shake a pod.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Pods lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni obaanyɛ onu dumɔwui lɛ ni miihoso yɛ mli lɛ he kɛ́ otsi pod lɛ.

english: Why does the ground around my plantain trees stay wet even when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ he ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ Ani mi-plantains lɛ mli efɔ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ hulu lɛ miitso waa moŋ?

english: Plantain stems store a lot of water inside them, and their wide leaves throw shade over the soil around their base, stopping the sun from drying out the ground too quickly.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ kɛ nu babaoo toɔ. Ni baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni hulu lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya tsɔ.

english: Can I spray crop protection chemicals on my farm at any time of the day?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening when the weather is cool and calm, because hot sun can evaporate the liquid quickly or scorch the plant leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni eyɛ kpoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha nu afee la oya loo eshã tsei ahe baai.

english: Why do fewer weeds grow in the parts of my field where I plant bushy beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ waaa kwraa yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ? Yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Bushy bean plants grow dense leaves close to the ground that create shade, which blocks light from reaching weed seeds so they cannot germinate easily.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ woɔ baai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni no haa hulutsoo baa. ni tsiɔ la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe No hewɔ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ mlɛo.

english: Why are my smaller crops growing pale and tall under my heavy plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ji lɛ No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekwɛɔ mi dumɔwui ni mli tse lɛ ashishi.

english: When plantain trees cast too much shade, smaller crops under them stretch upward towards the light and lose their green color because they cannot make enough food without direct sunlight.
ga: Beni plantains haa hulutsoo babaoo lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ he ni amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ baaje mli ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛji hulu la shɛɛɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Will spraying crop protector speed up how fast my crops grow or does it only stop insects?
ga: Ani nibii ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya loo ebaaha kooloi bibii lɛ akpa kɛkɛ?

english: Crop protectors mainly stop pest damage. By keeping pests away, the plant spends all its energy on fast growth and fruit production instead of healing from insect bites.
ga: Nibii ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ateŋ babaoo tsiɔ nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ lɛ anaa. Kɛtsɔ kooloi ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ni abaatsi naa lɛ nɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii kɛha dalɛ oya kɛ yibiiwoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaatsa kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ lɛ mli

english: Where do new plantain plants come from after I harvest the main tree?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni plantains heei lɛ jɛɔ beni mikpa tso titri lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plantain trees produce underground stems that sprout small side plants called suckers around the base, which grow into new producing trees after the main stem is cut.
ga: Plantains woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ suckers ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he, ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei heei beni afo tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the chemical sprays I buy for my maize farm sometimes fail to kill the pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbeee tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ bei komɛi lɛ?

english: Agro-chemicals require proper timing, exact measurement, and patience to work effectively. Spraying during heavy rain washes the medicine away before pests can absorb it, while using the wrong dosage or spraying at the wrong time of day reduces its power.
ga: Okwaayeli mli tsofafeemɔ heɔ be. Susumɔ ni ja kɛ tsuishitoo ni baaha etsu nii jogbaŋŋ Tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ hoɔ tsofa lɛ he dani tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aŋɔ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofa lɛ falɛ ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa mli lɛ haa tsofa lɛ hewalɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds keep growing back so quickly on my land even after I spray weedkiller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miidara oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ efɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weedkillers usually only kill the living weeds visible above ground. The soil holds hidden seeds that sprout as soon as sunlight and rain reach them, so controlling weeds requires repeating treatments or using mulching to block light.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni hiɛ ka ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ toɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ba pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ biɔ ni atsu he nii shii abɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii koni ekɛha hulutsoo.

english: Is it better to burn the bushes and cut wood on my land before planting, or leave them to rot?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ tsei ni afolɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu loo mahã amɛgboi?

english: Burning clears land quickly, but it destroys rich organic matter and good soil organisms. Leaving cut vegetation to decompose naturally feeds nutrients back into the dirt and helps retain soil moisture during dry periods.
ga: Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their tender leaves burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving scattered large trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that protects seedlings while they establish roots.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni eda lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa be mli ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: How can I tell when it is safe to plant my maize after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground receives two or three deep, soaking rains rather than planting after the very first light shower. Planting too early leaves seeds vulnerable to drying out if rain pauses for a week or two.
