ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni mli kwɔ enyɔ loo etɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ baagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome loo enyɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing tall stems and bushy leaves instead of storing food in their root tubers below ground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why should I avoid placing chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni mikɛwoɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ he?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that can burn plant stems and roots if applied directly against them. It should be placed in a small circle a few inches away so roots can draw in nutrients safely.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ akɛwo kooloo bibioo ko mli. No ji inchi fioo ko pɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields every year if I keep planting maize in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil. Rotating different crops keeps the soil balanced and healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: This problem, called blossom-end rot, happens when plants cannot absorb enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent prevents the fruit bottoms from turning black.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsi aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvested grain rot and attract insects so quickly inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikpa lɛ miifite ni egbala kooloi oya kɛmiiba mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvesting grain before it is completely dry leaves trapped moisture inside, creating a wet environment where mold grows and insects thrive. Sun-drying grain thoroughly until it is hard and brittle keeps storage pests away.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ akpamɔ dani amɛgbi kwraa. Baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli. shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni afeɔ Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ni kooloi bibii hu kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ. Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Keeping or planting shade crops like plantains or mature trees creates a protective canopy that provides shade and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa plants grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Nibii ni haa hulutsoo tsei, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei wuji ni akpaa loo amɛduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be baa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn cob even forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear signal that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for healthy green growth. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen-based fertilizer early in the crop's growth helps restore leaf color and improves yield.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ tso lɛ shishijee be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do extension agents recommend planting groundnuts or beans in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special root nodules that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil fertilizer. Intercropping them with maize feeds the soil naturally and helps the maize grow bigger without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni edara ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa babaoo awo mli tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Is it necessary for me to stake my yam vines with wood, or can I just leave them to creep on the ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tso adu sweet potato wain tsei? Aloo obaaha ekplekeshi shikpɔŋ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch more sunlight to feed the growing root underground, resulting in larger yam tubers and protecting the leaves from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛha shishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji, ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I cover the exposed soil around my crops with dry grass or cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ sũ ni ebɔle he lɛ awo mli lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔji yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering soil with dry organic material (mulching) acts like a blanket that stops the harsh sun from evaporating groundwater, prevents weeds from taking over, and slowly breaks down to enrich the soil.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ naa koni ekajɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛfite fiofio koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ aya hiɛ.

english: What is eating small holes into the heart of my young maize leaves and leaving dark droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni miiye yɛ bu bibioo lɛ mli? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ Ni eshiɔ ŋmãa ni tsuɔ yɛ emli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows deep inside the central leaves of maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended treatments into the leaf funnel at dusk or dawn effectively controls them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii yɛ baai amli yɛ gbɛkɛ mli loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if I leave them in the soil too long past harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: While cassava roots can store underground for a short while, prolonged rainy periods and soil pests like termites eventually attack mature roots, breaking down their tissues and causing rot.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmei shishifãi ato shikpɔŋ shishi be kukuoo moŋ, Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa shishifãi ni eda lɛ yɛ naagbee. Efiteɔ fãji ni ehaa egboɔ.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off without setting fruit during periods of extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like boron. Providing shade during hot spells and maintaining consistent watering helps the plant set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ boron. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa, ni afɔ amɛ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do new plantain plants grow if they do not produce seeds like maize or tomatoes?
ga: Te plantain hee baafee tɛŋŋ eda kɛji ewooo dumɔwui, tamɔ ŋmãa loo tomato?

english: Cultivated plantains do not produce fertile seeds; instead, they grow side shoots called suckers from their underground stems. Planting these young suckers reproduces exact copies of the mother plant.
ga: Plantain ni adu lɛ wooo dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii. Mohu ɔ, a jeɔ zugba a sisi tsohi nɛ a tsɛɛɔ ke tsohi nɛ a tsɛɛ ke tsohi a mi ɔ mi. Kɛ́ adu nɛkɛ tsei bibii nɛɛ, ebaaha tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ afee nɔ ko pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry heat period before the main rains actually settle. Seeds planted too early may sprout and then immediately dry up and die from the returning heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ be ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baa shi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: How long can a cocoa farm keep producing pods after I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ko baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii kɛji midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cocoa trees are long-term investment crops that usually start producing pods within 3 to 5 years and can continue bearing fruit for 20 to 30 years or more if properly pruned, shaded, and protected from diseases like swollen shoot.
ga: Cocoa tsei ji tso ko ni akɛwoɔ shika mli be kakadaŋŋ ni bei pii lɛ ejeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli, ni ebaanyɛ eya nɔ ewo yibii afii 20 kɛyashi 30 krokomɛi loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛji akɛ afolɔ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ, aha amɛ hulutsoo, ni atsĩ helai tamɔ tsitsii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate tender leaves and shallow roots. Without temporary shade from companion crops like plantains or cassava, direct sunlight causes them to lose moisture faster than their roots can absorb water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo be ko bɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantain loo cassava he lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over during heavy rains and winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; they rely on shallow root systems near the surface. When the heavy fruit bunch makes the plant top-heavy, wet soil combined with wind easily pulls the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Amɛdamɔɔ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ tsii lɛ, tso lɛ hu feɔ tsii. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ fata he lɛ baagbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize plants move nitrogen from their older lower leaves up to feed new growing leaves when nutrients in the ground are insufficient.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni miida lɛ niyenii be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii lɛ faaa.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every time I plant on the exact same piece of land without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu yɛ he kome ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Maize extracts high amounts of specific nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus from the dirt. Planting it continuously on the same plot exhausts those soil nutrients, resulting in weaker growth unless you rotate with legumes or add organic matter.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus, kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni baa shi. Ja okɛ legumes loo organic nibii fata he.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even though the stems and leaves look bushy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔji ni amɛji ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing tall stems and bushy leaves above ground instead of storing starch and swelling the tubers below ground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a hɛɛɔ starch ɔ mi, nɛ lɔ ɔ haa nɛ ngmami ɔmɛ fĩɔ.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the damp ground to capture maximum sunlight for leaf food production, which expands the tuber underground while reducing humidity that causes fungal diseases on leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la babaoo kɛha foliar niyenii feemɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli alɛɛ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii helai baa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards into small cup shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaves, or by intense heat stress causing the leaves to curl to conserve moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomato fruits during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High daytime heat combined with warm night temperatures dries out the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing proper fertilization and causing the plant to drop its flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Gbi mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Tsi fɔmɔ nii ni sa lɛ naa Ni enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: How does burning my field before planting affect the growth of my future crops?
ga: Te shãa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani maduɔ nii lɛ baaná wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: While burning clears brush quickly, it destroys organic leaf litter, kills helpful soil organisms like earthworms, and leaves the topsoil vulnerable to drying out and washing away under heavy rain.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shãa lɛ baaha brɔshi lɛ he atse oya moŋ. Shi efiteɔ baai ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ hu. Egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ oshara mli akɛ ebaagbi ni ebaaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight. They require temporary shade from fast-growing crops like plantains or shade trees to retain soil moisture and protect them until their canopy develops.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni abu he kɛyashi be mli ni ŋtayaa ko baaje kpo.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. This often happens when the same land is farmed repeatedly without adding compost, manure, or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ waa Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ atsu shikpɔŋ kome nɔ okwaayeli he nii shii abɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he.

english: Curled and patchy leaves are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or through using infected stem cuttings for planting.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Virus ko ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛbaa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa dumɔ nɔ

english: Why do caterpillars attack my maize crop so quickly right after the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-abele lɛ oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Warm weather and early rains cause fall armyworm eggs to hatch just as fresh, soft young maize shoots emerge, giving the caterpillars an abundant food source to multiply fast.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa asraafoi awui fɔ̃ɔ tamɔ abɛi bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni miije kpo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ náa niyenii babaoo ni amɛkɛbaafɔ oya.

english: Is burning the bush on my land before planting harmful to my soil?
ga: Ani tsei bibii ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ awui?

english: Yes, burning kills beneficial soil organisms, destroys organic matter that feeds plants, and leaves the topsoil exposed to being washed away by heavy rains.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei lɛ. kɛ gbɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I get very small cassava tubers when I plant my stems very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmeii bibii waa nɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots fight for the same limited nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in weak plants and smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering, which causes stress and prevents successful pollination.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ baa ni etsĩɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit when planted in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains require continuous water to grow and form fruit bunches. During dry periods, the plant slows down its growth process to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Nu he miihia plantains be fɛɛ be koni amɛdara ni amɛfee aduawai akui. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei haa amɛdalɛ baa shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: What causes my harvested maize grains to turn to powder after storing them in bags?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ tsɔɔ powda beni akɛwo kotoku lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Maize weevils lay eggs inside the grains, and the larvae eat the core from the inside out. Storing grain that isn't fully dried or not using airtight storage allows weevils to thrive.
ga: Abɛi ŋmeii woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Ni ŋmeii lɛ baaye ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛjɛ mli kɛya kponɔgbɛ. Dumɔwui ni egbiko kwraa loo akɛ vacuum efolɔko mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baawo ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my planted crops after I clear my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit naturally in the topsoil and are adapted to sprout rapidly as soon as sunlight and rain reach them, often outgrowing young crops that need more time to establish.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni atsake lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya kɛji hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ba pɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ daa fe tso bibioo ni biɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: When farmers keep talking about applying 'medicine' to their crops, what does that actually mean?
ga: Kɛ́ okwaafoi tee nɔ amɛwie ‘tsofa’ ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii yɛ amɛŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni no tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Medicine' is a local term farmers use for crop protection chemicals like pesticides, fungicides, and insecticides. While fertilizer acts like food to help plants grow, crop medicine acts like treatment to protect plants from pests, weeds, and diseases.
ga: Tsofa’ ji wiemɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi kɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa tsofai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi, ŋmeii kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi, eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa moŋ. Tsofai ni akɛtsaa tsei ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, jwɛi, kɛ helai ahe.

english: What is the product called 'Des Band', and how does it help my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Des Band’ ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Des Band is a crop protection chemical used by farmers to prevent and control harmful pests and diseases in fields, helping protect crops like pineapples from hidden attacks before major damage occurs.
ga: Des Band ji tsofa ko ni buɔ tsei ahe ni okwaafoi kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ oshara ni yɔɔ amɛŋmɔji amli lɛ anaa ni amɛkudɔ amɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe, tamɔ ŋmei, kɛjɛɔ tutuamɔi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ahe dani fitemɔ ni mli wa baanyɛ aba.

english: How do I know the right type of crop medicine to buy when my farm has a problem?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tso tsofa ni esa akɛ mahe beni miŋmɔ lɛ ebote haomɔ mli lɛ?

english: Different plant problems require different treatments: insecticides target insects, fungicides stop rots and mildews, and herbicides kill weeds. It is best to consult an extension officer to diagnose the exact issue before purchasing any chemical.
ga: Tsei ahe naagbai srɔtoi biɔ tsamɔi srɔtoi: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ kooloi anɔ. Fungicide haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kpaa. kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooobi mɔ ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ koni ekwɛ naagba lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani ohe tsofai komɛi.

english: Besides fertilizer, what else do I need to give my pineapples to make them grow well?
ga: Kɛfata ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ kroko ni ehe hiaa ni aha ŋmeii koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Pineapples need proper weed management, adequate water drainage, and regular protective treatments against common pests like mealybugs and fungal root diseases that fertilizer alone cannot fix.
ga: Pineapple biɔ ni akwɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ tamɔ mealybugs kɛ fungal root helai lɛ akwɛmɔ daa. ni ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ nyɛŋ atsu he nii.

english: Why are my pineapples struggling to grow even though I put enough fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ? Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli?

english: Fertilizer supplies nutrients, but if hidden diseases or pests are attacking the roots or leaves, the plant cannot absorb food properly. You may need specialized crop medicines to eliminate pests or rot hindering growth.
ga: Shi kɛji helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua shishifãi loo baai lɛ hu? Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Ekolɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ko atsu nii ni okɛjie tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsiɔ dalɛ naa lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: What special protection do pineapples need compared to faster-growing crops?
ga: Mɛɛ hebuu kroko he hiaa pineapple kɛ akɛto tsei ni daa oya lɛ ahe?

english: Because pineapples stay in the ground for a long time before harvest, they are exposed longer to soil pests and fungal rot. They require ongoing inspection and preventive chemical treatments to keep them healthy throughout their cycle.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ dani akpaa. No hewɔ lɛ, sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ yeɔ pineapple nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Ebiɔ ni akwɛ amɛnɔ be fɛɛ be, ni akɛ tsofai ni tsiɔ amɛnaa lɛ atsu nii koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛfɔmɔ be lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: How can I protect my farm against diseases if I cannot even tell when they first enter the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ helai ahe? Kɛji minyɛɛɛ makɛɛ bo be ni amɛba ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ.

english: Many crop diseases start small or live inside the soil before visible symptoms appear. Practicing preventive spraying on a proper schedule and inspecting leaf undersides and stems regularly helps stop outbreaks before they spread.
ga: Tsei ahe helai babaoo jeɔ shishi bibioo. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehiɔ shi dani ejieɔ hela lɛ he okadii lɛ akpo Nibii ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ baa shishi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni akpa helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do plant diseases seem to attack my crops suddenly without showing any early warning signs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ahe helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii trukaa ni mibɔko mi kɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Fungal spores and microscopic bacteria often infect a plant from the inside or through the roots. By the time you notice yellow leaves or rot on the outside, the disease has already been developing inside the plant for days.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal kɛ bacteria spores ni anaaa lɛ yeɔ tsei kɛjɛɔ amɛmli loo kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ona akɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ loo amɛmiifite yɛ kponɔgbɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela lɛ ebɔi tso lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ.

english: Should I wait to see signs of disease on my crops before spraying medicine, or should I spray early?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni mana hela he okadii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ dani mikɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ loo esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ mra?

english: It is usually better to apply preventive treatments early. Once a crop disease becomes visible across your field, severe damage has already occurred, making it much harder and more expensive to cure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ atsu nii mra, beni tsei ahe helai miitsɔɔ yɛ oŋmɔji amli lɛ. No mli lɛ, afite nibii babaoo momo. Enɛ haa helatsamɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa waa ni ejara hu wa.

english: Can crop diseases move from a neighbor's farm into my farm without me noticing?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ ajɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mileee?

english: Yes, many plant diseases spread invisibly through spores carried by wind, water runoff, contaminated farm tools, or insects moving from one field to another.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ahe helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ gbɛ ni anaaa nɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni kɔɔyɔɔ, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. loo kooloi bibii ni fãa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: Does the size of my farm determine how much harvest I will get?
ga: Ani bɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ da ha lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ nibii babaoo ni maná?

english: Not necessarily. A smaller, well-cared-for farm with healthy soil, proper spacing, and good weed control often yields more produce than a huge farm that is neglected or poorly managed.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Okwaafoi bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Bei pii lɛ amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo fe ŋmɔji wuji ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ nɔ loo akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Will planting my seeds very close together give me a bigger harvest from my small plot?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ?

english: No, planting too close makes plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves all the plants weak and thin, resulting in a smaller overall harvest.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fɛɛ fioo.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with beans or peanuts restores soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient away, or the soil may be exhausted from repeated planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii nɛɛ kɛya. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ kɛjɛ dumɔ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall stems but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ tso ni kɛlɛ shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen or if cassava plants are overcrowded, the plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves and branches above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ niji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato bulbs ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme stress, such as very hot days, dry soil, or nutrient shortage. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of saving energy to stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpe, tamɔ yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the leaves, or by viral diseases they spread, which prevents the plant from making food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛfee niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when heavy wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa waa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay near the surface. If you don't pile loose soil around the base of the plant, or if pests damage the underground bulb, wind can easily pull down a tree carrying a heavy bunch.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ ebɔleɛɛ tso lɛ shishi, loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala tsei ni yitsɔi wuji ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ashwie shi oya.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on sticks so their leaves can capture direct sunlight. The leaves use sunlight to manufacture food, which travels down to swell the big tuber under the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛ feɔ niyenii. ni tsi ehe kɛba shi ni eha yitso agbo lɛ shwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Do small weeds really harm my crops if my plants are already bigger than the weeds?
ga: Ani jwɛi bibii lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ kɛji akɛ mitsei lɛ dara fe jwɛi lɛ momo?

english: Yes, because weeds have aggressive roots that quietly steal water and plant food underground before your crops can reach them, even if the weeds look small on top.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dioo. Dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ Kɛji jwɛi lɛ tamɔ bibii yɛ ŋwɛi po.

english: Why should I dig up and check the deeper soil before choosing what crop to plant on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni makwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani mahala tsei ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil quality can change underneath the surface. Deep-rooted crops need good subsoil to anchor themselves and absorb nutrients, so checking lower soil layers helps you avoid planting crops that will stunt or fail once their roots grow deeper.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su baanyɛ atsake yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ shishi koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛŋɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ baaye abua bo ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni baagbɔjɔ loo amɛbaafite be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow very well on one section of my farm but stay stunted on another section of the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli shi amɛhiɛɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ fã kroko mli lɛ?

english: Soil composition and water depth change across different parts of a piece of land. One section might have rich soil that holds moisture, while another section may have shallow or sandy soil that drains away water and nutrients too fast.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii kɛ bɔ ni nu lɛ mli kwɔ ha lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hei srɔtoi, ni ekolɛ fãi komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. yɛ be mli ni ekroko hu baanyɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ loo ŋã ni nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii hoɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small and thin when I plant them in hard, compacted soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need loose, soft soil to expand properly. Hard or tightly packed soil squeezes the roots and prevents them from swelling into thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa ni ehaaa amɛfu ni amɛfee bulbs ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: How does planting my crops on sloped or hilly land affect how they grow?
ga: Te mi tsei ni miduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo gɔŋ nɔ lɛ saa amɛdalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: On sloped land, heavy rainwater quickly runs down the hill instead of sinking into the ground. This washes away topsoil and fertilizer, leaving crops at the top thirsty and short on food while crops at the bottom might get flooded.
ga: yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ Nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ oya kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baajie sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ye kumai ni amɛnáaa niyenii. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ nu mli.

english: Should I remove every single tree on my land before I plant my young plantains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu dumɔwui bibii?

english: No, keeping a few tall trees provides beneficial shade. Young crops can burn under full sun and get damaged by strong winds, so a little canopy cover keeps the ground cool and moist while roots establish.
ga: Dabi, tsei kakadaji fioo komɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Abaanyɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ afite. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ema shi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other and their roots fight over the same soil nutrients and water, reducing the tree's overall harvest.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni tso shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu kome mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ayibii fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow after I clear and burn all the vegetation on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mijie tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mishã amɛ lɛ?

english: Burning cleared bush creates a temporary ash layer, but heavy rain quickly washes it away from bare soil. This leaves the ground low in essential nutrients like nitrogen, causing maize leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashã lɛ feɔ sũ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ shwie lɛ oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does heavy rainfall wash away my crop fertilizer on a field that has just been completely cleared?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ hole miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔji amli ni ajie amɛ ehee lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Bare, cleared land lacks grass or plant cover to slow down rain. Water rushes quickly over the smooth surface, carrying away loose topsoil and fertilizer before crop roots can absorb them.
ga: He lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he, ni jwɛi loo tsei komɛi bɛ nɔ ni baaha nugbɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Nu hoɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Efoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse lɛ dani tso shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: How deep do I need to dig and loosen the soil before planting seed yams in my field?
ga: Te mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yams need loose soil at least two feet deep so the tubers can push downward easily. Hard soil beneath the surface blocks growth and results in short, bent, or stunted yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni kɛ hoo lɛ, elɛɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi enyɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ ashɛ shi oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsiɔ dalɛ naa. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii kukuji, ni ebɔle loo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do crops fail to grow in spots on my land where topsoil or sand was previously dug away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛɛɛ yɛ hei ni ajie ŋwɛi sũ loo ŋã yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Digging away topsoil removes the organic matter and rich nutrients plants need. The lower soil layer left behind is often hard, dry, and poor in nutrients, making it hard for roots to survive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni atsa lɛ jieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli wa, egbi, ni niyenii kpakpai bɛ mli. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaahi shi.

english: How does storing my harvested corn in a silo protect it better than keeping it in my house?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ baanyɛ abu ŋmãa lɛ he jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ shia mli lɛ?

english: A silo keeps out moisture, insects, and rodents that normally ruin stored grain, allowing your harvest to stay fresh for months so you can sell when market prices are better.
ga: Silo lɛ baabu he kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ, kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni baafite ŋmaa ni ato lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ehee nyɔji babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ kɛji jara nɔ jara lɛ tee hiɛ.

english: What causes my harvested grains to spoil or get moldy even after drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmaa ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛwo hulutsoo be mli po lɛ?

english: Grains mold when they still contain trapped internal moisture or pick up humidity during storage, which creates the right environment for hidden fungi to grow.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli loo amɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do weeds and wild scrub grow back so fast and choke my crops when I leave the farm for a short time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii daa oya ni amɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni mikɛ be kukuoo ko pɛ ehi shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Wild plants are very tough and compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, easily overtaking cultivated crops if the farm is left unmanaged.
ga: Koo mli tsei wa waa ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eye ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ oya kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ ŋmɔji anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do caterpillars and worms suddenly appear and eat up all my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii eba trukaa ni amɛye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Caterpillars hatch from eggs laid by moths on the leaves, and they feed continuously to grow, which can quickly strip a crop field if not caught early.
ga: Kplukai fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Ni amɛyeɔ nii be fɛɛ be koni amɛdara. Enɛ baanyɛ afite okwaayeli shikpɔji oya kɛji akɛ amɔmɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why are my maize plants growing thin and yellow when tall bush grass surrounds them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Tall weeds block sunlight from reaching your maize leaves and steal vital soil nutrients, causing the crops to starve and turn pale.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ o-corn baai lɛ ahe, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does wild bush spread so quickly into the edges of my cleared farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi miigbɛ eshwa oya kɛmiiya miŋmɔ ni ajie lɛ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Wild bushes have deep underground root networks and produce thousands of wind-blown seeds that quickly germinate and creep into open, cleared farmland.
ga: Koo mli tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni agbele naa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the correct dose of agrochemical to spray on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male agrochemicals ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ayibɔ?

english: The right chemical dose depends on following product instructions carefully using standard measuring tools, as applying too little will not control pests and applying too much can burn your crops.
ga: Tsofa lɛ falɛ ni sa lɛ damɔ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe lɛ anɔyeli jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ tsu nii lɛ, enyɛŋ eye tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ nɔ. Ni kɛ akɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii ashã.

english: What will happen to my farm if I apply too much chemical spray to kill weeds?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi anɔ lɛ tsu nii kɛgbe jwɛi?

english: Over-applying weed chemicals can remain in the ground, burn crop roots, kill beneficial soil insects, and lower your soil health for future planting seasons.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eshã tsei shishifãi, ni egbe shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. ni oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ aba shi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ bei.

english: Is it better to clear all big trees from my land before planting my crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majie tsei wuji fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Clearing trees opens up space and gives crops full sunlight, but leaving a few scattered shade trees protects the soil from heavy rain erosion and harsh sun.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ he ni tso lɛ yɔɔ lɛ naa, ni ehaa tso lɛ naa hulu la ni fa babaoo. Shi kɛ́ ashi tsei fioo komɛi pɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Will using heavy machinery to uproot trees and clear my land affect my crop yield?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni tsii ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛjie tsei ni mikɛjie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Heavy machinery clears land fast, but its weight can pack the soil tightly; breaking up the compacted soil after clearing helps crop roots grow deep for water and nutrients.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii tsuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii oya. Shi muji lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mligbalamɔ beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛhe nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct sunlight. They need partial shade from trees or food crops like plantain to protect their tender leaves and retain soil moisture while their root systems develop.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, humid, and overcrowded conditions. Pruning excess leaves and branches allows sunlight and air to dry the farm and reduce infection.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Baai kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaa helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can support. Only flowers pollinated by tiny insects like midges will form pods, and the tree naturally drops extra flowers if it lacks water or nutrients.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi ni kooloi bibii tamɔ midges lɛ pɛ feɔ pods. Ni tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli.

english: Why do cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to save water and stay alive. The roots underground remain safe and will start growing new leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaabɔi baai heei kwɛ̃mɔ kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why does cassava start to spoil so fast after I dig it out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mifo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots are cut from the stem and pulled from the soil, they react quickly with air and begin to deteriorate internally within two to three days unless processed or eaten.
ga: Beni afoɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni ajie kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ amɛnii oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bote mli, ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. ja atsu he nii loo aye

english: Why do we plant cassava using stem pieces instead of seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔkɛ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Stem cuttings grow much faster, root easily, and produce tubers that are guaranteed to have the same good qualities as the parent plant, whereas real seeds take much longer and vary in quality.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baadara oya kwraa. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ aaawo shishifãi ni afee bulbs ni yɔɔ nɔmimaa akɛ amɛhi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ heɔ be babaoo ni amɛhe yɔɔ srɔto lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce small bunches when there are many shoots around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miikwɛ̃ bibii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii babaoo ebɔle he lɛ

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for food and water. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main stem to produce larger bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha ŋmeii titri lɛ afee kuu agbo.

english: Why do plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and heavy tops, especially when carrying fruit. Supporting them with sturdy wooden props helps keep them upright during heavy winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii. titri lɛ kɛ́ amɛmiiwo yibii Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why does a plantain stem die after harvesting just one bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ gboiɔ beni akpa plantain kuu kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed to flower and fruit only once in its life. After harvest, that main stem naturally dies so that the suckers growing at its base can take over and produce the next crop.
ga: Afee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. kpamɔ sɛɛ Tso titri lɛ gboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nɔ ni amɛya nɔ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I plant cassava, plantain, and young cocoa together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei, plantain kɛ kookoo bibii ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting them together works well early on. Plantain provides early shade for cocoa, while cassava gives quick food harvests, but cassava should not be planted too close to young cocoa roots to avoid competition for nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, nanemɛi adumɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ mra. Plantains haa kookoo lɛ hulutsoo oya. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei feɔ niyenii oya Shi esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ tsɔ koni akaye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sunlight and dry Harmattan winds. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving natural shade trees protects young cocoa from severe heat and helps keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ Harmattan hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo ashi tsei lɛ koni amɛná hulutsoo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaabu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why are my healthy green cocoa pods suddenly turning black and rotting on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, dark, and humid conditions. Pruning excess cocoa branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods immediately stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ kookoo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la aba ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow starting from the tips down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves that form a V-shape from the tip usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or NPK at the right time restores healthy green leaves and improves crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyitsei tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be naa lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ ayibii aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Rotating them with heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni akɛ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: What causes these large holes in my maize leaves with sawdust-like waste inside the central stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant during the day to feed on young leaves, but targeted bio-pesticides or neem extract can control them early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai amli yɛ gbi mli koni amɛye baai bibii. Shi tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ amɛ mra.

english: Does it matter which direction I insert my cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes shoots to grow downward first, delaying sprouting and reducing tuber growth.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ sɛɛ ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow thin, crooked, and small instead of long and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ amli tsei, amɛhe ejɔ, ni amɛji bibii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become thin and bent when the soil is hard and compact or full of stones. Preparing soft, deep mounds or ridges allows the roots to swell easily into large, straight tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle ehe loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni asaa lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baafu ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks by tiny insects like thrips. Ensuring steady watering and light shade during heatwaves keeps the blossoms intact.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa amɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why should I remove extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Keeping only three shoots—a mother, a daughter, and a granddaughter—gives larger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ ahiɛ ŋmeii etɛ pɛ - nyɛ, biyoo kɛ nabi yoo - lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni da, ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ aba.

english: How does spreading dry grass or maize stalks around the base of my crops help them grow?
ga: He loo ŋmãa tsei ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material (mulching) keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the sun, stops weeds from growing, and adds nutrients as it breaks down.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa he yɛ be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ

english: Why should I cut off some of the leaves and branches from my crops while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai kɛ niji komɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni amɛmiida lɛ?

english: Trimming extra or dead branches helps the plant direct its food and water straight to making strong, healthy fruits instead of wasting energy on unwanted leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekwɛɔ niyenii kɛ nu nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ewo yibii ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni ataooo lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Should I trim all the unwanted branches off my crop at once, or should I do it little by little?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni misumɔɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli shikome loo mafee fiofio?

english: It is best to prune little by little over time. Removing too many branches at once shocks the crop, which can slow down its growth or make it weak.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa tso lɛ fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ ajie tsei niji babaoo shikome lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe afee shoo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo loo egbɔjɔ.

english: How do I know which branches on my crop I am supposed to cut off?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei niji ni esa akɛ mafolɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: You should remove weak branches, yellowing or dry leaves, branches touching the ground, and small extra shoots growing in the joints between main stems.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie niji ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni egbi Niji ni taa shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii bibii krɛdɛɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: What are these small extra shoots growing out of the sides of my plant stems?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei bibii lɛ? Ani eda kɛjɛ mitsɔne lɛ masɛi?

english: Those extra stems are called side shoots or suckers. They steal nutrients from the main plant, so removing them helps your main crop grow bigger and yield better.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ akɛ side shoots loo shoots. Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei titrii lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Is it bad if my crops are growing very tall and bushy without producing any fruit?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni yibii ko bɛ he?

english: Yes, when a crop becomes too bushy, it is using all its food just to grow leaves. Trimming the top and side shoots forces the plant to stop expanding leaves and start producing flowers and fruit.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bafee ŋmɔshi nibii tsɔ. Ekɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ baai. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋwɛi kɛ esɛɛgbɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akpa baai lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai feemɔ.

english: Do I need special tools to remove young side shoots from my plants?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni maná nibii krɛdɛɛi ni mikɛjie tsei amli ŋmeii bibii?

english: No, when side shoots are very young and soft, you can easily pinch them off with your thumb and fingers without damaging the main stem.
ga: Dabi, beni afã tsei lɛ ji gbekɛbii bibii lolo ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ oshishifa kɛ oniji amɔ mli oya. ni efiteee tso titri lɛ

english: How does cutting off crowded branches stop pests from attacking my farm?
ga: Te aniji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting crowded branches lets sunlight and fresh air flow through the plant. Most crop pests prefer dark, damp, crowded places, so keeping the plant open naturally drives them away.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afolɔ mli waa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Nibii ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo sumɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni mli efɔ, ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ, no hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ ni oooha amɛgbele lɛ baashwie amɛ.

english: Why do my crops get sick more easily when the leaves are too tightly packed together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela mɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya kɛ́ baai lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: When leaves are tightly packed, moisture gets trapped inside after rain. This wet environment helps diseases and mold grow quickly and spread across the crop.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Moisture ŋmɛɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa helai kɛ ŋmeii daa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers advise farmers to plant seeds in plastic bags before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ okwaafoi ŋaa koni amɛdu dumɔwui yɛ plastic kotokui amli dani amɛdu amɛwo ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ?

english: Planting in seedling bags protects tender roots from insects and harsh soil conditions early on, making it easier to nurture the crop until it is strong enough for the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔwui kotokui amli lɛ buɔ shishifãi bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi ni mli wa lɛ ahe mra. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛyashi be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔji ni mli tse.

english: Why do some farmers put bags around growing fruits on their trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ baagi woɔ amɛhe lɛ? Yibii ni aduɔ yɛ tsei anɔ?

english: Covering growing fruits with bags creates a physical barrier that keeps insects, birds, and harsh weather from damaging the fruit before harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ kotoku ha aduawai ni miida lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni tsiɔ kooloi bibii, okpoi, kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite aduawai lɛ dani akpa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly with broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes and dark dirt inside the growing center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni mli edɔ kɛ muji ni mli edɔ yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the central leaf tube of the maize plant and eats the young leaves. Treating the center of the crop early stops them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ abɛi bibii lɛ. Ni oookwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose all their leaves during the dry season, and is my crop dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ? Ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miigboi?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves on purpose when water is scarce to save moisture in their stems and underground roots. The plant is not dead; once the rains start again, it will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ baatsɔ yiŋtoo nɔ amɛshwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi tso lɛ shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ bɛ. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ Baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaaya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize crop turn pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build green leaves and grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly at the bottom stem of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is full of concentrated salts that can burn and destroy the plant's delicate roots if applied too close. Placing it in a small ring a few inches away from the stem allows roots to safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ he tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛwo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko mli lɛ, inchi fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ he lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the ground, while crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, helping restore land fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I process my harvested cassava into starch for products other than food?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ŋmei ni akpa lɛ mafee ashikishaŋ kɛha nibii krokomɛi ni jeee niyenii?

english: Yes, cassava roots contain high amounts of natural starch that can be extracted, dried, and refined into industrial raw materials for making clothes starch, paper adhesives, bio-polishes, and packaging material.
ga: Hɛɛ, adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii babaoo yɛ ŋmeii shishifãi amli. Abaanyɛ ajie, agbi ni atsake mli afee nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhei ni akɛfeɔ atadei amli ŋmɔtɔ, wolo nɔ glu, bio-polish kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize grain grow white mold when stored in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ kɛ́ akɛto kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Mold grows when grains are bagged while they still hold hidden moisture from the field. Sun-drying the maize until the kernels are completely hard before bagging prevents fungal growth and keeps grain safe.
ga: Fuji lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmaa wo kotoku mli yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ mli lolo. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa kwraa dani awo kotoku mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do hybrid seeds bought from agricultural shops yield more than seeds I save from my previous farm harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni aheɔ yɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred by crop scientists to combine strong traits like high yield, uniform growth, and pest resistance. Saved seeds gradually lose these combined strengths over generations.
ga: Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ahe nilelɔi fɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkɛ sui ni mli wa tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo, dalɛ ni tamɔ ekome, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ afata he Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ baaje mli fiofio. Nɛkɛ hewalɛi ni akɛfee ekome nɛɛ laajeɔ yɛ wala be fɛɛ mli.

english: How do sealed hermetic bags keep insects out of my stored beans without using liquid chemicals?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni kotoku ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ aha ŋmeii akabote kɔfi ŋmeii ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ amli ni mikɛ tsofai ni ji nu tsuuu nii?

english: Hermetic bags cut off all outside air so insects and their eggs inside the bag quickly run out of oxygen and die, preserving your dried crop without leaving chemical residue on your food.
ga: Vacuum kotokui lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ amɛwuji ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ baaná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa oya ni amɛbaagboi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ onibii ni egbi lɛ anɔ ni eshiuuu tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ oniyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear all the weeds and bushes before I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with young maize plants for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing the land completely before planting ensures your crop gets a strong start without being choked by wild growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie he ni odu lɛ dani odu lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni adebɔɔ mli dalɛ tsiii enaa.

english: Is it beneficial for me to plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize matures fast and is harvested within three to four months, leaving the cassava room to expand and mature over the rest of the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Shi gbɛ oha ŋmei lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I estimate how many bags of maize I will harvest from my one-acre farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa enyiɛ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji acre 1 mli lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: Your yield depends on seed quality, rain, and soil care. On average, using improved seed varieties and proper fertilizer on one well-managed acre can give you between 10 to 15 100kg bags of maize.
ga: O yibiiwoo lɛ damɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ. Kɛ aja mli lɛ, Dumɔwui ni asaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha oná ŋmãa kotoku ni tsiimɔ ji kilogram 10 kɛyashi 15 loo 100.

english: Why do my crop yields keep reducing every year even though I farm the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil every season. Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts the soil; practicing crop rotation with beans or adding manure helps restore soil fertility and yield.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ lɛ baaha sũ lɛ mli agbɔjɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ kɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How exactly does the government fertilizer help my crops grow better?
ga: Te maŋ nɔyeli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer provides essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that might be lacking in your soil. It acts like nutritious food, helping crops build strong roots, green leaves, and bigger fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium ni ekolɛ ebɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni shishifãi ni wa, baai eŋɔli, kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I replant seeds saved from my harvested hybrid maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields only in their first planting. If you save and plant seeds from that harvest, the second-generation crops will grow unevenly and yield much less.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji obua dumɔwui anaa ni odu kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee ekome ni amɛwooo yibii fioo kwraa.

english: As a female farmer with limited heavy labor support, which crops are easier for me to manage and yield well?
ga: Ákɛ okwaafonyo yoo ni enine shɛ yelikɛbuamɔ fioo nɔ kɛ nitsumɔ ni tsii Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha mi akɛ makwɛ nɔ ni mawo yibii kpakpai?

english: Vegetables like pepper and garden eggs, or legumes like cowpeas, require less heavy land clearing and mound-making compared to yam or cassava, making them easier to manage with light labor.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ mli Loo ŋmeii, tamɔ tsina ŋmeii, biɔ ni ajie amɛhe fioo kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii kɛ akɛto ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ahe. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ akɛ nitsumɔ ni waaa baatsu he nii.

english: What causes my tomato plants to grow lots of tall leaves but produce very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-tomato tsei lɛ baa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ waa shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus entirely on producing green leaves instead of flowers. Trimming extra leafy shoots and using balanced fertilizer encourages the plant to produce more tomatoes.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai eŋɔli ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo tomato babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crops turning yellow and wilting early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor drainage causing root rot. Adding a small amount of starter fertilizer or clearing blocked water paths usually restores green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko fata he loo ajie nu gbɛi ni atsĩ naa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking the sap from young leaves. Spraying early with neem oil extract or approved crop protection chemicals prevents damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ mra loo tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite.

english: Why should I plant big forest trees like Mahogany on my cocoa farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu koo mli tso agbo ko tamɔ mahogany yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni mafo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Big trees like Mahogany provide filtered shade that protects young cocoa from harsh sunlight, preserves soil moisture during dry periods, and helps your cocoa trees live and produce for many more years.
ga: Tsei ni eda tamɔ mahogany haa hulutsoo ni mli tse koni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni eye ebua ni o-cacao tsei lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii afii babaoo.

english: Why do some wild bushes near my farm make my crops get sick more easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela waa lɛ?

english: Certain wild bushes act as hidden host plants where disease-carrying insects live and multiply before flying over to infect your farm crops.
ga: Koo mli tsei komɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ. Kplukai ni kɛ helai baa lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛfɔɔ bii dani amɛfoɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Can I plant native trees like Funtumia alongside my crops without reducing my crop yields?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu maŋ tsei tamɔ Funtumia yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi?

english: Yes, if you plant native trees with proper spacing, they will protect your crops from strong winds and improve soil quality without stealing light or nutrients from your main crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ odu maŋ tsei ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli. Tsei nɛɛ baabu onibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ojuuu la loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei titrii lɛ amli.

english: How does heavy, standing water around my cocoa roots affect how the trees grow?
ga: Nu ni mli wa ni yɔɔ dioo ni ebɔle he fɛɛ. Te mi-kookoo shishifãi lɛ saa mitso lɛ dalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Standing water suffocates crop roots by blocking air, which causes root rot, stops the tree from absorbing nutrients, and weakens it against diseases.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni etsĩɔ naa lɛ nɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa helai srɔtoi baa amɛnɔ oya.

english: How do small insects spread diseases from one cocoa tree to another?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii gbɛɔ helai kɛjɛɔ cacao tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ?

english: Insects act as vectors by feeding on diseased plants, picking up the virus or fungus, and then injecting it into healthy trees when they move to feed on them.
ga: Kplukai tsuɔ nii akɛ mɛi ni kɛ hela baa kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛyeɔ lɛ nɔ. Na virus loo fungus No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛji amɛtsi amɛhe koni amɛye amɛ.

english: What is the best way to arrange shade trees on my farm so my cocoa still gets enough sunlight?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atoɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ koni kookoo lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Plant shade trees around the borders or in wide, even rows so they create a light canopy that filters the sun without completely blocking the light cocoa needs to make pods.
ga: Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa loo yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni mli kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ anɔ koni ofee ŋshɔkpɔi ni haa hulu la lɛ tsɔɔ mli ni etsĩii kookoo la ni he hiaa koni akɛfee ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ anaa kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves and dry up faster during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds pull moisture out of cocoa leaves faster than roots can draw water from dry soil, forcing the tree to shed leaves to conserve water and stay alive.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei ashwie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.
