english: Why is clearing weeds around the base of my trees important for stopping crop diseases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ he hiaa koni akɛtsi ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai anaa lɛ?

english: Excess weeds hold trapped moisture and create a dark, damp environment where disease-causing fungi and harmful insects thrive close to your crop roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɛɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shihilɛ feɔ duŋ, ni mli ejɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii ni kɛ hela baa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ yɛ otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How does mixing large timber trees with my crops keep my farm soil fertile for a long time?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei wuji ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafata he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Deep-rooted forest trees pull nutrients up from deep underground and drop leaves that rot on the ground, creating rich natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni amɛshiɔ baai ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛha onibii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot during times of heavy rain and high humidity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and trapped humidity allow fungal spores to grow and spread rapidly across cocoa pods, causing diseases like Black Pod.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli fɛɛ. Ekɛ helai srɔtoi tamɔ ŋmeii diji baa

english: Why do my maize crops grow much taller and stronger when I plow the land with a tractor before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ daa ni ehiɛɔ shi babaoo ni ehiɛ wa waa kɛ́ mikɛ mi-trakta lɛ tsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii dani midu lɛ?

english: Plowing loosens hard soil, allowing young crop roots to spread easily, breathe, and soak up water and nutrients deep in the ground, which helps plants grow strong and tall.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya, amɛmuɔ, ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛkwɔɔ.

english: How soon after plowing my farm with a tractor should I start planting my seeds?
ga: Beni mikɛ trakta tsu ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ Mɛɛ tɛŋŋ esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: It is best to plant right after plowing while the turned soil is still loose and moist, allowing seeds to quickly sprout before the topsoil hardens from the sun or gets overrun by weeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni atsake lɛ mli etse ni edɔ lolo lɛ. Enɛ ji koni eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya dani shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli wa kɛjɛ hulu lɛ mli loo jwɛi eyi nɔ.

english: How does deep plowing help protect my crops when heavy rains fall?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Deeply plowed soil acts like a sponge, allowing heavy rainwater to sink down to the roots underground instead of running over the surface and washing away topsoil and young plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Ha nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, e hoɔ kɛ tsɔɔ zugba a nɔ nɛ e shwieɔ zugba nɛ ngɛ nɔ ɔ kɛ tsehi bibihi a nɔ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to sprout if I plant them too deep into freshly plowed soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsu he nii ehee lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds contain limited energy; if planted too deep in loose soil, the young shoot exhausts all its strength trying to push up through the dirt and dies before reaching sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ hewalɛ babaoo. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji nɔ tsɔ lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni amɛbaagboi dani hulu la lɛ baashɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Why do crop roots struggle to grow in areas where heavy farm tractors drive frequently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔ mli traktɔi ni tsii fɔɔ tsɔne kudɔmɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy machinery crushes and packs the soil tightly together, creating a hard underground layer that acts like concrete, stopping root stems from growing deep to reach water.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ tsũ ko ni wa ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ kɔnkrit baa. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: How does planting my crops in straight rows after land preparation help them grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja beni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Straight rows give every plant its own clear space, sunshine, and air, preventing crops from crowding each other and fighting over nutrients in the soil.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni ja haa tso fɛɛ tso naa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ, hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkabua amɛhe naa ni amɛkaye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why do weeds seem to sprout faster than my crops right after land preparation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni misaa shikpɔŋ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Turning the soil with a tractor brings old buried weed seeds up to the surface where they get sunlight and air, causing them to germinate quickly alongside your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ trakta tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, jwɛi dumɔwui ni egbɔ ni afu lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are some crops growing faster on one side of my field than the other after plowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome fe fã kroko lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil depth and moisture differ across a field; crops grow faster in spots where the plow dug deeper and created softer soil that holds onto water longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ emli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Tsei daa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni hiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why should I leave old plant leaves on the field after clearing instead of burning them before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei ahe baai momoi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã dani odu?

english: Leaving old crop material to decay feeds the soil organic food and creates a cover that keeps the ground cool and moist, helping new crops survive dry weather.
ga: Nibii ni etsɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ koni amɛgboi lɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii. ni ofee nɔ ko ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why do crops planted at the very start of the rainy season perform better than those planted later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ hi fe nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Early crops take advantage of a natural rise in soil nutrients brought by the first rains, giving roots time to establish strongly before mid-season dry spells or heavy downpours hit.
ga: Tsei ni shwereɔ mra lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yaa hiɛ ni amɛnáa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa enáa be ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi ni wa dani be lɛ teŋgbɛ hɔmɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow before the crop is even ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ po efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen nutrients or are sitting in waterlogged soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving field drainage helps keep the leaves green and growing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii loo amɛta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni oooha ehi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni edaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall but produce very few seeds or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa shi amɛwoɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops often grow tall with few fruits when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer or too little sunlight, causing the plant to put all its energy into growing leaves instead of producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo hulu la fioo ko pɛ. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: What causes my tomato plants to drop their flowers before forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifo amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛwo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks key nutrients like calcium during flower development.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ akwɛmɔ be mli.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily whenever there is a strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their root systems are shallow, which happens if seeds are planted too close to the surface, if the land was not tilled deeply, or if the soil lacks potassium.
ga: Abɛi baagbee baai lɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ. aloo enyɛɛɛ etsu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium

english: How do I know the exact time my cassava is ready to dig up so I don't harvest too early?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ atsa ŋmei? No hewɔ lɛ wɔkpaaa nii mra tsɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack as the tubers swell underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy conditions when shade is too thick and air cannot flow freely through your farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli oya lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my yam plants curling up and showing dark spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling and dark spots on yam leaves are typically caused by leaf spot diseases or small insects like aphids that feed on the plant's sap and weaken it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato baa lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa ji leaf spot hela loo kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛhaa egbɔjɔɔ lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help both crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cowpea ni mikɛ mi-corn lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil through their roots, which acts as a natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa

english: What makes plantain suckers take so long to produce fruit after planting?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers grow slowly if planted in nutrient-poor soil without organic manure, or if weeds are allowed to steal water and nutrients from their roots during early growth.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ jwɛi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wither even when I water them during the middle of a hot sunny day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Watering under full hot sun causes fast evaporation and can heat up the soil around roots, stressing the plant. It is best to water early in the morning or late afternoon near the soil level.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa hulutsoo baa oya, ni ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli adɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ naa haomɔ. Esa akɛ awo nu lɛ mli leebi loo shwane mli, yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. As the maize grows, it pulls whatever nitrogen is left from its bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, causing the bottom ones to starve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Beni ŋmãa lɛ da Ejieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ. Enɛ haa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: How do cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have microscopic organisms living on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nibii bibii ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over time and allows pests and diseases that feed specifically on that crop to build up in the earth.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaya nɔ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture the energy needed to grow big tubers underground. Staking raises the vines into the light and keeps the leaves off damp ground where fungal diseases thrive.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha wain tso lɛ aná la ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekashwɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ shwereɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and tender roots that lose water faster than they can absorb it under direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains to protect them while their root systems mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my tomato roots with dry grass help them during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tomato shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the earth, keeps the roots cool, and retains soil moisture so the plants survive heat spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ahe jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ mli

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves to suck sap, or by viruses spread by these insects that disrupt normal plant leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Enɛ tsiɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the plant experiences stress, such as sudden hot spells, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen, which causes the plant to protect itself by aborting fruit production.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe, tamɔ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa fe nine. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ buɔ ehe he kɛtsɔ aduawai ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature and ready to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava shows signs of maturity when the lower leaves yellow and shed naturally, and the swelling tubers beneath cause cracks to form in the soil near the base of the main stem.
ga: Cassava jieɔ dalɛ he okadii akpo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ fee ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmeii ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ haa sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli fãa.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the ground if I plant them right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry period that leaves soil hot and dry. If a seed absorbs just enough water to swell but not enough to fully establish roots, it stops growing and rots in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ. Kɛji dumɔwu lɛ ŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfutu shi eshɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee shishifãi kwraa lɛ, Dumɔwu lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Is it normal for my cassava plants to lose their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa baaje mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Yes, cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry spells as a survival trick to save water. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing its tubers underground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛbu nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning light green and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for green growth. Applying fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure helps the plant regain its deep green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii waa ni ehaa ehe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruits when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing their pollen to dry up so flowers cannot set fruit. Giving the plants enough water and shade during peak afternoon heat helps them hold onto their blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa pollen ni egbi lɛ baa. No hewɔ lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii. Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How does using a tractor to plow my field help my crops grow better than using a hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ trakta ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe tsɔne ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: A tractor plows deeper into the ground, breaking up hard soil so that roots can spread quickly and reach deeper water and nutrients that hand hoes cannot easily uncover.
ga: Trakta lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Efoɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛyashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni nine ŋmei nyɛŋ ana mlɛo lɛ he.

english: Will spraying pesticide on my crops in the middle of a hot afternoon harm the plants?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ baaye tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, spraying during hot sunshine can burn the leaves because liquid droplets act like magnifying glasses, and heat makes the chemicals evaporate before they can work properly. It is best to spray early morning or late evening.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã baai lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu mli nu ni hoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. Ni dɔlɛ lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛnyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: What alternative crop can I plant after harvesting my maize to keep my soil rich?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts after maize restores nitrogen back into the soil naturally, making the land fertile for your next major crop.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Feemɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛha onibii wuji ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I plant pepper between my young oil palm trees while waiting for them to grow tall?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mu tsei ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping peppers or vegetables between young palm trees works well because the young trees do not shade the ground yet, giving you quick food and income while the main crop matures.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii loo aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii tsei ateŋ lɛ hu tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsei bibii lɛ eshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lolo. Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ niyenii kɛ shika nɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to yield bigger tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ekwɛ bulbs wuji lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground with stakes keeps leaves healthy and directs energy into growing large tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo he koni eha tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ ahe hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa bulb agboi ni miida lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cocoa pods are mature enough for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color from deep green or reddish-purple to a bright yellow or orange. Harvesting them at this stage ensures the beans inside are fully formed and rich in cocoa flavor.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo magenta kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ kookoo ni ŋɔɔ waa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants keep growing lots of vines and leaves but very few pods when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ wain tsei kɛ baai babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi pods fioo pɛ yɔɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa.

english: Too much water and excess nitrogen push the plant to produce extra stems and leaves instead of flowers. Once the heavy rains ease, the plant will shift its energy back into flowering and pod production.
ga: Nu babaoo kɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii kɛ baai babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ba shi lɛ Tso lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛyaa fɔfɔi kɛ pod feemɔ mli.

english: Why do my groundnut plants flower above the ground, but the nuts form under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ miikwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnut plants flower above the ground, but once the flowers are fertilized, they grow long stems called pegs that bend down and push themselves into the soil. The actual nut then grows underground inside a pod to protect itself from the sun and pests.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ, tsei kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my groundnut leaves turning yellow as the season comes to an end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is reaching full maturity and is transferring its energy into developing the nuts underground. When most leaves turn yellow and start falling, it is usually a signal that harvest time is near.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ewo fɔfɔi. ni ekɛ hewalɛ miitsu nii koni ekɛwo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Beni baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi Bei pii lɛ eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ.

english: How can I tell if my groundnuts are ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ makpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can check maturity by pulling up two or three plants across your field and opening the pods. If the inside lining of the shell is dark brown or black and the seeds fill the pod tightly, your crop is mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji eyɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni ooogbala kɛho ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ogbele ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mligbɛ fã lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ ebɔle amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edara ni esa kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do the stems snap and leave my groundnuts buried in the soil when I pull the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso lɛ tso lɛ fãa ni eshiɔ mi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛ́ migbala tso lɛ?

english: When groundnuts stay in the soil past their maturity date, the pegs holding the pods to the plant begin to dry out and weaken. When you pull the plant, these weak pegs break easily, leaving the pods trapped underground.
ga: Beni ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni amɛhoɔ be ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ lɛ he. Pin ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ he lɛ baabɔi gbimɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Kɛji ogbala tso lɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ baafo oya. ni haa pod lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why is it harder to pull my groundnuts out of the ground when the weather is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa waa akɛ abaajie ŋmeii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Dry soil bakes hard and tightly grips the nuts growing underground. When you yank the plant in dry soil, the stem breaks off at the surface, forcing you to dig out the buried groundnuts one by one with a hoe.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ shãa waa ni ehiɛɔ ŋmeii ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji ogbala tso ko kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Eshishifã lɛ baafo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ biɔ ni okɛ shɔvel atsa ŋmeii ni afu lɛ ekomekomei.

english: Is it better to harvest groundnuts right after a rain or when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaakpa ŋmei amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: It is best to harvest groundnuts a day or two after a light rain when the soil is soft and moist. Moist soil lets go of the pods easily, allowing you to lift the whole plant with all the nuts attached.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa ŋmei gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ, be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ baajɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli oya. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ owóɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni akɛkpɛtɛ he lɛ.

english: What kind of soil makes it easiest to harvest groundnuts without losing them underground?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ haa efeɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ akɛ abaakpa ŋmeii ni amɛlaajeee yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Loose, sandy-loam soils are best for groundnuts because they allow the stems to easily push into the dirt while growing, and they loosen up quickly at harvest so the pods pull out cleanly without snapping.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmei ejaakɛ ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya kɛ́ adu. ni ebaatse oya kɛji akpa No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ ajie pod lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni efoŋ.

english: Should I use a hoe to dig up my groundnut plants, or should I pull them with my hands?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei atsa ŋmei tsei lɛ loo mikɛ minine agbala amɛ?

english: It is best to use a hoe or garden fork to gently lift and loosen the soil around the roots first, then gently pull the plant. This prevents the stems from tearing and keeps the groundnuts attached to the main plant.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okɛ ŋmei loo abɔɔ mli ŋmei atsu nii blɛoo. Wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ ni okɛgbala mli klɛŋklɛŋ, no sɛɛ lɛ, gbalamɔ tso lɛ blɛoo koni akagbala shishifã lɛ ni okɛ ŋmei lɛ akpɛtɛ tso titri lɛ he.

english: What happens to groundnuts if I leave them buried in the ground for too long after they mature?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmeii anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ?

english: Leaving mature groundnuts buried in damp soil causes the seeds to rot, sprout early, or develop dangerous moulds like aflatoxin, which spoil the taste and lower the selling price at the market.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni edara ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo, amɛbaakwɛ̃ oya, loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aflatoxins yɛ mli, ni no baafite amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ ni ebaaha amɛ jara aba shi yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Do some groundnut varieties hold onto their pods better during harvest than others?
ga: Ani ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi hiɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ be mli fe ekrokomɛi?

english: Yes, bunch-type groundnuts grow in compact clumps and generally hold their pods more tightly to the main root, making them easier to pull out intact compared to spreading varieties that stretch far across the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii akui daa yɛ kui bibii amli ni bei pii lɛ amɛmɔɔ pod lɛ mli shiŋŋ kɛyaa shishifã lɛ he. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie lɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he kɛ akɛto srɔtoi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist until it grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip and moving down the center mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives plants their deep green color and energy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa tsei lɛ su eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni ehaa amɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce less food if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in that specific dirt.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ muji lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain sits in the ground without proper drainage, it drowns the roots and creates wet conditions where rotting fungi multiply.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha shihilɛ ko ni mli ewo fɔ aba he ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ babaoo yɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my pepper crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil, which is called mulching, keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly during dry hot weather, and stops heavy rain from washing away rich topsoil.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Will planting my maize seeds very close together give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba?

english: No, planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, weak stalks that produce tiny cobs or no grains at all.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo dumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to light to create energy for tuber growth. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun, preventing disease and helping the yam produce large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ taoɔ kane tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha tuber dalɛ. Staking kɛ baai lɛ baa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potatoes ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms. The moths prefer laying eggs inside the central leaf funnel of young maize because it offers shelter, and dry weather speeds up the hatching of their hungry caterpillars.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworms ji enɛɛmɛi. Kplukai lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ ejaakɛ eji he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Ni shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ fɔɔ oya.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures become excessively hot or when the soil gets too dry, causing the plant to shed its flowers to save water and stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.

english: How do weeds growing near my crops actually damage my harvest?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil food directly from your crops, while also providing a breeding ground for insect pests that spread diseases to your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛji hei ni kooloi ni baanyɛ agbɛ hela amɛshwã otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or excess water around the roots. Applying the right fertilizer like NPK or Urea when the soil is moist helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK loo urea wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my farm right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, applying fertilizer right before heavy rain will wash the nutrients away before the plant roots can absorb them. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after rain, rather than right before a rainstorm.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaatsɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooowo dani nugbɔ anɛ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and retain soil moisture, protecting the cocoa plants during their early stages.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Does it matter which direction I push my cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Ani he ni aduɔ ŋmei lɛ yɛ lɛ he miihia?

english: Yes, the small buds or nodes on the cassava stem must point upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the stems struggle to sprout properly, resulting in poor growth and low yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo nodes. Esa akɛ ŋmei lɛ tso lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Ebaawa akɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ̃. Enɛ haaa ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ni yibiiwoo hu faaa.

english: Tomato flowers usually fall off due to high heat, irregular watering, or sap-sucking insects. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting the crops from extreme heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ yɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ feɔ ekome ni abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai shwereɔ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden poles next to my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine, and lifting its leaves toward the sun using wooden stakes allows the plant to catch maximum sunlight, which fuels the growth of larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ tso ko tsu nii kɛwo baai lɛ anɔ kɛtee hulu lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni ji tsofa ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ daa lɛ

english: Why should I cut off some healthy-looking branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess foliage to let air and sunlight penetrate the tree canopy. This keeps the environment dry enough to prevent black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ jieɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni ekɛtsi black pod hela naa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo pods babaoo.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes inside the hearts of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid on the leaves and crawl into the center funnel of the plant to feed. Catching them early and applying recommended pest control clears them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli koni amɛyatao niyenii. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ atsu nii lɛ baajie amɛ kɛjɛ mli dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop harvest even if I give my crops enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds steal essential plant food, root space, and sunlight away from your crops. Even with enough water, weeds will outcompete your crops for soil nutrients if they are not cleared regularly.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tso niyenii ni he hia, shishifãi gbɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po lɛ Jwɛi hu haa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛhaa otsei lɛ kɛji ajieee amɛ daa.

english: How can I store my harvested maize seeds so insects do not destroy them before next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni kooloi akafite amɛ dani be ni baa lɛ aba?

english: Grains must be dried until completely hard and stored in airtight sacks or sealed containers. Adding approved grain preservation dust prevents moisture buildup and keeps destructive insects like weevils out.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi ŋmaa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa, ni akɛto kotokui loo tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ahe sũ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛbaafata he lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa ni ehaa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: How many years will it take after planting for my new cocoa farm to start producing pods?
ga: Beni midu mi-cocoa tso hee lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani ebɔi ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana usually begin fruiting within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years to start producing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Can I plant cassava alongside my young cocoa seedlings when starting a new farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛ́ mije ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: It is better to avoid planting cassava close to young cocoa because cassava is a heavy feeder that aggressively steals soil nutrients, water, and sunlight from the delicate cocoa seedlings.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo bibii lɛ he. Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmei ji niyenii ni tsii ni kɛ yiwalɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if the land I acquired in Ghana has good soil for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni miheɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni abaanyɛ adu kookoo yɛ nɔ?

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, dark, well-drained loamy soil that retains moisture during dry spells but does not become waterlogged or flooded when heavy rains fall.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli Shi nu shwieŋ nɔ loo nu shwieŋ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants drooping and turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that easily lose water under intense heat and dry Harmattan winds, causing them to wilt and turn yellow due to moisture stress.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ Harmattan latsaa ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shishi, ni no haa amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do mature cocoa trees shed a lot of their leaves at specific times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni eda lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop leaves during dry seasons as a survival mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation and conserve energy until rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛba nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ, ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds grow so rapidly immediately after I clear my land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni ajie he ni adu nii yɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing land exposes weed seeds dormant in the topsoil to direct sunlight and rain, triggering fast germination and aggressive growth because there is no canopy to block the light.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie he lɛ, ebaajie jwɛi dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ kpo. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, hulu la kɛ nugbɔ baa enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why is it important to leave tall economic trees on my cocoa farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi shika helɛtemɔ tsei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafolɔ tsei lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Tall shade trees protect cocoa from harsh sunlight, break strong damaging winds, maintain soil moisture, and drop leaves that rot to form natural fertilizer for the cocoa plants.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ekpãtãa kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii waa lɛ hiɛ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oshɛrɛ baai ni egboi lɛ oshwie koni okɛfee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha cacao tso lɛ.

english: What causes small cocoa pods to shrivel up, turn black, and die before they grow full size?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ diŋ, ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshɛɔ amɛdalɛ he?

english: This can be caused by cherelle wilt, a natural process where the tree thins out excess pods it cannot feed, or by fungal diseases like black pod disease triggered by high humidity and poor ventilation.
ga: Cherel tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ baanyɛ aha enɛ aba. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ejieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye lɛ. aloo kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela ni hulutsoo babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli.

english: Why are flowers falling off my cocoa trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers require tiny insects called midges for pollination; if the weather is extremely dry or if excessive chemical spraying kills these midges, the unpollinated flowers drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ nakai midge kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ fe nine lɛ gbeɔ mɛi nɛɛ. Fɔfɔi ni pollin bɛ mli lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Why do some ripe cocoa pods turn bright yellow while others turn orange or reddish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii komɛi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ? yɛ be mli ni pods komɛi feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo red.

english: Pod color depends on the cocoa variety; traditional Amelonado pods turn bright yellow when ripe, while Amazonia or hybrid types often start dark red or purple and turn orange-yellow when ready for harvest.
ga: Pod su lɛ damɔ kookoo henɔ lɛ nɔ. Kusum mli amelonado ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji ekwɛ̃. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ amelonias loo hybrids lɛ jeɔ shishi akɛ tsuru loo purple ni mli edɔ. ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ kɛji esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains grown alongside them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi cacao tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell before the real rainy season starts. If you plant too early, the soil can quickly dry up, causing seeds to wither before their roots can reach deeper water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my yam crop produce bigger tubers when I build high soil mounds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii wuji beni mitswa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ mibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Mounding creates loose, soft soil that gives yam roots room to expand freely without fighting hard earth, allowing the tubers to grow larger, smoother, and healthier.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaabɔ he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni ehaa sweet potato shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ akpee. Eyeɔ ebuaa yitso lɛ ni efeɔ agbo. ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kpakpa

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants start turning light yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyaa shishi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts. Applying fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore green growth and supports good cob development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji ŋmãa ni ataoɔ babaoo lɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ shweremɔ kpakpa.

english: Why does my cassava yield smaller roots when I plant it on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi bibii baa kɛji midu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting cassava repeatedly in the same spot drains essential nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating crops or leaving the land to rest helps restore fertility for better yields.
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ewoɔ nii ekoŋŋ koni ená yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do black spots quickly cover my cocoa pods whenever heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ haa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe oya lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates high humidity, which helps the Black Pod fungal disease spread rapidly. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm to dry pods faster and slow down the disease.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa, ni no yeɔ ebuaa black pod fungal hela lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi oya ni ehaa helai sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes curl their leaves inward to protect themselves from intense heat and slow down water loss through evaporation. Giving them adequate water helps reduce this stress.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi blɛoo kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds end up with tiny holes in them after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Storage weevils lay microscopic eggs on the pods in the field. Once the seeds are stored, the eggs hatch into larvae that eat their way out, leaving holes. Sealing seeds in airtight bags suffocates the insects.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ abua dumɔwui lɛ anaa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ kpojee lɛ, ni amɛshiɔ bu. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo vacuum kotoku mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do I still find small stones and dirt in my harvested grain even after running it through a processing machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyaa nɔ mitaoɔ tɛi bibii lɛ? kɛ muji ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ mli beni etsɔ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ amli po sɛɛ.

english: Machines remove the bulk of heavy debris, but they cannot separate small stones that are the exact same size and weight as the grain. Final hand-sorting by farmers is always needed to remove what the machine misses.
ga: Tsɔnei jieɔ jwɛi babaoo ni tsii. Shi enyɛŋ egbala tɛi bibii ni dalɛ kɛ amɛtsiimɔ tamɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Naagbee nibii ni okwaafonyo lɛ kɛ enine tsuɔ lɛ he miihia be fɛɛ be koni ejie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni tsɔnei lɛ elaaje lɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to dry my harvested maize thoroughly before taking it to a threshing machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ agbi kwraa dani mikɛwo ŋmãa-ŋmãa tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Wet corn kernels are soft and stick together, which causes processing machines to crush the grains instead of shelling them cleanly. Dry grain separates easily and preserves better after processing.
ga: Abele ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ baafee bɔdɔɔ ni amɛbaakpɛtɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaatse amɛhe. Dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ mli gbalaa mlɛo ni akɛtoɔ jogbaŋŋ beni atsu he nii agbe naa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight and intense heat. Tall forest trees or temporary shade crops like plantains shield young cocoa leaves from scorching, keep the soil cool, and retain soil moisture while the roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Koo mli tsei ni kɛlɛ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, and when the soil lacks it, the plant drains nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to support the growth of new top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni eye ebua ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and show yellow patches during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is typically caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by small insects called whiteflies. Whiteflies thrive during dry periods and suck plant juices, causing leaf distortion and reduced stem growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Whiteflies lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: If I plant my maize seeds closer together in the field, won't I get a larger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli Ani manyɛ makpa babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This stress results in thin, weak stalks that fall over easily and produce tiny or incomplete cobs, reducing your total harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shwieɔ shi oya. ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ni eshɛɛɛ he baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my yam tubers small and twisted even though the vines above ground look big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni efite lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ da ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ, shi.

english: Strong vine growth shows the plant receives enough sunlight, but deformed tubers happen when the soil underneath is too hard or stony for the tuber to expand smoothly, or when the soil lacks potassium.
ga: Wein tso lɛ dalɛ ni mli wa tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shi bulb ni efite lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ tɛi tsɔ ni bulb lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ. aloo be mli ni potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi?

english: Tomato flowers drop without forming fruit when temperatures are too high or when heavy rains wash away pollen before insects can fertilize them. Excessive nitrogen fertilizer can also cause the plant to drop flowers while growing foliage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa Efoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ dani kooloi bibii nyɛɔ amɛboteɔ gbalashihilɛ mli. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashwie shi beni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly drop their leaves after a few days of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need air in the soil to breathe. Standing water starves roots of oxygen, causing root rot and extreme stress, which forces the plant to shed its leaves in an attempt to survive.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce mostly leafy vines and no pods after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally fix their own nitrogen from the air into the soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer tricks the plant into putting all its energy into growing thick stems and leaves instead of making flowers and seed pods.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ saa amɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ lakaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli tse ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji

english: Why do my plantain trees snap and fall over easily before the fruit bunch is fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ fãa ni egbeeɔ shi oya dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees easily fall over if soil insects like root borers or nematodes damage the underground corm, weakening the plant's anchor in the soil, or if the soil lacks potassium to strengthen the stem against wind.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ root borers loo nematodes fite ŋmeii lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha tso lɛ mli awa ni ekɛte shi ewo kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my crop right after the first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds remain dormant in the soil for months and are naturally adapted to sprout immediately at the first soak of rain, whereas cultivated seeds require specific soil conditions and more moisture to wake up and start growing.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo. ni atsake amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko kɛ nu babaoo koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi dalɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to lay straight lines across my farm before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Laying straight lines helps you give every crop enough space to get sunlight, water, and nutrients. It also makes it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and walk through your farm without stepping on young plants.
ga: Linei ni ja ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ená hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni onyiɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ onaji shwieee tsei bibii anɔ.

english: Why should I divide my farm into different plots instead of planting everything on one big open space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aja miŋmɔ lɛ mli awo shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo du nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ ngɛ he ngua ko nɛ e ngɛ.

english: Dividing your farm into plots makes managing your crops much easier. It helps you keep track of planting dates, apply water and fertilizer evenly, and rotate different crops to keep the soil healthy and reduce pests.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ mlijaa yɛ shikpɔji amli Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ gbii ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ Okɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he daa. ni atsake ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shi

english: What happens to my crops if I do not clear and prepare the soil properly before planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ ni misaaa he dani miduɔ nii?

english: If the soil is not prepared well, weeds will quickly outgrow your young crops, water may pool and rot the roots, and the plant roots will struggle to grow deep into the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ asaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Jwɛi lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya fe onibii bibii lɛ. Nu baanyɛ afee ekome ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Ni tsei shishifãi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to raise some crops in a nursery first before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ tsei komɛi yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are delicate and easily killed by harsh sun, pests, or heavy rain. A nursery allows you to protect and care for them closely until they are strong enough to survive out in the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ waaa ni hulu la ni naa wa, tsɛŋemɔ helai, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ gbeɔ amɛ oya. Nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ gbekɛbii lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ amɛhe ni okwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Where is the best place on my land to set up a seedling nursery?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni abaanyɛ ato gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe?

english: A nursery should be set up close to a reliable water source on rich, well-draining soil, and ideally in a place protected from strong winds and harsh direct sunlight.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ ahi he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni esa akɛ ehi he ko ni abu he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why should my crop nursery always be located near a water source?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-nursery lɛ ahi he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Young seedlings need gentle, consistent moisture every day to grow strong roots. Having the nursery near water ensures you can easily water them daily without carrying heavy water containers across long distances.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ nu ni mli jɔ, ni yaa nɔ daa daa gbi koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ okɛ nu aha amɛ daa gbi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni awo tsɔnei ni tsiimɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ kɛya he ko shɔŋŋ

english: How often do I need to water young crop seedlings in the nursery?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mawo dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nu?

english: Seedlings usually need to be watered twice a day—once early in the morning before the sun gets hot and once in the cool late afternoon—so the soil stays moist without getting waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni afɔ dumɔwui anɔ nu shii enyɔ daa gbi—leebi maŋkpa dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ni nu akabote mli.

english: How do I know when my nursery seedlings are ready to be transplanted into the main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaawo amɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings are ready when they have developed 3 to 4 strong, true leaves and a sturdy stem, which usually happens a few weeks after germinating depending on the crop type.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛji amɛyɛ anɔkwa baa 3 kɛyashi 4 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ tso ni mli wa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ tso henɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my young plants sometimes shock or wither right after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, midumɔwui lɛ ahe feɔ gbeyei loo amɛgboɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Transplanting shocks young plants because their delicate roots are disturbed and exposed to hot sun. Moving them early in the morning or late afternoon, and watering them immediately, helps them recover quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ atsake tsei bibii lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ ahe feɔ amɛ yaa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbaa amɛnaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ. Shiɛmɔ leebi loo shwane mli No sɛɛ lɛ, ha lɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni eye ebua ni ehiɛ aya oya.

english: How does proper spacing between planted crops affect how much yield I get at harvest?
ga: Te gbɛ ni sa ni kã tsei ateŋ lɛ saa yibiiwoo ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When crops are spaced correctly, their roots do not fight each other for food and water in the soil, and their leaves get plenty of air and sun, leading to larger harvests and fewer diseases.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ ewuuuu niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Ni ebaai lɛ baaná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa anáa kpamɔ babaoo, ni helai hu baa shi.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, shielding young cocoa plants from the hot sun and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield smaller harvests when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots compete for the same sunlight, soil food, and groundwater, which starves the plants and stops them from growing fully.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ yeɔ akaŋ, ni no haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei lɛ ni ehaaa amɛdara kwraa.

english: Pale yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to produce healthy, green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help improve my soil for the next farming season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil with natural fertilizer for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: What causes small holes in my corn leaves and chewed-up tops in young plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ni aŋɔwo mli yɛ mi tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ

english: This leaf damage is caused by caterpillars such as the Fall Armyworm, which crawl into the growing tops of young corn plants to feed on the tender new leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ afitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miida lɛ ayiteŋ koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When pepper plants experience severe heat and lack of water, they drop their flowers as a survival mechanism to conserve moisture and keep the main plant alive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ he lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni eha tso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why is it crucial to remove weeds around my maize plants while they are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni madu mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Young maize plants have short roots that easily lose the competition for soil nutrients and sunlight against aggressive, fast-growing weeds.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji, ni no haa amɛfeɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ akaŋshii mli kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni teɔ shi woɔ jwɛi ni daa oya ni feɔ basabasa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during peak sun hours to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the heat, helping the plant hold onto its water.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulutsoo baa lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tomato tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli.

english: Why does my cassava become hard and woody if I leave it in the soil too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni efeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: As cassava plants mature past their prime or experience dry weather, they draw energy back out of the root, leaving behind tough, dry fibers instead of soft starch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ dara fe bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ loo amɛna kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ, Amɛgbalaa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛbaa sɛɛ. Eshiɔ tsɔji ni wa ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo najiaŋ.

english: Why do seeds stored in a damp sack fail to germinate properly when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛto kotokui ni mli efɔ mli lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Excess moisture causes stored seeds to absorb water too early or grow mold, which damages or kills the tiny plant embryo inside before it reaches the farm soil.
ga: Fɛ̃i babaoo haa dumɔwui ni ato lɛ shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baaha tsei amli fɔmɔ kotokui bibii lɛ adara. Mɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fite loo amɛgboi dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the exact time to plant my maize when the major rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa?

english: Maize seeds need consistent soil moisture to germinate properly. It is best to plant immediately after the first two or three heavy, steady rains of the season. Planting during the very first light rain is risky because a sudden dry spell can heat the ground and ruin the seeds before they fully sprout.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ bei enyɔ loo etɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli Klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbimɔ trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ ni egbe dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why do my cassava plants take much longer to produce tubers if I plant them near the end of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava needs plenty of water during its early months to develop strong root systems. When planted late, the dry harmattan season arrives before the plant establishes deep roots, causing the growth to slow down significantly until the next rainy season.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia Cassava yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa aba lɛ, kɛ́ adu sɛɛ mli lɛ, harmattan lɛ mli nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa dani tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ baa. Enɛ haa dalɛ baa shi kwraa kɛyashiɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are signs of water stress. Cocoa trees reduce leaf surface area or shed leaves to protect themselves from intense sunlight and conserve whatever moisture is left in the root system.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nu he haomɔ he okadi. Cocoa tsei lɛ baa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi loo amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save energy so it can survive harsh conditions instead of spending food on growing fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why does my tomato plant grow lots of lush green leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes tomatoes to focus all their energy on leafy vegetative growth. Shifting nutrient balance toward phosphorus and potassium signals the plant to stop making extra leaves and start producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tomato kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa phosphorus kɛ potassium nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai krokomɛi ni ekɛfataa he lɛ feemɔ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai feemɔ.

english: Is there a specific time of day I should spray liquid fertilizer or pest control on my crops?
ga: Ani be ko yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon. During these cooler hours, calm winds keep chemicals from drifting, leaf pores open to absorb liquid quickly, and hot sunlight won't dry out or burn the leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. Yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ kpoo baatsi tsofai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu oya. Ni hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ haŋ baai lɛ agbi loo eshãŋ.

english: How often should I clear weeds around my young yam mounds so they do not affect growth?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi abɔle mi sweet potato pile lɛ he koni ekaná edalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Weeds should be cleared every three to four weeks during the first few months. Young yam vines grow slowly initially, and early weeding prevents weeds from taking away sunlight, space, and soil nutrients meant for the yam.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ daa otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli. Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra Enɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju hulu la, he ko kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛha sweet potatoes.

english: Why do my plantain stands produce small bunches if I leave all the suckers growing together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ mli fãa bibii bibii lɛ? Ni kɛji mishi ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛfee ekome kɛdara hu?

english: Extra suckers act as competitors, stealing water, food, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Cutting back extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, allowing the main plant to put all its nutrients into a large fruit bunch.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ akaŋshilɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ aba ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ woɔ aduawai akuu agbo ko mli.

english: Why do armyworms attack my maize field so rapidly right after the shoots emerge?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-ŋma ŋmɔji lɛ oya beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths look specifically for soft, tender green shoots to lay their eggs. Young maize leaves are soft and easy for newly hatched caterpillars to eat, allowing pest populations to explode within a few days.
ga: Caterpillar ŋmeii taoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkɛwo amɛwui. Abɛi bibii ahe baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo kɛha ŋmeii ni efɔ ehee lɛ akɛ amɛaaye. Enɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why does cowpea perform better than plantain or cocoa in drier northern regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe plantain loo kookoo yɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpai ni mli egbi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea is naturally adapted to dry conditions with deep roots that seek deep soil moisture and tough leaves that prevent water loss. It grows and matures quickly during short rainy periods, unlike water-heavy crops like cocoa or plantain.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli, ni eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ baai ni wa ni tsiɔ nu ni sɛɛ efoɔ lɛ naa. Edaa ni ekwɛɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ tsei ni haa nu babaoo, tamɔ kookoo loo plantains.

english: Why are my crop plants starting to turn yellow and die one after the other on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ komekomei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops die one by one, it usually means a disease or pest is actively spreading through the soil or from plant to plant. Early detection helps you remove infected plants before the sickness spreads across the entire field.
