ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi komekomei Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛtee tso kroko nɔ. Nibii ni anaa mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ dani hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oyale lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: If I plant a new crop variety given by agriculture officers, is it guaranteed that it will not die from sickness?
ga: Kɛ midu tso henɔ hee ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko kɛha mi lɛ, Guarantee akɛ hela mɔŋ bo ni ogbo kwraa?

english: New crop varieties are bred to resist specific diseases, but they are not indestructible. They still require proper soil nutrients, correct watering, and protection from other diseases or extreme weather conditions.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi heei koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Shi anyɛŋ akpata hiɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa hu he miihia amɛ. nu ni ja ni akɛhaa kɛ helai krokomɛi loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa lɛ akwɛmɔ

english: How can the officers from the agriculture department help me when a strange disease attacks my farm?
ga: Te Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ onukpai lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ kɛ́ hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ batutua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Extension officers can visit your farm to inspect sick plants, identify the specific cause of the outbreak, and give you exact recommendations on treatments, field hygiene, or better planting methods.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi baanyɛ aya oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyakwɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ nɔ pɔtɛɛ ni kɛ hela lɛ ba ni okɛ ŋaawoo ni mli ka shi faŋŋ aha yɛ tsamɔ he Okwaafoi amli hetsemɔ loo gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii.

english: What should I do immediately with the few plants that are dying so the rest of my farm doesn't catch the sickness?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ tsei fioo komɛi ni miigboi lɛ? Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli bii ni eshwɛ lɛ akaye hela?

english: Carefully uproot the sick plants and burn or bury them far away from your farm. Always wash your hands and tools after handling infected crops so you do not carry the germs to healthy plants.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni oshã loo ofu amɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, kɛ́ ota tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe lɛ, afɔ oniji kɛ onitsumɔ dadei ahe. Enɛ ji koni okɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akatsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why would an improved seed variety fail and die out on my land even though it was meant to help us survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛgboi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni eye ebua wɔ ni wɔhi shi lɛ?

english: An improved variety may fail if the disease in your soil is different from what it was bred to fight, or if environmental factors like severe drought, poor soil fertility, or incorrect planting depth put too much stress on the plant.
ga: Henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ helai ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ nɔ ni esa akɛ tso lɛ kɛkpe lɛ he. aloo kɛji shihilɛ mli nibii tamɔ hɔmɔ ni naa wa Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii Aloo, dumɔ ni mli kwɔ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa tso lɛ nɔ.

english: If a disease kills most of my crops this season, can I clear the land and plant the exact same crop next season?
ga: Kɛji hela gbe miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli. Ani manyɛ majie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ ni madu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is best not to plant the same crop immediately because disease germs stay alive in the soil. Rotating your field with a completely different crop starves the germs and helps clear the soil for future planting.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shikome ejaakɛ helatsɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi kwraa tsake ŋmɔji amli lɛ, ebaaha helatsɛ lɛ aye hɔmɔ, ni eye ebua ni etsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know if my crops are dying because of a disease or simply because the soil is bad?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji helai miigbe miŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛkɛ hewɔ?

english: Diseases usually cause rotting, spots, or sudden wilting that spreads progressively from plant to plant, whereas poor soil causes uniform slow growth or yellowing across the whole farm without rotting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela kɛ fitemɔ baa. Spots loo trukaa ŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ aya hiɛ blɛoo, efee ekome loo efee ŋmɔŋ ni efiteee.

english: Is there any way to save my remaining healthy crops after more than half of my farm has already died?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ beni miŋmɔ lɛ mli nɔ ni fe fã egbo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, you can create a clear boundary space between the sick and healthy areas, apply the right protective spray recommended by extension officers, and stop walking from infected zones into healthy zones.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oto husui ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ hei ni helatsɛmɛi yɔɔ kɛ hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ateŋ. Kɛ tsofai ni sa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ atsu nii taakɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ wo ŋaa lɛ. ni okpa nyiɛmɔ kɛjɛ he ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya he ni hewalɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: At what stage should our local farming group call for emergency support from the district agriculture department?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli esa akɛ wɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi akuu lɛ atao oyaiyeli yelikɛbuamɔ kɛjɛ Kpokpaa lɛ nɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ?

english: You should report to the agriculture office as soon as you notice unusual plant deaths spreading across multiple neighboring farms, before the disease wipes out the entire community's harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ obɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ amaniɛ pɛ kɛji ona tsei agbele ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. dani hela lɛ baakpata akutso lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do a few single plants stay green and strong while all the surrounding plants are dying from disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei fioo komɛi pɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ gboiɔ lɛ? Helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ?

english: Some individual plants possess natural genetic strength that makes them stronger against specific diseases. Observing these surviving plants can help officers identify strong traits for future breeding.
ga: Tsei komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ nii ahe hewalɛ ni haa helai komɛi nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛnɔ. Tsei ni hiɛ ka nɛɛ akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua onukpai lɛ ni amɛna sui ni mli wa ni baaha amɛfɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for strong green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients away or when the roots stay soaked in water for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ ewo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: How do I know which direction to stick cassava stems into the ground when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole gbɛ ni obaadu o-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small raised buds or 'eyes' on the stem—they should always point upwards toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the shoots will struggle to grow upwards, resulting in tiny roots and poor cassava yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii ni awó nɔ loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaawa akɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii kɛ ŋmei yibii ni ehiii baa.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy and humid weather. Removing the infected pods immediately and pruning extra tree branches lets in sunlight, which stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the weather gets too hot or dry, the plant drops its flowers to conserve water and energy to stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni wala ahi shi.

english: Why is it important for me to stake my yam vines with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ atswa mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall sticks so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. The more sunlight the leaves receive, the more food they send down into the ground to grow large yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia ni amɛná niji kakadaji koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, babaoo ni abaamaje niyenii kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do so many small plantain shoots grow around my main stem, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ. mi tsɔne titri lɛ Ni ani esa akɛ mafo mli?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers, and they steal food, water, and sunlight from the main mother plant. You should prune away most of them, leaving only one strong sucker to take over after you harvest the main plantain bunch.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ofo mli babaoo. Tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baashwɛ ni baaye enajiaŋ beni okpa tso titri lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop during the afternoon heat even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes water to evaporate from the leaves faster than the roots can suck water from the soil. Placing dry grass or mulch around the base of the pepper plants keeps the soil cool and reduces water loss.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Pepper tsei lɛ ashishi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my land better for my next crop?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria on their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil fertilizer. When the plants decay, they leave this free fertilizer behind for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni tsei fiteɔ Amɛshiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are tiny green caterpillars eating holes through my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye bu kɛmiitsɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Moths lay tiny eggs on the undersides of cabbage leaves, which hatch into caterpillars that eat the tender foliage. Checking under the leaves regularly and spraying natural neem seed oil repels the caterpillars before they ruin the head.
ga: Moths woɔ wɔji bibii. Yɛ cabbage baa ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akwɛ baa lɛ shishi daa ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem dumɔwui amli fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ashwie ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛkpãtã ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crops much more during the first month than later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli fe sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop plants have small, shallow roots and few leaves, so weeds easily overpower them by stealing water, light, and soil nutrients. Once your crops grow taller, their big leaves shade out the ground, preventing weeds from growing.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ yɔɔ, no hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ kunim oya kɛtsɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ onibii lɛ dara lɛ Ebaai wuji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up tightly like tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is very hot, crops lose water quickly through their leaves. Rolling their leaves into tubes is a natural defense mechanism that reduces the surface area exposed to the heat, helping the plant hold onto its water until the weather cools down.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ awoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he ni haa he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains flooded my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe just like they need water. When water sits on the farm for too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil, causing the roots to suffocate and rot from fungal diseases.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ahe helai amli.

english: How does putting dried animal manure and dead leaves on my land help my crops grow bigger than using nothing?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi kɛ baai ni egboi ni mikɛfataa mishikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa fe kɛji mifeee nɔ ko?

english: Animal manure and decaying leaves act as natural food and a sponge for the soil. They break down to release nutrients slowly to the plant while helping the soil hold onto water for a longer time during dry spells.
ga: Koolooi ashwiei kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ sponji kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Amɛ fiteɔ fiofio koni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ amɛha tso lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why should I plant my crops far apart when planting them close together seems like it would give me more harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ? Akɛni etamɔ nɔ ni amɛdumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ haa mináa ŋmaa babaoo hewɔ lɛ?

english: Crops are like children at a dining table; if too many sit closely together, nobody gets enough food. Proper spacing ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water to grow big and produce healthy yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tamɔ gbekɛbii. Yɛ niyeli okpɔlɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛji amɛtara amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, mɔ ko mɔ ko naaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ agbo ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant cassava on the exact same farm patch every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Cassava feeds heavily on specific nutrients in the soil. Planting it in the same place every year completely empties the soil of those nutrients and allows pests that feed on cassava to multiply and stay in that ground.
ga: Cassava yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ haa nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmei lɛ koni amɛshwere ni amɛhi nakai he lɛ.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last maize harvest yield less corn than the certified seeds I buy from the agrovat shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe kɛjɛ Agrovat lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred in laboratories for strong yields and disease resistance. The seeds you save from harvested crops lose those special strengths in the next generation, resulting in weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ laboratori ko mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ. Dumɔwui ni okɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ baafite nakai hewalɛ kroko lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my rice leaves turn yellow and stop growing when weeds start covering the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa kwɛ̃mɔ kɛ́ jwɛi bɔi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ hamɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal nitrogen—the chemical that keeps leaves green and healthy—from the soil faster than rice can. Without enough nitrogen, the rice leaves lose their green color and cannot make food to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ nitrogen. ni ji tsofa ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe ŋmãa Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ baafite amɛ eŋɔli su ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear all the large forest trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ pɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are fragile and burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Large forest trees provide critical shade and cool air, acting as a shelter while the young cocoa roots establish themselves.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ koo agbo lɛ mli lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ he ko ni mɛi hiɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ toɔ amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my maize far faster during a dry spell than during a heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain physically washes young armyworms off the maize plants and drowns them. In dry weather, the caterpillars survive easily and multiply rapidly, while the drought-stressed maize is too weak to resist them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ asraafoi bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ amɛ shwieɔ nu mli. yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi mlɛo ni amɛfɔɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa ni hɔmɔ emɔ lɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eshi.

english: Why do birds suddenly start flocking to my rice farm just when the rice heads begin to swell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi jeɔ shishi amɛbua amɛhe naa trukaa yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli kɛji ŋmãa yitsei lɛ je shishi amɛfutu pɛ?

english: When rice grains start forming, they fill with a sweet, liquid juice known as the 'milky stage.' Birds prefer eating the grains at this soft stage because it is easy to consume and full of energy.
ga: Beni ŋmãa ŋmaa lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ eyi kɛ nu ni mli tse ni atsɛɔ lɛ 'milk stage'. Okpoi sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmaa yɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi nɛɛ mli ejaakɛ eyeli waaa ni amɛhe wa waa.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure early in the plant's growth helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: If I put fertilizer directly against the stem of my pepper plant, will it grow faster?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo pepper tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ Ani ebaada oya?

english: Putting fertilizer directly against the stem can burn and kill the plant. It is best to place fertilizer in a circle a few inches away from the stem so the roots can safely spread out and drink the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ ashã ni egbo. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ kooyigbɛ ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛnuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, which love to hide in the center whorl of young corn plants. Spraying recommended insecticides early in the morning or sprinkling dry sand or ash into the leaf center can help destroy them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall cutworms ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo okɛ ŋã ni egbi loo sũ shwie baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni efite amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads during wet, rainy weather. Pruning extra tree branches to let sunlight in and removing infected pods quickly keeps the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji krokomɛi amli koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot in the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away from the roots so they stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Koni ehi shi ni egbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why is it better to push cassava stem cuttings into the ground at an angle instead of laying them flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni oookɛ amɛ afɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at an angle pushes the buds deeper into the moist soil, helping roots grow strong and produce large tubers down deep where heat cannot dry them out.
ga: Yucca niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yaa shɔŋŋ ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha amɛgbi.

english: Why does clearing weeds around my yam mounds make my yams grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Mi ŋmɔtɔ ni mikɛto lɛ ha mi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kwɛ̃?

english: Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your yam plants need. Keeping the mounds weed-free ensures all soil food goes directly into making bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni o-sweet potato tsei lɛ taoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ jwɛi ni ato lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or using too much nitrogen fertilizer can stress tomato plants and make their flowers fall off. Watering regularly at the soil level and switching to a phosphorus-rich fertilizer encourages flowers to turn into fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ ni eha amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ tsakemɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains develop tiny holes and turn to dust in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni ebatsɔ sũ yɛ nitoohe?

english: Weevils are tiny bugs that eat inside stored grain and lay eggs. Drying your maize until the grains are very hard and storing them in sealed airtight bags stops weevils from surviving and destroying your harvest.
ga: Moth ji kooloo bibioo ko. ni yeɔ dumɔwui ni ato ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii Kɛ́ ogbi o-ŋmãa lɛ mli kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ mli wa waa ni okɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shi ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not go very deep into the soil, and heavy fruit bunches make the trees top-heavy. Using strong wooden poles to prop up fruiting plants helps keep them standing during heavy winds and rain.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Ni aduawai akui ni tsii tsiiɔ tso lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa tsu nii koni akɛfi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdamɔɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green and grow leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure can help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛha baai lɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long because of poor drainage. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water run off so the roots can breathe and stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. sɛɛ tsɛ tsɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing proper plant nutrients helps flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What will happen if I plant my crops very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes the stems thin and weak, resulting in a much smaller harvest compared to well-spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi kwraa kɛ akɛto tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do extension officers advise me not to plant seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ ewooo mi ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from past harvests, especially hybrid seeds, lose their strength and yield much less crop. Buying fresh, certified seeds ensures your plants grow strong, resist diseases, and produce maximum yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ amli Titri lɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ Ebaafite hewalɛ ni ebaawo yibii fioo kwraa. Dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni ooohe lɛ baaha otsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ, amɛte shi amɛwo helai, ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantains growing beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa ni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and provide living shade like an umbrella, keeping the cocoa cool and moist during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ehaa hulutsoo be tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is already moist after a rain and when plants are actively growing. Applying it on dry soil can burn plant roots, and applying it right before heavy rain can wash it away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ, kɛ be mli ni tsei miida jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso shishifãi. Ni okɛwo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa koni ekɛfɔ tso shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is healthy enough to give me a good yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, holds water well without staying swampy, crumbles easily in your hand, and has living earthworms. You can also get your soil tested by an extension agent to know its exact nutrient levels.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmeii bɛ mli, efoɔ oya yɛ enine mli, ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni hiɔ mli. Obaanyɛ oha extension agent hu aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ koni ele bɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ fa ha pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the central leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni maye mi-baby corn lɛ teŋ baai lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. They hide inside the funnel of the maize leaves; spraying early in the morning or late in the evening when pests are active helps protect your plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu otsei lɛ ahe.

english: How does clearing weeds early help my crops produce a bigger harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing them early removes this competition, allowing your crops to take all the food they need to grow big and yield more.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baajie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya. Kwɛmɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer pods now than when I was younger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe be mli ni miji gbekɛ fioo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees reach a peak age after which their yields naturally decline and they become more vulnerable to diseases. Clearing out old, low-yielding trees and replanting with fresh, disease-resistant varieties helps restore high yields to your farm.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shɛɔ afii ni amɛyeɔ fe fɛɛ he ni nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii babaoo lɛ ni okɛ tsei heei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni yibii babaoo aku sɛɛ aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What is the benefit of planting new hybrid cassava stems instead of reusing stems from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei heei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ adumɔ he? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ŋmei tsei baatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: New hybrid cassava stems are specially bred to resist common diseases like cassava mosaic virus and mature much faster, giving you larger tubers in less time compared to older traditional varieties.
ga: Afee ŋmei tsei heei ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛte shi ewo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ tamɔ ŋmei mosaic virus lɛ. ni edaa oya kwraa Enɛ haa onáa ŋmeii wuji yɛ be fioo mli kɛ akɛto blema ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weed seeds grow back so much faster than my crop seeds after I clear my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally adapted to the local environment and can lie dormant in the soil for years waiting for sunlight. Crops are more delicate and require early weeding and attention so they do not get choked out.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ ni emɛ hulu la afii babaoo Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ mli wa waa ni ebiɔ ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra. koni akatsi tso lɛ naa

english: Is it harmful to burn my farm debris after clearing land for a new crop?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ mashã miŋmɔ mli sũi ni efite lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ kɛha dumɔwui heei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning clears the land fast, but extreme heat destroys valuable nutrients and helpful organisms in the topsoil. Cutting plant debris and leaving it to rot naturally turns it into organic compost that feeds your next crop.
ga: Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei amli jwɛi ni oha egbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow during dry spells in the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ shweremɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen or water. During dry spells, roots cannot draw nutrients easily from dry soil, so applying manure early and planting with the start of the rains keeps plants green.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Shishifãi nyɛŋ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he mra. Ni kɛ́ adu beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee eŋɔli.

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by root diseases like bacterial wilt that attack from inside the soil. Planting tomatoes in a different field each season prevents these soil organisms from building up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi helai tamɔ bacteria wilt ni tutuaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu tomato yɛ saatsoi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do I need to prune excess branches and leaves from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tso niji kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Pruning lets sunlight and fresh air pass through the tree canopy. This lowers dampness around the trunk, preventing black pod disease from taking hold and spreading to other pods.
ga: Tso ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ aba shi, ni ebaatsi black pod hela lɛ naa koni ekamɔ ni egbɛ eshwa pod krokomɛi anɔ.

english: How do I know when my sweet potatoes are ready to harvest so they do not rot in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Sweet potatoes are ready when their leaves begin turning yellow and drying up. Leaving tubers in the soil too long past maturity makes them vulnerable to soil pests and fungal rotting.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eshɛ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii yɛ sũ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ.

english: What causes my pepper plant flowers to fall off before forming pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper ŋmɔtɔi?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences high heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Watering consistently during the flowering stage and adding compost helps the tree hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce fruit compared to my neighbor's plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantains require rich organic soil and space to feed. If too many suckers grow around one main plant, they fight for nutrients, which delays fruiting; cutting extra suckers allows the main plant to fruit faster.
ga: Plantains he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ, ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ he ko ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa aduawai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Tso yibii krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii oya.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for the plant. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves to stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni haa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛye ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: How can I tell if my farmland needs fertilizer before I start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: If your soil is hard, pale in color, or your crops grew poorly in the previous season, the land lacks nutrients. Adding well-rotted animal manure or organic fertilizer restores soil health so crops can grow well.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, ehiɛ su, loo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koolooi ashishifãi ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops wilt under the hot sun even though it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ miiho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ? Ni nugbɔ nɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ?

english: Hot afternoon heat makes plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can pull it from dry topsoil. Covering the soil around the crops with dry grass or leaves keeps the ground cool and traps moisture.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Mulching around Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems very close together to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing leaves room for each plant to grow large, thick tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ bulbs agboi ni mli tse.

english: Why is it better to buy certified maize seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from harvested crops lose their strength and give lower yields in the next season. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist diseases, handle harsh weather, and produce larger harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli ni ebaawo yibii babaoo yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. Nitsumɔ ni kɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe ni ekɛ nitsumɔ babaoo haa

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving green dirt inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji eŋɔli yɛ tsei lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the plant's leaves during the day and feeds on them. Applying early treatments like neem oil solution or recommended sprays protects the leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ tsei ahe baai amli yɛ gbi mli ni eyeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai tamɔ neem fɔ mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting and turning soft underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifee blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Soft rot occurs when heavy rain sits in the soil without draining, causing fungal diseases that rot the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away.
ga: Rot baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ baa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain suckers turning yellow and curling before they even fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Curling yellow leaves on plantain suckers are often caused by tiny worm-like pests called nematodes or soil fungi attacking the roots. Planting clean suckers on fresh land stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ nematodes loo fungi ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse yɛ shikpɔŋ ŋmɔŋ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and high heat without burning. They need temporary shade crops like plantains to protect them until their roots grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ ni amɛshãaa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their small flowers without forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? yɛ yibɔi babaoo mli ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔi efeee?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or lack of pollinating insects. Keeping shade trees and maintaining soil moisture helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ Tso lɛ he ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen. When the soil does not have enough nitrogen, the plant cannot make green chlorophyll, which slows down growth and reduces your harvest yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee klorofil ni ji eŋɔli. Enɛ baaha shweremɔ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips, aphids, or mites that feed on plant sap. Spraying with recommended organic or chemical insecticides early protects the young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites ni yeɔ tso mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai bibii ahe.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is rich enough to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good soil is usually dark, crumbles easily in your hands, and holds moisture without getting waterlogged. If your crops grow very slowly and look pale without clear pest damage, your soil lacks essential nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa mli tseɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu bɛ mli Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa blɛoo waa ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi efiteee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is eating the soft leaves inside the center of my maize stalks, and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso teŋ lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ tsɔɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: That damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the growing whorl of the plant. You can protect your crop by applying approved insecticides or putting clean sand mixed with wood ash into the center of the stalks early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ naagbai lɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii loo ŋã ni he tse ni akɛ tso sũ efutu mli lɛ ni okɛaawo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ mra lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off before they can grow into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when the plant lacks nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps prevent flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ bɛ daa Aloo kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ calcium lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava stems when setting up a new farm?
ga: Kɛ́ ato ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ, te esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Plant cassava stems about 1 meter apart in rows that are also 1 meter apart. Giving them enough space prevents them from competing for sunlight and allows room for large tubers to expand underground.
ga: Aduɔ Yucca tsei lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mita kome hu. Kɛ́ aha amɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye hulu la he akaŋ, ni ebaaha gbɛ aha ŋmeii wuji lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to manufacture food for growing big tubers under the soil. Staking lifts the leaves into the sunlight and prevents soil diseases from attacking the wet foliage on the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli ni ehaaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ akatutua baai ni efɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds when my crops are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Clearing weeds early gives your crops a strong head start so they can produce a bigger yield.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ ashi akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa onibii lɛ hewalɛ babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to cut off some branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji komɛi lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let in air and sunlight, which dries out excess moisture and prevents black pod disease. It also directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ agbi. ni etsi black pod hela lɛ naa Ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ hu tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell the right time to plant my crop seeds at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Plant after the ground has received at least two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the soil. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if a hot spell follows.
ga: Dumɔ beni kɛ hoo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko ba.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or shade trees next to my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide shade to protect young cocoa leaves and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight for the same soil nutrients and water, resulting in thin stalks and smaller ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ hu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni abele toi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Yam leaves need to reach up to capture maximum sunlight to produce food, which flows down into the ground to feed and swell the growing yam tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashɛ ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni ehaa yam ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make green leaves and food; adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛwo baai kɛ niyenii eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my land better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa he ni miyɔɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally adding free nutrients back into the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops even when my crops are taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɔ fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Underneath the ground, weed roots actively steal water and plant food away from your crop's roots, starving your crop even if it seems bigger above ground.
ga: Yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, jwɛi shishifãi juɔ nu kɛ tso niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara fe shikpɔŋ lɛ moŋ.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves and small green caterpillars inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ bu bibii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like Fall Armyworms, which feed on tender leaves and destroy the center of the plant if left untreated.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ baai bibii ni amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ mli kɛji atsaaa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop growing during warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that drain sap from the undersides of young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering, as a self-defense mechanism to save energy when stressed.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he koni akɛto hewalɛ he kɛji mɔ ko miihao.

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack open from expanding tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I align my crop rows in a specific direction instead of planting anywhere on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ moŋ fe ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Aligning your rows with the direction of the sun ensures all your crops get equal sunlight throughout the day, preventing taller plants from shading smaller ones and helping them grow uniformly.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ to he ni hulu lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Ehaa tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛha tsei bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How does intense sunlight affect my young crops after planting?
ga: Te hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ beni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: Excessive direct sunlight can scorch tender young leaves and rapidly dry out the soil, causing seedlings to wilt before their roots are established enough to pull moisture from deep ground.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ dani shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Does changing the distance between my crop rows help them handle hot weather better?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni kã mi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, proper spacing allows air to flow freely while preventing leaves from overcrowding, which helps lower field temperatures and retains moisture in the soil under the plant canopy.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ mli latsaa baa shi, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ tsei ashishi.

english: Why do my plants seem to bend and grow toward one side of the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mitsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiida kɛmiiya ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ?

english: Crops naturally lean and stretch toward the brightest source of sunlight so their leaves can capture maximum light energy to make food for growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baatsɔ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbala amɛhe kɛya hei ni hulu la ni kpɛɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ jɛɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ la hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛfee niyenii kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why is it recommended that I try new farming techniques on a small plot before changing my whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɔ akɛ aka okwaayeli gbɛ̀i heei akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ lɛ? dani etsake ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ

english: Testing new methods step-by-step on a small area allows you to learn how the crop responds without risking your entire yield or spending too much money at once.
ga: Gbɛi heei akamɔ Gbɛjianɔtoi ni afeɔ yɛ he ko bibioo lɛ haa okaseɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii amɛhaa ni okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ wooo oshara mli loo okɛ shika babaoo efiteee shikome.

english: How does improving my land gradually make my crops yield better over time?
ga: Mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔyaa lɛ baafee fiofio. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Taking things step-by-step gives you time to manage soil health, improve planting patterns, and correct mistakes without exhausting your labor or financial resources.
ga: Nibii ni ooofee shikome shikome lɛ haa onáa be ni okɛkwɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha bɔ ni aduɔ nii ahaa lɛ aya hiɛ ni osaa tɔmɔi ni okɛ onitsumɔ loo oshika akafite.

english: How long after clearing my land should I wait before planting my crops?
ga: Beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Waiting a short period after clearing allows cut weeds to dry up and enrich the soil as organic matter, while also giving you space to mark out proper, clean planting rows.
ga: Mɛɛmɔ lɛ yɛ kuku. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa jwɛi ni afo lɛ ni egbiɔ ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa gbɛ ni okɛkadiɔ dumɔwui ni sa ni he tse lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant seeds immediately after clearing bush without planning my row layout first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie tsei bibii lɛ ni mitooo line lɛ he gbɛjianɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Planting without layout planning leads to irregular spacing, making it harder for crops to get enough sunlight and making future weeding and harvesting much more difficult.
ga: Dumɔ ni atooo he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baaha gbɛ ni jɛkɛmɔ afee ekome. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaana hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ni enɛ haa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa waa.

english: What basic checks can I do to make sure my farm caretakers planted my crops correctly?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee kwɛmɔi mafee koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ mɛi ni kwɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miidu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: You can check if the crop rows are straight, if seeds were planted at consistent distances, and if young plants are coming up evenly across the entire field.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ja loo amɛjaaa. Ani adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ yeɔ egbɔ? ni tsei bibii ni miida pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Ani nakai eji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Why do my crops dry up faster on open, cleared fields compared to areas near trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ amli kɛ akɛto hei ni bɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Open land leaves crops exposed to full sun and strong winds that quickly evaporate soil moisture, whereas nearby trees filter the wind and provide gentle shade that keeps the soil cool.
ga: He ni agbele naa lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ni amɛhaa hulutsoo blɛoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily scorch under direct sun. Plantains or shade trees act as natural umbrellas, protecting seedlings from heat and keeping the soil moist so their roots can establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess branches so sunlight and air can pass through the tree. This prevents fungal diseases and forces the tree to send its food and energy into growing bigger cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ yaa kookoo ŋmɔji wuji ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai baafata he.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop when the tree is stressed by drought, extreme heat, or lack of nutrients. They also need tiny insects called midges to pollinate them; without proper moisture and shade, these midges cannot survive to do their job.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Amɛmiitao kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ hu koni amɛwo amɛmli. Kɛji hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ lɛ, Nɛkɛ gbɔmɛi nɛɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi ni amɛtsu nii.

english: Can I plant orange trees together on the same land with my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu citrus tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ cocoa tsei?

english: Yes, orange trees provide good permanent shade for cocoa and give you extra fruit to sell. However, you must space them far enough apart so their roots do not fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, citrus tsei haa hulutsoo be ni hiɔ shi daa kɛhaa kookoo kɛ aduawai krokomɛi ni akɛbaahɔɔ, shi kɛlɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ amɛ abɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛshishifãi lɛ akatswa akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ he.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, damp conditions. Pruning your trees and clearing weeds allows sunlight and wind to dry the pods faster, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Tsei lɛ ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Why is a strange green plant growing directly out of my cocoa branches and making the tree weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei eŋɔlii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ miida kɛmiijɛ mikoo niji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛmiiha tso lɛ miigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: That plant is mistletoe, a parasite that steals water and nutrients directly from your cocoa tree. You must cut it off below where it attaches to the branch before it weakens and kills the host tree.
ga: Nakai tso lɛ ji mistletoe. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ ofo lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ he ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ he lɛ dani egbɔjɔ ni efite tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is missing key plant nutrients like nitrogen, or the ground is waterlogged and choking the roots. Adding proper fertilizer or improving land drainage will help restore the leaves to green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni ekɛmiimɔ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli jogbaŋŋ loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ aku sɛɛ afee amɛ eŋɔli.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing much fewer pods than they used to ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii babaoo fioo fe afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their natural production slows down and they become weaker. You can restore your yield by applying fertilizer, doing heavy pruning, or gradually replacing old trees with newer hybrid varieties.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tso ko ye afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nibii ni efeɔ lɛ baa shi ni egbɔjɔɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaawo mli lɛ nɔ. Kpãa tsei lɛ amli waa loo fiofio lɛ, okɛ tsei heei ni akɛfee tsei lɛ atsake tsei momo lɛ.

english: Why is it better to leave fallen leaves on the farm floor instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaashi baai ni egbee shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fe ni ashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Fallen leaves act as a blanket over the soil, trapping moisture during dry weather and preventing weeds from growing. As they decay, they turn into natural compost that feeds the roots of your crops.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ Beni amɛfiteɔ Ebaatsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ.

english: What is the best food crop for a new farmer to plant while waiting three years for cocoa to yield?
ga: Mɛni ji niyenii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni okwaafoi heei baanyɛ adu yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ afii etɛ dani kookoo lɛ awo yibii?

english: Plantain and cassava are ideal because they provide quick income and food within the first year. Plantains also serve a double purpose by giving necessary shade to young cocoa plants while they grow.
ga: Plantains kɛ cassava hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhaa shika oya kɛ niyenii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Plantains hu tsuɔ yiŋtoi enyɔ he nii kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for healthy green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain saturates the soil, preventing roots from breathing and absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread a plant virus, or by the plant curling its leaves to protect itself from extreme heat and dry soil conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Aloo bɔ ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off the tree trunks without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to pollinate them. If there is hot, dry weather, too much shade, or lack of plant nutrients, the tree drops unpollinated flowers to save its strength.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ, edɔ, ni eyɛ hulutsoo be babaoo. loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ ni bɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee nɔ lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ahi shi.

english: What makes my pepper plants drop their flowers before growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifo amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani midu amɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from high temperatures, irregular watering, or when insects fail to visit and pollinate the flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ ayasara ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why does planting maize in the exact same field every year give me smaller harvests each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Maize draws the same nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting it continuously drains the soil's food reserves and allows soil-borne pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu lɛ daa lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have adapted to quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before young crop seeds can fully establish their roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Dani dumɔwui bibii lɛ baawo shishifãi kwraa

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: When rain saturates soil without proper drainage, water blocks air from reaching the roots. This suffocates the roots and creates wet conditions where soil fungi easily rot the tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni nu tsɔɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ baa ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: Why does covering the dirt around my crops with dry leaves keep them alive during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around Miduɔ miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai ni egboi koni amɛye amɛbua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Dry leaves act as a blanket called mulch. Mulch traps moisture in the dirt, keeps the ground cool, and prevents the hot sun from evaporating water away from plant roots.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Mulch mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so I can get more plants on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and a smaller overall harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantain suckers planted next to them on new farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii amli yɛ amɛmasɛi yɛ ŋmɔ hee ko mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide crucial shade and keep the air moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight, which burns their leaves and dries out soil moisture quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a cooler environment and holds soil moisture while the young cocoa trees grow stronger.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ ashã ni eha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Beni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa waa lɛ,.

english: Why are my maize crops weaker and producing smaller cobs when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmãa fioo beni midu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting maize too close together forces the crops to compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This stress prevents individual plants from getting enough food to build large, heavy cobs.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing leaves in young maize are usually a sign that the soil is low in nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for leafy green growth, or that waterlogged soil is choking the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward during hot hours as a natural defense to reduce their surface area, trapping moisture inside and preventing water loss from sunlight.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. Taakɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni akɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtsiɔ nu ni hulu la lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ naa

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upward and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaf undersides, or by a viral infection spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the stems and leaves look very tall and big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛlɛ waa ni amɛdara moŋ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or is overly packed, cassava spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of swelling its roots underground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo eyi mli obɔ fe nine lɛ, Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha eshishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my yam vines need to be tied to wooden stakes to yield bigger tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akpɛtɛ tso ko he koni maná bulbs wuji lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine, and lifting its leaves off the ground with stakes allows them to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight powers food production in the leaves, which is stored in the underground tuber.
ga: Atomɔ ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo. Hulu la haa hewalɛ kɛha niyenii feemɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli, ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather gets too hot, when watering is uneven, or when there is a lack of bees and insects to pollinate the flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii koni amɛwo yibii lɛ faaa.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains and high humidity encourage Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet conditions, especially when air cannot flow freely through crowded branches.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ blackpod hela baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli oya.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy bunches, especially if underground pests like nematodes or stem borers have damaged the roots and stem base.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi jwɛi ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ fite shishifãi kɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants wilting and turning yellow when the heat gets strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight. High heat causes them to lose water faster than their roots can absorb it, leading to wilting and leaf damage if they do not have enough shade cover.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ baai lɛ afitemɔ baa kɛji hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ.

english: How does extreme sun exposure affect my cocoa pods while they are growing?
ga: Te hulu la ni naa wa lɛ saa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Excessive sunlight and heat stress can cause cocoa trees to drop young pods prematurely to save water, resulting in smaller harvests and sun-damaged pods.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛ dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha cacao tsei lɛ ajie amɛbii bibii lɛ ashwie shi oya koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni hulu la lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How does planting shade trees help keep the soil around my crops cool during dry hot days?
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ amli?

english: Shade trees block direct sunlight from hitting the ground, which reduces soil evaporation, lowers ground temperature, and keeps soil moisture available longer for crop roots.
ga: Tsei tsiɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i baa shi kɛha tsei shishifãi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Can I use a solar-powered pump to water my cocoa farm during the dry season?
