ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ hulutsoo be mli pɔmp aha mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Yes, solar-powered pumps use free sunlight to draw water from rivers or boreholes to irrigate your farm, helping you keep your crops hydrated during dry months without spending money on fuel.
ga: Hɛɛ, pɔmpii ni akɛ hulu hewalɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛgbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ faai loo nubui amli kɛshwieɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nu. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli ni ofiteee shika yɛ fuɛl he.

english: Why do my crops dry out much faster around March compared to other times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kwraa yɛ March mli lɛ? kɛ akɛto afi lɛ mli bei krokomɛi ahe

english: In Ghana, March falls near the end of the dry season when the sun is particularly intense and ground water reserves are low, causing the soil and crops to lose moisture very quickly.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, March baagbee shi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ miihe aba naagbee lɛ. Enɛ ji be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa titri, ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ hu faaa. Enɛ haa sũ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya.

english: Is it bad to water my crops in the middle of the day when the sun is burning hot?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ mawo midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ gbi teŋ be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Yes, watering under direct hot sunlight causes rapid evaporation so water doesn't reach the roots efficiently, and water droplets on leaves can magnify sunlight and cause leaves to burn. It is best to water early in the morning or late afternoon.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa hulutsoo baa oya. No hewɔ lɛ nu nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ. Ni nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha baai lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ afɔse nu lɛ leebi loo shwane mli.

english: Why do so many cocoa farms in our area mature and get ready for harvest at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji babaoo ni yɔɔ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ edara ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees respond to seasonal weather patterns like rainfall and temperature changes across the region, causing trees planted under similar conditions to flower and bear mature pods around the same months.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ tsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ be kɛ bei amli tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ latsaa tsakemɔi yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ ahe nii. Enɛ haa tsei ni akwɛ̃ yɛ shihilɛi ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ mli lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni eda yɛ nyɔŋ kome mli.

english: How can I tell that my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods change color when ripe; green pods turn to a vibrant yellow, while red or purple pods turn to an orange-yellow color. Ripe pods also make a hollow sound when tapped gently.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tsuru loo purple lɛ feɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Yibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu feɔ gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ fioo.

english: Why are some of my cocoa trees producing many pods while neighboring trees yield very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Yield differences are usually caused by variations in soil nutrients, tree age, sunlight exposure, proper pruning, and how well pest and disease infections are managed on each tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli nibii ni tsakeɔ lɛ kɛ srɔtofeemɔi ni baa yibiiwoo mli lɛ baa. Tso lɛ afii, hulu la, ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi anɔ lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ amɛhaa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown or black while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and excessive dampness, causing pods to rot before they fully mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fe nine. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your maize plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient needed for healthy growth. Rain often washes nitrogen out of the upper soil, so applying compost, well-rotted manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps feed the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ Nugbɔ lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he shwiemɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aná niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by these insects. Spraying neem oil or soapy water early can help keep these pests under control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ ŋmeii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwieɔ nɔ mra Amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines spread all over the soil but produce very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen (often from excessive fertilizer or rich manure), sweet potato plants focus all their energy on growing thick leaves and long vines instead of storing nutrients below ground in the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ (Bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli.) Sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni mli tse kɛ wain tsei kakadaji ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami ɔ kɛ toɔ zugba a sisi ngɛ tso ɔ mi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, extreme dry spells, or irregular watering. Maintaining steady moisture in the soil with mulching helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ, hɔmɔ ni naa wa, loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ mulching tsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their small green pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? lots dani etsɔ agbo

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra young pods (a process called cherelle wilt) if they do not have enough water, sunlight, or soil nutrients to support all of them to maturity.
ga: Cacao tso lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. (nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherry wilt) kɛji amɛbɛ nu, hulu la loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaye abua amɛ kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Why do my bean plants grow big green foliage but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes produce their own nitrogen from the air through their roots. Giving them additional nitrogen fertilizer causes them to put all their energy into leaves rather than flowers and seed pods.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Ejieɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ e-nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ haa amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ashishifãi najiaŋ

english: Why do my okra pods become hard and tough to cut instead of soft and good for cooking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ wa ni ewa akɛ aaakpa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee blɛoo ni sa kɛha nihoomɔ lɛ?

english: Okra pods grow rapidly and become woody and fibrous if left on the plant too long after flowering. Harvesting the pods every few days while they are still young and tender keeps them soft and encourages the plant to make more.
ga: Roselle ŋmeii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ. Pod fɛɛ pod ni oookpa Gbii fioo komɛi ni eyɛ gbekɛ lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaha pod lɛ afee blɛoo ni ewo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni efee babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest under the ground without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava shows it is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, the main stem turns woody, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open as the tubers swell.
ga: Yucca jieɔ bɔ ni eda lɛ kpo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Tso titri lɛ tsɔɔ tso. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my new plantain suckers dry up and die shortly after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei heei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni midu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers often fail to grow if their root base (corm) was damaged during removal, planted in dry soil without shade, or infected with tiny worms called nematodes that prevent the sucker from drinking water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ ada kɛji amɛshishifã (tuber) lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ. Aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni hulutsoo bɛ nɔ. aloo ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ahe Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes ni tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekanu nu ni enu nu.

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil to feed the maize, while their broad leaves cover the ground to shade out weeds and trap moisture in the earth.
ga: Cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What do people mean when they talk about 'September maize', and when should I plant to harvest around that time?
ga: Mɛni gbɔmɛi tsɔɔ kɛ́ amɛmiiwie ‘September ŋmãa’ he? Ni mɛɛ be esa akɛ odu nii kɛha nikpamɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli?

english: In Ghana, 'September maize' refers to maize planted during the minor rainy season (usually around July or August in the southern belt) so that it matures for harvest in September. Planting with the start of these minor rains ensures the crop gets water while growing and dry weather when ripening.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, ‘September ŋmãa’ tsɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli. (Be pii lɛ, aaafee July loo August yɛ Anaigbɛ) koni akɛha ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ koni akpa yɛ September mli. Dumɔ ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa nu be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli nu hu baa kɛji amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain can waterlog the soil and wash away nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green. Waterlogged soil also starves the roots of air, preventing the plant from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha nu afee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ nitrogen ajɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehiɛ eŋɔli. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ hu haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: How many months does it usually take for maize to be ready for harvest after I plant it?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmãa feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most maize varieties grown in Ghana mature in 3 to 4 months (90 to 120 days). Early-maturing varieties can be ready in about 75 to 85 days, while late varieties take longer.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli (gbii 90 kɛyashi 120). Nɔ ni shwereɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ yɛ aaafee gbii 75 kɛyashi 85 mli, yɛ be mli ni nɔ ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo.

english: I want to try growing cotton; how does a cotton plant grow compared to food crops like maize?
ga: Miisumɔ ni maka cotton dumɔ makwɛ. Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa kɛ akɛto niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa he?

english: Cotton grows as a small shrub rather than a tall grass like maize. Instead of producing cobs, it forms green pods called bolls that eventually split open to reveal white fluffy cotton fibers.
ga: Cottonwood daa akɛ tso bibioo ko yɛ jwɛi kakadaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmãa najiaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee cob lɛ Efeɔ ŋmeii eŋɔli ni atsɛɔ amɛ bɔɔlu. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ efoɔ koni ejie tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kpo.

english: How will I know that my cotton crop is mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cotton tsei lɛ edara ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Cotton is ready for picking when the green bolls dry out, crack open, and expose clean, fluffy white cotton. You should harvest it during dry sunny weather to keep the fiber clean and dry.
ga: Odonti lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji ŋmeii eŋɔli lɛ egbi, amɛgbala, ni amɛjie odonti yɛŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni he tse lɛ kpo. Esa akɛ okpa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ŋmeii lɛ ahe atse ni amɛgbi.

english: Does cotton need as much rain as maize, or can it handle dry spells better?
ga: Ani nugbɔ babaoo he miihia cotton tamɔ ŋmãa? Aloo ebaanyɛ edamɔ hɔmɔ bei anaa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cotton has a deep taproot that allows it to tolerate dry spells better than maize once established. While it needs rain during early growth, it actually prefers dry conditions when the cotton bolls open.
ga: Odonti yɛ shishifã ni mli kwɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi anaa jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa ni ato ama shi lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ he miihia lɛ yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ moŋ, shi yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, esumɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛji ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fã pɛ.

english: Why do my maize cobs end up small with many missing kernels inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ ji bibii ni ŋmãa babaoo elaaje mli lɛ?

english: Missing kernels usually happen because of poor pollination, which occurs if the maize suffers from severe heat or drought right when the silks and tassels are forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa yɛ pollination ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa ba ŋmãa lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni siliki kɛ ŋmãa lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Why do my crops start flowering when they are still very short and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi fɔfɔi be mli ni amɛji kukuji ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: When crops face extreme stress—such as a sudden lack of water or poor soil—they panic and flower early to produce seeds before they die, even if they haven't grown to full size.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ haomɔi ni naa wa kpe, tamɔ nu ni bɛ trukaa loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ, Amɛsheɔ gbeyei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi mra koni amɛwo dumɔwui dani amɛgboi. Kɛ́ amɛdarako kwraa po.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or get full of insects soon after I store it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ loo eyiɔ obɔ kɛ kooloi bibii kɛji mikpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize spoils or attracts insects like weevils if it is stored before being thoroughly dried. High moisture inside the grain allows mold to grow and creates ideal conditions for pests to multiply.
ga: Abɛi baafite loo ebaagbala kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ akɛto dani egbi. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together in the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows fast and is harvested within four months, leaving the slow-growing cassava to take over the field and mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji ejwɛ mli. Ha ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate intense, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a soft canopy that lowers soil temperature and holds moisture, giving young cocoa the protection it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa abuɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my healthy cocoa tree when I want it to give me more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ? Be mli ni oosumɔ ni oná pods babaoo

english: Pruning removes unnecessary inner branches and suckers that steal food from the tree. Opening up the tree allows sunlight and air to reach the trunk, which encourages healthy flower growth and prevents moisture from staying trapped and causing pod decay.
ga: Tso lɛ mli niji kɛ ŋmeii ni juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ. Tso lɛ ni agbeleɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ daraa waa ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akabote mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn completely black and soft while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ kwraa beni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, dark environments with poor air movement. Regularly removing diseased pods from the farm and trimming low branches helps keep the air dry enough to stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, duŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ aya jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli daa kɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe tseee ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper distance ensures its roots can spread freely and its leaves get enough light to produce high crop yields.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛhe. Tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni aaaha ehi shi yɛ he ko ni sa lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa. Ni tsei lɛ baai lɛ baaná la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my plant leaves are turning yellow because of poor soil or from a lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo nu ni bɛ hewɔ?

english: Water stress causes leaves to wilt, curl, and feel dry during the day, while nutrient shortages usually cause older leaves to turn yellow gradually while the stem stays soft. Adding organic manure or local fertilizer restores missing nutrients to bring back green growth.
ga: Nu he haomɔ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe egbi yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ daa fiofio. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo. Kɛ́ akɛ organic loo maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How do weeds harm my crop when they are just growing on the ground next to my trees?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on the farm by taking away water, fertilizer, and soil nutrients meant for your crop. Clearing weeds around the base of your plants ensures all available soil food goes directly into feeding your crop.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ okɛbaatsu nii lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ yaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree bring out many flowers, but most of them fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ pods?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant experiences sudden heat stress, severe dry spells, or insect damage during the flowering stage. Keeping soil covered with organic matter and managing pests early keeps the tree calm so flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ trukaa. Gbimɔ ni naa wa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui mra lɛ baaha tso lɛ afee kpoo No sɛɛ lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ bafeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do pests like capsids cause more damage to my cocoa leaves and young shoots right after the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids lɛ fiteɔ mi-cocoa baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Capsid bugs thrive in warm weather and love to feed on the tender new leaves and shoots that grow right after rain. Checking your farm early for damaged shoots allows you to spray recommended treatments before the bugs spread across the whole farm.
ga: Capsid kooloi lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ. Ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛye baai kɛ ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Bɔni afee ni ona ŋmeii ni efite lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How does spreading dry leaves around the base of my crops help them grow better?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he Te mi tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tso lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry leaves or plant material, called mulching, acts as a blanket over the soil. It stops the sun from drying out the ground quickly, keeps plant roots cool during hot days, and slowly breaks down into rich plant food.
ga: Baai ni egbi loo tso mli nibii ni agbɛɔ ashwãa ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ baatsu nii akɛ mulching blanket. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, ni fiofio lɛ, ejaraa mli etsɔɔ tsei niyenii ni jara wa.

english: Is it safe for my soil if I plant heavy crops like cassava on the exact same land every single year?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests built up in that crop to remain in the ground. Rotating different crops or letting the land rest allows the soil to rebuild its strength for future planting.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ebua amɛhe naa yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Aloo, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ atswa ehewalɛ ema shi ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does it take a few years for my new cocoa trees to start producing pods after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso hee lɛ heɔ afii fioo komɛi dani ebɔi ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tree crops like cocoa spend their early years developing strong root systems and sturdy trunks to store energy before they are mature enough to flower and carry heavy pods.
ga: Tsei tamɔ kookoo yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Koni afee shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ tsei ni mli wa ni akɛto hewalɛ dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛná ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: How do I know if my farmland has the right soil for planting permanent trees like cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha tsei ni hiɔ shi daa tamɔ kookoo?

english: Cocoa trees need deep, rich, well-drained soil that holds moisture well without getting waterlogged, allowing their long taproots to drink water even during dry periods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia kokoo tsei. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli Enɛ haa taproot kakadaŋŋ lɛ nyɛɔ enuɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli po.

english: Why do some of the tiny young cocoa pods on my tree turn black and shrivel up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mitsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often cherelle wilt, a natural process where the tree sheds extra pods it cannot feed due to a lack of water, nutrients, or sunlight, though it can also be caused by insect pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni tsei yɔɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye yɛ nu, niyenii, loo hulu la ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ, eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ ŋmeii hu kɛbaa moŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow and flower so quickly right after the main rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rainwater dissolves plant food in the soil so root systems can easily absorb it, which triggers fast stem growth and encourages the crop to produce flowers.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ oya. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adara oya ni ewo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi.

english: What happens to my tree crops when the rains stop and the dry season lasts too long?
ga: Mɛni baa mi tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ tsɔ?

english: During long dry spells, trees shed their leaves to reduce water loss and protect their main stems, temporarily halting fruit production until rainfall resumes.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he. Amɛbaakpa aduawai afeemɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is cocoa plentiful in the market during certain months but completely absent at other times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fa babaoo yɛ jara nɔ yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli, shi ebɛ kwraa yɛ afi lɛ mli bei krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods follow seasonal flowering and fruiting cycles tied to regional rainfall, leading to a major harvest period followed by off-season months where very little crop matures.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ nyiɛɔ be mli fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo ni kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ falɛ yɔɔ tsakpaa lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ hiɛ kɛyaa ŋmaakpamɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji nyɔji ni be ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ fioo pɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: How can I earn money from my farm while I wait several years for my newly planted trees to yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ tsei heei ni adu lɛ afii babaoo koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can practice intercropping by planting fast-growing crops like plantains, cassava, or maize between the young tree rows to harvest food and sales income in the short term.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ intercropping atsu nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains, cassava, loo ŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ tsei bibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ koni okpa niyenii ni oná jarayeli ni heɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to hire extra farm hands during crop harvest when I managed planting alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi krokomɛi yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli be mli ni mikome too miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops like cocoa requires intensive manual work—plucking pods, splitting them, and gathering beans—that must be completed rapidly before pods rot on the tree.
ga: Nibii ni akpãa tamɔ kookoo lɛ biɔ ni akɛ niji atsu nii waa, tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ atsemɔ, dumɔwui lɛ amli gbalamɔ, kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anaabuamɔ. Esa akɛ afee enɛ oya dani ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I tell when my tree crops are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mitsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Most tree crops show clear visual changes when ripe, such as cocoa pods changing color from green or red to a bright yellow or orange.
ga: Tsei pii jieɔ tsakemɔi ni kadiɔ mɔ kpo beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ, tamɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse nɔ.

english: Why must I ferment and dry my cocoa beans carefully before taking them to the buying shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ mi-kookoo lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni mahã egbi dani mikɛya shwapo ni akɛheɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Proper fermentation and drying remove moisture so the beans do not mold, while developing the rich chocolate flavor needed to fetch good market prices.
ga: Kɛ́ afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ ni egbi lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ená tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni he hiaa koni anyɛ ana jara kpakpa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do small insects seem to attack my crops right when they are mature and almost ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji amɛdara kwraa ni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ pɛ?

english: As crops mature, they become sweeter, softer, and more nutritious, which naturally attracts insects looking for an easy food source just before you harvest them.
ga: Beni tso lɛ daa lɛ, ebafeɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ, nɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii ni miitao niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛbaa amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa. dani obaakpa nii

english: Why are tiny insects gathering on the flowers of my crops, and will this hurt my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afɔfɔi anɔ lɛ? Ni ani enɛ baaná bɔ ni mitsuɔ nii ehaa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Insects are drawn to flowers for their sweet nectar. However, if they destroy the flowers, the crop cannot form fruit or seeds, which greatly reduces your total harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii sumɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛtao fɔfɔi amli nu. Shi, kɛji amɛfite fɔfɔi lɛ, Crops nyɛŋ awo yibii loo dumɔwui. Enɛ baaha onitsumɔ fɛɛ ni otsuɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do insects appear on my farm only at specific times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects follow natural breeding cycles that depend on weather, rain, and heat. They tend to multiply rapidly when conditions match the time your crops are producing food.
ga: Kplukai nyiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, nugbɔ, kɛ dɔlɛ nɔ. Amɛfɔɔ shweremɔ oya kɛji shihilɛi kɛ be mli ni otsei lɛ miiwo niyenii lɛ kpã gbee.

english: How can I tell if insects are starting to spoil my crop before the whole field gets damaged?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miibɔi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afitemɔ dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ efite?

english: You can spot early pest attacks by regularly inspecting the undersides of leaves, young flowers, and stems for small bugs, tiny holes, or sticky residue.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ mra kɛtsɔ baai, fɔfɔi bibii, kɛ tsei lɛ ashishi ni oookwɛ daa lɛ nɔ. Koni ana kooloi bibii, buji bibii, loo nibii ni eshwɛ ni shwieɔ shi

english: What is the best way to protect my plant flowers from being destroyed by bugs?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mabu mitso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni kooloi akafite amɛ?

english: You can protect flowers by using the correct, safe pest control methods recommended by agricultural experts, and by keeping the farm clear of weeds where bugs like to hide.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu ofɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni ja ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni okwaayeli he nilelɔi kɛhaa lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni haa kooloi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ ni abaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli akafee nɔ ko lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my crops to rot or spoil so quickly in the field right before I pick them?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛfiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikpaa amɛ?

english: Spoilage often happens when insects bite into the plant tissues, creating open wounds that allow rot, bacteria, and fungi to enter and decay the crop quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fitemɔ baa kɛji kooloi ŋmɔ tso lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa pilamɔi ni agbele naa ni haa ŋmeii, helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Do different types of insects attack different parts of my crop like the leaves versus the flowers?
ga: Kplukai srɔtoi tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fãi srɔtoi, tamɔ baai kɛ fɔfɔii?

english: Yes, some insects specialize in biting soft leaves, while others prefer sweet flowers or fruit, which means you may need specific control methods depending on which part is attacked.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii komɛi he esa waa yɛ baai bibii ni amɛyeɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi sumɔɔ fɔfɔi loo aduawai ni ŋɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ gbɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ nii lɛ atsu nii. Edamɔ fã ni atutuaa lɛ nɔ.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me keep my crops from spoiling?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi koni miŋmɔshi nibii akafite lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Extension officers are trained to identify specific pests, teach you the right timing for pest control, and share proven techniques to keep your farm healthy and yield high.
ga: Atsɔɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ koni amɛyoo kooloi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Tsɔɔmɔ be ni sa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ. ni okɛ ŋaai ni ana he odaseyeli ni baaha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii lɛ aha.

english: If insect pests attack my flowering crops, will the plants recover on their own without my help?
ga: Kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tutua mi tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Ani tso lɛ baatsa ehe kɛji miyeee mibuaaa lɛ?

english: Crops rarely recover from heavy pest attacks on their own. Without proper action, insects can destroy the flowers and ruin the entire crop before you can harvest.
ga: Ewa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aná hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa ko ni baa lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛji akɛ nifeemɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ afite fɔfɔii ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Is it safe to spray my crops when they are full of flowers?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ beni fɔfɔii eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: You must be careful when spraying flowering crops. Applying the wrong product or spraying at the wrong time of day can damage the blossoms or drive away helpful insects like bees that help your crops produce fruit.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ oofɔ fɔfɔi tsei anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni ejaaa tsu nii loo okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite fɔfɔii loo eshwie kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when I leave tall weeds around them instead of clearing them with a slasher?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle mihe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaajie jwɛi kɛtsɔ slash gbɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds removes this competition, allowing your crops to absorb the food and moisture they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to burn the bushes on my farm or clear them using a slasher?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo mikɛ slashers baatsu nii?

english: Clearing with a slasher is better for soil health because burning destroys beneficial soil organisms and organic matter. Leaving slashed plant material on the ground acts as mulch, which traps moisture and returns nutrients to the soil.
ga: Kɛ akɛ tsɔne tswa shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ejaakɛ shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ mli nibii ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow and roll up during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up and turn yellow to conserve water and protect themselves from heat stress. When dry soil lacks water, the plant cannot transport necessary nutrients like nitrogen up into its leaves.
ga: Abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni nu bɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen aya ŋwɛi kɛya baai lɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as intense heat, lack of water, or low soil nutrients like phosphorus. Proper watering and nutrient management encourage the flowers to set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni faaa. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted directly under open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni mli tse lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense heat. They require shade trees or temporary nurse plants like plantains to shelter them from the sun until their roots and canopies are established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛɔ amɛ nɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsi hulu lɛ naa kɛyashi shishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ baaje shishi.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers if I plant the stems too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting cassava stems too close forces the roots to fight for limited space and soil nutrients underground. This results in thin stems and small, low-yielding tubers instead of large, heavy roots.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná he ko ni faaa kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ bulbs bibii ni woɔ yibii fioo lɛ baa yɛ shishifãi wuji ni tsii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow bushy leaves but produce very small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai akui shi aduawai bibii waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes tomato plants to put all their energy into leaf growth rather than fruit development. Pruning excess branches and balancing soil nutrients encourages bigger fruit growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he nii moŋ fe aduawai lɛ adalɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden egg plants curling and covered in tiny green bugs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by sap-sucking insects like aphids. As they feed on the underside of the leaves, they drain the plant's nutrients and leave behind damage that distorts leaf growth.
ga: Koolooi ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ aphids, kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi, be mli ni amɛyeɔ baa lɛ shishi. Ehaa tso lɛ mli niyenii kpakpai lɛ hoɔ ni eshiɔ nibii ni efiteɔ ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my yam leaves during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dark spots on leaves during wet weather are usually fungal infections triggered by high air humidity and trapped water. Spacing plants properly improves airflow and helps leaves dry faster, reducing fungal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ nu ni emɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa. He ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ gĩɔ oya. Ha fungal lɛ dalɛ aba shi

english: Why does my cassava become hard and woody if I leave it in the ground too long after it matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni efeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava reaches full maturity, the plant converts starch back into tough plant fibers. Over-mature roots become woody, lose their soft texture, and become difficult to process or sell.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ ekoŋŋ etsɔɔ tso mli ŋmei ni mli wa. Shishifãi ni eda lɛ bafeɔ tsei. Nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ ni ewa akɛ aaatsu he nii loo ahɔ̃ɔ

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout if I plant them when the soil is too dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds need moisture to wake up and start growing. If the soil is dry, the seed stays dormant or dries up and dies underground before its roots can stretch out.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baakã he amɛhi shi. Aloo egbiɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkpãa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is rich enough for planting maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa?

english: Good soil for maize feels moist, crumbles easily in your hand, and is dark in color. If the soil is pale, stony, or too sandy, your maize roots will struggle to find enough food and water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha ŋmãa lɛ baanu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Egbeeɔ nine mli oya ni ehiɛ su ji ediŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, tɛi, loo ŋã tsɔ. Abɛi shishifãi lɛ baaná naagba yɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is sitting around the roots for too long. Adding organic manure or fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. Aloo nu ko ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by intense heat, uneven watering, or poor soil nutrients. Without steady water and shade from extreme sun, the plant sheds flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji nu kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ bɛ daa lɛ, Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop during hot afternoons even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Cassava plants temporarily droop or curl their leaves during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing water. They will naturally stand back up once the sun goes down and temperature cools.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli loo amɛbaabɔle amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu akafite. Amɛbaadamɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my maize is fully mature and ready to pick from the field?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves and outer husks turn brown and dry, and a small black layer appears at the bottom of the kernel when you scrape it off the cob.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ. kɛ fã bibioo ko ni ji ediŋŋ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi kɛji okɛ amɛ shwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does drying my harvested maize directly on bare dirt ruin the grain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ ni migbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Drying maize directly on bare ground picks up dirt, insects, and moisture from the soil. This introduces mold spores that spoil your cobs and lower the quality of your harvest.
ga: Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shwieɔ muji, kooloi bibii, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ o-cob lɛ baa ni ehaa okpamɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does mold grow on my maize if I store it in bags right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji mikɛwo kotokui amli beni akpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain still holds moisture inside. If you pack it into bags immediately, the trapped water creates damp heat, which causes green or black mold to grow quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli lolo. Kɛji okɛwo kotoku mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ Nu ni emɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni ji eŋɔli loo ediŋŋ lɛ daa oya.

english: Why do small insects turn my stored maize into white powder after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tsakeɔ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ powda yɛŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils attack maize if the grain was not dried completely or if the storage bags were dirty. Keeping grains dry and stored in clean, tightly sealed containers stops insects from damaging them.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii baatutua ŋmãa kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa loo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ mli ewo muji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmaa lɛ wo tsɛnsi ni mli tse ni atsĩ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite.

english: How does separating broken or discolored grains help me sell my maize for a better price?
ga: Te ŋmeii ni ekumɔ loo amɛhe su etsake lɛ mligbalamɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mahɔ̃ɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Buyers pay more for clean, uniform grains because bad or broken grains rot quickly and attract pests. Sorting out bad grains makes your whole supply look attractive, clean, and healthy to buyers.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛha dumɔwui ni he tse ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni efite loo ni ekumɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya ni egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Nibii ni ehiii ni ooohala lɛ baaha onibii fɛɛ ni okɛhaa lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo, nɔ ni he tse, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if an agrochemical I buy at the market is officially certified for my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ agrochemicals ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni amralo lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ akɛ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii?

english: Certified chemicals have approved regulatory labels (such as COCOBOD or EPA approvals in Ghana) clearly printed on the container, including batch numbers, active ingredients, and English/local usage instructions. Licensed agro-dealers sold these authentic products, whereas fake ones often lack proper seals or clear labels.
ga: Tsofai ni awo he hewalɛ lɛ yɛ mla naa hegbɛ he woji (tamɔ COCOBOD loo EPA hegbɛ yɛ Ghana) ni akala yɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ faŋŋ. Nɔ ni fata he ji batch yibɔ, nibii ni tsuɔ nii kɛ Blɔfo/maŋ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ nitsumɔ he. Okwaayeli nibii ajalɔi ni yɔɔ gbɛŋmɛɛ wolo lɛ hɔ̃ɔ nɛkɛ nibii diɛŋtsɛ nɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ amalei lɛ bɛ stamp ni sa loo niŋmaa ni yɔɔ faŋŋ.

english: Can I mix my weedkiller and insect spray together in the same tank to save time when spraying my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ afutu tanki kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Mixing unapproved combinations of chemicals can ruin their effectiveness, burn your crop leaves, or create toxic reactions. You should only combine specific chemicals if the manufacturer's label or an agricultural extension officer explicitly confirms they are compatible.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ he lɛ baanyɛ afite bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ. Shãa otso lɛ baai lɛ loo feemɔ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ gbeyei. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai komɛi afata he pɛ kɛji akɛ tsofafeelɔ lɛ wolo loo okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ ma nɔ mi faŋŋ akɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee.

english: It is best to spray early in the morning (before 9 AM) or late in the afternoon. High midday sun evaporates the chemical too quickly before plants absorb it, and hot weather combined with strong wind can cause the chemical drift to burn healthy crop parts or waste your input.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi (dani 9:00 a.m.) loo shwane mli. Hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya tsɔ dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fata he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ni hoɔ yɛ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ loo eha nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ afite.

english: What will happen to my cassava crop if I use more spray chemical than the bottle instructions recommend?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii babaoo fe gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ tɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Using more chemical than instructed will not kill pests faster; instead, it can burn the plant's leaves, poison the soil, waste your money, and cause pests to build resistance to the chemical over time.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ egbeŋ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ oya. Shi ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã. Ehaa sũ lɛ fiteɔ, efiteɔ shika, ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ tsofai lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsofai lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or it is suffering from root damage caused by waterlogging or pests like the Fall Armyworm. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or applying approved pest control helps restore leaf greenness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo amɛshishifãi efite yɛ nu ni hoɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet, and humid conditions. Pruning shade branches to let in sunlight, weeding around the trunks, and spraying certified copper-based fungicides early in the season protects the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fɔ̃ɔ ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo Fɔlɔmɔ tsei ni haa hulu la lɛ abote mli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ahe ni akɛ tsofa ni akɔɔble yɔɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying even though the soil is wet with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt or root rot fungus in the soil. When roots rot from infected or overcrowded soil, they can no longer transport water up into the plant stems, causing the plant to wilt even in wet soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsu nu kɛya tso lɛ shishi dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei gboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: Flower drop occurs when plants face heat stress, uneven watering, or attack by tiny pests like thrips. Keeping the soil evenly moist and protecting young flowers with approved crop protection sprays prevents flower loss.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa amɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ fɔfɔi bibii ahe ni akɛ tsofa ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ buɔ he lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantain trees planted right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu dumɔwu yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct tropical sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and provide living leaf umbrellas that supply necessary shade and moisture while the cocoa roots become established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwaa lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with thin stems but producing very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, they shade each other out and compete for sunlight. The plants spend all their energy growing tall stems to reach the sun instead of sending nutrients down to grow thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ tsei lɛ baaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmaa tsei ni kɛlɛ koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsu niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shi koni ekɛ bulbs ni mli tse lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive the harsh sun. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves, acting as temporary shade crops while providing extra food and income for your household while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai wuji. Etsuɔ nii akɛ tso ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa oshia lɛ náa niyenii kɛ shika kroko be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers so they grow well?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-plantain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Plantains should be spaced about 3 meters (10 feet) apart from each other. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and airflow, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ plantains lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10). Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: How do I choose the right plantain suckers from my field for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni sa kɛha dumɔ?

english: Look for maidenhead or sword suckers that have narrow, lance-like leaves and strong, thick bases. Avoid suckers with wide, broad leaves early on, as they produce weaker plants and smaller bunches.
ga: Taomɔ oblayoo bulbs loo klante ŋmɔji ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishi ni mli wa ni mli wa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe mra. Ejaakɛ ebaaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni efee ŋmeii bibii.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to plant plantains in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ Ghana?

english: The best time to plant plantains is at the beginning of the major rainy season, around April to May. This gives the young suckers enough soil moisture to establish strong root systems before the dry season.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Aaafee April kɛyashi May Enɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tso lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: It is normal for older, lower leaves to turn yellow and dry up as the plant directs energy to new growth and fruit. However, if upper leaves yellow early, it usually means your soil lacks nitrogen or moisture.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ baai ni edara kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi be mli ni tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ woɔ dalɛ hee kɛ yibii amli lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cut down small extra suckers growing around one main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fata he lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Plantain tso titri kome jeɔ kpo.

english: If too many suckers grow around one main plant, they fight for nutrients and water, resulting in smaller fruit bunches. Removing extra suckers leaves only 2 or 3 at different growth stages for a better yield.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ, Ebaatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ 2 loo 3 pɛ yɛ dalɛ fãi srɔtoi amli koni ená yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over during strong winds right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani akpaa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and top-heavy fruit bunches. You can prevent them from falling by propping up the fruiting trees using bamboo poles or sturdy wooden forks for support.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsiimɔ fe fɛɛ. Obaanyɛ otsi otso lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni wa ni okɛfiɔ aduawai tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: I have been weeding my farm manually with a cutlass for years, so why are my plantain yields still dropping?
ga: Mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ efo miŋmɔ lɛ mli afii babaoo nɛ. Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain yibiiwoo lɛ miiba shi lolo lɛ?

english: Frequent manual weeding close to the plant can damage the shallow roots of plantain trees. Using mulch—covering the soil with dry leaves—suppresses weeds naturally while protecting root systems from your cutlass.
ga: Nine ni akɛjieɔ jwɛi shii abɔ yɛ tsei ahe lɛ baanyɛ afite dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Mulch ni akɛtsuɔ nii—ni akɛ baai ni egboi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ—yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ o-daggers lɛ ahe.

english: How can I keep my farm soil fertile without spending too much money on chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ni mikɛ shika babaoo akawo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli?

english: You can build soil fertility naturally by leaving crop residues, such as cocoa husks or plantain leaves, to rot on the soil. Planting leguminous cover crops like beans also adds natural nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ oma adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ tamɔ kookoo ŋmɔji loo plantain baai ni oooshi lɛ nɔ. shwiemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ Legume ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do plantains behave during the dry harmattan season, and how can I protect them?
ga: Te plantains feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa?

english: During the harmattan, plantains slow down growth and lose leaves to conserve water. You can protect them by spreading a thick layer of dry organic mulch around the base of the stem to hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ Plantains lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni amɛbaafite amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni ooogbɛ ashwã nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebɔleɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if a piece of land is suitable for growing maize before I clear it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ko nɔ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔ dani mafo mli?

english: Dark, soft soil rich in decaying leaves holds moisture well and usually indicates fertile ground that will support strong maize roots and healthy leaves.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni baai ni fiteɔ eyi mli obɔ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni baaye abua ŋmãa shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted directly in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that shields the young trees from heat until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he kɛyashiɔ tsei lɛ daraa waa.

english: Why is it better to raise pepper seeds in a small nursery bed instead of sowing them directly on my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ? Ehi jogbaŋŋ moŋ akɛ mafolɔ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: A small nursery bed allows you to protect tiny seedlings from harsh weather, heavy rains, and pests in a manageable space, ensuring only healthy plants get moved to the main field.
ga: Nursery saatsoi bibii yeɔ ebua bo ni obuɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe. kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi gbohii, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ he ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ mli Enɛ baaha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ajie kɛya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves is a sign that your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for green leaf growth and large cob formation.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔlii adalɛ kɛ ŋmeii wuji afeemɔ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge lush leaves above ground but tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa agboi ni kwɛɔ daa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant puts all its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of storing food in its underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why do my plantain trees dry out so fast during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose moisture quickly and shallow roots that dry out easily. Covering the base of the plant with dry leaves or straw helps retain water in the soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants drop off without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or a lack of water, as the plant tries to save energy rather than produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pepper tso lɛ miitao ni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do some seeds I save from my previous harvest fail to sprout when planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their ability to sprout if stored improperly or if they come from hybrid plants that do not produce viable seeds for a second generation.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ baanyɛ afite nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he jogbaŋŋ loo kɛji akɛ amɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni nyɛɛɛ amɛwo dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii ahaa yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why does my land yield less crop when I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops grow so slowly and look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, stealing light, water, and soil nutrients that your young crops need to grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my newly planted cocoa seedlings die or stop growing soon after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ gboiɔ loo amɛkpaa dalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that easily dry out under harsh sunlight or in poor soil. They need temporary shade, adequate water, and well-prepared soil to establish their roots safely during the first year.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, nu babaoo, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ koni amɛshishifãi ama shi shweshweeshwe yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli.

english: How do I choose the right cocoa variety to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala kookoo henɔ ni sa ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Different cocoa varieties have different strengths, such as high pod yields, faster maturity, or resistance to diseases like Black Pod. Extension officers recommend improved hybrid varieties that match your local rainfall and soil conditions for the best harvest.
ga: Cocoa henɔi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ hewalɛi srɔtoi, tamɔ ŋmeii ni fa babaoo, ŋmeii ni shwereɔ oya, loo helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii diji. Mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee lɛ he ŋaa koni aná ŋmaa ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young crops wither and dry up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crops have short root systems that cannot reach deep underground water. Without shade plants like plantains or shade trees to reduce direct heat and protect the soil moisture, the hot sun rapidly dries out the seedlings.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa koni ekɛba dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ oya.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa plants when setting up a new farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafo mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ miito ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Spacing cocoa plants properly—usually about 3 meters by 3 meters—gives each tree enough room for its roots to gather soil nutrients and its leaves to catch sunlight without competing with neighboring trees.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei ateŋ—bei pii lɛ, aaafee mitai 3 kɛ mitai 3—haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ abua niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anaa, ni ebaa lɛ hu aná hulu la ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings on an old farm site where old trees were recently cut down?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ ŋmɔ shikpɔŋ momo ni afo tsei momoi yɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ nɔ?

english: Replanting on old farm sites can be difficult because the soil nutrients may be exhausted and old crop diseases might remain in the ground. The soil often needs time to rest, along with organic fertilizer or manure, to regain its fertility before new seedlings will grow well.
ga: Okwaafoi ashikpɔŋ momo ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni wa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baanyɛ afite ni tsei ahe helai momo lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ he hiaa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he Koni aku sɛɛ aba babaoo mli dani dumɔwui heei adara jogbaŋŋ

english: Does burning the bush before planting help my crops grow better or does it ruin the soil?
ga: Ani mi jwɛi lɛ ni mikɛshãa dani miduɔ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ loo ebaaye shikpɔŋ lɛ awui?

english: While burning clears the land quickly, it destroys beneficial soil microbes, burns off organic plant matter, and leaves the soil dry and exposed to erosion. Clearing without burning keeps the soil richer and moister for your young crops.
ga: yɛ be mli ni la ni ashãa lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Metabolize organic plants ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni efite Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ashãaa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young plants turning yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is missing important nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil around the roots has too much standing water, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛmu niyenii.

english: Why do heavy weeds cause my crops to produce small fruits and grow slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni tsii lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii bibii ni amɛdaraa blɛoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on the farm—they aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight away from your crops, leaving the main plants starved and unable to grow strong or yield big fruits.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ ŋmɔ mli Amɛjuɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ni enyɛɛɛ eda waa loo ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why is it necessary to trim small unwanted branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Namɔ sumɔɔɔ ni eshiɔ kookoo tso lɛ?

english: Trimming or pruning removes weak and useless branches so the tree can direct its energy into growing healthy stems and developing cocoa pods. It also allows air and sunlight to pass through the tree, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ afo loo afo lɛ, ejieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ hewalɛ ama tsei akutsei ni wa ni amɛfee kookoo ŋmeii. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la hu tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: What causes my small cocoa pods to turn black and rot before they get big?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo dani eda.

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, overly shaded, and humid conditions. Pruning dense branches to let in sunlight and spraying recommended fungicides help protect young pods from rotting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ Shade babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo, ni afolɔ mli babaoo koni hulu la aba mli kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves turning brown and drying up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade from taller plants like plantains or shade trees because full, direct sunlight burns their sensitive leaves and dries out the soil moisture they need to grow.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni baaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa kookoo tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ni ehaa sũ mli nu ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli agbi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná gbɛ babaoo?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to weak, thin stalks and tiny cobs instead of a healthy harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose all their leaves to full sunlight, which helps the plant produce the energy needed to swell large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni amɛbaji lɛ fɛɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo bulb agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of a maize stalk usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni amɛma tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa.

english: Is dry chicken manure as good for my vegetables as chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei ni egbi lɛ hi kɛha mi aduawai lɛ tamɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ?

english: Yes, well-rotted chicken manure provides rich nutrients like nitrogen to your crops while also improving the soil's ability to hold water, making it very effective for vegetables.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo tamɔ nitrogen baa onibii amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa aduawai.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa baadu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and naturally put it back into the soil, which feeds the neighboring maize plants and improves soil fertility.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ

english: What causes holes in the center whorl of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn plant lɛ ring lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which crawl into the soft central leaves of the young corn plant to feed during the night or early morning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye nii gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upward and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground if I harvest them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain makes the soil waterlogged, starving the cassava roots of air and creating ideal conditions for soil fungus to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plants do not get regular water, causing the plant stress so it drops its blossoms to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ, ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores nutrients so the plant can grow healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a crop family that pulls natural nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally, helping your maize grow stronger without needing as much expensive artificial fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata tsei aweku ko ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua oŋmei lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa afee.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ?
