english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the ground during hot weather so you water less often, stops weeds from taking over, and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. koni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I clear all the shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ hulutsoo tsei fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and burn easily under the harsh direct sun. Keeping taller shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides living umbrellas that shield the young plants from direct heat until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ahã tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa tɛ̃ɛ he kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to make energy that grows big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil where they would rot or catch fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha egbo loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ aba enɔ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantain tsei titri lɛ ahe lɛ etee.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same food and water in the soil, resulting in small plantain bunches. Pruning extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoots, ensuring heavy and full bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Plantain muu lɛ fɛɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ, tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Akɛ nɔmimaa haa akɛ abaaná tsɔne ni tsii, ni eyi obɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by sudden hot dry weather, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: What is making holes in my young maize leaves and leaving sawdust-like dirt in the center shoots?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ bu ni amɛshiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that hides inside the central shoot of maize to feed on tender leaves. Spotting them early and applying proper biological or chemical treatments protects the growing point of the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ koni eye tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ ayɔse amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni sa ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Wrinkled and curling pepper leaves are caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the juices out of the leaves and spread plant sicknesses. Spraying neem oil or soapy water helps control these pests and lets new leaves grow normally.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli ni egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni eye ebua baa heei ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are fully ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, typically around 9 to 12 months after planting. You can also carefully dig around one stem to check if the tuber size meets your market needs before harvesting the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa tso lɛ he hu koni okwɛ kɛji tuber lɛ dalɛ kɛ nɔ ni jara lɛ taoɔ lɛ kpãa gbee dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Doc, why do my young cassava and fruit plants need protection when I first put them in the soil?
ga: Datrɛfonyo, mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni abu mi-cassava kɛ mi-dumɔwui lɛ ahe beni mikɛ amɛ duɔ shikpɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young plants are tender and vulnerable to harsh sunlight, strong winds, and heavy rain. Providing early protection or shade keeps the foliage cool and holds soil moisture until roots are strong enough to support full growth.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe oya. Hebuu loo hulutsoo mra he miihia. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua dalɛ ni yeɔ emuu.

english: How does planting plantain next to my young fruit trees protect them from dying?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ mi aduawai tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ abu amɛhe koni amɛkagboi?

english: Plantains grow rapidly with broad, heavy leaves that act as natural canopy shades. They shield young saplings from direct sun scorch and maintain a humid microclimate around the tender roots.
ga: Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsii ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Amɛbuɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ni mli edɔ lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe.

english: What happens to my young tree seedlings if I leave them exposed without any cover?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ ni mihaaa nɔ ko?

english: Unprotected saplings can suffer severe leaf burn, rapid soil dehydration, and stunted growth, often leading to a high death rate during hot or dry spells.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abuuu amɛhe lɛ baanyɛ ana baai shãa ni naa wa. Nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa gbele babaoo baa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa loo nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my young crops are getting enough protection from the sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi dumɔwui lɛ miiná hebuu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he?

english: Protected crops display vibrant green leaves without brown dried edges, show steady stem elongation, and do not wilt heavily during the hottest hours of the afternoon.
ga: Tsei ni abuɔ he lɛ baaná baai eŋɔli ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɛ amɛhe ni egbi. Tso lɛ mli lɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni egbooo waa yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Doc, what is the main benefit of growing 'prɛkɛ' seeds on my farm?
ga: Datrɛfonyo, mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ‘prɛkɛ’ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Prɛkɛ' (prekese) trees produce pod-like seeds that are highly valued as a aromatic cooking spice and traditional medicine, providing both household health benefits and strong market demand.
ga: Prɛkɛ’ (prekese) tso lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni tamɔ pod ni abuɔ waa akɛ tsofa ni akɛhooɔ nii ni ŋɔɔ kɛ blema tsofa. Ehaa shia hewalɛnamɔ he sɛɛ kɛ jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do some farmers add small pieces of prɛkɛ seeds when storing or cooking staple grains like corn and rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ prakse dumɔwui bibii fataa he lɛ? Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmaa ni he hiaa waa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa toɔ loo ahooɔ lɛ

english: Prɛkɛ seeds contain natural aromatic compounds that add favorable flavor to cooked grains and act as an organic pest deterrent when kept alongside stored food crops.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ yɛ prak dumɔwui amli ni haa dumɔwui ni ahoo lɛ feɔ fɛo. ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ akɛto niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ masɛi.

english: Is it profitable for me to sell harvested prɛkɛ seeds at the market, or should I save them all for home use?
ga: Ani maná sɛɛnamɔ kɛji mikɛ prakk dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ hɔ̃ɔ jara nɔ? Aloo esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ ato koni mikɛtsu nii yɛ shia?

english: It is best to do both; saving a portion provides your home with spice and medicinal uses, while selling the surplus at local markets offers a reliable source of supplemental cash flow.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofee enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Shika ni okɛto lɛ fã ko baaha oshia lɛ afee nɔ ni tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii. yɛ be mli ni nibii ni fa fe nine ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ haa anáa shika kroko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Why do food crops like cassava and plantain grow so well when planted together in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ plantain kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he kome yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Cassava and plantain draw nutrients from different soil depths and produce different canopy heights, making maximum use of sunlight and space while protecting the soil surface from erosion.
ga: Cassava kɛ plantain jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ srɔtoi amli ni amɛfeɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai srɔtoi. Kɛ hulu la kɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ he kɛjɛɔ shwiemɔ he.

english: Can I plant staple food crops like corn and rice alongside other seed crops on the same field?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Kɛfata dumɔwui krokomɛi ahe Ani ebaanyɛ ehi shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping staple grains with complementary plants can maximize land output and reduce pest risks, provided crops are spaced properly so they do not choke each other out for light and water.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii babaoo aba ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛji akɛ akɛ tsei lɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ. koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ la kɛ nu he

english: Why do tree crops take so much longer to yield good financial benefits compared to food crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani tsei woɔ shika he sɛɛ kpakpa lɛ? Kɛ akɛto niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei he

english: Trees spend their first few years developing deep root structures and heavy wood stems; though slow to start, mature trees yield continuous high-value harvests for decades without needing re-planting.
ga: Tso lɛ heɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani enáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni tsii. Eyɛ mli akɛ eje shishi blɛoo moŋ Shi tsei ni eda lɛ yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce better crops if I leave it unplanted for a season or two?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji mishi nɔ ni miduuu nii be kome loo enyɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving land unplanted, or letting it lie fallow, gives the soil time to rest and rebuild its natural nutrients, organic matter, and beneficial soil life so it can regain its strength for future planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ashiɔ ni aduuu nɔ ko loo nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ emaa shi. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: How can I tell if my farm land has lost its strength and needs a break?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ hewalɛ miiho ni ehe miihia ni mafo mli?

english: Signs of exhausted soil include stunted crop growth, yellowish leaves, soil that hardens into crusts after rain, and getting lower yields each season despite using good seeds.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite lɛ ahe ji tsei ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ akɛ dumɔwui kpakpai tsuɔ nii moŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield less every year when I keep planting the same field continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Be ni maya nɔ madu nii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Continuous planting drains specific nutrients from the soil faster than nature can replace them, depleting the land's energy and leaving crops weak.
ga: Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni adebɔɔ baanyɛ atsake amɛ. Ehaa hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Can I rely only on chemical fertilizers instead of letting my land rest, or does the soil still need natural recovery?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia adebɔɔ mli tsakemɔ lolo?

english: Chemical fertilizers offer a quick food boost for plants, but resting the land restores soil structure, water retention, and long-term organic health that artificial fertilizers cannot replace.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ kɛ niyenii woɔ tsei amli oya. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooohe ajɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ekoŋŋ. nu ni ahiɔ mli kɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli hewalɛnamɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ nyɛŋ atsake

english: Why is proper soil preparation so important before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Good soil preparation creates a strong foundation by loosening hard earth, allowing crop roots to easily expand, trap water, and feed on nutrients deep in the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ kpakpa haa shishitoo ni wa baa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya, amɛhiɛɔ nu mli, ni amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: What can I add to my field to help the soil hold water and regain its strength?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nɔ ko afata miŋmɔ lɛ he koni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Adding organic materials like compost, dried animal manure, or leaf litter acts like a natural sponge, helping the soil store moisture and releasing nutrients slowly to your crops.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi, loo baa mli jwɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ejieɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli fiofio.

english: How does covering bare ground with dry grass or leaves help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni mikɛhaa hei ni nɔ bɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering bare soil, or mulching, protects the ground from burning direct sunlight, keeps moisture in the dirt, and slowly breaks down into rich food for the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ ni oooha lɛ baaye abua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How does changing the types of crops I grow on my land keep the soil from wearing out?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsakemɔ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ akafite?

english: Different crops feed on different nutrients and attract different pests. Rotating crops prevents the soil from running out of specific nutrients and breaks the cycle of plant diseases.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ srɔtoi ni amɛgbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii komɛi ahi shi, ni efiteɔ tsei ahe helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ.

english: How do planting legumes like beans help bring my tired land back to life?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mitai lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Leguminous crops take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, acting as natural fertilizers that restore fertility to worn-out land.
ga: Legumes lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Does deep plowing help restore my soil's strength or can it hurt my farm land?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ loo ebaanyɛ eye miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ awui?

english: Light tilling loosens soil for roots, but plowing too deeply or frequently destroys beneficial soil life, dries out ground moisture, and weakens the land over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ nii fioo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛyaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ loo shii abɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbiɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How much water do my young pawpaw plants actually need when I first put them in the soil?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa mi-pawpaw tso bibioo lɛ beni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young pawpaw plants only need a small amount of water right after planting to help their roots settle. Giving them too much water at this early stage can rot their tender roots and destroy the seedling.
ga: Nu fioo pɛ he hiaa pawpaw tsei bibii lɛ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ koni eye ebua amɛshishifãi lɛ ni amɛwa. Nu ni fa babaoo yɛ shishijee mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi bibii lɛ agbo ni egbe dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my pawpaw trees wither and die when rainwater collects around their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pawpaw roots are very sensitive and need air to breathe. When water sits around the stem for too long, it drowns the roots and causes root rot, which quickly kills the tree.
ga: Pawpaw shishifãi lɛ waaa waa ni ehe hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi tso lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbo Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbo oya.

english: What kind of soil or land setup is best for planting pawpaws so water doesn't drown them?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha pawpaws ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkagbee nu mli?

english: Pawpaws grow best in well-drained soil, such as sandy loam, or on gentle slopes where excess rainwater can run off easily instead of forming standing puddles around the roots.
ga: Paw paws daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ ŋã nɔ. aloo yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ waa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ajɛ mli oya lɛ nɔ Moŋ lɛ, ehaa nu ŋmɔtɔ ko bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Should I build mounds for my pawpaw plants or plant them directly on flat ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matswa gɔŋ maha mipapaya tso lɛ loo madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Building raised mounds is often better, especially in rainy areas, because it elevates the base of the plant and prevents waterlogging around the root zone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaama gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ. Titri lɛ, yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ewoɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ nɔ, ni ehaaa nu akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How often should I water my pawpaw farm during the dry months?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo PawPaw Fam lɛ nu yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Instead of keeping the soil soaked every day, water them moderately two to three times a week. This provides enough moisture for survival without over-saturating the soil.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ daa gbi lɛ Ha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha wala ahi shi ni ehaaa sũ lɛ mli ajɔ fe nine.

english: What should I do to protect my newly planted crops if the rain suddenly stops for a few days?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu ehee lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ trukaa gbii babaoo?

english: If the rain halts right after planting, manually pour a light splash of water at the base of each seedling to keep the soil slightly damp so the young roots do not dry out and die.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Okɛ onine awo nu fioo ko nɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi. koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ fioo Koni shishifãi bibii lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: How do I know if my newly transplanted seedling has successfully taken root in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui heei ni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye omanye yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: A seedling has successfully taken root when it starts producing firm, fresh green leaves and stands strong when gently touched, showing that the roots are gripping the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui baanyɛ atswa shishifãi omanye kɛji amɛ bɔi baa ni wa, eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. Ni kɛ́ ata he fioo lɛ, edamɔ shi shiŋŋ, ni no tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miimɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Can giving my crops too much water cause harm even during hot weather?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ po mli?

english: Yes, excessive water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, which suffocates the roots and causes the leaves to turn yellow and drop off, even on hot sunny days.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ waa lɛ po nɔ

english: Why do some of my seedlings die within a few days of moving them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: This happens due to transplant shock, usually caused by root damage or roots drying out during the move. Watering the planting hole lightly helps the roots adjust quickly.
ga: Enɛ baa mli yɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ hewɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni efite loo shishifãi ni egbi yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ dumɔ bu lɛ mli blɛoo Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe oya.

english: How can I tell whether my plant is dying from lack of water or from too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ miigbo yɛ nu ni faaa loo nu ni fa babaoo hewɔ?

english: A thirsty plant has dry, crisp, curling leaves and dry soil, whereas an overwatered plant has soft, drooping, or yellowing leaves while the soil around it remains wet and muddy.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni egbi, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebɔle ehe kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Tsei ni nu babaoo baa amɛnɔ lɛ baaná baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni shwieɔ shi loo ŋmɔŋ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Efɔ lolo ni eyɛ muji

english: Why shouldn't I just scatter my maize seeds randomly across the farm instead of planting them in rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mijaa ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ ŋmãa mli?

english: Planting in straight rows with proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong cobs, while also making it much easier for you to weed and care for the farm.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: My maize leaves are turning yellow from the bottom of the stalk going up, why is this happening?
ga: Mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi. Mɛni hewɔ enɛ ji nakai lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: I found small caterpillars eating the young leaves inside the center of my maize plants, what are they doing to my crop?
ga: Miyana ŋmeii bibii ni miiye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Mɛni amɛfeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms, a destructive insect pest. They destroy the plant's growing center, which can kill the crop if you do not protect the farm early with recommended pesticides or safe remedies.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii. Amɛfiteɔ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji obuuu oŋmɔ lɛ he mra. kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ.

english: How do I know when the major rainy season has really started so I don't waste my seeds in dry soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ eje shishi diɛŋtsɛ koni okashi odumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ?

english: Avoid planting after the very first rain because the soil can dry out quickly afterward. Wait until the ground receives two or three good, steady rains within a week so the soil holds enough moisture for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi oya yɛ sɛɛ mli. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ otsi kome mli. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land without them hurting each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni miyeee mihe awui?

english: Yes, this is called intercropping. Maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly at first, so they do not compete heavily for light and soil food early on.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ intercropping. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli, no hewɔ lɛ ekɛ niyenii ni waaa kɛ shikpɔŋ babaoo etswaaa akaŋ yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops weak and produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients that your crops need to thrive. Clearing weeds early removes this competition so your crops get all the nourishment to grow big and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ajie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya. Bɔni afee ni onibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and heat. Leaving tall shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby protects the delicate cocoa plants until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo odu plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada ni efee hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my harvested maize rot or turn moldy when I put it in sacks right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotokui amli beni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize still holds moisture inside the grains. Storing it immediately traps dampness which creates mold, so you must sun-dry the cobs until the grains are completely dry and hard before bagging them.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akɛto amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbi kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ agbi kwraa dani okɛwo kotoku mli.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant seeds from the maize harvest I got last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli dumɔwui toɔ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from improved or hybrid varieties lose their yield strength in the second generation. Buying fresh certified seeds each season ensures strong growth and much higher harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ loo dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛdara waa ni amɛkpa nii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering helps the plant retain flowers and form healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, or heavy rains have washed the plant food too deep into the ground where the roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa tsei aniyenii hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: What happens to my crop seeds if I plant them too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If you plant seeds too deep, they use up all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil to find sunlight, causing them to either sprout very weak or die underground.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ waa koni amɛna hulu la lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ waa loo amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with few leaves when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ yɔɔ amɛhe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight and air, causing them to stretch tall and weak instead of growing strong leaves and stems.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛbaatswa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he akaŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Mohu ɔ, mo tsɔ baa kɛ tsohi nɛ a ngɛ he wami.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves curl upwards during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up during hot afternoons to reduce the surface area exposed to the strong sun, which helps the plant save water and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow even if I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot dry period that dries out the topsoil, killing the young seeds before their roots can grow deep enough to find moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ be ni mli edɔɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli gbiɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kpatamɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahiɛ dani shishifãi lɛ ada kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ baakpe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without turning them into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or when there are no tiny insects in the farm to transfer pollen from flower to flower.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Yɛ ŋmɔji amli koni akɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli

english: Why do my cassava roots begin to rot in the ground when the rainy season is too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Too much rain causes water to sit around the cassava roots, cutting off oxygen and allowing underground fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu feɔ ekome kɛbɔleɔ he. Kassava shishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa cassava shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce such small yields at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients that your crops need to produce big tubers, grains, or fruits.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛwo bulb agbo, dumɔwui, loo aduawai.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as natural food for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to use wooden sticks to lift my yam vines off the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso agbala sweet potato wain tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so they can make food faster, while keeping the leaves off the damp ground where diseases easily spread.
ga: Akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ woɔ ŋtayaa mli koni amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛhoo oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: How can I increase the number of cocoa bags I harvest from my farm every season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha kookoo kotokui ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Increasing your harvest requires consistent management practices like regular pruning, weed control, applying proper nutrients, and following expert advice from extension officers to maximize pod production per tree.
ga: Onibii ni oooha lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ biɔ ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oookpa daa. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋaawoo ni he esa ni jɛ extension nitsulɔi adɛŋ lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ koni aná pod babaoo yɛ tso fɛɛ tso mli.

english: Can a small cocoa farm produce a high number of harvest bags if I manage it well?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo ko baanyɛ afee ŋmaakpamɔ kotokui babaoo kɛji mikwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, proper farm management, accurate tree spacing, and intensive care can dramatically increase yield per acre, allowing a smaller farm to produce a harvest comparable to a larger, poorly maintained farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Kɛ kwɛmɔ ni mli wa baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ waa yɛ acre kome mli. Ehaa ŋmɔji bibii woɔ yibii tamɔ ŋmɔji wuji ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What helps my young cocoa trees gain strength so they do not die easily?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛgbooo oya?

english: Young cocoa trees gain strength when protected from harsh sunlight with shade plants, given proper soil nutrients, and kept free from competing weeds and pest damage during their early stages.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe wa waa kɛji akɛ akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ bu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Na niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eha jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ kɛ mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees, especially young ones, suffer under intense direct sunlight. Providing temporary shade crops like plantains prevents sun scorching and keeps moisture in the soil to sustain tree growth.
ga: Cocoa tsei, titri lɛ tsei bibii lɛ, naa amanehulu yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei tamɔ plantains ni akɛhaa amɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei lɛ aya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do some of the flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without growing into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when the tree lacks enough water or nutrients, or when pests attack the blossoms. Keeping the soil healthy and managing pests ensures flowers mature into full cocoa pods.
ga: Blossom drop baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ adara ni amɛfee kookoo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why should I work with an agricultural extension officer to manage my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko atsu nii koni ekwɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Extension officers share proven techniques for pest control, disease prevention, and proper farm sanitation, helping you avoid costly mistakes and improve your overall crop output.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ jaa ŋaai ni ana he odaseyeli kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ. Helai atsimɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ ni sa Yeɔ ebuaa bo ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ tɔmɔi ni jara wa he. ni oha oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know the correct steps to follow when establishing a new cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛi ni ja ni esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ beni atoɔ kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Consulting local agricultural officers and following recommended guidelines on land preparation, shade provision, and seedling selection ensures your new cocoa farm grows strong from the start.
ga: Okwaayeli he onukpai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ asusumɔi kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni akɛha yɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ dumɔwui ahalamɔ he lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ. Ye obua ni okwɛ koni o-cocoa ŋmɔ hee lɛ aya hiɛ waa kɛjɛ shishijee.

english: How does clearing weeds around my cocoa trees help them produce better?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te mi cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital water and soil nutrients away from cocoa trees. Keeping the farm clean allows the cocoa roots to absorb all available nourishment needed for healthy pod growth.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn black on the branch before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ dani tsei lɛ aniji lɛ daa?

english: Black pod disease is caused by excess moisture and fungal growth. Pruning overcrowded branches and removing affected pods helps air flow through the farm and keeps remaining pods healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ amli ni ajie ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eye ebua ni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What basic routine effort do I need to put into my farm every week to keep the crops healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ehe hiaa ni mabɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa otsi koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ?

english: Weekly maintenance includes inspecting trees for early signs of disease or pests, removing dead branches or diseased pods, and clearing unwanted regrowth around the bases of the trees.
ga: Nɔ ni fata otsi fɛɛ otsi saamɔ he ji tso lɛ mlikwɛmɔ koni ana hela loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui mra. Niji ni egboi loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ajiemɔ.

english: How do I measure the right amount of liquid chemical into my knapsack sprayer so I don't burn my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu tsofa ni ji nu ni akɛwoɔ misɛɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ ni sa lɛ he? Koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akashã

english: Always use a standard measuring cup or the bottle cap provided by the manufacturer to get the exact dose. Adding too much chemical wastes your money and damages crop leaves, while adding too little makes the treatment ineffective against weeds and pests.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ susumɔ kɔɔpoo loo tɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni mɔ ni fee lɛ kɛhaa lɛ atsu nii koni onine ashɛ shika pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji shika fitemɔ ni efiteɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofa fioo ko pɛ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe tsofa lɛ akatsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Can I keep leftover mixed chemical inside my spraying machine to use on my farm next week?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni efutu ni eshwɛ lɛ awo tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ koni mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli otsi ni baa lɛ?

english: No, once chemicals are mixed with water, they start losing their strength within hours and can degrade inside the tank. It is best to mix only what you can finish spraying on the same day.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai miifutu nu Tsofa lɛ baabɔi ehewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli. ni ebaanyɛ efite yɛ tanki lɛ mli Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ nɔ ni obaanyɛ ogbe naa ni okɛshwie nɔ lɛ pɛ afutu yɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: Why should I avoid spraying my crops with agrochemicals during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ agrochemicals ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: The heat from the afternoon sun causes liquid chemicals to evaporate into the air before the plant or pest can absorb them. Spraying early in the morning or late in the afternoon ensures the chemical stays wet long enough to work.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo shwane lɛ, ehaa tsofai lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni etsuɔ ​​nii.

english: Why does a spray I bought stop killing the pests on my farm after I use it several times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni mihe lɛ kpa kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ agbemɔ beni mikɛtsu nii shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Insects can build immunity if you use the exact same chemical repeatedly over time. Switching between different recommended pest control products keeps pests from adapting and ensures your spray remains effective.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ atswa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ ama shi kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tsakemɔ yɛ nibii ni akɛbuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋaa lɛ ateŋ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ koni amɛtsake amɛhe. ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-spray lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some weed killers destroy my crops while others only kill the grass around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gbeɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ pɛ.

english: There are selective and non-selective weed killers. Non-selective chemicals kill every green plant they touch, whereas selective chemicals are specially made to target only specific weeds like grass without harming major crops like cassava or corn.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaa kɛ nɔ ni halaaa fɛɛ yɛ. Tsofai ni halaaa tso lɛ gbeɔ tso fɛɛ tso eŋɔli ni amɛkɛkpeɔ lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, afee tsofai ni ahala lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni akɛtutua jwɛi komɛi pɛ, tamɔ jwɛi, ni eyeee shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei awui.

english: What brings mice and rats to my farm, and how can I stop them from destroying my seeds?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite midumɔwui lɛ?

english: Rodents are attracted by bushy farm borders, fallen seeds, and uncleaned trash where they can hide. Keeping your field boundaries clear and setting safe rodent baits around the farm edges before planting keeps them away.
ga: Gbalaa ŋmeii kɛyaa ŋmɔji ni jwɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. dumɔwui ni egbee shi kɛ jwɛi ni he tseee yɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtee amɛhe amɛwo mli. Ha he lɛ husui lɛ afee faŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe awo ŋmɔ lɛ naa dani odu koni amɛkashɛ he ko.

english: What happens to the chemical I spray if heavy rain falls right after I finish on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni migbe ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the spray off the leaves before the plant or pest can absorb it, making the treatment fail. Try to spray when you expect at least two to four hours of dry weather so the chemical can dry and take effect.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ he dani tsei loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. ha tsofafeemɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ko Bɔɔmɔdɛŋ ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ beni okpaa gbɛ akɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ hulu lɛ baagbi lɛ. koni tsofai lɛ agbi ni amɛtsu nii

english: Is buying cheaper agrochemicals always the best way to save money on my farm?
ga: Ani agrochemicals ni jara waaa lɛ ahemɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ shika toɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cheaper chemicals are sometimes diluted or low quality, meaning you have to spray many times to see results. Buying genuine chemicals recommended by extension officers saves you money in the long run because they work on the first try.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ, akɛ tsofai ni jara waaa lɛ woɔ nu mli loo ehiii kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛwo mli shii abɔ koni ona nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa. Tsofai diɛŋtsɛ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsofai lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni ooohe lɛ baaha okɛ shika akafite yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ejaakɛ amɛtsuɔ nii kɛjɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kaa lɛ mli.

english: Why is liquid chemical leaking onto my back while I am spraying my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni ji nu lɛ ho kɛba misɛɛ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaks usually occur when rubber rings or seals inside the sprayer pump become dry, loose, or cracked. Replacing these small rubber parts stops dangerous chemicals from soaking your body and saves your chemical from wasting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu hoɔ kɛji akɛ rɔbɔt ŋmɛlɛ loo nɔ ni akɛfiɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi, egbɔjɔ, loo egbɛ eshwa. Kɛ́ okɛ rɔba fãi bibii nɛɛ tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ akabote ogbɔmɔtso lɛ mli, ni ehaa tsofai lɛ akafite.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow even though I regularly clear weeds and spray my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is lacking vital soil nutrients like nitrogen or is suffering from excess water around the roots. Spraying for pests or weeds does not feed the plant, so you need to apply proper fertilizer like NPK to restore its healthy green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo jwɛi anɔ lɛ haaa tso lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK atsu nii koni otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong green leaves. Rain can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying fertilizer like NPK early gives them back their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK fata he lɛ, etsɛŋ ni ebaaha amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking juices from the underside of the leaves. As they feed, they cause the leaf to warp and can spread sickness to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela agbɛ ashwã tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off the tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can support, so dropping some is normal. However, if too many fall off, it usually means the tree is lacking water, direct shade, or vital plant nutrients in the soil.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shwiemɔ komɛi ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Shi, kɛji akɛ efo babaoo lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu, hulutsoo, loo tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it from the ground. As long as the plant springs back up by evening, it is just resting to protect itself from heat.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ lɛ Eji hejɔɔmɔ kɛkɛ ni okɛbu ohe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when excess water sits around the roots in heavy soil, suffocating the plant. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily, keeping tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kpɛtɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Ha oyitso ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do the leaves of my corn plants have ragged holes like someone shot through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ mɔ ko ni etswa amɛ tu kɛtsɔ mli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in corn leaves are caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworm feeding on the young leaves inside the center funnel. Treating the center funnel early destroys the caterpillars before they ruin the entire crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa ji ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ mra Efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: What is causing small black spots to appear on my young cocoa stems and pods?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii baa? Yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ kɛ mi-pods lɛ anɔ

english: Black spots on cocoa stems and pods are caused by small sap-sucking insects called mirids or akate. They bite the plant to feed, leaving dead, dark spots that can cause branches to dry up if not managed.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids loo akates lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei kɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛkɔɔ tsei kɛha niyenii. Eshiɔ ŋmeii diji ni egboi ni baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aniji lɛ agbi kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and cool soil young cocoa trees need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa cacao tsei bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb up wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɔ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make the food that grows the large tuber underground. Lifting the vines on stakes keeps them off the ground and catches maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii beni amɛduɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ owó wein tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛbaaná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crop after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo midumɔ nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is two to three weeks after planting, once the seeds have sprouted and developed roots to take in food. Putting fertilizer down before roots form allows rain to wash it away.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo mli ji otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Beni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni akɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli dani shishifãi lɛ shwere lɛ, ebaaye ebua nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛshwieɔ amɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct, harsh sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the surrounding soil. Planting shade crops like plantains around young cocoa acts like an umbrella, keeping the seedlings cool and moist while they establish roots.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leafy branches, but the tubers under the ground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ niji babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing tall and making leaves above ground instead of sending energy down to expand the tubers. Tubers need potassium in the soil to grow thick and heavy.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃ ni eha ebaai lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛha bulb lɛ aya hiɛ. Tubers he miihia potassium yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsii.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime heat gets too intense or when the plant experiences sudden water stress. Severe heat or lack of water prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to shed the unfertilized flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpeɔ trukaa lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to heap the soil into mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabua sũ naa mawo gɔŋ mli dani madu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yam tubers grow downwards and need loose, uncompacted soil to expand freely without resistance. Creating mounds also improves water drainage, which prevents the yam tubers from sitting in waterlogged soil and rotting during heavy rains.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ daa kɛyaa shi ni ehe hiaa ni shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ shi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã amɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi amɛnaa. Gɔji ni afee lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ akatara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do black spots spread quickly across my cocoa pods during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: The black spots are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, humid weather. Rain drops splash the fungal spores from infected leaves and soil onto healthy pods, spreading the infection rapidly.
ga: Black Pod hela, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my maize stems grow very thin and fall over easily when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tsei babaoo amli lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to each other, the seedlings fight for light, water, and soil food. To beat their neighbors to the sunlight, they stretch upwards rapidly, resulting in tall, weak stems that break easily in the wind.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Koni etswa akutsoŋbii lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Amɛbaatsɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ atsei kakadaji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ fãa oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly like tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl as a defense mechanism to protect themselves from hot sun and dry winds. Rolling the leaves reduces the surface area exposed to the air, helping the plant trap moisture and prevent water loss.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa he ni kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsiɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my bearing plantain trees keep falling over after a strong wind, even when the plant looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ miigbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots concentrated near the surface. As the heavy bunch of fruit grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, and if the shallow roots are weakened by poor soil or pests, strong winds can easily pull the entire plant out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni ebua amɛhe naa yɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji aduawai akuu lɛ dara yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili. Ni kɛji akɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahewɔ lɛ? Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala tso muu fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop giving flowers and fruit when the continuous heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Excessive water fills up soil air gaps, suffocating pepper roots and making it hard for the plant to take up nutrients. The cloudy weather also reduces sunlight, which slows down the plant's food production and causes it to stop flowering.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ehaa ewaa ahaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ Atatu hu haa hulu la lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii feemɔ baa shi ni ehaa tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tougher and have aggressive root systems built to grab water and soil nutrients instantly. They wake up from the dry season faster than domestic crops, allowing them to quickly shade out slow-growing seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ, ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni afee koni ejie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Amɛteɔ shi kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli oya fe shia tsei. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ahaa dumɔwui ni daraa blɛoo lɛ anɔ oya.

english: How long should I wait to harvest my vegetables after spraying them with pest chemicals?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa aduawai beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie nɔ sɛɛ?

english: Crops absorb chemicals to kill pests, but they need time to break down those chemicals naturally. If you harvest too soon, the chemicals remain inside the leaves and fruits, making the food unsafe for market and human consumption.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Shi eheɔ be dani nakai tsofai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛji okpa mra tsɔ Tsofai lɛ baakã baai kɛ aduawai lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa niyenii afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha jarayeli kɛ adesai aniyeli.

english: How do I know if the agricultural chemicals I am buying are safe to use on my food crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji okwaayeli mli tsofai ni miheɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ miniyenii ni miduɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Approved chemicals will have clear registration labels from agricultural authorities. Using unapproved or banned chemicals can leave dangerous toxic residues in your harvested food and permanently damage your soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baaná wolo ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo mli ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛjɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe lɛ dɛŋ. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ loo ni agu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashi tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ niyenii ni akpa lɛ mli. ni ekɛ fitemɔ aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya naanɔ.

english: Why does the government extension office care so much about how we dry and store our harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli nitsumɔhei ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ susuɔ bɔ ni amɛbaafee amɛgbi amɛ ŋmãa ni amɛkpa lɛ ni amɛkɛto lɛ he waa lɛ?

english: Improperly dried maize grows mold that produces invisible toxins called aflatoxins. These toxins cannot be cooked out and can cause severe illness in people and livestock who eat the contaminated grain.
ga: Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni no kɛ tsofai fɔji ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ aflatoxins lɛ baa. Anyɛɛɛ ahoo tsofai fɔji nɛɛ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela ni naa wa aba gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ dumɔwui ni mli ewo muji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn yellow and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or when heavy rains trap water around the roots, preventing them from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mɔ nu ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu ni amɛye nii.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience severe heat stress or lack sufficient water. The plant discards the flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out completely.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni naa wa loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: What makes my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifoɔ amɛ?

english: Root rot happens when excessive rainwater collects in the soil without draining properly. Fungi thrive in waterlogged soil and feed on the flooded roots, causing them to decay.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ nu babaoo bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Fuŋ lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ, ni no haa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my black cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up right on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji diji lɛ miitsɔ diŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, over-shaded farms when rain drops splash fungal spores from tree to tree.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Eji tsɛŋemɔ hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli ewo fɔ, ni shade yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why do tiny white bugs swarm my cowpea leaves mostly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yɛŋ Amɛfɔɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ ahe shweremɔ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Insects like whiteflies multiply faster in hot, dry weather because there are no heavy rains to wash them off the leaves, and warm temperatures speed up their egg-hatching cycle.
ga: Koolooi tamɔ whiteflies fɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni egbi mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baafɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ bɛ. Ni hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ haa amɛfɔmɔ be lɛ yaa oya.

english: How does mixing cassava and beans in the same field protect my farm from pests?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe?

english: Planting different crops together confuses insect pests so they cannot easily spread across the whole field. Additionally, beans naturally enrich the soil with nitrogen, which helps the cassava grow stronger.
ga: Tsei babaoo ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ futuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔji amli mlɛo. Kɛfata he lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ daa waa.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so fast when I pack them in wooden crates right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo adekai amli beni mikpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly if they are harvested while wet or left in direct sunlight after picking. Heat trapped inside tight crates causes moisture build-up, creating the perfect environment for bacteria to rot the soft fruit.
ga: Tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ ni efɔ lɛ loo ashi yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ adeka ni mli wa lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni haa aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Is it good practice for me to plant maize and cassava together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly and matures later. This allows you to harvest two different crops from the same field without them choking each other.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo ni ehiɛɔ blɛoo. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli ni amɛtsiii amɛhe gbɛ.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot soil, reduces disease, and helps produce much larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ, ebaaha helai aba shi, ni eye ebua ni aná sweet potatoes ni dara babaoo.

english: Why should I remove the extra small shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain baai lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, known as suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for food and water. Leaving only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main tree gets enough energy to bear big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ashi niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsu niji agboi ni tsii lɛ ahe nii.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from high heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently damp and balanced helps the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Which way should the buds face when I push cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Kɛji ootswa ŋmei nine awo shikpɔŋ lɛ Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ matsɔ mihiŋmɛii anɔ?

english: The buds on the stem cutting must point upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new sprouts to struggle to reach the surface, leading to weak growth and small roots.
ga: Esa akɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii baa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants provide tall, wide leaves that create living shade to protect tender cocoa plants during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai kakadaji ni mli kwɔ ni feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the leaf tips usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize relies on for strong growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ŋmãa biɔ ni ekwɛ̃ waa Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does growing groundnuts or cowpeas help improve my soil for the next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans extract nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and the roots rot in the ground, that trapped nitrogen feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni shishifãi lɛ egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ Nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my vegetable leaves whenever it rains heavily for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ aduawai ahe baai anɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain and damp air create ideal conditions for fungal diseases to multiply and spread through water splashes. Leaving enough space between plants allows the wind to dry the leaves and lower disease risks.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii helai agbɛ ashwã ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛtsɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Shi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aha baai lɛ agbi ni helai aba shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe su etsake lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies carrying a virus, or severe water stress. Controlling pests and watering evenly helps keep the leaves flat and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni hiɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to build strong stalks and stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaha efee tsei ni wa ni ehiɛ eŋɔli su lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller and weaker even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibii ni egbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal food, water, and sunlight from your crops, taking away the essential resources your plants need to mature fully.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Efiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when they get full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in harsh direct sunlight, so they require shade trees to keep them cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei lɛ aná tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall bamboo sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei lɛ awo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni ŋmei tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight, which helps the plant make food to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot in the soil when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with stagnant water, it starves the roots of air, allowing rot-causing organisms to destroy the cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpata ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ.

english: How do I know when it is safe to plant my seeds after the dry harmattan period ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ beni Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: You should wait until the land receives two or three heavy, consistent rains so the soil holds enough deep moisture to keep germinating seeds alive.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ daa. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahi nu ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii aya nɔ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the fruit bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems, and as the heavy fruit bunch grows at the top, strong winds can easily pull the entire plant out of the loose ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. ni kɛ́ aduawai akuu ko ni tsii kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala tso muu fɛɛ kɛjɛ he ko ni etse ehe lɛ mlɛo.

english: Excessive heat or irregular watering stresses the tomato plant, causing it to drop its flowers to conserve energy instead of producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my healthy green cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly when high humidity and rainfall keep the farm constantly damp.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign of tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids that attack young leaves and transmit viruses to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ he okadi. ni tutuaa baai bibii ni ekɛ hela lɛ yaa tso lɛ nɔ

english: Can I just use any type of fertilizer I find in the store for all my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anaa yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ eko fɛɛ eko atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ anɔ?

english: No, crops need specific types of plant food depending on what they produce. If you give a plant the wrong fertilizer, it will only grow big green leaves but will not produce any fruit, seeds, or tubers for you to harvest.
ga: Dabi, tsei biɔ tsei niyenii srɔtoi komɛi. Edamɔ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei ni ejaaa lɛ amli lɛ Ebaaná baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji pɛ shi ebaawooo yibii, dumɔwui, loo bulbs ni okɛbaakpa.

english: If I give my tomato plants extra fertilizer every week, will it make them give me more fruit?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mi tomato tsei lɛ amli daa otsi lɛ, Ani ebaaha miwo yibii babaoo?

english: Too much fertilizer can stress or burn the plant's roots. Instead of giving you more tomatoes, the plant will spend all its energy growing thick leaves or it might even drop its flowers without setting fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ loo eshãa amɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha bo tomato babaoo lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni mli tse. Aloo eko ɔ, e ma nyɛ ma ha nɛ fɔfɔi ɔmɛ nɛ a puɛ si nɛ e wo we yiblii.

english: Why do my crops stay small and weak even when I water them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daraaa ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough for crops to grow produce. Plants need nutrients from the soil to form fruits and seeds, so if your soil lacks plant food, water will only keep the plant alive without helping it yield.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa koni tsei akwɛ̃ nibii. Tsei hia niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee aduawai kɛ dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe niyenii Nu haa tsei hiɔ shi ni ehaaa nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall and leafy, but not forming big corn cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ebɔɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii wuji.
