english: When maize gets too much nitrogen food without other balanced nutrients, it stores all the energy in its leaves and stem instead of using that energy to fill out the corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha ŋmãa nitrogen babaoo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmãa ŋmeii amli ekoŋŋ lɛ

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any peppers start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by incorrect feeding, extreme heat, or irregular watering, causing the plant to save its energy rather than produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ niyenii ni esaaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ toɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why are my cassava roots very small and thin even though the stems above ground look huge?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni da waa lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much leafy fertilizer and not enough root-building food like potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food in the underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ baai ahe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni niyenii ni haa shishifãi tswaa, tamɔ potassium lɛ faaa lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baawo baai ni miida lɛ mli moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stop growing when water stays on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe and absorb food from the soil. When water floods the roots for too long, they choke and cannot feed the plant, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu ni amɛjie niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekɛ niyenii aha. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Does poor soil quality affect how my harvested vegetables store after picking?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ saa bɔ ni akɛ aduawai ni akpa lɛ toɔ beni akpa amɛ sɛɛ lɛ he?

english: Yes, crops grown in poor soil without the right nutrients end up weak inside, which causes them to rot quickly in transport or at the market instead of staying fresh for buyers.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ ni niyenii kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbɛfaa mli loo yɛ jara nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efee ehee aha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than the crops I planted carefully?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that quickly steal the food, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, leaving your crops starving and unable to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛwooo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What happens to my maize if I plant the seeds too close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Planting too close forces the crops to fight each other for soil food and light, resulting in thin, weak stalks that cannot support heavy corn ears.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi ŋmãa toi ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do foreign buyers reject some of my farm produce even when it looks fine to me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ ekomɛi eyɛ mli akɛ amɛhi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi moŋ?

english: International and premium buyers have strict standards regarding size, color, skin marks, and chemical residues. Meeting these specific requirements ensures your produce qualifies for high-paying export markets.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ yɛ mlai ni mli wa ni kɔɔ dalɛ, su, hewolo nɔ okadi kɛ tsofa ni eshwɛ lɛ he. Taomɔ nii pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ ni oooshɛ he lɛ haa onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha jarayeli hei ni shika babaoo yɔɔ mli ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some crop varieties sell for higher prices in the city market than my local varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihei fe mimaŋ tsei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: City buyers and traders often prefer improved seed varieties because they stay fresh longer during transport, have a uniform look, and meet the specific cooking preferences of urban consumers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii kɛ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ sumɔɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaahi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ. Ha ehiɛ afee tamɔ nɔ kome ni etsu maŋbii ni yeɔ nii lɛ ahiamɔ nii pɔtɛɛ ni kɔɔ niyenii homɔ he lɛ ahe nii

english: Why do buyers pay higher prices for crops grown without synthetic chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ tsei ni aduɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi tsuuu nii lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Many modern consumers and export markets place a high value on health and safety, willing to pay premium prices for food free of chemical residues that meets organic standards.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ jarayelɔi kɛ jarayeli hei babaoo ni akɛ nibii yaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ kɛ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he hiaa waa. Amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛwo nyɔmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ waa kɛha niyenii ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bɛ mli ni kɛ bɔɔ nii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe mlai lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ.

english: How can I prevent my harvested vegetables from spoiling quickly before getting to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ anaa koni ekafite oya dani maya jara nɔ?

english: Harvesting early in the cool morning and storing produce in shaded, ventilated containers slows down water loss and decay, keeping the crops firm and fresh for buyers.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli kɛ nibii ni adu lɛ ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsii ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ afite ni efite fioo. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ehee kɛhaa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ.

english: How can I store my harvested maize so that insects do not destroy it in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni kooloi akafite yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Drying grains properly until they are hard and keeping them in sealed airtight bags deprives insects of moisture and oxygen, preserving your crop's quality for many months.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ anaaa nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni okwɛ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ nyɔji babaoo.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava so it stays good for processing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni enyɛ etsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months when starch content is highest; harvesting too late makes the roots woody and hard to sell, while harvesting too early yields small tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ayeɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ be mli ni emli ŋmei lɛ fa fe fɛɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee tsei, ni ebaawa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ. yɛ be mli ni kpamɔ mra tsɔ lɛ kɛ bulbs bibii baa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant grow vibrant leaves needed to nourish large, full corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ wala mli ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms fall off without producing fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shwieɔ yibii ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and soil dryness cause heat stress, making tomato plants drop flowers to save energy. Consistent watering and mulching help protect the plant so it can set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Ha tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he koni ewo yibii.

english: Black Pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and deep shade. Pruning dense branches lets air and sunlight in, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave space between my crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing prevents plants from competing for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, allowing each plant to grow stronger and yield larger, healthier produce.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edara waa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I test a new fertilizer on a small patch of land to see if it works before applying it to my whole field?
ga: Mibaaka ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko makwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko. Koni mana kɛji etsuɔ ​​nii dani mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: To test a new product, choose a small section of about 10 to 20 plants in your field. Apply the recommended amount of the new product to only those plants, leaving the rest of your farm on your usual routine, and observe differences in leaf color, growth speed, and fruit size over two to three weeks.
ga: Ani oosumɔ ni oka nibii heei okwɛ? Halamɔ fã bibioo ko ni tsei aaafee 10 kɛyashi 20 yɔɔ mli yɛ onitsumɔhe nine lɛ mli. Kɛ nibii heei lɛ atsu nii yɛ bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ mli yɛ nakai tsei lɛ pɛ anɔ. Shi oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛha odaa nifeemɔi. ni okwɛ srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ baa lɛ su dalɛ oya kɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ mli yɛ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli.

english: Why are my maize crops still yellow and weak even after I applied the fertilizer I bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ ewo mli moŋ?

english: Crops need moisture to absorb nutrients. If the soil is too dry, the roots cannot take up the fertilizer. Additionally, applying the wrong type of fertilizer or putting it too far from the roots will prevent the crop from responding.
ga: Tsei lɛ hia ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Anyɛɛɛ afee shishifãi lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛfata he lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni ejaaa wo mli loo okɛwo shishifãi lɛ ahe shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akatsu nii.

english: What is the correct method to apply chemical spray on my crop leaves so they do not get burned?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ tsofai shwieɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni akashã?

english: Spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is not hot. Avoid spraying during the heat of the midday sun, as high temperatures combined with liquid chemicals can burn and scorch delicate plant leaves.
ga: Okɛshwie nɔ leebi loo shwane mli. Be ni hulu lɛ edɔɔɔ lɛ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo ni naa wa ni akɛ tsofai ni ji nu fata he lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni ashã tsei ahe baai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ.

english: How long does it usually take for my crops to show signs of improvement after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jieɔ hiɛyaa he okadii akpo beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Foliar fertilizers sprayed directly on leaves show results quickly, usually within 3 to 5 days. Fertilizers applied to the soil take longer, typically around 1 to 2 weeks, because they must first dissolve in moist soil before roots can absorb them.
ga: Foliar fertilizer ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baatsɔɔ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa oya. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ gbii 3 kɛyashi 5. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ heɔ otsi 1 kɛyashi 2 fe nakai ejaakɛ esa akɛ nibii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: How can I tell if an agrochemical or seed product I bought is genuine and will work on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ agrochemical nibii loo dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ ji anɔkwale ni ebaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Always buy from registered agro-dealers and look for official registration seals from regulatory bodies like the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) or the Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA). Check that the container is fully sealed and that the expiry date has not passed.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, hemɔ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ni aŋma egbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ dɛŋ. Ni taomɔ wolo ni aŋmalaa mɔ gbɛi awoɔ mli lɛ he stamp ni jɛ nitsumɔhe ko ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ tamɔ Shihilɛ He Buu Nitsumɔhe (EPA) loo Niyenii kɛ Okwaayeli He Nitsumɔhe (MoFA) lɛ dɛŋ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ atsĩ tsɛnsi lɛ naa ni ehoko be ni esa akɛ ekɛtsu nii lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them directly under full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that dry out quickly in intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them during their first two years to protect them while their root systems mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa amɛnɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their blossoms without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Blossom drop happens when plants experience stress from high heat, lack of water, or excess nitrogen fertilizer. Too much nitrogen causes the plant to spend its energy growing thick leaves instead of holding onto flowers and setting fruit.
ga: Blossom drop baa kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine mli. Nitrogen babaoo haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo baai ni mli tse. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ fɔfɔii ahe ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: If I plant my crops very close together to fit more on my land, why do the stalks grow thin and yield poorly?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ hu? Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni yibiiwoo lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: When crops are spaced too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes the plants stretch tall and skinny for light without building the strength to produce large ears or tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo koni amɛhe la lɛ ni amɛtswaaa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaafee toi loo yitsei wuji.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually not caused by lack of water, but by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding on the underside of the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jeee nu ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Shi kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni yeɔ baai ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow well during the major rainy season but fail during the minor rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli shi amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The minor rainy season in Ghana has shorter, less reliable rainfall and higher heat. Crops suffer because soil moisture dries up before the plants finish flowering and developing seeds, requiring extra water management or short-duration crop varieties.
ga: Nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ Ghana lɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo. anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nɔ ni eyɛ dɔlɛ ni fa babaoo Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ naa amanehulu be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Enɛ biɔ nu he gbɛjianɔtoo kroko loo tsei srɔtoi ni hiɔ shi be kukuoo.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up and turn yellow when it stops raining for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to conserve moisture during dry spells. Yellowing happens because dry soil prevents roots from absorbing essential nutrients, leaving the plant hungry and stressed.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Yellow baa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni amɛhaoɔ.

english: What can I do on my farm to keep water in the soil when rain becomes very small?
ga: Mɛni mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry leaves, straw, or grass—known as mulching—keeps the soil cool and stops sunshine from evaporating the soil's moisture quickly.
ga: He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa Atsɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi hu tsuɔ nii akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afee oya.

english: Why are my corn cobs coming out small and missing many grains this harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ je kpo fioo ni elaaje ŋmãa babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn cobs fail to fill properly when the plant suffers from water shortage or poor nutrition during its flowering stage, which prevents full pollination of the grains.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ atsake ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei lɛ na nu ni faaa loo niyenii ni esaaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ afee pollination kwraa.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my corn after the early rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the rain penetrates deep into the soil over a few consistent days, ensuring young seeds have enough moisture to grow without drying out if the rain stops temporarily.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kukuoo ko.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever strong winds and rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems. When heavy fruit bunches develop and wet soil becomes soft, wind easily pushes them over unless you mound dirt around the base or support them with strong wooden sticks.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatsɔ mli oya. Ja okɛ muji ebɔle shishitoo lɛ he loo okɛ tsei ni wa tsu nii kɛfi sɛɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my plantain plants drying up and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishi baai lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally shed their older bottom leaves to send precious water and food upward to support new leaf growth and the heavy fruit bunch, especially when water is low.
ga: Plantains shwieɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni jara wa aya ŋwɛi koni eye ebua baai heei kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ adalɛ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very big on one side of my land but remain weak and small on another side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi loloolo lɛ, egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ bibioo yɛ fa kroko lɛ nɔ?

english: Soil quality and water drainage vary across a field. Areas with shallow soil, rocks, or poor water holding capacity retain fewer nutrients, causing crops in those spots to struggle.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ, tɛi, loo nu ni nyɛɛɛ ahi mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo pɛ ahi mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nakai hei lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops start flowering earlier than expected when the weather is very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High heat and lack of water cause crops to panic and rush into flowering early so they can produce seeds to survive before dying from drought.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ gbeyei ni amɛyaa oya koni amɛwo dumɔwui ni amɛhi shi dani amɛgboi yɛ hɔmɔ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crops when the rains are weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds have deep, tough root systems that steal light rains quickly before young crop roots can reach the water.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni juɔ nugbɔ fioo oya dani tso bibioo lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ nu lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops look stronger and greener when I plant beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans naturally gather nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil, which acts as a natural food supply for surrounding crops like maize.
ga: Beans buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: This is often caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus stops the leaves from making food properly, causing them to curl, turn yellow, and reduce the overall cassava yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ haaa baai lɛ ahoo jogbaŋŋ. haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa ŋmei fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi

english: Can diseases travel from an infected farm to my healthy field on my cutlass and boots?
ga: Ani helai baanyɛ aya kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ni hela emɔ mli kɛya miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli kɛ dade kɛ bɔɔtu?

english: Yes, invisible germs, fungi, and plant viruses stick easily to soil on your cutlass, boots, and hands. Cleaning your tools with soap, water, or heat before moving to a new field prevents spreading sickness to healthy plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai ni anaaa, ŋmeii, kɛ tsei amli helai baanyɛ akpɛtɛ dade, bɔɔtu, kɛ oniji ahe oya. Kɛ́ okɛ samla, nu, loo la tsu nii kɛtsumɔ nibii ahe dani okɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do some extension officers advise us to burn diseased crop stems after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi komɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ ashã tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Putting diseased crop stems on a fire kills the harmful germs, viruses, and insect eggs living inside them so they cannot survive in the soil and attack your next planting season.
ga: Kɛ́ ashã tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbeɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, kɛ kooloi bibii ni hiɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ shishi koni enyɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etutua odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ hu tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl inward during extreme heat to save moisture. Rolling up reduces the leaf area exposed to the hot sun and wind, preventing the plant from drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli koni eye ebua ni ehiɛ fɛ̃i mli. Kɛ́ okɛwo ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baashɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Tsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkagbi

english: Tomato flowers drop when the heat is too extreme or when the soil lacks moisture. Without enough water during hot weather, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my corn turn yellow in a V-shape down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shishigbɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing down the center of older maize leaves means the plant lacks nitrogen. The corn plant pulls available nitrogen from its lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ baa ŋmãa baai momo lɛ ateŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei gbalaa nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I coat my seed yam pieces with wood ash before planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso sũ awo sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ahe dani madu?

english: Freshly cut yam pieces have open cuts that easily catch rot fungi and soil pests. Coating the cut pieces in wood ash dries out the wound and shields the seed from germs in the ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni afo ehee lɛ Gbɛjegbɛi ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafee mlɛo. Kɛ́ okɛ tso sũ ni afo lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha pilamɔ lɛ agbi, ni ebaabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily during strong rains and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that are often weakened by microscopic soil worms called nematodes. Damaged roots cannot hold the heavy stem in wet, loose soil when wind hits.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bei pii lɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ yɛ sũ ni mli efɔ ni etse lɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer directly to my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve into a form that roots can safely drink. Applying concentrated fertilizer to dry soil can burn and destroy the crop's root system.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ gbɛ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why is it best for me to spray my crop medicine early in the morning around 7:00 AM?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafɔ mi tsei lɛ anɔ aaafee ŋmɛji kpawo leebi lɛ?

english: Spraying early in the morning prevents chemicals from evaporating quickly in the hot sun and ensures the plant leaves absorb the treatment effectively while air temperatures are cool and wind is low.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ leebi lɛ haaa efo oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni ehaa tso lɛ baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ tsofa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu faaa lɛ.

english: Why does crop medicine burn my plant leaves when I spray during hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso tsofa shãa mitso lɛ baai lɛ kɛ́ mikɛshwie nɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High afternoon temperatures cause liquid chemicals to dry too fast and intensify on the leaf surface, which damages the leaf tissue and causes burning.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ ni amɛfeɔ babaoo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ekɛ shãa baa.

english: Can I add palm oil to my crop spray mixture before spraying my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei fɔ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ amli dani mikɛshwie ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Adding small amounts of oil acts as a natural sticker that helps chemicals cling to leaves, but using too much can coat the leaves completely and block the plant from breathing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ mu fioo ko fata he lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa tsofai lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ahe. Shi kɛ akɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ahe kwraa ni eha tso lɛ akamu.

english: Why does my farm chemical float on top of the water in my mixing container instead of dissolving?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ mli tsofai lɛ miiho yɛ nu ni yɔɔ mi-mixing container lɛ mli lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsɔ mli lɛ?

english: Oil-based chemicals do not mix easily with cold water unless you stir thoroughly or pre-mix the chemical with a small amount of water first before filling the tank.
ga: Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ futuuu mlɛo. Ja okɛ tsofai lɛ efutu jogbaŋŋ loo okɛ nu fioo ko futu mli dani okɛwo tanki lɛ mli.

english: Why should I avoid using dirty water from ponds when mixing my crop medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ ŋshɔ mli lɛ he kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miifutu tsofa?

english: Mud and organic matter in dirty water bind to the active ingredients in farm medicine, making the chemicals weak and ineffective against crop diseases and pests.
ga: Muji kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ nu ni mli ewo muji mli lɛ kɛ nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai amli lɛ kpaa gbee. Enɛ haa tsofai lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ahelai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsamɔ mli.

english: How do traditional herbal plants like Dadwensɛm help protect my crops against insects?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema tamɔ Dadwensɛm lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe?

english: Certain traditional plants contain natural bitter compounds that act as organic repellents, driving away insect pests without harming the crops when extracted properly in water.
ga: Kusum tsei komɛi yɛ nibii ni mli wa ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii akɛ nibii ni tsiɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ anaa. Eshwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii awui kɛji ajie lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu mli.

english: How do I identify Kubanwa damage on my crops and manage it on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mayɔse Kubanwa ni efite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni makwɛ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Kubanwa causes leaves to yellow or develop spotty lesions; clearing surrounding weeds and applying targeted crop medicine early stops it from spreading to healthy plants.
ga: Kubanwa haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo fãji ni bɛ faŋŋ baa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ajieɔ mra kɛ tsofafeemɔ ni akɛtoɔ tsei ahe lɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Should I apply liquid crop medicine when the soil is completely dry or when it is damp?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ nu mli tsei ahe tsofa atsu nii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛ́ edɔ?

english: Crop medicine works best when soil has moderate moisture because wet soil helps plant roots safely absorb nutrients and treatments without chemical shock.
ga: Tsofafeemɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ tsofai ni tsofai kɛbaa lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Will rain wash away the medicine I just applied to my crop leaves?
ga: Ani nugbɔ lɛ baaho tsofa ni mikɛwo mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: If heavy rain falls within two hours of spraying, it will wash away the medicine before the plants absorb it, meaning you will need to reapply once the leaves dry.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ mli yɛ tsofa lɛ ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Tsofa lɛ baaho dani tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe baahia ni okɛwo mli ekoŋŋ kɛ́ baai lɛ egbi.

english: How can I get crop spray to stick to slippery leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha tso lɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ akpɛtɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Mixing a recommended sticker agent or mild soap surfactant into your spray helps the solution spread evenly and stick to smooth leaf surfaces even during light rains.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ stika ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ loo tsofa ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ futu tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsofa lɛ agbɛ ashwã pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo po mli.

english: Why are my neighbor's cocoa trees producing so many pods while mine produce very few?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo shi minɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: High cocoa yields are not a secret or trick. They come from consistently following good farming practices like regularly pruning excess branches, weeding, and applying the right fertilizer at the right time.
ga: Cocoa ni fa babaoo lɛ jeee ŋaa loo teemɔŋ sane. Enɛ jɛɔ okwaayeli nifeemɔi kpakpai ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa, tamɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ daa lɛ mli. jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Is there a special trick to make my cocoa trees bear fruit faster?
ga: Ani teemɔŋ sane krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ ni baaha cacao tsei awo yibii oya?

english: There are no magic tricks to crop growth. Cocoa trees bear fruit faster and better when given proper shade while young, clean soil without weed competition, and adequate nutrients.
ga: Majik ŋaa ko bɛ ni akɛbaakwɛ tsei anɔ. Cocoa tsei woɔ yibii oya ni amɛwoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛwo amɛhe hulutsoo jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ji gbekɛ ni ehe tse, ni jwɛi akaŋshii bɛ mli. ni eyɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Why does cutting off branches from my cocoa tree help it produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or unnecessary branches so sunlight and air can reach the main trunk. This directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ tso wulu lɛ he. Enɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai krokomɛi baafata he.

english: Why do cocoa flowers fall off my tree before turning into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ anɔkwa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the tree lacks sufficient water or nutrients, or when pests attack them. Proper soil nourishment and controlling insects help flowers stay on the tree and turn into healthy pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm's soil is missing the food my cocoa needs to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa mi-kokoo lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, cocoa leaves turn yellow, trees grow slowly, and yields drop. Testing your soil or feeding it with organic compost and recommended fertilizers restores these nutrients.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, Cocoa baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. tsei lɛ daraa fiofio ni nibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baa shi Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa loo niyenii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ haa lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ akɛ niyenii nɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some cocoa farms stay green in the dry season while mine dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni minɔ lɛ ŋmɔji lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Farms that keep larger shade trees protect their cocoa from direct heat. The shade trees keep the air cool and hold moisture in the soil, preventing the cocoa trees from drying out.
ga: Okwaafoi agboi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Etsiɔ kookoo tsei anaa koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the branch before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads in wet, overly shaded farms. Removing infected pods quickly and pruning tree foliage allows sunlight and air to dry out the moisture and stop the rot.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni afolɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ekpaa fitemɔ.

english: What makes the young leaves on my cocoa trees curl up and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni haa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like capsids. Applying approved pest control treatments early keeps the insects away and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Enɛ baaye abua ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akashɛ amɛhe ni ebaatsi baai heei adalɛ naa.

english: Why should I keep shade trees on my cocoa farm instead of clearing every tree away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni mafo tso fɛɛ tso?

english: Shade trees shield young cocoa plants from heavy sun and harsh winds. Their fallen leaves also decay into rich food for the soil, helping your cocoa grow stronger.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ hu fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni sũ eyi mli obɔ. Ye obua o-cocoa lɛ ni ehiɛ wa.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly help my cocoa crops perform better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and light away from your cocoa trees. Keeping your land clear ensures all the nourishment in the soil goes straight to feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Covering the soil around crop roots shields the ground from direct hot sunlight. This helps the soil hold onto water much longer, so your plants do not dry out quickly between rains.
ga: Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei gĩii oya kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ.

english: How does water moving through buried logs or wood help my vegetable garden?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tsei loo tsei ni afu lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ?

english: Buried wood acts like a natural underground sponge. When rainwater passes through the wood, it soaks up water and releases it slowly to crop roots over many weeks, keeping the soil moist even during dry spells.
ga: Tso ni afu lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ shishi sponji. Kɛ nugbɔ ho kɛtsɔ tso lɛ mli Ebaaŋɔ nu ni ejie lɛ fiofio. Koni tsei lɛ ahi shi otsii babaoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po.

english: What happens to crop roots if water stays trapped around them for too long without draining?
ga: Mɛni baa shishifãi ni adu lɛ anɔ kɛji nu hi amɛhe? Be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ajieee nu lɛ?

english: When soil gets too waterlogged and water cannot pass through, the plant roots cannot breathe oxygen. This causes the roots to rot and slows down plant growth until the excess water drains away.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli. Tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ amu kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ daraa fioo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why is it necessary to put a layer of topsoil over rotting leaves and crop waste in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ awo baai ni miifite kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Putting soil over organic waste seals in moisture and heat while inviting beneficial earthworms and soil bugs to break down the leaves into rich food for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛwoɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ hiɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ nine koni amɛfite baai lɛ, ni ekɛ niyenii babaoo haa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does organic manure take a very long time to work compared to chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ heɔ be babaoo lɛ?

english: Organic manure must be slowly broken down by soil organisms into tiny nutrients before plants can absorb them. Although it takes time, it improves your soil health for several farming seasons.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ akumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli fiofio. kɛya niyenii bibii amli dani tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ Eyɛ mli akɛ eheɔ be moŋ Shi eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ kɛha okwaayeli bei babaoo.

english: Why do extensions officers advise farmers to let compost sit for months before putting it on crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ okwaayeli nɔ lɛ woɔ okwaafoi ŋaa koni amɛshi ŋmɔshi nibii nyɔji babaoo dani amɛdu nii lɛ?

english: Fresh animal dung and plant waste need time to break down fully. If used immediately, the heat produced during decomposition can burn plant roots and harm young seedlings.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi heei kɛ tsei amli jwɛi heɔ be dani amɛfiteɔ kwraa. Kɛ akɛtsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, la ni jɛɔ mli baa yɛ be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni eye tsei bibii lɛ awui.

english: Is it better to give my crops fertilizer bit by bit or all at once?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii fiofio loo fɛɛ shikome?

english: Applying fertilizer bit by bit allows crops to feed gradually as they grow. Adding too much at once can burn the roots and lead to wasted nutrients washed away by heavy rains.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he fioo fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ fiofio. niyenii ni enine shɛ nɔ beni edara lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ babaoo fata he yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni eha niyenii ni efite lɛ atsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does adding too much fresh animal manure to my farm bed stall crop growth at first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii heei babaoo ni akɛfataa tsei ni yaa hiɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ damɔ klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Too much raw organic material requires soil organisms to work extra hard to decompose it, temporary tying up available soil nutrients and oxygen so crops have to wait before they can grow.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ babaoo lɛ haa ehe bahiaa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ atsu nii waa fe tsutsu lɛ koni amɛgbala mli. Ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kpãa gbee yɛ be kukuoo mli. Enɛ ji koni esa akɛ tsei amɛ dani amɛdara.

english: How can mixing dry wood chips or sawdust into hard clay soil help my crops over time?
ga: Te tso mli ŋmeii ni egbi loo ŋmeii ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Wood breaks down slowly in the soil, opening up hard ground so that water and roots can pass through more easily, though it takes a couple of seasons to see the full improvement.
ga: Tso lɛ baafo fiofio kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Egbeleɔ hei ni wa lɛ anaa koni nu kɛ shishifãi lɛ abote mli mlɛo. Eyɛ mli akɛ ebaahe bei fioo komɛi dani ana hiɛyaa ni yeɔ emuu moŋ.

english: How does rainwater help feed my crops after I put manure on top of the farm bed?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ nu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo miŋmɔ mli saatsoi lɛ amli sɛɛ?

english: As rainwater trickles down through the top layer of manure, it dissolves nutrients and carries them directly to the root zone where the crop can drink them in.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nu ho kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli lɛ, Nutrients lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ amɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ he ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ anu amɛ yɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my plantain plant is mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-plantains lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A plantain plant is ready for harvest when the leaves start turning yellow and the green fingers become plump and rounded rather than sharp and angular. The small dried flowers at the tip of the plantain fingers will also rub off easily.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛniji eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. fɔfɔi bibii ni egbi Ewaaa akɛ aaatsi niji ahe lɛ hu.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop dry up when it gets close to harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miigbi beni kpamɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: When crops mature, they naturally redirect all their energy and nutrients away from the leaves and into the seeds, fruits, or tubers. This makes the leaves turn brown and dry up, which is a normal sign that the plant has finished growing.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Amɛtsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛyaa dumɔwui, aduawai, loo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ asasu ni amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eda.

english: How do I know if cassava under the ground is ready without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ efee klalo ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves dry up and fall off, leaving a mostly bare stem. You can gently clear the topsoil around one plant at the edge of your field to check the size of the roots before harvesting the rest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ fa ko bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. Obaanyɛ Ojie shikpɔŋ sũ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ fiofio. Dumɔ eko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni okwɛ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ dara ha dani okpa nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain plant take almost a full year before it starts fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi muu fɛɛ dani ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Plantain plants need to build a thick stem and many large leaves first to gather enough energy from sunlight and soil. Only after accumulating enough strength over several months can the plant produce a heavy flower stalk and fruit bundle.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ aná tsei ni mli tse kɛ baai wuji babaoo dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛbua hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni ebua hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa naa yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli pɛ kɛkɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔii babaoo kɛ aduawai akui.

english: Why do my crops grow so much slower during the dry season compared to the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plants use water to carry nutrients from the soil up into their stems and leaves. Without adequate water during dry periods, the plant goes into a survival mode, slowing down its growth until water becomes available again.
ga: Tsei kɛ nu tsuɔ nii kɛ tereɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ dalɛ ni abaaha eya shi fioo kɛyashi nu aba ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my crops taking longer to yield fruit than my neighbor's crops planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Crops can mature slowly if the soil lacks key nutrients, if weeds are competing with them for food, or if they receive too little water. Improving your soil with compost and keeping weeds low helps plants mature on schedule.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ adara fiofio kɛji akɛ niyenii titrii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi lɛ kɛ niyenii he akaŋ. Aloo kɛji nu fioo pɛ onine shɛɔ nɔ Sũ lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ jwɛi ni oooha ehi shi lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara yɛ be naa.

english: What kind of work do I need to be doing on my plantain farm between planting and harvest time?
ga: Yɛ dumɔ be kɛ kpamɔ be lɛ teŋ Mɛni ehe hiaa ni mafee yɛ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: During the growth period, you need to weed regularly around the bases, cut away dead or diseased leaves to prevent pests, cut off extra sucker shoots, and prop up heavy fruiting plants with strong wooden stakes so they don't fall over.
ga: yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ Ebaabi ni okɛ jwɛi awo shishigbɛ lɛ he daa, ni ofolɔ baai ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ fɛɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafee nɔ ko. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ. ni amɛkɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why do my heavy plantain plants fall over right before the fruit gets ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and a full bunch of fruit makes the top of the plant very heavy. Strong winds or wet, soft soil can easily pull the roots out, so supporting the stem with a Y-shaped wooden pole is necessary as the bunch grows.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni aduawai akui lɛ haa tso lɛ yiteŋ feɔ mlɛo waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ tsei ni tamɔ Y aye abua ŋmeii lɛ ahe be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why did my crop produce very tall stems and lots of leaves but very little yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ waa kɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When plants get too much nitrogen or are planted too close together, they spend all their energy fighting for sunlight by growing tall and leafy instead of putting energy into forming fruits or roots.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baawu amɛshi hulu kɛtsɔ amɛshweremɔ kɛ baai ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee aduawai loo shishifãi.

english: What am I supposed to do with my land right after I finish harvesting my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: After harvest, clear dead plant material and leave healthy leaves or stalks to decompose on the soil as mulch. This protects the soil from heat and adds organic nutrients back into the land for your next crop.
ga: yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Okɛ tso nibii ni egboi lɛ ashwie nɔ ni oshi baai loo shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ekɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it better to plant my young seedlings early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu tsei bibii leebi loo shwane?

english: Planting late in the afternoon is usually better because the soil cools down and young seedlings will not immediately get scorched by the harsh midday sun. This gives them the whole night to absorb moisture and recover from planting stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mli ejɔ, ni hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ shãaa dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ahe haomɔ mli gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to leave wide spaces between my mango trees when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔshi he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ yɛ mango tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ wɔmiidu amɛ lɛ?

english: Mango trees grow large roots and wide branches over time. Leaving enough space prevents neighboring trees from competing for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in healthier trees and larger fruit harvests.
ga: Mango tsei yɛ shishifãi wuji ni shwereɔ niji babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ ashi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ, ni akpaa aduawai babaoo.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes when the sun is very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during intense heat as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant trap moisture and prevent water from escaping through evaporation.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my mango trees drop many of their flowers before the fruits even start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo dani aduawai lɛ po jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop flowers mainly due to sudden dry spells, lack of water during early flowering, or insect pests like thrips. Giving the trees consistent moisture and protecting flower clusters from pests helps the flowers turn into full fruits.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ, ekolɛ trukaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahewɔ. Nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ mli mra loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ thrips. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ mli fũu daa, ni abu fɔfɔi akui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Exhausted soil causes crops to grow very slowly, turn pale green or yellow instead of dark green, and produce thin stems with small yields even when there is enough rain.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo waa. Etsɔɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ ni tso bibioo ko feɔ Yibiiwoo ni baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ.

english: Can I plant beans or groundnuts underneath my young mango trees, or will it harm the trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mango tso shishi? Aloo ebaaye tso lɛ awui?

english: Planting groundnuts or beans under young fruit trees is actually helpful. These legumes pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the tree while giving you an extra crop to harvest.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ aduawai tsei bibii ashishi lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ehaa bo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni okɛbaakpa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning light yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems from agricultural officers is the best way to keep your farm clean.
ga: Nɛkɛ baai lɛ ni ebɔle ehe nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ. Okwaayeli nitsulɔi ni duɔ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli atse.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my fruit trees if I want a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mitso lɛ niji komɛi kɛji miitao yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes dead, weak, or overcrowded branches so the tree does not waste food and water on them. It opens up the tree canopy to sunlight and air, which reduces diseases and encourages the tree to produce bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni egboi, ni egbɔjɔ, loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ajieɔ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ akashi niyenii kɛ nu yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe kɛhaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa helai baa shi, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my crops reduce the final amount of food I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa naagbee niyenii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. This starves your main plants and leaves them too weak to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ oya. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ anɔ, ni ebaaha egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekpa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my mangoes so they ripen well without rotting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ okpa mango koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekafite?

english: Mangoes are ready to pick when they look full and plump, and the flesh around the stem turns slightly yellow, even if the rest of the skin is still green. Picking them at this stage allows them to ripen safely off the tree.
ga: Mango lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji etamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni loo ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fioo. Eyɛ mli akɛ hewolo lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo moŋ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛshwere shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong leaves. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the top young leaves to keep growing, causing the older leaves at the bottom to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda. Enɛ haa baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How does covering the ground around my crops with dry leaves and grass help them grow better?
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ hamɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves (called mulching) keeps the soil cool under the strong sun, traps water in the ground so you water less, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly turns into natural fertilizer as it rots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa Enɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli shii abɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaye nɔ ni fiofio lɛ etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni egboɔ lɛ.

english: Can I just cut any part of an old cassava stem to plant a new cassava farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo ŋmei tso momo ko fã ko koni mikɛdu ŋmei tso hee?

english: No, it is best to cut planting sticks from the middle section of a healthy, mature cassava plant that is 8 to 12 months old. The tips are too soft and rot easily, while the very bottom is too old and hard to sprout strong roots.
ga: Dabi, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ niji kɛjɛ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ teŋgbɛ. Tips lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ ni egboɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ wa ni ewa akɛ amɛaakwɛ̃.

english: Planting maize on the same soil every year drains all the specific food maize needs and gives soil pests a permanent home. Switching your farm to plant groundnuts or cowpeas after maize helps put food back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ haa abele lɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni eha kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahi shi daa. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔ lɛ kɛfee ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do I need to clear away extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Extra shoots (suckers) steal water and food from the main mother plantain tree. If you cut them away and leave only one or two strong shoots, all the nutrients will go into making one big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi krokomɛi (tsoji) juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛji ofolɔ amɛ ni oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ baaya plantain tso agbo ko ni tsii mli.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes in the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves up high to catch maximum sunlight. Catching sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to swell the yam tuber under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ awo ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni enine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii. ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young corn leaves and dirty dust in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai kɛ sũ ni mli ewo muji ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip (the funnel) of the maize plant and eats the tender leaves before they unfold. Treating the central funnel early with neem oil extract or approved insecticides helps save the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi (cones) lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem mu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsa tso lɛ.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the daytime weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Extreme heat or water stress damages the pollen inside the flower so it cannot produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ, ni no haaa ewo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct, hot sunlight and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains near young cocoa protects their delicate leaves from burning and keeps the surrounding air moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaabu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look dead in the hot afternoon even if the soil was wet in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi po?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, crops lose water from their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. The plant purposely wilts to reduce its size and protect itself from losing more moisture, and it usually bounces back once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsɔɔ yiŋtoo ko nɔ amɛgboiɔ koni amɛba amɛdalɛ shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow big ears. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their green color and improve your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛsu eŋɔli kɛ amɛtoi wuji lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha okpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my cabbage leaves, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ naa?

english: Tiny holes are usually caused by small caterpillars or beetles chewing on the leaves. Spraying an organic neem leaf solution or recommended biopesticide early in the morning helps repel these pests before they destroy your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem baa mli tsofa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oshwie kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava cuttings in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmei niji yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be planted about 1 meter apart from each other. Giving them enough space allows the roots to swell into large, heavy tubers without competing for soil nutrients and water.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afo lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii ni amɛyeee akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without forming any tomatoes when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato flowers to dry out and fail to pollinate, which makes the plant drop them to save energy. Covering the soil around the plants with dry grass mulching keeps the roots cool and helps retain fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaaa amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ashɛrɛɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashwieɔ shi koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their high-yield strength in the second generation, producing weak plants with small cobs. Buying fresh certified seeds every planting season ensures strong growth and high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ haa amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. This feeds the soil and provides natural fertilizer that helps your maize grow taller and stronger.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell when my yam crop is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam is ready to harvest when the leaves above ground naturally turn yellow and completely dry up. This signals that the plant has stopped growing leaves and transferred all its energy into the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbi kwraa. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ etee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why does my pepper plant have many green leaves but very few peppers growing on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pepper fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them grow bushy leaves instead of flowers and peppers. Using fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to bloom and set plenty of fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛná baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees curl up and turn dry during the Harmattan?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind pulls moisture out of leaves faster than young roots can drink water from dry soil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa trees from dry winds and harsh sunlight.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why are my bean seeds taking so long to sprout after planting them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds require adequate soil moisture to wake up and begin sprouting. If planted in dry soil without rain or watering, the seeds stay dormant or can dry out completely before they get a chance to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi kwɛ̃mɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nugbɔ loo nu bɛ mli Dumɔwui lɛ ŋmɛɔ loo amɛgbiɔ kwraa dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do I need to cut down my cocoa tree completely if only a few branches are showing signs of disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ fɛɛ? Be mli ni niji fioo komɛi pɛ yɔɔ hela lɛ he okadi?

english: Diseases like the cocoa swollen shoot virus spread throughout the entire tree's system, even into the roots. Cutting off just a few branches won't stop the sickness, and keeping the tree on your farm will cause the disease to spread to your healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Helai tamɔ kookoo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛ eshwa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ. kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ po nɔ Niji fioo komɛi pɛ ni afolɔ lɛ haŋ hela lɛ akpa. Ni tsei lɛ ni ooohi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Can disease from an old, dying cocoa tree move to healthy young trees planted nearby?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ajie helai ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ ni egboi amli lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, insects like mealybugs can easily carry viruses from infected or dying cocoa trees to nearby healthy plants. Rain splash and shared farming tools can also transfer fungal diseases like black pod from infected trees to fresh seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni jɛ cacao tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ loo egboi lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya. Nugbɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ hu baanyɛ agbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji ashwã, kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛya dumɔwui heei anɔ.

english: If I agree to cut down my diseased cocoa farm, how many years will I have to wait before new trees start bearing fruits?
ga: Kɛ mikpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ mafolɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani tso hee ko aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually begin flowering and producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, which is much faster than traditional cocoa trees that used to take up to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, ni enɛ yaa oya fe afii enumɔ ni kookoo tsei ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ heɔ tsutsu lɛ.

english: What is the benefit of participating in a government cocoa rehabilitation program instead of managing diseased trees on my own?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ nɔyeli lɛ kookoo sɛɛkuu gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli ni mɔ ko kɛ ehe aaawo lɛ he? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni bo diɛŋtsɛ obaatsa tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Rehabilitation programs provide expert support to properly clear diseased roots, treat the soil, and supply high-yielding, disease-resistant seedlings so your farm can recover completely and yield far more cocoa in the long run.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ haa ŋaalɔi yeɔ amɛbuaa koni ajie shishifãi ni helai emɔ amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ, atsa shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni aha dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛŋ aye amɛnɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kwraa ni ekɛ kookoo babaoo aba yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Can I plant fresh cocoa seedlings in the exact same spot where I just cut down an old, diseased cocoa tree?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mifoɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ ni helai emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: It is risky to plant directly in the old spot immediately because disease germs and pests can remain in the remaining underground roots. The old roots need to be removed or allowed to decay, and the soil prepared before planting new seedlings.
ga: Eyɛ oshara akɛ ooodu yɛ he ko ni etsɛ tɛ̃ɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ amli. Ehe miihia ni ajie shishifãi momo lɛ loo aha amɛgboi. ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani odu dumɔwui heei

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantains next to my newly planted cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tsei ni adu ehee

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and can easily dry out or burn under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide broad leaf shade to protect young cocoa trees during their first few years while also giving you food and income.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi loo amɛshã yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa roots are shallow and cannot reach deep underground water during dry spells. Without temporary shade trees or mulching to trap soil moisture, the harsh dry winds strip water from their leaves faster than roots can absorb it.
ga: Kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi lɛ bɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer and smaller pods even though I weed the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo ni amɛmiifee bibii eyɛ mli akɛ mifoɔ jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their natural capacity to draw nutrients and produce heavy pods declines. Even with proper weeding, old trees become less productive and more prone to disease, making replanting necessary.
ga: Beni cacao tsei lɛ daraa kɛhoɔ afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ baa shi. Kɛji akɛ ajie jwɛi jogbaŋŋ po lɛ, tsei ni egbɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo, ni helai hu baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya. Ehaa ehe hiaa ni adu ekoŋŋ

english: Why does my cocoa tree grow tall and thin with very few branches when planted close to other trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ niji fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, they stretch upward to compete for limited sunlight. This causes them to spend energy growing tall stems instead of developing thick, sturdy branches that hold heavy cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛkɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ nihi nɛ a mi wa nɛ a haa kookoo tso nɛ tsii ɔmɛ ngɛ he nɛ a ngɛ ɔ.

english: Why is it important to cut off side shoots and extra branches from my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ kɛ tsei niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unwanted branches that steal valuable nutrients and water away from the main stem. It helps the cocoa tree build a strong main trunk and allows air and light to circulate, which reduces disease.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni ataooo ni juɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni etswaa tso titri ni mli wa. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la tsɔɔ mli. ni baanyɛ aye abua ni helai aba shi

english: Why do my young maize leaves roll up tightly into pencil shapes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ ebɔle ehe shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee pensil yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to cut down on water loss during intense heat. It shrinks the leaf surface exposed to the direct sun so the crop doesn't dry out completely.
ga: Abɛi baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Ehaa baa lɛ hiɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbiɛɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my maize plants look like someone shot small holes through the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko efo bu bibii kɛtsɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ?
