english: This hole pattern is typical damage from Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the leaf whorl while the plant is young. Catching them early and placing ash, sand, or recommended bio-pesticides into the central whorl stops them.
ga: Nɛkɛ bu nɛɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ fitemɔ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ sũ, ŋã loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo teŋgbɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ baatsi amɛnaa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense daylight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, shielding the delicate cocoa seedlings from direct sun until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tso bibioo ni miida oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Buu kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my main plantain stem producing very small bunches after so many young shoots grew around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso titri lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ebɔle ehe lɛ sɛɛ? Mi plantain titri lɛ

english: When too many suckers grow around a mother plantain, they compete heavily for water and nutrients. Pruning the extra shoots so that only one or two strong suckers remain ensures big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu ko he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii agbo ni tsii aba.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge stems and bushy leaves but tiny tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tso agbo kɛ baai bibii, shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil makes cassava spend its energy growing foliage above ground instead of feeding the roots. Cassava needs balanced soil nutrients and potassium to swell its underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ potassium ni sa jogbaŋŋ he miihia cassava koni eha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of just spreading across the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight needed to produce food for tuber growth, while keeping the leaves off damp soil where fungal diseases easily spread.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni ená hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛ niyenii aha tuber lɛ koni ekwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akafee shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ yɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why are the blossom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is blossom-end rot, caused by calcium deficiency in the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular—drying out completely and then flooding the soil.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. No ji, ha egbi kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are all the flowers falling off my pepper plants without forming any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when exposed to extreme heat stress or sudden dry spells. Regular, consistent watering and light shade during peak midday heat helps the blossoms set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ kpe. Nu ni akɛhaa daa, daa kɛ shade yɛ hulutsoo be mli haa aduawai baa.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my corn turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the tip and moving down the central vein of older lower leaves indicates nitrogen deficiency. The plant is stealing stored nitrogen from older leaves to keep top leaves green.
ga: Yellowing lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni eyaa shishi kɛyaa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ fã lɛ mli. Etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tso lɛ miiju nitrogen ni ato kɛjɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni eha baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahi eŋɔli.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers recommend planting groundnuts before planting maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei dani adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnut roots feature beneficial bacteria that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. After harvest, that left-behind nitrogen naturally fertilizes the soil for the next maize crop.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmei shishifãi amli. yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my local Ghanaian maize seeds survive the dry season better than the imported seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ Ghana ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ ni miheɔ lɛ?

english: Local seed varieties have naturally adapted over many generations to Ghana's weather patterns and high temperatures, making them hardier during dry spells compared to foreign seeds bred for different climates.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ etsake amɛhe amɛwo Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ mli yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Ehaa ewaa waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ ni afɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi anaa lɛ ahe.

english: Is it better for me to save seeds from my local harvest or buy new imported hybrid seeds every year?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato loo mahe dumɔwui heei ni akɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ daa afi?

english: Local saved seeds cost nothing and are naturally adapted to local conditions, while imported hybrid seeds can yield more under ideal conditions but lose their strength in the next generation, requiring you to buy new ones every season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ aheee nɔ ko, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ maŋ lɛ mli shihilɛi amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ shihilɛi ni sa amli. Shi ebaafite ehewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ehe bahiaa ni ohé dumɔwui heei daa afi.

english: How can I know if a foreign crop seed will perform well in my local soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji maŋsɛɛ tsei dumɔwui baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mimaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Foreign seeds must be tested for your specific ecological zone in Ghana, as crops bred for cooler or wetter regions often struggle with local heat, native pests, and soil conditions.
ga: Esa akɛ aka maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ kɛha he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ fɔɔ naagbai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ naa waa. Kuu lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry periods to conserve water and protect its underground roots, sprouting new leaves automatically when the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli ni ebu eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Baai heei baakwɛ̃ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any peppers when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress to pepper plants, making them drop their flowers to save energy and water until temperatures cool down to a level where fruits can safely form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Ha amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ kɛyashɛ he ko ni aduawai baanyɛ afee shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and drying up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods often dry up due to fungal diseases like black pod disease or excessive exposure to direct sunlight when there are not enough shade trees in the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ lɛ hewɔ beni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ faaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my farm help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Te tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-ŋmei srɔtoi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, leaving behind a natural fertilizer that feeds the maize crop planted after them.
ga: Cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ashiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni akɛha ŋmãa tsei ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rain and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay near the soil surface, making heavy-bearing plants top-heavy and easy for strong winds to push over unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii lɛ feɔ tsii ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa kɛtsɔɔ mli mlɛo. Ja nɔ ko ni akɛ tso fee lɛ yɛ.

english: Why are insect pests attacking my foreign cabbage crop much more than my local garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mi maŋsɛɛ kaabii tsei lɛ fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mimaŋ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Local traditional crops have developed natural chemical defenses and tough leaves over time, whereas many foreign leafy crops are softer and sweeter, making them easier targets for local pests.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli tsei ená tsofai ni buɔ amɛhe kɛ baai ni wa yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛmli ŋɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root rot, where excess water or soil bacteria block the water channels inside the plant stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. He ni nu loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ anaa lɛ.

english: Why is it important to prepare a nursery bed for my rice seeds before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni asaa ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ashishi dani adu awo ŋmãa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A nursery bed acts like a safe daycare for young seeds. It protects them from harsh weather, birds, and weeds, allowing them to sprout strong roots so that when you transplant them, they settle quickly into the main field.
ga: Nursery saatsoi tsuɔ nii akɛ shweshweeshwe shihilɛhe kɛha dumɔwui bibii. Ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, okpoi, kɛ jwɛi ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaahi shi oya yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when it is time to remove the grass or leaf cover from my seedbed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ majie jwɛi loo baai ni ha midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: You should remove the protective cover as soon as you see tiny green shoots starting to push up through the soil, usually within a few days. Leaving the cover on too long will block sunlight and smother the young seedlings.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ kɛji ona ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli pɛ. Shishijee ni ajieɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Bei pii lɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli Kɛ́ ashi nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ hulu la lɛ naa ni eha dumɔwui lɛ afee duŋ.

english: How many days should I leave my rice seedlings in the nursery bed before transplanting them?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ ashi ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ adu amɛ?

english: Rice seedlings should generally stay in the nursery bed for about 14 to 21 days (two to three weeks). By this time, they have developed 3 to 4 strong leaves and sturdy roots ready for the main field.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli gbii 14 kɛyashi 21 (otsii 2-3). Amrɔ nɛɛ ni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 3 kɛyashi 4 kɛ shishifãi ni wa lɛ, amɛfee klalo kɛha dumɔ titri.

english: Can using traditional herbs or green leaves on my soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani maŋ lɛ mli tsofai loo baai eŋɔli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, spreading specific local leaves or herbs over your soil acts as a natural mulch. As they decompose, they keep the soil moist, suppress weeds, and add nutrients that feed your crop roots naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai loo tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Beni amɛfiteɔ lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ fataa he

english: Why do some elders put crushed plant leaves on nursery beds before sowing crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai komɛi kɛ tsei ahe baai ni atswa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ dani amɛduɔ lɛ?

english: Certain plant leaves contain natural oils that repel harmful insects and fungi in the soil. Using these traditional botanical treatments gives young seeds a cleaner environment to germinate safely.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli fɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni eshwieɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ tsei komɛi ahe baai lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ nɛkɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema beaŋ nɛɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa shihilɛ ni mli tse ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it safe to rely on traditional herbal methods for protecting my crops from pests?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ mihe baafɔ blema tsofa-kɛ-ŋma gbɛi anɔ koni mikɛbu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe?

english: Traditional herbal methods can be very effective because elders identified plants with natural pest-repelling properties. Combining these traditional remedies with good field timing and clean farming gives high crop yields.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ onukpai lɛ kɛɔ akɛ tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kɛ́ akɛ blema tsofai nɛɛ fata dumɔ bei kpakpai kɛ okwaayeli ni he tse he lɛ, ehaa anáa yibii babaoo.

english: What does it mean when someone says my rice crop has 'settled' in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛɛ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ ‘ehi shi’ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: When rice has 'settled,' it means the transplanted seedlings have overcome transplant shock, anchored their new roots deep in the mud, and are actively absorbing water and nutrients to grow.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ‘gbee shi’ lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni adu lɛ nyɛɔ eyeɔ ŋmãa ni adu lɛ he gbeyeishemɔ nɔ kunim. Okɛ shishifãi heei awo muji lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni ekɛ ekãa shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha dalɛ.

english: How can I check if my young rice seedlings are healthy enough for the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ titri lɛ?

english: You can pull up two or three seedlings across your seedbed to inspect them. Healthy seedlings will have firm white roots, thick stems, and vibrant green leaves rather than weak or yellowing shoots.
ga: Obaanyɛ ogbala dumɔwui fioo komɛi awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni okwɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shishifãi eyɛŋ ni ma shi shiŋŋ, tsei atsei, kɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. Yɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ

english: Why should I cover my seedbed with plant material right after sowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei ahe nibii aha midumɔwui lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu lɛ?

english: Covering the seedbed keeps the soil cool and moist, prevents hot sunlight from drying out the seeds, and stops heavy rains from washing your seeds away before they take root.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ashishi ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Tsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekagbi dumɔwui lɛ. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekɛfɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛwo shishifãi.

english: How many rice seedlings should I plant together in one spot when transplanting?
ga: Kɛ́ aadu tsei krokomɛi lɛ, tsei enyiɛ esa akɛ adu yɛ he kome?

english: It is best to plant 2 to 3 healthy seedlings together in each hole. Planting two or three ensures that if one seedling fails, the remaining ones will still grow into a full, bushy plant.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ bu fɛɛ bu mli. Tsei enyɔ loo etɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha kɛji dumɔwu kome gbo lɛ, Tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ baaya nɔ adara ni amɛtsɔ tsei bibii ni eda.

english: My cocoa leaves are drying up during the dry season. How can I protect my trees from heat and drought?
ga: Mi kookoo baai lɛ mli egbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mitsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he?

english: You can protect your trees by mulching, which means covering the soil around the tree trunk with dry leaves or grass. This acts as a blanket that traps moisture in the ground and prevents the sun from drying out the roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu otsei lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa, ni ehaa hulu la lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: What are the early signs that my cocoa trees are suffering from water shortage before they die?
ga: Mɛni ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiye nu he naagba dani amɛgboi?

english: The earliest signs are leaves wilting during mid-day heat, yellowing leaves at the bottom of the tree, and tiny young pods dropping off before maturing.
ga: Okadi ni tsɔɔ mra fe fɛɛ ji baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi teŋgbɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ ŋmeii bibii Gbeeɔ shi dani amɛshwereɔ.

english: What is compost, and how can it help my crops survive long periods without rain?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Compost is a mixture of decayed farm waste, animal manure, and leaves. When added to soil, it acts like a sponge that holds onto rainwater for a long time, giving crops water even during dry spells.
ga: Kompost ji ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni egbo, kooloi ashishifã, kɛ baai ni afutu. Kɛ́ akɛfata sũ lɛ he lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji, ni emɔɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po.

english: Why are my neighbor's cocoa trees healthy while mine on the same land are struggling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ cacao tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni mi cacao tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Differences usually come down to soil nutrients, shade levels, or moisture retention. Feeding your soil with organic compost and maintaining shade trees can restore struggling cocoa trees.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔ lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii, bɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ ha, loo bɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hiɔ shi ehaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni akwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha kookoo tsei ni miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I cut down my dry cocoa trees and plant food crops like cassava or plantain instead?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tsei ni egbi lɛ ni madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo plantains moŋ?

english: Cutting down mature cocoa completely can mean losing future long-term income. Instead of removing all of it, you can prune struggling trees, add shade, and plant food crops in between to get quick income while cocoa recovers.
ga: Kookoo ni egbɔ lɛ nɔ ni abaatsi kwraa lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ shika ni anáa wɔsɛɛ lɛ ni baafite be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooojie fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ Obaanyɛ ofolɔ tsei ni miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, okɛ hulutsoo afata he, ni odu niyenii yɛ nifeemɔ lɛ mli koni onine ashɛ shika nɔ oya yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ he waa lɛ.

english: Why is cocoa considered a stronger business crop than food crops like maize or yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ kookoo akɛ eji shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa fe niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a high-value cash crop with a steady market and set purchasing prices, whereas food crops depend heavily on local market prices which go up and down daily.
ga: Cocoa ji shika helɛtemɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa. Eyɛ jarayeli ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ jara ni ato ni akɛheɔ nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ jara ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ nɔ, ni jara lɛ tsakeɔ daa gbi.

english: Can I plant food crops together in the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu niyenii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Yes, planting food crops like plantain and cassava alongside young cocoa is beneficial. Food crops provide shade to protect young cocoa from direct sun while giving you food and income while cocoa matures.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantain kɛ cassava ni akɛfataa kookoo bibii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Niyenii tsei haa hulutsoo be ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: My cocoa trees stopped producing pods after a bad dry season. Can they bear fruit again or should I clear them?
ga: Mi cacao tsei lɛ kpa ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa ko sɛɛ. Ani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii ekoŋŋ loo esa akɛ majie mli?

english: Do not clear them immediately. Cocoa trees often pause production under stress to survive; with proper pruning, shade management, and organic fertilizer, they can recover and fruit again next season.
ga: Kaajie amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei kpaɔ nitsumɔ be kukuoo ko yɛ nɔnyɛɛ shishi bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaanyɛ ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ ni ewo yibii ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: My crops are dying even though I tend to them daily. Is this caused by bad soil, weather, or something else?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miigboi eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɔ amɛ daa gbi moŋ. Ani shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, loo nɔ kroko hewɔ eba lɛ nakai?

english: Sudden decline is almost always caused by unseen pests, root diseases, or severe soil dehydration rather than bad luck. Investigating the roots and soil usually reveals the exact physical cause.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni anaaa, shishifãi ahe hela, loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa lɛ baa shi trukaa. Yɛ shweremɔ gbonyo najiaŋ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlipɛimɔ jieɔ nɔ pɔtɛɛ ni kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ naagba lɛ baa lɛ kpo.

english: How do shade trees help cocoa trees survive during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Shade trees reduce direct heat on cocoa leaves, lower air temperatures around the farm, and prevent water in the soil from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ kookoo baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ.

english: How do I test a new crop like soybean on my land to see if it will yield well before planting my whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka ŋmɔshi nibii heei, tamɔ soybeans, makwɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni mana kɛji ebaawo yibii kpakpai dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can plant a small test plot on one section of your farm to observe how the seeds sprout, withstand local weather, and produce pods before investing in larger quantities of seeds.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ fã ko nɔ koni okwɛ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amɛhaa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ekɛ pods baa dani ekɛ eshika woɔ dumɔwui babaoo mli.

english: Why do some of my bean seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛdu shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if planted too deep, if the soil lacks moisture, or if soil insects and fungi damage the seeds before they can germinate.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What is the best time of the year to plant soybeans in Ghana to get the best harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu soybeans yɛ Ghana koni ená yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Soybeans yield best when planted at the onset of the main rainy season so that the plants receive consistent moisture while flowering and filling their pods.
ga: Soybean woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be beni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ eyiɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I plant beans or soybeans instead of planting maize every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo soybean yɛ ŋmei najiaŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize continuously drains nutrients from the ground, while beans and soybeans trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, keeping your land fertile for future crops.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ soybean lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii wɔsɛɛ.

english: Does planting legumes like cowpea or soya improve the soil for other crops I plant later?
ga: Ani ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo soybeans ni miduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, legumes leave behind natural nitrogen in the soil through their root nodules, which acts as a free fertilizer for the next crop you plant in that field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shiɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Can I plant soybeans and maize together in the same field?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu soybean kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize with soybeans helps maximize space, reduces weeds, and allows the soybean plants to enrich the soil while the maize grows tall.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ soybean duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ, ehaa jwɛi lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa soybean tsei lɛ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shweremɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of leafy branches but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil or planting in heavy shade encourages the plant to put all its energy into growing green leaves rather than forming flowers and pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hulutsoo ni mli wa ni miida lɛ baawo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu baai eŋɔli ni miida lɛ he nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: Why are the leaves of my soybean plants turning yellow when they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can be a sign of poor water drainage, a lack of essential soil nutrients, or damage to the roots caused by insect pests.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛbaa lɛ.

english: How can I protect my bean flowers from dropping off before they turn into pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi dani amɛtsɔ ŋmeii?

english: Flower drop is often caused by heat stress, lack of water during flowering, or tiny pests like thrips attacking the buds, which can be controlled with timely spraying of organic or approved insecticides.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ he haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ Abaanyɛ akudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli loo ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be naa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my soybeans are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-soybean lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Soybeans are ready to harvest when the leaves turn brown and drop off, and the seed pods turn dry and golden-brown, making a rattling sound when you shake them.
ga: Soybean lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbee shi. ni dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbaatsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa gbee ni tswaa kɛji okpokpo lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or the ground is waterlogged from heavy rain, which prevents roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a free natural fertilizer for your maize crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn tsei lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my farm after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii beni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist—usually two to three weeks after sprouts appear. Applying fertilizer during dry dry-spells can burn and destroy plant roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ otsii 2-3 beni ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees often drop flowers when they suffer from extreme sun heat, lack of water, or attacks from insects like mirids. Maintaining moderate shade trees helps keep flowers attached.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatu ni ha amɛhe lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ha hulutsoo be ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: What causes the leaves of my tomato plants to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a plant virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by severe heat stress when plants don't get enough water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when they start bearing heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and soft. When a heavy bunch grows, wind can easily pull the plant down. Supporting the trunk with a strong bamboo or wooden prop prevents falling.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ. Kɛji kuu lɛ da lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ agbala tsei kɛba shi mlɛo. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekagbee shi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting leaves quickly inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ oya yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when exposed to warmth and moisture, thinking it is time to grow in the soil. Keeping your storage barn well-ventilated, cool, and shaded delays early sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛwo hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Jwɛŋmɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ okwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oha otsu lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ bote mli jogbaŋŋ, eyɛ fɛ̃i, ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How can I stop my cassava roots from rotting in the ground during the rainy season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away to protect the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli koni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if the early rain is enough for me to start sowing my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Do not plant after just one rainy day. Wait until the rain penetrates deep into the soil (about hand-depth) and stays moist for a few consecutive days before planting.
ga: Kaadu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ gbi kome pɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. (aaafee o-palm lɛ dalɛ) ni oha ehi shi gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ dani okɛdu.

english: How do I recognize Fall Armyworm damage on my maize farm early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mayɔse Fall Armyworm nibii ni efite yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mra?

english: Look for ragged holes on young leaves at the center funnel of the maize plant, along with tiny sawdust-like waste. Finding this early allows you to treat the crop before major damage occurs.
ga: Taomɔ bu yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli. kɛfata he lɛ, fãji bibii ni tamɔ ŋmei Namɔ enɛ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohereɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala dani nɔ ko wulu baafite.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build strong green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why aren't my seeds coming up after I buried them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds planted too deep run out of stored energy before their shoots can push through the soil to reach sunlight. Planting seeds at a shallow depth—about two to three times the size of the seed—helps them sprout quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔɔɔ—aaafee dumɔwu lɛ dalɛ toi enyɔ loo shii etɛ—yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and ground nutrients. This competition makes the plants grow tall and thin, resulting in smaller cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bɛ kwraa.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves high up into the sunlight. When leaves get full sunlight, they create more energy for the plant, which leads to bigger and healthier yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa baa.

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or poor insect pollination. Maintaining shade trees and keeping soil moist helps flowers stay on the branches and grow into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao tso lɛ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ehiii Tso lɛ ni oooha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any peppers start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when temperatures get too high, water is given unevenly, or there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering and balanced fertilizer prevent the flowers from falling off early.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Ha nu ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi mra.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water cuts off oxygen to the roots and encourages soil fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds blow before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani kpamɔ baa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy and easy to push over. Supporting the stems with sturdy wooden poles helps them carry the heavy fruit without falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Ha efee nɔ ni tsii ni efee mlɛo akɛ oootsi. Tso ni wa ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa anyɛɔ awoɔ aduawai ni tsii ni agbeee shi.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that spread plant viruses. Protecting plants with insect nets or applying mild organic sprays like neem oil helps keep insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii abu tsei ahe loo akɛ tsofa ko ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ tamɔ neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Why are insects chewing holes in my cowpea leaves right after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-cowpea baai lɛ amli beni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young cowpea sprouts have soft, sweet leaves that attract pests like beetles and caterpillars. Spraying a mixture of neem leaf extract early in the morning creates a bitter barrier that keeps pests from eating the young shoots.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni akɛfutu mli lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni mli wa ni tsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds keep growing back so quickly on my land even after I clear the whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɛkɛ? Kɛji mijie ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ po?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil for a long time and quickly sprout whenever rain and sunlight hit the cleared ground. Removing weeds before they produce seeds or planting cover crops helps smother them and slow down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni hulu la baatswa he ni agbele lɛ. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi dani amɛya dumɔwui amli loo adu nɔ ko ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ ni amɛdaraa fioo.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil is low in nitrogen, an essential food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing trees like plantains next to them provides shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller crops when I plant many seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Giving each crop proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food to yield large produce.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu fioo, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ba tsei ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekpa nii babaoo.

english: What is causing small holes in my pepper leaves and making the fruits drop early?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi pepper baai lɛ anɔ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya?

english: Small holes and falling fruit are typically caused by insect pests like caterpillars or fruit flies feeding on the crop. Spraying natural neem water or appropriate insecticides can keep these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai amli ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii kɛ aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsi kooloi nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the bottom of my vegetable plants help them stay healthy in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the heat. It keeps the roots cool and damp, and slowly breaks down to feed the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ, baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i, ni fiofio lɛ, efiteɔ akɛ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer cassava tubers when I plant cassava on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmei shishifãi fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil over time. Rotating crops by planting beans or groundnuts after cassava restores vital nutrients to the earth naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛtsɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa adebɔɔ mli je lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable crops droop and look dead during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can absorb it from the soil. Watering early in the morning or late in the evening gives plants time to soak up moisture safely.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: Removing extra side branches, or suckers, prevents the tomato plant from wasting its energy on extra leaves. This directs all the plant's food toward growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baatsi tomato tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Enɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer right before a heavy downpour of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away off the farm before the roots have time to drink it in. Applying fertilizer when the soil is slightly damp—and not during heavy storms—ensures the crop actually absorbs it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii dani shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo—ni jeee yɛ ahum ni naa wa ko mli lɛ—baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aŋɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn brown when I cut down all the large shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Large trees provide natural shade and keep the surrounding air and soil moist, protecting sensitive cocoa seedlings from heat stress until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crops turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ adara ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people tell me that planting cowpeas or groundnuts will make my farm soil richer for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through root nodules. This acts as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni no gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to push long wooden stakes into the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa tso kakadaŋŋ ko lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum exposure to sunlight to create food for tuber development. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, improves sunlight intake, and prevents fungal diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha tuber lɛ shweremɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rains and winds arrive before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ba dani kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the ground. When heavy rain softens the soil and fruit bunches grow heavy, wind easily uproots them unless the stems are supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni aduawai akui lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi amli oya. ja tsɔne ko ni akɛ tso fee lɛ fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the plant from producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafee pepper lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on leaf sap, or by viruses transmitted by insects. Controlling these pests early stops leaf deformation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kudɔɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Ehaa baa lɛ fitemɔ kpaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or irregular watering. Severe temperature changes or water stress disrupt pollination, causing the plant to shed its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Dɔlɛ tsakemɔi ni naa wa loo nu mli haomɔ tsiɔ pollination naa. ha tsei afɔlɔ

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when the rainy season becomes extremely wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil deprives the roots of oxygen and creates damp conditions where soil fungi thrive and cause root decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni efee shihilɛ ni mli edɔ Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daa ni amɛhaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Repeatedly planting maize on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil continuously and allows maize-specific pests and soil diseases to build up in high numbers over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why should I avoid pouring water over my vegetable leaves during the middle of a hot, sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ nu ni mikɛshwieɔ aduawai ahe baai anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ he?

english: Watering under direct afternoon sun causes rapid evaporation before roots absorb moisture, and water drops on leaves can magnify heat or cause stress to sensitive foliage.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa hulutsoo baa oya dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Ni nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dɔlɛ aya hiɛ loo ekɛ haomɔ aba baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to mix chemical powder with our maize seeds before planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ okɛ tsofa powder afutu ŋmãa dumɔwui dani odu lɛ?

english: The chemical powder, known as seed dressing, protects the seeds underground from being eaten by insects, birds, and soil fungi so that almost every seed you plant can germinate successfully.
ga: Tsofa powda ni ale lɛ hu akɛ dumɔwui ahe tsofa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dumɔwui ahe koni ŋmeii, okpoi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akaye amɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu ni odu lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the plant juices. Spraying recommended organic treatments like neem oil or insecticides early helps protect young shoots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔse mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmeii bibii ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce tiny black pods that dry up on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Baai diji ni egbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning shade trees to let in sunlight and removing infected pods promptly stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ afolɔ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaakpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and produce heavy ears, so applying NPK or urea fertilizer at the right time fixes this.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ toi ni tsii aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: How does covering my soil with dry leaves and grass help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai kɛ jwɛi ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil, called mulching, keeps the ground moist by stopping sunlight from drying out the earth, blocks weeds from growing, and keeps crop roots cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ hulu la ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring regular watering during hot spells helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tsei ahe loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills air spaces in the soil with water, suffocating cassava roots and encouraging harmful fungi that cause root rot. Harvesting mature cassava before prolonged heavy rains prevents losses.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei ni eda dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni akafite.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting even when I store them in a cool barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams are living plant stems that naturally rest after harvest, but after a few months, internal triggers signal them to wake up and sprout to grow a new plant for the next season.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni amɛyaa wɔɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ Nɔ ko ni kanyaa amɛ yɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ amɛ akɛ amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei heei kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: How do I know if the weedkiller chemical I sprayed on my farm is working properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: A working weedkiller will cause weed leaves to wilt, turn yellow or brown, and dry up within three to seven days, showing that the chemical has successfully stopped the weed from growing.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni tsuɔ nii lɛ baaha jwɛi baai lɛ agbi. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni egbi yɛ gbii etɛ kɛyashi kpawo mli. Atsɔɔ akɛ tsofai yeɔ omanye ni amɛkpaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen if heavy rains flood the field and stop the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ ko nɔ nu ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why does my cassava produce big leafy stems above ground but very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich manure, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of tubers. Cassava needs potassium in the soil to build big, healthy roots underground.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ bulbs baatsu nii. Potassium he miihia cassava yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni shishifãi wuji ni mli wa akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to plant my seeds after the first rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil into a ball in your palm and let it drop. If it crumbles easily, it has the right moisture for seeds to sprout; if it turns into sticky mud, it is too wet; if it falls apart like dry dust, it is still too dry.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ fioo ko mli yɛ bɔɔlu mli yɛ onine mli ni oha eta shi. Kɛji efo mlɛo lɛ Fɛ̃i ni fa bɔ ni sa baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji etsɔ muji lɛ, no lɛ edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji efolɔ tamɔ sũ ni egbi No mli lɛ egbi tsɔ lolo.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the crop from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies that hide under the leaves, suck the plant juices, and spread diseases that stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi, ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni tsiɔ tso lɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are wilting because of hot sun or because of a soil disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hewɔ loo hela ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: If a plant wilts in the hot afternoon sun but stands up healthy again early in the morning, it is just thirsty or heat-stressed. If it stays droopy even in the cool morning, a soil disease or root rot is attacking it.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ gboi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Shi amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba hewalɛ ekoŋŋ leebi. Etsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye lɛ kɛkɛ loo eyɛ haomɔ kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli. Kɛji etee nɔ egbee shi yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli po lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ hela ji lɛ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ miitutua lɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin, weak, and fall over easily when I plant many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli tseee, egbɔjɔ ni egbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food. This forces them to stretch tall and thin to reach the sun, making their stems too weak to hold cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii ahe akaŋshii mli. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee shwiili bɔni afee ni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ emɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Is it good for me to plant cassava and maize on the same piece of land at the same time?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in three to four months, leaving plenty of room and light for the slower cassava to grow afterwards.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the soil is too dry, when temperatures get too high, or when there are no bees or wind to shake the pollen inside the flower to make fruit grow.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ ada.

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, which usually occurs when soil moisture jumps between very dry and very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ shwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees take much longer to produce fruit bunches during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ aduawai akui yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants need a lot of water to move nutrients from the soil up to the leaves and fruit. Without enough water, the plant slows down its growth process to survive, delaying fruit development.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya baai kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo.

english: Why is it important for me to harvest my cocoa pods on bright, sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii yɛ gbi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sunny weather allows you to open pods and begin drying the beans immediately under daylight. Prompt drying prevents moisture from building up inside the fresh beans, which stops mold and rot from destroying your crop.
ga: Hulu lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ ogbele ŋmeii lɛ ni obɔi kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ agbimɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɔfi ŋmɔji heei lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akafite onibii lɛ.

english: Does the time of day I harvest my cocoa pods make any difference to bean quality?
ga: Ani be ni akɛkpaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ baa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe?

english: Harvesting earlier in the day when there is good sunlight gives you maximum daylight hours to gather pods and extract beans so that fermentation and drying can start cleanly without night-time moisture settling on wet beans.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa ŋmaa lɛ mra yɛ gbi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha oná ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo ni okɛbua ŋmeii lɛ anaa ni okɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aje shishi yɛ gbɛ ni he tse nɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ akashɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I harvest my cocoa pods when it is actively raining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikpaa kookoo ŋmeii beni nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ?

english: Rain spreads fungal spores like black pod disease across your farm on tools and hands, and wet weather makes it difficult to start the crucial bean drying process immediately after opening pods.
ga: Nugbɔ gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ nitsumɔ dadei kɛ niji anɔ. Ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaaje ŋmeii ni he hiaa lɛ agbimɔ nitsumɔ lɛ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ŋmeii lɛ agbele amɛhe lɛ.

english: How does sunlight affect how my cocoa tree produces and ripens its pods?
ga: Te hulu la lɛ saa bɔ ni mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Sunlight provides energy for the tree to produce food through its leaves, which fuels pod growth, helps pods turn from green/red to yellow/orange, and increases overall bean yield.
ga: Hulu la haa tsei hewalɛ koni amɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfee niyenii. ni haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii/tsuru kɛyaa ŋmeii/ŋmei. ni eha ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ

english: Will picking ripe cocoa pods as soon as they are ready actually increase my yield?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni mikɛbaatsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, harvesting ripe pods promptly prevents energy waste on overripe pods and encourages the tree to direct its nutrients toward growing new pods and flowers for the next cycle.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni akpaa lɛ tsiɔ hewalɛ ni baa trukaa yɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ amli lɛ naa. ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa aba koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii kɛ fɔfɔi heei kɛha fã ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What happens if I leave fully ripe cocoa pods hanging on my trees for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Overripe pods attract pests, become breeding grounds for rot and black pod disease, and the beans inside can germinate or spoil, leading to lost income.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Ebafeɔ he ni helai kɛ ŋmeii diji fɔɔ yɛ. Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛfite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shika ni anáa lɛ ni laajeɔ

english: How often should I walk through my farm to harvest ripe pods during the peak season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayakpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni mɛi fa babaoo lɛ?

english: You should harvest regularly every two to three weeks during the main season so you catch pods at peak ripeness before diseases can settle in.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa nii be fɛɛ be. Otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ yɛ be titri lɛ mli Enɛ ji koni amɔmɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ dani hela lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Mature pods change color clearly; green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange or light yellow, signaling that the beans inside are fully formed.
ga: Pods ni eda kwraa lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su yɛ faŋŋ mli. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmɔtɔi ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ebɔi kwraa.

english: Does harvesting ripe pods right away help protect my remaining green pods from diseases?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni ajieɔ lɛ buɔ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, removing ripe pods removes potential sources of fungal infection, keeping the environment cleaner and safer for young, developing pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie he ni ŋmeii lɛ jɛɔ lɛ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli tseɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Should I gather every available ripe pod I see during a farm visit or wait until all trees are full?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabua ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni minaa yɛ be mli ni miyasaraa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ anaa loo mamɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ mli eyi?

english: You should harvest whatever ripe pods are available immediately rather than waiting, as leaving even a few ripe pods behind risks pod rot and pest infestation.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni yɔɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni ooomɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ eshwɛɔ. Oshara ni yɔɔ pod rot kɛ kooloi ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my groundnut plants turn yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe. While groundnuts fix their own nitrogen from the air using tiny bumps on their roots, poor soil conditions or bad root nodules can prevent them from getting enough food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ saa nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ he moŋ, shi shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo ŋmeii ni bɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant groundnuts in the exact same spot on my land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil every year depletes specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Rotating groundnuts with crops like maize or cassava breaks disease cycles and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛ tsei ahe helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Peanuts kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ. Efoɔ helai ni baa lɛ amli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut flowers fall off, and will I still get nuts from the crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ miiho ni ani maná ŋmeii kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lolo lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers are supposed to fall off after pollination. Once the flower drops, a small stem called a 'peg' grows downward and pushes itself into the soil, where the actual groundnut pod grows underground.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ agbo yɛ pollination sɛɛ. Kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi lɛ, tsei bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji bean pod diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up or fold together during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ ekome yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves fold or roll during the hottest parts of the day to protect themselves from losing too much water. By shrinking the area exposed to the sun, the plant saves moisture until the cool evening comes.
ga: Okɛ baai lɛ abɔ he loo okɛwo mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni obu ohe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ lɛ ni eeefee bibioo lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be baa.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my seeds too close together on my four acres?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni ji acre ejwɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with weak, thin plants that produce fewer pods and smaller nuts.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tso ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: When is the best time for me to weed my crop field so the plants grow strong?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeding should be done early, within the first 3 to 6 weeks after planting. Removing weeds while crops are young stops the weeds from stealing sunlight, water, and fertilizer before the crop leaves grow big enough to shade the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ mra, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 6 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aju hulu la, nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani tso lɛ baai lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Is it good for my soil if I grow maize and groundnuts together in the same field?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting maize and groundnuts together is very good for the land. Groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil, which helps feed heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni eshiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Can I put fresh manure from my goats and chickens directly around my young crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ too kɛ tsina ŋmei hee awo mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh animal manure is too strong and releases heat and chemical gases as it breaks down, which can burn young plant roots. It is best to dry and decompose manure in a pile for a few weeks before spreading it on your farm.
ga: Manure hee mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔ ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ tsofai fɔji kɛjɛɔ mli beni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii ashishifãi ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ofite yɛ ŋmeii amli otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛgbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I test if the groundnut seeds I saved from my last harvest are still good for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji akɛ ŋmei dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ hi lolo kɛha dumɔ?

english: You can test your seeds by placing 10 of them in a moist cloth in a warm spot for a few days. If 8 or more sprout, your seed batch is strong and ready to be planted in the field.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka dumɔwui lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ gbii fioo komɛi, kɛji akɛ 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui akuu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my groundnuts without digging up the whole crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Groundnuts are usually ready when the plant leaves start turning yellow and dry up. You can dig up just two or three test plants; if the inside of the pods has dark markings and the nuts fill out the shells, it is time to harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii efee klalo kɛji tso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ okɛ kaa tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ atsu nii. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli yɛ okadii diji ni ŋmeii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ, no lɛ be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient found in fertilizer or compost that helps crops grow strong and stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like potassium in the soil.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why is it risky to plant my crop seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often wet the surface soil without soaking deep enough, so if a dry spell follows, the newly sprouted seeds will dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛwooo mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji hɔmɔ ba nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the small shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to steal food and water from the main plant, which leads to small and weak plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantain tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when there are no bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense direct sunlight, so larger shade trees are needed to protect them like an umbrella until they mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei wuji abu kookoo tso lɛ he tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: What is causing the small ragged holes in the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ

english: Small holes in corn leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like fall armyworms that hide inside the central leaves and feed on the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why does my land yield less cassava when I plant it on the exact same field three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmei fioo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil, making it exhausted unless you rotate with nitrogen-fixing plants like cowpeas or groundnuts.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa sũ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ja okɛ tsei ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ amɛhe.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves toward sunlight so they can manufacture food efficiently, which directly expands the size of the tuber beneath the soil.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akwɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ amli alɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the leaves near the bottom turn yellow and fall off, and cracks start forming in the soil around the main stem.
