ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmeii jeɔ shishi efeɔ yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, tomato leaves lose moisture faster than roots can pull it from the ground, causing the plant to temporarily droop to conserve water until evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ tomato tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni nu ahi mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when heavy rain falls for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for a long time. This drowns the roots by blocking air and allows harmful soil fungi to grow and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to spread dry grass around the stems of my crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwie miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around your crops acts like a protective blanket. It blocks the hot sun from drying out the dirt, keeping the soil moist and cool so your crops do not dry up quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Nibii ni adu lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa muji agbi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi oya.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to settle well before planting my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: If you plant after just one quick rainfall, the seeds may sprout and then quickly dry up and die if the sun returns for a week without more rain to sustain them.
ga: Kɛji odu yɛ nugbɔ kuku ko sɛɛ shikome pɛ Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi oya ni amɛgboi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba otsi kome ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ni baaye abua amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning light yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food in the soil. It can also happen when the soil is waterlogged and the plant cannot feed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tsei nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves or passing a leaf disease to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli loo ni gbɛɔ foliary hela kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my main crops to stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ afee bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for survival. They drink the soil water, steal the plant food you apply, and block sunlight from reaching your crop leaves.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhi shi. Amɛnuɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ amli. ni otsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot survive direct harsh sunlight. They need shade trees over them to filter the sun and keep the air cool while they are establishing roots.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu la lɛ mli ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no bees around to move pollen inside the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baajie pollen awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it good for my soil to plant beans or cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii fataa mi-ŋmei lɛ he lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that grab good plant food from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally feeds the soil and helps your maize grow better.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ tsei niyenii kpakpai. kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I prune or cut off extra branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo majie niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that waste plant energy, forcing the crop to send all its water and food into growing larger, healthier fruit instead of just leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni he ehiaaa ni fiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ atsu enu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ he nii koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. yɛ baai kɛkɛ najiaŋ

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like whiteflies or thrips that spread viruses. The plant curls its leaves as a reaction to the infection and pest stress, which slows down its growth if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Tsei baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe haomɔ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the temperature gets too high or when the plant lacks sufficient water and soil nutrients. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to save energy by dropping flowers instead of growing fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Ekɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni ejieɔ yɛ aduawai ni ekwɛɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there holes in my young maize leaves with tiny brown dust inside the central stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ sũ bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? Yɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The pest feeds on the soft inner leaves of the growing maize plant and leaves behind waste that looks like fine sawdust.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli baai bibii lɛ. ni eshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei kpakpai.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight. They require temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava planted nearby to protect their delicate leaves from heat while their root systems establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ tswaa amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts make the soil better for my next season's maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii adumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. After harvest, that left-over nitrogen feeds the soil and helps future crops like maize grow greener and stronger.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Akɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to be moist after rain before putting fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying dry fertilizer to dry soil can burn the roots and cause the fertilizer to evaporate or blow away without benefiting the crop.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ la loo efo kɛya, ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ ko kwraa baaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like straws during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during intense heat as a natural defense mechanism to conserve water. Reducing the leaf surface area exposed to the sun helps the plant slow down water loss through evaporation.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa nu ni amɛlaajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground when the rains become very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require well-drained soil with air pockets to breathe. When heavy rains cause water to pool in the soil without draining, it smothers the roots and promotes fungal rot underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ amu lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to cut off the small extra shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, known as suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers ensures the main tree gets maximum energy to produce larger bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ babaoo ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee panicle agbo.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need maximum exposure to sunlight to generate food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows the leaves to catch more sun and airflow, which helps the plant build larger tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its lower leaves when the weather gets dry to save water and protect itself until the rains return.
ga: Cassava baagbee shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when the plant lacks sufficient water, which stops the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ baaha tomato fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small holes eaten through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by pests like fall armyworms feeding on the soft leaves, which can reduce your yield if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ baa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and making the plant stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaves and spreading viruses to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper mli lɛ baa.

english: Why should I remove some of the young shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many young shoots (suckers) forces the main plantain tree to share food and water, which results in much smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii bibii babaoo (ŋmeii) lɛ, ebaanyɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu aha. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture enough sunlight to produce energy, which directly helps the underground yam tuber grow big and heavy.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off some branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mifolɔ kookoo niji komɛi ni edara lɛ?

english: Pruning lets sunlight and fresh air inside the cocoa tree, which prevents diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa baa kookoo tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji anaa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil better for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally feeding the soil with free nutrients for your next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the soil when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil starves the underground cassava roots of air, causing fungal rot to develop before you get the chance to harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akafee ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa fungal rot baa dani onáa hegbɛ ni okpa ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why does rice grow better when there is standing water on the field compared to maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants are adapted to thrive in wet conditions where standing water stops harmful weeds from growing and keeps nutrients accessible to the roots.
ga: Atsakeɔ ŋmãa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni nu damɔ shi yɛ lɛ koni jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akakwɛ̃, ni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why should I seal or paint over a fresh cut on my cocoa tree branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo mafee kookoo niji ni afo ehee lɛ he mfoniri?

english: When you cut a cocoa branch, it creates an open wound on the tree. Applying a protective sealant immediately keeps rain, insects, and fungal diseases from entering the fresh cut and causing rot.
ga: Kɛji ofo kookoo nine Ebaaha pilamɔi ni agbele aba tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ wo loo lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ ŋmeii ahe helai anaa koni amɛkabote loo hee lɛ mli ni amɛha egbo.

english: How quickly do I need to apply sealant after I finish pruning my cocoa tree branches?
ga: Beni mifolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ agbe naa lɛ Etsɛ tɛŋŋ ehe baahia ni mikɛ tsofa ni haaa nu abote mli lɛ awo mli?

english: You should apply the sealing compound right after making the cut while the wound is fresh. Delaying allows pests and airborne spores to settle inside the exposed wood.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ awo pilamɔ lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni eyɛ ehee lolo lɛ. Be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ hiɔ tso ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my cocoa tree if I leave freshly pruned edges open to the rain?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi ŋwɛigbɛi ni afolɔ ehee lɛ koni nugbɔ lɛ anɛ?

english: Unsealed cuts collect rainwater, which creates a warm, wet environment for fungus to grow. This fungal growth can cause the branch or main trunk to rot from the inside.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ni atsĩii naa lɛ buaa nugbɔ nu naa, ni no haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akwɛ̃. Nɛkɛ ŋmei nɛɛ dalɛ baanyɛ aha tsei niji loo tso titri lɛ agbo kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to trim and prune the edges of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Pruning removes overcrowded and unproductive branches, allowing sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree while helping you spot and manage disease early.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wooo yibii lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni oyɔseɔ hela lɛ mra ni okwɛɔ nɔ.

english: Can diseases spread from one tree to another when I cut my cocoa branches?
ga: Ani hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ kɛ́ mifolɔ kookoo niji?

english: Yes, airborne fungal spores easily invade open wounds left on freshly cut branches. Sealing the cuts blocks these spores from establishing an infection that could spread to nearby trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ atutua pilamɔi ni agbele yɛ tsei niji ni afo ehee lɛ anɔ. mlɛo Kɛ́ atsi he ni afo lɛ naa lɛ, ehaaa nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akafee hela ko ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Is it really necessary for me to spend money on tree cut sealing paste for my farm?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafite shika yɛ tso ni akɛfoɔ tsei ahe lɛ he tsofa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, using tree sealant acts like a protective bandage. It saves you money in the long run by preventing serious infections that can destroy mature, pod-producing cocoa trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa onáa shika yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛtsɔ helai ni naa wa ni baanyɛ agbe cacao tsei ni eda kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni etsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if an unsealed branch cut on my cocoa tree is rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei niji ni afolɔ yɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifite?

english: If the cut area turns soft, dark brown, or black, or if you see fuzzy mold or smelly fluid oozing from the cut surface, the branch wound is infected and rotting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ he ni afo lɛ batsɔ la lɛ, eji ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ, loo kɛji ona ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ faŋŋ loo nu ni shãa mɔ ni miiho kɛmiijɛ hewolo ni afo lɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela emɔ pilamɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lɛ ni egbo.

english: Does the way I cut a branch off my cocoa tree affect how well it heals?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ kookoo tsei lɛ saa kookoo tso lɛ he?

english: Yes, making a clean, smooth cut makes it much easier to coat the entire wound completely with sealant, helping the tree grow fresh bark over the cut smoothly.
ga: Hɛɛ, fã ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ akɛ nɔ ko ni akɛfiɔ pilamɔ he lɛ baawo pilamɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii heei jogbaŋŋ yɛ pilamɔi anɔ.

english: Can I use regular mud to cover the cut branches on my cocoa trees instead of buying sealant?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ muji ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ aha tsei niji ni afo yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni mahe nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, mud contains moisture and soil bacteria that can actually trap fungus inside the open wood. Chemical or wax-based tree sealants are formulated to repel water and kill germs.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ sũ mli helai ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso ni agbele lɛ mli lɛ yɛ muji mli. Afee nibii ni akɛ tsofai loo wax fee lɛ koni ekɛshwie nu ni egbe helai ni gbeɔ mɔ.

english: Should I apply wound sealant to my cocoa trees during both the wet and dry seasons?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛfiɔ pilamɔi ahe lɛ atsu nii yɛ cacao nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be fɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, sealing cuts is crucial in both seasons. In the wet season it blocks moisture and fungal spores, while in the dry season it prevents the tree from losing vital water through the cut.
ga: Hɛɛ, seal ŋmɔmɔ he hiaa yɛ bei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli. Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, etsĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa. yɛ be mli ni yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaje nu ni he hiaa lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark conditions. Spraying approved fungicides and cutting away dense, shady branches lets sunlight in to keep your pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ. Akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ ni afoɔ tsei niji ni mli ewo muji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha hulu la abote mli koni eha o-pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to spray chemical medicine on my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofai afɔ kookoo tsei anɔ?

english: You should spray early in the rainy season when fungal diseases start to breed, and during early morning or late afternoon hours when there is little wind so the medicine sticks properly to the leaves and pods.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni tsɛŋemɔ helai jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. kɛ leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ ni baaha tsofa lɛ akpɛtɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What causes insects to attack my crops more during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: In dry weather, pests look for water inside green stems and leaves to survive. Because heavy rains are not washing them away, their population grows faster and damages crops more aggressively.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ, ŋmeii taoɔ nu yɛ tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛhi shi. Ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ shwieee amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛyibɔ ​​yaa hiɛ oya ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant food that keeps leaves healthy and green. Adding fertilizer or animal manure restores this nutrient to the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni efeɔ eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ etɔ ni ehe miihia ni aha lɛ niyenii?

english: Tired soil produces smaller crop yields, weak stems, and pale leaves, and weeds may start taking over easily because the earth has run out of vital nutrients from continuous planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, tsei lɛ ahe waaa kɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni jwɛi baanyɛ aje shishi amɛye nɔ oya ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ daa lɛ mli baa.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from water stress, pest damage, or lack of nutrients. Keeping soil moist and protecting blossoms from insects helps those flowers turn into full pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. Akpãtãa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahiɛ. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Pruning extra branches allows fresh air and light to circulate through the canopy. This prevents disease-causing dampness and helps the tree direct its energy into growing big pods instead of excess leaves.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ la hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ hela baa lɛ naa, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔi wuji ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai ni fa fe nine baatsu nii.

english: Why do my young crop shoots dry up quickly even when it rains a little bit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ fioo po lɛ?

english: Young plant roots are very short and stay near the surface where intense hot sun dries out the topsoil fast. Giving them partial shade or mulching around the roots holds moisture in the ground longer.
ga: Tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ yɛ kuku waa ni amɛbɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ, he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbiɔ oya lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo fã ko ha loo okɛ sũ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last harvest give me smaller yields than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and can carry hidden diseases. Certified seeds are bred specifically to resist local pests and produce uniform, high-yielding crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ aba. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be

english: How does planting plantains alongside my cassava help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantain ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Planting different crops together provides natural shade, prevents soil erosion during heavy rains, and slows down the spread of pests that usually target single crops.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni bei pii lɛ amɛtutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii komekomei lɛ agbɛfaŋ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in straight lines across my farm instead of just scattering them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu kɛkɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines helps organize your field, making it easier to care for the plants and clearly observe how evenly the seedlings sprout and come up from the soil.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atoɔ he lɛ he gbɛjianɔ. Ehaa tsei akwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo Ni obaanyɛ ona bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ daa ni amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How will I know if my seeds are sprouting properly after I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ midumɔwui lɛ miikwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When you plant in marked lines, it is easy to check along the rows to see if green shoots are coming up uniformly above the ground.
ga: Kɛji odu yɛ ŋmeii ni akadi lɛ anɔ lɛ Ewaaa akɛ oookwɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ koni ona kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Can an extension officer show me the exact method to plant my seeds correctly?
ga: Ani extension nitsulɔi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ mi gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ dumɔwui?

english: Yes, agricultural officers can guide you through making proper lines and demonstrating the right planting steps so your crop emerges successfully.
ga: Hɛɛ, wɔ okwaayeli nitsulɔi lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ bo yɛ gbɛi ni ja nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ bo gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I am buying seeds, what is the difference between a three-month crop and a four-month crop?
ga: Kɛji miheɔ dumɔwui Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ nyɔji etɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nyɔji ejwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ?

english: A three-month crop is a fast-growing variety that matures quickly for an early harvest, while a four-month crop takes a longer time to complete its growth cycle.
ga: Nyɔji etɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni daa oya ni baakwɛ̃ oya kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa mra. Yɛ be mli ni tso ni yeɔ nyɔji ejwɛ lɛ baahe be babaoo dani egbe edalɛ be lɛ naa lɛ.

english: How do I choose which seed variety to buy when preparing for the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni esa akɛ mahe beni miisaa mihe kɛha be lɛ?

english: You can select seeds based on how fast you want them to grow, choosing a quick three-month variety or a four-month variety depending on your rainfall and farm schedule.
ga: Obaanyɛ ohala dumɔwui yɛ bɔ ni osumɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ nyɔji etɛ loo nyɔji ejwɛ express henɔi ni oooha lɛ nɔ. Edamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ kɛ be ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of the seed varieties I buy take longer to grow than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni miheɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Different plant varieties have distinct growth behaviors; some are bred to mature quickly within three months, while others naturally require four months to reach harvest.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Afɔ kooloi srɔtoi komɛi koni amɛdara oya yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ nyɔji ejwɛ dani amɛkpaa nii.

english: If I plant a three-month crop variety, will it give me food or income faster than a four-month variety?
ga: Kɛji midu tso ni eye nyɔji etɛ Ani ebaaha niyenii loo shika oya fe tso ni eye nyɔji ejwɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, three-month varieties grow rapidly and reach maturity earlier, allowing you to harvest sooner than you would with a four-month variety.
ga: Hɛɛ, nyɔji 3 srɔtoi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa oya. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nyɔji 4 mra fe srɔtoi lɛ.

english: If I buy a fast-growing three-month seed variety, do I need to plant it differently than a four-month variety?
ga: Kɛ mihe dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli Ani esa akɛ madu lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe nyɔji ejwɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yes, short-duration varieties like the three-month crop often have specific planting methods to ensure they establish quickly and yield well within their short timeframe.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kukuoo, tamɔ tsei ni yeɔ nyɔji etɛ lɛ yɛ gbɛi pɔtɛɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛdaraa koni amɛkwɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why is it important for me to ask about the maturity time of seeds before buying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabi be ni midumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ lɛ he sane dani mahe lɛ?

english: Knowing whether a seed is a three-month or four-month variety helps you adopt the correct planting technique and plan your seasonal farm work properly.
ga: Kɛ́ ole kɛji dumɔwu ko eye nyɔji etɛ loo ejwɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ gbɛi ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ atsu nii ni oto oŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ naa.

english: Does a four-month crop variety grow at the same speed as a three-month variety?
ga: Ani nyɔji ejwɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ daa oya tamɔ nyɔji etɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: No, a four-month variety develops at a slower pace over a longer period, whereas a three-month variety is designed for faster growth and early maturity.
ga: Dabi, nyɔji ejwɛ mli henɔi lɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Yɛ be mli ni afee nyɔji etɛ srɔtoi lɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why should I plant another crop in the empty spaces between my main crops instead of leaving the land clear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei krokomɛi yɛ he ni kã miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Instead of leaving the area open

english: Planting useful secondary crops in empty spaces makes full use of your land, reduces space for weeds to grow, and provides extra food or income before your main crop matures.
ga: Nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni ji enyɔ ni ooodu yɛ hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ he ni jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ niyenii loo shika kroko aha dani onibii titri lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to plant quick-growing crops like maize in the open spaces between my cassava plants?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ he ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, because maize matures fast and is harvested in about three to four months, long before the cassava grows large enough to spread and cover the whole field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Dani ŋmei lɛ baatsɔ agbo bɔ ni sa ni egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: If I plant two different crops in the same field spaces, won't they fight over nutrients and water?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, Ani tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe etswaŋ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ?

english: They will not fight if chosen correctly. Crops with shallow roots and deep roots feeder from different soil levels, and some crops even share nutrients with their neighbors.
ga: Amɛwuuu kɛji amɛhala nɔ ni ja. Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi anɔ. Ni tsei komɛi po kɛ amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ jaa niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why is it better to measure spaces and plant in straight rows instead of scattering my seeds freely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooosusu he ni odu lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ? Mohu ɔ, a gbaa dumɔwu ɔmɛ yaka.

english: Row planting ensures every plant gets equal access to sunlight and soil nutrients, while leaving clear paths for you to walk, weed, and apply fertilizer easily.
ga: Row dumɔ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eshiɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ehaa bo ni obaanyɛ onyiɛ, okɛ jwɛi atsu nii, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli mlɛo.

english: How do I know if my crops are planted too close to each other in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ adu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If crops are too close, they will stretch up tall and thin competing for light, have yellowish leaves, and produce very small or weak yields.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee mlɛo koni amɛye la he akaŋ, amɛbaaná baai ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo loo amɛwoɔ yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kwraa.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant tall plantains in the spaces next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ midu dumɔwui kakadaji yɛ he ni mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get burned easily by intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains create wide leaves that provide living umbrella shade and retain soil moisture for young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ kɛhaa kookoo bibii lɛ.

english: What happens to my smaller crops if the crops planted in between them grow too tall?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji tsei ni kwɛ̃ yɛ teŋ lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ?

english: If neighboring crops block all sunlight, the smaller crops will become weak and stunted. You must prune or harvest the taller crop to let sunlight through.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsi hulu la lɛ naa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ loo okpa tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni hulu la atsɔ mli.

english: Why is it good to plant beans or groundnuts in the spaces between my main crop rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni miduɔ titri lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the ground, naturally fertilizing the soil for neighboring plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ

english: How does planting crops in between empty spaces help keep my soil moist during hot periods?
ga: Te tsei ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Leafy crops act as a green cover over the soil, shading the ground from direct hot sun and keeping water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ eŋɔli. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. ni etsĩ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya.

english: Can covering empty field spaces with leafy crops reduce how often I have to weed my farm?
ga: Ani tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni akɛhaa hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, because leafy plants block sunlight from hitting the bare soil, preventing dormant weed seeds from germinating and taking over your land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Tsɔɔmɔ ni oŋɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ

english: Why should I treat or spray my crop seeds before planting them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsu midumɔwui lɛ ahe nii loo mafɔ amɛ nɔ dani madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Treating seeds before planting acts like a protective vaccine. It prevents soil-borne fungi and insects from destroying the seeds before they can germinate and grow into healthy crops.
ga: Dumɔwui akwɛmɔ dani adu lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ koolooi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akafite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants get leaf spots and rot when I let weeds grow thick around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ baa nɔ tsɔi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ miha jwɛi shwere babaoo yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds trap humidity and hold unwanted pests and plant diseases close to your crops. Keeping the base of your plants clean allows air to flow, which prevents fungal diseases from destroying your tomatoes.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai ni ataooo lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ onibii lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ shishitoo lɛ he tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akafite tomatoi lɛ.

english: What happens to my maize plants if I do not add fertilizer or manure to the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Crops need proper feeding just like animals. Without fertilizer or nutrient-rich compost, maize plants become weak, turn yellow, and produce small, underformed cobs.
ga: Niyenii ni sa he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ kooloi pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ lɛ Abele tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ. etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛhe bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn pale yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your crop is hungry for key soil nutrients like nitrogen. Giving the soil organic manure or fertilizer restores the green color and helps build large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ he hɔmɔ miiye onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ humus loo organic fertilizer wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua ni afee ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die when planted in open sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains creates a cool umbrella that protects the young cocoa until it gets older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ baa.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around yam mounds with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool and prevents precious moisture from evaporating, protecting the underground yam tubers from drying out.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni jara wa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Buu sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Can I plant special flowers or crops around my farm to attract pests away from my vegetables?
ga: I can plant flowers or special crops around it. Ani manyɛ mafee okwaayeli koni mikɛgbala tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛ mi-aduawai lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, planting certain border plants (trap crops) draws destructive insects away from your main crops onto those border plants, keeping your valuable harvest safe.
ga: Hɛɛ, husu nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi (trap plants) ni ooodu lɛ baagbala kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ he kɛba nakai husu nɔ tsei lɛ anɔ. Koni onibii ni jara wa lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why is it bad to pour water over the top leaves of my pepper plants in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ ooofɔse nu yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water droplets on leaves during hot hours can burn the plant tissue and create wet conditions that invite leaf diseases. It is best to water directly at the root base early in the morning.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ mli fãji ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ mli hela aba lɛ aba. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ leebi.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak stalks and poor yield.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why should I prune off the small extra branches on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Jiemɔ ŋmei lɛ kɛjɛ tomato lɛ mli.

english: Removing non-essential side branches (suckers) directs all the plant's energy and food into producing larger, healthier fruit rather than extra unnecessary foliage.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa (tso lɛ yibii) ni ajieɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii fɛɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe baai krokomɛi ni he ehiaaa ni ashɛrɛ ashwie.

english: Why do my maize plants produce smaller cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the roots and leaves compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to grow big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my land stay fertile?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni akɛfataa ŋmãa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa?

english: Cowpeas and other leguminous plants take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Maize uses a lot of nitrogen to grow, so planting cowpeas alongside maize acts like a natural fertilizer boost.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi kɛ nitrogen babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni akɛfataa ŋmãa he.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing on cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant stems prevents this virus from destroying your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ odu tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akafite onibii.

english: Why is it better to leave cleared weeds to decay on the farm instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ koni amɛgbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni aaashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Burning cleared weeds destroys good soil nutrients and kills helpful earthworms. Leaving the weeds on top of the soil acts as mulch, keeping the ground cool, retaining moisture, and feeding the soil as it decays.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ajɔɔ Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: How can buying improved seed varieties from the agro-dealer help me harvest more food than using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ baaye abua mi ni makpã niyenii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛbaahere kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ mli lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are bred to naturally resist common Ghanaian crop diseases and endure dry spells better. They produce higher yields and grow more uniformly than older saved seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ Ghana tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛyeɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ fe dumɔwui momo ni ato.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the leaves of my cabbage plants damaging my final harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ fiteɔ mi-naagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Leaves act as the plant's food factory by catching sunlight to make energy. When caterpillars destroy the leaves, the plant loses its ability to feed itself and cannot form a strong, solid head of cabbage.
ga: Baai tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhe kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛmɔɔ koni ekɛfee hewalɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ kpata baai lɛ ahiɛ Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ eye ehe niyenii dɔŋŋ, ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ kaabe yitsei ni wa ni wa aba.

english: Why do my tomato leaves drop and wilt in the afternoon heat even when the ground feels wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During extreme afternoon heat, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it from the wet soil. Watering very early in the morning helps the plants build up water reserves before the sun gets too hot.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ebuaa nu naa dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if I delay planting until weeks after the major rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛ otsii babaoo to dumɔ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rains release a large flush of nitrogen trapped in the dry soil. Planting early allows your young crops to capture this natural nutrient boost and avoid high pest populations that build up later in the season.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ jieɔ nitrogen babaoo ni emɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ kpo. Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli niyenii. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo ni baabua amɛhe naa yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil and get insects so quickly in normal sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni kooloi bibii woɔ kotokui ni afɔɔ namɔ amli oya lɛ?

english: Normal woven sacks allow air and humidity to reach the grain, encouraging mold growth and giving insects like weevils room to breathe and reproduce. Using airtight hermetic bags starves pests of oxygen and keeps grains dry.
ga: Baagi ni akpɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shɛɔ ŋmaa lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni ehaa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ muɔ ni amɛfɔɔ bii. Kɛ́ akɛ vacuum bags tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ, ni ebaaha ŋmaa lɛ agbi.

english: Why does my land produce less food every year when I plant the same crop on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly draws out the exact same nutrients from the topsoil without giving it time to replenish. Rotating different crops or adding compost helps restore balance and keeps the soil productive.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ be haaa koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ Nibii srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ Loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct intense sunlight. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides necessary shade to keep the soil moist and protect the young leaves from burning.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii duɔ lɛ baaha amɛná hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha baai bibii lɛ akashã.

english: Which way should I point the buds when planting my cassava stem cuttings in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: You should always plant cassava cuttings with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky so that the stems can easily sprout above ground and grow properly.
ga: Esa akɛ odu yucca tsei niji ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to fully settle before planting my crops instead of planting right after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa lɛ fɛɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell. If you plant too early, your seeds will sprout and then dry up and die in the hot soil before the continuous rains arrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with tall sticks as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ niji kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Staking exposes the yam leaves to direct sunlight, allowing the plant to capture light and make more food, which results in larger tubers underground.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ la babaoo ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when the plant experiences water stress, which prevents successful pollination and fruit formation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ naa.

english: How do groundnuts help make my soil better for maize planted in the next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii?

english: Groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots. When the roots decay after harvest, they leave this nitrogen in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ Amɛshiɔ nitrogen nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛye ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do sword suckers grow better than broad-leafed suckers when planting new plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ klante tsei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni shwieɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛ́ adu plantains heei lɛ?

english: Sword suckers have a stronger root system and pointed leaves, allowing them to establish faster and yield heavier bunches compared to broad-leafed suckers.
ga: Klante tsei lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa amɛtoɔ amɛhe shi oya ni amɛwoɔ aduawai akui ni tsii fe ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing in a V-shape indicates that the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy green leaves and strong growth.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ ni hi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or by a virus spread by whiteflies feeding on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yeɔ baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves with dark dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni muji ni tsuɔ waa yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the leaf whorl, and the dark dirt is the waste left behind by the pest.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni muji ni tsuɔ waa ji jwɛi ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shĩɔ yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I plant my maize in straight lines with measured spaces instead of just scattering the seeds across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni sɛɛ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ

english: Planting in straight lines with proper spacing ensures every maize plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛkwɛ̃. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: Why do experienced cocoa farmers always plant plantains right next to their new baby cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Be fɛɛ be lɛ, afɔɔ kookoo tsei ehee.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under the harsh sun. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist for young cocoa trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hia kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛha kookoo tsei bibii.

english: Why do I need to make big soil mounds to plant my yams instead of just digging small holes in the flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe bahia ni ama gɔŋ agbo ko ni akɛduɔ ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofo bu bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to expand and grow long and thick. Soil mounds give tubers soft earth to grow easily while preventing water from gathering around the roots and causing rot.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara ni amɛdara ni amɛfee shwiili. Gɔŋ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa sũ mli ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃, yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: How do I know if my soil is rich enough to grow healthy cassava without buying chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni miheee tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ?

english: Dark, soft soil filled with broken-down leaves and organic matter is naturally rich. If your soil is very pale or hard and sandy, adding animal manure or compost will help give your cassava the nutrients it needs to produce big roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ediŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ baai ni egbee shi kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa loo ewa ni eyɛ ŋã Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo kooloi ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni shishifãi wuji lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for nitrogen. Heavy rains can wash away nutrients in the topsoil, so adding fertilizer or compost will help your maize regain its green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during hot afternoons to save water by reducing the surface area exposed to direct heat. It is a natural way for the plant to protect itself from drying out when temperatures are very high.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi he ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ nɔ. Eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ he.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any peppers actually start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very high heat, extreme dryness, or lack of soil nutrients. Keeping moisture steady around the roots helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops, and why do they hurt my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally wild and tough, so they quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil food meant for your crops. Removing weeds early stops them from starving your plants and reducing your final yield.
ga: Jwɛi ji jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu onibii lɛ amli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baatsi hɔmɔ ni tsei lɛ yeɔ lɛ naa, ni ebaaha naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: What is causing tiny holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: Holes in the inner leaves of young corn are usually caused by caterpillars like fall armyworms feeding inside the center stalk. Catching them early and applying recommended pest treatments saves the growing point of the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ, ni egbee shi koni amɛbaye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni akwɛ he ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa yɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it really necessary for me to tie my tomato plants to wooden sticks as they grow taller?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ tsei ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Staking holds your tomato branches off the wet ground, keeping the leaves and tomatoes clean. This stops soil-dwelling insects from eating your crop and prevents wet-soil fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ tomato niji kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni baai kɛ tomatoi ahe atse Enɛ haaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii helai lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do some parts of my farmland need more fertilizer than other parts to grow cocoa well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ fãi komɛi ahe hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? Koni adu kookoo kpakpa

english: Soil quality varies across different spots on the same land. Areas with poor soil or heavy weed growth lose nutrients faster, so crops in those specific spots require extra fertilizer to get the nutrients needed to produce healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha yɛ hei srɔtoi. yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ nɔ Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo jwɛi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ baafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nakai hei pɔtɛɛi lɛ ahe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to throw government-supplied fertilizer directly onto dry soil around my cocoa trunks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashɛrɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ashwie shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi cacao lɛ ji nɔ fɔŋ.

english: Fertilizer applied directly onto dry stems or dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste nutrients through evaporation. Fertilizer must be applied in moist soil around the tree's outer drip line so the roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ niyenii ni fiteɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ. Drip line ni yɔɔ tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe

english: How do wild weeds growing close to my cocoa seedlings affect the fertilizer I apply?
ga: Te koo mli jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-koko dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients away from young cocoa seedlings, leaving the crop starving and slowing its growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ ni edalɛ baa shi.

english: I noticed a strange parasite growing on my cocoa branches that locals call agyana; how does it affect my crop?
ga: Miyɔse tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni miida yɛ mikookoo niji lɛ anɔ. ni maŋbii lɛ tsɛɔ lɛ Aguiana Te enaa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Agyana is a parasitic plant that attaches directly to cocoa branches and drains the water and food meant for the cocoa tree. Over time, this weakens the tree, reduces pod yield, and can dry out entire branches if it is not pruned off.
ga: Agyana ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ kookoo niji ahe tɛ̃ɛ, ni ehaa nu kɛ niyenii haa kookoo tso lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ehaa ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ niji muu fɛɛ agbi kɛji akɛ afolɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are ready to be harvested?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungal attack that thrives in overly damp, crowded, or heavily shaded farms. Excessive moisture allows fungal spores to spread quickly across developing pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ tsɔ, mɛi eyi mli obɔ, loo hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: What causes my young cocoa trees to turn yellow and drop leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaai shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and delicate leaves that lose moisture quickly in direct heat. Without adequate soil moisture or shade protection, heat stress causes the leaves to yellow and fall off.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ shɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛmli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Heat stress haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why do cocoa trees grow very well in some Ghanaian villages but struggle to yield in neighboring areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana akrowai komɛi amli lɛ? Shi esa akɛ amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ waa koni amɛná nibii ni amɛduɔ yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Cocoa requires rich, deep forest soil and reliable rainfall. Neighboring villages might have different soil types, such as rocky or sandy soil, that do not retain water or nutrients as effectively.
ga: Cocoa biɔ koo shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Akrowai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ aná sũ henɔi srɔtoi, tamɔ tɛ sũ loo ŋã. ni nyɛŋ ato nu loo niyenii kpakpai ahe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but only a few turn into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers require tiny insects like midges for pollination alongside adequate plant nutrients. If the tree lacks nutrients or faces drought stress, it will shed unpollinated or weak flowers naturally.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii biɔ kooloi bibii akɛ nɔ ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛfata tso lɛ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa he. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo ekɛ hɔmɔ haomɔ kpeɔ. Tsei ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ amɛhe loo amɛfɔfɔi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baajɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwie shi.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend leaving large shade trees on cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ ashi tsei wuji yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Large shade trees shield delicate cocoa leaves from harsh sunlight, keep the soil cool, and prevent the farm from drying out completely during long heat waves.
ga: Tsei ni eda ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why does cutting off extra branches on my cocoa trees help them produce bigger cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni niji krokomɛi ni fata he ni mifoɔ yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ cocoa ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-essential branches so the tree does not waste valuable water and nutrients on useless leaves. It directs all energy straight into developing large, healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akafite nu kɛ niyenii ni jara wa yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Etsɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make food, or that the plant is getting too much water around its roots. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps restore green, healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛfee niyenii loo tsei miiná nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores nutrients like nitrogen naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing, usually a few weeks after germination and again during flowering. Applying it during heavy rain will wash it away, while applying it during dry weather can burn plant roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei miida jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛ́ okɛtsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaafɔ ehe. Yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso shishifãi ashã.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in harsh sunlight. They require partial shade from nurse crops like plantain or shade trees for their first two to three years to retain moisture and survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli koni amɛná hulutsoo ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting too close causes crops to compete aggressively with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants with smaller yields compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni sa lɛ ahe.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit, making them top-heavy and easy for wind to tip over. Supporting the stems with strong wooden props helps keep them standing until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo ni egbeeɔ shi oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Cassava root rot usually happens when excess water stays trapped around the roots in poorly drained or waterlogged soils. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps extra rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bote shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely hot, when soil moisture changes drastically from dry to wet, or when small insects attack the blossoms. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps prevent this.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: How do weeds harm my crops if there is plenty of space on the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Even with open space, weeds steal fertilizers, water, and sunlight directly from the soil surrounding your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get the nourishment needed to grow well.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ eji he ko ni agbele moŋ, shi jwɛi hu juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha otsei titrii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I use natural solutions like neem leaves to protect my crops from insect attacks?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ adebɔɔ mli tsabaai tamɔ neem baai abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, crushing neem leaves in water creates a natural spray that repels many chewing and sucking insects without harming crops or soil, making it a safe and affordable pest control method.
ga: Hɛɛ, neem baai ni akumɔ awo nu mli lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni shwieɔ kooloi srɔtoi babaoo ni shwieɔ nii ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ baa ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ awui. Enɛ haa efeɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni jara waaa ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and build strong stems. Applying manure or nitrogen fertilizer early helps the leaves turn green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ mli ni amɛma tsei ashishifãi ni wa. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he mra Ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress, irregular watering, or a shortage of essential plant nutrients like potassium and calcium during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tsei, tamɔ potassium kɛ calcium ni bɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide necessary shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes its roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shishifãi shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my crops too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This produces weak, tall stalks with smaller yields and makes it easier for diseases to spread.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo, ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo.

english: How can I tell if caterpillars are attacking my maize field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Caterpillars, such as the Fall Armyworm, leave ragged holes with torn edges on leaves and deposit moist, sawdust-like dirt inside the center whorl of the maize plant.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ shĩɔ bu ni etsilɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni etse yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. ni ebuaa muji ni mli efɔ ni tamɔ ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ naa yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is transmitted by tiny whitefly insects that suck sap from the plant and weaken its leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ baa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ nɔ ni amɛhaa baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the hot afternoon even when the soil feels slightly wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the soil. Adding organic mulch around the stems lowers soil temperature and helps plants hold onto moisture.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Organic mulch ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.
