english: What happens to my crop roots when heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni baa mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo?

english: Standing water drowns roots by blocking oxygen in the soil. Without air, roots begin to rot and cannot absorb nutrients, causing the plant to turn yellow and eventually die.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni naagbee lɛ egboɔ.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer when the ground is dry or after it rains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist after a moderate rain so the roots can absorb it immediately. Applying it on dry soil can burn roots, while heavy rain can wash it away completely.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo lɛ sɛɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the branches and leaves grow very big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ niji kɛ baai lɛ ekwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing tall stems and thick foliage instead of storing food in the underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight burns their foliage and dries out the topsoil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides a cool shelter and keeps moisture in the soil while the cocoa gets established.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ ŋmɛɔ ehe shi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over before the bunches are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy bunches, especially during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a double bamboo prop gives the plant the stability it needs to hold the fruit until it matures.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ asɛɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei enyɔ fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ aduawai lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebaadara.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a signal that the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients too deep for the roots to reach. Applying the right nitrogen fertilizer restores leaf color and speeds up growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛtee shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my groundnut plants look bushy and healthy, but the pods under the dirt are empty when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa lɛ? But the underground pods were empty when I harvested them.

english: Empty groundnut pods happen when there is not enough calcium in the soil during the pod-forming stage. The plant still grows big leaves, but without calcium, the seeds inside the pods cannot develop properly.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni pod lɛ feɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji lolo. Shi kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ hu nyɛŋ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot, when the plant receives irregular water, or when insects do not visit to pollinate them. Keeping soil moisture steady with mulch helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nu nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii baaa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why does grass grow so much faster than my rice in the early weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally tougher and absorb nutrients and water faster than young rice seedlings. Clearing weeds early within the first month gives your rice plants access to sunlight and food so they can outgrow the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ mli wa yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu oya fe ŋmãa dumɔwui bibii. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha o-rice tsei lɛ aná hulu la kɛ niyenii. Koni jwɛi lɛ adara oya

english: Why do small black bugs attack my cowpea crop mostly when the flowers begin to open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji lɛ tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ fe fɛɛ beni amɛjeɔ fɔmɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Insects like flower thrips are naturally attracted to cowpea flowers because of their sweet nectar and pollen. Inspecting the field right when budding starts allows you to act before the insects destroy the young pods.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips lɛ sumɔɔ cowpea fɔfɔii yɛ amɛmli nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ je shishi amɛkwɛ lɛ, ebaaha onyɛ ofee nɔ ko dani ŋmeii lɛ afite ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when I plant them in flat soil during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long. Building mounds or raised ridges lifts the stem so excess rainwater drains away, allowing the roots to breathe and grow big tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ woɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ koni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ha shishifãi lɛ amu ni oha bulb lɛ agbo.

english: Is it really necessary to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni atswa tsei kakadaji koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam leaves produce food for the tuber using sunlight. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground so leaves catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from dirt-borne diseases, leading to much larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tuber lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. koni baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo ni eha ehe atse kɛjɛ helai ni muji kɛbaa lɛ ahe Ekɛ yitso ni da kwraa baa.

english: Should I water my pepper plants every single day during the dry season to get good fruit?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa gbi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba?

english: Watering every day can drown the roots if the water does not drain away. It is better to water deeply every few days and place dry grass mulch around the base to keep moisture trapped in the ground longer.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa gbi lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi kɛji akɛ ajieee nu lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Esa akɛ awo mli nu babaoo be fɛɛ be. gbii fioo komɛi ni okɛ sũ ni egbi aha shishigbɛ lɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can I just plant my maize and leave it to grow without adding fertilizer or manure?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa ni mahã ekwɛ̃ ni mikɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsuuu nii?

english: Just like animals, crops need proper feeding to stay healthy and yield well. Without nutrient-rich plant food like manure or fertilizer, crops become weak, stop growing properly, and produce very little harvest.
ga: tamɔ kooloi Niyenii ni sa he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha hewalɛ kpakpa kɛ yibiiwoo. Kɛji tsei aniyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baafee gbɔjɔmɔ. ekpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ

english: Why are my pepper leaves turning yellow even though I gave them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu eha amɛ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is under stress from a lack of proper nutrients in the soil. Even with enough water, crops need balanced soil food to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ niyenii ni sa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji nu fa bɔ ni sa po lɛ, Dumɔwui hu he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: What causes my tomato plants to drop their flowers before growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tomato tsei lɛ miifo amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛdu aduawai?

english: Heat, dry conditions, or pest attacks cause extreme stress to tomato plants. When stressed, the plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy for survival rather than making fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa tomato tsei anɔ. Kɛ́ haomɔ ba Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei baawo yibii lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my cassava crops if they are just growing next to them?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye mi-cassava tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛmiidara yɛ amɛmasɛi?

english: Weeds cause silent stress by stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your cassava, essentially starving your crops and slowing down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ haomɔ baa kɛtsɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ejuɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves curl up and burn when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive heat creates intense stress on young crops. Strong direct sunlight dries out the leaves faster than the young roots can draw water from the soil.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Does it matter where on my land I plant my vegetables, or will they grow anywhere?
ga: Ekɔɔɔ he eko he ni miduɔ aduawai yɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Aloo ani aduawai baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: The environment matters greatly because crops need specific soil types, good drainage, and the right amount of sunlight. Planting in an unsuitable location will cause the crops to struggle and eventually die.
ga: Shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ he hiaa waa ejaakɛ tsei biɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko. nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulu la ni sa Dumɔ yɛ he ko ni esaaa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɔi ŋmɔlɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbo.

english: Why do my crop seeds rot in the ground after heavy rains instead of sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: When soil stays flooded with water, it starves the seeds of air. Too much water creates a harsh environment that causes seeds to drown and rot before they can grow.
ga: Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ mli dumɔwui lɛ baaye hɔmɔ. Nu babaoo haa shihilɛ ni mli wa baa ni haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers wither and die right after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ kroko mli lɛ?

english: Moving a plant to a new location causes initial transplant shock. If the young plant does not receive immediate shade and moisture to recover from this stress, it will dry up.
ga: Tso ko ni ajieɔ kɛyaa he hee lɛ haa mɔ naa kpɛɔ ehe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be mli ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji tsei bibii lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛjɛ haomɔ mli lɛ, Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi.

english: Why is my crop farm taking much longer to produce fruit than my neighbor's farm planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei aŋmɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii fe mikutsoŋnyo ŋmɔ ni miida yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Crops require good care throughout their life cycle to mature on time. Early stress, poor soil preparation, or inadequate nutrients delay flowering and slow down fruit development.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɛ tsei jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli koni amɛdara yɛ be naa. Haomɔ yɛ shishijee mli shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ ni ehiii loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ Ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ hu sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Can I just leave my crops to nature after planting, or do I need to inspect them regularly?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mahã adebɔɔ beni midu nii sɛɛ? Aloo ehe miihia ni makwɛ mli daa?

english: Leaving crops completely unattended exposes them to unseen stress factors like disease or pest damage. Regular checks allow you to catch issues early before they kill your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, ekɛ haomɔi ni anaaa tamɔ helai loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kpeɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona naagbai mra. Dani ebaakpãtã oŋmɔshinii lɛ ahiɛ

english: Why does some rice smell naturally sweet like perfumed rice while growing, but other rice has no smell at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ tamɔ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmãa henɔi komɛi bɛ ŋmɔlɔ kwraa?

english: Certain aromatic rice varieties naturally produce a special fragrance compound in their leaves and grains as they mature, whereas standard local varieties do not carry this genetic trait.
ga: Omɔ henɔi komɛi ni ŋɔɔ waa lɛ jieɔ tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni ŋɔɔ waa yɛ amɛbaai kɛ amɛŋmãa lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni akutsoŋ henɔi ni yɔɔ lɛ bɛ nɛkɛ fɔmɔ su nɛɛ.

english: What makes a rice plant produce long, slender grains instead of short, round ones?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei náa dumɔwui kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ dumɔwui kukuji ni yɔɔ kokroo najiaŋ?

english: Grain length is determined by the specific variety of seed you plant; long-grain varieties are bred to stretch their grains during the seed-filling stage, while short-grain varieties naturally store their starch in a rounder shape.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni dumɔwu lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ha. Afɔɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui kakadaji lɛ koni amɛha amɛdumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ atsɛ yɛ be mli ni awoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui kukuji sɔrɔtoi lɛ kɛ starch toɔ yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my rice leaves turn yellow and stay short instead of growing tall and dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee kuku yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing and slow growth usually mean the rice plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or is stressed by poor water drainage, which stops it from making the green chlorophyll it needs to feed itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmã tso lɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ miihao lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee klorofil eŋɔli ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛye ehe lɛ.

english: Does rice always need to stand in deep flooded water to grow well on my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ ŋmãa adamɔ nu ni mli kwɔ mli be fɛɛ be koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Not all rice requires flooded water; while paddy rice thrives in flooded fields to suppress weeds, upland rice varieties can produce good yields in normal moist soil with regular rainfall.
ga: Omɔ henɔi komɛi biɔ nu afua. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli koni ejie jwɛi lɛ. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my rice plants sprout many extra stems from one seed while others only produce a single stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ niji babaoo krokomɛi kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu kome mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi Nine kome pɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Rice plants sprout extra fertile stems (called tillers) when given proper spacing, adequate nitrogen fertilizer, and good weed management early in their growth.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛhe yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ. (ni atsɛɔ lɛ spade) kɛji akɛ aha lɛ he ko ni sa Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ jwɛi akwɛmɔ kpakpa yɛ shishijee bei amli

english: Why do my rice grains break into small pieces when they go through the milling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli fãa bibii bibii kɛ́ etsɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice grains crack internally and break during milling if the crop was left too long in the sun before harvest, or dried too quickly on hot pavement, making the inner grain brittle.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa mli fãa yɛ mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa beni ashɛreɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa, loo egbi oya tsɔ yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my crop so the grains stay strong?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn a golden-yellow color and the lower grains feel hard when pressed, rather than soft or milky.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Ni shishigbɛ dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ anyɛ amɛnɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee bɔdɔɔ loo mliki su

english: Why shouldn't I spread my harvested grain directly on the bare ground to dry in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ koni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Drying grain directly on bare ground exposes it to ground moisture, soil dirt, and intense direct heat that causes cracks in the grain and invites fungus.
ga: Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa sũ mli nu. muji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ ni haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli fãa kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Can I save a portion of the rice I harvested this season to plant as seed for the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa ni mikpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ eko ato koni mikɛdu akɛ dumɔwui kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: You can save seeds from standard open-pollinated varieties, but if you planted hybrid seeds, saving them will result in lower yields and uneven grain sizes in the next crop.
ga: Obaanyɛ obua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni agbele naa lɛ amli. Shi kɛji akɛ odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid Retaining lɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi ni ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ hu akafee ekome yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do small insects appear inside my closed bags of stored grain after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi dumɔwui kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storage insects often lay invisible eggs on the grain while it is still in the field, which hatch inside the bag if the grain is stored with too much moisture or in a warm room.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmaa nɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Amɛbaafɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo yɛ tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil. Planting companion crops like plantains provides living shade umbrellas that keep the soil moist and shield the young plants.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, a key food maize needs to grow. Adding poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer near the base of the plant helps restore leaf color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ adu Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifã loo nitrogen ŋtayaa fata he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe su aku sɛɛ aba ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and covered in tiny white insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: These insects are whiteflies, which suck sap from the leaves and spread diseases like Cassava Mosaic Virus. Clearing surrounding weeds and using recommended organic or chemical sprays can control their spread.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii yɛŋ. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni egbɛɔ helai tamɔ cassava mosaic virus lɛ eshwaa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni agbeɔ kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why should I make large soil mounds instead of planting my seed yams flat in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ matswa gɔŋ agbo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu sweet potato dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, deep soil so they can grow long and fat without resistance. Soil mounds gather rich topsoil and prevent heavy rains from waterlogging the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ bɔni afee ni amɛdara kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee fɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi amɛnaa. Gɔŋ lɛ buaa ŋwɛi sũ ni jara wa lɛ naa ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ yitso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rot before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. Water your tomato plants consistently so they can move calcium from the soil into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Ha o-tomato tsei lɛ nu daa koni amɛjie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of soil nutrients, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why should I cut off extra sucker shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: If too many suckers grow at once, they compete with the main stem for water and nutrients. Keeping only 1 to 3 healthy suckers ensures the main stem grows strong and yields large fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida shikome lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii 1 kɛyashi 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ adara waa ni ewo yibii akui wuji.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any peppers form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by excessive heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Mulching the soil to keep it cool and moist helps the plant retain its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni fe nine, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ ni edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai amli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stunted even if I rain-water my farm every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the resources they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do small beetles bore tiny holes into my dried maize grains after I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ladybugs bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu bibii lɛ? Eyaa mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli beni mikɛto sɛɛ?

english: These beetles are grain weevils that lay eggs inside moist or poorly dried corn. Thoroughly drying your maize to a low moisture content and storing it in airtight bags protects the grain from insect infestation.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji dumɔwui ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ni mli edɔɔɔ loo egbi mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni hulutsoo be fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli, ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebuɔ ŋmãa lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Can I grow pepper on my farm during the dry season, or does it only survive in the rainy season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu pepper yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli? Aloo ani abaanyɛ adu yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Pepper can grow in both rainy and dry seasons. While rain makes planting easier, growing pepper in the dry season with simple watering allows you to harvest when market supply is low and prices are higher.
ga: Abaanyɛ adu pepper yɛ nugbɔ be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be fɛɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ haa dumɔ feɔ mlɛo moŋ. Shi ŋmɔtɔ ni aduɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ nu ni yɔɔ mlɛo Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa be mli ni jara nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa ni jara hu yaa hiɛ.

english: What does organic farming mean, and how can it protect my crops without buying chemical sprays?
ga: Mɛni ji organic okwaayeli shishi? And how can I protect my crops without buying chemical sprays?

english: Organic farming uses natural tools like manure, compost, and plant-based pest sprays instead of artificial chemicals. It improves your soil health over time and keeps crops safe using low-cost local materials.
ga: Organic okwaayeli kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ tsofai ni akɛfee nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ najiaŋ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. ni akɛ maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni jara waaa lɛ atsu nii ni akɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers plant hot pepper alongside their main vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ yɛ amɛ aduawai titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Hot pepper contains natural chemicals that smell strong and taste spicy to insects. Planting pepper next to other crops acts as a living shield that repels pests without using synthetic chemicals.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsofai yɛ chili peppers mli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa ni shwieɔ koolooi. Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni tsofai ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ahe ehiaaa.

english: How can I keep my crop roots from drying out and dying during the hot harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ harmattan be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves—a practice called mulching—traps moisture in the ground and shields delicate roots from harsh sun and dry winds.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ŋmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebuɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and rot when the rains get too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills all the spaces in the soil, the roots choke because they cannot get air. Raising your planting beds allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping roots healthy during downpours.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he fɛɛ he ha. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe kɔɔyɔɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa yɛ nugbɔ be mli

english: How can I make my soil richer for my crops without spending money on bags of chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ kotokui amli?

english: Adding well-rotted cow or chicken manure and decomposed leaves directly into the soil feeds the plants naturally, improves water retention, and keeps the land fertile for future farming.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsina loo wuɔ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ kɛ baai ni egboi fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii. Ha nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I start my pepper seeds in a small nursery bed instead of sowing them directly in the big farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ

english: Pepper seeds are small and delicate, making them easy targets for ants, birds, and heavy rainfall. A nursery allows you to protect and feed seedlings until they are strong enough to survive on the main field.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa efeɔ he ko ni ŋmeii, okpoi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he oya. Nursery haa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni ohaa amɛ niyenii kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close to each other on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing lets air flow freely, reducing fungal diseases and helping plants produce larger fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow slowly and yield very little food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that drink up the water and soil food meant for your crops. Removing weeds early gives your crops full access to nutrients so they can grow faster and yield more.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why is it harmful to plant the same pepper crop on the exact same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmɔtɔ henɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in the land. Alternating with crops like corn or beans starves the pests and keeps the soil balanced.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha hɔmɔ agbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and burning when the sun is bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their young leaves dry out faster than their roots can absorb water. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby creates a soft, shielded environment that protects cocoa seedlings during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What happens to my yam crop if I leave the vines to grow along the ground instead of giving them sticks to climb?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ miha wain tso lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ niji ni akwɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ najiaŋ hu?

english: Yam vines naturally seek height to catch sunlight. When left on the ground, the leaves shade each other, reduce energy production, and are exposed to warm, wet soil where fungal diseases can easily destroy them, leading to much smaller tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei taoɔ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛji ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Baai lɛ baaha amɛhe. Tsɔɔmɔ hewalɛ ni anáa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni efɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ oya lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ yitso bibioo kwraa baa

english: Why are the center leaves of my young maize plants curling up and showing small holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ?

english: This leaf behavior is caused by pests like fall armyworms feeding inside the leaf whorl. The insect hides deep inside the rolled leaves to stay safe from sunlight while eating the plant's soft growth centers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ subaŋ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall flukes ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he beni amɛyeɔ gbekɛbii bibii ni daraa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward into little cups and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efolɔ amɛhe ewo kɔɔpoi bibii amli ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl upward as a reaction to sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies under the leaves, or because of a virus passed on by those insects. The plant distorts its leaves as it suffers from nutrient loss and sap damage.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ahetoohamɔ mli. aloo yɛ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ahewɔ Tso lɛ fiteɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni efiteɔ kɛ nu ni efiteɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why is my cassava farm growing very tall stems with thick green leaves, but the tubers underground are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei lɛ kɛlɛ waa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava plants direct all their energy into leafy top growth instead of underground storage. The plant uses its food reserves to build tall stems rather than expanding its roots into heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ebaa lɛ yiteŋ lɛ, ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Tso lɛ kɛ niyenii ni ekɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi ni kɛlɛ moŋ fe ni eeewo shishifãi lɛ amli ni etsɔ bulbs ni tsii.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with soil bacteria to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the cowpea plant dies after harvest, this nitrogen breaks down into the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmei tso ko ni kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ejie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tsina tso lɛ gbo yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ fiteɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa henɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: High temperatures stress tomato plants and make their pollen dry out and become sterile. When pollen fails to fertilize the flower, the plant intentionally drops the blossom to save energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gĩɔ ni efeɔ nɔ ni nyɛɛɛ afɔ nii. Beni pollen lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afee fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ. Tsei hu baafee amɛyiŋ akɛ amɛbaashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite.

english: Why do my vegetable crops look sad and wilted in the afternoon heat but stand up straight again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛye awerɛho ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the soil, causing temporary wilting. Overnight, when air temperatures cool down, root pressure catches up and restores water to the leaf cells.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Gbi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Shishifãi lɛ ahe hewalɛ fiɔ nu lɛ ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa baa lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over so easily after heavy rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots near the soil surface rather than a deep taproot. When heavy fruit bunches mature, the plant becomes top-heavy, and rain-soaked soil softens the ground until the shallow roots lose their grip.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji akɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, tso lɛ baaná nɔ ni tsii fe fɛɛ. Ni sũ ni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why does lowland rice grow better when there is standing water around the stems in the early stages?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa folo lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ beni nu yɛ lolo yɛ ŋmãa lɛ he yɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties have special hollow stems that pump air down to their roots even when flooded. The standing water prevents weeds from taking over the field while keeping the soil loose enough for rice roots to absorb nutrients easily.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mli ewo muji ni shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli kɛji nu shwie shi po. Nu ni yɔɔ lolo lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaha ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔ ni sa koni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya.

english: Why is it necessary for me to walk through and inspect my crop field every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ mli ni makwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi lɛ?

english: Just like watching over family members to keep them safe, daily monitoring allows you to spot early signs of pest attacks, diseases, or water stress before they spread and destroy your whole harvest.
ga: Nakai nɔŋŋ eji yɛ weku lɛ mli bii akwɛmɔ koni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe lɛ he. Daa gbi nibii amli kwɛmɔ yeɔ ebua bo ni onaa okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai, loo nu mli haomɔ miiba mra dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfite onibii fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my young crop plants are developing healthily after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ miiya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Healthy young crops will display firm stems, vibrant green leaves, and steady new growth every few days without yellowing, wilting, or dark spots.
ga: Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ. baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ kɛ dalɛ hee yaa nɔ daa gbii fioo komɛi ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I correctly use a manual seed planter cup to sow seeds in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ dumɔwui adumɔ kɔɔpoo ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ atsu nii koni mikɛdu dumɔwui jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fill the container with seeds, press the tool into prepared soil to the recommended depth, release a single seed unit, cover it lightly with soil, and repeat the process steadily along your planting line.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui awo tsɛnsi lɛ mli. Nyɛɛ dɛŋdade lɛ nɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni asaa he lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ he lɛ. Jiemɔ dumɔwui lɛ ekomekomei. Okɛ sũ fioo aha he. Ni okɛ nifeemɔ lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be yɛ odumɔ line lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why should I avoid dropping too many seeds into one planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ he?

english: When too many seeds grow in one spot, the young plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients, resulting in weak stems and poor yields.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome Tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: How deep should I cover small seeds like tomatoes when placing them in the soil?
ga: Te esa akɛ makɛ dumɔwui bibii, tamɔ tomato awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi tɛŋŋ?

english: Small seeds should only be covered with a thin layer of fine soil—about twice the thickness of the seed—so the tiny sprout has enough energy to break through the surface.
ga: Esa akɛ aha dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ. kɛ sũ kpakpa ni mli tseee pɛ (ni ji dumɔwu lɛ shwiemɔ shii enyɔ) koni eha dumɔwu lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How many days should I wait to see tomato seedlings sprout out of the ground after sowing?
ga: Kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ, gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mana tomato dumɔwui ni je kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Under warm Ghanaian weather conditions and with adequate soil moisture, tomato seeds typically sprout and emerge above the soil within 5 to 10 days.
ga: Yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ shishi. Tomato dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaaya nɔ amɛho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii 5 kɛyashi 10 mli.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout even after I plant and water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ beni midu ni miwo amɛ nu po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to come up if they are buried too deep, eaten by insects, damaged by extreme dry heat, or exposed to excessive water that rots them under the soil.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. ŋmeii yeɔ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni mli egbi waa lɛ efite lɛ Aloo nu babaoo ebote mli ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do young vegetable seedlings lean in one direction after coming out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ beni amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young plants naturally lean toward the direction of sunlight so their leaves can capture the energy needed to manufacture food for growth.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha dalɛ.

english: Is it better to plant tomato seeds directly on the main farm or start them in small nursery containers first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo aaadu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii bibii amli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: It is best to start tomato seeds in small cups or nursery beds where you can protect the delicate seedlings before transplanting them to the main field when they are stronger.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni obɔi tomato dumɔwui yɛ kɔɔpoi bibii amli. loo nursery plot Obaanyɛ obu dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe dani okɛ amɛ awo saatso wulu lɛ nɔ beni amɛhe wa lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my young crop plants turn yellow soon after emerging?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji amɛje kpo amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of bottom leaves often signals that the plant roots are suffering from too much water in the soil, lack of nitrogen, or poor root aeration.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli, nitrogen bɛ mli, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nyɛɛɛ aya mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops die when I plant them immediately after the first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often just a temporary shower before a dry spell. Planting too early means the soil underneath is still dry and hot, which burns the young seeds before the full rainy season begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ ni baa be kukuoo ko pɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ. Dumɔ mra tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ shãa dani nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even when the leaves above ground look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, soft soil to swell up. If the ground is packed too hard or lacks proper nutrients, the plant puts all its energy into leaves instead of expanding its roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi bɔni afee ni amɛfuu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo niyenii ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce less harvest when I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the field year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant is missing essential food in the soil, usually nitrogen, or that the ground has too much water around the roots, preventing them from breathing.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji nitrogen. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛmuɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak with small fruits when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛ aduawai bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight and soil food, stretching upward to reach the light instead of building strong stems and big fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni oooshɛ nɔ koni enine ashɛ la nɔ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ yiblii nguahi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is the plant's natural defense mechanism to protect itself from extreme heat and reduce water loss through evaporation during the peak sun hours.
ga: Baai lɛ akumɔ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni eha nu ni laajeɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn up when I clear all the large shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa beni mijieɔ cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need direct shade to survive early growth. Large trees act like giant umbrellas that shield the delicate young cocoa leaves from scorching sun and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdara oya. Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce a poor harvest even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yibii kpakpai aba eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops, effectively starving your plants during critical growth periods.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye otsei lɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: How does using proper machinery or tools to loosen the soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔnei loo nitsumɔ dadei ni sa ni mikɛbaatsu nii koni mikɛgbala shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Loosening the soil deeply allows water to soak in better and enables roots to spread easily to reach nutrients that sit deeper in the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ abote mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo koni amɛshɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ ahe

english: Why do small insects suddenly appear and eat my crop leaves right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii baa trukaa koni amɛbaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Warm and wet weather creates ideal conditions for insect eggs in the soil to hatch rapidly, causing a sudden rise in pests looking for soft fresh leaves to eat.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha koolooi wuji ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ baafɔ̃ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai taoɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. ba koni ebaye nii trukaa

english: Why do buyers complain about small stones mixed in with my harvested rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ wieɔ amɛshiɔ tɛi bibii lɛ? ni akɛfutu mikpamɔ lɛ?

english: Stones usually get mixed into rice when the crop is dried directly on bare ground or threshed on the soil, which lowers the quality and makes people dislike buying local rice.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ tɛi futuɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo atswa ŋmãa lɛ. Enɛ baaha nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha mɛi asumɔɔɔ ni amɛheɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa.

english: How do dirt and pebbles get into my crop grains if they grow on stalk heads?
ga: Te muji kɛ sũ baafee tɛŋŋ abote midumɔwui lɛ amli kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ stem bulbs nɔ?

english: Dirt and stones enter the crop after cutting, especially when stalks touch the muddy soil or when grains are spread on uncovered dirt to dry under the sun.
ga: Muji kɛ tɛi baabote ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli beni afo lɛ sɛɛ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ta muji lɛ he. aloo kɛ́ agbɛ dumɔwui ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ahako nɔ koni amɛgbi yɛ hulu lɛ shishi.

english: What happens to my crop grains if I dry them directly on the bare ground after harvest?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji migbi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Drying grains on bare soil allows them to collect dirt, sand, and pebbles, which makes the crop hard to sell and can damage processing equipment later.
ga: Nibii ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ haa ebuaa muji, ŋã kɛ ŋmeii anaa, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa, ni ebaanyɛ efite nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: What does it mean when people say local rice needs to be 'polished'?
ga: Kɛ́ mɛi kɛɛ akɛ esa akɛ ‘akɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: Polishing is a mechanical process that cleans and removes the rough outer layers of the rice grain, making it smooth, shiny, and pleasant to eat.
ga: Polishing ji tsɔne ko ni tsuɔ nii ni ejieɔ ŋmãa lɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa ni mli ewo muji lɛ. Ehaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ekpɛɔ ni ŋɔɔ.

english: What machine can I use to remove stones from my harvested grain before taking it to the market?
ga: Mɛɛ tsɔne manyɛ mikɛjie tɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmaa ni akpa lɛ mli dani mikɛya jara nɔ?

english: A destoning machine uses vibrating screens and air movement to separate heavy stones and dirt from lighter crop grains, leaving you with clean rice.
ga: Shredder lɛ kɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hosoɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ ehe lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛgbalaa tɛi ni tsii kɛ muji kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni hiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa onine shɛɔ ŋmãa ni he tse nɔ

english: Can using the wrong processing equipment spoil my harvested grain?
ga: Ani nibii ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ?

english: Yes, if processing machines are poorly maintained or incorrectly set, they can crush grains, break seeds, or introduce dirt, damaging your hard work from the field.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo atooo he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ efolɔ ŋmaa, efolɔ ŋmaa, loo ekɛ muji aba. Enɛ baanyɛ afite onitsumɔ ni wa ni otsuɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: How does the way I cut my crop in the field affect how easy it is to process with machines?
ga: Te bɔ ni afoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ saa bɔ ni tsɔnei baanyɛ atsu he nii mlɛo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cutting crops too close to the soil gathers muddy stems and rocks, which can jam milling machines and contaminate the entire batch during processing.
ga: Kɛ́ afo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaabua ŋmeii kɛ tɛi anaa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ muji awo ŋmɔlɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why is locally grown rice sometimes less popular with town buyers than imported rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, maŋbii ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ fe ŋmãa ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa lɛ?

english: Town buyers often prefer imported rice because it is thoroughly cleaned of stones and polished, whereas local rice traditionally contains grit if not processed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa ejaakɛ ehe miihia ni atsumɔ tɛi lɛ ahe ni afee amɛ fɛfɛo jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does removing the outer skin and polishing my harvested grain help me earn more money?
ga: Ani mihewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ ni mafolɔ midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua mi ni maná shika babaoo?

english: Yes, clean and polished grains look attractive, taste better, and cook evenly, allowing you to charge higher market prices compared to uncleaned grains.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmaa ni he tse ni akpɛ́ lɛ feɔ fɛo, eŋɔɔ, ni ehoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa okɛ jarayeli jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe ŋmaa ni he tseee lɛ toɔ he.

english: Why should I care about modern processing machines if my crop already grew well in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maná ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe miishɛɛ lɛ? Be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Growing a good crop is only half the work; proper processing removes foreign debris and transforms rough grain into a clean product that consumers enjoy eating.
ga: Nibii kpakpai ni aduɔ lɛ ji nitsumɔ lɛ fã pɛ. Kɛ́ atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ maŋsɛɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmãa ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni he tse ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛye.

english: When is the best time for me to clear and prepare my land before planting yams in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni masaa he dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ Ghana?

english: Land preparation should ideally begin during the dry season between December and February so the soil is ready before the main rains start in March or April. Early clearing allows the soil to soften and reduces pest carryover.
ga: Esa akɛ aje shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ December kɛ February teŋ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee klalo dani nugbɔ titri lɛ aje shishi yɛ March loo April mli. Nibii ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it better to make large earth mounds for yams instead of planting them in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofee gɔŋ agbo kɛha ŋmeii moŋ fe ni ooodu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounding loosens the topsoil so yam tubers can grow long, thick, and deep without facing hard soil resistance. It also improves drainage, which keeps the planted seed yam from rotting in heavy rains.
ga: Mounding haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tsiɔ amɛnaa lɛ ekpeee. Ehaa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ hu, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni sweet potato dumɔwui ni adu lɛ akafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: What happens to my planted seed yams if the rains delay for too long after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-sweet potatoes ni midu lɛ nɔ kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ?

english: If seed yams sit in hot, dry ground without rain, they can dry out, get attacked by termites, or rot before sprouting. Covering your mounds with dry leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool and saves moisture while you wait for rain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ tara he ko ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi, ŋmeii baatutua amɛ, loo amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) ha gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ nugbɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if the seed yams I bought are healthy enough to sprout well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy seed yams should feel firm to the touch, be free from soft rot or white fungus spots, and show tiny green buds or sprouts starting to form at the top head.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa kɛji mɔ ko ta he. Ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ. ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii ni jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eyitso lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden stakes to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ he hiaa tsei ni akɛkwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Wooden stakes hold the vines up off the wet ground toward the sun, which boosts tuber growth and prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Tsoi ni akɛfee tsei lɛ ŋmɛɔ wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni efɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tuber lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaaa folier helai aba.

english: Can I plant yams on the exact same piece of land where I harvested yams last season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: It is best to rotate crops and avoid planting yams back-to-back on the same land. Yams use up a lot of soil nutrients, and planting in the same spot allows soil pests and diseases to build up and attack your new crop.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ahe. Sweet potatoes kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Ni kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛtutuaa onibii heei lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my yams are fully mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni sweet potatoes lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yams are ready for harvesting when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow, dry up, and die back, usually 6 to 8 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, amɛgbi, ni amɛgboi, bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: What causes my harvested yams to rot quickly when I store them at home, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto shia? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Yams rot quickly if they get bruised during harvest, are left in hot sunlight, or are kept in a warm, closed room. Storing them in a shaded, well-ventilated barn on raised wooden racks prevents rotting.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Ashi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Aloo akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni aŋã mli. Kɛto ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ tso shĩa ko ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni akafite.

english: What major costs should I plan for before I begin farming yams this season?
ga: Mɛɛ shika titri esa akɛ mato he gbɛjianɔ dani mabɔi sweet potato okwaayeli yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Your main expenses will be buying quality seed yams (which usually take the largest part of your budget), paying for labor to clear land and build mounds, buying climbing stakes, and clearing weeds.
ga: Oshika titri ni ofiteɔ ji sweet potatoes ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahemɔ. (Be pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ oshika ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ mlijaa babaoo.) Nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo koni akɛjie shikpɔŋ ni akɛma gɔji. Hemɔ tsei ni akɛkwɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ ni ojie jwɛi lɛ.

english: How many yams can I expect to harvest if I plant one mound with a seed yam?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ sweet potato dumɔwui wo ŋmei ŋmei kome mli lɛ, ŋmei enyiɛ manyɛ makpa?

english: Generally, one healthy seed yam planted in a good mound will grow into one main, large market-sized yam tuber by the end of the season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato dumɔwu kome ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni adu yɛ ŋmei kpakpa mli lɛ baatsɔ sweet potato tuber agbo ko ni dalɛ tamɔ jara nɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when there is too much rain on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain washes away essential nitrogen nutrients from the topsoil and floods the roots. When roots are underwater, they cannot breathe or absorb food, causing the leaves to turn yellow from nutrient starvation.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ nitrogen nibii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ nu. Beni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ nu shishi Amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛmu niyenii. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants keep growing very tall with thick leaves, but the tubers underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are planted too close together, the cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves and stems to reach sunlight instead of storing food in its underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei baato niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into fruit during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, making them sterile. When fertilization fails due to high temperatures, the plant drops the blossoms to conserve its water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. sterility Kɛji fɔmɔ nyɛɛɛ aya nɔ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into small tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking the sap from young leaves and transmitting viruses that distort leaf growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ mli ni amɛhaa helai ni fiteɔ baa lɛ dalɛ lɛ.

english: How do fall armyworms cause so much damage to young maize shoots so quickly?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni asraafoi akuu ni egbee shi lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmãa bibii oya nɛkɛ?

english: Fall armyworm caterpillars target the soft inner whorl of young maize plants where leaves are tender and sweet. They feed hidden inside where rain cannot wash them off, destroying the growth center of the stem.
ga: Autumn caterpillars lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ amli ŋtayaai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Amɛnaa niyenii ni akɛtee mli yɛ he ni nugbɔ nyɛŋ ashwie lɛ. Efiteɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ dalɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and shade. Rain splashes the fungus from the soil or infected pods onto healthy ones, causing them to turn dark and rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Nugbɔ haa ŋmeii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii diji kɛ ŋmeii baa.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop relies on and allows soil-borne pests and diseases that favor that crop to build up in high numbers.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ damɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ ni fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli babaoo.

english: Why do groundnuts need loose, sandy soil to give a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ he hiaa ŋmeii koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they grow stalk-like 'pegs' that must push down into the soil to form nuts. Loose soil allows these pegs to easily bury themselves and expand into healthy pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ashɛre ŋmei fɔfɔi ko he lɛ, efeɔ ‘peg’ ko ni tamɔ ŋmei ni esa akɛ ashɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee ŋmei lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ amɛbaafu amɛhe ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and collapse around the trunk before the fruit bunch is full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ tso lɛ he dani aduawai lɛ eyi lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Panama disease or root nematodes attacking the vascular system inside the trunk, blocking water and nutrients from reaching the upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Panama hela loo root nematodes ni tutuaa lá ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Etsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cucumber plants produce many flowers at first, but no fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kukumba tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ shishijee mli shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Cucumber plants usually produce male flowers first to attract bees, followed by female flowers that bear fruit. If there are no bees around to transfer pollen from male to female flowers, fruits will not form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kukumba tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛkɛgbala ŋmeii. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ji fɔfɔi yei ni woɔ yibii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bɛ ni baajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei anɔ lɛ, Fruit efeŋ.

english: Why do farmers in Ghana plant crops in two different seasons, around April and September?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ duɔ nii yɛ be sɔrɔtoi enyɔ mli lɛ? Aaafee April kɛ September

english: Ghana experiences two distinct rainy periods in a year—the major rainy season starting around April and the minor rainy season around September. Planting during these periods ensures your crops get enough rainwater to grow without relying on artificial irrigation.
ga: Ghana naa nugbɔ bei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ yɛ afi mli: Nugbɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi aaafee April. ni nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ ji aaafee September. Dumɔ yɛ nɛkɛ bei nɛɛ amli lɛ haa onibii lɛ naa nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛshwere ni okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔɔ nu ni akɛfee lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time in April to put my maize seeds into the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa yɛ April mli ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: You should plant maize after the soil has received two or three steady, heavy rains in April. Planting in dry soil before steady rain comes can cause the seeds to dry up or be eaten by insects before they sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ odu ŋmãa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni naa wa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ April mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ enɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo kooloi aye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What happens to my crops if the early rain in April comes late?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji April shishijee nugbɔ lɛ ba sɛɛ?

english: When the rainy season is delayed, the crop's growth period gets cut short. Plants may suffer from heat stress early in their life and may not get enough rain later on to produce full yields before the dry season starts.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ, tso lɛ dalɛ be lɛ feɔ kuku. Tsei baanyɛ ana dɔlɛ he haomɔ yɛ amɛshihilɛ shishijee mli. ni ekolɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii aba jogbaŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi.

english: Which crops are best for me to plant during the shorter September rain season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ yɛ September nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo lɛ mli?

english: The September season is shorter than the April season, so it is best to plant fast-growing crops like cowpeas, beans, vegetables, or short-duration maize varieties that mature in 60 to 90 days before the rain stops.
ga: September be lɛ yɛ kuku fe April. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ tsina ŋmei, ŋmei, aduawai loo ŋmei srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kuku ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 mli dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa.

english: Can I plant and harvest cassava twice in the same year like I do with maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ni makpa ŋmei shii enyɔ yɛ afi kome mli tamɔ ŋmei?

english: No, cassava takes between 9 to 12 months or longer to mature fully. While fast crops like maize can yield twice a year in April and September, cassava stays in the ground through both rainy seasons.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani eshɛɔ ŋmei he. Eyɛ mli akɛ mra be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli yɛ April kɛ September mli moŋ. Shi ŋmei baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops give a bigger yield during the April planting season compared to the September one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ April ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ akɛto September he lɛ

english: The April season usually brings more consistent rainfall and longer sunny periods over several months, giving crops more water and energy to grow bigger leaves and produce higher yields than in September.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, April be lɛ mli lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be, ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ nyɔji babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa nu kɛ hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛwo baai wuji ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ September mli.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant the exact same crop on the same farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly and allows pests and soil diseases to multiply. Rotating different crops, like planting beans after maize, restores soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ kɛkɛ lɛ ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow much faster during the warm, wet months than during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ nyɔji ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli fe hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need heat, sunlight, and water to make food through their leaves. Warm temperatures combined with steady rain stimulate root activity and help the plant take up soil nutrients quickly.
ga: Tsei hia dɔlɛ, hulu la, kɛ nu koni amɛ fee niyenii kɛtsɔ amɛ baai lɛ anɔ. He ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow and curl up when it stops raining for a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ otsi kome lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are signs that the plant is under water stress. The crop rolls its leaves to conserve moisture and slow down water loss through evaporation while waiting for rain.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nu he haomɔ shishi. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fiofio kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ nugbɔ lɛ.

english: How can I protect my crops from drying out if the rain stops earlier than expected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves, a method called mulching. Mulch acts like a blanket that shades the soil, keeps it moist, and protects plant roots from hot sun.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi akpɛ onibii lɛ. Atsɛɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ akɛ mulching. Mulch tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he

english: Why do my young cocoa plants start turning yellow and dying when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from intense sunlight and high temperatures. Without shade trees or temporary crops like plantain to cover them, intense sun causes leaf burn, severe water loss, and eventual death.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ latsaa ni naa wa he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha baai lɛ ashã. nu ni elaaje waa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbo

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants rolling up tightly like tubes during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to save water. By rolling into tight tubes, the leaf surface exposed to the direct heat reduces, preventing excess moisture from evaporating.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ nu he. Kɛtsɔ ekɛwo paipii ni mli wa mli lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ anɔ ni latsaa lɛ baa shi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekaho.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my green maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves in a V-shape signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is short, the plant drains nitrogen from its older, lower leaves and sends it to the growing top leaves, causing the bottom ones to yellow and die.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen bɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots taste bitter and stay hard even after boiling them for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ ahoo ŋmei shishifãi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ po lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become bitter and tough when harvested during dry spells or past maturity. Drought stress causes the plant to concentrate bitter protective chemical compounds (cyanogenic glycosides) inside the tuber.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ akpa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli loo kɛ́ amɛdara kwraa. Hɔmɔ he haomɔ haa tsei lɛ náa tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ babaoo. (cyanogen glycosides) ni yɔɔ yitso lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my stored seed yams start sprouting on their own in the barn before the rain even starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ po bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have a natural internal biological clock that breaks dormancy after a period of rest. Even without soil or rain, warmth in the storage barn signals to the yam that its resting period is over and it is time to sprout.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni fiteɔ wɔɔhe yɛ hejɔɔmɔ be ko sɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ loo nugbɔ bɛ po lɛ Dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ tsũ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ sweet potato lɛ akɛ ehejɔɔmɔ be lɛ eho. Ni be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ afee ehee.

english: Why are the young top leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and shriveling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ lɛ?

english: Curling top leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or whiteflies feeding on young leaf sap, or by a virus carried by these insects. The feeding damages leaf cells, making them grow unevenly and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ lɛ nɔ Niyenii fiteɔ baa mli wala yibii. Enɛ haa baa mli wala yibii lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛkuɔ amɛhe.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers just drop off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato?
