english: Tomato flowers drop off without forming fruit primarily because of high temperatures or dry air. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower so it cannot fertilize, causing the plant to shed the useless bloom.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi hewɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ bɔni afee ni enyɛŋ ewo fɔfɔi. Ehaa tsei fɔ̃ɔ ni he ehiaaa

english: Why does my plantain tree produce a very small bunch of fruit if I leave all the young shoots growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mishi ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ hu?

english: Leaving too many suckers around a main plantain stem causes them to compete for water, sunlight, and soil food. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only two or three stems, allowing the main plant to direct all its energy into making large fruit bunches.
ga: Ni aaashi ŋmeii lɛ abɔle ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tsei fioo komɛi pɛ, ni enɛ haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ aduawai akui wuji.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants split into many branches close to the ground while others grow straight up like poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi mli gbalaa kɛfeɔ niji babaoo ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu daraa jaŋŋ tamɔ akulashiŋi lɛ?

english: Branching habits depend mainly on the cassava variety. Early-branching cassava types form bushy, low canopies that shade out weeds early, while non-branching types grow straight tall stems that focus energy upward before branching.
ga: Niji ahe su lɛ damɔ ŋmei henɔ lɛ nɔ titri. Kasava ni niji shwereɔ oya lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ, jwɛi su ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni bɛ niji lɛ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni ja ni kɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋwɛi dani amɛwoɔ niji.

english: Why do small green cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up when they are only the size of my finger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Koni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi be mli ni amɛdalɛ tamɔ minine lɛ?

english: Small black shriveled cocoa pods are usually caused by a natural process called 'cherelle wilt,' where the tree discards extra pods it cannot afford to feed, or by Black Pod disease caused by fungal infection in wet weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘cherelle wilt’ ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha lɛ lɛ mli baa. aloo kɛjɛ black pod hela ni fungal hela kɛbaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tip down the middle of the bottom leaves, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ baa lɛ naa kɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling up and the plants staying short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kuku lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by whiteflies. Spraying with soapy water or natural neem oil solution helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when watering is irregular. Giving plants steady water at the roots and providing light shade during extremely hot afternoons helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ nu yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe, ni aha amɛ hulutsoo yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over before the bunch is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily if tiny worms called nematodes or stem borer insects weaken their roots and base. Mulching well and using healthy, clean suckers for planting creates strong roots that can hold the heavy tree in strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbee shi oya kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes loo kooloi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛshishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii beni aduɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni wa ni baanyɛ atswa tsei ni tsii lɛ ama shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my cowpea leaves during warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cowpea baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: White powdery spots are a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which thrives when plants are crowded together. Spacing your seeds properly lets air flow through the leaves and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Powda yɛŋ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni ale lɛ akɛ powdery mildew. ni daa kɛji akɛ abua tsei anaa babaoo Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: How do weeds hurt my yam crop if the yams are growing underground?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye mi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Even though yams grow under the soil, the leaves above ground need sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to make food for the tuber. Weeds steal these resources from the yam leaves, resulting in smaller tubers.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ, Shi shikpɔŋ nɔ baai lɛ hu he miihia hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha bulb lɛ. Jwɛi juɔ nibii nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ sweet potato baai amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant plantain suckers alongside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ kookoo tsei bibii duɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in bright sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide broad leaf shade and preserve soil moisture, acting as natural umbrellas to protect cocoa trees during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei bibii ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts in my field after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients from the soil, but groundnuts actually put nitrogen back into the dirt through their roots. Rotating them restores soil fertility naturally and breaks crop disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shi yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsakeɔ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ ni efo tsei ahe helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: Why does my soil become hard and dry out quickly after I burn the bush on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya beni mishã jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic matter like dead leaves that act like a sponge to hold moisture and keep soil soft. Leaving dry plant waste to rot as mulch keeps the soil cool, fertile, and moist for a longer time.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni ekɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni eha sũ lɛ afee blɛoo. Ha tsei ni egbi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ agbo ejaakɛ mulch yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ewoɔ nii, ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: If I mix too much water into my crop spray, will it still kill the bugs on my maize?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo futu tso lɛ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli hu? Ani ebaagbe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abele lɛ mli lɛ lolo?

english: Adding too much water dilutes the active ingredients in the chemical, making the spray too weak to control pests effectively and allowing insects to build resistance to the medicine.
ga: Nu babaoo ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni yɔɔ tsofa lɛ mli lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsofa lɛ

english: Can I use muddy river water to mix pesticides for my cassava farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji afutu tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛha mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Muddy water contains dirt particles and minerals that bind to the active chemicals, neutralizing the medicine before it even touches your plants. Always use clean, clear water for mixing chemicals.
ga: Muji bibii kɛ minerals ni kɛ tsofai ni tsuɔ nii kpãa gbee yɔɔ nu ni mli ewo muji mli. ni ehaa tsofa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani eshɛɔ tso lɛ he po. Kɛ nu ni mli tse ni mli tse atsu nii be fɛɛ be kɛ́ oofutu tsofai.

english: Does leaving mixed chemical spray in a bucket for a few days make it less effective?
ga: Ani kɛ́ ashi tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ yɛ tanki lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, once agrochemicals are mixed with water, they begin to break down rapidly. Using leftover spray days later reduces its strength and will not protect your crops properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ okwaayeli tsofai futu nu mli. Amɛbaabɔi fitemɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni eshwɛ lɛ wo mli yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hewalɛ aba shi, ni ebuuu onibii ahe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves look scorched after I spray them with medicine in the hot midday sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mikɛ tsofa shwie amɛnɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Spraying during high heat causes the water in the chemical mixture to evaporate quickly, leaving concentrated chemical droplets that scorch and bleach the leaves. Spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon instead.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eshiɔ tsofa ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Okɛshwie nɔ leebi loo shwane mli moŋ.

english: Why are white powdery spots spreading on the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ miigbɛ eshwa mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: White powdery spots are usually caused by a fungal infection called powdery mildew or by sap-sucking pests like mealybugs that cover themselves in a white wax to protect against heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew ji nɔ ni kɛ powda yɛŋ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ mealybugs, ni kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ haa amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes healthy green crop leaves to turn pale white or yellow as they grow?
ga: Mɛni haa tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ eyɛŋ loo ŋmɔŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Leaves lose their green color when crops lack vital soil nutrients like nitrogen or iron, or when flooded soil damages the roots and prevents the plant from absorbing food.
ga: Baai lɛ laajeɔ amɛ su eŋɔli kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen loo dade. aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni ehaaa tsei lɛ aŋɔ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves have a white chalky coating on them after spraying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baa lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ chalky beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Certain protective medicines, like fungicide powders, leave a dry white residue on the leaves to act as a physical shield against fungal spores trying to enter the plant.
ga: Tsofai komɛi ni tsiɔ hela naa, tamɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii Eshiɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni egbi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni etsu nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ ŋmeii ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbote tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa.

english: Should I dilute liquid fertilizer with extra water when feeding young tomato plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ nu kroko awo nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ mikɛ tomato tsei bibii miiha niyenii?

english: Yes, young plants have delicate roots that burn easily. Diluting liquid fertilizer properly ensures the roots absorb nutrients safely without being damaged by strong chemical salts.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya. Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ efiteee amɛ.

english: How soon should I re-apply medicine on my crops if heavy rain falls right after I spray?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ oya tɛŋŋ?

english: If rain falls within two hours of spraying, it washes the medicine off before the plant can absorb it, requiring another application once the leaves dry.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ mli beni afɔ lɛ tsofa lɛ sɛɛ Tsofa lɛ baaho dani tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. ni esa akɛ akɛwo mli ekoŋŋ kɛ́ baai lɛ egbi.

english: Why do pests keep coming back to my garden even after I sprayed medicine on the plants twice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwie tsei lɛ anɔ shii enyɔ moŋ.

english: Pests return if the medicine was diluted too much, if spray didn't reach the underside of leaves where eggs hatch, or if pests in neighboring farms migrated back to your crops.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji akɛ ajie tsofa lɛ mli nu babaoo. Kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ eyashɛɛɛ baai lɛ ashishi he ni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ lɛ Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ fã kɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: If I want to start crop farming in Ghana, should I plant fast-yielding crops like maize or long-term crops like cocoa?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ yɛ Ghana Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo?

english: Fast-yielding crops like maize or vegetables mature in three to four months, giving you quick income to support your farm, while long-term crops like cocoa take several years to start producing but generate steady income for decades. Many successful farmers start with quick-yielding crops to fund their long-term crop investments.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai baashɛ shweremɔ he yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa onáa shika oya ni okɛkwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ajeɔ nitsumɔ shishi shi ehaa shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Okwaafoi babaoo ni yeɔ omanye lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii mra koni amɛkɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or is sitting in waterlogged ground. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea and ensuring good field drainage will help your plants turn healthy and green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo eyɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea tsu nii, ni okwɛ koni nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize on the same piece of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works very well because maize grows tall fast and is harvested within three months, while cassava grows slower and takes over the space after the maize is harvested, maximizing your land use.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Ejaakɛ abele daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when exposed to strong direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out easily under hot sun. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to shield them during their first two years until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni ekɛ hebuu aha yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do fall armyworms suddenly appear and destroy my crop right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ jeɔ kpo ni amɛfiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths fly in during the early rains to lay thousands of eggs on fresh, tender leaf shoots. The eggs hatch quickly, and the caterpillars feed aggressively on young leaves, so early scouting after rains is essential.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fãa kɛbaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli koni amɛbawo ŋmeii akpei abɔ yɛ baai bibii heei anɔ. Wɔɔji lɛ baafo oya. Ni ŋmeii lɛ kɛ gbeyeishemɔ baaye baai bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, skɔuti ni afeɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ he miihia waa.

english: Why do my pepper plant blossoms keep dropping off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off pepper plants when the weather gets too hot, when the soil is too dry, or when nitrogen fertilizer levels are too high. Regular watering during dry spells and balanced fertilization will help flowers set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ pepper tsei anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fa tsɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I plant my tomato seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When tomatoes are planted too close together, they fight for air, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This causes weak, tall stems, increases humidity that leads to fungal diseases, and results in smaller overall fruit yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tomatoi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tomatoi kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni kɛlɛ. Fɛ̃i ni yaa hiɛ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ fioo.

english: Why did my planted seeds rot in the ground instead of sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when buried too deep in the dirt or when planted in overly wet soil that lacks air. Planting at the correct shallow depth and avoiding over-watering allows seeds to get the oxygen and moisture needed to germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni aaadu yɛ he ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni sa ni ajie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kpo lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: When is the best time in the Ghanaian rainy season to plant my cassava sticks?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni akɛduɔ ŋmei?

english: The best time to plant cassava is at the start of the major rainy season. This allows the cuttings to establish strong root systems in moist soil before the drier periods set in.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei ji nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shishijee. Enɛ haa tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ dani hulutsoo be lɛ shɛɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is rich enough to expand my vegetable production?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha aduawai akwɛmɔ aya hiɛ?

english: Rich soil is dark, soft, crumbly, and full of earthworms, holding moisture well without becoming muddy. If your previous crops grew thick dark leaves and yielded well without heavy inputs, your soil is ready for expansion.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ yɛ ediŋŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni okɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ yɛ baai ni mli edɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tsuuu nii lɛ, Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo agbɛnɛ akɛ ebaagbɛ eshwa.

english: This usually happens when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant automatically moves its remaining nitrogen to the young leaves at the top and the developing cobs, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ ŋmei ni miiya hiɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a viral infection spread by insects. The feeding damages the leaf tissue as it grows, causing it to twist and pucker.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Niyenii kpataa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ ahiɛ beni edaa lɛ. ni haa ekpãa ni ekpãa

english: Why do my vegetable crops look withered in the middle of the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: In very hot sunlight, plants lose water from their leaves faster than the roots can suck water out of the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from drying out, and it will usually stand upright again once the heat lowers in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer in the soil. Extreme heat damages the pollen, so the flowers fail to fertilize and the plant drops them.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen lɛ. Anyɛɛɛ aŋɔ fɔfɔi lɛ awo mli ni tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my maize cobs have missing kernels at the top end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ bɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛi naagbee lɛ?

english: Empty cob tips happen when pollination fails during dry weather. If heat or drought dries out the maize silks before airborne pollen can reach them, the grains at the tip cannot form.
ga: Cob trick ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Kɛji dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ ha ŋmãa siliki lɛ gĩ dani ŋmãa ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ shɛ he lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ naagbee lɛ efeŋ.

english: Why do my garden eggs grow lots of tall green leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi aduawai fioo pɛ amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: Adding too much rich manure or nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and branches instead of flowers. Lowering nitrogen helps the plant switch energy into fruiting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ tsei aniji yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛyaa yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full tropical sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains provides shade and keeps the ground cool while the young cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daraa lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines yield smaller tubers when I leave them to spread on the ground instead of using stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa bulbs bibii beni mihaa amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ tso baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Staking raises the yam leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the growing tuber. Vines on the ground shade each other and are more likely to catch fungal diseases from damp soil.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha bulbs ni miida lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ wain tsei haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller fruit bunches when I leave all the suckers growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii bibii beni mihaa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: All the sucker shoots surrounding the main plantain stalk compete for the same food, water, and sunlight in the soil. Removing extra suckers allows the mother plant to direct all its nutrients into growing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Main plantain tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ emli niyenii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when rain falls heavily for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood waterlogged soil, air cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown and decay under the ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni ehaa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food crops need to grow strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves turn dark green again so the plant can make bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ekoŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my farmland get dry and cracked so quickly just a few days after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ?

english: Soil dries out quickly when it lacks organic matter and is left bare under the direct heat of the sun. Spreading dry grass, crop leaves, or animal manure over the soil helps hold water like a sponge and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli, ni ashi lɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi, baai, loo ŋmei shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi tamɔ sponji ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing lots of bushy green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Adding too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cowpea plants focus all their energy on growing leaves instead of flowers and pods. Cowpeas actually make their own plant food from the air into the soil, so they need very little fertilizer to produce pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Cowpeas feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ koni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before any tomatoes form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or a sudden lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil regularly damp and providing light shade during very hot afternoons helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni oha hulutsoo yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices from under the young leaves. Spraying the leaves with neem oil or soapy water helps clear the pests so healthy new leaves can open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe ŋmeii lɛ koni baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why is the bottom part of my cabbage heads starting to rot while still growing in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kaaba yitso shishi jeɔ shishi egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Cabbage bases rot when rainwater sits around the roots for too long, encouraging fungal diseases in the wet soil. Planting cabbages on raised earth mounds allows extra water to drain away easily so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cabbage shishi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Kaabeji ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do I need to clear the soil into high mounds before planting my cassava cuttings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ mli dani adu ŋmei niji lɛ?

english: Mounding creates deep, soft earth that makes it easy for cassava roots to swell into large, thick tubers. It also keeps water from standing around the roots and rotting the crop during heavy rains.
ga: Mounding haa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehaaa nu akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and twisted even though I water the field regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni efite waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams grow crooked and small when the soil under them is too hard for tubers to expand, or when the vines lack tall stakes to climb. Giving vines stakes allows the leaves to catch sun and feed the underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes bafeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ bibioo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo beni wain tso lɛ bɛ akulashiŋi ni kwɔ ni ekɛkwɔɔ lɛ? Wein tsei ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ.

english: Cocoa pods are fully ripe when their color changes completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting only ripe pods ensures the beans inside ferment properly for good chocolate flavor.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ shi kwraa kɛ́ amɛtsake amɛhe su kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuru lɛ baatsake ni etsɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛ tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ aba.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over so easily whenever strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when underground pests like weevils or microscopic worms eat away their roots. Supporting the plants with bamboo props and planting clean suckers keeps the roots strong and grounded.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii ye amɛshishifãi lɛ. Tsei ni akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant beans and maize together on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei fee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Beans grab nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which acts like natural fertilizer for the maize. In return, the tall maize stalks give support to the climbing beans, helping both crops yield more.
ga: Beans lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition causes them to grow thin stems and produce much smaller tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa amɛnáa tsei bibii ni amɛwoɔ tsei bibii kwraa.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to come up after I plant them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need moisture to wake up and start growing roots. If the soil is too dry, the seeds stay asleep or dry out and die before they can sprout through the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛte shi ni amɛje shishifãi lɛ adalɛ shishi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ loo amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are missing essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from their roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the plant lacks enough water, or if insects damage the blossoms before fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Be mli ni tsei bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Weeds are wild plants that adapt easily to poor conditions. They quickly steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops unless you clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛi ni ehiii amli oya. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya. Ja otsi mli klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there are no plantain trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under strong, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and provide large leaves that act like umbrellas to shade and cool the young cocoa.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni baanyɛ ashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ hulutsoo ni ehaa edɔɔɔ.

english: How do I know if my soil needs fertilizer before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu tsei?

english: If your crops from the previous season grew slowly, had pale or light green leaves, and gave very small harvests, your soil has lost its nutrients and needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni odu kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ miida blɛoo lɛ Na baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why does a crop buyer reject some of my harvested yams even when they look big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpooɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ ekomɛi eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eda moŋ?

english: Buyers look for produce that is healthy and lasts long. Yams with small insect holes, rot, or soft spots will spoil quickly during transport to the market, even if they are large.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Sweet potato ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli He ni egbo loo he ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baafite oya beni akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ amɛdalɛ dara po.

english: Why are insects eating holes in my cabbage leaves, and how does it hurt the crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te eyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Leaves act as the plant's food factory by absorbing sunlight. When insects destroy the leaves, the cabbage cannot feed itself, stopping it from forming a firm head.
ga: Baai tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhe kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛŋɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kooloi bibii kpata baai lɛ, Kaabaji nyɛŋ ana niyenii yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe. Ehaa ewaa akɛ oooha oyitso ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential plant food, or the field is overly wet. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving drainage helps the leaves regain their green color so the plant can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. aloo ŋmɔji lɛ amli edɔ tsɔ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge leaves above ground but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or excess moisture, cassava plants direct all their energy into growing top foliage instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ baato niyenii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ebaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom end rot, and it happens when the plant cannot move enough calcium to the fruit, usually caused by irregular watering or dry soil spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛya aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are the young leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, or by viruses spread by these insects while feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I tie my yam vines to wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akpɛtɛ tso he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up toward sunlight so they can make more food for the root, while keeping foliage off wet ground reduces the risk of fungal diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aje hulu la mli bɔni afee ni amɛha shishifãi lɛ niyenii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil better for the next season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans have tiny root nodules that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, creating natural food for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi bibii. No mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: This drop is called cherelle wilt, and it is the cocoa tree's natural way of reducing its load when it lacks enough water or food to support every pod to maturity.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ nu ni hoɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherelle wilt ni eji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebaa jatsu lɛ shi kɛ́ ebɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua pod fɛɛ pod kɛyashi ebaada.

english: Why is my cashew tree producing many flowers but very few actual nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cashew flowers fail to set nuts when insect pests attack the blossoms or when high humidity triggers fungal infections that burn the flowers before nuts can develop.
ga: Cashew fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ato ŋmeii ahe gbɛjianɔ kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni fa babaoo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni shãa fɔfɔi lɛ baa dani ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plant leaves wilt in the hot afternoon sun even if the soil still feels damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ.

english: In extreme heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil, causing leaves to temporarily droop to conserve water until evening.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do I need to drain the water out of my rice field before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli dani akpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Draining the water signals the rice plants to stop growing and focus on drying and ripening the grains uniformly, while making the ground firm enough to walk on and harvest.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmãa lɛ ni eeegbi ni eha ekwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ anyiɛ nɔ ni akpa nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Leaving mature shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains alongside them creates living shade that protects the young trees until they are mature and strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni akɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni daa oya ni aduɔ yɛ he kome Ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to catch maximum sunlight to make the food that grows big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which prevents fungal rot and allows every leaf to receive sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ fungal rot naa ni ehaa baa fɛɛ baa nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ.

english: Which kind of plantain sucker should I dig up from my old farm to start a new field?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain tsei esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—these have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and strong, thick bases. Avoid 'water suckers' that already have wide leaves, as they grow slowly and produce smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmɔlɔ’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tseee ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishitoo ni mli wa ni mli tse. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ‘sucker shoot’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ momo lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ tsei bibii.

english: What is eating the soft inner leaves of my young maize plants and leaving small black pellets inside?
ga: Mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ baai bibii lɛ ni miyeɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii diji bibii shwieɔ mihe. Mɛni yɔɔ mli?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars called Fall Armyworms that hide in the growing tip of the maize plant. You can manage them by spraying early in the morning or late evening, or by dropping clean sand mixed with wood ash directly into the center of the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni okɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛtsɔ ŋã ni he tse ni akɛ tso sũ efutu mli lɛ ni oooshwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small cups and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛmiikpa tso lɛ dalɛ naa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites, or viruses transmitted by insects. Spraying the leaves early with a mild neem tree oil mixture or soapy water helps keep these sucking pests away.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites. loo helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ Ni akɛbaafɔ baai lɛ anɔ mra Kɛ neem tso mli fɔ ni mli ejɔ ni akɛfutu mli. Aloo nu ni akɛ samla ewo mli lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akamu amɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning soft and black before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently damp and adding wood ash to the soil can help prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni akɛ tso sũ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ enaa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my green maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a 'V'?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ su mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the base of a maize plant mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for strong leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore the green colour and healthy growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai ni wa lɛ adara lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots rot after harvest, they leave this natural food in the soil for the next crop to feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots go soft and spoil quickly if I dig them up right after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji akɛ atsa ŋmei ni akpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause cassava plants to soak up large amounts of excess water, making the roots watery and reducing starch. It is best to wait two or three sunny days after rain for the soil moisture to settle before harvesting cassava.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ baa shi. Esa akɛ omɛ gbii 2-3 yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi dani okpa ŋmei.

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: The hot, dry Harmattan wind draws water out of plant leaves faster than roots can drink it from dry soil, causing stress that forces plants to shed flowers. Covering the soil around plant roots with dry grass (mulching) helps lock moisture in the soil during dry spells.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli. Enɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi baa. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct harsh sunlight. Leaving taller shade trees or planting plantains alongside them provides essential shade that preserves soil moisture and prevents the young leaves from burning.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Shi tsei kakadaji ni haa hulutsoo loo dumɔ tsei bibii yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ehaa baa bibii lɛ akashãa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is an essential nutrient for leaf growth, and applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Ni kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating the soft central leaves inside my young maize stems overnight?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-babi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli lɛ ni ayeɔ he nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides inside the whorl of the plant during the day and feeds at night. Early detection and applying targeted organic or chemical treatments inside the leaf funnel can protect the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ tsei akui amli yɛ shwane mli, ni etaoɔ niyenii gbɛkɛ. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, plants compete intensely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward trying to reach light instead of using their energy to produce strong stems and fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi, ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha la moŋ fe ni amɛaafite hewalɛ koni amɛkɛfee tsei kɛ aduawai ni wa.

english: Why do older farmers cover the ground around their vegetable roots with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps the sun from drying out the soil, keeps root temperatures cool, and stops weeds from growing easily.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shishifã lɛ mli latsaa lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the field, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants keep falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinators like bees. Keeping soil moisture consistent helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛbaa lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii baa lɛ ni bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and rot inside the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around them for too long, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal diseases to spread. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I cut off extra side branches from my tomato plants when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ amli be mli ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Pruning extra side branches prevents the plant from wasting nutrients on excess foliage, allowing it to direct its energy into growing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ yɛ afã lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii babaoo kɛya baai lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my crops still looking weak even though I applied fertilizer on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔji amli moŋ lɛ?

english: If weeds are present, they steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight intended for your crops. Weeds usually grow faster than crops, so weeding before applying fertilizer ensures your plants get the nutrients.
ga: Kɛji jwɛi yɛ lɛ, amɛbaaju ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi daa oya fe tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli dani akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why do my bean plants make the soil better for the crops I plant after them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bean plants are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop finishes, this nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Bean tsei ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji akɛ adu nii agbe naa lɛ Nitrogen nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen or standing in flooded soil. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer and improving soil drainage will turn the leaves healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo edamɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I place fertilizer directly touching the stem of my plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, putting fertilizer right against the stem can burn and kill the plant tissues. It is best to apply fertilizer a few inches away from the stem where the roots can safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ ashã ni egbe lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Can I grow beans in the same farm bed alongside my maize plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ saatso ko nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ mi ŋmeii tsei lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, growing beans and maize together is a great practice called intercropping. The beans cover the ground to stop weeds and feed nitrogen into the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa ni atsɛɔ lɛ intercropping. Mulch beans koni ekpa jwɛi lɛ ni ekɛ nitrogen awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to develop strong stems and full yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tso lɛ shishi ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why do weeds weaken my crops if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than farm crops and aggressively absorb the water, food, and light in the field. Clearing them early prevents them from starving your crops and reducing your final harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ, ni amɛmɔɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ la ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ waa. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni hɔmɔ akaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ni ebaaha onaagbee ŋmaa lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: How do crops like millet manage to grow well even during dry weather in the north?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooyigbɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Millet has deep, spreading roots that search far underground for moisture, along with leaves that hold onto water efficiently, allowing it to survive long dry spells without dying.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni taoɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Kɛ baai ni baanyɛ ato nu jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛgbooo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without producing fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ amɛwo hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries out the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing proper pollination. When flowers are not pollinated, the plant drops them to conserve its energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Beni fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ pollination lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: How can I tell that my cassava plants are ready to be dug up from the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually mature when its lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall, and the ground around the stem base begins to crack as the roots swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda beni eshishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my stored bean seeds and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-beans ni ato lɛ mli Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Small holes in stored beans are caused by tiny insects called weevils. Drying your harvested beans fully in the sun before storing them in airtight containers stops these pests from destroying them.
ga: Kplukai bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kɔfi yibii ni ato lɛ amli lɛ baa. Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmei. Kɛ́ ogbala ŋmeii ni okpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani okɛwo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akafite amɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing from the bottom leaves upward usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and grow. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little food it has left to the top new leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda. Kɛ nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei lɛ anɔ. Ha baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to put chemical fertilizer on my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa, no hewɔ lɛ ani no ehiii kɛha mi?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture in the soil to dissolve so the plant roots can safely drink it in. If applied to bone-dry soil, the strong chemicals in the fertilizer will draw water out of the roots instead, scorching and killing your crops.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shãa ni okpãtã oŋmɔshinii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do people say I should plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally feeding the soil. Planting them alongside maize keeps the soil rich so your maize grows better without tiring out the land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aha niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa Edumɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa. Enɛ baaha o-abele lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices. As they feed, they introduce viruses that distort the leaves and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Amɛkɛ helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the fruit bunches are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani aduawai akuu lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when tiny pests called nematodes or stem borers eat away the roots and trunk base hidden underground. Without a solid root system anchored in the soil, the heavy plant snaps under its own weight or light wind.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ dumɔwui anɔ. Ale amɛ akɛ nematodes loo stem borers, ni amɛyeɔ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ Tsei ni tsii lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsiimɔ shishi loo kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I cut down all the big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mifoɔ cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily and dry out. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains nearby creates a cool umbrella shelter that protects the tender cocoa plants while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Shade ni akɛhaa loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Enɛ haa shade ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or dry. Extreme heat damages the flower's pollen, preventing it from producing a tomato, so the plant drops the flower to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen lɛ. Ehaa enyɛɛɛ ekɛ tomato aba. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛ tsei awo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce big tubers underground. Keeping the leaves off the wet ground also protects them from rotting diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ to hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the field during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains leave standing water around the roots, the soil becomes waterlogged, choking the roots and encouraging rot-causing fungi to destroy the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu bua ehe kɛbɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous tomato harvest produce weaker crops than shop-bought hybrid seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi tomato kpamɔ ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Shop-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred in labs to combine strong traits for just one generation. The seeds saved from that harvest lose those special qualities, resulting in uneven growth, smaller fruits, and weaker disease resistance.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ fɔɔ yɛ laboratori ko mli krɛdɛɛ koni akɛ sui ni mli wa afata he kɛha yinɔ kome. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Yibii lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni helai ni tsiɔ mɔ naa lɛ baa shi

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because direct sunlight burns their foliage and dries up the soil moisture around their tender roots before they establish themselves.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani amɛmaa shi.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close to each other, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani manyɛ makpa babaoo?

english: No, planting maize too close together causes plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and smaller or empty cobs.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when it rains heavily for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess water trapped in poor-draining soil prevents oxygen from reaching the cassava roots, creating conditions for fungi to grow and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni etsi shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaashɛɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛi baa ni ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛfite shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat the inner leaves of my young maize plants during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths and feed on the soft, inner whorl leaves of maize plants, especially during dry weather.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii tsei amli baai bibii lɛ, titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why should I wait a few weeks after putting fresh chicken manure on my land before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ otsii fioo komɛi beni mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee efata mishikpɔŋ lɛ he dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure generates strong heat and high ammonia levels as it decomposes, which can burn seeds and root systems if planted immediately.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ haa dɔlɛ babaoo kɛ ammonia babaoo baa be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛji akɛ adu amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds on my farm grow faster and look healthier than the crop seeds I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ fɛo fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to the local soil and weather, allowing them to absorb water and fertilizer faster than cultivated crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or poor pollination can stress tomato plants, causing them to shed their blossoms to save energy instead of forming tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo tomato.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and hard right on the branch during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads quickly through rain splashes and high moisture, destroying the beans inside.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji hydrophilic fungus ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo nɔ. Efiteɔ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts on the farm plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring the nutrients that maize took away during the previous season.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ niyenii ni ŋmãa lɛ jie yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my yam leaves and vines turn brown and die off near the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni be lɛ naagbee lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: When yam vines dry up, it means the plant has stopped growing leaves and transferred all its stored energy down into the tuber, signaling that the yam is fully mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Beni sweet potato wain tso lɛ egbi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa ebaa lɛ shweremɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ etee shi kɛtee bulb lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is suitable for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Cocoa trees need deep, dark soil that holds moisture well but does not flood. If your land has rich soil that stays moist without soaking in stagnant water, it has the ideal natural potential for cocoa roots to grow deep and produce heavy yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli kwɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli jogbaŋŋ shi nu shwieee nɔ lɛ he miihia koko tsei. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Ojogbaŋŋ, adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ko yɛ ni baaha kookoo shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Can I plant cocoa on land where shallow crops like corn did not grow well?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, it is possible. Different crops draw nutrients from different depths. While shallow crops rely only on the topsoil, deep-rooted cocoa trees can reach nutrients and moisture far below the surface, provided the soil drainage is good.
ga: hɛɛ ebaanyɛ eba mli Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔkpɔi ni mli kwɔ srɔtoi amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ nɔ moŋ, shi cacao tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ náa niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hi

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains during their first few years to protect them from heat and retain soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small, young pods before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Dani ebaada kwraa?

english: When a cocoa tree lacks enough water, nutrients, or shade, it gets stressed and deliberately drops its tiny young pods—a process called cherelle wilt—so it can save energy to keep the remaining tree alive.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tsei lɛ bɛ nu, niyenii, loo hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, Kookoo tso lɛ haoɔ ni ejɛɔ etsuiŋ eshwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashwieɔ shi. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ wilting hela. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni eha cacao tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do some cocoa trees produce pods in three years while older ones take five years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii etɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni eheɔ afii enumɔ dani kookoo tso ko shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Newer hybrid cocoa varieties are specially bred to grow faster and start bearing fruit in 2 to 3 years, whereas traditional older varieties naturally take 5 years or more to yield pods.
ga: Atsɔse kookoo henɔi heei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ waa lɛ heɔ afii 5 loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: What causes my cocoa swollen stems and yellowing leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Swollen stems and pale yellow leaves are major signs of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease (CSSVD). It is a serious viral infection spread by insects that destroys the plant's food pathways and slowly kills the tree if left unchecked.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu kɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadii ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli hela (CSSVD) lɛ yɛ. Eji hela ko ni hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli ni koolooi gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ niyenii gbɛ lɛ, ni egbeɔ tso lɛ fiofio kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What should I do if I find one diseased cocoa tree with swollen branches on my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni amɛniji efuu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You must cut down and safely remove the infected tree immediately, along with surrounding contact trees. Leaving an infected tree on the farm allows insects to spread the virus to all your healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni okɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ashwie amrɔ nɔŋŋ. kɛfata tsei ni ebɔle he lɛ he Tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni oooshi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa kooloi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa o-cocoa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What are those tiny white insects hiding under my cocoa leaves, and do they harm my crop?
