ga: tsɛŋemɔ hela bibioo Mɛni ji mɛi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi kokoo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ? Ni ani amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Those tiny white insects are mealybugs. They suck the sap from your cocoa trees to feed themselves and, more dangerously, act as carriers that transport damaging plant viruses like Swollen Shoot from tree to tree.
ga: ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ Nomɛi ji mealybugs. Amɛmuɔ cacao tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ koni amɛkɛye amɛhe. Ni nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ ji akɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ nɔ ni kɛ tsei amli helai ni kɛ naagbai baa, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ, jɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ yaa.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cocoa trees too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting trees too closely forces them to compete for sunlight and soil nutrients. It also traps moisture under a dark, dense canopy, which creates the perfect humid environment for black pod disease to spread quickly.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ hu yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ashishi. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni black pod hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees need fertilizer to grow properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your cocoa trees have pale, yellowish leaves, grow very slowly, or stop producing healthy pods, it usually means the soil nutrients are exhausted and need replenishment with cocoa-specific fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cacao tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, edaa blɛoo waa, loo ekpa ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa ni ehe bahiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɔɔ kookoo he lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure will restore their green color and help them grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of soil food, leaving the land weak. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. gbɔjɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ tsina kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my crops very close together in the field?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to small and weak harvests. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to produce larger crops.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni egbɔjɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why is it important to use wooden stakes to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ awo mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines onto stakes exposes the leaves to full sunlight so the plant can make more food. It also prevents leaves from rotting on the damp ground, allowing the tubers below ground to grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. Ehaa baai hu shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: What is making tiny holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the center growing point of the plant. Spraying neem leaf extract or appropriate insecticides early in the morning will protect your crops from them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaabu onibii ahe kɛjɛ enɛɛmɛi ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally built to survive harsh weather and poor soil with very little water. Removing them early is critical because they steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni adebɔɔ fee koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ nu fioo mli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ehe miihia ejaakɛ ejuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: How do I stop my cassava roots from rotting in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water sits around them for too long. Planting your cassava stems on raised dirt mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away quickly, keeping the roots safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ta amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. O-cassava tso lɛ ni ooodu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. ni oha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why should I cover the bare dry soil around my crop roots with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during sunny days, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu lɛ mli la ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under direct heat. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby creates living shade trees that protect the young cocoa from hot sunlight until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Baaha tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ aba ni baabu kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off before any tomatoes grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plants experience extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of water. Giving your tomato plants steady water at their base during hot spells keeps the flowers attached so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ he. Ha o-tomato tsei lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ koni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow strong, or that too much water around the roots is stopping the plant from taking up food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. loo nu ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi babaoo tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and look dry during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up during hot afternoons to shade themselves and prevent water from escaping, but if they stay dry and rolled up, it usually means the soil needs more water or tiny insects like whiteflies are sucking the sap from the leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsi nu naa koni ekajɛ mli. Shi kɛji akɛ amɛgbi lolo ni amɛkpãtã hu? Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ. Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cowpea plants turning dark purple?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves are often a sign that the crop cannot get enough phosphorus from the soil, which usually happens in poor soil or when cold, wet ground stops the roots from growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ enaaa fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ loo kɛ́ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the air gets too hot or when the soil dries out, because the plant drops its flowers to save energy and water just to stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop have huge green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall leafy stems above ground instead of sending food down to build fat roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni yɔɔ fɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight; they need shade trees or plantains nearby to act like living umbrellas while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni efee enii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the soil instead of sprouting after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen in the soil to wake up and grow. When the ground stays soaked in standing water for days, the seeds choke and rot before they can push shoots above ground.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛte shi ni amɛdara. kɛji akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu ni ekã shi mli gbii babaoo Dumɔwui lɛ baatsi ni amɛbaagboi dani abaanyɛ ashɛre ŋmeii lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there tiny ragged holes all over the fresh leaves inside my corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli lɛ fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by fall armyworm caterpillars, which hide deep inside the growing center of the young maize plant and chew through the leaves before they open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cutworm ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni akɛtee ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛ.

english: Why does my plantain crop collapse and fall over even when there is no big storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ miiho lɛ? He ni ahum wuji bɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny worms called nematodes or stem borer insects eat away the roots and the base of the plantain stalk underground, leaving the heavy plant without a firm grip on the soil.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shi tsei ni tsii lɛ ni nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow so thin and weak when weeds grow close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe waaa be mli ni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your crops, effectively starving the planted crop until the weeds are removed.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye tsei lɛ kɛyashi be mli ni jwɛi lɛ baaje mli.

english: What is Agra rice, and why are so many farmers in Ghana planting it instead of old local seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji Akara Omɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ duɔ Accra ŋmãa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kusum dumɔwui lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Agra rice is an improved rice variety bred to perform very well in Ghanaian conditions. It yields more bags per acre, matures faster, and produces strong grains that do not break easily during milling compared to traditional local seeds.
ga: Akara ŋmãa ji ŋmãa ko ni atsɔse lɛ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Ghana shihilɛi amli. Ewoɔ baagi babaoo yɛ acre kome mli, ekwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ewoɔ dumɔwui ni mli wa ni fiteee oya yɛ be mli ni aŋmɔɔ lɛ kɛ akɛto blema maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ahe.

english: How do I know if seeds brought from abroad or official dealers will actually grow well on my farmland?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ loo kɛjɛ maŋ onukpai ni jaa lɛ adɛŋ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni mikwɛɔ okwaayeli lɛ yɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds perform best when they are adapted to your local rainfall, temperature, and soil. Certified seeds sold through government-approved channels in Ghana have been tested in local soils to ensure high germination rates and good crop yields before reaching farmers.
ga: Dumɔwui tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛtsake amɛhe kɛha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, dɔlɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛtsɔɔ gbɛi ni Ghana nɔyeli lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ akwɛɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ koni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai dani amɛshɛɔ okwaafoi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest produce smaller yields when I replant them the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo beni mikɛwoɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds gradually lose their vigor and can carry hidden diseases from the previous season. Buying fresh, certified seed ensures you get uniform growth, disease resistance, and full yield potential every planting season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi fiofio ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ aba. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha amɛdara be fɛɛ be, helai akamɔ amɛ, ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ daa be fɛɛ be mli.

english: Why do my rice plants turn yellow and stop growing when water sits still in my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: While rice needs water, stagnant water starves the roots of fresh air (oxygen). Without oxygen, the roots cannot breathe or absorb essential soil nutrients, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and stunts the plant's growth.
ga: be mli ni ŋmãa he hiaa nu Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa (oxygen) shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛhe niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa tsei lɛ daraaa.

english: Why do my rice crops fall over flat on the ground just before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miigbee shikpɔŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: This is called lodging, and it happens when crop stems are too tall or weak to support heavy grain heads. It is usually caused by applying too much nitrogen fertilizer, planting seeds too closely, or strong winds during the grain-filling stage.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ abobaahe. Ni ebaa kɛ́ tso lɛ tso lɛ kwɔ tsɔ loo ebɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfi dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa yɛ be mli ni awoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How long does Agra rice take from the day I plant it until it is ready for harvesting?
ga: Be enyiɛ Akara ŋmãa heɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ he ni abaakpa?

english: Agra rice takes about 110 to 120 days (around 3.5 to 4 months) to mature. This shorter growth period helps farmers harvest early before the dry season begins or fit two farming cycles into a rainy season.
ga: Akara ŋmãa heɔ aaafee gbii 110 kɛyashi 120 (aaafee nyɔji 3.5 kɛyashi 4) dani eshɛɔ. Nɛkɛ shweremɔ be kuku nɛɛ haa okwaafoi kpaɔ nii mra dani hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi loo amɛshɛɔ hulutsoo be mli okwaayeli sɛɛkuu enyɔ he.

english: How do I know the exact right time to put fertilizer on my rice crops so it doesn't go to waste?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni mikɛwo mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli ŋmãa koni amɛkafite?

english: Rice needs fertilizer at specific key growth stages: early on for building roots and shoots (about 2 weeks after planting), and again during panicle initiation (when the stem thickens before producing seeds). Applying fertilizer during heavy rains or too late in the season causes nutrients to wash away before roots can drink them.
ga: Omɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ dalɛ bei titri mli titri: mra dani ekɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii aba (aaafee otsii enyɔ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ) kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ shishijee be mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. (Beni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ.) Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ.

english: Why does my rice produce empty, light husks with no real grain inside at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ hiɛ ŋmãa ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ bɛ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Empty grains happen when the crop suffers from severe drought, extreme heat, or lack of nutrients during the flowering stage. If the plant does not get enough food and water at this exact moment, it cannot fill the seed shells with starch.
ga: Dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ amɛmli yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli. Kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkɛ starch afata dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted seeds during the first month of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni midu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that naturally grow fast to claim sunlight, water, and soil food. Clearing weeds early in the first 3 to 4 weeks allows your young crop seedlings to establish strong roots and build a leaf canopy that shades out future weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni daa oya koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he sɛɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa odumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛfeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa jwɛi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the center shoots of my young rice plants turning white and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ futafuta ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: This damage, called 'deadheart,' is caused by stem borer insects. The worm-like larvae burrow inside the stem and eat the inner tissues, cutting off the flow of water and nutrients to the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘tsui gbele’ lɛ, jɛɔ kooloi ni boteɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ amli. Lalai ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Efoɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni hoɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ naagbee ni miida lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need to be planted under larger plants like plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu mi-kokoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Planting them under plantains provides natural shade that protects tender leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ dumɔwui ashishi lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb up tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse ŋmei tso ko koni enyɛ ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need maximum sunshine on their leaves to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high off the damp soil, which also prevents diseases from ruining the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akafite baai lɛ hu.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a survival trick used by cocoa trees to conserve water when soil is dry. Fewer leaves mean less moisture escapes into the hot air, allowing the tree to survive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ko ni cacao tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi. Baai fioo tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ joɔ foi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ nɛɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Heat stress prevents proper pollination, so the plant sheds the blossom instead of growing a tomato.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Tsei lɛ gbee shi yɛ tomatoi ni amɛbaadu lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Growing maize repeatedly in the same spot strips the soil of specific plant foods that corn needs to thrive. Rotating your plot with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts good nutrients back into the dirt naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná tsei amli niyenii komɛi ni he hiaa abɛi koni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaha niyenii kpakpai aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young corn plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn is hungry for nitrogen, which is a main food plants use to stay green and grow. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the central leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that loves to hide in the soft inner leaves of corn. Checking your field early and spraying with recommended biological or target treatments prevents them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa baa mli ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ shwie amɛnɔ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn dark and spoil within two days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ mli beni atsa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Unlike crops with tough skins, cassava roots breathe heavily and decay rapidly once detached from the living plant. Processing them quickly into gari or flour preserves them before air and moisture cause rotting.
ga: Esoro lɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ ahe. Cassava shishifãi lɛ muɔ waa ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ oya lɛ, ehaa ehiɔ shi dani kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa egboɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over right when the bunches of fruit get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji aduawai lɛ je shishi amɛdara pɛ?

english: Plantain stems are top-heavy, and heavy fruit bunches pull them down, especially if wind pushes them or if soil pests have weakened the root system underground. Supporting the stem with a strong wooden prop keeps the tree standing.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ amli tsii. ni aduawai akui ni tsii gbalaa tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ba loo kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi.

english: How can I tell underground groundnuts are ready for harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can test harvest readiness by pulling up two or three sample plants around the farm. If the inside of the pods shows dark brown markings and the seed skins are firm and fully colored, your field is ready to pull.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka kpamɔ he saamɔ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ ni ooogbala kɛbɔle ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ mli wa ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaagbala.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them directly under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need temporary shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their delicate leaves and quickly dries out soil moisture. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa gives seedlings the shelter and cool environment they need during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná he ko ni amɛhi kɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa seedling from a nursery is strong enough to be planted in my main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: A healthy cocoa seedling ready for transplanting should have strong, dark green leaves, a firm woody stem, and an undamaged taproot. Avoid seedlings with pale leaves, spotted foliage, or weak stems, as they will struggle to survive the stress of moving into the open field.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu lɛ aná baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ, tso ni wa, kɛ shishifã ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, baai sɔrɔtoi, loo amɛshishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛje haomɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli ni amɛyaa lɛ mli baa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut off unnecessary branches and parasitic plants from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa kɛ tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches and removing parasitic weeds opens up the tree crown to allow sunlight and breeze to flow through, which reduces fungal diseases. It also ensures the tree directs all its nutrients toward producing big cocoa pods instead of feeding useless stems.
ga: Tso lɛ mli jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ baagbele tso lɛ yiteŋ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa shi Ekwɛɔ hu koni tso lɛ aŋɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmɔji wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ niyenii

english: What causes my cocoa flowers to dry up and fall off before they turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop without fruiting due to poor soil nutrients, prolonged dry spells, or a lack of natural pollinating insects like midges. Maintaining moderate shade, preserving humidity, and avoiding heavy pesticide spraying during peak flowering helps insects pollinate the flowers successfully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni bɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. aloo adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii tamɔ midges ni bɛ, ni haa hulutsoo be ni sa mli. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ shi babaoo yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ ni oootsi ohe kɛjɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni kooloi ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ aye omanye.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and rot during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This rot is caused by a fungal infection commonly known as Black Pod disease, which thrives in cold, wet, and humid conditions. You can prevent it by clearing weeds around the base, pruning thick foliage to let air in, and picking ripe pods promptly so the disease does not spread.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ lɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ black pod hela. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ ni ooojie kɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ ni oookpa koni kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ atsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvesting when their outer skin completely changes color—usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange. Harvesting pods when fully ripe ensures the beans inside have built up the natural sugars required for proper fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. aloo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ mli Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, ehaa kɔfi ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli sugar ni he hiaa koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cover my freshly extracted cocoa beans with plantain leaves for a few days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baa haa kookoo ŋmeii ni ajie ehee lɛ ahe gbii fioo komɛi dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Heaping cocoa beans under plantain leaves allows natural fermentation to happen, which kills the seed germ, removes bitterness, and develops the rich chocolate flavor and brown color. Skipping this step produces flat, bitter beans that cocoa buyers will reject.
ga: Okɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ato plantain baai lɛ ashishi koni ewo adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ ahe hewalɛ. Enɛ gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa tsokolate lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ otsi gbɛ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔfi yibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ baakpoo enɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my established cocoa trees turning light green instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Light green or pale leaves usually mean the soil is running out of essential nutrients like nitrogen. Applying well-decomposed organic manure or approved cocoa fertilizers around the root zone helps restore leaf health and improves your harvest yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛhe su tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ nii loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛbɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni eha baa lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha okpamɔ lɛ mli yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Which large trees can I keep on my cocoa farm that will provide shade without stealing food from my cocoa?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei wuji manyɛ mahi mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baaha mihe ajɔ mi ni mijuuu niyenii kɛjɛɛɛ mi-kokoo lɛ mli?

english: Leguminous forest trees like Albizia species make good shade trees because their deep taproots draw water from far underground without competing with cocoa roots. They also capture nitrogen from the air and drop leaf litter that naturally fertilizes your topsoil.
ga: Koo mli tsei tamɔ Albizia haa hulutsoo kpakpa ejaakɛ amɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni amɛkɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ yeee akaŋ. Amɛmɔɔ nitrogen hu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛshiɔ baai amli jwɛi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: How does the traditional 'Abunu' system work when I enter an agreement to establish a cocoa farm for a landowner?
ga: Te kusum nifeemɔ ni ji ‘Abunu’ lɛ tsu nii eha tɛŋŋ beni mikɛ mihe wo kpaŋmɔ ko mli akɛ mato kookoo ŋmɔ maha shikpɔŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: In the 'Abunu' sharecropping system, the tenant farmer clears the land, plants the crops, and manages the cocoa until it reaches maturity and starts bearing fruit. Once established, the farm and its yields are divided into two equal parts—one half for the landowner and one half for the farmer.
ga: Yɛ ‘Abunu’ sharecropping gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli lɛ, okwaafoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, amɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni amɛkwɛɔ kookoo lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ekwɛɔ ni ebɔi yibiiwoo. Kɛji ato shishi lɛ, abaaja ŋmɔ lɛ kɛ emli nibii amli awo fãi enyɔ ni yeɔ egbɔ, fã kome ji shikpɔŋtsɛmɛi, ni fã kroko lɛ ji okwaafoi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow before the ears are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing important plant food like nitrogen in the soil, or they are getting either too much water or too little.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. loo nu babaoo loo fioo ni anáa

english: Pepper plants often shed their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when they do not get enough water, which stresses the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tso lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my tomato stems wilt and die suddenly even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ po lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting is often caused by tiny diseases or insects in the dirt that damage the roots, stopping water from moving up into the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela bibioo ko kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa trukaa. loo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ Enɛ haa nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How does mixing animal manure into my land help my crops grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛfutuɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural plant food and helps the ground hold water better, making it easier for crop roots to feed and grow.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller every season when I plant the same crop on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo daa be mli beni midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop every year removes the exact same nutrients from the dirt without giving the soil time to rebuild itself.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds will not sprout if they are buried too deep, if the ground is too dry and hard, or if the seeds are old and spoiled.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni ewa loo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ ni egbo

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin when I plant the stems very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo beni adu shishifãi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete with each other for space, water, and soil food, so none of them can grow fat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso ko bɛ ni baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do young crops dry up fast in the dry season while older crops stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ fɛ̃i be mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Young plants have small roots near the top of the dirt where it dries out quickly, while older crops have long roots that reach water deep underground.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii. Ebɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ, ni egbiɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi kakadaji ni shɛɔ nu mli shɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves get burnt when I clear all the large trees around my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shãa beni mijie tsei wuji ni bɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and need partial shade from bigger trees to protect them from strong sun heat and heavy drying winds.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crops whenever rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild and tough, so they can take up water and soil food much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ gbeyei ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide temporary shade, protecting the young cocoa plants from heat stress and dry soil.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi he.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the season helps restore green growth and increases yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, dark environments. Pruning heavy tree branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods quickly prevents the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Fɔ̃ɔ ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa koni hulu lɛ ashɛ he kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to be harvested from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before they can grow into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop due to extreme heat, dry soil, or irregular watering. Mulching the soil around the base helps keep the ground cool and moist so fruits can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ hewɔ. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ baa.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that spread viruses. Controlling these insects early keeps the leaves expanding normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of soil nutrients. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni okɛ babaoo aku sɛɛ aba oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to push wooden poles into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi tso ko awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to grow healthy leaves and make big tubers underneath. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, preventing rot diseases and giving them maximum access to sun.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la koni amɛkwɛ baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee bulbs agboi yɛ amɛshishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fitemɔ naa ni oha hulu la lɛ ashɛ he babaoo.

english: Should I plant my seeds as soon as the very first rain falls in the major season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛ?

english: It is better to wait until the rains are regular and consistent. The very first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that can scorch young seeds and dry out newly germinated sprouts.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa ni ebaa shi. Bei pii lɛ, be kukuoo ko nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. No haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when I put fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ fɔmɔ nii woɔ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the growing season ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa feɔ ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava and maize together allows you to make the best use of your land and labor. Maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months for early income or food, while cassava takes longer to mature and fills out the space after the maize is cleared.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ oshikpɔŋ kɛ onitsumɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli koni akɛha shika loo niyenii yɛ shishijee mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛɔ ni eyiɔ jɛmɛ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: If I plant my crops very close to each other, will I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and small yields. Proper spacing gives each crop enough room to grow strong and produce maximum yield.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle to survive when I plant them in an open field without larger trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong, direct sun which burns their leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that shield the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni wala yɔɔ mli aba koni ebu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: How does covering the soil around my plants with dry grass or leaves help them during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the ground around your plants with dry plant material acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, and slowly decomposes to add nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso nibii ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya oya yɛ latsaa mli ni efite fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow before the crop is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ebaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on growing maize usually mean the plant is short on key nutrients like nitrogen or is not getting enough water. Adding organic manure or the right fertilizer restores green growth and helps the cobs fill out well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ organic loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop and curl up during the hot afternoon even when the ground is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Pepper leaves curl or droop in intense afternoon heat to protect themselves from losing water too quickly through their leaves. Once the midday sun cools down in the evening, the leaves usually stand back up.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni baatsɔ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ teɔ shi.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yam tubers when I plant yam on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ sweet potato ŋmeii bibii beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same spot repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your crops or planting beans and peas helps the soil rest and regain its strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ. Ebaaha niyenii mli nibii komɛi aje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni enáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to keep clearing weeds even after my crops have grown bigger than the grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maya nɔ mafo jwɛi lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ da fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds continuously steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your crops no matter how tall your crops get. Regular weeding ensures all the nutrients in the ground go directly into developing your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli be fɛɛ be. Ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ha lɛ he. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ koni onibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots growing around my plantain stem instead of leaving them all to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain tsei lɛ je kpo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha fɛɛ aya hiɛ lɛ

english: Leaving too many shoots around one plantain stem causes them to compete with each other for food, leading to small bunches. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant produces a large, heavy bunch that commands a good price.
ga: Ni aaashi ŋmeii lɛ abɔle Plantains babaoo ni yɔɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ baaha amɛye niyenii he akaŋ. causing a small bouquet Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ to lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei agboi ni tsii ni kudɔɔ jara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it helpful to apply heavy chemical fertilizer to my crops when they are already flowering?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni tsii baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli be mli ni amɛmiiwo fɔfɔi momo lɛ?

english: Applying high-nitrogen fertilizer while crops are flowering can cause the plant to grow more leaves instead of forming fruits, or cause flowers to drop off. Fertilizers must be applied at the right stages so the plant focuses its energy on developing healthy food or tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo wo tso lɛ mli be mli ni tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ awo baai babaoo yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. aloo eha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ be ni sa mli koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ ama niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ anɔ.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the bottom up, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for deep green leaves and healthy growth, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps fix this.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ dalɛ kpakpa baa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do tiny holes appear on my corn leaves with dark dirt inside the plant stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni muji ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ tso lɛ tsei lɛ amli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that hides inside the young corn plant and eats the leaves before they open. Catching them early and applying recommended sprays or neem liquid stops them from ruining the harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem spray loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ atsu nii koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm because their roots steal the water and nutrients meant for your crop, and their leaves block sunlight. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to soil food.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct strong heat from the sun. Tall shade trees or quick-growing crops like plantain act like umbrellas, shielding the delicate cocoa leaves from burning until the crop matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ adamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains hu tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Buu kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crop yields drop when I plant seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, space, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed well and produce bigger fruits or cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, ŋwɛi, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha niyenii kpakpa kɛ aduawai loo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my yam farm need wooden poles for the vines to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ he hiaa tsei ni akɛwoɔ wein tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tuber using sunlight on their leaves. Staking the vines spreads the leaves out to catch direct light, which helps the yam under the ground grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaagbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa koni enine ashɛ la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ agboi babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when heavy rain falls for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ waa otsii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water drowns the roots and allows fungal diseases to spread. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my farm right before a big downpour of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes loose fertilizer off the topsoil and away from your field before the plant roots can drink it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is moist but strong rain is not falling.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔji amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enɛɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience severe heat stress or lack of water. The plant discards the flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out during high heat.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ kpe. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil every season and lets maize-specific pests live in the dirt. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts restores the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow green and leafy. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure early will help the leaves turn dark green and produce big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná toi wuji.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen food from the air and store it in their roots and leaves. When you harvest them and let their plant remains rot in the farm, they leave natural fertilizer behind in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen nibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Beni okpaa amɛ ni ohaa amɛtsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they are stressed by dry weather, poor soil food, or attack from small sap-sucking insects like mirids. Keeping proper shade trees, feeding the soil, and managing insect pests will help the flowers stay on and grow into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. niyenii ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen, tsei akwɛmɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: What makes my tomato leaves curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies, or by extreme heat and drought. Controlling whiteflies early and keeping the soil evenly moist helps protect the plant leaves so they stay flat and open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli Early Whitefly Control Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe.

english: Planting seeds too close together causes plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and smaller yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food and room to produce larger, healthier crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that builds the tuber underground. Climbing up stakes lifts the leaves off the ground away from damp shade and diseases, allowing them to catch full sunlight to grow bigger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni feɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaa gbee kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo kɛ helai ahe. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdu sweet potatoes wuji.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when there is heavy rain and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and heavy fruiting bunches make the tree top-heavy. Supporting fruiting trees with strong wooden props and mounding extra soil tightly around the base keeps them stable during storms.
ga: Plantain shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ fɔfɔi ni tsii ni woɔ yibii lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ aduawai asɛɛ ni akɛ shikpɔŋ kroko ni akɛfata he lɛ toɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he shiŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my young crops so much in the first few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ baa shi kwraa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crop seedlings and quickly steal the water, soil food, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early in the first month gives your crops a strong advantage to establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, sũ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ oya. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ kpele yɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaatswa lɛ mli.

english: Why is it risky to plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell, which dries out the topsoil and scorches germinating seeds. Waiting until the rains become regular ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to grow strong roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni eshãa dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛ́ oomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen fertilizer in the soil, or the soil has become waterlogged, preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and become crinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when there is an imbalance of nutrients in the soil.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu bɛ tsei amli loo be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, the remaining leaves turn a darker green, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Baai ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting shoots even when I haven't planted them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ lɛ? Ni miduuu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams naturally break their resting period after a few months of storage because heat and humidity trigger the tuber to wake up and begin new growth.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite amɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛto lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, latsaa kɛ latsaa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ teɔ shi ni amɛjeɔ dalɛ hee shishi.

english: Why do some plantain suckers grow into strong plants while others stay thin and produce small bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi yɛ mlɛo ni amɛjara mli bibii bibii lɛ.

english: Suckers with narrow, sword-like leaves have stronger roots and food reserves than suckers with broad leaves, allowing them to grow faster and produce larger fruit.
ga: Tsofɔi ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ klante lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni niyenii babaoo toɔ he fe tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees away before planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct sunlight; they need partial shade from shade trees or food crops like plantains to keep their tender leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ hulutsoo tsei loo niyenii tsei, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbaa bibii lɛ akashã.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural food source that helps nearby maize plants grow better.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my swamp rice crop need so much standing water in the field during its early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peat ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he hiaa nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns competing weeds and keeps the soil soft and wet, which helps young rice roots absorb plant nutrients easily.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ agbo, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa tso lɛ mli niyenii lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do we plant cassava using pieces of the stem instead of planting seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔkɛ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava seeds take a long time to grow and often produce weak plants. Using healthy stem cuttings allows the new plant to grow faster and produce large, reliable tubers that are identical to the strong parent plant.
ga: Cassava dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa ni bei pii lɛ amɛwoɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ shishi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso hee lɛ ada oya ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni tamɔ fɔlɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ aba.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green so the crop can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my maize plant is about to start forming cobs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-abele tsei lɛ miibabɔi ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: When flowers called tassels appear at the very top of the stem and soft silky threads show on the side, the plant is starting to form cobs. This is when the plant needs plenty of water so the cobs fill up with kernels.
ga: Beni fɔfɔi ni atsɛɔ amɛ tassels lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ ni siliki kpãai ni yɔɔ blɛoo jeɔ kpo yɛ esɛɛgbɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ baabɔi fɔfɔi feemɔ. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei he hiaa nu babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui eyi ŋmei lɛ mli obɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to catch light and make food for the underground tubers. Staking also keeps the leaves off the hot, wet soil, which prevents diseases and rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná la ni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baa lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai kɛ fitemɔ baaa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much fertilizer. Giving your plants steady watering and light shade during the hottest hours helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: What causes the leaves on my cassava plant to look wrinkled and patchy with yellow and green spots?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ? Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: This is caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects or by planting infected stems. You can protect your farm by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and removing affected plants early.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa, ni ŋmei bibii yɛŋ loo tsei ni tsɛŋemɔ hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu ni ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ mra lɛ nɔ.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering or a lack of calcium in the plant as the fruit develops. Keeping the soil moist continuously and adding wood ash or agricultural lime to the soil prevents this.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli be mli ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ tso sũ loo okwaayeli mli sũ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why is it so important for me to clear weeds when my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Clearing weeds within the first month gives your crops a strong start to produce a good harvest.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa kpamɔ kpakpa.

english: Why does my maize wither so quickly whenever the rain stops for just two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ oya nɛkɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ otsii enyɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Maize has roots that stay close to the surface, where the top soil dries out quickly under the sun. Spreading dry grass or leaves around the bases of the plants helps trap moisture in the ground during dry periods.
ga: Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baagbi oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛaawo Tsei lɛ ashishitoo he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the big trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight because intense heat burns their tender leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving large shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa from direct sun and holds soil moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ la ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu dumɔwui ni daa oya yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land before growing my maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ dani madu be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, the leftover nitrogen enriches the soil, helping your next crop of maize grow taller and greener with less need for expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni obaakpa Nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii. Ye obua o-maise ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ akafite ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do I need to heap the soil into big mounds before planting my yam seed pieces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabua muji babaoo naa dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, and well-drained soil to expand into large, healthy tubers. Building mounds creates deep, loose soil that gives the tubers room to grow while preventing water from collecting around the roots and causing rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni etsɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Gɔŋ ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa bulbs lɛ daa lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekabua ehe naa. shishifãi kɛ fitemɔ

english: Why does swamp rice yield better when there is standing water kept on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni nu ni ato yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Standing water smothers weeds that would normally compete with the rice for nutrients and light. Rice plants are specially adapted to thrive in flooded conditions, so the water keeps them well-hydrated while naturally keeping pests and weeds under control.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni kulɛ ekɛ ŋmãa baatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ la. Afee omɔ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛshwere yɛ shihilɛi ni nu afua yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, nu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejɛɔ adebɔɔ mli eyeɔ kooloi bibii kɛ jwɛi anɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves are a sign that your maize plant is starving for nitrogen. Because nitrogen moves inside the plant, the corn takes food from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps fix this issue.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nitrogen lɛ nyiɛɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa heɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmãa hee ni eda yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed almost all their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to conserve water and prevent drying out. The plant is not dead; it goes into a resting state underground and will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the first rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni egbiɔ koni akɛto nu he ni akagbi. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebabote shikpɔŋ shishi hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli. ni ebaakwɛ tsei heei kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.
