english: Why are my tomato blossoms falling off the plant instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too hot, water supply is uneven, or the soil lacks nutrients like calcium and phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and feeding the soil helps flowers stay on and develop into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. Aloo niyenii kpakpai tamɔ calcium kɛ phosphorus bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ niyenii ha shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids hiding on the undersides of the leaves, or viruses spread by these insects. Spraying the leaves with neem oil or targeted insecticides helps stop the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni gbeɔ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekpa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra green shoots growing from the bottom trunk of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These extra shoots, called chupones, steal valuable water, nutrients, and energy away from the main tree. Removing them directs all the plant's food into producing bigger and healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupones lɛ juɔ nu ni jara wa, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ehaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ nii, ni ehaa kookoo ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize thoroughly before putting it into storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ kwraa dani mikɛwo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize contains moisture that encourages dangerous molds like aflatoxins to grow and attracts grain-eating insects like weevils. Drying the corn completely keeps the grain hard, safe for consumption, and protected for long-term storage.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aflatoxin lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmeii. Abele ni agbiɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha niyeli ni abuɔ he kɛha be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is a main plant food, or the soil has too much trapped water. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii titri ko bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo ni ato Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans on my land make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has special roots that pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth to feed your next crop naturally.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle leaves of my maize and leaving small dirt behind?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ ŋmãa lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ ni eshiɔ muji fioo ko yɛ esɛɛ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing part of the maize plant. Applying approved insecticides or putting a mixture of neem leaf extract or clean sand inside the plant's funnel early in the morning can stop them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni daraa lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii loo akɛ neem baa mli nu loo ŋã ni mli tse ni akɛfutu tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ahe leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which transmit viruses to the plant. Controlling these insects early using neem oil sprays or soapy water helps keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni kɛ hela lɛ yaa tso lɛ nɔ Mra ni akɛyeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo nu ni akɛ samla tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes the plants tall and weak, resulting in smaller harvests compared to crops planted with proper spacing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni egbɔjɔ Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto tsei ni adu yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight and heat because their leaves and roots are soft. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantain around young cocoa creates a umbrella that protects them from drying out in the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahewɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, awo cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa cacao tsei lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when there is not enough plant food in the soil. Keeping the soil moist with regular watering and covering it with dry grass mulch helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my crops when the plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni tsei lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will quickly steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight your crop needs to establish strong roots. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crops get all the food they need to start strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ oya koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because the excess water stops air from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. suffocate Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to build tall stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up to catch direct sunlight, which helps the leaves make food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also prevents leaves from getting rot diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkafiteɔ.

english: Why are my crop yields lower nowadays even when I plant at the same time every year in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni miduɔ amrɔ nɛɛ miiba shi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli daa afi yɛ Ghana moŋ lɛ?

english: Weather patterns have changed over time, causing unpredictable rainfall and hotter sun. Planting according to traditional months can lead to crop loss if the rains come late or stop too early.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba kɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ waa baa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ kusum nyɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ loo ekpa mra tsɔ.

english: How does sudden intense sun mixed with irregular rain affect my growing rice?
ga: Te hulu la ni naa wa trukaa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaná mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Flucutuations in sun and rain stress the plants. Extreme heat dries out soil moisture quickly, while irregular rain prevents the roots from taking up enough nutrients to fill the grain heads.
ga: Hulu la ni tsakeɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haoɔ tsei. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: How many bags of rice should I reasonably expect to harvest from one acre of land?
ga: Esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa ŋmãa kotokui enyiɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ?

english: Under standard good management and average weather conditions, a farmer can expect to harvest around 30 to 35 bags of rice per acre.
ga: Yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ shishi. Okwaafoi baanyɛ akpa ŋmãa kotokui aaafee 30 kɛyashi 35 yɛ acre kome mli.

english: Why do my farm yields change every year even when I don't change how I farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ tsakeɔ daa afi lɛ? Shi kɛlɛ, mitsakeŋ bɔ ni mifeɔ okwaayeli mihaa lɛ.

english: Yearly yield changes happen because natural factors like sun heat, rain timing, and pest pressures shift every season, directly impacting how much crop survives to harvest.
ga: Afi mli ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi baa ejaakɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ tsakeɔ daa be, ni enaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni eshwɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How much rice seed do I need to plant on my one-acre farm for a good harvest?
ga: Nibii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji acre 1 mli koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Using around 87 kilograms of quality seed per acre ensures enough plant density without overcrowding, allowing each plant enough space and soil nutrients to yield well.
ga: Kɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni miihe ashɛ 87 kg tsu nii yɛ acre kome mli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ayi fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛyimɔ obɔbɔ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What happens if I plant too much seed on my acre of land to try and get more harvest?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre lɛ nɔ koni mikɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Planting too much seed causes crops to crowd each other out. They fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and smaller, fewer grains.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ amɛhe. Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii.

english: Why does my rice turn yellowish during short dry spells in the middle of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: When the soil dries out during hot spells, crop roots cannot absorb nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow from lack of nutrients.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi yɛ be mli ni latsaa Tso lɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Where is the best place on my land to plant rice if the rainfall is unpredictable?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmã kɛji nugbɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baa?

english: Low-lying areas or inland valley bottoms hold water longer during dry spells, protecting your rice crop when the rain fluctuates.
ga: Hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo jɔɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ haa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ o-rice tsei lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ.

english: How can I protect my crops if the rain stops unexpectedly before harvest time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa dani kpamɔ be shɛ?

english: You can protect your crops by using drought-tolerant seed varieties, keeping soil covered with organic material to trap moisture, or setting up simple water storage systems.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. loo ama gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛtoɔ nu he

english: Is it true that modern farming conditions in Ghana require different methods than what our elders used?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli shihilɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ biɔ gbɛi sɔrɔtoi fe nɔ ni wɔ onukpai lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Yes, because rainfall patterns and temperatures have shifted, older planting calendars may no longer match the seasons, so farmers must adapt by using improved seeds and water management.
ga: Hɛɛ, be mli ni nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be tsakeɔ lɛ. Ekolɛ dumɔwui kalanda momo lɛ kɛ bei lɛ kpaaa gbee dɔŋŋ, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ atsake amɛhe kɛtsɔ dumɔwui kɛ nu he gbɛjianɔtoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are getting too much shade or not enough shade from the bigger trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo tso ko miiná hulutsoo babaoo loo enáaa hulutsoo bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ tsei wuji amli?

english: Too much shade makes cocoa trees grow tall and thin with very few pods because they cannot get enough sunlight. Too little shade turns leaves yellow and burns young pods, especially during the hot dry season.
ga: Kɛ́ hulutsoo tsei lɛ fa babaoo lɛ, ehaa cacao tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo, ni amɛnáaa ŋmeii fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa amɛnáaa. Kɛji akɛ akɛ shade fioo pɛ tsu nii lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shãa. Titri lɛ, yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How many years after planting will my hybrid cocoa seedlings start producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni mi-hybrid cocoa dumɔwui lɛ baabɔi ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit in 2 to 3 years with good care, whereas older traditional cocoa varieties take about 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and shady conditions during the rainy season when water stays on the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing light green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by small whiteflies.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ ji mɛi ni hiɛɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make green leaves and grow strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to prune or cut extra branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo maŋɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or useless branches so the tree spends its food and energy on growing big, healthy cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmɔji wuji ni mli wa fe nɔ ni ehe baahia ni ekɛ baai krokomɛi afata he.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves in dry weather to save water and protect themselves from dying of thirst when there is no rain.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kumai he kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: What causes the flowers on my tomato plants to fall off without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences water stress, which prevents the flowers from forming fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Enɛ ɔ haa nɛ fɔfɔi ɔmɛ nyɛ we nɛ a wo yiblii.

english: Why do plantain leaves split into ribbons during heavy wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ fãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves split on purpose so strong winds can pass through easily without tearing down the entire plant trunk.
ga: Akɛ yiŋtoo gbala plantain baai lɛ amli bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa anyɛ atswa amɛ nɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbalaŋ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, strong roots that are built to steal food, water, and sunlight before domestic crops can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni abɔ amɛ koni amɛju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani maŋ tsei lɛ anyɛ ama amɛhe shi.

english: Why do my maize leaves look fine during the day, but when I wake up in the morning, parts of them are eaten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ fɛo waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ? Shi beni mite shi leebi lɛ, aye eko?

english: Pests like fall armyworms and cutworms are nocturnal. They hide in the soil or deep inside the plant leaves during the hot day to protect themselves, and then come out at dusk to feed on your crops.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms kɛ cutworms lɛ yeɔ gbɛkɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsei ahe baai amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Kɛkɛ lɛ, amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ gbɛkɛ mli koni amɛbaye oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my groundnut plants close up tightly at night like they are sleeping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ ŋmɛɔ gbɛ gbɛkɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛwɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnut leaves naturally fold up at night to conserve moisture and protect themselves from cold night winds, opening back up in the morning to catch sunlight.
ga: Peanut baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe gbɛkɛ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni tswaa gbɛkɛ lɛ he. Egbeleɔ ehe ekoŋŋ leebi koni eha hulu la abote mli.

english: How can I protect my garden crops from insects that only come out to destroy leaves in the night?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ baai lɛ ahe gbɛkɛ?

english: Applying an organic neem seed extract spray late in the afternoon coats the leaves with a bitter taste, preventing night-feeding pests from eating your plants when they emerge at dusk.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsi gbɛkɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ otsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye otsei lɛ beni amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are growing well underground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ?

english: A healthy canopy with lush green leaves and a thick, sturdy main stem shows that the cassava plant is successfully manufacturing food and storing reserves in its underground tubers.
ga: Kpoji ni mli wa ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tso titri ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ niyenii ni ekɛhaa kɛ nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops turning yellow along the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yellow leaf edges usually mean the plant is lacking potassium in the soil or is struggling to take up water, which prevents nutrients from reaching the tips of the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ahe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ potassium yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo enyɛɛɛ ejie nu. Enɛ haaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ayashɛ baai lɛ ashishi.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off before forming any pepper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or lack of water. Keeping the soil constantly moist and shaded with mulch helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ emli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni awo mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the stalks of my young maize plants turning purple?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves and stalks on young maize are a sign of phosphorus deficiency, often caused when the soil is too cold or overly waterlogged for roots to absorb nutrients.
ga: Baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: When planted too close, crops compete fiercely for light. They spend all their energy growing tall to reach the sun instead of developing strong stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ la yeɔ akaŋ waa. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛshɛ hulu lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa, nɛ e woɔ yiblii nɛ tsii.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants adapted to the environment, allowing them to absorb rainwater and soil nutrients far quicker than introduced crop plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya kwraa fe nibii ni aduɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves dry up and turn brown when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive. Direct, unshaded sunlight burns their soft leaves and evaporates soil moisture before the roots can drink it.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Can I cut a single large yam tuber into smaller pieces to plant, or will it rot in the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafolɔ sweet potato tuber agbo kome mli bibii bibii koni mikɛdu? Aloo ebaagbo yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can cut a large yam tuber into smaller pieces to plant. As long as the cut pieces are allowed to heal properly before planting, each piece will grow into a complete, healthy yam plant that yields a good harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofolɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji amli bibii bibii kɛha dumɔ, kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ ŋmeii ni afo lɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsa jogbaŋŋ dani adu. Eko fɛɛ eko baatsɔ sweet potato tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baaha yibii kpakpai aba.

english: How heavy or big should a yam tuber be if I want to cut it up for seed?
ga: Te esa akɛ sweet potato tuber lɛ adara loo etsii aha tɛŋŋ kɛji oosumɔ ni ofo mli ni ofee dumɔwui?

english: A healthy tuber weighing around one kilogram is ideal for cutting into smaller seed pieces. This size gives each cut piece enough stored energy to sprout strongly and build a good root system.
ga: Tubers ni wa, ni tsiimɔ aaafee kilogram kome lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui lɛ afolɔ bibii bibii. Nɛkɛ dalɛ nɛɛ haa fã fɛɛ fã hewalɛ ni ato ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ekɛ shishifã kpakpa aba.

english: How do I keep cut yam pieces from rotting before they sprout in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mifo lɛ naa koni ekafite dani ekwɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: After cutting the tuber, let the moist cut surfaces dry in a shady, well-ventilated spot for a day or coat them with clean wood ash. This forms a protective layer that stops soil germs and moisture from causing rot.
ga: Beni afo yitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Ha he ni afo lɛ ni efɔ lɛ agbi yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli gbi kome. Aloo okɛ tso sũ ni he tse awo mli. Enɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekafite.

english: How long does a cut seed yam usually take to sprout out of the soil?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ dani yam dumɔwui ni afo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Under good soil moisture and warm temperatures, a cut seed yam usually begins to sprout and push its first shoots above the soil within three to four weeks after planting.
ga: Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulutsoo be shishi lɛ Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato dumɔwui ni afo lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ.

english: Why should I try new planting methods when the traditional way has always worked for my family?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka gbɛ hee ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ makwɛ? Akɛni blema gbɛi lɛ etsu nii eha miweku lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ lɛ.

english: Traditional methods work, but improved techniques help you produce much more crop from the same size of land while using fewer planting materials, saving you money and increasing your total harvest.
ga: Kusum gbɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii Shi ŋaai ni atsake lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ nibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ he ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni okɛ dumɔ nibii fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii Okɛ shika ato ni oha onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know if a new crop practice will actually produce a bigger harvest on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha yibii babaoo aba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: New practices are tested to improve how plants get light, water, and soil nutrients. You can test a new method on a small patch of your farm first to see how much more it yields compared to your old plot.
ga: Amɛkaa nifeemɔi heei amɛkwɛɔ koni amɛha bɔ ni tsei lɛ naa la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ. Obaanyɛ oka gbɛi heei okwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko. lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona bɔ ni ebaawo yibii babaoo fe oŋmɔ momo lɛ.

english: Why do yams grow better in high soil mounds rather than on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ amli fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand smoothly underground. Mounds provide loose earth for the tubers to grow big without pushing against hard ground, and they prevent water from standing around the roots.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Gɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛtsiii shikpɔŋ lɛ waa. ni otsi nu naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe

english: Why do my yam plants need tall sticks to climb on while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa niji ni kwɔlɔ koni ekwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves produce food for the underground tuber using sunlight. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground so leaves get full exposure to the sun and stay safe from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. koni baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe

english: Will planting my seed yams closer together give me a higher harvest?
ga: Ani sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha yibii babaoo aba?

english: No, planting too close forces the crop to fight for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in very small tubers. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets what it needs to grow full-sized yams.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehe awo hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii waa baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ sweet potato ni dalɛ fa babaoo.

english: What happens if I plant my seed yam too deep in the mound?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If planted too deep, the young shoot burns through all its energy trying to reach the surface and may emerge weak or fail to sprout at all. Planting at a moderate depth keeps the seed safe and allows quick sprouting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, Young shoots lɛ shãa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni miitao ni eshɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ̃ fioo loo ekwɛɛɛ kwraa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni ehaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest every year even though I clear and farm the exact same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mitsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the earth as they grow. When you farm the same patch of land continuously without adding manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil becomes exhausted, resulting in lower yields each season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ oya nɔ otsu shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni no haa yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy green leaves and strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni wa.

english: If I plant my crops closer together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small plot of land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani minɔ ni?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leads to weak, thin stems and smaller overall yields compared to properly spaced crops.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my seeds die after sprouting when I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboi yɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot dry spell that bakes the topsoil. Seeds sprout with the initial wetness, but young roots quickly dry out and die if steady rains haven't fully set in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ hulutsoo be ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ shãa lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishijee mli. Shi shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ daa.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which thrives in high humidity. Overgrown shade trees and unpruned cocoa branches trap damp air around the pods, allowing the fungus to spread easily.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni shwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Shade tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine kɛ kookoo niji ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni ebɔleɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, too much nitrogen fertilizer, or poor air movement can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their blossoms before fruit can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ baa.

english: Why does my cassava grow tall with lots of leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has excess nitrogen or when the plant receives too much shade, cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves rather than storing food in its underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ náa hulutsoo babaoo. Yucca lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings grow better when I plant plantains next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Broad-leafed plantains grow quickly to provide shade and trap moisture, keeping the soil cool while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Broadleaf plantains lɛ daa oya koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wither so quickly during a short dry spell while my neighbour's crops stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔji lolo lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil forces roots to stay near the surface where ground dries quickly. Adding organic matter like compost helps loosen soil, allowing roots to grow deeper where moisture remains longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my farm than the seeds I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants naturally adapted to local climate and poor soil conditions, allowing them to absorb available water and light much faster than domesticated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ la ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni akɛkwɛɔ shia lɛ amli lɛ.

english: The first rain often heats up dry soil without leaving enough long-lasting moisture. If you plant right away, seeds might sprout and then quickly dry up and die before the main rainy season settles in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaaa efee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi oya ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba.

english: Why are my maize leaves rolling up tightly into tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from hot sun and dry winds. It is the plant's natural way of reducing surface area so it loses less water through evaporation.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebaa ehiɛ he lɛ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, nu fioo pɛ laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my traditional maize seeds yield less food nowadays compared to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi blema ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ŋmɛnɛ fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: Weather patterns and soil conditions have changed over time. Old seed varieties often struggle with hotter temperatures and irregular rainfall compared to newer, drought-tolerant seed varieties.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni egbɔ lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I leave dried weeds on top of my soil instead of burning them after clearing my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ?

english: Leaving dry vegetation covers the soil like a blanket, keeping it cool, preventing soil water from evaporating in the heat, and slowly decomposing into natural fertilizer.
ga: Tsei ni egbi ni ashiɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni fiofio lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does planting yam on the exact same piece of land every year make my harvest smaller each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes ni miduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Yam draws heavy nutrients from the soil. Planting it in the same spot continuously exhausts those specific nutrients and allows pests and diseases that attack yam to build up in the soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes gbalaa niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny without producing good fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. They spend all their energy growing taller to reach light instead of building strong stems and fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛdara ni amɛyashɛ la he moŋ fe ni amɛaafee tsei kɛ aduawai ni wa.

english: Extreme heat or inconsistent watering stresses pepper plants. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy just to keep itself alive instead of making fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli kɛkɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do armyworms damage my maize farm more severely during warm, dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ waa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures speed up how fast armyworm eggs hatch and grow, while dry weather weakens the maize plants, making it easier for pests to consume the crop quickly.
ga: He ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii akui lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛdaraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their lower leaves during hot, dry periods to cut down on water loss. Dropping leaves helps the plant preserve water in its stems and underground roots.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ, ni nu hɔmɔ baa koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtoɔ nu yɛ amɛshishi shishi tsei kɛ amɛshishifãi amli.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year if I keep planting the same crop on the same field without resting the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ mihe lɛ?

english: Crops feed on specific nutrients in the soil. Planting the same crop continuously exhausts those specific foods, leaving the soil worn out and unable to support strong crops for future seasons.
ga: Tsei yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ fiteɔ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts have natural power in their roots to feed the soil with fresh air nutrients, acting as a natural food restorer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli ni amɛkɛ aerobic niyenii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I make mounds across my sloped land instead of planting straight down the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa gɔŋ yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Mounds built across a slope act as small walls that stop heavy rains from washing away your rich topsoil and fertilizer down the hill.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ama yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo bibioo ko. No baatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do farmers cover the ground around yam mounds with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, holds water in the ground longer during heat, and rots over time into extra soil food.
ga: Hay tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni egboɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burn and turn brown when there are no shade trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle direct afternoon sun. Shade trees act like large umbrellas, protecting young crops until their stems become strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ shwane mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: If I plant my cassava very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe lɛ Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting cassava too closely makes the plants fight for soil food and light, resulting in many tiny, thin tubers instead of heavy, healthy ones.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei ni aduɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye niyenii kɛ la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji yitsei bibii babaoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ yitsei ni tsii ni he wa najiaŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop in the hot afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: Hot afternoon sun causes plants to lose water faster through their leaves than roots can drink it up. Drooping is the plant's way of protecting itself from drying out, and it usually bounces back by evening.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Foji ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, ekuɔ esɛɛ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ

english: What happens to my maize if I delay removing weeds from the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ shwie shi?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your maize. Leaving them too long stunts your maize plants and leaves you with tiny cobs.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-ŋmã lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oshi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha o-corn tsei lɛ afee shoo ni ebaaha oná ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why should I cut off extra stems from my tomato plants when they are growing thick leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ tomato tsei lɛ amli be mli ni tomato lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Removing extra stems helps the plant direct all its energy and water into producing large, juicy fruits instead of wasting energy on useless leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni mli ewo nu. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why is it important for me to check under my plantain leaves early every morning for insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ plantain baa lɛ shishi daa leebi koni mana kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli?

english: Spotting pests early allows you to stop them before they multiply into an army that can destroy your whole farm's harvest.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni anaa mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpa amɛ dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ asraafoi ni baanyɛ akpata oŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why is clay soil recommended for cocoa farming in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ajieɔ shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ he ŋaa kɛhaa kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Clay soil holds onto water and nutrients much better than sandy soil, keeping the cocoa tree roots well-fed and moist throughout the season.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ hiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai amli jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋã nɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo shishifãi lɛ yeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can I plant cocoa on farmland that is mostly sandy soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ babaoo lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa trees struggle in pure sandy soil because sand drains water away too fast and lacks the rich nutrients needed to support heavy cocoa yields.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ ŋã lɛ hoɔ oya tsɔ, ni niyenii babaoo ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee cocoa babaoo lɛ bɛ mli.

english: How do stones in my soil affect the growth of my crops?
ga: Te tɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Stones prevent crop roots from spreading deep into the earth to gather water and nutrients, which can leave your plants weak and stunted during dry periods.
ga: Tɛi tsiɔ tsei shishifãi anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛbua nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha otsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛhe afee shoo yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: What kind of crops can grow well if my farmland has a lot of small rocks and stones?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yɛ tɛi bibii kɛ tɛi wuji babaoo?

english: Hardy crops like cassava or certain legumes handle rocky ground better than sensitive cash crops like cocoa, though removing stones always helps roots grow deeper.
ga: Dumɔwui ni wa tamɔ sino loo ŋmãa komɛi tsuɔ tɛi ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe shika dumɔwui ni waaa tamɔ kookoo. Eyɛ mli akɛ tɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be moŋ.

english: Is it possible to turn rocky or stony land into a good farm?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ atsɔ tɛsaa loo tɛsaa shikpɔŋ nɔ afee ŋmɔ kpakpa?

english: Yes, by clearing away large rocks and repeatedly adding organic manure or compost, you can build up healthy topsoil over stony ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ tɛi wuji ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli shii abɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ ofee shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ hei ni tɛi yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why does rainwater disappear so quickly on sandy parts of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ laajeɔ oya yɛ ŋãi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large, loose particles with big gaps between them, causing water to drain straight down past the root zone instead of soaking in.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii wuji. Enɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shishifã lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni eeeŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has clay soil or sandy soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ?

english: Take a handful of wet soil and squeeze it: clay soil will stick together and form a smooth ball, while sandy soil feels gritty and crumbles easily.
ga: Mɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ ni okɛmimɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baakpɛtɛ ehe ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋã su ni efoɔ oya lɛ.

english: How can I improve sandy soil so that my crops don't dry out?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi?

english: Mixing decomposed leaves, crop waste, or animal manure into sandy soil helps it hold onto moisture and supplies essential food to your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egboi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite, loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii futu ŋã sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do crops grow very well in one village but poorly in a neighboring area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ akrowa kome mli shi ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Soil composition changes from place to place; one area may have naturally rich clay soil, while nearby land might be mostly sand or stones.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome kɛyaa he kroko. He ko baanyɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni ji adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ. yɛ be mli ni hei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋã loo tɛi babaoo.

english: What should I check in my soil before deciding to clear land for a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ yɛ dani makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ majie shikpɔŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ hee?

english: Check that the soil has a good amount of dark clay or loam, is free of heavy stone layers, and retains moisture well after rain.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná shikpɔŋ loo sũ ni mli edɔ ni sa. Tɛ ni tsii ko bɛ jɛmɛ. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow when it rains continuously for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain washes away essential nutrients like nitrogen from the topsoil and waterlogs the ground. This prevents plant roots from breathing and absorbing food, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa tso shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How do I know if the first rain of the season is enough for me to start planting my corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛje ŋmãa dumɔ shishi?

english: The ground needs to be wet deep enough (about a hand's depth) to support germination. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɔ bɔ ni sa. (aafee tso kome) koni eye ebua dumɔwu lɛ Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Mɔdɛŋ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwu lɛ akwɛ̃ ni egbo kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my corn plants grow very tall and thin with small ears when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛtoi bibii yɔɔ mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to catch light instead of building strong stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛmɔ la lɛ, ni no najiaŋ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei akutsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do crops planted close to big shade trees yield much less corn than those in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ tsei wuji ahe lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kwraa fe tsei ni adu yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Trees block the sunlight that crops need to manufacture their food, and tree roots steal water and nutrients from the soil, leaving little for the crops.
ga: Tsei tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná niyenii lɛ naa. Ni tsei ashishifãi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ko fioo pɛ eshwɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested corn spoil and grow mold if I store it right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji mikpa lɛ beni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains contain high moisture. Storing them wet creates a warm, damp environment where mold and pests thrive, so grains must be thoroughly dried in the sun before storage or sale.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ ni efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ, ni mli edɔ baa. he ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu mli dani akɛto loo ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my dried corn grains split or break easily when I prepare them for sale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ fãa loo efoɔ oya kɛ́ misaa mihe koni mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: If corn is dried too quickly under extreme heat or left out in alternating rain and strong sun, the grains develop internal stress cracks, causing them to shatter easily during handling.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa gĩ oya tsɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi loo ashi lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni tsakeɔ ehe kɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ haomɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, efoɔ oya beni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous corn harvest produce smaller yields than certified seeds from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their strength and vigor in the second generation, whereas certified seeds are specifically bred to resist diseases and produce high yields every time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop produce huge green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Having too much nitrogen in the soil causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do small holes suddenly appear in the central leaves of my young maize plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by early-stage pests like fall armyworms that crawl into the funnel of the plant and eat the tender growing leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mra be mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my crops in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive tough conditions. They have aggressive root systems that suck up water and fertilizer much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni heɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build healthy green leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or a balanced nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their dark green color and strength.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ni ja fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ su ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pod flowers drop off without turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their blossoms when they are stressed by too much direct sunlight, prolonged dry weather, or attacks by tiny pests like mirids (capsids). Maintaining shade trees and treating pests helps the flowers turn into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo shɛ amɛhe. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ he hulutsoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plants from fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the sap from young leaves. Spraying the underside of the leaves with neem oil or a mild soapy water solution helps get rid of these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie baai lɛ ashishi. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛya.

english: What causes my tomatoes to develop dark, rotten patches on the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi diji kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi dani ekwɛ̃?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually because watering is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding wood ash or lime to the soil helps prevent this rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite nɛkɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is suitable for planting cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmei dumɔ?

english: Good soil for cassava feels loose and drains water easily without becoming waterlogged or sticky like clay. Loose soil is essential because it allows cassava roots to expand and grow large tubers underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmei lɛ mli tse ni nu hoɔ oya ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli loo ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he tamɔ shikpɔŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he miihia waa ejaakɛ ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my crop field dry out so quickly even after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil loses moisture fast when it lacks organic material or is left bare under direct sunlight. Covering the topsoil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) acts as a shield to keep water in the soil longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli loo ashi lɛ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni oookɛwo mli Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe (mulching) tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he, ni ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or beans in the same farm plot with my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting beans or cowpeas alongside maize is very beneficial. Legumes take nitrogen from the air and naturally feed it into the soil, which acts as a free fertilizer for your maize plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Legumes lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn tsei lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking so long to grow after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers grow slowly when planted in hard, uncompacted soil, or when competing with heavy weeds for nutrients and water. Clearing weeds regularly and putting rich compost around the base speeds up their growth.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ sũ ni wa ni mli edɔɔɔ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ ekɛ jwɛi ni tsii miitswa akaŋ koni ena niyenii kɛ nu. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ daa. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni edalɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yam tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are mature and ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow, dry up, and die down at the end of the rainy season, showing the plant has finished storing energy underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni baai lɛ kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ eto shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots turn dark and spoil just two days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ mli edɔ ni egbo yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni atsa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots spoil quickly because they contain high moisture and react rapidly with air once cut from the plant stem. To avoid losses, cassava should be processed into gari, flour, or consumed shortly after harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ oya kɛji afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ hewɔ. koni akafite Esa akɛ afee Cassava gari, ashikishaŋ loo aye yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build green leaves and grow tall. It can also happen if the soil is too waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛmu niyenii.

english: How can I tell that my cassava plants are ready for harvesting without digging up all the roots?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa ni okɛ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava plants show they are mature when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off the stem, and the soil right around the base of the plant begins to crack open from the tubers swelling beneath.
ga: Cassava tso tsɔɔ akɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ bulb ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can feed. The tree intentionally sheds unpollinated or weak flowers so it can save its energy and water to grow just a few high-quality pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ, ni fa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshiɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe loo ni bɛ hewalɛ. Bɔni afee ni akɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ato koni akɛkwɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves to shrink the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, which reduces water loss during extreme heat. Once the sun goes down and temperatures drop, the leaves uncurl.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛ shwie he ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ baa shi. Beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why is it important for me to cut away the extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain tsei wuji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to put all its energy into growing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ awo dumɔwui wuji ni tsii ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to push tall sticks into the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi tsei kakadaji awo shikpɔŋ koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for the tuber underground. Staking also keeps leaves off the wet soil where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my farm make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil. When the cowpeas are harvested, that extra plant food stays behind to nourish your next maize crop.
ga: Cowpea tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Be ni esa akɛ akpa tsina ŋmei Nakai tso niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ baakã he ahi shi koni akɛha oŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the tiny green peppers dropping off my pepper plants before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ chili bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baagbee shi kɛjɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani etsɔ agbo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop young fruit when they suffer from uneven watering or sudden extreme heat. Giving your plants consistent moisture and mulching around their roots helps them hold onto their peppers until harvest.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛyibii bibii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa loo hulutsoo ni naa wa trukaa lɛ miipiŋ. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ mli fũu daa ni akɛ sũ wo amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni abaakpa.

english: Why are my cabbage plants drooping in the morning even when the ground feels wet from rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kaaba lɛ shwieɔ shi leebi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil is usually a sign of root rot or pests attacking the roots underground. When the roots are damaged by disease, they cannot suck up water to feed the leaves, even if the soil is full of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji shishifãi ni egbo loo ŋmeii ni tutuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he okadi. Kɛ hela efite shishifãi lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛnu nu ni amɛkɛha amɛbaai lɛ niyenii kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ po.

english: Why does my stored maize turn into powder and get full of small holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani eyi obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Tiny insects called weevils bore into the dry maize grains to feed and lay eggs. If the maize was not dried thoroughly before storage or was kept in an open sack, weevils multiply quickly and destroy the grains.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli koni amɛtao niyenii ni amɛwo amɛwui. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto loo akɛwo kotoku ni agbele mli lɛ, Weevils lɛ faa oya ni efiteɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and weak even when I plant good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. When weeds grow close to your plants, your crops have to fight for survival instead of using energy to grow big leaves and healthy produce.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ otsei lɛ ahe lɛ Ehe baahia ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awuu koni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaafite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdu baai wuji kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning light green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow fast. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, will I harvest more food from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too close together causes plants to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow strong and yield a larger overall harvest.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eda waa ni ewo yibii fɛɛ ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up and look tired during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni etɔ amɛ ni amɛkpãtã yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Crops roll or curl their leaves during high heat to trap moisture and prevent water from evaporating too quickly. They usually refresh themselves in the cooler evening or after receiving water.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ loo amɛshwieɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛha amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛhe yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli loo beni amɛná nu sɛɛ.

english: Why are small holes appearing all over the leaves of my garden eggs and vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ekɛ ehe miiwo eggplant kɛ aduawai ahe baai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Small holes are caused by insects like beetles or caterpillars chewing on the leaves for food. Inspecting the undersides of leaves early in the morning helps you find and treat these pests before they damage the crop further.
ga: Buji bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ladybugs loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai kɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni otsa amɛ dani amɛya nɔ amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves, but producing tiny roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is planted in very hard soil, it uses all its energy to build green stems and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa waa nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize in the same field without harming the maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni miyeŋ ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: Yes, cowpeas and maize grow well together because cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, which helps feed the maize while covering the ground to stop weeds from spreading.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni aha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmãa shwieɔ nɔ koni jwɛi akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and nourished helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni aha lɛ niyenii daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant fail to come up out of the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if they are planted too deep in the soil, if the soil is too dry, or if insects eat them underground before they can push through the surface.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji adu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi ye amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsi amɛhe kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do black spots appear on my crop leaves during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black spots in wet weather are usually caused by fungal diseases that thrive in high humidity and moisture. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to dry the plants and keep fungi away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii helai ni yaa hiɛ yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ baa. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tso lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves, or the ground is flooded with water which prevents the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my armyworms attack my maize leaves so quickly right after the plants sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi-corn baa lɛ oya beni tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths prefer laying their eggs on fresh, tender leaves of young maize crops. Once the eggs hatch, the young caterpillars immediately feed on the soft leaves to grow.
ga: Caterpillar ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛwo amɛwui lɛ yɛ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ji ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fɔ ni amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii Amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛkɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ baai bibii koni amɛdara.

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when temperatures become too hot or when there is a sudden dry spell without enough water, causing the plant to save its energy rather than produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni hɔmɔ ba trukaa ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kwɛɔ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: What makes my garden pepper plants stay short and bushy without growing tall?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe ehiaaa?

english: Pepper plants remain stunted if the soil is too hard for the roots to expand, if there are tiny pests like nematodes eating the roots under the ground, or if the soil lacks proper nutrients.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baakã he afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes ni yeɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ, loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa.

english: Why do my watermelons start rotting from the bottom while they are still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelons lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ kɛmiijɛ shishi be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Watermelons rot on the bottom when they rest directly on wet soil, allowing dampness and soil diseases to break through the skin. Placing dry straw or wood underneath the fruit prevents this.
ga: Watermelon baagbo yɛ shishigbɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ hewolo lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo tsei ni egbi wo aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn out watery and soft instead of firm when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee nɔ ni wa kɛ́ akpa lɛ?
