english: Cassava roots become watery if they are harvested during heavy rainfall when the plant is holding extra water, or if the field sits in waterlogged soil for too long before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ naa nu kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni tsei lɛ toɔ nu babaoo. aloo kɛji akɛ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ehi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing crooked shapes instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ ebɔle shi moŋ ni amɛfee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers bend and grow crooked when the soil underneath is stony, packed hard, or full of tree roots that block the tuber from pushing straight down into the earth.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ baakoto ni amɛkoto kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ ji tɛi, ewa, loo tsei shishifãi eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my newly planted cocoa trees burn and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mikoo tso ni midu ehee lɛ nɔ lɛ shãa ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves scorch because they are too tender to handle direct sunlight and dry Harmattan winds; they need temporary shade plants like plantains to protect them while their roots grow deep.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ejaakɛ amɛdarako tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains kɛha hebuu yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over on their own before the bunches are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when microscopic worms called nematodes or banana weevils eat away the underground roots, leaving the plant without a strong grip in the soil.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii lɛ ye shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing plenty of big leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When cowpea plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich compost, they put all their energy into growing leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ, tsinabii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in a clear open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava nearby provides shade and keeps the air moist until the young cocoa trees are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ebaaha hulutsoo be aba ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso bibioo lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crops turning yellow while the plant is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Heavy rains can also wash this nitrogen deep into the soil where plant roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ aho nitrogen nɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop and wilt during the afternoon heat even when the ground is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: When the sun is very hot, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it from the ground. Drooping is the plant's way of reducing leaf surface area exposed to the sun to conserve water until the afternoon heat cools down.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji gbɛ ko ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbaa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛyashi shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when the plant experiences sudden changes in water supply. Without proper pollination from insects or wind during stress-free conditions, the flower dies before forming a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na tsakemɔ trukaa yɛ nu jɛɛhe lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ kooloi loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ pollination ni sa yɛ shihilɛi ni haomɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagboi dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ toi bibii lɛ? Kɛji oodu dumɔwui babaoo Ha dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli.

english: Crops planted too close together compete heavily with each other for soil food, sunlight, and water. When they fight for resources, they spend all their energy just trying to grow tall rather than producing large, heavy cobs.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, hulu la kɛ nu mli beni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ koni amɛkɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmei agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up short, crooked, and small in hard soils?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ kukuji, amɛhe ejɔ, ni amɛji bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow by pushing down into soft soil. Hard or compacted soil acts like a wall, preventing the tuber from expanding long and smooth, forcing it to bend or stop growing altogether.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli jɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo. Etsiɔ yitso lɛ naa koni ekafee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Anyɛɔ enɔ koni ekoto loo ekpa dalɛ kwraa.

english: Why does my maize yield better when I plant groundnuts on the land during the previous season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ wo yibii jogbaŋŋ beni midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When you harvest groundnuts, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free fertilizer for the next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmei ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my cassava tubers to remain small even if cassava is a tough plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifee mi ŋmei lɛ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei lɛ ji tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal soil food, fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from the cassava. If the cassava plant lacks these resources during its early growth, it cannot store extra food in its roots to form big tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ ŋmei lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ bɛ nibii nɛɛ yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ, Enyɛŋ ekɛ niyenii ni fa fe nine ato eshishifãi lɛ amli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my cowpea crop grow lots of big green leaves but very few beans during heavy rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli?

english: Too much water and abundant soil moisture trick the cowpea plant into thinking it should keep growing leaves and stems instead of reproducing. The plant focuses on vegetative growth rather than making flowers and pods.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ lakaa cowpea tsei lɛ ni amɛsusuɔ akɛ esa akɛ amɛkwɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã. Tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ podi afeemɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plant curl up and turn yellow during hot, dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling during dry spells is often caused by sap-sucking pests like mealybugs or green mites that multiply quickly in warm, dry weather. They suck the juice out of the leaves, causing them to curl, turn yellow, and wither.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs loo green mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Amɛmuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. ha etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbo

english: How do I know if there is a good market demand for my crop before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji jara kpakpa miitao miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani madu?

english: You can determine market demand by observing how quickly buyers purchase the crop, whether local customers come back for more, and if traders are actively looking to buy it in large quantities.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole nɔ ni jara lɛ taoɔ kɛtsɔ bɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya lɛ nɔ. Ani maŋ lɛ mli jarayelɔi miiku amɛsɛɛ amɛmiiba koni amɛbahe babaoo? Ni ani jarayelɔi miitao ni amɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ babaoo?

english: Is there a good market for selling Ghanaian farm produce to people living abroad?
ga: Ani jara kpakpa ko yɛ ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ nibii ni jɛ Ghana ŋmɔji amli lɛ aha mɛi ni yɔɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, Ghanaian crops and farm products often have high demand among Ghanaians and international buyers abroad, especially when the produce maintains its traditional taste and high quality.
ga: Hɛɛ, Ghana ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ okwaayeli nibii ji nɔ ni Ghanabii kɛ majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ taoɔ waa be fɛɛ be. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ hiɛ eshishijee ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ekpakpafeemɔ ni nɔ kwɔ mli.

english: Why do some farm products sell out much faster in the market than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli nibii komɛi ahɔ̃ɔ oya fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Products sell faster when they offer consistent quality and superior taste, which creates high customer demand and encourages buyers to purchase in large quantities.
ga: Nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ hɔ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ amɛhi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe ŋɔɔ waa. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ nibii babaoo, ni ewoɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛhe nii babaoo.

english: Why is the taste of my harvested crop so important for my farm business?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ he hiaa miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ?

english: The taste of your produce directly affects customer loyalty; once buyers verify that your crop tastes good, they will always return to buy from you again.
ga: Bɔ ni onibii lɛ ŋɔɔ ha lɛ saa anɔkwayeli ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ yeɔ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji hɔlɔ lɛ ema nɔ mi akɛ onibii lɛ ŋɔɔ pɛ. Amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaahe nii kɛjɛ odɛŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I get local buyers to keep coming back to buy crops from my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha maŋbii ni heɔ nii lɛ aya nɔ aku amɛsɛɛ aba koni amɛbahe nibii ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Focus on producing crops with great taste and consistent quality, because satisfied buyers will always come back once they know your produce tastes great.
ga: Kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Ejaakɛ mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni amɛmiishɛ amɛhe lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba be fɛɛ be kɛ́ amɛle akɛ onibii lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: What does it mean for my farm if I am able to produce my crop in large quantities?
ga: Mɛni ebaatsɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji manyɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Harvesting in large quantities allows you to supply bigger market buyers, meet export demands, and earn more income while satisfying continuous market demand.
ga: Nikpamɔ babaoo lɛ haa onyɛɔ ohaa mɛi ni baahe nii yɛ jarayelihe wulu ko mli. Tsɔɔmɔ nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ ahe hiamɔ nii ni oná shika babaoo yɛ be mli ni otsuɔ jarayeli nibii ahe nii daa.

english: How can I store my harvested produce for a long time without it losing its good quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ minibii ni mikpa lɛ ato be kakadaŋŋ ni ehilɛ-kɛhamɔ lɛ akafite?

english: Using cold storage or refrigeration allows certain crops to stay fresh and retain their original taste for up to a year, preventing spoilage and loss of income.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni mli ejɔ loo friji tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛ shishijee ŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ afi. Tsi nibii ni fiteɔ kɛ shika ni baafite lɛ naa.

english: Will putting my farm produce in a refrigerator change its taste when I take it out later?
ga: Ani nibii ni mikɛwoɔ friji mli lɛ baatsake bɔ ni eyɔɔ fɛo ha kɛ́ mijie kɛjɛ mli sɛɛ mli?

english: No, proper refrigeration preserves the crop's natural flavor so that even after sitting in the fridge for a long time, it remains just as good as when it was freshly stored.
ga: Dabi, friji ni sa haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ hiɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ eta friji lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ po lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ lolo tamɔ beni ajie lɛ ehee lɛ.

english: Is it possible for processed Ghanaian crops to stay fresh for up to a whole year?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ Ghana tsei ni atsu he nii lɛ baahi shi ehee afi muu fɛɛ?

english: Yes, if the crop is properly prepared and kept in cold storage like a fridge, it can maintain its quality and taste for up to a year.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ asaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto tsu ko ni mli ejɔ tamɔ friji mli. Ebaanyɛ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi afi kome.

english: How does storing my crops long-term help me handle market demand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni mikɛ jarayeli nibii ni taoɔ lɛ kpeɔ?

english: Long shelf life allows you to hold onto your produce without spoilage, giving you the flexibility to sell in large quantities whenever market prices and demand are highest.
ga: Shihilɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni okɛtoɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ onibii lɛ toɔ ni efiteee. Enɛ haa onáa hegbɛ ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ nibii babaoo be fɛɛ be ni jarayeli jara kɛ nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ baaya hiɛ fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do I find small insects inside my mango seeds when I cut the fruit open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina kooloi bibii yɛ mango dumɔwui lɛ amli beni mifoɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: That insect is the mango stone weevil. The adult beetle lays its eggs on very young fruit, and the larva bores all the way into the center seed where it stays hidden while developing.
ga: Nakai kooloo lɛ ji mango tɛ ŋmei. Kpɔŋɔi ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ aduawai bibii waa anɔ. Ni ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwu lɛ teŋgbɛ, ni ekɛ ehe teeɔ jɛmɛ beni edara lɛ.

english: How can a mango look perfectly healthy on the outside but be rotten on the inside?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni mango afee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ shi egbo yɛ emli hu?

english: Pests like the stone weevil enter the fruit when it is tiny, and the outer skin heals over seamlessly. The insect grows silently inside the seed, only causing damage to the surrounding flesh later on.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ tɛ ŋmeii boteɔ aduawai lɛ amli kɛ́ amɛji bibii. ni epidermis lɛ tsaa jogbaŋŋ Kplukai lɛ daa dioo yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli shi amɛfiteɔ fãji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. sɛɛ mli pɛ

english: What is this 'stone weevil' that other farmers keep talking about?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘tɛ ŋmei’ ni okwaafoi krokomɛi wieɔ he lɛ?

english: The stone weevil is a specific insect pest that targets mangoes. It lives and feeds inside the hard inner pit (or stone) of the fruit, taking over the inside as the mango matures.
ga: Tɛ ŋmei ji ŋmei pɔtɛɛ ko ni yeɔ mango nɔ. Ehiɔ shi ni eyeɔ nii yɛ aduawai lɛ amli bu (loo tɛ) ni wa lɛ mli, ni ekɛ mligbɛ lɛ yeɔ najiaŋ kɛ́ mango lɛ shwere.

english: Why do my mangoes seem to spoil suddenly right when they become ripe and sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango lɛ fiteɔ trukaa kɛ́ ekwɛ̃ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: As the mango ripens, the stone weevil inside the seed finishes its growth. It eats its way out of the seed into the flesh, causing rapid decay just when the fruit is ready to harvest.
ga: Beni mango lɛ shwere lɛ Tɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃. Eyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni eboteɔ loo lɛ mli. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: How do insects manage to get into the hard stone inside a mango?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii boteɔ tɛi ni wa ni yɔɔ mango mli lɛ amli?

english: The insects do not bore through the hard stone of a full-grown mango; they enter when the fruit is very young and soft. The egg hatches on the baby fruit and the tiny grub easily crawls into the forming seed.
ga: Kplukai boteee mango ni eda lɛ tɛi ni wa lɛ amli. Ebaa be mli ni aduawai lɛ darako kwraa ni eyɛ blɛoo lolo lɛ. Wɔɔji shwieɔ aduawai bibii anɔ, ni ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli oya.

english: Why does the fruit flesh right next to the mango pit turn dark and mushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mango bu lɛ masɛi lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: When a seed insect like the stone weevil completes its development, it burrows out of the inner pit into the fruit flesh to emerge, leaving rot and soft dark patches around the pit.
ga: Kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni woɔ dumɔwui, tamɔ tɛ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ, Ebaajɛ mligbɛ bu lɛ mli ebote aduawai lɛ amli koni eje kpo. Ashi ni egbo ni ehiɛ okadii diji ni bɛ faŋŋ yɛ bu lɛ he.

english: Does an insect living inside the seed affect the tree itself or just the fruit?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni hiɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ saa tso lɛ he loo aduawai lɛ pɛ?

english: The stone weevil only damages the fruit and its seed; it does not harm the leaves or trunk of the mango tree itself, but it can spoil your entire harvest if left uncontrolled.
ga: Tɛ ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ aduawai kɛ emli dumɔwui pɛ. Eyeee mango tso lɛ baai loo eshishifãi lɛ awui. Shi ebaanyɛ efite onibii fɛɛ kɛji akɛ okwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is there any way to tell if my young mangoes have insects in their seeds before harvesting?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ ale kɛji mi mango lɛ yɛ kooloi yɛ emli dumɔwui lɛ amli dani akpa?

english: It is difficult because the tiny entry hole heals quickly without leaving a trace. Farmers usually detect an outbreak by checking fallen premature fruit or cutting open sample fruit early in the season.
ga: Ewa ejaakɛ bui lɛ daraaa. Ebaatsa oya ni eshiŋ nɔ ko nɔ ko. Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi naa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛtsɔ aduawai ni egbee shi mra lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ loo amɛfoɔ amɛmli yɛ be lɛ mli mra.

english: Does leaving rotten or fallen mangoes on the ground cause more pest issues next season?
ga: Ani mango ni ashiɔ ni egboɔ loo egbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo aba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, because stone weevils can survive inside the fallen mango seeds on the ground through the dry season and hatch to attack your new fruit crop when the next season starts.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ mango dumɔwui ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. ni ofo koni otutua onibii heei lɛ beni be ni baa lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ.

english: At what stage should I start protecting my mango trees so insects do not get into the seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mabɔi mi mango tso lɛ hebuu? Koni kooloi akabote dumɔwui lɛ amli?

english: Protection needs to start early during flowering and fruit setting. Once the fruit grows large and the seed hardens, the insect is already safely sealed inside where sprays cannot reach it.
ga: Esa akɛ aje hela lɛ naatsii shishi mra. Yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo be mli Beni yibii lɛ daraa ni dumɔwui lɛ mli waɔ lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, abaatsi kooloo lɛ naa shweshweeshwe. he ni spray lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ

english: If my soil already has green grass growing, why do I still need to put fertilizer to feed my crops?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ jwɛi eŋɔli momo lɛ Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii lolo?

english: Wild grass needs very little nourishment to survive, but farm crops like maize or cassava need extra nutrients—like plant food—to produce big tubers and healthy grains. Adding fertilizer gives the crop the right energy to grow strong and yield well beyond basic survival.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo pɛ he hiaa koo mli jwɛi koni amɛhi shi, shi ŋmɔ mli nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he hiaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ tsei aniyenii he miihia koni aná ŋmeii wuji kɛ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ haa amɛnáa hewalɛ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii ni fe shishijee wala.

english: What actually happens to the crop when I put food like manure or fertilizer around its base?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ mikɛ niyenii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe?

english: When you put fertilizer in the soil, rainwater dissolves it so the plant's roots can drink it up. These nutrients travel up the stem to help the crop grow taller, build green leaves to capture sunlight, and form healthy fruits or seeds.
ga: Kɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Niyenii nibii nɛɛ yaa tso lɛ yiteŋ koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃. Bɔɔ baai eŋɔli koni onine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. ni ewoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui ni mli wa

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests now compared to when I first cleared the land years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they pull natural nutrients out of the earth. Over time, continuous farming wears out the soil's natural food supply, so without adding fertilizer or letting the land rest, crop performance declines.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ baafite adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli loo kaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe. No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ amɛhaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and fail to grow even after I apply fertilizer during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops cannot swallow dry plant food. Water is required to dissolve fertilizer so the roots can absorb it; without moisture in the ground, the crop cannot take up the nutrients provided to it.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ami tsei aniyenii ni egbi. Nu he miihia koni akɛjie ŋmɔshi nibii koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni amɛnáa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ kɛkɛ.

english: How many years can a tree crop like cocoa keep producing good harvests before it gets too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ tso ko tamɔ kokoo baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: Tree crops usually take a few years to establish, reach their peak production between 8 to 10 years of age, and then hold steady for a while before yield naturally declines as the trees grow old and require rehabilitation.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ daa lɛ heɔ afii fioo komɛi dani amɛshɛɔ yibiiwoo ni fe fɛɛ he yɛ amɛ afii 8 kɛyashi 10 wala be mli, no sɛɛ lɛ amɛhiɔ jɛmɛ be fioo dani yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa ni ehe hiaa ni afee amɛ ehee lɛ.

english: If I keep feeding my cocoa trees with fertilizer every year, will the yield keep increasing forever?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo kookoo tsei lɛ amli daa afi lɛ Ani yibiiwoo lɛ baaya hiɛ kɛya naanɔ?

english: No, every crop has a natural biological limit. Feeding the tree helps it reach its full potential during its peak years, but after reaching full maturity around 8 to 10 years, yields level off rather than growing bigger endlessly.
ga: Dabi, tsei fɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ahe husui. Otsei lɛ ni oooha amɛ niyenii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛshɛɔ amɛhewalɛ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he yɛ amɛdalɛ afii ni fe fɛɛ lɛ amli. Shi yɛ aaafee afii 8 kɛyashi 10 ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ agbo ni bɛ naagbee.

english: Why do my crops stop growing taller after a certain point and start developing fruits instead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko sɛɛ ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops go through distinct growth stages. In the beginning, they focus all their energy on growing roots, stems, and leaves, but once fully grown, they switch their energy to producing seeds, fruits, or pods for harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ dalɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi amli. Shishijee lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi, tsei ashishifãi, kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ, shi beni amɛdaraa lɛ, amɛtsakeɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛyaa dumɔwui, aduawai, loo ŋmeii ni akɛbaakpa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it better to raise seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu awo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: A nursery acts like a safe home for tender young plants. It shields young seedlings from harsh weather, strong heat, and pests until they develop sturdy roots and stems that can survive on the main farm.
ga: He ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shia ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, dɔlɛ, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baaná shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant multiple crop seeds together in the exact same spot on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ be kome mli yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted together in one spot, they compete with each other for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to produce strong stems and full yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he kome lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa ni woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend cutting back old branches from established fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afo tsei ni woɔ yibii ni adu momo lɛ aniji momo lɛ?

english: Old or shaded branches waste the plant's food and energy without bearing much fruit. Pruning removes these weak parts so the food absorbed by the roots goes directly into growing healthy new branches and larger fruit.
ga: Niji ni egbɔ loo ni yɔɔ shade lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ fiteɔ ni ewooo yibii babaoo. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ nɛkɛ hei ni bɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛ niji heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai wuji baa.

english: How do I know when I should stop planting new seeds for the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ makpa dumɔwui heei adumɔ kɛha be lɛ?

english: Planting timing depends heavily on rain patterns; once the major rainy window passes, planting new seeds is risky because young crops will not get enough moisture to mature before the dry season sets in.
ga: Be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ damɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ nɔ waa. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eho. Dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ tsei bibii lɛ naaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛshwere dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Is it okay for me to keep adding fertilizer to my crops even after they have grown tall?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ maya nɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe beni mikwɛ̃ po?

english: No, crops need fertilizer mostly during their early growth and flowering stages. Applying fertilizer too late wastes your money and can actually burn or damage mature crops without increasing your yield.
ga: Dabi, tsei lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii titri yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa kɛ fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, efiteɔ shika, ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo efite ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ ni ehaaa yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I store my harvested corn so that insects do not destroy it before I can sell it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni kooloi akafite lɛ dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Make sure your corn is completely dry in the sun until the grains are hard, then store it in airtight hermetic bags or raised granaries to block moisture and keep destructive pests out.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni o-abele lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ amli baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto kotoku loo ŋmɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli koni ebu he kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ he, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akabote mli.

english: Can I harvest a small amount of green maize early to feed my family, or will that ruin the rest of the farm?
ga: Minyɛ mikpa ŋmãa fioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli mra. Koni makwɛ miweku lɛ? Aloo no baafite ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ?

english: You can safely harvest a little green maize early for immediate family use without damaging the rest of the field, as long as you pick gently without snapping neighbouring stalks or disturbing nearby roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ shishijee koni akɛtsu nii yɛ weku lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okpataaa he ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɛ Shii abɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii fiofio ni okɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akumɔɔ loo ogbaaa shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa.

english: How can I make my small farm operate like a real business instead of just planting to feed my family?
ga: Mafee ŋmɔ bibioo ko. Atsuɔ minɔ lɛ he nii tamɔ jarayeli nitsumɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu niyenii kɛkɛ ni okɛkwɛ oweku lɛ?

english: Treating farming as a business means keeping simple notebooks to track your spending on seeds and fertilizer, calculating your profits, and planning harvest sales when market prices are highest.
ga: Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ akɛ jarayeli nitsumɔ tsɔɔ akɛ aŋmalaa wolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Koni okwɛ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afiteɔ lɛ, bu sɛɛnamɔi ahe akɔntaa, ni oto gbɛjianɔ koni ohɔ̃ɔ nibii ni adu lɛ be mli ni jara wa fe fɛɛ.

english: How does new research from scientists actually help a farmer like me on my land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niiamlitaomɔ hee ni jeŋ nilelɔi fee lɛ baanyɛ aye abua okwaafoi tamɔ mi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Research creates improved seed varieties that resist local pests and dry spells, giving you bigger harvests and stronger crops using the same amount of land and effort.
ga: Nibii amlitaomɔ eha afee dumɔwui srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa yibii babaoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa kɛtsɔ he kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to grow different kinds of crops instead of planting only maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ makwɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa kɛkɛ?

english: Growing multiple crops protects your income if a pest or drought destroys one specific crop, and different plants feed the soil in different ways to keep your field healthy.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oshika he kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo hɔmɔ kpata nibii ni oduɔ lɛ eko hiɛ. Ni tsei sɔrɔtoi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ gbɛ̀i srɔtoi anɔ. Koni oŋmɔji lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ

english: What happens to my soil if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows field pests to build up, leading to smaller harvests over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ ekome Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I tell that my corn is completely mature and ready for full harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Corn is ready for full harvest when the outer husks turn dry and brown, the silks turn dark, and pressing a grain produces a firm, dry residue instead of milky liquid.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kwraa kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Siliki lɛ etsɔ ediŋŋ. Ni kɛ́ anyɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni eshwɛ ni egbi ni mli ewo muji lɛ feɔ nu ni tamɔ mliki najiaŋ.

english: Why do insects usually show up to attack my crops right when they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, kɛ́ amɛbɔi fɔfɔii lɛ, kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Flowering crops produce sweet scents and rich nutrients that naturally attract pests looking for food, which is why checking your farm weekly helps you spot and manage insects before they cause harm.
ga: Tsei ni fɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni taoɔ niyenii lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni otsi fɛɛ otsi mlikwɛmɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona kooloi bibii ni otsa amɛ dani amɛye mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops wilt and turn light green during a short dry spell, even when the surface soil looks dark?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ moŋ

english: Maize plants need moisture deeper down where their feeding roots are located. Heat causes leaves to lose water faster than the roots can pull it up from dry subsoil, leading to leaf wilting and nutrient slowdown.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ hia ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dɔlɛ haa baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni egbi lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper plant roots rot when water sits on my field for days after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need oxygen trapped in the soil to breathe. When water covers the ground without draining, the roots drown, stop absorbing food, and easily get infected by soil fungi.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efooo lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haaa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aná. ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ lɛ oya

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural defense mechanism to conserve moisture. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss and survives on storage roots underground until the rain returns.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi ji ŋmei adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli. Kɛtsɔ baai ni eshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haaa nu ni efiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shishifãi ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do young cocoa trees struggle and die if I clear all the tall trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgboi kɛji mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive intense direct heat and full sunlight. They need shade trees to lower temperatures, trap moisture in the air, and shield their delicate foliage until they grow strong.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la fɛɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing big bushy green leaves but very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ jwɛi agboi ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ.

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer causes tomatoes to focus all their energy on leaf and stem growth. To trigger abundant flowering and fruiting, crops need balanced nutrients including phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tomato kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. Fosfɔs kɛ potasium fata he Koni eha fɔfɔi kɛ yibii babaoo aba

english: Why does planting cowpeas alongside my sorghum help the sorghum grow greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du cowpea lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔŋ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen gas from the air and converts it into natural plant food in the soil. Nearby crops like sorghum feeder off this extra nourishment.
ga: Cowpeas ji legume weku lɛ mlinyo, ni ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ feedlot sorghum lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ fataa he.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and taller than my yam plants right after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkwɔ fe mi sweet potato tsei lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, quick-spreading roots designed to steal surface water and soil food before domesticated crops can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya. Afee amɛ koni amɛju nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai dani shĩa tsei lɛ anyɛ ama shi.

english: How will using a small motorized water pump help my dry-season vegetables yield better than bucket watering?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu pɔmp bibioo ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua aduawai ni yɔɔ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai fe nu ni akɛ baagi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: A motorized pump allows you to give crops deep, steady watering regularly without disturbing the soil structure around roots, keeping plants stress-free and growing quickly.
ga: Pɔmp ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu woɔ onibii amli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa efeɔ ekome. ni egbaaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa Ehaa tsei lɛ bɛ haomɔ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: What is drip irrigation, and how does it help crops thrive with less water?
ga: Mɛni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua tsei ni amɛdara kɛtsɔ nu fioo ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ?

english: Drip irrigation uses narrow pipes to deliver water drop-by-drop right at the crop's roots. This keeps soil continuously moist where the plant needs it while preventing water loss to evaporation or weeds.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ paipii bibii tsuɔ nii ni ekɛ nu lɛ yaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ hei ni tsei he hiaa yɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo loo jwɛi amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my rice plants form empty, dry husks when a hot spell hits while they are flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tsei lɛ tsɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishi yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: High temperatures during flowering dry out the pollen grains before they can fertilize the flower, preventing the grain inside from forming properly.
ga: He ni mli edɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ beaŋ lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ mli fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ fɔmɔ nii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaf tips of my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without protective shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh heat and retain moisture in the soil, the intense sun scorches the leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo. ni nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii bɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Koni ekɛtsi dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize crops turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong, green foliage. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farmland before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Rotating your crops this way feeds the soil naturally so your next crop grows stronger with less expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ atsake ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara waa kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni jara waaa lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to place cassava stem cuttings in the ground when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole gbɛ ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ oodu?

english: You should check the tiny nodes or buds along the stem where leaves grow. These buds must point upward toward the sky; planting them upside down confuses the plant, delaying root formation and leaf growth.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ mli. loo fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ tsei ni baai jɛɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ tso lɛ da ni ehiɛ efo shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afutu. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ afeemɔ kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out very small and thin when I plant stem cuttings very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ, kɛ́ midu tsei ni afolɔ mli lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots compete heavily with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Giving each plant proper space ensures root systems have enough room and food to develop big, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋshii mli waa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: What is causing ragged holes and sawdust-like material in the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu kɛ nibii ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They crawl deep into the growing center (the funnel) of young maize plants to chew on delicate green leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛshwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ hei (cones) lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my pepper fruits turning black and squishy while still hanging on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ shishi miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ be mli ni ekã shi lolo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the soil moisture changes too drastically between wet and dry, preventing the plant from absorbing enough calcium to build strong fruit walls.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ashishigbɛ fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake waa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛma aduawai gbogboi ni wa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my crops while the seedlings are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings grow slowly at first and will quickly lose the battle against fast-growing weeds, which steal vital soil moisture, nutrients, and sunlight required for early development.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ daraa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. ni abaaye enɔ kunim oya yɛ ta ni awuɔ ashiɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ mli. Enɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa, niyenii kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa kɛha mra be mli shweremɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to put wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward to catch sunlight for energy. Staking lifts the foliage off damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and encouraging larger tuber growth beneath the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la kɛha hewalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni ehaa tsei wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant before they turn into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells without water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which causes the plant to produce leaves instead of holding onto flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni nu bɛ mli loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food in the soil. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen away, so adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aniyenii titri Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell which end of a cassava stem cutting should face up when I am planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ ekwɛ ŋwɛi beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small bumps or nodes where leaves used to grow on the stick. Make sure those bumps are pointing upward toward the sky before pushing the stem into the soil, otherwise the plant will struggle to grow roots.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso nine lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani okɛ tso lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, tso lɛ baaná naagba yɛ shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my corn seeds very close to each other in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in thin stalks and very small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ, ni no haa amɛnáa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when planted directly in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in strong heat. They need temporary shade plants like plantains to shelter them from full sun while their roots establish deep in the ground.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛná hulutsoo be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible. When the leaves get enough light, they produce the energy required to grow large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni he wa lɛ aba.

english: Why is it risky to plant all my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often a 'false start' followed by a long dry spell. If the soil dries up completely after your seeds germinate, the young seedlings will die before the main rainy season sets in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘amale shishijee’ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba.

english: Why do crops grow better in dark black soil compared to reddish sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ diŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni ŋã tsuru yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Dark soil contains rich decomposed plant material (humus) that holds onto water and plant nutrients much better than light sandy soil, feeding your crops consistently.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ nɔ tsei ni egbo (humus) babaoo yɔɔ mli. Ehiɛɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii kpakpai amli jogbaŋŋ fe sũ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli ni mli tse. Ha onibii lɛ niyenii daa.

english: What causes ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli fãa?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like Fall Armyworm caterpillars that burrow into the central leaves of the plant. Spotting them early allows you to treat the crop before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa ŋmɔshi nibii dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop soft black spots on the bottom when I water them heavily from above?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli waa kɛjɛ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Watering heavily from above splashes soil onto the fruit and stems, spreading fungal diseases. It can also unevenly affect how the roots absorb calcium, causing the bottom of the fruit to rot.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ waa kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baaha sũ ashwie aduawai lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba. Ebaanyɛ ená calcium ni shishifãi lɛ nuɔ lɛ hu nɔ hewalɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ ashishi fiteɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same piece of ground three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, lowering your harvest over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How many years will I have to wait after planting cocoa before the trees start producing pods?
ga: Kɛ́ odu kookoo sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, while older traditional varieties can take 4 to 5 years. Once established, cocoa trees can continue producing pods for over 30 years with basic care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ewo mli yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5, kɛji adu pɛ. Cocoa tsei baanyɛ aya nɔ awo ŋmeii fe afii 30 kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What short-term food crops can I plant to feed my family while waiting for new cocoa trees to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ni heɔ be kukuoo manyɛ makwɛ koni mikɛha miweku lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni cacao tsei heei akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Crops like plantain, cassava, maize, and cocoyam are ideal to plant alongside young cocoa trees because they grow quickly, provide food and income in the first few seasons, and do not harm the young cocoa.
ga: Tsei tamɔ plantains, cassava, ŋmãa kɛ kookoo hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya. Eji niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ bei fioo lɛ amli ni eyeee kookoo bibii lɛ awui.

english: Can I grow plantains on the same piece of land with my young cocoa plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting plantains with young cocoa is a recommended practice. The plantains grow tall fast and provide essential shade to protect delicate young cocoa leaves from scorching heat during the sunny dry season.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ adu dumɔwui kɛ kookoo bibii. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he.

english: How do shade trees help my farm survive the dry Harmattan season in Ghana?
ga: Bɔ ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ ni ba yɛ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ

english: Permanent shade trees keep the soil cool, trap moisture in the ground, and block harsh dry Harmattan winds from drying out your cocoa plants, helping the farm stay green throughout the dry spell.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni etsĩɔ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni egbi lɛ naa koni ekahã o-cocoa tsei lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Which food crops require less heavy physical labor to maintain as I get older?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ he ehiaaa tsɔ akɛ makwɛ nɔ beni midaa lɛ?

english: Cassava and plantain require high effort mainly during planting and harvesting, but require less daily soil turning compared to crops like tomatoes or cabbages. Mature cocoa trees also require less intensive soil digging once fully canopy-covered.
ga: Cassava kɛ plantain biɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo titri yɛ dumɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli. Shi ebiɔ shikpɔŋ ni atsakeɔ daa gbi lɛ fioo kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ tomato loo kaabe he. Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ hu biɔ ni akumɔ amɛ waa fioo kɛji akɛ aha ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: What should I do if my cocoa trees have grown too tall for me to reach and harvest safely?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ kɛlɛ tsɔ ni minyɛɛɛ mashɛ he ni makpa shweshweeshwe?

english: You can perform heavy pruning or structural cutting to lower the tree canopy. Extension officers can teach you how to cut back high branches or train a lower shoot from the base so pods grow within easy reach.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee tso lɛ he ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii loo tsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ koni oha tso lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ bo bɔ ni ooofee ofolɔ tsei niji ni kɛlɛ lɛ. Aloo kasemɔ bɔ ni oootswa tu kɛjɛ shishigbɛ koni eha pod lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do many flowers drop off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: A single cocoa tree produces thousands of tiny flowers, but naturally sheds most of them because it lacks enough water, nutrients, or sunlight to turn every flower into a full pod. Proper fertilizer and pruning help the tree keep more flowers.
ga: Cacao tso kome woɔ fɔfɔi bibii akpei abɔ, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ amɛbɛ nu, niyenii loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi afee ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ wo fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ, ni afolɔ tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the branch before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet and overly shaded conditions. Removing the infected pods immediately and pruning extra foliage lets air flow through and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ kɛ hei ni hulu enyɔ shi fe nine lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni afolɔ tsei ahe tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni ekpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods as they get older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni egbɔ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their canopy thickens, blocking sunlight from reaching lower branches where pods grow, while soil nutrients wear out. Pruning overgrown foliage and adding organic or mineral fertilizer will stimulate old trees to start producing high yields again.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ da Eshishifã lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ afo baai ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ amli ni akɛ organic loo mineral fertilizer fata he lɛ, ebaawo tsei momo lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is good enough to support cocoa trees for many years?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ cacao tso nɔ afii babaoo?

english: Good soil for long-term cocoa farming should be deep, dark, crumbly, and drain excess water easily while staying moist. If weeds and leafy crops grow easily on the land without quickly turning yellow, the soil is likely healthy for cocoa.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ kookoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni mli kwɔ, ni eyɛ ediŋ, ni egbɛ eshwa, ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ajɛ mli oya yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji jwɛi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo ni amɛtsɔko ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo.

english: Why do my maize grains turn out different colors and uneven sizes on the same cob when I plant seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ahe sui kɛ amɛdalɛi yɛ ŋmãa kome nɔ beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When you plant saved seeds from hybrid maize, the crop crosses with different nearby crops. This causes the grain traits to split and mix up, resulting in uneven quality, variable sizes, and crops that buyers reject at the market.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ hybrid corn mli lɛ Akɛ tsei srɔtoi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ foɔ Cultivation mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ asui lɛ mli gbalaa ni amɛfutuɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji su ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee Variable size kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and dying before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is its main food for leafy growth. The plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves, signaling that your soil needs nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall and bushy above ground but leaving me with very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen makes cassava waste its energy building tall stems and heavy leaves. To get thick tubers, the crop needs balanced nutrients like potassium, which directs the plant's food storage downward into the roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ hewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ekwɛɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni tsii. koni ená yitso ni mli wa Tsei lɛ ahia niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium, ni baaye abua tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ato kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep dropping off the plants during the hot dry season without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni pepper ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause severe stress to pepper plants, forcing them to shed their flowers to save water and keep the main plant alive. Giving the crop light shade and regular water keeps flowers attached so fruit can set.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa pepper tsei anɔ. Nyɛɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni ajie amɛ shi koni nu akafite ni eha pepper tso lɛ ahi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ la ni mli jɔ kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa ha tso lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ atswa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants blossom with many healthy flowers but then end up with empty or very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miifɔlɔ kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo shi eshishifãi fioo pɛ loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called flower thrips attack cowpea flowers right when they open, sucking out the juice and damaging the internal parts. Because the flowers are ruined inside, the plant cannot form pods.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ flower thrips lɛ tutuaa cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ pɛ. Ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ mligbɛ nibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ emli. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee pods.

english: Why does my harvested maize grow mold and spoil inside storage bags even after I dried the cobs in the sun for two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ gbii enyɔ egbi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ.

english: Maize grains can feel dry on the outside while remaining damp deep inside the core. If you bag the grain before moisture levels drop throughout the entire kernel, sweat builds up inside the sack and causes quick mold growth.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmãa lɛ baanu he akɛ egbi yɛ kponɔgbɛ shi eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ mligbɛ tɔ̃ɔ. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo kotoku mli dani nu ni mli edɔ lɛ ba shi yɛ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ amli lɛ, Latsaa buaa ehe naa yɛ kotoku lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa oya.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree branch before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ dani amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a water mold that multiplies in dark, damp conditions under heavy tree shade. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and moving air dry out the pods, stopping the rot from spreading across the farm.
ga: Fungi ni yɔɔ nu mli ni faa yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsei ni mli tse lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi. Tsi ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam plants produce very thin tubers if I leave the vines to crawl on the bare ground instead of staking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni mli tseee waa kɛji mishi wain tsei lɛ koni amɛkplekeshi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ amɛ baawo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam leaves are like mini solar panels that produce food for the tuber below. Staking lifts and spreads the leaves into full sunlight, allowing the vine to make maximum food and send it down to swell the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ tamɔ hulutsoo be mli nibii bibii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: Soil-borne organisms can infect the roots and block the tiny tubes inside the stem that carry water upward. Even if the soil has moisture, the damaged root system cannot push water up to the leaves under hot sunshine.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atswa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsi tsɔnei bibii lɛ anaa. Yɛ tso lɛ mli ni hiɛɔ nu kɛyaa ŋwɛi Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ Shi shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛre nu kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya baai lɛ amli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do tiny insect holes suddenly appear in my dry maize grains after I store them in sealed sacks for a month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ bu lɛ je kpo trukaa yɛ mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ? No sɛɛ lɛ, mikɛwo kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli nyɔŋ kome.

english: Weevils often lay microscopic eggs inside the grain while the crop is still maturing in the field. Once you bag the dry maize, those hidden eggs hatch inside the sack and the young beetles start eating their way out from the inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛwui bibii lɛ amli yɛ dumɔwui amli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ okɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ wo kotoku lɛ mli Nakai ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baafɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Ni ladybug lɛ baaje shishi eye nii kɛjɛ emli.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees on the same land with my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide essential shade for young cocoa plants, protecting them from intense sunlight that can burn and damage them.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ. Buu cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni baanyɛ ashã cacao tsei lɛ ni efite amɛ lɛ he.

english: Can direct sunlight kill my cocoa trees if I do not provide cover for them?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbe mi-cacao tsei lɛ kɛji mikɛ he ko haaa amɛ?

english: Yes, intense sun beating down directly on young cocoa trees can scorch their leaves and dry them out, preventing them from growing properly.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, hulu ni tswaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha amɛgbi. tsiɔ dalɛ ni sa naa

english: Is plantain a suitable shade crop for cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani plantain ji tso ni sa kɛha kookoo dumɔwui?

english: Yes, plantain is very effective because its broad leaves create natural shade umbrellas that shield sensitive young cocoa plants from heat stress.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa ejaakɛ amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni nuɔ he waa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: At what point in the farming calendar should I plant plantain under my cocoa?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli yɛ dumɔ kalanda lɛ mli esa akɛ madu plantain yɛ kookoo tso shishi?

english: The best time to plant plantains on your farm is immediately after you complete your cocoa harvesting operations.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ odu plantains yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ji beni ogbe kookoo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What kind of farm work am I supposed to carry out around September?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ esa akɛ matsu yɛ September mli?

english: September is an ideal month for treating the farm and doing maintenance work after finishing crop harvest activities.
ga: September ji nyɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔ mli tsamɔi kɛ amɛhe saamɔ beni agbe ŋmaakpamɔ nitsumɔi lɛ anaa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Should I plant my plantain trees before or after I finish harvesting my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu plantains dani akpa kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo yɛ be mli ni akpa?

english: You should wait until right after your harvest is completed before planting the plantain suckers on the farm.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi be mli ni kpamɔ lɛ agbe naa dani okɛ dumɔwui awo oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How soon after clearing and harvesting my land do I need to establish shade for new crops?
ga: Beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Mɛɛ be ehe baahia ni mawo ŋmɔshi nibii heei ahe shade?

english: Shade crops like plantain should be planted right after harvest so the ground is shielded before the harsh sun burns any fresh crop growth.
ga: Esa akɛ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ he dani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ashã tsei heei ni eda lɛ.

english: How does good rainfall impact the success of my newly planted plantains and cocoa?
ga: Te nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ lɛ saa kookoo dumɔwui kɛ tsei ni adu ehee lɛ omanyeyeli he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Plentiful rainfall gives young plantains and cocoa seedlings the water they need to establish strong roots and thrive in the farm soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa ni amɛshwere yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to pay attention to how rain fell in the previous year when planning my planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ asusu nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ he beni atoɔ dumɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ?

english: Past rainfall patterns help you understand if soil moisture levels were sufficient to support healthy establishment of new plantain and cocoa crops.
ga: Yinɔsane mli nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni onu shishi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua plantain kɛ cocoa tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ashishitoo.

english: Will my plantains grow well if the weather remains sunny without good rainfall after planting?
ga: Ani mi-plantains lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ tee nɔ ehi shi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, newly planted crops require good, reliable rainfall following harvest time to take root properly and grow enough to provide shade.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni adu ehee lɛ he miihia nugbɔ kpakpa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Koni etswa shishifãi jogbaŋŋ ni eda bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulutsoo aha.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which acts as food for leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rain causes waterlogging around the roots, preventing the plant from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni haa baa lɛ daa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu shwie shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do so many flowers drop off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: It is natural for cocoa trees to produce thousands of flowers and naturally drop most of them because the tree cannot support that much fruit. However, excessive flower drop can be caused by dry weather, nutrient shortages, or insect pests.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tso ko baawo fɔfɔi akpei abɔ ni amɛteŋ babaoo baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shi, akɛni cacao tsei nyɛŋ awo yibii babaoo nakai hewɔ lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi fe nine aba. niyenii ni esaaa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui

english: Which direction should I point the buds when I am burying my cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ matsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ beni miduɔ yucca tsei aniji lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should always be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots will waste energy trying to grow around the stem to reach sunlight, resulting in weak plants and smaller roots.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afo lɛ be fɛɛ be ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛyitso lɛ, Tsobii lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara yɛ amɛhe. tso lɛ mli koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by the Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. It can also happen as a reaction to sudden hot weather or irregular watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus, ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Ebaanyɛ eba hu akɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli baa.

english: Why should I remove some of the small sucker shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Too many sucker shoots compete with the main plant for water, light, and nutrients. Pruning them down to leave only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to concentrate its energy on growing a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, la kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tso agbo ko ni ebaakwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to lift and stake my yam vines with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tsei ni tsei kakadaji yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ ni madu?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, improving sunlight exposure and preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni enine shɛɔ hulu la babaoo nɔ. ni etsi baa helai anaa

english: Why are the bottoms of my pepper fruits turning black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Black, soft bottoms on peppers are caused by a condition called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium. This is usually caused by irregular watering, which stops the roots from taking up calcium consistently.
ga: Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo diŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium daa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize help my soil?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally fertilize the soil, reducing the need for chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why shouldn't I cut off all the lower green leaves of my oil palm tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Green leaves produce the energy and food that the oil palm tree needs to grow heavy fruit bunches. Cutting off healthy green fronds starves the tree and reduces your oil yield.
ga: Baai eŋɔlii haa hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa mu tsei koni amɛwo amɛyibii ni tsii lɛ. Kɛ́ afo baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye tso lɛ, ni ebaaha mu ni ajieɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is it worse to leave weeds in my farm during the first month of planting than later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kwraa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ mli fe sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and easily choked out by weeds competing for light, water, and nutrients in the first few weeks. Once your crops grow tall and leafy, they shade the ground and naturally suppress weeds.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli, beni onibii lɛ daraa ni eyɛ baai lɛ gbeɔ amɛ oya. Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaagbe jwɛi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I use a sharp saw or pruning shear to cut thick branches on my cocoa trees instead of breaking them by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei niji loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ atsu nii? yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ onine baafo mli.

english: Breaking branches by hand leaves rough, open tears on the tree that take long to heal and invite rot-causing fungi. Using a sharp saw makes a clean cut that heals quickly and keeps the tree healthy.
ga: Niji ni akɛ niji shwieɔ shi lɛ haa tso lɛ mli yaafo ni mli wa ni heɔ be babaoo dani etsaa ni efɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ nine. Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha pilamɔ lɛ he atse ni etsa oya, ni ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off excess sucker shoots from the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers compete with the main tree for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the mother plant to produce larger bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haa tso nyɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Is it bad to use a cutlass that was used on a sick plant to prune healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ akɛ dade ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baafo kookoo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, farm tools like cutlasses and saws carry invisible plant germs on their blades. Cutting a healthy tree with an uncleaned tool transfers diseases like cocoa swollen shoot virus or black pod from the infected plant to healthy ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli nibii tamɔ dadei kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ tsei Tsei amli helai ni anaaa lɛ yɛ tsɔnei lɛ anɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛ nibii ni he tseee foɔ lɛ haa helai tamɔ cocoa bud loo black pod virus gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather to save water and prevent itself from drying out. When the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing tubers underground.
