ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni nu akafite ni amɛkagbi. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes or sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso loo tso ni akɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and catch maximum sunlight to manufacture plant food. Climbing vines produce much larger and healthier yam tubers than vines left creeping on the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná tsei niyenii. Wein tsei ni akwɔɔ lɛ baaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛná hewalɛ fe wein tsei ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young maize stalks fall over easily when a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over if their root systems are weak or shallow, usually due to poor soil structure or shallow planting. Heap soil around the base of the stalks (earthing up) to give the roots extra support.
ga: Abɛi baagbee shi kɛji akɛ eshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo amɛmli ekɔɔɔ. Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo dumɔ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Okɛ sũ abɔle tso lɛ shishi (kɛyashi sũ lɛ he) koni eha shishifãi lɛ aye abua amɛ babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shaded conditions. Removing the infected black pods and cutting away excess shade branches lets air in and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Ajieɔ ŋmeii diji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shade lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli ni ekpa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: What makes my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni haa mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root rot. Invisible germs block the tubes inside the stem that carry water up to the leaves, causing the plant to dry out from the inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Helai ni anaaa lɛ tsiɔ tsɔnei ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli ni kɛ nu yaa baai lɛ amli lɛ anaa. Gbimɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛ emli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a 'V' shape from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ su mli kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the tip of lower leaves in a 'V' shape shows the plant is lacking nitrogen food. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the leaves stay green and produce full corn cobs.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ ‘V’ su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Can I grow my crops using only water, or do I always have to put them in the ground?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu pɛ atsu nii kɛdu tsei? Aloo esa akɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ be fɛɛ be?

english: While some seeds can sprout in water, soil is essential for long-term growth because it holds roots firmly in place and supplies nutrients and air that water alone cannot provide for crops like cassava or maize.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui komɛi baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nu mli moŋ, Shi shikpɔŋ he miihia kɛha be kakadaŋŋ mli dalɛ. Ejaakɛ emɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shiŋŋ, ni ehaa niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa. Nu pɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: How do my crops eat their food from the soil if they don't have mouths?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji amɛbɛ daaŋ?

english: Crops drink their food through their roots. Nutrients in the ground dissolve in soil water, and the plant sucks up this liquid mixture to feed its stems, leaves, and growing fruit.
ga: Tsei nuɔ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Ni tsei shwieɔ nu ni akɛfutuɔ nɛɛ koni amɛkɛye amɛshishifãi, amɛbaai, kɛ amɛyibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Can I give my crops too much water, or is more water always better for them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu fe nine? Aloo ani nu babaoo hi kɛha nakai tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: Too much water can drown your crops because plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. If the ground stays constantly soaked, the roots rot and the plant cannot absorb nutrients.
ga: Nu babaoo baanyɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ nu mli ejaakɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛmu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does the water I give my crops end up inside fruits like tomatoes and peppers?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni nu ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ boteɔ aduawai tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli?

english: A plant works like a pump. Its roots pull water from the soil and push it up through the stem into the developing fruit, filling it up so it grows large, juicy, and healthy.
ga: Nitsumɔhe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ pɔmp. Eshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ lɛ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ ahe. Okɛ amɛ awo mli koni amɛdara, amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops need so much more water once they start showing flowers and small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛbɔi fɔmɔ kɛ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Building fruits takes a massive amount of energy and liquid. If the crop lacks water during flowering and fruiting, it will drop its flowers or produce dry, weak harvests.
ga: Yibii afeemɔ biɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu babaoo waa. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo be mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi loo ebaawo tsei ni egbi ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Curling leaves is a crop's way of protecting itself from losing water. By shrinking the leaf area exposed to the hot sun, the plant saves internal moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Baai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ he. Tsei haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ amɛmli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛtsɔ baa he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaa shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow much faster with rainwater than when I water them by hand from a well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa oya kɛ mikɛ nugbɔ nu tsuɔ nii fe beni mikɛ nine shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ nu bu mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater picks up natural nitrogen gas from the air, which acts like a mild, natural fertilizer. Rain also cools the ground and wets the soil evenly, helping roots spread and feed easily.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo Nugbɔ hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛyeɔ nii mlɛo.

english: How deep down into the ground should I put my seeds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: A good general rule is to plant a seed at a depth equal to two or three times its thickness. Planting too deep starves the seedling of air, while planting too shallow lets the sun or birds ruin it.
ga: Mla kpakpa ni afɔɔ namɔ ji ni adu dumɔwui kɛyashɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ amɛmli ŋtayaa lɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ adu nii jogbaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee blɛoo tsɔ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha hulu la loo okpoi afite lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers soak their seeds in water before planting them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ wui woɔ nu mli dani amɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soaking seeds softens their hard outer coats and signals to the seed that it is time to wake up, which helps them sprout much faster and more evenly once put into the dirt.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo nu mli lɛ, ehaa amɛsɛɛ fã ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo. ni etsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛte shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kwraa ni amɛfeɔ ekome kɛ akɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither quickly after I move them into direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ amɛ tee he ko ni hulu la kpɛɔ yɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have short, delicate roots that cannot pull water from deep underground yet. They need temporary shade and regular watering until their roots grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lolo. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛ nu ni afɔɔ amɛ daa kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ ahe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulutsoo be muu lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: How far apart should I plant my maize seeds so they get enough food and light?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he tɛŋŋ koni maná niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Planting maize about 75 cm between rows and 40 cm between plants gives each crop enough room to draw nutrients, sunlight, and soil moisture without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ aaafee 75 cm yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ kɛ 40 cm yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaŋɔ niyenii, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding young cocoa plants and retaining soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tso bibioo ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know if my field is properly prepared before I put in my cassava cuttings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ asaa mihe lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ?

english: Properly prepared land has loose, weed-free soil with good drainage. Tilling or mounding the soil allows cassava roots to penetrate easily and expand into large tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse. jwɛi bɛ mli Nu kpakpa yɛ jɛmɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ boteɔ mli oya ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are some of my bean seeds failing to sprout after I put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep, if the soil is too dry or overly waterlogged, or if the seeds were damaged or stored improperly before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ tsɔ loo dumɔwui lɛ efite loo akɛto he jogbaŋŋ dani adu.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly like tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. The maize plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sun, helping it conserve water during dry heat.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nu baa shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants dropping off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off due to stress from high temperature spikes, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollinators during the flowering stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Why do I need to prune extra branches and leaves from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji kɛ baai krokomɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to allow sunlight and fresh air to pass through, which reduces fungal diseases like black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to turn yellow and curl upward?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are commonly caused by sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit viruses, or by a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why do my pepper fruits develop black, sunken patches on the bottom before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi diji ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant during fruit development, often triggered by inconsistent soil moisture.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: How can I tell when my yams under the ground are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Yams are mature and ready for harvest when the leaves and vines above ground naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up, signaling that energy storage in the tuber is complete.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ yitso lɛ mli lɛ egbe naa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings on my new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make food and stay green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer, such as urea or well-rotted manure, helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted about 1 meter apart from each other. Proper spacing gives the roots enough room underneath the soil to expand into large tubers and stops plants from competing with each other for sunlight and water.
ga: Esa akɛ adu tsei ni afo lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji. ni etsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la kɛ nu he akaŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same spot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains all the specific nutrients maize needs and lets soil pests multiply. Switching to crops like groundnuts or cowpeas after maize puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and starves out soil pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɛi lɛ baaje mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ Tsakemɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei nɔ beni ŋmãa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ. kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ajiemɔ

english: Why do I need to clear tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves out to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground, helping the plant convert sunlight into energy to build large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ hulu la lɛ amɛwoɔ hewalɛ mli koni amɛkɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat or dry soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering and putting dry grass mulch around the base protects the roots and helps flowers stay on to become fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ nɔ. Kɔni lɛ buɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are there small holes and ragged edges on the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii kɛ amɛhe ni etse lɛ?

english: Small holes inside the funnel of young corn plants are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the tender leaves. Spotting them early and applying recommended pest treatments into the leaf whorl stops them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ona amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ naagbai babaoo aba. Ni kɛ akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsu nii yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Is it better for my pepper crops if I water them early in the morning or in the middle of the day?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-pepper tsei lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi loo gbi mli?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the soil absorbs the moisture before the heat of the day. Watering in the hot sun causes water to evaporate too fast and can scald hot leaves with heated droplets.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã ni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ atsɔ mli

english: Should I apply my fertilizer to the soil right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, applying fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm will cause the water to wash the nutrients away into gutters before the roots can take them in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp after a rain.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli dani nugbɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa nubui lɛ amli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil waiting for rain, and they are wild plants adapted to grow very aggressively. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing the water, fertilizer, and light meant for your crops.
ga: Akɛ jwɛi dumɔwui futuɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛmiimɛ nugbɔ. Ni eji koo mli tso ko ni etsake ehe koni eda oya waa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ.

english: Officer, why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape from the tip backward, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to stay dark green and grow tall.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, feemɔ V su kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛya sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdara.

english: Why are the bottom branches of my oil palm trees turning yellow and drooping down before time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Oil palms need a lot of potassium and magnesium to feed their leaves. When these nutrients are low in the soil, the tree starves its older bottom branches to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Mu tsei ahe miihia potassium kɛ magnesium babaoo koni amɛbaai lɛ akwɛ̃. Beni nɛkɛ niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ shishigbɛ niji ni egbɔ lɛ koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them directly in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and easily scorched by strong sunlight. Cocoa seedlings need shade from taller trees or plantains during their first two years to keep their leaves cool and retain soil moisture.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji loo dumɔwui adɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni amɛha baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Yam leaves produce food for the tuber using sunlight. Staking lifts the vines high off the ground so every leaf catches maximum sunlight, helping the plant make enough food to swell the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tuber lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa aná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ afuu.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, drink water and steal nutrients meant for the main plantain tree. Removing most of them leaves only one or two strong suckers and allows the main tree to produce a heavy, healthy bunch.
ga: Tsobii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ baanu nu lɛ ni amɛju niyenii ni haa plantain titri lɛ yeɔ niyenii. Kɛ́ ojie emli babaoo lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni efeɔ tso ni tsii ni wa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off off the plant without turning into tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tomato pollen becomes dry and sterile when temperatures get too hot. Without successful pollination, the plant drops the blossoms to save its energy rather than attempting to grow fruit.
ga: Tomato pollen lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni egbi ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when heavy rain leaves water standing on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu hiɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain water saturates the field for days without draining, oxygen is cut off, causing the underground tubers to drown and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, jɛmɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbii babaoo ni nu ko bɛ ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Afoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How can swamp rice survive growing in standing water when my maize rots in the exact same condition?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa ahi shi yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli? Beni ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shihilɛ kome mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have hollow air tubes inside their stems and roots that act like tiny snorkels, pumping air from above water down to their submerged roots—something maize plants cannot do.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi ni mli ewo muji yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ mumɔ tsɔnei bibii. Ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ nu lɛ yiteŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishifãi ni ebote nu lɛ shishi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ko ni ŋmãa tsei nyɛŋ afee.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. As they suck the juice underneath the leaves, they inject viruses or cause physical damage that makes the leaf roll inward.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ Ebaawo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amli loo ekɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ naagbai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli lɛ baa.

english: Why does my cowpea crop flower much faster when I plant in August compared to when I plant in April?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi mra kwraa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ August mli lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be ni adu yɛ April mli lɛ he?

english: Cowpeas react to daylight patterns. As the days shorten slightly toward the late rainy season, the plant receives a biological signal that triggers it to stop making leaves and start flowering quickly.
ga: Cowpea hereɔ hulutsoo be mli la ni tsoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ gbii lɛ bafee kuku fioo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ Tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ahe okadii ni haa ekpaa baai lɛ feemɔ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi feemɔ oya.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers beside my young cocoa seedlings on my new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Plantain suckers grow fast and provide broad leaf umbrellas that shield the young cocoa plants from heat, keeping the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa baa ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tsei koni makwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and improves airflow, which prevents leaves from rotting on the damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la lɛ he ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants move available nitrogen from older lower leaves up to young growing top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei jieɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants without forming any fruits during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely high, tomato pollen becomes dry and inactive, preventing proper fertilization. The plant senses it cannot make seeds and drops the flowers to conserve its strength and water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ baagbi ni ebaafee nɔ ni tsuuu nii. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ nii ni sa naa Tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ enyɛɛɛ ewo dumɔwui ni ejie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Upward leaf curling in pepper is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, or viruses spread by them. The insects suck the juices out of young leaves, causing them to distort as they expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Kooloi lɛ nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli. kɛ sɛɛkuu baa beni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with green leaves but produce only thin roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is planted in heavily shaded areas, it puts all its energy into growing stems and foliage instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei ná nitrogen babaoo loo adu yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ, Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi kɛ ebaa lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my maize cobs stay very small when I plant three or four seeds together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii nɛkɛ beni mikɛ ŋmeii etɛ loo ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When multiple seeds grow in the same hole, their roots fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This crowd competition weakens all the stalks and leads to smaller cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ kɛhaa nu. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la. Asafo babaoo akaŋshii haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant pepper or tomato on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ loo tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Crops in the same plant family attract the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them in the same spot year after year lets those pests build up in large numbers in the soil, damaging future harvests.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ tsei aweku kome mli lɛ gbalaa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha nakai ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni kɛ wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ

english: Why does planting cowpea or groundnut make my soil better for the maize I plant in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpea and groundnut have natural root bacteria that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, that stored nitrogen fertilizes the soil naturally for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi amli helai ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nitrogen ni ato lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid putting solid fertilizer around my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ni mikɛbaabɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve into a form roots can drink. On dry soil, concentrated chemical fertilizer draws water out of the roots instead, burning and damaging the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ nɔ ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ. Ekɛ la baa ni efiteɔ tsei.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are sick with a serious disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela ni naa wa miimɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Look out for unusual symptoms like swollen stems or branches, red veins or yellowing patterns on young leaves, and small or misshapen pods. If you see these signs, your trees may have a severe viral infection that needs urgent attention.
ga: Taomɔ okadii ni yɔɔ srɔto tamɔ tsei loo tsei niji ni efuu. Gbɛjianɔtoi tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli Kɛji ona okadii nɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ otso lɛ yɛ hela ko ni naa wa ni jɛɔ mli baa ni biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ oya.

english: How can an officer from the Agriculture department help me manage my cocoa farm?
ga: Te onukpai ni jɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni makwɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Agricultural extension officers inspect your crops for hidden pests and diseases, advise you on the right treatment methods, and guide you on proper farming practices to restore and improve your yield.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ baakwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ mli. Ha ŋaawoo yɛ gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsaa mɔ lɛ he. ni otsɔɔ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni sa ni baaha onibii ni onáa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha eya hiɛ.

english: Why would an agricultural officer tell me to cut down my cocoa trees instead of just spraying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ tsofa baashwie nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Certain viral infections, like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease, live deep inside the tree's tissue where chemical sprays cannot reach. Cutting down the infected tree is the only way to stop the disease from spreading to healthy trees.
ga: Virus helai komɛi, tamɔ cocoa bud swelling disease Amɛhiɔ tso mli fãji amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What happens to my crops if I leave my farm neglected and unattended for a long time?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mishi miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ ni kwɛɛɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Neglected farms quickly get overgrown with weeds and become safe havens for pests and fungal or viral diseases. Over time, these unmanaged diseases can destroy all your crops and lower your soil quality.
ga: Oya nɔŋŋ ni jwɛi shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ amli, ni amɛfeɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ helai ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ baanyɛ afite onibii fɛɛ ni efite oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can a disease on a neighbor's overgrown farm spread to my healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Ani hela ko ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mi-cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, insects like mealybugs as well as wind and shared tools can easily carry diseases from an unattended nearby farm onto your healthy crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛhaa lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni atsaaa amɛ lɛ amli kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli oya.

english: Do I need special machines to cut down old diseased cocoa trees, or is a cutlass enough?
ga: Ani tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi komɛi he miihia mi koni mikɛfolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ? Aloo dade ko kɛkɛ fa?

english: While a cutlass works for small bushes, using specialized equipment like motorized chainsaws makes it much faster, cleaner, and safer to cut down large, woody cocoa trunks right at the base.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ akɛ daggers atsu nii yɛ jwɛi bibii anɔ moŋ, Shi kɛ akɛ nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ power saw tsu nii lɛ, efeɔ oya kwraa, ehe tseɔ, ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaafo tsei wuji ni akɛ tsei fee cacao yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to apply chemicals after cutting down infected cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofai atsu nii beni afo kokoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Applying recommended chemicals after cutting helps kill any remaining disease-carrying insects (like mealybugs) hiding in the debris and prevents fungal growth on cut stumps.
ga: Tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii beni afo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni egbe kooloi bibii ni hiɛ helai ni eshwɛ (tamɔ mealybugs) ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ fɛɛ. ni etsĩ ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ tsei ni afo lɛ anɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings immediately on land where sick trees were just cut down?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni afo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait and properly treat the land first. Clearing out all root debris and spraying remaining pests ensures that the soil is safe before you introduce fresh, healthy seedlings.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni omɛ ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ehe hia ni ojie shishifãi fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ ni okɛ tsofai fɔji ni eshwɛ lɛ afɔ nɔ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe dani odu dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my newly planted cocoa trees are growing healthy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kokoo tso ni midu ehee lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy young cocoa trees produce frequent fresh leaf flushes, have smooth green stems without swellings, and display vibrant green leaves free of yellow patches or burnt edges.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baawo baai tsuji ni kpɛɔ. Eyɛ tso eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni fuumɔ ko bɛ he. ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ko bɛ he.

english: What simple steps can I take to prevent disease outbreaks on my cocoa farm?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni mafee koni helai akaje kpo yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Regularly inspect your trees, keep weeds low, prune excess branches for good airflow, clean your farm tools, and report any strange leaf or stem changes to an agricultural extension officer immediately.
ga: Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ amli daa, tsi jwɛi lɛ anɔ, ni ofolɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Tsumɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe ni obɔ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ baai loo tsei lɛ amli lɛ he amaniɛ. Ha okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ ale amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer, or using well-decomposed manure, helps the leaves turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛdara waa.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing leaves of maize plants. Catching them early and spraying recommended insecticides or natural neem seed extract helps protect your harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem dumɔwui ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits in the soil for too long without proper drainage. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to flow away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu babaoo hoɔ. Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need plenty of sunlight to make food and grow big tubers underground. Using tall stakes holds the leaves up toward the sun and keeps them off the wet ground where leaf diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo koni amɛhoo ni amɛdu bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ, ni ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu, he ni baa helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from severe heat, dry spells, or insect attacks like mirids. Keeping shade trees on your farm and protecting cocoa from sap-sucking insects helps flowers develop into full pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, hulutsoo be, loo kooloi bibii, tamɔ hulu la miitutua amɛ. Kɛ́ oha tsei lɛ fee hulutsoo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni obu cacao lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when heavy winds blow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that can struggle to support the heavy weight of the plant and fruit bunch. Supporting the stem with a strong bamboo pole or wooden fork (propping) keeps the plant upright against strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye amɛbua tso lɛ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tso ni wa loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei (fiɔ sɛɛ) fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and making the plants stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni eha tso lɛ miifee bibioo lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies that transmit leaf diseases. Spraying the underside of the leaves with soapy water or appropriate pest sprays keeps these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ni hiɛɔ baai helai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and soft before the fruit gets red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani aduawai lɛ feɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit combined with irregular soil moisture. Keeping the soil consistently moist through regular watering and adding wood ash or lime to the soil helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai amli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa lɛ. Kɛ́ oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ tso sũ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: How does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mulching bare soil around Te mikɛ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, traps water in the soil so it doesn't dry out fast under the hot sun. It also stops weeds from taking over and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni jwɛi akaye nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my farm so it doesn't waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekafite?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil right after a light rain so the crop roots can drink it up immediately. Applying fertilizer to very dry ground can burn roots, while applying it during heavy downpours can wash the food away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha niyenii lɛ afite.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which gets washed deep into the soil by heavy rains, or that the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe and absorb nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass around your plants is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool under the strong sun, holds moisture in the ground longer, and stops weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ ni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cowpeas or beans together with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa afata ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas out of the air and put it into the soil through their roots. This natural nitrogen feeds the maize crop without you needing to buy extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ haa oŋmei lɛ niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that shade the young cocoa like an umbrella, keeping them cool and moist during their first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha kookoo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it necessary to build high mounds of earth before planting yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow long and thick underground, so they need loose, soft soil to expand easily. Making mounds loosens the earth and allows heavy rainwater to drain away so the tubers do not rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɔ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Gɔji ni amaɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, a major pest that feeds on the soft inner leaves of young corn. Checking your farm early and applying recommended pesticides or neem extract early in the morning destroys them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ baafite ŋmɔji nɛɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off without forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers if they lack water, if the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium, or if tiny sap-sucking insects like mirids attack the flower buds.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji nu bɛ amɛmli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ potassium, loo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ mirids lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves dry up and drop off, and cracks appear in the soil near the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ gĩ ni amɛgbee shi Ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one generation only. If you plant the seeds saved from that harvest, the new crop will grow unevenly, yield much less grain, and suffer more from diseases.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ kɛhaa yinɔ kome pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nibii heei baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Yibiiwoo fioo kwraa ni helai yeɔ amanehulu babaoo

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot fast if they are picked when completely soft, left in direct sunlight after picking, or packed tightly in plastic bags where heat and moisture build up.
ga: Tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ beni eyɛ blɛoo kwraa lɛ. Shi ni hulu lɛ ashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ beni okɛto sɛɛ. Aloo akɛwo plastic kotokui amli jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ buaa ehe naa yɛ lɛ.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to plant new trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu tsei heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant trees is at the start of the rainy season, usually from April or May up until September. Planting during this window ensures the trees get enough water to settle into the soil and grow well.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu tsei ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ April loo May kɛyashiɔ September. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ samflɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it still safe for me to plant tree seedlings as late as August or September?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe lolo akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ August loo September naagbee gbɛ?

english: Yes, you can still plant up until September while the rains are still active. However, planting earlier around April or May gives the young trees even more time to establish strong roots before the dry season comes.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu nii lolo kɛyashi September be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ miinɛ lolo lɛ. Shi, kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra, yɛ April loo May aaafee lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná be babaoo ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: How long is the main window of time I have to safely plant my crops and trees?
ga: Be enyiɛ ehe baahia ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsei shweshweeshwe?

english: In Ghana, the main planting window lasts for several months, starting when the rainy season begins in April or May and continuing through September.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, samflɛ titri ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ hiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo. Nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ April loo May mli, ni eyaa nɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ September.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my trees when the rainy season starts instead of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli moŋ fe nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ?

english: Planting at the beginning of the rainy season gives young trees continuous moisture so they can build deep roots, whereas planting during the dry season leaves them without water, causing them to dry up and die.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaha nu akafee nɔ ni bɛ, ni ebaaha tsei lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: What will happen to my new tree seedlings if I plant them without waiting for the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi dumɔwui heei lɛ anɔ? Kɛji midu nii ni mimɛɛɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ?

english: If you plant seedlings before the rains begin, the dry soil and heat will cause water stress, leading to poor growth or the death of most of your seedlings.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui dani nugbɔ lɛ je shishi Shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui babaoo edaaa jogbaŋŋ loo amɛgboiɔ.

english: How do the early rains help my young tree seedlings survive and grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa?

english: Early rains soften the soil and supply constant moisture, allowing young root systems to spread easily and absorb the nutrients required for healthy development.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni eŋɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ edara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my food crops grow much better when planted right at the onset of the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ adu be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: The start of the rainy season provides consistent water without harsh sun, giving seeds and young plants the ideal moisture they need to germinate, take root, and grow strong.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee baaha nu aba daa ni hulu la ni naa wa bɛ mli. Ehaa dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa nu ni sa jogbaŋŋ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃, amɛshishifãi ni amɛdara waa.

english: Can I plant trees on the same land where I am planting my regular food crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mifɔɔ niyenii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant trees alongside your food crops when the rainy season starts. Combining crops and trees helps maximize your land and improves overall farm production.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu tsei yɛ oniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Nibii ni aduɔ kɛ tsei ni akɛaafee ekome lɛ baaye abua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni eha ŋmɔ mli nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is combining tree planting with my crop farming a good solution for my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei adumɔ kɛ tsei adumɔ ni akɛaafata he lɛ ji tsabaa kpakpa kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Integrating trees into your crop field creates a sustainable farming system that protects the soil, provides shade, and improves your farm's productivity over time.
ga: Tsei ni okɛwoɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoo ni yaa nɔ daa ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ehaa hulutsoo, ni ehaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baa.

english: What should I prepare on my farm before the April and May rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ masaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ anɛ yɛ April kɛ May mli?

english: Before the rains start, you should clear your land, prepare your farm layout, and secure your tree seedlings and seeds so you are ready to plant immediately when the rains begin.
ga: Dani nugbɔ baanɛ Esa akɛ ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Saamɔ ŋmɔ he mfoniri ni osaa dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui Bɔni afee ni ofee klalo akɛ obaadu kɛji nugbɔ lɛ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad shade umbrellas and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees mature over their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction is up when I am planting cassava stem cuttings in my field?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni obaadu o-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ?

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes on the stem where old leaves grew; these buds should point upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes poor sprouting and weak root yields.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nodes lɛ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni baai momo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yitso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ni shishifãi lɛ hu baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do we heap soil into large mounds before planting yams instead of planting them in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔbuaa muji babaoo naa dani wɔduɔ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ fe ni wɔbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose soil to expand into big tubers easily. Mounding also improves water drainage, preventing the seed yam from rotting underground during heavy rainfall.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni etsɔ bulbs agboi oya. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ hu haa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry before the corns are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient. Adding compost, aged manure, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base helps restore green leaves and boost cob size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii momo, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ he fɛɛ he. Tso lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eha cob lɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field make the soil better for my maize later?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This leaves natural fertilizer in the soil for the crops planted in the next season.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I put fresh chicken manure directly around my young crop stems?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee awo he fɛɛ he. Ani mi gbekɛ fioo lɛ baanyɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is too strong and generates heat as it decomposes, which can burn plant roots. It is best to mix it with soil and dry plant matter to compost for a few weeks before applying it.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa beni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ tsei ni egbi baafutu mli koni ekɛwo ŋmɔtɔ mli otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛtsu nii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the sap, or a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early helps protect new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai heei ni daraa lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, uneven watering, or a lack of insect pollination can stress the plant and cause flowers to drop. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be Aloo, kooloi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná haomɔ ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crops grow slowly and look weak when weeds grow close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil food. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the sunlight and nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the rainy season is steady enough for me to put my maize seeds in the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Wait until the rain has soaked the soil deeply at least two or three times in a short period. Planting after just one light shower can cause seeds to sprout and then wither if a dry week follows.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa kɛ hoo lɛ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji otsi kroko ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed newer top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Fertilizer works best in two splits: apply NPK fertilizer about 1 to 2 weeks after planting to support root development, and top-dress with Urea or Ammonium Sulfate 4 to 6 weeks after planting when the crop is growing rapidly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ: Okɛ NPK nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ awo mli aaafee otsi 1 kɛyashi 2 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. ni akɛ urea loo ammonium sulfate afɔ nɔ yɛ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 sɛɛ beni adu tsei lɛ beni tsei lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and drying up on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during damp, rainy periods in overly shaded farms. Pruning farm trees to let in sunlight and clearing infected pods helps control its spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afo ŋmɔ mli tsei amli koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ bɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites, which can also spread leaf curl viruses. Spraying neem oil extract or appropriate insecticides helps manage these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips loo mites, ni baanyɛ agbɛ baa lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ashwã lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do small dark spots appear on my groundnut leaves before harvest?
ga: No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmei baa nɔ dani akpaa lɛ.

english: Dark spots on groundnut leaves indicate leaf spot disease, caused by fungi that multiply in humid weather. It causes leaves to fall early, which reduces nut size. Rotating crops with maize or cassava helps break the disease cycle.
ga: Nibii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmei baa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ baa mli hela ni ŋmei ko ni fɔɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya, ni no haa nut lɛ dalɛ baa shi. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal rots to attack. Planting on raised mounds or ridges in well-drained soil prevents waterlogging.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu akabote mli.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing thin and twisted instead of thick and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji mlɛo ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become thin and bent when the soil is too hard, stony, or insufficiently loosened. Creating tall, soft soil mounds or ridges gives tubers the space they need to expand smoothly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ, tɛi yɛ nɔ, loo ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa tuber lɛ naa he ni he hiaa lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of pollination. Keeping soil consistently moist and mulching around plants helps keep root zone temperatures cool.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall when tiny root-eating pests called nematodes or banana weevils damage their anchor roots. Planting clean, treated suckers and supporting heavy fruiting trees with wooden props prevents them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ amɛ ŋwɛi shishifãi lɛ. Aduɔ tsei ni he tse ni atsa amɛ. ni amɛkɛ tso nibii fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why are my rice seeds germinating at different times instead of sprouting all together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ekome lɛ?

english: Uneven germination occurs when seeds are sown at different soil depths or when soil moisture is inconsistent. Planting seeds at a uniform depth of 2 to 3 centimeters in a well-prepared seedbed ensures even sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ srɔtoi anɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ fe sɛntimitai 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ dumɔwui atsu ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ po akwɛ̃.

english: Why should I buy improved seed varieties from agricultural researchers instead of just planting seeds saved from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔ ko dɛŋ? Mohu ɔ, i du dumɔwuhi nɛ a he yi kɛ je ye nyagbe ngma kpami ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred for high yield, fast growth, and resistance to local diseases. Seeds saved from a previous hybrid harvest lose these special qualities in the next generation, resulting in weaker plants and smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛná yibii babaoo, amɛdara oya, ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsutsu hybrid ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baafite nɛkɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Will high-yielding corn seeds from researchers still produce a good crop if I cannot afford chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni jɛ niiamlitaolɔi lɛ adɛŋ lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai lolo kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds have the potential for higher yields, but they need good nutrition to reach that potential. Without fertilizer or rich soil managed with manure or compost, these plants will not produce their maximum possible harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ yɛ nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaawo yibii babaoo. Shi niyenii kpakpa he miihia amɛ koni amɛshɛ nakai nyɛmɔ lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii etsu he nii lɛ bɛ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ nyɛŋ akpa amɛ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know the correct spacing and number of corn seeds to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa kɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ayibɔ ni esa akɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting one or two seeds per hole at recommended distances (usually 75 cm between rows and 40 cm between holes) prevents plants from competing with each other.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ ni aduɔ yɛ bu fɛɛ bu mli yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛto lɛ. (bei pii lɛ, 75 cm yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ kɛ 40 cm yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ) baaye abua ni tsei akatswa amɛhe akaŋ.

english: What happens to my maize harvest if I plant too many seeds close together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Planting too closely forces the plants to fight for limited light, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak stalks that fall over easily and produce tiny or empty corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ena la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya. ni afɔ ŋmãa bibioo ko loo ŋmãa ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is short on nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for green leaf growth. The plant moves nitrogen from older leaves to feed newer leaves, turning the bottom ones yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli kɛyaa baai heei amli. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up tightly like straws during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a natural defense mechanism corn uses to survive heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, helping it conserve water during dry periods.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni enyɛ ehi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Tsei haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ

english: Why does the tassel flower grow at the top of my corn plant before the cobs appear on the side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miikwɛ̃ yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ dani ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ amɛsɛɛgbɛ lɛ?

english: The tassel at the top makes pollen, which wind carries down to the silks growing out of the cobs below. Every silk that receives pollen creates one full kernel of corn on the cob.
ga: Tassels ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ jieɔ pollen. ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ woɔ shi kɛyaa siliki ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli Siliki kpã fɛɛ kpã ni nine shɛɔ pollen nɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa toi muu kome.

english: How does heavy rainfall during the flowering stage affect my corn yield?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ saa mi ŋmãa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain during flowering can wash pollen off the tassels before it reaches the cob silks. If the silks do not receive pollen, the cobs will form with missing kernels or empty patches.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe fɔfɔi lɛ ahe dani eshɛ cob silk lɛ he. Kɛji siliki lɛ enine shɛɛɛ pollen nɔ lɛ Cob lɛ baaná dumɔwui ni elaaje loo hei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why are there small ragged holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni muji ko yɛ ni tamɔ ŋmei?

english: Ragged holes and powdery waste inside the leaf funnel indicate Fall Armyworm caterpillars are eating your young corn. Catching this early is important so you can protect the growing tip before the plant is destroyed.
ga: Buu ni ekumɔ kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ miiye obi lɛ ŋmãa. Ni ooomɔ lɛ mra Enɛ he hiaa koni onyɛ obu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe dani tso lɛ afite.

english: Can I plant beans or cowpeas between my rows of maize without reducing my maize harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ ni mikɛ ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi?

english: Yes, planting legumes like beans alongside maize is beneficial. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which helps feed the maize while giving you two different harvests from the same field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ayeɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, anáa ŋmãa sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do some of my papaya trees produce flowers but never grow any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Papaya trees naturally have male and female plants. Male trees only produce pollen and flowers to fertilize female trees, while female and hermaphrodite trees are the ones that can actually bear fruit.
ga: Papaya tsei yɛ tsei ni ji hii kɛ yei yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ pollen kɛ fɔfɔi kɛhaa tsei ni ji yei pɛ. Yɛ be mli ni yei kɛ hermaphroditic tsei ji tsei ni baanyɛ awo yibii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why are my cucumber plants producing plenty of flowers but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kukumbai lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwoɔ aduawai fioo lɛ?

english: Cucumber plants grow both male and female flowers on the same vine. If bees or other insects are not visiting your farm to carry pollen from the male flowers to the female flowers, the fruits will not grow.
ga: Kukumba tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei fɛɛ yɛ wain tso kome nɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii loo kooloi krokomɛi Amɛyaaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyawo fɔfɔi hii amli pollen kɛya fɔfɔi yei amli. Yibii lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ.

english: Why do the flowers at the top of my maize plant look completely different from the ones on the sides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ srɔto kwraa yɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ afã lɛ he lɛ?

english: Maize plants have male and female parts on different spots. The tassel at the top is male and sheds pollen into the wind, while the silks on the side cob are female parts that catch the pollen to form corn grains.
ga: Abɛi tsei yɛ nuu kɛ yoo fãi yɛ hei srɔtoi. Tassels ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ji hii ni amɛshwieɔ pollen yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. yɛ be mli ni siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ ji yoo fã ni mɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebafeɔ ŋmei ŋmeii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and scorching?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally cannot tolerate strong direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains grown alongside them to shield them until their roots and leaves are fully mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ he kome kɛha hebuu kɛyashi shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ baadara.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava naturally shows maturity when its bottom leaves start yellowing and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to swell and crack open.
ga: Yucca lɛ daa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Is it normal for my plantain suckers to look like they are dying right after I plant them?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mi plantain tsei lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiigboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, newly transplanted plantain suckers usually shed their old outer leaves to save water while building strong roots underground before they push out new green shoots.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, plantain suckers ni adu ehee lɛ shwieɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai momo lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni amɛmaa shishifãi ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛshwieɔ ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before producing any tomatoes?
