ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛwo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers naturally fall off without fruiting when exposed to extreme dry heat, sudden water shortage, or heavy downpours that wash away their pollen.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli egbi mli. Nu ni faaa trukaa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their leaves suddenly when the weather gets too dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai trukaa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their leaves as a natural defense mechanism during hot, dry spells to reduce water loss and protect the main stem from drying out.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛ baai lɛ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ yɛ dɔlɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Bɔni afee ni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni aha tso wulu lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb, while cassava grows straight on its own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baakwɛ̃ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Yams are naturally climbing vines that need support stakes to spread their leaves towards sunlight, which provides the energy needed to produce large underground tubers.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do weed control chemicals kill the grass on my farm without harming my maize crop?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ agbe jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni eyeee ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: Selective weed chemicals are designed to recognize differences in leaf shape and plant nature, targeting broadleaf weeds or unwanted wild grasses while leaving maize unharmed.
ga: Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahala lɛ koni akɛtsɔɔ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha lɛ mli. Ekɛ ehiɛ fɔɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo loo koo mli jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shi ŋmãa lɛ ni nɔ ko akafee lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I clear and heap the soil into mounds before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛwo mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Mounding the soil loosens it so root crops like cassava and yam can grow bigger easily, while also keeping excess rainwater from standing around and drowning the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oootswa lɛ baaha egbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei baanyɛ adara oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in neat straight lines instead of scattering them like I usually do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni ja nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui tamɔ bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ

english: Planting in lines gives each crop enough space to get sunlight, nutrients, and water without fighting its neighbors, and it makes weeding much easier for you.
ga: Tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa enáa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulu la, niyenii, kɛ nu baatsu nii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. Ni ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: If I plant my cassava seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small plot?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too close forces crops to fight each other for food and light, resulting in thin plants with small tubers instead of big, healthy yields.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ bulb bibii baa. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ ngmɔ agbo nɛ ngɛ he wami.

english: What can I do to save my maize when rain doesn't fall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni abaanyɛ afee koni akɛbu ŋmãa he kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves traps moisture in the ground longer, keeping the soil cool and hydrated even during dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie Oŋmɔshinii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli po.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant maize on the exact same farm plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil year after year, so switching to legumes like beans or groundnuts helps put good food back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni oyeɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Ku osɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why does fertilizer burn and kill my crops when I put it right at the base of the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shãa ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshinii lɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is strong like salt, and direct contact burns the skin of the plant. It should be buried a few fingers away from the stem so the roots can drink it safely.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe wa tamɔ ŋmei. ni kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ hewolo. Esa akɛ afu lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi pɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is starving for soil food like nitrogen, or that the roots are getting either too much water or not enough.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛnaaa nu bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do insects seem to attack my crops more when the sun is hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: During hot and dry weather, crops get weak from thirst, making it easier for pests to attack them to drink the sweet liquid inside their leaves and stems.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Dumɔwui baagbɔjɔ kɛjɛ kumai hewɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ baatutua amɛ koni amɛnu nu ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to clear weeds when my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops need all the food and water in the soil to grow strong roots, and fast-growing weeds will steal those vital resources and choke your young crops.
ga: Niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia dumɔwui bibii koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baaju nakai nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ni ebaafite oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young tomato plants wilt and look dead right after I move them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving plants shocks their roots when they are disturbed, but transplanting late in the evening and watering them right away helps them recover overnight.
ga: Tsei ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ baaha amɛshishifãi lɛ akpokpo kɛji akɛ ahao amɛ. Shi kɛ́ adu tso lɛ gbɛkɛ ni awo lɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ nyɔɔŋ kome mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and harsh Harmattan winds. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their tender leaves from sunscorch and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Koni abu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and dirt that looks like sawdust inside the top of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing center (whorl) of the maize plant and eats the leaves. Applying an approved insecticide or neem seed extract directly into the center of the plant early in the morning or late evening will control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei (rings) lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem dumɔwui ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ.

english: Which direction should the buds point when I cut cassava stems and plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔsemɔ lɛ atsɔɔ beni afoɔ ŋmei tso ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You should always plant cassava stem cuttings with the green buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the plant to waste energy turning its shoots around, resulting in weak growth and smaller tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ adu ni ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Tso lɛ ni edaa kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa efiteɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ eshishifãi ni etsakeɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyitsei lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop off when the crop is stressed by extreme afternoon heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and placing mulch around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and helps flowers stay on to turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be fɛɛ be ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ abɔle tso lɛ shishi koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I tell by looking at my crop leaves that the soil needs more fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛtsɔ tsei ahe baai ni mikwɛɔ lɛ nɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: When older leaves at the bottom of your crops turn light green or yellow while the upper leaves stay green, the plant is short on nitrogen. Adding well-decomposed animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help the plant regain its dark green color.
ga: Be ni baai lɛ daa lɛ, tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ eŋɔli. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni efite jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ jie

english: The small shoots (suckers) steal food, water, and sunlight from the main stem. Removing most of them and leaving only one strong sucker ensures the main plant gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii (tso lɛ) juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo ni ashi sucker ni mli wa kome pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ plantains wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp wet ground, protecting them from rot and diseases while helping the yam tubers grow much bigger.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafite kɛ helai srɔtoi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and pale even when it rains a lot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that drink up the water and food in the soil faster than your crops can. Removing weeds early stops them from starving your crops of essential light, water, and nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ ni nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my vegetable plants curling up tight and growing smaller than normal?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibioo fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Tight leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids that suck the plant's juices and spread viruses. Controlling these insects early with insecticidal soap or neem oil stops the leaf curl from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛji akɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the soil stays cool and the plant roots can drink deeply. Watering during the hot afternoon causes most of the water to dry up in the sun before the roots can use it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛya shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko agbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do some rice varieties grow better in my region than the ones brought in from Accra?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa ni akɛjɛɔ Accra kɛbaa lɛ?

english: Different rice varieties are bred for specific soil types, rain patterns, and temperatures. A variety that thrives in the humid south near Accra may struggle in drier northern regions because its roots and leaf structure are not adapted to local weather conditions.
ga: Omɔ henɔi srɔtoi Akwɛɔ amɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be. Tsofai srɔtoi ni shwereɔ yɛ anaigbɛ kpokpaa ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ Accra lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ kooyigbɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ esaaa he ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if seed supplies arrive late and I plant my rice weeks after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bashɛ sɛɛ ni midu ŋmãa otsii komɛi sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Late planting means your rice crop will miss the peak rainfall period when it needs water most, especially during flowering. This water shortage can cause poor grain formation and result in much lower harvests.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-rice tsei lɛ baafee mɛi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa, be mli ni nu he hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Nu ni faaa nɛɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmaa akafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ aba shi babaoo.

english: If seed rice is kept in a warehouse for a long time before I buy it, will it still sprout properly in my field?
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa ŋmaa to nitoohe be kakadaŋŋ dani ahe Ani ŋmãa baakwɛ̃ lolo yɛ wɔŋmɔji amli?

english: Seeds stored in hot or humid conditions lose their energy over time. If the seeds are kept too long without proper cool and dry storage, fewer of them will germinate, and the young plants that do sprout will grow weakly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛto shihilɛi ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui to be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni akɛtooo jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi lɛ, Dumɔwui fioo pɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ŋmeii ni baa lɛ baakwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young rice plants start turning yellow when the soil dries out for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni mikɛgbi shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rice plants need standing water or moist soil to dissolve and carry nitrogen from the soil into their roots. When the soil dries out, the plant cannot absorb nitrogen, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow from lack of nutrients.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛtsɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nitrogen. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are some of my rice plants sprouting many side-stems while others stay thin with only one stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ekomɛi shwereɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ ŋmeii bibii kome pɛ lɛ?

english: Sprouting side-stems, called tillering, depends on the seed variety, proper plant spacing, and soil fertility. Healthy soil with enough fertilizer gives the plant energy to branch out and produce more stems, which leads to more grain heads.
ga: Atsɛɔ sɛɛgbɛ shweremɔ akɛ tillering ni damɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ anɔ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha otso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛ niji afee niji babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Can rough handling of seed bags during long-distance transport affect how my rice grows after planting?
ga: Ani dumɔwui kotokui ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ baaná ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, rough transport can cause tiny invisible cracks in the outer shell of the seed. These cracks allow dampness and fungi to enter early, causing the seed to rot in the soil instead of growing into a strong plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛfaa ni mli wa. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmeii bibii aba. Anaaa yɛ dumɔwu lɛ kponɔgbɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ mli oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is my rice starting to flower early when the plants are still very short and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice lɛ miibɔi fɔmɔ oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ yɛ kukuji ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: When rice plants experience severe stress—such as prolonged dry spells or extreme heat—they try to reproduce quickly before dying. This survival response makes them produce flowers early, leading to short plants and very few grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpe, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo latsaa ni naa wa waa lɛ, Amɛbaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfɔ oya dani amɛgboi. Nɛkɛ yiwalaheremɔ hetoo nɛɛ haa amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi oya. Enɛ haa tsei kukuji kɛ dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster in my field than the rice seedlings I just planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni midu amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to local conditions and can absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than newly planted crop seeds. If not cleared early, weeds steal light and food from your rice seedlings, stunting their growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ebaanyɛ ejie nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ Kɛji ajieee kwraa kɛjɛɛɛ mli mra Jwɛi lɛ juɔ la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha dalɛ lɛ akpa.

english: Why are many of the rice grains on the head empty shells with no white rice inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo yɛ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ amɛyitsei anɔ shi ŋmãa yɛŋ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty rice heads usually happen when the plant lacks water or suffers from high temperatures right at the moment of pollination. Without enough moisture, the plant cannot fill the grain shells with starch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa yitsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli loo hulutsoo ni naa wa miikpe yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ amɛkɛ starch afata dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Why are some parts of my rice field ready for harvest while other parts are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ fãi komɛi efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ ŋmɔji lolo lɛ?

english: Uneven ripening happens when different seeds get mixed together in the supply bag, or when soil moisture is uneven across your field. Seeds of different varieties mature at different speeds, making harvest timing difficult.
ga: Nibii ni shwereɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji dumɔwui lɛ Futu amɛhe yɛ niyenii kotoku mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ejaaa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Dumɔwui srɔtoi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Enɛ haa nikpamɔ be lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa.

english: Why should I use a knapsack sprayer instead of just splashing liquid chemicals on my crops with a cup?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ kɔɔpoo najiaŋ?

english: A spraying machine breaks liquid into fine droplets that cover every part of the plant evenly, ensuring the chemical works effectively without wasting money or damaging the crops.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ gbálaa nu lɛ mli bibii bibii. No haa tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ehaa tsofai lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni shika fiteee loo efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How does using a proper spraying machine help improve my crop yield?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsɔne ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ atsu nii aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: A spraying machine delivers an accurate and uniform layer of protection across your plants, preventing insects and diseases from destroying your harvest.
ga: Sprayer lɛ haa otsei lɛ ahebuu pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ fã ko po. Etsiɔ kooloi bibii kɛ helai anaa koni amɛkafite onibii.

english: Why should I spray the upper leaves of my crops instead of just spraying near the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni mabɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Pests often gather on tender top leaves, and spraying the top parts ensures that vulnerable new growth is fully protected and nourished.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Ni kɛji akɛ afɔ ŋwɛi nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha abu ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ ni aha amɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know if I am applying the right amount of chemical spray to my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsu nii?

english: You must follow the recommended mixture guidelines from your extension officer or product label, because using the wrong amount will fail to protect your crops.
ga: Esa akɛ onyiɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni jɛ nibii ahe nitsulɔ loo nibii ahe wolo lɛ sɛɛ. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ okɛ falɛ ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, ebuuu onibii ahe.

english: What happens if I use less spray chemical than recommended to save money?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsu nii fioo fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii koni mikɛto shika he gbɛjianɔ?

english: Using less chemical than required weakens the treatment, allowing pests or diseases to survive and continue damaging your farm.
ga: Tsofai fioo ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe bɔ ni aŋmala lɛ baaha tsofafeemɔ lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai srɔtoi baa Hi shi ni oya nɔ ofite oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why did my crop spray fail to kill the pests on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-crop spray lɛ egbeee kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spraying usually fails if you do not use proper application tools, mix the wrong chemical dosage, or fail to spray essential parts of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii kɛji akɛ okɛ nibii ni sa tsuuu nii. Tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛfutuɔ loo tso lɛ fãi ni he hiaa lɛ ni akɛshwieee nɔ

english: What is a top spray and why is it important for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji top spray? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: A top spray is a liquid nutrient or protective chemical applied directly onto the upper leaves of a plant to help it absorb treatments quickly.
ga: Top spray ji nu ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua lɛ ni ekɛ tsofa lɛ atsu nii oya.

english: Can plants absorb food and liquid through their leaves or only through their roots?
ga: Ani tsei baanyɛ atsɔ amɛbaai loo amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ pɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu?

english: While roots drink water from the soil, leaves can directly absorb liquid nutrients from a top spray, giving young crops a fast boost to grow stronger.
ga: yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli Baai lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni ji nu kɛjɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ náa hewalɛ oya koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why is it important to spray my crops when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Protecting crops while they are young prevents pests and diseases from attacking tender shoots before the plant is strong enough to recover.
ga: Kɛ́ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni amɛdarako lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baatutua ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anaa dani tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens to my young plants if I skip spraying them early in the season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mifo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: If you skip early spraying, pests and diseases can easily overwhelm small plants, causing poor growth or complete crop failure later in the season.
ga: Kɛji otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofa ni okɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he mra lɛ Kooloi srɔtoi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai Ebaanyɛ eye tsei bibii anɔ kunim mlɛo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ loo amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwraa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly because the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri ejaakɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating holes inside the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms. They hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant to eat the soft growing parts, and you can manage them by applying neem leaf extracts or recommended treatments into the center funnel early in the morning.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmãa bibii ni eda lɛ. Ni obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ni oookɛwo tsɔnei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli leebi maŋkpa lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains beside them creates a living umbrella that shields the young cocoa and keeps the ground cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa hulutsoo baa koni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over during small windstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni tsii lɛ gbee shi yɛ ahum bibioo ko mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not go deep into the earth. When the plant carries a heavy bunch of fruit, wind easily pulls it down, so supporting the stem with a strong wooden prop helps hold it up until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ tso lɛ wo yibii babaoo Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛba shi mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fĩ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efi amɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in the dirt for too long without draining away. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow off, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out high in the sunlight to produce energy for big underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground where they could easily catch diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela baanyɛ amɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without growing into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or gets irregular amounts of water. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔ tomato.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices out of the young leaves. Controlling these insects early with soapy water or appropriate spray stops the leaves from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni sa ni akɛ saamɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do weeds in my farm make my main crops grow small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ afee bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the dirt. Clearing weeds regularly leaves all the soil nutrients available for your main crops to feed on and grow big.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi daa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni otsei titrii lɛ aye niyenii ni amɛdara.

english: How does mixing dry animal manure into the dirt help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure improves the soil by feeding crops natural nutrients and helping the ground retain moisture much longer during hot periods.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be babaoo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and turn brown during the bright sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ egbo ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft, delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot drink water fast enough to replace what the strong sun dries out. They need shade crops like plantains to shelter them during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ anu nu oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he nyɔmɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do plantain suckers grow so slowly when I plant them directly under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tso agbo ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants need direct sunlight and lots of water to grow fast. Big trees block the sunlight and their large root systems steal the water and nutrients from the soil before the plantain roots can reach them.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa Ni amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani plantain shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any peppers when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain knocks the delicate flowers off the stems and washes away the pollen needed to form fruits. Soil that stays too wet also chokes the roots, causing the plant to drop its flowers in stress.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ atsi shishifãi lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ hewɔ.

english: What will happen to my maize crop if I plant the seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ sɛɛkuu mli?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks and very small cobs with missing kernels.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome, ni no haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ bibioo kwraa ni dumɔwui lɛ bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves at the bottom of my maize plants turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛyiteŋgbɛi lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Bottom leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant steals nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does wild grass grow so much faster than my crop seedlings after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ da oya fe mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild grasses have wild, aggressive roots already adapted to local soils. They absorb water and nutrients immediately after rain, while cultivated crop seedlings take longer to settle their roots and start growing.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei, ni yɔɔ basabasa ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni tso dumɔwui ni adu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛjeɔ dalɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes turn soft and spoil so fast if I wait a few days for a buyer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egboɔ oya kɛji mimɛ gbii fioo komɛi kɛha mɔ ni baahe lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to ripen and breathe after being picked. High temperatures speed up this process, causing the fruit walls to break down, lose water, and rot quickly if kept in warm conditions.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ ni emuɔ beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baaha nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya oya. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ gbogboi lɛ gbeeɔ shi, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully formed and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is ready for harvest when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, the stem becomes thick and woody, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack as the expanding tubers push the soil up.
ga: Cassava efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ fee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ tso. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso ni mli elɛɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: If I leave my mature maize standing in the field while searching for a buyer, will the crop be damaged?
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmɔ ko ni ŋmãa ni eda yɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko teŋ be mli ni otaoɔ mɔ ni baahe lɛ, Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baafite?

english: Leaving dry maize standing in the field exposes the cobs to rain, weevils, mold, and birds. This lowers the quality of your grain and can ruin the harvest before a buyer arrives.
ga: Abele ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa nugbɔ, ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ okpoi baa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa oŋmaa lɛ baa shi, ni ebaanyɛ efite kpamɔ lɛ dani mɛi ni baahe nii lɛ aba.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green shoots even when left inside a dark barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living plant stems that go to sleep after harvest. After a few months of rest, warm air naturally signals the yam to wake up and start growing shoots for a new season.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli ni yaa wɔɔhe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Beni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ete shi ni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ kɛha be hee lɛ.

english: Why won't my crops grow properly on land that was previously used for illegal mining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shika tsuru ni mla eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mining strips away the fertile topsoil where crops get their food and compacts the ground so roots cannot breathe. Restoring the soil requires clearing leftover debris, breaking up hard ground, and adding organic matter like compost before planting again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsaa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii ni akɛyeɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akamu. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ saamɔ biɔ ni ajie sũ ni efite lɛ, akumɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli, ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he dani adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer harvests every year even when I clear weeds regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi yɛ nɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they take nutrients out of the earth. Simply clearing weeds stops competition, but without replacing nutrients using fertilizer, animal manure, or compost, the soil becomes tired and worn out.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛkɛ lɛ haa akaŋshii lɛ kpaa. Shi kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsakeee niyenii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaafite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I remove all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily burn in full sunlight. They need shade trees to block harsh sun and trap soil moisture while their roots are still developing.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry weather, poor nutrients, or heat. Maintaining shade and keeping soil covered with organic leaf mulch helps trees stay hydrated so flowers can turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehiii loo dɔlɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ha nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a cocoa tree's way of surviving drought. By shedding leaves, the tree loses less water through evaporation so its main stem and roots can stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni cacao tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi Tso lɛ nu fioo pɛ fiteɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing smaller pods than they did years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their internal systems slow down, making it harder to move food from roots to branches. Pruning old branches or gradually replanting with fresh seedlings revives yields.
ga: Beni cacao tsei hiɔ shi fe afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛmli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ abaajie niyenii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ. Niji momoi ni aaafolɔ loo fiofio ni akɛ dumɔwui heei baadu ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let light and air through helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are tiny insects causing my young green cocoa pods to develop dark spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiha mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ miifee ŋmɔtɔ diji lɛ?

english: These spots are caused by mirids (capsids), small sap-sucking pests that inject toxic saliva into the pod tissue. Applying recommended crop sprays at the right time prevents them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Mirids (capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni kɛ nu ni yɔɔ gbeyei woɔ pod lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii.

english: If I plant my cocoa trees very close together, will I get a larger harvest per acre?
ga: Kɛ midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná yibii babaoo yɛ acre kome mli?

english: Planting too closely causes trees to fight each other for sunlight and soil food, making them tall and weak. Properly spaced trees grow wider, stay healthier, and yield more pods per tree.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɔɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni okɛ pods babaoo aba tso fɛɛ tso nɔ

english: Will planting food crops like cassava near my young cocoa trees hurt the cocoa?
ga: Niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ahe Ani ebaana ŋmei nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: Cassava roots grow thick and consume a lot of soil nutrients and water, which can starve young cocoa seedlings. Crops like plantain or cocoyam are better neighbors because they provide shade without smothering cocoa roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii mli nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha hɔmɔ aye kookoo tsei bibii. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ plantain loo cocoa lɛ hi fe tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo ni amɛtsĩii cocoa shishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense heat and full sun. Without taller shade trees or food crops like plantain around them, direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains bɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa koni wala ahi shi lɛ agbi.

english: Why do I need to put stakes up for my yam vines instead of letting them spread across the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make energy that grows big tubers under the ground. Lifting the vines up on wooden stakes keeps them exposed to light and protects the leaves from soil-borne diseases and rot.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wein tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa la náa wein tsei lɛ anɔ, ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa kɛ fitemɔ he.

english: Why are the leaves at the bottom of my young maize plants turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛyiteŋgbɛi lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. When soil nutrients run low, the plant moves food from its older bottom leaves to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many green leaves, but produce tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted too close together, it puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ ŋmei baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when water is low. Extreme heat stresses the plant, preventing the flower from successfully forming a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ faaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves. As they feed, they damage leaf growth and can spread plant viruses that stunt the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Efiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tsei amli helai ni haa tsei lɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my maize plants have ragged holes in the leaves and dark dirt inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ yɛ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It crawls into the hidden central growth point of the young maize plant to eat soft leaves, leaving behind dark droppings as it feeds.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ he ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ amɛsɛɛ beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year when I plant maize on the same plot repeatedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop season after season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving the earth time to recover, while also allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ nɔŋŋ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slower and stay smaller than usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiifee bibioo fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. When weeds are present, your crops cannot get enough food to grow properly.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la be mli ni jwɛi yɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout and rot in the ground when I plant right after a heavy flood?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ ni amɛgbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ nu afua ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen in the soil to sprout. When the ground is completely flooded, water fills all the air pockets in the soil, suffocating the seeds and causing them to rot before they can grow.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ Nu lɛ baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear away all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikpaa cacao tsei wuji lɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight. Large shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young plants from drying out in the heat and keeping the soil moist enough for their weak roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Buu tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ latsaa be mli. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow from the middle of the leaf to the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves are a clear sign that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food component in the soil that plants use to make strong green leaves.
ga: Abɛi baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why is it helpful for my farm if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and pull it down into the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the soil so neighboring crops like maize get extra plant food without buying chemical fertilizers.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ ana tsei niyenii krokomɛi ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing heavy leaves and thick stems above ground, but giving me small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ baai ni tsii kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess rich manure, the cassava plant gets confused and uses all its energy building lush green leaves at the top instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ Yucca tsei lɛ futuɔ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ ŋmeii baato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves fold up and tear during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally fold and curl their leaves during intense heat to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun. This helps the plant trap moisture inside its stem so it survives the long dry months.
ga: Plantains lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni hulu la ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds early before my young cassava starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Dani ŋmei abifao lɛ baaje shishi eda?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will quickly steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your cassava roots have a chance to establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii. ni ejuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Dani o-cassava shishifãi lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni amɛfee

english: Why do small worms hide inside the middle heart of my maize stalk where it is hard to reach them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ ni ewa akɛ aaashɛ he lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm crawl into the deep center of the maize funnel because it is wet, soft to chew, and hides them from hot sunshine and predatory birds.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ejaakɛ amɛmli edɔ, amɛmli ŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛkɛ amɛ teeɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ okpoi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting, shrinking, and curling upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsi amɛhe, amɛmiigbɔjɔ, ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny, invisible sucking insects like mites or thrips that drink the leaf juices and pass along plant viruses that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips Amɛnuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛhaa tsei amli helai ni haaa amɛdara lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do I need to build high soil mounds before I put my seed yams into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High, loose soil mounds give yam tubers soft earth to stretch downward without running into hard, compact soil, which allows them to grow straight, wide, and long.
ga: Gɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ náa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shwereɔ kɛyaa shishi ni ejooo foi kɛboteee shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa tɛ̃ɛ, amɛlɛɔ, ni amɛlɛɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomato fruits during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When air temperatures get too high during hot afternoons, the heat damages the delicate pollen inside tomato blossoms, causing the unfertilized flowers to dry up and drop off.
ga: Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, latsaa lɛ kpataa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ ahiɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong green leaves. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or organic manure gives the plant the food it needs to turn green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can saturate the soil with excess water, depriving root crops like cassava of air and causing them to drown and rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily and keeps the roots safe.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni fa fe nine. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛmiigbee nu mli ni amɛgboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the sunny season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate stems and leaves that easily lose moisture under strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a living umbrella that shields the young trees until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ hulutsoo ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ aha. kɛyashi tso lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa

english: What is making holes in my corn leaves and leaving small dark droppings in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa baa lɛ mli ewo bu ni eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ? Okɛwo tso lɛ teŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the middle leaf whorl of the maize plant to feed. Spraying an approved insecticide or neem seed mixture early in the morning or late evening helps control these caterpillars before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye nii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem dumɔwui ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving your plants steady water at the base and avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizers during flowering encourages the blossoms to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli nu yɛ amɛshishigbɛ kɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and prevents moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun. It also blocks weed seeds from growing and breaks down over time to enrich the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu la lɛ shwieɔ oya lɛ shwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui hu anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkafite yɛ be ni sa mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii babaoo.

english: What will happen if I plant my crops very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition leaves all the plants thin and weak, resulting in smaller yields than if you had spaced them properly.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi fe kɛji okɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil consumes all the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil-borne diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility by putting nitrogen back into the dirt.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ biɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi taoɔ, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ aba. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that steal water and fertilizer away from your main crops before the crops can absorb them. Clearing weeds early in the growing cycle ensures your crop gets all the nourishment you put into the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli dani tso lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, onibii lɛ naa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these sucking pests early using recommended organic or chemical sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ mra. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsofa mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build green leaves. This happens when the soil lacks fertilizer or when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ sũ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fite niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers always tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them first naturally enriches your soil with free fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ mra baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are tiny worms eating deep holes inside the green funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that loves to hide inside the central growing tip of maize plants to feed on tender leaves. If left untreated, they destroy the plant's ability to grow leaves and produce corn ears.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe awo ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli koni eye baai bibii. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Efiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly droop and dry up within two days even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ gboi yɛ gbii enyɔ mli lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: This sudden collapse is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that blocks the tubes inside the plant stem. It stops water from moving up to the leaves, making the plant look thirsty even in moist soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ anaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu akaya ŋwɛi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni kumai miiye lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ po nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop almost all their flowers before any young pods form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are under stress from prolonged dry heat, lack of soil nutrients, or attacks from sap-sucking insects like mirids. The tree drops flowers to save its own energy for survival.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛyɔɔ latsaa ni mli egbi lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen lɛ tutuamɔi lɛ, tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees keep falling over at the roots just when the bunch is getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain lɛ tsii waa lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ gbee shi kɛtee shishifãi lɛ anɔ eyɛ mli akɛ He ni niji lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ agboi yɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be easily weakened by underground pests like root nematodes or stem borers. Without strong roots to anchor them, the weight of a growing plantain bunch pulls the whole tree down during rain or wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ oya. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ ni baaha ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ he lɛ Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli tsiimɔ lɛ baagbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi yɛ nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ be mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains fall for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa otsii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains leave standing water around the roots, the soil becomes waterlogged, choking the roots and causing rot-causing fungi to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu bua ehe kɛbɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. Leaving tall shade trees protects young crops from sun damage and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and make my crops produce smaller harvests during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that drink water and absorb soil fertilizer much faster than farm crops. When weeds grow close to your crops, they steal sunlight and food, leaving your crops stunted.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni nuɔ nu ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ Amɛjuɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii. Ehaa onibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots in the barn after a few months even without water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii eŋɔli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi po sɛɛ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living plant stems that go into a natural resting state after harvest. Once their internal biological clock detects a change in temperature and season, they break dormancy and sprout to prepare for new growth.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ shihilɛ ni bɛ mli mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ na tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ hulutsoo kɛ be mli lɛ Amɛfoɔ wɔɔhe ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha dalɛ hee.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow early in the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for the plant's leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni no ji niyenii kɛha tso lɛ baai lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm get very hard and dry up quickly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil gets hard when it lacks organic matter like decayed leaves and compost. Adding manure or plant mulch improves the soil structure so it can hold water longer like a sponge.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally feeds neighboring crops like maize and restores soil fertility.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do black spots appear on my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii diji yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, damp conditions. Pruning extra shade branches lets in sunlight and airflow to keep the pods dry and reduce the disease.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaakpɛ tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle he koni eha tsei lɛ agbi ni helai aba shi.

english: How do I stop tiny beetles from destroying my harvested dried maize in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaje kpo? Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpata ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ hiɛ ni akɛto?

english: Maize weevils attack stored corn when it is not fully dry or sealed properly. Drying your maize thoroughly under the sun and storing it in airtight bags keeps moisture and pests out.
ga: Abɛi ŋmei tutuaa abɛi ni ato lɛ kɛ́ egbiko kwraa loo atsĩko naa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaabu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extremely hot weather causes heat stress in pepper plants, forcing them to shed flowers to conserve water. Watering them regularly and providing light shade helps preserve the flowers.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛfɔ fɔfɔi koni nu akafite. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need soil that drains water easily. When soil remains soaked with excess water for days, the roots cannot get oxygen and begin to rot underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees suffer when all the large forest trees around them are removed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ naa amanehulu lɛ? Ani ajie kɛjɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct harsh sunlight. Tall shade trees protect cocoa seedlings from scorching heat and preserve moisture in the air and soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I measure space between my tomato plants instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu bɔ ni mi-tomato tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ he moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing gives each tomato plant enough room to access sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing, while allowing wind to pass through and prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tomato tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa enáa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛ ehe akaŋ akaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ naa.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the rains are unreliable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nugbɔshiimɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Instead of planting on a fixed calendar date, wait until the ground receives steady, heavy rains for a few consecutive days so the soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ gbi pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ lɛ, Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, a key nutrient they need to grow. When plants do not get enough nutrients from the soil or when excess rain washes nitrogen away, their leaves lose green color and growth slows down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ Kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo lɛ, nitrogen lɛ laajeɔ. Baai lɛ laajeɔ amɛ su eŋɔli ni amɛdalɛ baa shi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and humid conditions. Excess shade and overcrowded branches trap moisture, allowing the fungus to spread quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Shade babaoo kɛ tsei niji ni eyi obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantains on the same land where I am planting new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ kookoo hee yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture for young cocoa trees during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo ni ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy, poorly drained soil. Raising planting mounds or ridges helps drain excess rainwater away from the roots, keeping them dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ awó gɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my corn plants and leaving small brown droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the center whorl of corn plants during the day to feed on young leaves. Catching them early before they destroy the growing point is essential to saving the crop yield.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi mli koni amɛye baai bibii. Amɛ ni abaamɔ amɛ mra dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ he miihia waa koni akɛhere ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ ayiwala.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is healthy enough to support a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua nikpamɔ kpakpa?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, crumbles easily in your hands, holds moisture, and contains living creatures like earthworms. Hard, pale, or crusty soil lacks organic matter and needs manure or compost to rebuild its fertility.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ su ni tsuɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ekɛtswa eshishitoo mlai lɛ ema shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close to each other to get more plants on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayi afa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots compete for the same nutrients and water in the soil, while their leaves block each other from sunlight. Proper spacing ensures every plant receives enough light and food to produce larger yields.
