ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive in tough conditions, so they absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing food and choking your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni amɛkafo onibii amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants dry up and wilt suddenly even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gĩɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by root rot or bacterial wilt, where tiny organisms block the tubes inside the stem that carry water upward. Practicing crop rotation and avoiding planting peppers in the exact same spot every year stops these diseases from building up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. he ni wala yibii bibii Ebaatsi paipi ni yɔɔ tsɔne lɛ mli ni hiɛɔ nu kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ naa. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooodu yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ he. Ebaaye ebua ni helai nɛɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: How do changing rainfall dates affect when I should put my seeds in the ground?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ gbii ni tsakeɔ lɛ baaná be ni esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Seeds need continuous soil moisture to sprout and grow strong roots. Planting after just one early rain can cause seeds to dry out and die if a dry spell follows, so waiting until the major rainy season fully settles protects your seed investment.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ adu shikome pɛ yɛ leebi nugbɔ ni nɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ omɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu odumɔwui ni okɛwo mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my oranges tasting sour even though they look big and yellow on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange lɛ ŋɔɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Oranges turn yellow due to cooler night temperatures, but they need enough sunlight and soil nutrients like potassium to build up sugar. Harvesting too early or lacking nutrients leaves the fruit sour despite its bright color.
ga: Oranges tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni mli ejɔ hewɔ. Shi hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli tamɔ potassium he miihia amɛ koni amɛkɛfee sugars. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ bɔ ni ehiɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: What causes dark, rough spots on the skin of my oranges, and why do buyers complain about it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mihewolo nɔ lɛ baa? Ni mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miiwie huhuuhu yɛ he lɛ?

english: Dark spots are usually caused by insect damage or fungal diseases on the surface. Even if the inside fruit is still good, buyers reject or pay less for spotted fruit because it rots faster during transportation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji baa. Shi kɛlɛ, aduawai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hi lolo. Shi mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ loo amɛwoɔ nyɔmɔ fioo kɛha aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ejaakɛ egboɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Why are my orange trees dropping a lot of small green fruits before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo dani amɛdara kwraa?

english: Trees drop young fruit when they suffer from water stress, extreme heat, or nutrient shortages. The tree naturally sheds extra fruit it cannot support to keep itself alive during dry spells.
ga: Tsei woɔ yibii kɛ́ nu he naagbai, latsaa ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa. Tso lɛ woɔ yibii krɛdɛɛi ni nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why does my citrus tree produce plenty of flowers, but very few turn into actual oranges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Flowers fail to set fruit if there are not enough bees for pollination, if heavy rains wash away pollen, or if the tree lacks essential micronutrients like boron during the flowering stage.
ga: Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha pollination bɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa pollen lɛ kɛya. Aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii bibii ni he hiaa tamɔ boron yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why are the oranges from my orchard very small and dry inside when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni jɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛmli egbi beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Small and dry oranges occur when the tree experiences drought while the fruit is filling up with juice, or when too many fruits are growing on a single branch competing for the tree's limited food.
ga: Akutu bibii ni egbi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ na hɔmɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ eyi kɛ nu. Aloo beni aduawai babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso nine kome nɔ tsɔ koni amɛkɛye akaŋ yɛ tso lɛ niyenii fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ he lɛ.

english: How does regular watering during the dry season affect the fruit size of my crop?
ga: Te nu ni mikɛhaa daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Providing steady water when the fruits are expanding allows the tree to build juicy, plump pulp inside the skin, resulting in heavier and larger fruits that command better prices.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa beni aduawai lɛ miigbɛ eshwa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa ehewolo lɛ mli. Enɛ haa aduawai ni tsii ni dara ni kudɔɔ jara lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my fruit trees turning yellow while the veins stay dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni fãji lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves with green veins signal a nutrient deficiency, usually zinc or iron. This happens when the soil is depleted or too dry for the tree roots to absorb minerals properly.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni fãji eŋɔli yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji zinc loo dade. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ loo egbi tsɔ ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ minerals lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will cutting away extra branches on my orange tree help me get bigger fruit?
ga: Ani niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-orange tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mafolɔ lɛ baaye abua mi ni mawo yibii wuji?

english: Yes, pruning removes weak or dead branches so sunlight and air can reach the inner parts of the tree. This reduces disease and directs all the tree's energy into growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso lɛ niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egbɔjɔ loo egboi lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa helai baa shi ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Do oranges continue to ripen and get sweeter after I pick them from the tree?
ga: Ani ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ sɛɛ?

english: No, unlike bananas or mangoes, citrus fruits stop ripening the moment they are plucked. You must leave them on the tree until they are fully sweet before harvesting.
ga: Dabi, jeee tamɔ banana loo mango. Citrus yibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kɛji ajie amɛ pɛ. Esa akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa dani akpa.

english: Why do my harvested fruits spoil so quickly before I can sell them to market buyers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya dani ahɔ̃ɔ ahaa mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Fruit spoils quickly if it is pulled violently off the tree, creating small tears at the stem where fungi enter. Using sharp shears to clip the stem leaves the fruit sealed and extends its shelf life.
ga: Yibii lɛ baagbo oya kɛji akɛ agbala lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛ yiwalɛ. ni kɛ yaafo bibii baa Yɛ tso lɛ shishi he ni ŋmei lɛ boteɔ mli lɛ Nɔ Skɛs ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ ahi shi ni eha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do I see so many ants crawling around the cashew nuts on my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii babaoo ni miiho kɛmiibɔle ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Ants are usually attracted to the sweet sap produced by the cashew apple or the sugary waste left behind by smaller sap-sucking insects. In many cases, the ants are just feeding on the surface juices rather than eating the hard cashew nut itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni ŋɔɔ ni jɛɔ cashew ŋmeii amli lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii. loo molasses ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ shiɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ nu lɛ hiɛ lɛ kɛkɛ moŋ fe cashew ŋmeii ni wa lɛ.

english: Are the ants on my cashew trees actually destroying the nuts, or are they just walking on the surface?
ga: Akpɔlɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifite ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo nyiɛmɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Most ants only walk on the surface to feed on fruit juice or sap. However, their presence often means smaller hidden pests, like thrips or mealybugs, are underneath them doing actual damage to the cashew surface.
ga: Aŋkroaŋkroi babaoo nyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛye nu loo nu mli nu pɛ, shi kɛlɛ bei pii lɛ amɛhiɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ thrips loo mealybugs. Yɛ shishi lɛ, amɛfiteɔ cashew ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: How can I tell if an insect is damaging the inside of my cashew nut or just the outer skin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miitutua mi-cashews lɛ loo amɛmiitutua mi-cashew lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ pɛ?

english: Surface damage usually leaves dry brown scars or dark marks without penetrating the hard shell. Internal damage typically shows visible entry holes, sticky gum leaking out, or a soft, rotten shell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni egbi loo ŋmeii ni tsuɔ ni eboteee ŋmeii ni wa lɛ amli baa. Bei pii lɛ, mligbɛ nibii ni efite lɛ jieɔ bu ni anaa kɛboteɔ mli lɛ kpo. Gum ni kpɛtɛɔ he lɛ je kpo. aloo eyɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egbo

english: Why do insects always seem to cluster right where the cashew nut joins the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ he ni cashew ŋmeii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: The point where the cashew nut attaches to the cashew apple is soft, moist, and rich in fresh juice. This creates a hidden, sheltered spot that naturally attracts ants and tiny sap-eating bugs.
ga: He ni cashew ŋmeii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, edɔ ni nu hee eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa he ko ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ wuo lɛ.

english: Are all ants in my cashew farm harmful to my crop?
ga: Ani ŋmeii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mi-cashew ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: No, not all ants are harmful. Some types, like red weaver ants, are actually beneficial because they hunt and kill major cashew pests like the cashew bug and leaf-mining caterpillars.
ga: Dabi, jeee ŋmeii fɛɛ yeɔ mɔ awui. Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii komɛi, tamɔ red weaver ant lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ ejaakɛ amɛgbeɔ ŋmeii ni he hiaa tamɔ ŋmei ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbeɔ amɛ.

english: Could the way I harvest and collect my cashews be causing ants to swarm the nuts?
ga: Ani bɔ ni akpaa cashews lɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii abote ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: Yes. Leaving ripe cashews on the damp ground for too long allows the sugary cashew apples to bruise and leak juice, which quickly attracts swarms of ants and other soil insects.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi cashew ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu lɛ ajɛ mli. Enɛ gbalaa ŋmeii akui kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ. oya oyai

english: What causes tiny rough marks to form on the surface of my raw cashew nuts?
ga: Mɛni kɛ okadii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa? Yɛ mi cashews ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Rough surface marks are often caused by very small insects, like thrips, that scrape and feed on the skin of young nuts. As the nut grows, those scraped areas turn into dry, brown scars.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii waa, tamɔ thrips, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ahewolo ni amɛyeɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋwɛi okadii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ Nakai hei ni akpɛ́ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do some of my cashew apples look like other tiny creatures are living inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew lɛ ekomɛi tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ bɔɔ nii bibii ni hiɔ amɛmli lɛ?

english: Certain pests, like the cashew apple borer, lay eggs inside the soft fruit. The hatching larvae burrow into the apple to feed, creating tunnels that look like tiny creatures are living inside.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui komɛi tamɔ cashew aduawai borers lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ aduawai bibii amli. Lalabii ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ apɔle lɛ mli koni amɛtao niyenii. Enɛ haa tsɔne ko ni tamɔ nɔ ni bɔɔ nii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. hiɔ mli

english: How does keeping my cashew farm clear of weeds help control insects on my trees?
ga: Te mi-cashew ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds and overgrown bush provide breeding grounds and shaded pathways for ants and other pests to reach your trees. Clearing the farm forces pests away and exposes them to natural predators.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ji hei ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi fɔɔ kɛboteɔ mli. Tsei ahe gbɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ ajie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akabote mli ni ebaaha amɛyashɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: If I see black marks on the outside of my cashew apples, does it mean the nut attached to it is spoiled?
ga: Kɛji mina he ko ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ cashew ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni ekpɛtɛ he lɛ ekumɔ?

english: Not necessarily. Black surface marks are often just light cosmetic damage from insects feeding on the skin. In most cases, the valuable seed inside the hard nut shell remains healthy and undamaged.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, okadii diji ni yɔɔ hewolo lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nibii bibii pɛ ni kooloi ni yeɔ hewolo lɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ. Yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ Dumɔwui ni jara wa ni yɔɔ ŋmei ŋmei ni wa lɛ mli lɛ baahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow from the tip downward, it usually means the crop is starving for nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe and feed.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ kɛba shi lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛna niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the fruit starts growing large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems. As the heavy bunch of fruit grows, the plant becomes top-heavy, so strong winds or soft wet soil can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Kɛ́ aduawai babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ oooshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ja okɛ tsei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high up on stakes so they can catch direct sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce energy, which sends food down to build large yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tso ko nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. ni tsuɔ niyenii kɛyaa shi koni efee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in heavy rain when water pools in heavy soil without proper drainage. Soaking in standing water starves the roots of air and allows soil fungal rot to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli, kɛ́ nu lɛ tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo nu ni ekã mli lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ baaha shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha sũ mli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ atutua amɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and wilt in the afternoon heat even if I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, pepper leaves lose moisture into the air faster than the roots can pull water from the soil. The plant temporary wilts to save water, but usually recovers once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔɔ. Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei gboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shi bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ, amɛhe jɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land year after year lead to smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haaa yibiiwoo babaoo aba lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer directly into the hole with my new seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ bu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛfataa dumɔwui heei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Unsprouted seeds do not have roots yet to drink fertilizer, and strong chemical fertilizer touching a delicate seed directly can burn or kill it before it can germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ekwɛko lolo lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni amɛbaanu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ mli. Ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo agbe amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Cocoa flowers drop naturally if the tree is stressed by drought, excessive heat, or insect damage. Proper shade management and pest control help the flowers stay on the tree to produce pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ, latsaa ni naa wa loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Shade nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee pods.

english: What makes caterpillars hide and eat deep inside the funnels of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛboteɔ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ?

english: Insects like the Fall Armyworm lay their eggs inside the central leaf funnel of young corn because it is soft, moist, and offers shelter from birds and heat while they eat the fresh leaves.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli edɔ, ni amɛhaa okpoi kɛ dɔlɛ he jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ abɛi heei lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep seeds that wake up instantly when rain falls, allowing them to steal available soil water and plant food faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tso ko ni wa, ni dumɔwui lɛ mli kwɔ, ni kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni eteɔ shi. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ ni amɛduɔ niyenii oya fe bɔ ni tsei baanyɛ afee.

english: When is the right time for me to plant my corn after the dry season ends?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: You should plant after the first continuous heavy rains settle the soil moisture, usually around March or April for the major season, to ensure seeds germinate without drying out in the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ odu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni okɛtsake shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee March loo April kɛha be titri lɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbiŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are sitting in excess water, which prevents them from taking up essential nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall but fail to produce full ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miida shi ewooo abele toi ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Maize plants fail to form full cobs when planted too close together or when they face drought stress during the critical flowering and silking stage.
ga: Abɛi tsei nyɛŋ afee toi ni eyi obɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ ekɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ kpe yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, common pests that hide inside the growing center of the maize plant and eat the tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ni eyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to measure space between my crops instead of planting seeds closely together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu he ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo du dumi ɔ he nɛ bɛŋkɛ he.

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without competing with its neighbors, leading to healthier crops and higher yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ akutsoŋbii akaŋ akaŋ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Can I plant cassava in the same field with my maize at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows fast and is harvested early, leaving space for the slower-growing cassava to expand its roots later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Enɛ haa gbɛ haa ŋmei lɛ ni edaa fiofio koni sɛɛ mli lɛ eshishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help my soil before I plant my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume plants like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as natural fertilizer that feeds your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and show pale yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that weakens the plant and stops the cassava tubers from growing big.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even when it rained a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Ni nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ?

english: Hot sunlight causes leaves to lose water faster than shallow roots can pull water from the soil, causing temporary wilting until temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa amɛgbiɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees dry up their outer leaves during severe dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ haa esɛɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains drop or dry out their large outer leaves during dry periods to conserve water inside the main stem so the whole plant does not die.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai wuji lɛ loo amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni nu bɛ lɛ koni nu ahi tso lɛ shishi. Koni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ akagbo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves regain their rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛná amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How come growing groundnuts or beans in my field makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a special family of plants that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested, those roots decay and leave natural fertilizer in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei aweku krɛdɛɛ ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpaa yibii lɛ Nakai shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and short roots that burn quickly under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides shade and moisture, acting as a natural umbrella while the cocoa is young.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves to catch sunlight, which powers the growth of the tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the wet ground, preventing leaf diseases and maximizing sun exposure.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ egbɛ baai eshwa koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. ni tsirɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ adalɛ Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi baa hela naa ni oha hulu la aya hiɛ

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and drop off during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a self-defense trick cassava uses to save water during dry weather. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation and preserves its energy inside the roots until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji ŋaa ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he ni ŋmei kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli. Kɛtsɔ ebaai ni eshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei haa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. ni eha hewalɛ ahi shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over during heavy rains and strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that spread sideways near the topsoil instead of digging deep. When heavy rain softens the soil and the fruit bunch gets heavy, strong winds can easily tip the plant over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa sɛɛgbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni aduawai akui lɛ feɔ shwiili. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha tsei akumɔ oya.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the fresh funnel leaves in the middle of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ni maye cone baai heei yɛ mi-abele ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft growing center of the maize plant. Checking fields early and applying neem extracts or approved insect treatments directly into the plant funnel can control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tsɔɔ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha akudɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When fields get waterlogged with standing water, the roots drown from lack of oxygen, allowing soil fungi to enter and cause rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu ni damɔ shi lɛ eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and proper watering helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni sa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the bottom ends of my tomato fruits turn black and flat before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit while it grows. Irregular watering often prevents the plant from absorbing calcium properly, so maintaining steady moisture in the soil helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ haaa amɛná calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need plantains planted right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily scorched by direct, harsh sunlight. Planting plantains nearby provides fast shade with their wide leaves, keeping the young cocoa cool and preserving moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa kookoo baai lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for green growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the maize regain its green color and grow bigger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etsɔ agbo.

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to branch out, catch enough light, and produce plenty of healthy peppers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ewo niji heei. Na la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ni obaanyɛ ona chili ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ babaoo.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant beans or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are special crops that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally enriches the land and acts as a free fertilizer for neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why does insect damage on my cabbage leaves stop the head from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni tutuaa mi-cabbage baai lɛ miiha yitsei lɛ miikpa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves act like food factories for the plant using sunlight. When insects eat holes in the cabbage leaves, the plant loses its power to make food, preventing it from forming a tight, heavy head.
ga: Baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii nitsumɔhei kɛha tsei ni kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii lɛ. Kɛji kooloi ye bu ni yɔɔ kaabii baai amli lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛfee niyenii dɔŋŋ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmeii ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings rot in the ground when I plant them during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive water fills up the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the cassava cuttings. Without air, soil fungi and bacteria easily attack and rot the stem cuttings before they can sprout roots.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei niji lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tutuaa niji lɛ oya ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ dani shishifãi lɛ daa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep dropping off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or prolonged dry soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist during the flowering stage helps the plant retain its blossoms to grow tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛha tomato ni akwɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce less food even when I water my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your main crops. Removing weeds regularly ensures all available soil food goes directly to growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii titrii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni akɛ sũ mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛkwɛ otsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and getting soft in my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni ebafee blɛoo yɛ mi-stash lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that react to warmth and moisture by trying to grow into new plants, which uses up their stored food. Storing yams on raised racks in a cool, well-ventilated barn stops them from sprouting too soon.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni tsuɔ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i he nii kɛtsɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛdu tsei heei lɛ nɔ. ni yeɔ niyenii ni ato lɛ fɛɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato shĩai ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ shĩa ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkadara oya tsɔ.

english: Why do certified seeds bought from the dealer give a better harvest than seeds I save from last year's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni jaa lɛ adɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ dumɔ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially produced to resist diseases and grow uniformly strong. Seeds saved year after year lose their strength, leading to smaller yields and weaker plants.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛdara waa be fɛɛ be. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why does the direction I face my crop rows matter when I am planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ni mikɛkwɛɔ mitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ he hiaa beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Planting your rows in an east-to-west direction allows your crops to receive sunlight evenly throughout the day as the sun moves across the sky, preventing taller plants from casting continuous shade on smaller ones.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛyaa anaigbɛ lɛ haa nibii ni aduɔ lɛ naa hulu la po yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli beni hulu lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Tsi tsei kakadaji anaa koni amɛkafee hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɛ tsei bibii anɔ.

english: How does strong wind affect my maize field, and can the way I arrange my rows help?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ saa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni ani gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atoɔ line he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua?

english: Strong winds can easily push down tall maize plants before harvest. Aligning your planting rows perpendicular to the direction of the local wind creates a barrier that slows down wind speed and protects your crops.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa ŋmãa tsei kakadaŋŋ ashwie shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ dani akpa. Kɛ́ oto dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa lɛ he lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa oya ni ebuɔ onibii ahe.

english: If I have a vast piece of land, why shouldn't I just plant my crops as close together as possible to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ wulu Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, which leads to weak plants and a lower overall yield.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulu lɛ mli wa waa Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow long stems with thin roots when planted under dense leaf canopy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi kakadaji kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛji akwɛ yɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava requires full sunlight to manufacture food for root development; under heavy shade, the plant uses all its energy stretching upwards toward the light instead of fattening its underground tubers.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni enyɛ ená niyenii kɛha shishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ. shishi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni ekɛ ehe shwieɔ shi kɛyaa la lɛ he lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ bɔlbui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear all the large trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally thrive under filtered shade because direct tropical sunlight overheats their leaves and dries out the topsoil before their young roots can reach deeper groundwater.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ amli adɔ fe nine. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ dani shishifãi bibii lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce the amount of leaf surface area exposed to the hot sun, which helps it conserve water when moisture loss is high.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ fa babaoo.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my crops when I plant them straight down a hillside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ midumɔi lɛ kɛyaa kɛji midu yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting downhill creates natural pathways for heavy rainwater to speed up, eroding fertile topsoil and washing away seeds; planting across the slope slows down water so the soil can absorb it.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yaa oya. Efiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why do my legume crops like cowpea or groundnuts make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes live together with helpful bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into soil food, leaving behind natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes hiɔ shi yɛ symbiosis mli kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshiɔ kɛhaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does an extension officer tell me I need a high budget at the start just to clear and line my field properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ ehe miihia ni maná shika babaoo yɛ shishijee mli koni mikɛjie mihe lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛto he lɛ?

english: Investing money upfront in proper land clearing, spacing, and certified seeds prevents crop overcrowding and disease spread, ensuring higher long-term yields that recover your initial investment.
ga: Shika ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ kɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa anáa sɛɛnamɔi ni fa babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni onáa shika ni okɛwo mli shishijee lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I prune off lower branches from my tomato plants when they look healthy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli be mli ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ ni amɛji eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Removing lower branches prevents soil-borne diseases from splashing onto leaves during rain and directs the plant's food supply away from leaf growth and directly into growing larger fruit.
ga: Afoɔ tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ koni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ akashwie baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Ni enɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii jɛɛhe lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni daa lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. If they do not have taller shade crops like plantains or cassava planted nearby, the hot sun scorches their fresh leaves, causing them to dry up and turn yellow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha baai heei lɛ ashã. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves off the ground to capture maximum sunlight. When the leaves receive plenty of sunlight, the plant produces more energy, which flows down to build larger and heavier yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ baajie hewalɛ babaoo kpo. Enɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is my maize field turning pale yellow even though there has been plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential food plants need to stay green and grow fast. Heavy rain can wash nutrients out of the soil, leaving the plants hungry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha tsei aye hɔmɔ

english: Why do other farmers plant groundnuts in the same field alongside their maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi duɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are special crops that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally, helping the maize grow bigger without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why are flowers falling off my tomato plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or dry soil. When the plant gets stressed by high temperatures, it drops its blossoms to conserve water and energy to stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa ha tsei hao lɛ Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ wala nɔ lɛ he.

english: When too many young shoots grow around the main plantain stem, they steal water and nutrients from it. Cutting away all but one or two strong shoots ensures the main tree has enough strength to grow a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii dara kɛbɔle tso wulu lɛ he tsɔ lɛ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ nakai tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ fɛɛ amli, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdumɔwui babaoo baa.

english: Healthy cassava foliage with bright green leaves and sturdy stems usually indicates that strong roots are forming underground. If the leaves are curled, yellowed, or stunted, the tubers underneath are likely small or diseased.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ shishifãi ni wa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ miifee shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe, amɛfee ŋmɔŋ, loo amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ekolɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baafee bibii loo hela emɔ amɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the leaf juices, or by a virus spread by those insects. Controlling these tiny pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kudɔɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why does witchweed (Striga) keep coming back in my cereal fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei (striga) lɛ yaa nɔ ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa miŋmaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that thrives in poor, exhausted soils by attaching itself directly to the roots of maize or sorghum to steal food. Improving soil fertility with manure or compost helps the crop grow strong enough to resist the weed.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni egbɔjɔ nɔ. Amɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛju niyenii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ jwɛi.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable garden in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli Aloo leebi hi fe no?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the cool ground allows the roots to absorb water before the sun can evaporate it. Watering in the hot sun can waste water and damage tender foliage.
ga: Nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ he ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu la lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite nu ni efite baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide shade and keep moisture in the soil, helping the cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or the soil is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving field drainage helps the leaves regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo oha nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray pesticides on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because the air is cooler and calm. High heat in the middle of the day can evaporate the chemical too fast or burn the plant leaves when combined with the spray.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni eyɛ dioo. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ loo eshã tso lɛ baai lɛ kɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ fata he.

english: How do I know when my cassava is mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when its lower leaves dry up and fall off, leaving bare stems, and the ground around the base of the plant starts to crack from the expanding roots underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi, ni amɛshi shishifã lɛ, ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the blossoms dropping off my tomato plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when weather is too hot, water supply is irregular, or soil lacks nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the plants helps flowers stay attached and produce tomatoes.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. Aloo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be fɛɛ be ni oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo tomato.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my farm make my crops grow smaller and weaker?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa waa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops when the soil is dry or after rain?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Always apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain. Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into the ground so roots can absorb it; putting fertilizer on dry ground can burn the roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough light for leaf growth. Lifting vines off the wet soil prevents leaves from rotting and helps the plant send more energy down to build larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛbaa lɛ aya hiɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haaa baai lɛ agbo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa shi koni ekɛfee bulbs wuji.

english: Why should I buy certified hybrid seeds instead of planting saved seeds from last year's maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation, leading to smaller yields and uneven growth. Certified hybrid seeds are specially produced to grow uniformly and produce high yields every season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo aha yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: How can I tell if my vegetables are getting too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu babaoo miihe mi-vegetables lɛ?

english: Overwatered vegetables show soft, yellow leaves and droopy stems even when the soil is wet. If the soil stays muddy and smells sour, root roots are drowning from a lack of air in the soil.
ga: Aduawai ni awo amɛ nu fe nine lɛ baajie baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ tsei ni egbɔjɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo muji lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miigbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I stop stray goats and farm animals from entering my field and destroying my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tooi ni elaaje kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote miŋmɔji amli ni amɛfite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can protect your farm by planting a living fence around your land using fast-growing, thorny shrubs like Jatropha or Gliricidia. This keeps wandering animals out while clearly marking your farm boundaries.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ gbogbo ni hiɛ ka ni ooodu obɔle he lɛ nɔ. oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ jatropha loo glicidia lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni kooloi ni elaaje lɛ akabote ohe yɛ be mli ni okadiɔ oŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to plant my food crops directly along the border next to my neighbor's field?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu miniyenii yɛ husu ni kã mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting right on the boundary line can lead to crop damage if your neighbor's livestock wanders over or if chemical sprays drift from their land. Leaving a narrow buffer zone or grass strip protects your crops from external disturbance.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ husui anɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akutsoŋbii lɛ akooloi lɛ fã kɛtee he fɛɛ he loo kɛji tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ oshi he ko ni yɔɔ bibioo loo jwɛi line lɛ, ebuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nibii ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ ni baafite ohe lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and rolling up during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up and turn yellow when the crop is stressed by extreme heat or a lack of water and soil nutrients. Rolling the leaves is the plant's natural way of reducing water loss through its leaves.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni elaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛwoɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience environmental stress, such as very high temperatures, uneven watering, or poor soil fertility. The plant sheds flowers to conserve energy until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa kpe. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii Tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and leafy, but the roots underneath stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant directs all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do tiny holes appear on my cowpea leaves every time the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ tsina ŋmeii ahe be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: The start of the rainy season creates ideal conditions for leaf-feeding insects like beetles and caterpillars to multiply. Spraying natural deterrents like neem leaf extract early on prevents these pests from consuming the crop leaves.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ baai tamɔ ladybugs kɛ caterpillars koni amɛfɔ. Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsiɔ nii anaa tamɔ neem baa mli nu lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ mra Ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if I leave them growing in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miha amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for essential resources like soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. If not weeded early, they starve your crops and reduce your final harvest.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la. Amɛbaahã hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛbaaha onaagbee ŋmaa lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the surface of the soil. As the heavy fruit bunch grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and can easily tip over during high winds without wooden stakes for support.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji aduawai akuu ko ni tsii kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛi Tsei lɛ hu ji ŋwɛi-tsii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfo amɛhe oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli ni yelikɛbuamɔ he ehiaaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my tomato plants rotting near the wet ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain splashes soil onto the lower leaves, fungal diseases present in the soil infect the plant. Removing the bottom leaves and mulching the ground around the stem prevents splash-back and keeps the plant dry.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, sũ shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ tsei. Ajieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsiɔ kickback naa ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves up to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep dropping off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or attacks from insects like mirids. The tree naturally sheds flowers it cannot support to save energy.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Tsei baafɔ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni anyɛɛɛ aye abua koni akɛ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very thin even when the leaves on top look lush and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers underneath.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing tubers under the ground. Climbing stakes helps spread the leaves out in the sun and keeps them off the damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Tsoi ni akwɔɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa hulu lɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni no ji he ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and turning thick and shiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekpɛɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cowpea seedlings fall over and die just a few days after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is called 'damping-off,' caused by soil fungi that thrive when the ground is too wet. The fungi rot the weak stems of young seedlings right at the soil line.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘Damping’ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Fung lɛ fiteɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll up tight into tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔne ko yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water during intense heat. It shrinks the leaf surface exposed to the sun so the plant can save moisture.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akaje mli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Ehaa baa ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce fewer fruit bunches during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palms need constant soil moisture to develop fruit. During dry periods, the tree slows down flowering and fruit growth to preserve water and stay alive.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛwo yibii. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tso lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai adalɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: When planted too close, maize plants compete with each other for light, water, and soil food. This makes all the stalks thin and weak, resulting in very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu Abele tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantain trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii amli yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs in its first years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Can I use the same planting machine for both rice and groundnuts on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsɔne kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, but you must adjust the machine settings or change the seed plate first. Groundnut seeds are much larger than rice grains, so using the wrong setting will crush groundnuts or release too many rice seeds at once.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ otsake tsɔne lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ loo otsake seed disc lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Peanut dumɔwui lɛ dara kwraa fe ŋmãa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ he ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akpɔtɔ loo amɛjie ŋmeii babaoo shikome.

english: How do I properly adjust a small manual seed planter before taking it to my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsake dumɔwui adumɔ tsɔne bibioo ko ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ dani madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Before planting, test the machine on a flat surface. Adjust the seed outlet gap according to the seed size so that only one or two seeds drop at a time at consistent intervals as you move forward.
ga: Dani obaadu lɛ, kaa tsɔne lɛ okwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Tsakemɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishijee gbɛ lɛ mli yɛ dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ naa bɔni afee ni dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ aba shi yɛ be kome mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli beni oyaa ohiɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I switch from planting my crops by hand to using a small walking planter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛ niji kwɛɔ nɔ kɛya tsei bibii ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ anɔ?

english: A planter saves labor and time while placing seeds at equal depths and distances. This uniform spacing allows your crops to get equal sunlight and nutrients, making weeding and harvesting much easier.
ga: Mɔ ni duɔ nii lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ kɛ be baa shi yɛ be mli ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ he ko ni mli kwɔ kɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɛkɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ po haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why does my groundnut crop need soft, loose soil compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he hiaa mi-peanut tso lɛ kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: After flowering, groundnut plants send down stems called pegs into the soil where the nuts grow underground. Soft soil makes it easy for these pegs to penetrate and develop into full, healthy pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei tso lɛ wo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa ewaa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baabote mli ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni eye emuu.

english: Why are my groundnut seeds failing to sprout when I plant them deep in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnut seeds need oxygen and warmth near the soil surface to sprout. If buried too deep, the seedling burns all its stored energy before reaching sunlight and rots underground.
ga: Peanut dumɔwui he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ dɔlɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ shãa amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ dani hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is planting rice in straight rows better than broadcasting seeds by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni akɛ niji duɔ lɛ?

english: Row planting prevents overcrowding, ensures equal light for every plant, and makes it easy to walk through the field for weeding or using small farm machinery without damaging the rice.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akafee mɛi babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei fɛɛ ni amɛnáa la ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaatsɔ ŋmɔji amli koni ajie jwɛi loo akɛ tsɔnei atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔji bibii amli ni afiteee ŋmãa lɛ.

english: How does wet soil affect the way my seed planter works in the rice field?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ saa bɔ ni dumɔwui ashwãa tsɔne tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: If the soil is overly wet or muddy, mud will stick to the planter wheels and block the seed discharge tube. Soil should be moist enough to hold seed, but not sticky enough to clog the machine.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo eyɛ muji tsɔ Muji lɛ kpɛtɛɔ dumɔwui ashwiilii ahe ni etsĩɔ dumɔwui atsɔnei lɛ anaa. Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ dumɔwui lɛ. Shi jeee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baatsi tsɔne lɛ naa.

english: What should I keep in mind when using imported farm machinery on local Ghanaian soil?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ maha ehi mijwɛŋmɔ mli kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsɔnei ni akɛba maŋsɛɛ miitsu nii yɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Imported equipment is often designed for flat, soft fields. You must calibrate depth controls carefully to handle harder local soils and ensure local technicians can service the machine.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afee nibii ni akɛbaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Esa akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ akwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ha lɛ nɔ koni onyɛ okɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji ni wa babaoo lɛ atsu nii. ni amɛkwɛ koni maŋ lɛ mli ŋaalɔi lɛ anyɛ atsu tsɔnei lɛ ahe nii.

english: Why do some small planters work better for smallholder farms than large tractor-drawn equipment?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi bibii komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ okwaafoi aŋmɔji bibii amli fe tsɔnei wuji ni trakta gbalaa lɛ?

english: Small planters are affordable, lightweight, and easy to maneuver around stumps and uneven terrain common on small family farms without requiring fuel or heavy towing equipment.
ga: Nibii bibii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ jara waaa, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ he fɛɛ he lɛ waaa. Tsei akui kɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Enɛ ji nɔ ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ weku ŋmɔji bibii amli. ni fuɛl loo nibii ni tsii ni akɛgbalaa tsɔne lɛ he ehiaaa

english: Why are my crops coming up unevenly across the field after using a mechanical planter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ejaaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ beni mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Uneven crop growth happens when planter depth settings are loose or inconsistent. Seeds planted too deep germinate slowly, while shallow seeds dry out or get eaten by birds.
ga: Tso lɛ dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji akɛ dulɔ lɛ mlibotemɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli ejɔ loo ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. Dumɔwui ni adu mli tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. be mli ni dumɔwui ni mli ekɔɔɔ Ani ebaagbi loo okpoi baaye lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct sunshine dries out their delicate leaves and burns the surrounding soil. Leaving some larger shade trees or planting plantains alongside the young cocoa protects them from heat stress while they establish.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha ebaai bibii lɛ agbi ni ebaashã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa beni aduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoot suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: When too many suckers grow around the main plantain stem, they steal food and water from the parent plant. Pruning away the extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, which allows the main tree to produce much bigger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ plantain tsei ni dara ni tsii waa.

english: Yam vines need sunlight on all their leaves to manufacture energy for the tuber growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground where they could rot or catch diseases, allowing maximum sunlight to reach the leaves so the tubers grow large.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akadamɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo hela aba amɛnɔ. Ha hulu la babaoo ashɛ baai lɛ ahe bɔ ni aaanyɛ koni eha bulb lɛ afee wuji.

english: Why are my cassava tubers soft and rotting underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when water sits around their roots for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away from the root tubers, keeping them dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs for green growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the maize the nutrients it needs to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ŋmãa lɛ adara. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by hot weather, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist and avoiding excessive heavy fertilizers helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up into tight tubes during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, helping the plant conserve water during the hottest part of the day. Providing shade or adequate watering at the root level early in the morning helps reduce leaf curling.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ha yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe leebi lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests if I plant maize on the same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly consumes the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and encourages crop-specific pests to live in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Esa akɛ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni ewo tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it important for me to remove weeds while my crops are still small seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji dumɔwui bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have small roots and easily lose the fight against fast-growing weeds for water, light, and soil nutrients. Removing weeds early ensures the young crops get all the food they need to build strong stems.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ oya koni amɛná nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei bibii lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: How do I know it is safe to sow my seeds after the first rain of the season arrives?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ eba lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Sowing immediately after the very first rain is risky because the ground might dry out if the rains stop for a few weeks. It is best to wait until two or three steady rains have thoroughly soaked the soil before putting seeds in the ground.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ enyɔ loo etɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani okɛ dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.
