english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and dry out easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the essential shade and cool moisture young cocoa needs during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha kookoo bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it good for my land if I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize on the same farm?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa fata ŋmãa he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting beans or cowpeas with maize helps the land. Legumes take nitrogen naturally from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the maize and reduces how much fertilizer you need to buy.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ. Legumes lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni ehaa ŋmãa ni esa akɛ ohe lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I buy fresh seeds from the agro-dealer instead of just planting the maize grains I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Seeds saved from modern high-yielding crops lose their vigor in the next generation. Planting saved seeds usually produces weaker stalks and smaller cobs, whereas fresh certified seeds guarantee strong, uniform growth and high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ haa hewalɛ, dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ yibii babaoo baa.

english: Why do my crops grow very well right after I clear fresh bush, but yield less when I plant on the same land the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ beni mijie jwɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ? Shi ewooo yibii babaoo beni midu yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Clearing fresh bush leaves behind a rich layer of organic matter that feeds the first crop. Once that initial plant food is used up by the harvest, the soil loses its natural fertility unless you replenish it with manure, compost, or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ sũ tsei lɛ, ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni haa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Beni shishijee tso niyenii lɛ etee yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ebɔɔ su mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: Why do my vegetable beds stay moist longer when I cover the soil with dry grass or palm fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable bed lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves creates a protective barrier called mulch. This barrier shields the soil from the hot sun, stopping water from evaporating quickly so root systems stay cool and damp.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ gbɛtsii nii nɛɛ baabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya Koni shishifã lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ

english: Why does dried chicken manure make my crops stay green longer than chemical fertilizer alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ haa mi tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ fe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli pɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer gives plants a fast boost of nutrients that can quickly wash away in heavy rain. Chicken manure improves the actual structure of the soil and releases nutrients slowly over a long time.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya, ni ebaanyɛ efo oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ haa bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fiofio yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by tiny insects called whiteflies that spread a plant disease, or because the cassava is dropping leaves to save water during long dry spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii kɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly ni gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa lɛ. Aloo akɛni ŋmei miijie baai lɛ koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do extension officers ask me to cut off the bottom leaves and stems of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔ lɛ bi mi akɛ mafo mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ?

english: Removing the lower leaves keeps them from touching the wet soil where fungal diseases live. It also lets air flow freely around the plant base and directs energy into growing bigger tomato fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shishigbɛ baai lɛ, no haaa amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hu bɔleɔ ehe. tso shishitoo ni ehaa hewalɛ kɛha tomatoi wuji akwɛmɔ

english: Why is it important for me to sow my maize right after the first major rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Early planting allows crop roots to catch the initial natural burst of nutrients in wet soil and ensures the maize flowers and forms grains before the rains stop early.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi ni amɛnáa adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui dani nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ oya.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or get full of insects when I put it into sacks right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ efite loo eyi kɛ ŋmeii beni mikɛwoɔ kotokui amli beni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize holds high moisture inside the grains. If you do not dry the cobs thoroughly in the sun before bagging, trapped moisture causes mold to grow and invites weevils to eat the grain.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbiko dani okɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, Trapped moisture haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ ni efɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ nine koni amɛye dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon when the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun. This helps the plant trap moisture and stop water from evaporating too quickly during dry or hot periods.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni hulu la ni baa baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off without turning into fruit during this dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai yɛ nɛkɛ hɔmɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water, they experience heat stress and drop their flowers to save energy and moisture for their own survival instead of spending it on fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Amɛkɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kpeɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite yɛ aduawai ahe lɛ

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from lack of rain or if they have caught a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii miigboi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ loo hela hewɔ?

english: Drought stress usually causes whole sections of a farm to wilt evenly during hot afternoons and slightly revive at night, whereas plant diseases usually start on individual plants with spots, color changes, or rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ he haomɔ haa ŋmɔji muu fɛɛ shwieɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ. amɛfeɔ ekome yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni amɛhe jɔ fioo gbɛkɛ lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛhe su tsakeɔ, loo amɛfiteɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: If the rains fail and I carry water from a nearby dam or river, can I use it directly on my vegetable crops?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ni mijie nu kɛjɛ faa loo faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu atsu nii yɛ aduawai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, dam or river water is safe for crops, but it is best poured directly onto the soil near the root area rather than splashed on the leaves, which can spread fungal diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni yɔɔ faai loo faai amli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi esa akɛ afɔse ashwie shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ he ni shishifã lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofɔse yɛ baai ni baanyɛ agbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ashwã lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why do crops planted right at the water's edge near a river or pond sometimes turn yellow and stunt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei ni adu yɛ faai loo ŋshɔi ahe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen to breathe just like they need water. Soil that is completely waterlogged drowns the roots, stopping them from absorbing nutrients and turning the leaves yellow.
ga: Tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haaa amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How often should I water my crops manually from a nearby water body to keep them healthy?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ miniji afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu kɛjɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: It is better to water crops deeply two or three times a week so the moisture goes deep into the root zone, rather than watering lightly every day, which quickly evaporates in the heat.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tso lɛ nu shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli koni nu lɛ abote shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, mo ha lɛ nu blɛuu daa ligbi, nɛ lɔ ɔ maa tsɔ oya ngɛ la mi tso ɔ mi.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crop roots with dry grass or palm leaves help them during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, shields the ground from direct hot sunlight. This keeps the soil cool and stops soil moisture from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: How does poor rainfall affect the way underground crops like cassava and yams grow?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ saa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ŋmei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Without enough moisture in the soil, root and tuber crops cannot produce enough food in their leaves, which leads to small, thin tubers that yield very little harvest.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: The first rain is often a 'false rain' followed by a long dry period. If young seeds sprout and the soil immediately dries out, the delicate seedlings will die before the true rainy season sets in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘amale nugbɔ’ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui bibii kwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aba.

english: Which food crops can I plant that will still grow well if the rainy season turns out to be short this year?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii abaanyɛ adu ni amɛshwere lolo kɛji akɛ afee nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kuku yɛ afi nɛɛ mli?

english: Short-duration crops like cowpeas, early-maturing maize, millet, or sweet potatoes require less water overall and can be harvested quickly before the water supply runs out.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ tsina ŋmãa, ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ biɔ nu fioo yɛ fɛɛ mli ni abaanyɛ akpa oya dani nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baaho.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil is rich enough to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Dark, loose soil that holds moisture well without becoming waterlogged and has plenty of earthworms usually indicates rich, fertile land suitable for healthy crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli, ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii, ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ adumɔ.

english: Why does my land produce less food when I plant the exact same crop on it year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo yɛ be mli ni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that prefer that crop to build up in the field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ tsei ni miida lɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why are my mangoes not as sweet as the ones sold in the city markets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔ mangoi lɛ ŋɔɔɔɔ tamɔ mangoi ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ?

english: Mangoes become sweeter when the tree receives plenty of direct sunlight, proper potassium nutrients during fruiting, and the fruits are allowed to mature fully on the tree before harvesting.
ga: Mango lɛ ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ hulu la kpɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Na potassium niyenii ni sa yɛ yibiiwoo be mli. Ni aŋmɛɔ yibii lɛ gbɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpaa.

english: What makes my harvested fruits good enough to sell to buyers who ship produce overseas?
ga: Mɛni haa mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ maha mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni amɛkpaa lɛ kɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Export buyers look for clean, undamaged fruits of uniform size and shape that are free from insect bites, diseases, and chemical residues.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nibii kɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ taoɔ aduawai ni he tse ni efiteee. Ha elɛɛmɔ kɛ ehiɛ su ni yaa nɔ daa Ehe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ, helai kɛ tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell the right time to pick my fruit so it ripens properly after harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa aduawai koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nikpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Fruit is ready for harvesting when the shoulders around the stem swell up, the skin color begins shifting from dark green to light green or yellow, and the flesh inside turns yellowish.
ga: Yibii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni tsitsi ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ efuu. Hewolo nɔ su jeɔ shishi etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛyaa eŋɔli ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ nɔ. ni loo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do crops planted under big shady trees grow tall and thin without producing much yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ kwɔlɔ kɛ kuku shi amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make their own food; without enough light, they stretch upward searching for sun instead of spending energy to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii. Kɛji la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛtao hulu lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water fills the tiny air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots so they cannot absorb essential nutrients like nitrogen, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛhe niyenii ni he hia tamɔ nitrogen, ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my fruit trees drop off before turning into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off prematurely due to dry spells, a lack of essential nutrients like phosphorus and boron, pest attacks, or extreme heat during the blooming stage.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ boron ni bɛ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Why are worms getting inside my fruit while it is still growing on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii boteɔ mi yibii lɛ amli be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Fruit flies lay tiny eggs under the skin of young fruits, which hatch into maggots that feed on the soft flesh as the fruit ripens.
ga: Yibii amli ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Yɛ tso yibii bibii lɛ ahewolo shishi Ni baatsɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ loo ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji tso yibii lɛ ekwɛ.

english: How do fertilizers help my crops grow bigger and yield better food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo niyenii kpakpa?

english: Fertilizers supply essential plant food—such as nitrogen for leafy growth, phosphorus for strong roots, and potassium for sweet, heavy fruits—that the soil may be lacking.
ga: Nyɔŋtsere ji tso niyenii ni he hia jɛɛhe, tamɔ nitrogen kɛha baai adalɛ. Fosfɔs kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ potassium kɛha aduawai ni ŋɔɔ ni tsii. ni ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. They need shade from bigger trees or plantains to protect their tender leaves from drying out until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli baawo mli bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tips even though it has been raining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ yitsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow fast. Adding nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall and thin with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko.

english: Why do my cassava roots start spoiling just a few days after I harvest them from the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a hard protective skin like yams, so once dug up, air enters them quickly and causes internal rot within two to three days unless they are processed or eaten.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ atsa shikpɔŋ lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli oya ni ekɛ mligbɛ fitemɔ baa yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. ja atsu he nii loo aye

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight for their leaves. More sunlight on the leaves helps the plant make food, which makes the yam tubers underground grow much bigger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha amɛbaa lɛ. Hulu la babaoo ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shwereɔ babaoo.

english: Why do flowers fall off my tomato plants without producing any tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni tomato yibii ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough water. Heat stress stops the flowers from forming seeds, so no fruit can grow.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai ko nyɛŋ akwɛ̃.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juice from young leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I remove some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Too many shoots around one plantain stem fight with each other for water and nutrients. Removing the extra ones leaves just one or two strong suckers, which produces bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni ebɔle plantain tso kome he lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ojie nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. ni haa plantain tsei wuji baa

english: Why shouldn't I put fertilizer right next to the stem of my crop when applying it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ?

english: Putting chemical fertilizer directly against the plant stem can burn the delicate stem and roots. It is better to place it a few centimeters away in a ring so the roots reach for it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ amɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ amɛhe shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does rice grow so well when there is standing water on the field while other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ be mli ni nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal tubes in their stems that allow air to reach their roots underwater, while the standing water prevents weeds from growing and competing with the crop.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ mligbɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ nu shishi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Why are my young coconut trees taking so many years to produce their first fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ?

english: Coconut trees take time to mature depending on the variety; dwarf varieties usually produce in 3 to 5 years, while traditional tall varieties take 7 to 10 years. Good soil nutrients, adequate rainfall, and full sunlight speed up this growth process.
ga: Kokoo tsei heɔ be dani amɛdaraa, ni enɛ damɔ bɔ ni amɛji srɔtoi lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ji dwarf lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 7 kɛyashi 10. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa Kɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo baaye abua ni nɛkɛ dalɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my coconut trees turn yellow and droop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often indicate water stress or a lack of key soil nutrients like potassium and nitrogen. During dry spells, the tree drops older leaves to save water and keep its center growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu mli haomɔ loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei shiɔ baai momoi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ada.

english: Why do my coconut trees produce very small nuts when I plant them close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ahiɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When coconut trees are planted too close, their leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots fight for the same soil nutrients and groundwater. Spacing them properly allows every tree to get enough light and food to produce large nuts.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tso ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ amli lɛ naa. Ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei fɛɛ naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: What will happen to my crops if I irrigate them with muddy water from a river polluted by gold mining?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ faa ko ni shika tsuru ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ efite lɛ mli lɛ shwie amɛnɔ?

english: Water contaminated by galamsey operations contains heavy metals like mercury and heavy mud that choke roots, poison the soil, stop crops from absorbing food, and make any harvested food unsafe to eat.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ Galamsey nitsumɔhei lɛ mli lɛ yɛ dade ni tsii tamɔ mercury kɛ muji ni tsii ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa. Poison ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Haaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akaŋɔ niyenii ni ehaa niyenii ni akpa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Why is it so difficult for crops to grow on farm land where people have previously dug for gold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ abaadu nii yɛ okwaayeli shikpɔji ni be ko ni eho lɛ gbɔmɛi tsaa shika tsuru yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mining strips away the rich topsoil where plant nutrients live and leaves behind compacted subsoil or poisonous chemicals, making it hard for roots to spread or absorb water and minerals.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsaa lɛ jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni tsei ahe nibii yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni eshiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ ni mli edɔ loo tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni eshiɔ yɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaajara loo amɛŋɔ nu kɛ shika tsuru.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and rot when water sits flooded on my land for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu afua nui ba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water covers the roots for days, it cuts off oxygen, causing root rot, which leaves the plant unable to take in food, leading to yellowing and death.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha shishifãi lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo Ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii. Ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ gbele baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops burning and turning brown along the boundary near polluted water runoff?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shãa ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa he ni bɛŋkɛ nu fɔŋ ni hoɔ lɛ?

english: Polluted chemical runoff carries high levels of salts and toxic metals that get sucked up by plant roots, causing leaf scorch where the edges dry out and turn brown.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛ dade ni tsei shishifãi lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ fa babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ shãa yɛ amɛshishigbɛ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Can I plant crops like cassava or maize between my young coconut trees without harming them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ ni miyeee amɛ awui?

english: Yes, intercropping is safe while coconut trees are young as long as you leave a wide ring around each tree trunk so the food crops do not steal fertilizer or crowd out the coconut roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni ŋmei tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ. Shii abɔ ni obaashi kooloo ni mli kwɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishifã Enɛ ji koni niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ akaju ŋmɔshi nibii loo akawo ŋmei shishifãi amli.

english: Why do my crops grow greener and stronger when I leave cleared weeds to decompose on the soil around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waɔ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ koni amɛgbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Decomposing weeds act as organic mulch, keeping the soil cool and moist while slowly breaking down into natural plant nutrients that feed the crop roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tso mli niyenii ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do pests like beetles attack my weak coconut trees more than the healthy ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ladybugs lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ fe mi ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Insects can detect when a plant is weak from bad soil or poor watering. Healthy, well-nourished trees produce strong natural chemical defenses that keep pests from damaging them easily.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ ana be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo nu ni ehiii hewɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni mli wa ni tsiɔ tsofai anaa. Enɛ haaa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ akpata amɛhiɛ mlɛo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moist climate it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing starting from the tips of lower leaves usually means the soil is lacking nitrogen. Maize requires lots of nitrogen to stay green and produce full ears, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ toi ni eyi obɔ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do I need to clear tall trees and push wooden stakes into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei kakadaji ni matsɔ tsei ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants store energy in underground tubers by capturing sunlight through their leaves. Lifting the vines up onto stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight while preventing soil-borne fungal diseases from destroying the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛnaa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛtee tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa koni ekafite baai lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Will planting cowpeas or beans on my land make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop season ends and the roots rot, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is making the leaves on my pepper bushes curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding on the sap under the leaf. Spraying appropriate insecticides or soapy water early keeps these insects from stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo nu ni akɛ saamɔ ewo mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni kooloi nɛɛ akafee tsei lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot when heavy rain sits on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits continuously on the field without draining away, oxygen gets cut off, allowing rotting fungi to attack and destroy the underground tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Afoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant my rice seeds in straight rows instead of scattering them by hand across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni akɛ nine aaatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures every rice plant gets an equal share of space, light, and nutrients. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much faster and easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei fɛɛ naa he ko, la kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, kɛ nikpamɔ hu yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do groundnut flowers grow downward and bend into the dirt after they open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts bloom above ground, but the actual nuts grow underground. After the flower is pollinated, it forms a stalk called a peg that pushes itself down into the warm soil where the pod can safely mature.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi nuts diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollin sɛɛ lɛ Efeɔ tso ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ ada shweshweeshwe yɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know which part of a mature cassava stem is best to cut and plant for new crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso ni eda lɛ fãi ni esa akɛ afo ni adu kɛha dumɔwui heei?

english: The best cuttings come from the hard, woody middle section of a healthy stem. The top soft green part rots too quickly, and the very bottom base is often too woody and slow to sprout.
ga: Nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni afolɔ lɛ jɛɔ tso ni mli wa ni yɔɔ tso mli lɛ teŋgbɛ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya tsɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ lɛ ji tso tsɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ mlɛo.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying healthy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure gives the plant the nourishment it needs to turn green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer near the roots of my crop instead of broadcasting it over the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ moŋ fe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Plants drink water and take up food through their roots, not their leaves. Placing fertilizer near the roots allows soil moisture to dissolve the nutrients so the roots can soak them up directly without risking burning the leaves.
ga: Tsei nuɔ nu ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ, shi jeee kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa sũ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni oshara ko bɛ he akɛ baai lɛ baashã.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out very small when I plant the stem cuttings close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa lɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close, their roots fight each other underground for limited nutrients, water, and growing room. Proper spacing ensures each root has enough space and soil nutrients to swell into large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii ni fa fioo, nu kɛ he ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it important for me to plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ emasɛi? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that scorch under strong sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural shade umbrellas, protecting young cocoa trees from extreme heat and preserving soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shade. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds get full of small holes after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani eyi obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛto lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Tiny insects called seed weevils lay eggs in the stored beans, and the larvae eat their way out from the inside. Thoroughly drying your seeds and storing them in airtight containers deprives the insects of oxygen and stops them from damaging your crop.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ kɔfi yibii ni akɛto mli lɛ amli. ni ŋmeii lɛ baaye nii kɛjɛ mligbɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, ni ebaaha amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛnáa hegbɛ amɛkpaa lɛ?

english: Underground yam rot is often caused by water staying trapped in the soil, which creates a breeding ground for fungi and bacteria that attack the tuber. Planting on raised mounds allows excess water to drain away, keeping the yams healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni etsi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato fitemɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ mli wa

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without producing any peppers during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the pepper plant, forcing it to shed its flowers to save water and stay alive. Providing light shade and maintaining consistent soil watering helps the plant hold onto its flowers so peppers can develop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛshwie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse haa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them survive the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyeɔ Harmattan hɔmɔ lɛ nɔ kunim lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, which shields the ground from the hot sun and dry winds. This shield slows down water evaporation from the soil, keeping moisture near the roots so your plants stay hydrated longer.
ga: Hay tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch, ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he. Nɛkɛ tsɔne nɛɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oooha ebɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism where the tomato plant rolls its leaves to shrink the surface exposed to the hot sun, preventing rapid water loss. The leaves usually uncurl once temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Baai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he ni tomato tsei tsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ afee bibioo. Bɔni afee ni nu akafite oya lɛ Baai lɛ fɔɔ shwiemɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when heavy rains and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not anchor deeply into the soil. When heavy rains soften the earth and winds push against the heavy bunch of fruit, the shallow roots can pull free, which is why propping up heavy trees with wooden stakes prevents them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ ni tsei ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkagbee shi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to make green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea will help the plants turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people tell me not to plant maize on the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko miikɛɛ mi akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt and allows pests to build up in the soil. Swapping maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts free nitrogen back into the soil and keeps the land healthy.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ebaafite niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmãa baatsake ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Enɛ baaha nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the trees before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal sickness that thrives in damp, dark environments. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight reach the trees and clearing weeds around the base helps keep the pods dry and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni duŋ ewo mli. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ he, ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Kɔnii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛkpaa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice out of young leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Spraying the plants with neem seed extract or safe insecticides will keep these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air is too hot or when the plant gets stressed from dry soil. Watering your plants regularly around the base and putting dry leaves around them keeps the roots cool and helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe daa ni akɛ baai ni egbi fɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ he Tso lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs lots of sunshine on its leaves to manufacture food for the heavy tubers underground. Lifting the vines onto stakes exposes the leaves to maximum sunlight and keeps them off the wet ground where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni shwereɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. ni etsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ, ni no ji helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ jɛɛhe

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are ready to be dug up from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off. You can test by carefully digging around one plant to check if the tubers are large enough before harvesting the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa ni ooofee jogbaŋŋ kɛbɔle he lɛ nɔ. Nitsumɔhe kome ni baakwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa dani akpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Which young shoots should I cut from my plantain tree to plant a new field?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei bibii esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ dumɔwu ko mli koni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: Choose 'sword suckers', which are young shoots with narrow, spear-shaped leaves and thick bases. These shoots have stronger energy to grow fast and produce large bunches compared to shoots that already have wide, flat leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘sword shoot’, ni ji tso bibioo ko ni baai lɛ mli tseee, ni tamɔ lance, ni eshishigbɛ lɛ mli tse. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni mli wa ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛfeɔ kui wuji. Kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ momo lɛ ahe.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning or in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo mawo amɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the soil is cool, allowing the plant roots to drink fully. Watering in the hot sun causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can take it up.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Anyɛɔ anuɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kwraa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket over the dirt. It blocks weeds from coming up, keeps the soil moist for longer periods, and stops the hot sun from burning the roots of your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and curling up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a living umbrella that shields the seedlings from the sun and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ haa shade ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the center instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost early in the plant's growth helps it regain a dark green color and yield healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha etoi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upwards and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or aphids transmitting viruses. Controlling these pests early using neem oil spray or suitable insecticides prevents leaf twisting and protects fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. Ni aaaye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ ni sa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ ashishi ni ebu aduawai ni baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their yellow flowers without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miishwie amɛfɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛduuu tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and feeding the soil helps the flowers set into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwie shi pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni akɛ niyenii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do some farmers plant beans together in the same field with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa feɔ ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which feeds the neighboring maize plants. Intercropping also covers the soil to suppress weeds and maximize land harvest.
ga: Beans mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli, he ni eyeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli lɛ hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ koni ekɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmaa babaoo aba.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my seeds when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received two to three steady, deep rains that soak thoroughly into the soil, rather than planting after the very first light shower which can leave seeds to dry out.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni naa wa ni baa shi shii 2-3 ni baatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, duɔ ngɛ hiɔmi kekleekle nɛ ɔ se, nɛ lɔ ɔ ma nyɛ ma ha nɛ duwu ɔmɛ nɛ a gbi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to make food. Staking raises the leaves off the ground, maximizing sunlight exposure and resulting in much larger tubers under the soil.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ akwɛ̃. Staking baaha baai lɛ awó amɛhe nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Na hulu la babaoo ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni dara babaoo

english: What is making small holes in my maize leaves and leaving brown, sawdust-like dirt inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Spraying an approved pesticide or neem solution directly into the central funnel of the plant early in the morning destroys the pest before it ruins the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaakpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava rots underground when water stays around the roots in heavy or poorly drained soil, encouraging fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away.
ga: Cassava fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nu ebɔle ehe. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni kanyaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my mature cocoa tree if I want it to yield more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji ni edara lɛ ekomɛi kɛji miisumɔ ni maná ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches, allowing sunlight and air to circulate through the tree canopy. This reduces humidity that causes black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce fresh flowers and pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔtɔi heei.

english: How do I calculate the size of my farm in hectares if I only measure in acres?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ he akɔntaa yɛ hectares mli kɛji akɛ akɛ acre pɛ susuɔ he?

english: One hectare is equal to roughly two and a half acres. Knowing your farm size in hectares helps you buy the exact amount of seed, fertilizer, and chemical spray you need without wasting money.
ga: Hectare kome kɛ aaafee acre enyɔ kɛ fã yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛji ole bɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ da ha yɛ hectares mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohé dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa bo ni okɛ shikatoohe lɛ efoŋ.

english: How many kilograms of harvested crop standardly fit into one large market bag in Ghana?
ga: Nibii ni akpaa lɛ kilogram enyiɛ baanyɛ awo jarayeli kotoku agbo ko mli yɛ Ghana?

english: In Ghana, a standard full bag or sack of dried produce like maize, grain, or cocoa is generally measured at 50 kilograms.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, kotoku loo kotoku ni akɛ nibii ni egbi, tamɔ ŋmãa, dumɔwui loo kookoo woɔ mli lɛ tsiimɔ ji kilogram 50.

english: How can I estimate how many 50kg bags of maize I will harvest from a field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa ni abaanyɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmãa kotoku kome ni tsiimɔ ji kilogram 50 mli lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: Harvest estimates depend on your soil and seed type, but a well-managed hectare of maize under good conditions usually yields between 40 to 60 standard 50kg bags.
ga: Nikpamɔ he akɔntaabuu damɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ dumɔwu henɔ nɔ. Shi ŋmãa ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛ kpakpa shishi lɛ baawo yibii ni ji 50kg kotokui ni ji 40 kɛyashi 60.

english: How much seed do I need to buy to cover a field of two and a half hectares?
ga: Dumɔwui enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mahe koni manyɛ matsu hectare enyɔ kɛ fã he nii?

english: For crops like maize, you generally need about 20 to 25 kilograms of seed per hectare, so a two and a half hectare field will require around 50 to 60 kilograms of seed.
ga: Kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui aaafee kilogram 20 kɛyashi 25 he miihia bo yɛ hectare kome mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji hectare enyɔ kɛ fã lɛ baabi aaafee dumɔwui kilogram 50 kɛyashi 60.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant the seeds too close together on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the plants compete with each other for light, water, and soil food. This makes the stems grow thin and weak, resulting in very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why does proper spacing between crop rows help reduce diseases on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei akui ateŋ lɛ haa helai baa shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving enough space between rows allows sunlight and wind to dry off wet leaves. Damp, crowded leaves create a warm environment where fungi and diseases thrive.
ga: Shi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi. Baai ni mli ewo muji, ni mli efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ mli dɔɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii kɛ helai shwereɔ yɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small when I plant them in overcrowded soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fe nine nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need space and loose soil to expand under the ground. Overcrowded fields limit space and nutrients, causing the plants to produce thin, woody roots instead of big tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia he ko kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Hei ni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ tsiɔ gbɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa. Ha tso lɛ aná shishifãi bibii. Yɛ yitso agbo najiaŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when there are no shade trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have sensitive leaves that cannot tolerate direct intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains provides temporary shade to protect the young trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crop turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant is short on nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing tall and bushy but forming very few grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when there is too much nitrogen early on but a lack of essential nutrients or water during the flowering stage, preventing proper cob development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa tsɔ yɛ shishijee mli. Shi niyenii ni he hiaa loo nu bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haaa ŋmei lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy growth, and when there is not enough, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed the younger growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ. Ni kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: What will happen to my maize harvest if I plant my seeds very close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the maize plants are forced to steal light, water, and soil nutrients from each other. This results in tall, thin, weak stalks that produce very small cobs or no corn ears at all.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, anyɛɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii waa loo amɛbɛ toi kwraa.

english: What is eating ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown powder in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ekumɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that hides in the central funnel of the plant. The brown powder is the pest's waste, and if it is not controlled early with proper pesticides or biological controls, it destroys the growing heart of the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Brown powder ji nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai shwieɔ shi. Ni kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ mra kɛ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. Ebaakpata tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a cleared open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight because it burns their soft leaves and dries out their roots quickly. They need shade crops like plantains or fast-growing trees around them for the first two to three years to keep them cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Enɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ ashã ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei krokomɛi ni daa oya ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ loo etɛ lɛ koni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil remains flooded or waterlogged for too long without proper drainage. The excessive water starves the roots of oxygen and creates a breeding ground for fungi that decompose the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nu babaoo baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. ni efee he ko ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the wet ground towards the sun so they can catch maximum light to make food. Leaving vines on the soil increases leaf diseases from damp soil and lowers the total yield of large tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potatoes kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he koni amɛná la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛkɛhoo nii. Wein tso lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa helai ni jɛɔ sũ ni mli edɔ mli baa lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni eha ŋmeii wuji ni anáa lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot, dry, or when there is sudden heavy rain. Extreme heat damages the flower's pollen, making it impossible for the plant to produce fruit, so it drops the unfertilized flower to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, edɔ tsɔ, loo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, ajieɔ fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ koni akɛto hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. As these pests feed on the leaves, they deform the tissue and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, thrips, loo mites, loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baai lɛ. Tissue lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why should I remove some of the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: If too many sucker shoots grow around one plantain stem, they compete with the main tree for nutrients and water. Pruning them down to leave just the main bearing tree, one medium sucker, and one small sucker ensures you get large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Amɛkɛ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ mli koni eshi tso titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ pɛ, tso lɛ shishifã kome ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ, kɛ tso lɛ shishifã bibioo kome lɛ, ebaaha oná plantain tso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yield even if my farm gets plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal the fertilizers and minerals from the soil before your crop roots can reach them. They also overcrowd your plants and can harbor pests and diseases that damage your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shika tsuru kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Amɛhaa otsei lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ ahe jɛɛhe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying the right fertilizer or compost will help restore their green color and improve yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and crisp when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily dry out. They need shade from plants like plantains or fast-growing shade trees to protect their leaves until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo tsei krokomɛi ni daa oya lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving tiny dark droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that burrows into the center of the maize plant. Spraying approved insecticides early in the morning or late evening when the worms are active helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni shwieɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ miitsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites that spread plant viruses. Using recommended sprays or neem oil mixtures helps eliminate the insects before they destroy the whole plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo neem fɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi bibii lɛ dani amɛkpãtã tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when heavy rains fall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Excess water staying around cassava roots prevents air from reaching them, causing rot fungi to attack the tubers. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away quickly.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle Kasa shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ kasa shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I harvest more food from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani minyɛŋ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients, resulting in weak plants and tiny harvests. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to feed and produce big fruits.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ewoɔ aduawai wuji.

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm; their roots steal fertilizer and water from the soil faster than your crops can take them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the same nutrients from the soil and lets pests built up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts helps restore soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures become too hot, water supply is irregular, or bees are not visiting to pollinate them. Consistent watering and mulching around the roots helps keep the soil moist and reduces heat stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. Aloo ŋmeii lɛ ebaaa koni amɛbafee pollination. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo he haomɔ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ oŋɔ tso kakadaŋŋ? Ba ni okɛ hama atswa sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni okwɔ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight powers the leaves to make food, which then flows down to build large, heavy tubers under the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la haa baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efoɔ kɛbaa shi ni efeɔ ŋmei agbo ko ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting flooded with water. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How does covering my farm soil with dry leaves help my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egboi wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground, prevents weeds from growing, and breaks down over time to enrich the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the plant, or by a virus carried by those insects. Controlling these pests early helps the plant produce normal, healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ hiɛ lɛ mli Kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai ni sa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my tomatoes have black, rotten spots on the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ?

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, happen when the plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences uneven watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent and adding agricultural lime helps fix this problem.
ga: Nibii diji ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ okwaayeli mli ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or insect attacks from pests like capsids. Providing adequate shade, nutrition, and pest protection helps the trees hold onto their flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ adɛŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo, niyenii, kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe lɛ haa tso lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How can I prevent my plantain trees from falling over when the wind blows hard?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi plantain lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa waa?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and heavy fruit stalks, making them easily blown over by strong winds. Supporting the main stem with strong bamboo or wooden props prevents the tree from breaking or uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa bo kɛbɔle he. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the soil before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in the ground when water sits in the soil for too long without proper drainage. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and growing soft in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ni edaa blɛoo kɛ́ akɛto lɛ?

english: Stored yams sprout and lose weight when kept in warm, bright, or damp conditions. Storing tubers in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded yam barn slows down sprouting and keeps the tubers firm longer.
ga: Atomɔ ni akɛto lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ebaagbɔjɔ kɛji akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni kpɛɔ, loo fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baato ŋmeii atoohe ko ni mli ejɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulutsoo baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ fioo ni eye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist and the crop is actively growing, usually a few weeks after germination. Applying fertilizer during heavy rain washes it away, while applying it during a severe dry spell can burn the roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaafɔ ehe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Why do I need to leave space between my maize plants instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough nutrients and light to produce large, healthy ears of corn.
