ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmãa toi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do people plant plantains right next to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tso bibioo?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and can easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when the soil has too much water, preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔii dani pepper lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or when given too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant grow leaves instead of keeping its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛhao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo beni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa baai yɛ fɔfɔi ni ehiɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like stone a few days after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛsaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like rotted leaves or animal manure. Adding compost helps break up heavy soil so roots can stretch easily and water can soak in deeper.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai ni egboi loo kooloi afɔfɔi bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni egbɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni nu lɛ abote mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable farm in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil can absorb the moisture before the sun gets too hot. Afternoon water evaporates into the air quickly before the roots get a chance to drink.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Nu ni yɔɔ shwane mli lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ naa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I clear the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie sleeping in the soil for years. Clearing the ground lets sunlight reach those seeds, waking them up to sprout rapidly before your planted crops have a chance to shade them out.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni asaa lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nakai dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Ewoɔ dumɔwui hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛha amɛhe.

english: How do worms get inside my maize stems and ruin the crops?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii boteɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Moths lay tiny eggs on the maize leaves. When the eggs hatch into caterpillars, they bore straight into the soft center of the stem to feed where rain and chemical sprays cannot easily reach them.
ga: Kplukai woɔ wui bibii yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ. Kɛ́ wuji lɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛbatsɔmɔɔ ŋmeii. Amɛfoɔ bu yɛ tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye nii yɛ hei ni nugbɔ kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aya jɛmɛ oya lɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent plants to yield high harvests. If you save seeds from that harvest, the new plants will be weak and produce much smaller yields than the original hybrid seed.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei heei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in heavy soil around the roots for too long. Excessive standing water drowns the roots and allows underground fungal diseases to attack and spoil them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bote shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. shishifãi be kakadaŋŋ Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ atutua amɛ ni amɛha amɛgboi.

english: Can I plant pawpaw together with my main crops on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu papaya kɛfata miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, pawpaw grows well alongside other crops, but it is best to keep things simple by planting only pawpaw as your companion crop so it does not compete heavily for nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, Paw Paw daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe. Shi ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nibii afee mlɛo kɛtsɔ paw paws ni ooodu tamɔ bɔ ni ohefatalɔ lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni akaye akaŋ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo he

english: Is it better to plant many different crops together or just stick to one secondary crop like pawpaw?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooodu tsei babaoo yɛ he kome loo ooodu tso ni ji enyɔ tamɔ pawpaw fɔfɔi kɛkɛ moŋ?

english: Planting just one companion crop like pawpaw alongside your main crop makes field management easier and prevents crops from choking each other out.
ga: Tso kome ni fata he, tamɔ paw-paw, ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ afee mlɛo. ni etsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkakpɛtɛ amɛhe

english: Why do some farm advisors recommend planting pawpaw alongside other crops instead of larger trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ŋaawolɔi komɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu pawpaw yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe moŋ fe tsei wuji lɛ?

english: Pawpaw trees grow straight up and have light foliage, meaning they provide good yield without blocking too much sunlight from reaching nearby plants.
ga: Pawpaw tsei lɛ daa ni amɛhiɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ abaawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni atsĩii hulu la babaoo naa koni ekashɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Can I plant new young seedlings in a field where older, mature crops are already growing?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni etsɛ ni eda babaoo yɔɔ mli momo lɛ mli?

english: Yes, both young and mature plants can grow well together on the same plot if you give them enough space so the older plants do not block light or water from the younger ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei bibii kɛ tsei wuji fɛɛ baanyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛji oha lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa Enɛ ji koni tsei ni edara lɛ akatsi la loo nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: How do older, bigger plants affect the growth of younger seedlings planted near them?
ga: Te tsei ni edara kɛ nɔ ni dara lɛ saa dumɔwui bibii ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Older plants can offer helpful protection and shade, but if planted too close, their large roots and leaves can take away water and sunlight from the younger seedlings.
ga: Tsei ni edara lɛ baanyɛ aha hebuu kɛ hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi wuji kɛ amɛbaai lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ amli.

english: How can I ensure both my older crops and younger crops thrive together on the same plot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mitsei wuji kɛ bibii lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ saatso kome nɔ?

english: You can ensure both grow well by maintaining proper spacing and ensuring the younger plants receive sufficient water and sunlight away from the heavy shade of older crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ koni amɛ fɛɛ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni sa ni oooha tsei bibii lɛ aná nu kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ tsei ni edara lɛ ashishifã ni mli edɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my pawpaw crop take so long to show growth after I put the seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pawpaw tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani edaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw plants spend their early weeks building a strong root system underground before you see noticeable growth above the soil.
ga: Pawpaw tsei yeɔ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Koni afee shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli wa Dani obaanyɛ ona dalɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops take a long time to show signs of improvement after I apply fertilizer or water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjieɔ hiɛyaa he okadii akpo beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu wo midɛŋ lɛ?

english: Plants absorb nutrients gradually through their roots, so it often takes several weeks before you see visible changes like new leaves or thicker stems.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ fiofio. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, eheɔ otsii babaoo dani onaa tsakemɔi ni anaa, tamɔ baai heei loo tsei ni mli tse.

english: What happens to small crops when I plant tall crops right next to them?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu tsei ni kwɔlɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi?

english: Tall crops will shade shorter crops; while some shade is good for young plants, too much shade can slow down their growth.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ baaha tsei ni yɔɔ kuku lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulutsoo be komɛi hi kɛha tsei bibii moŋ, Shi hulutsoo babaoo baanyɛ aha amɛdalɛ aba shi.

english: How much space should I leave between pawpaw plants so they do not crowd each other?
ga: Gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi yɛ mi-pawpaw tsei lɛ ateŋ koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe?

english: Spacing pawpaw plants about 2 to 3 meters apart gives both young and mature trees enough room to spread their leaves and absorb ground nutrients.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã pawpaw tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji aaafee mitai 2 kɛyashi 3, ni ehaa tsei bibii kɛ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwãa ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my land has good soil for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ kookoo?

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, rich in dark organic matter, and drains water easily without becoming waterlogged, allowing root systems to grow deep and absorb essential nutrients.
ga: Kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ. Eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ waa ni ehaa nu hoɔ oya ni ehaaa nu lɛ ahi shi Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn yellow in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight; they require temporary shade crops like plantains to protect them while their roots and leaves develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra branches and shoots growing on my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ Extra kɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Removing non-essential shoots prevents the tree from wasting water and food on useless leaves, directing energy and nutrients toward producing larger, healthier pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite nu kɛ niyenii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa anáa hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa anáa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady, and overly wet conditions when rain droplets splash spores onto the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ hei ni efɔ fe nine. Beni nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ spores nɔ yɛ pods lɛ anɔ

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná he ko babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting trees too closely causes them to compete for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which reduces total pod production and creates a damp environment where diseases spread quickly.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haaa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Enɛ haa pod ni afeɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi. ni eha shihilɛ ko ni mli edɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Flower drop happens when the tree experiences stress from dry weather, poor soil nutrition, or a lack of beneficial insects like tiny midges that pollinate the flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni bɛ, tamɔ kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava in the same field right next to my young cocoa plants?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Cassava grows very aggressive root systems that steal nutrients and water from young cocoa trees, so lighter crops like plantain or cocoyam are better choices for temporary shade.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa mli. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni ajuɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni hiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ plantains loo cocoa ji tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be kukuoo mli hulutsoo.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are yellowing because of weak soil or bad weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii hewɔ?

english: If leaves turn yellow uniformly across the field despite having rain, the soil is usually lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, meaning fertilizer or organic manure is needed.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo humus he miihia.

english: Cocoa pods are mature and ready for harvesting when their outer skin fully changes color, usually turning from green or dark red to a bright yellow or orange.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ eda kwraa ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛkponɔgbɛ lɛ etsake su kwraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops whenever the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baaje shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to absorb water and surface nutrients quicker than cultivated crops, which is why early clearing is necessary to keep them from choking your farm.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni otsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsi oŋmɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are my crops turning yellow and wilting even though I water them regularly from the nearby river?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu shwieɔ amɛ nɔ daa kɛjɛɔ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Muddy or chemical-polluted water from upstream dumping clogs soil pores and harms crop roots, preventing plants from absorbing nutrients even when the ground feels wet.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji loo tsofai ni fiteɔ nii kɛjɛɔ faa lɛ hiɛ lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ anaa ni eyeɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ awui. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ po.

english: What happens to my vegetable roots when I irrigate them with thick, muddy river water instead of clean water?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-vegetables shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ faa mli nu ni mli edɔ ni mli ewo muji wo amɛmli yɛ nu ni mli tse najiaŋ?

english: Heavy mud and silt coat the delicate root tips and form a hard crust on the soil surface, suffocating the roots so they cannot breathe or absorb essential minerals.
ga: Mu kɛ sũ ni tsii haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛhe mineral ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Will using dirty water full of waste and runoff lower my tomato harvests?
ga: Ani nu ni mli ewo muji kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaha mi-tomato yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, dirty water contains toxins and harmful bacteria that rot tomato roots and stunt fruit growth, resulting in smaller, diseased yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai fɔji kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni haa tomato shishifãi fiteɔ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ daraa fioo lɛ yɛ nu ni mli ewo muji mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni helai bɛ mli lɛ fioo.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering because of bad water quality rather than a lack of rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu ni ehiii hewɔ moŋ fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ?

english: If your crop leaves turn yellow, develop unusual spots, or drop off while the soil is still moist, the water source likely contains harmful chemicals or heavy silt damaging the roots.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛná he ko ni yɔɔ srɔto, loo amɛgbee shi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. Ekolɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo sũ ni tsii ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu jɛɛhe lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves get brown spots and stay small on land close to stream areas where mining activity happens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faa ko ni ajieɔ shika tsuru yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water and soil around mining sites often carry heavy metals and harsh chemicals that burn root tissues, stopping maize from taking up the food it needs to grow tall.
ga: nu kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ Bei pii lɛ, dade ni tsii kɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni shãa shishifãi lɛ yɛ Mine lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants die off so quickly when waste from nearby activities washes into my farm during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ gboiɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ jwɛi ni jɛɔ nifeemɔi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Vegetables like peppers have delicate roots that burn easily when exposed to chemical waste in runoff water, causing the plant to collapse rapidly.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ tsofai ni fiteɔ nii ni yɔɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo mli, ni no haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why are my cassava plants shedding their leaves early when grown near dirty water sources?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni nu jɛɛhe ni mli ewo muji yɔɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava roots absorb contaminated water, the plant experiences severe stress and drops its leaves to conserve energy and try to survive.
ga: Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ Tsei lɛ naa haomɔ ni naa wa ni amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛhi shi.

english: How can I keep my farm land healthy so my children can still grow good crops on it in the future?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ koni mibii lɛ anyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lolo wɔsɛɛ?

english: Protecting local streams from waste dumping and avoiding harmful land destruction preserves the natural life in the soil, keeping it fertile for generations to come.
ga: Akutso lɛ mli faai ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ jwɛi he kɛ shikpɔŋ hiɛkpatamɔ ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ he tsimɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni adebɔɔ mli wala ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii kɛhaa yinɔi babaoo ni baaba lɛ.

english: How does keeping the stream near my farm clean help my cocoa trees produce more pods every year?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mihaa ehe tseɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo daa afi?

english: Clean water feeds beneficial soil organisms that break down leaf litter into natural fertilizer, giving cocoa trees the steady nutrients they need for rich pod production over many years.
ga: Nu ni mli tse lɛ haa nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni gbálaa baai amli jwɛi lɛ mli kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ be fɛɛ be koni ekɛwo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli.

english: Why does leaving natural trees along the riverbanks near my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mishi adebɔɔ mli tsei yɛ faa lɛ naa ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Trees along riverbanks act as natural filters that trap mud, dirt, and chemical runoff before they reach your farmland, keeping groundwater safe and clean for your crop roots.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ faa lɛ naa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni shwieɔ muji, muji, kɛ tsofai ni hoɔ lɛ dani eshɛɔ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe ni ehe tseɔ kɛha otso lɛ shishifãi.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil. Planting food crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and preserves moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Niyenii nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose their flowers without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress, nutrient deficiency, or insect attacks from pests like mirids. Ensuring proper shading, soil fertilization, and pest management helps flowers develop into mature pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. niyenii ni esaaa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen, shading, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuamɔ. Ni kɛ́ akwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni eda.

english: Why is it necessary for me to cut off extra shoots and branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii kɛ amɛniji krokomɛi?

english: Pruning removes non-producing branches so air and sunlight can circulate through the tree. This reduces humidity that causes black pod disease and directs the tree's energy toward making large, healthy pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni wooo yibii lɛ ajieɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow even though it is raining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen fertilizer. While rain supplies water, plants still need proper nutrients in the soil to stay green and build big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ lɛ haa nu moŋ, shi niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same piece of land three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, leading to poorer yields every year.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shishijee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi.

english: How do I know which direction to place cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava ŋmɔtɔi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems struggle to sprout and root growth underground will be poor.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu lɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ Ewa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ hu baafee nɔ ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden sticks to climb up as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb stakes so their leaves can spread out to catch sunlight, which powers the plant to build large tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off the wet ground to avoid rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over during heavy rains and winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains fall over because their root systems are shallow or damaged by pests like root nematodes and stem borers. Supporting fruiting trees with bamboo props and planting healthy suckers keeps them upright.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ loo nibii ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes kɛ stem borers lɛ ahewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ yibii amli kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading viruses. Using neem oil spray or insect traps helps stop these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo bug zapper ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akpa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my garden vegetables in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ mibɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water vegetables early in the morning so the plants absorb water before the sun gets hot. Watering in the afternoon heat causes water to evaporate rapidly and can scorch leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha o-vegetables lɛ nu leebi koni tsei lɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya ni ebaaha baai lɛ ashã.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and can wither easily. Fast-growing plantain trees provide necessary shade and maintain soil moisture, acting as a natural shelter for cocoa trees in their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi oya. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe kɛha cacao tsei lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my pepper crops too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, air, and nutrients, leading to thin stems and smaller fruits. Proper spacing gives each plant room to branch out and bear more vegetables.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ aduawai bibii. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ tsu fɛɛ tsu mli niji jeɔ kpo ni enine shɛɔ aduawai babaoo nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea at the right time helps restore green leaves and improves grain yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eha dumɔwui ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi loo ŋmei baai yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, stops water from drying up quickly under the sun, and prevents rain from washing away the fertile topsoil.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulu la shishi. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas in the same farm together with my maize crop?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is very beneficial because cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, naturally feeding the maize crop and improving soil quality without extra fertilizer costs.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ni okɛ ŋmãa kroko fataaa he.

english: Why don't the seeds I saved from my last hybrid harvest give me good yield like the initial ones I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ minaagbee hybrid kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiii tamɔ dumɔwui ni mihe klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds (F1) are specially produced to give high yields in the first planting season. If you save and plant seeds from that harvest, the offspring lose those strong traits, resulting in smaller yields and uneven plant growth.
ga: Afeɔ Hybrid (F1) dumɔwui lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ shweremɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛji ohere ni odu dumɔwui kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Seshibii lɛ baafite nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu daaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: How can I prevent my cassava roots from rotting underground before harvest time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa?

english: Underground root rot in cassava is usually caused by water collecting around the roots in flat or hard soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse loo shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmei mli lɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: What is eating the young inner leaves of my maize plants and leaving tiny black spots?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii diji bibii?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the growing center of maize. Applying recommended sprays or targeted neem extract into the whorl early in the morning helps protect the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ wo ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ he leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of essential nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing organic manure helps the flowers stay attached and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does leaving weeds on my farm reduce the final harvest I collect?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa naagbee ŋmaa ni mibuaa naa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds act like competing plants that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your main crop. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your crops get full access to food and grow to their full potential.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii babaoo ni amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: How long does a coconut seedling usually take to start producing fruits after I plant it in my field?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei dumɔwui jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi beni midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Hybrid coconut varieties usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties take 6 to 8 years. Proper watering, sunlight, and early fertilization speed up this process.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 8. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: What causes my young coconut leaves to turn yellow and dry up, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Yellowing leaves are often a sign of nutrient deficiency (like nitrogen or potassium), poor soil drainage, or drought stress. Adding well-rotted manure or fertilizer around the root zone helps the palm regain its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ (tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium) faaa, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. loo haomɔ ni jɛɔ hɔmɔ mli baa Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ woɔ he Shishifã lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant crops like cassava or maize between my young coconut trees, or will it damage them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ? Aloo ebaaha tso lɛ afite?

english: Yes, you can intercrop during the first 3 to 4 years while the coconut trees are still short. Planting food crops like beans, maize, or cassava helps maximize your land use and keeps the soil covered without harming the young palms if given enough space.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tso lɛ awo mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmei tso lɛ yɔɔ kuku lolo lɛ. Niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ tsuɔ nii babaoo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeee tsei bibii lɛ awui kɛji he ko yɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Why are the small green coconuts falling off my trees before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop is usually caused by sudden dry spells, lack of soil nutrients, or insect pests. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and applying potassium-rich fertilizer or ash helps keep the fruits attached until maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ aduawai ni fiteɔ oya baa ji ni amɛgbi trukaa. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Kɛ́ akɛ sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ fee ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo sũ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: How does a long dry season affect my mature coconut trees and the meat inside the nuts?
ga: Te hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ saa ŋmei tsei ni eda kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extended dry periods reduce fruit size, thin out the coconut meat, and cause early nut drop. Placing dried leaves or grass mulch around the base of the tree retains soil moisture and keeps the palms healthy during dry weather.
ga: Be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛgbiɔ lɛ baaha aduawai lɛ adalɛ aba shi. Ha ŋmei loo lɛ afee mlɛo ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo oya Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How far apart should I space my coconut seedlings when planting a new farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu ŋmɔ hee?

english: Coconut palms need plenty of sunlight and root room. Spacing them about 7.5 to 8 meters apart in rows ensures their leaves don't shade each other when fully grown, leading to maximum fruit yields.
ga: Hulu la babaoo kɛ shishifãi he miihia ŋmei tsei. Kɛ́ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 7.5 kɛyashi 8 kã tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akatsĩ amɛhe naa beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa babaoo.

english: Is it more profitable for me to sell harvested coconuts raw or to process them into oil?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ he akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ mi-coconuts ni akpa lɛ loo mafee amɛ fɔ?

english: Processing fresh coconuts into oil or copra usually brings higher profits than selling raw nuts. Processed products store longer, reduce crop waste, and sell for higher prices in urban markets.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmeii heei ni afee lɛ fɔ loo ŋmeii amli lɛ he fe ŋmeii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ. Abaanyɛ akɛ nibii ni afee lɛ ato be kakadaŋŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable before I spend money expanding my coconut farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa dani mafite shika koni mikɛgbala ŋmei ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Coconuts thrive best in deep, well-drained sandy loam soil with good sunlight. If water stays pooled on your land for days after heavy rain, the roots can rot, making it unsuitable without proper drainage channels.
ga: Kokooi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni hulu la babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Shishifãi lɛ hu baanyɛ agbo. Enɛ haa esaaa kɛji akɛ gbɛ ni sa bɛ ni nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ mli.

english: What natural organic manure can I use to make my coconut trees produce heavier nuts?
ga: Mɛɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ mikɛtsu nii koni mi-ŋmei tso lɛ awo ŋmeii ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Poultry manure, cow dung, and wood ash (which is rich in potassium) are great organic choices. Applying them around the root zone once or twice a year boosts fruit size and nut meat thickness.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei, tsina ŋmei kɛ tso ŋmei (ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli) ji tsofa ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ahala. Kɛ́ okɛwo shishifã lɛ he shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ adara kɛ amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What causes large holes chewed into the top stems of my young coconut palms?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-kokoo bibioo lɛ yiteŋ shwie bu agbo ko?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Rhinoceros beetle, which burrows into the growing crown of the tree. Clearing rotting logs from around your farm and placing sand or salt mixtures in leaf pockets helps deter them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rhinoceros ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni shwieɔ tso ko ni miida lɛ yiteŋ Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni egboi kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ni okɛ ŋã loo ŋoo ni akɛfutu mli awo baai kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi amɛnaa.

english: Why do my tomatoes start rotting so quickly after I pick them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ oya nɛkɛ beni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and ripen rapidly after being harvested, especially in hot weather. Small bruises from handling or moisture left on the skin create easy entry points for bacteria and fungi to quickly spoil the fruit.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli fãji bibii Kɛjɛ he ni mɔ ko kɛ ehe loo ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ lɛ, helai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ abote gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli oya ni eha aduawai lɛ afite oya.

english: Why does the skin of my tomatoes split open on the plant after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato hewolo lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When tomato plants take up a sudden large amount of water after a dry period, the inside of the fruit expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to crack open.
ga: Beni tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ mli loo lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do some of my ripening tomatoes develop pale, soft patches on the side facing the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ fioo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulu lɛ fã ni kwɛɔ lɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as sunscald. When tomato plants do not have enough leaves to cover the fruits, direct, intense sunlight cooks the exposed side of the fruit, damaging the skin and flesh.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ hulutsoo. Kɛji akɛ tomato tso lɛ bɛ baai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai lɛ anɔ Direct lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa baaha aduawai lɛ fã ni je kpo lɛ ashwere. ni yeɔ hewolo kɛ loo lɛ awui lɛ

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without turning into small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Extreme day or night temperatures, lack of consistent watering, or applying too much nitrogen fertilizer can stress the plant, causing it to drop its blossoms to conserve energy.
ga: Gbi loo gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa waa nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ daa Loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná haomɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves inward to reduce the amount of surface exposed to hot air and sun, which helps them retain moisture and reduce water loss through evaporation.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellowing of the lower leaves indicates that the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant naturally moves the available nitrogen from older leaves at the bottom to support new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crop stems grow tall and thin with very few leaves when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they compete for limited sunlight. The plants use most of their energy stretching upward to reach the light instead of building thick stems and strong leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa. Tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná la. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a he wa.

english: Why do some of my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die within a few days even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ekomɛi gboɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This sudden wilting is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that enters through the roots and blocks the plant's internal water transport tubes, causing it to collapse quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni shikpɔŋ ni boteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni tsiɔ nu ni akɛyaa tso lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ kɛbaa. ni haa efoɔ oya

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning small, distorted, and patchy yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji bibii, ni amɛtsake, ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This symptom is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies as they feed on the sap.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ jɛ Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ hiɛɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ be mli ni amɛyeɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft and watery if I leave them in the ground past the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, amɛfeɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu lɛ?

english: When mature cassava tubers sit in waterlogged soil for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, which causes fungi and bacteria to rapidly rot the starchy tubers inside the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara kwraa lɛ, amɛtaraa shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Oxygen nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in strong, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide the necessary shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for limited space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in a much smaller harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná he ko ni faaa, hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkwɔ, amɛgbɔjɔ, ni amɛgbɔjɔ, ni no haa yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa.

english: How do I know the best time of the year to start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ maje tsei afeemɔ shishi?

english: The ideal time to start planting is right at the beginning of the major rainy season, typically around April or May in southern Ghana, so the seeds get steady rainfall to grow strong roots.
ga: Be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ aje dumɔ shishi ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee April loo May yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ naa nugbɔ daa koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before producing pods during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛjeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ amɛmli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from water stress or high heat to save their energy for survival. Ensuring adequate shade trees on the farm helps keep the farm cool and protects the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ nu mli haomɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa miikpe amɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli ajɔ ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the ground is waterlogged and preventing the roots from breathing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata cacao tso ni eda lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning extra or dead branches opens up the canopy so light and air can pass through. This prevents damp conditions that breed diseases and allows the tree to focus its energy on growing healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ gbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni akafee ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ hela baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa tree to turn black and dry up?
ga: Mɛni miiha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during cold, wet weather when there is too much moisture trapped under the tree canopy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni etsi ehe yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Weeds steal the moisture, natural soil nutrients, and added fertilizer meant for your crops. Keeping the farm clear of weeds leaves all the food in the soil available for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛbaafata onibii ahe Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi akafee nɔ ko lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha onibii.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when their color completely changes—usually from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to bright orange-yellow—indicating the beans inside are fully mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji amɛhe su tsake kwraa—bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. aloo kɛjɛ etsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse—ni tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together is a good practice because maize grows fast and is harvested early, leaving the space open for the slower-growing cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, abele daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi he ko koni ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ atsɔ sɛɛ mli.

english: Can crops get sick from tiny germs that I cannot see with my eyes just like people do?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aná hela kɛjɛ helai bibii ni mikɛ mihiŋmɛii nyɛŋ ana tamɔ bɔ ni gbɔmɛi baanyɛ ana lɛ mli?

english: Yes, plants can get infected by tiny germs called viruses and bacteria that are invisible without a microscope. These germs enter the plant's internal sap system and cause leaves to curl, turn yellow, or stop growing, even when there are no visible worms on the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai bibii baanyɛ atsɔ tsei anɔ. Atsɛɔ amɛ muawai kɛ muawai. ni anyɛɛɛ ana kɛji akɛ akɛ tsɔne bibioo ko tsuuu nii Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ boteɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli. ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ekpaa dalɛ Kɛji ŋmeii ni anaaa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ po.

english: How can I tell if my plant's leaves are turning yellow because it needs food or because it has a virus?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ niyenii he miihia lɛ loo eyɛ hela ko?

english: Nutrient hunger usually makes entire leaves turn evenly yellow, starting from the bottom of the plant. A viral sickness usually causes irregular yellow patches, mosaic patterns, twisted leaves, or stunted new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ haa tso lɛ baa muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ po. Kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, hela ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni ejaaa, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi heei ni egbɔjɔ baa.

english: Can using my cutlass on a sick plant spread sickness to my healthy crops?
ga: Ani mi-dagger ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, just like germs spread through human blood, plant viruses travel in the plant's liquid sap. When you cut a diseased plant, infected sap sticks to your cutlass blade and gets injected directly into the next healthy plant you trim.
ga: Hɛɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ gbɔmɔ lá mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tso mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fãa gbɛ yɛ tso mli nu mli. Kɛ́ ofo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ Nu ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ otsɔne lɛ he ni akɛwoɔ tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ofoɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do small insects like flies spread invisible diseases between my crops?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii agbɛ helai ni anaaa lɛ ashwã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Insects act like carriers. When a small insect feeds on the sap of a sick plant, it picks up the invisible virus. When it flies over and bites a healthy crop, it passes that germ directly into the healthy plant's sap.
ga: Kplukai feɔ amɛnii tamɔ vectors. Beni kooloi bibii yeɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ. Ebaamɔ helai ni anaaa lɛ. Kɛji efo ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ŋmɔ lɛ Ekɛ helatsɛ lɛ yaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: If I plant stem cuttings from an old cassava farm, can they carry hidden sickness into my new land?
ga: Kɛji midu tso nine kɛjɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ momo ko mli lɛ Ani ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba mishikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, viruses live inside the internal sap of the plant. Even if a stem cutting looks healthy on the outside, it can carry the virus inside it, meaning the new plant will grow up already infected.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ hiɔ tsei amli nu lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ ni afo lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ, Shi ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ awo emli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei heei baakwɛ̃ momo ni hela baamɔ amɛ.

english: Can wild weeds growing around the edges of my farm pass diseases to my crops?
ga: Ani koo mli jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli?
